The result of a deletion is root-valid at some height: some uniform height
at which every non-root node holds between `t - 1` and `2 * t - 1` keys. The
height is that of the rebuilt tree; no relation to the height of the input
is claimed (see the module documentation).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.deleteRebuild_validRoot
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, ∃ height, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.ValidRoot t height (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.deleteRebuild t x tree)
statement:
public theorem deleteRebuild_validRoot [LinearOrder α] {t : Nat} (ht : 2 ≤ t) {x : α}
    {tree : BTree α} : ∃ height, ValidRoot t height (deleteRebuild t x tree)

docstring:
The result of a deletion from a root-valid tree is root-valid at the
same height, or one less when a root merge collapsed the root.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.delete_validRoot
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t height : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, tree.Ordered → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.ValidRoot t height tree → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.ValidRoot t height (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.delete t x tree) ∨ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.ValidRoot t (height - 1) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.delete t x tree)
statement:
public theorem delete_validRoot [LinearOrder α] {t height : Nat} (ht : 2 ≤ t)
    {x : α} {tree : BTree α} (hOrd : Ordered tree)
    (hv : ValidRoot t height tree) :
    ValidRoot t height (delete t x tree) ∨
      ValidRoot t (height - 1) (delete t x tree)

docstring:
The result of a deletion is root-valid at some height: the height of
the input or one less (see `delete_validRoot`).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.delete_validRoot_exists
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.IsBTree t tree → ∃ height, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.ValidRoot t height (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.delete t x tree)

docstring: The empty B-tree: a leaf with no keys.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.empty
signature: {α : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α
statement: public def empty : BTree α

docstring:
The inorder flattening of a tree: the keys of a leaf in list order, and
for an internal node the flattenings of the children interleaved with the
separator keys. Children or keys beyond the interleaving pattern of a
well-formed node are appended in order, so every key of the tree occurs in
the flattening: surplus children contribute their flattenings in order and
surplus keys contribute themselves in order (see `flatten_node_nil_cons`
and `flatten_node_cons_nil`). Computed in linear time by `flattenAux`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten
signature: {α : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α → List α
statement: public def flatten (tree : BTree α) : List α

docstring:
Append the inorder traversal of a tree to an existing suffix in linear
time: subtrees interleaved with separator keys, accumulated without
recopying left results. The suffix is built right to left: at an internal
node the suffix passed to each child already holds everything to its right,
so `flattenAux child suffix` only prepends that child's keys, and each key
is copied once (as part of its node's key list at a leaf, or by one `cons`
for a separator). Children or keys beyond the interleaving pattern of a
well-formed node are appended in order (see `flatten`), so every key of
the tree occurs in the result.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flattenAux
signature: {α : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α → List α → List α
statement: public def flattenAux : BTree α → List α → List α

docstring: `flattenAux` prepends the flattening of its tree to the suffix.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flattenAux_eq
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α) (suffix : List α), t.flattenAux suffix = t.flatten ++ suffix
statement:
public theorem flattenAux_eq (t : BTree α) (suffix : List α) :
    flattenAux t suffix = flatten t ++ suffix

docstring:
The flattening of a deletion from a B-tree is the erasure of the key
from the flattening of the original tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_delete
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.IsBTree t tree → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.delete t x tree).flatten = tree.flatten.erase x

docstring:
The flattening of a deletion is the erasure of the key from the flattening
of the original tree. Orderedness is the side condition; no occupancy
hypothesis on the input beyond `2 ≤ t` is needed.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_deleteRebuild
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, tree.Ordered → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.deleteRebuild t x tree).flatten = tree.flatten.erase x

docstring: Deleting the same key twice has the same flattening as deleting it once.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_deleteRebuild_deleteRebuild
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, tree.Ordered → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.deleteRebuild t x (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.deleteRebuild t x tree)).flatten = (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.deleteRebuild t x tree).flatten

docstring:
Deleting an absent key leaves the flattening, hence the stored set,
unchanged. The tree itself may be rebuilt to a different shape with the same
flattening.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_deleteRebuild_of_not_mem
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, tree.Ordered → x ∉ tree.flatten → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.deleteRebuild t x tree).flatten = tree.flatten

docstring:
Deleting the same key twice has the same flattening as deleting it
once.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_delete_delete
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.IsBTree t tree → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.delete t x (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.delete t x tree)).flatten = (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.delete t x tree).flatten
statement:
public theorem flatten_delete_delete [LinearOrder α] {t : Nat} (ht : 2 ≤ t)
    {x : α} {tree : BTree α} (h : IsBTree t tree) :
    flatten (delete t x (delete t x tree)) =
      flatten (delete t x tree)

docstring:
Building a tree from a strictly increasing list returns exactly that list
as the flattening. This is the specification of `fromList` on sorted input
that the specification of `deleteRebuild` is reduced to.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_fromList_of_pairwise
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {keys : List α}, List.Pairwise (fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 < x2) keys → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.fromList t keys).flatten = keys
statement:
public theorem flatten_fromList_of_pairwise [LinearOrder α] {t : Nat} (ht : 2 ≤ t) :
    ∀ {keys : List α}, keys.Pairwise (· < ·) → flatten (fromList t keys) = keys

docstring:
The flattening of an insertion is sorted insertion into the flattening of the
original tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.IsBTree t tree → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.insert t x tree).flatten = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.orderedInsert x tree.flatten

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_leaf
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {keys : List α}, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.leaf keys).flatten = keys
statement:
public theorem flatten_leaf {keys : List α} :
    flatten (.leaf keys : BTree α) = keys

docstring:
Deleting a key decreases the number of stored keys by one when the key
was present, and leaves it unchanged otherwise.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_length_delete
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.IsBTree t tree → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.delete t x tree).flatten.length = if x ∈ tree.flatten then tree.flatten.length - 1 else tree.flatten.length
statement:
public theorem flatten_length_delete [LinearOrder α] {t : Nat} (ht : 2 ≤ t)
    {x : α} {tree : BTree α} (h : IsBTree t tree) :
    (flatten (delete t x tree)).length =
      if x ∈ flatten tree then (flatten tree).length - 1
      else (flatten tree).length

docstring:
Deleting a key decreases the number of stored keys by one when the key was
present, and leaves it unchanged otherwise.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_length_deleteRebuild
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, tree.Ordered → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.deleteRebuild t x tree).flatten.length = if x ∈ tree.flatten then tree.flatten.length - 1 else tree.flatten.length
statement:
public theorem flatten_length_deleteRebuild [LinearOrder α] {t : Nat} (ht : 2 ≤ t) {x : α}
    {tree : BTree α} (h : Ordered tree) :
    (flatten (deleteRebuild t x tree)).length =
      if x ∈ flatten tree then (flatten tree).length - 1 else (flatten tree).length

docstring:
Inserting a present key leaves the flattening length unchanged, and inserting an
absent key increases it by one.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_length_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.IsBTree t tree → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.insert t x tree).flatten.length = if x ∈ tree.flatten then tree.flatten.length else tree.flatten.length + 1
statement:
public theorem flatten_length_insert [LinearOrder α] {t : Nat} (ht : 2 ≤ t) {x : α}
    {tree : BTree α} (h : IsBTree t tree) :
    (flatten (insert t x tree)).length =
      if x ∈ flatten tree then (flatten tree).length else (flatten tree).length + 1

docstring:
Splitting a node's key and child lists at a separator splits its
flattening at that separator, provided the left lists are in the
well-formed ratio of one more child than keys.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_node_append_cons
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {median : α} {keys₁ : List α} {children₁ : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α)} {keys₂ : List α} {children₂ : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α)}, children₁.length = keys₁.length + 1 → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.node (keys₁ ++ median :: keys₂) (children₁ ++ children₂)).flatten = (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.node keys₁ children₁).flatten ++ median :: (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.node keys₂ children₂).flatten
statement:
public theorem flatten_node_append_cons {median : α} :
    ∀ {keys₁ : List α} {children₁ : List (BTree α)} {keys₂ : List α}
      {children₂ : List (BTree α)},
      children₁.length = keys₁.length + 1 →
      flatten (node (keys₁ ++ median :: keys₂) (children₁ ++ children₂) :
          BTree α) =
        flatten (node keys₁ children₁ : BTree α) ++
          median :: flatten (node keys₂ children₂ : BTree α)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_node_cons
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {key : α} {keys : List α} {child : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α} {children : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α)}, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.node (key :: keys) (child :: children)).flatten = child.flatten ++ key :: (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.node keys children).flatten
statement:
public theorem flatten_node_cons {key : α} {keys : List α}
    {child : BTree α} {children : List (BTree α)} :
    flatten (.node (key :: keys) (child :: children)) =
      flatten child ++ key :: flatten (.node keys children)

docstring:
Flattening a node with no children returns its separator keys in
order. This covers nodes with more keys than a well-formed node would
have.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_node_cons_nil
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {key : α} {keys : List α}, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.node (key :: keys) []).flatten = key :: (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.node keys []).flatten

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_node_nil
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {child : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.node [] [child]).flatten = child.flatten
statement:
public theorem flatten_node_nil {child : BTree α} :
    flatten (.node [] [child] : BTree α) = flatten child

docstring:
Flattening a node with no separator keys concatenates the flattenings
of its children in order. This covers nodes with more children than a
well-formed node would have.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_node_nil_cons
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {child : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α} {children : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α)}, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.node [] (child :: children)).flatten = child.flatten ++ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.node [] children).flatten
statement:
public theorem flatten_node_nil_cons {child : BTree α}
    {children : List (BTree α)} :
    flatten (.node [] (child :: children) : BTree α) =
      flatten child ++ flatten (.node [] children)

docstring: Flattening a node with neither keys nor children is empty.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_node_nil_nil
signature: ∀ {α : Type u}, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.node [] []).flatten = []
statement:
public theorem flatten_node_nil_nil :
    flatten (.node [] [] : BTree α) = []

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.flatten_node_pair
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {median : α} {left right : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.node [median] [left, right]).flatten = left.flatten ++ median :: right.flatten

docstring: Build a B-tree by inserting the list from right to left into the empty tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.fromList
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → ℕ → List α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α
statement: public def fromList [LinearOrder α] (t : Nat) : List α → BTree α

docstring:
The flattening of an insertion result, placing a promoted median between the two
trees it separates.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.grownFlatten
signature: {α : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.InsResult α → List α
statement: public def grownFlatten : InsResult α → List α

docstring:
Split-returning insertion into a subtree. The auxiliary `insList` walks the separator
and child lists of an internal node from the left, descends into the unique child whose
separator range contains the key, and rebuilds the lists on the way back, inserting the
extra child and promoted median when that child split. The rebuilt node is then passed
through `mkNode`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.ins
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → ℕ → α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.InsResult α
statement: public def ins [LinearOrder α] (t : Nat) (x : α) : BTree α → InsResult α

docstring:
Insert into a leaf's key list, splitting the leaf around the median key when the
inserted list exceeds `2 * t - 1` keys.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.insLeaf
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → ℕ → α → List α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.InsResult α
statement: public def insLeaf [LinearOrder α] (t : Nat) (x : α) (keys : List α) : InsResult α

docstring:
Insert a key into a B-tree of minimum degree `t`, growing a new root with a single
separator exactly when the old root splits. Inserting an already-present key returns a
tree with the same flattening.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.insert
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → ℕ → α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α
statement: public def insert [LinearOrder α] (t : Nat) (x : α) (tree : BTree α) : BTree α

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.instMembership
signature: {α : Type u} → Membership α (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α)
statement: public instance : Membership α (BTree α)

docstring: The number of keys stored at the root of a tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.keyCount
signature: {α : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α → ℕ
statement: public def keyCount : BTree α → Nat

docstring:
The greatest key of a tree, found by descending the rightmost spine:
at each internal node, recurse into the last child only. Each step splits
a child list of length at most `2 * t`, so on a valid tree this costs
`O(t * height)`; it never materializes the flattening. The characterization
as the last key of the flattening is `exists_maxKey_flatten` below.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.maxKey
signature: {α : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α → Option α
statement: def maxKey : BTree α → Option α

docstring:
A key is in the result of a deletion exactly when it was in the
original tree and is not the deleted key.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.mem_delete
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x y : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.IsBTree t tree → (y ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.delete t x tree ↔ y ≠ x ∧ y ∈ tree)

docstring:
A key is in the result of a deletion exactly when it was in the original
tree and is not the deleted key.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.mem_deleteRebuild
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x y : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.IsBTree t tree → (y ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.deleteRebuild t x tree ↔ y ≠ x ∧ y ∈ tree)

docstring: A key is in a tree built from a list exactly when it is in the list.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.mem_fromList
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {xs : List α}, x ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.fromList t xs ↔ x ∈ xs
statement:
public theorem mem_fromList [LinearOrder α] {t : Nat} (ht : 2 ≤ t) {x : α}
    {xs : List α} : x ∈ fromList t xs ↔ x ∈ xs

docstring: Inserting a key adds exactly that key to membership.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.mem_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x y : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.IsBTree t tree → (y ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.insert t x tree ↔ y = x ∨ y ∈ tree)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.mem_leaf
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {x : α} {keys : List α}, x ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.leaf keys ↔ x ∈ keys
statement:
public theorem mem_leaf {x : α} {keys : List α} :
    x ∈ (leaf keys : BTree α) ↔ x ∈ keys

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.mem_node
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {x : α} {keys : List α} {children : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α)}, x ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.node keys children ↔ x ∈ keys ∨ ∃ child ∈ children, x ∈ child

docstring:
Merge two trees of the same height and a separator key between them
into a single node: the keys concatenate around the separator and the
children concatenate. Used when both trees hold `t - 1` keys, so the
result holds `2 * t - 1`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.merge
signature: {α : Type u} → α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α
statement: def merge (sep : α) : BTree α → BTree α → BTree α

docstring:
The least key of a tree, found by descending the leftmost spine. The
characterization as the first key of the flattening is
`exists_minKey_flatten` below.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.minKey
signature: {α : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α → Option α
statement: def minKey : BTree α → Option α

docstring:
The smart constructor for internal nodes after insertion below: keep the node when it
has at most `2 * t - 1` keys, and split it otherwise.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.mkNode
signature: {α : Type u} → ℕ → List α → List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.InsResult α
statement: public def mkNode (t : Nat) (keys : List α) (children : List (BTree α)) : InsResult α

docstring: The deleted key is absent from the result.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.not_mem_delete
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.IsBTree t tree → x ∉ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.delete t x tree
statement:
public theorem not_mem_delete [LinearOrder α] {t : Nat} (ht : 2 ≤ t) {x : α}
    {tree : BTree α} (h : IsBTree t tree) : x ∉ delete t x tree

docstring: The deleted key is absent from the result.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.not_mem_deleteRebuild
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.IsBTree t tree → x ∉ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.deleteRebuild t x tree
statement:
public theorem not_mem_deleteRebuild [LinearOrder α] {t : Nat} (ht : 2 ≤ t) {x : α}
    {tree : BTree α} (h : IsBTree t tree) : x ∉ deleteRebuild t x tree

docstring: Deletion preserves orderedness of the result.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.ordered_delete
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.IsBTree t tree → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.delete t x tree).Ordered
statement:
public theorem ordered_delete [LinearOrder α] {t : Nat} (ht : 2 ≤ t) {x : α}
    {tree : BTree α} (h : IsBTree t tree) : Ordered (delete t x tree)

docstring:
Deletion preserves orderedness of the result, in the form recorded by
`IsBTree.deleteRebuild`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.ordered_deleteRebuild
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : ℕ}, 2 ≤ t → ∀ {x : α} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α}, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.deleteRebuild t x tree).Ordered
statement:
public theorem ordered_deleteRebuild [LinearOrder α] {t : Nat} (ht : 2 ≤ t) {x : α}
    {tree : BTree α} : Ordered (deleteRebuild t x tree)

docstring:
Split a nonempty list into all but its last element and its last
element.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.splitLast
signature: {α : Type u} → List α → Option (List α × α)
statement: def splitLast : List α → Option (List α × α)

docstring:
Split an overfull internal node around its median separator: the left tree keeps the
first `t - 1` keys and first `t` children, the median key is promoted, and the right tree
keeps the remaining keys and children.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.splitNode
signature: {α : Type u} → ℕ → List α → List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.InsResult α
statement: public def splitNode (t : Nat) (keys : List α) (children : List (BTree α)) : InsResult α

docstring:
The height of a tree following first children: leaves have height `0`
and an internal node is one taller than its first child. For a valid tree
this is the height index of `Valid`/`ValidRoot`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree.treeHeight
signature: {α : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BTree α → ℕ
statement: public def treeHeight : BTree α → Nat

docstring:
A ball tree over points `Fin d → Int`: empty, a point leaf, or a node
carrying a bounding sphere (center and squared-radius bound) over two
children.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree
signature: ℕ → Type
statement: inductive BallTree (d : Nat)

docstring:
The bounding-sphere invariant: at a node with center `c` and squared-radius bound
`bound`, every point in either subtree lies within squared distance
`bound` of `c`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.Valid
signature: {d : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree d → Prop
statement: inductive Valid : BallTree d → Prop

docstring:
Builds a ball tree by recursive halving: the center is the first point,
the bound is `radiusSq` over the whole list, and the children are built
from the two halves of the list.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.build
signature: {d : ℕ} → List (Fin d → ℤ) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree d
statement: def build : List (Fin d → Int) → BallTree d

docstring:
Squared Euclidean distance between two points, as a natural number:
the sum over coordinates of `(p i - q i) ^ 2`, computed over the integers
and converted to `Nat`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq
signature: {d : ℕ} → (Fin d → ℤ) → (Fin d → ℤ) → ℕ
statement: def distSq (p q : Fin d → Int) : Nat

docstring: Squared distance is symmetric.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq_comm
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} (p q : Fin d → ℤ), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq p q = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq q p
statement: theorem distSq_comm (p q : Fin d → Int) : distSq p q = distSq q p

docstring: Every point of `pts` lies in the sphere computed by `radiusSq`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq_le_radiusSq
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} {c p : Fin d → ℤ} {pts : List (Fin d → ℤ)}, p ∈ pts → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq c p ≤ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.radiusSq c pts
statement:
theorem distSq_le_radiusSq {c p : Fin d → Int} {pts : List (Fin d → Int)}
    (hp : p ∈ pts) : distSq c p ≤ radiusSq c pts

docstring:
A weak triangle inequality for squared distance, with the factor `2`
coming from `(x + y) ^ 2 ≤ 2 * (x ^ 2 + y ^ 2)` coordinatewise. This is
the estimate that makes bounding-sphere pruning sound without square
roots.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq_le_two_mul
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} (a b c : Fin d → ℤ), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq a c ≤ 2 * (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq a b + Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq b c)
statement:
theorem distSq_le_two_mul (a b c : Fin d → Int) :
    distSq a c ≤ 2 * (distSq a b + distSq b c)

docstring: The length of the point list is the size of the tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.length_toList
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree d), t.toList.length = t.size
statement: theorem length_toList (t : BallTree d) : t.toList.length = t.size

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.length_toListAux
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree d) (acc : List (Fin d → ℤ)), (t.toListAux acc).length = t.size + acc.length
statement:
theorem length_toListAux (t : BallTree d) (acc : List (Fin d → Int)) :
    (t.toListAux acc).length = t.size + acc.length

docstring: Membership in the search of a built tree, stated on the input.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.mem_search_build_iff
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} (pts : List (Fin d → ℤ)) {query p : Fin d → ℤ} {radius : ℕ}, p ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.build pts).search query radius ↔ p ∈ pts ∧ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq query p ≤ radius
statement:
theorem mem_search_build_iff (pts : List (Fin d → Int))
    {query p : Fin d → Int} {radius : Nat} :
    p ∈ (build pts).search query radius ↔
      p ∈ pts ∧ distSq query p ≤ radius

docstring: Membership in the search of a valid tree, stated on its point list.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.mem_search_iff
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree d}, t.Valid → ∀ {query p : Fin d → ℤ} {radius : ℕ}, p ∈ t.search query radius ↔ p ∈ t.toList ∧ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq query p ≤ radius
statement:
theorem mem_search_iff {t : BallTree d} (h : t.Valid)
    {query p : Fin d → Int} {radius : Nat} :
    p ∈ t.search query radius ↔ p ∈ t.toList ∧ distSq query p ≤ radius

docstring:
Membership in the point list of a built tree is membership in the
input.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.mem_toList_build_iff
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} (pts : List (Fin d → ℤ)) (p : Fin d → ℤ), p ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.build pts).toList ↔ p ∈ pts
statement:
theorem mem_toList_build_iff (pts : List (Fin d → Int)) (p : Fin d → Int) :
    p ∈ (build pts).toList ↔ p ∈ pts

docstring:
The squared-radius bound for a sphere centered at `c` covering `pts`:
the maximum squared distance from `c` to a point of `pts`, or `0` if `pts`
is empty.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.radiusSq
signature: {d : ℕ} → (Fin d → ℤ) → List (Fin d → ℤ) → ℕ
statement: def radiusSq (c : Fin d → Int) (pts : List (Fin d → Int)) : Nat

docstring:
Similarity search: the points of the tree within squared distance
`radius` of `query`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.search
signature: {d : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree d → (Fin d → ℤ) → ℕ → List (Fin d → ℤ)
statement:
def search (t : BallTree d) (query : Fin d → Int) (radius : Nat) :
    List (Fin d → Int)

docstring:
Accumulator similarity search: the points of the tree within squared
distance `radius` of `query`, collected in front of `acc` in linear time.
A node with center `c` and bound `bound` is pruned when
`2 * (bound + radius) < distSq c query`, since by `distSq_le_two_mul` no
point of the subtree can then lie within the query ball.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.searchAux
signature: {d : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree d → (Fin d → ℤ) → ℕ → List (Fin d → ℤ) → List (Fin d → ℤ)
statement:
def searchAux : BallTree d → (Fin d → Int) → Nat →
    List (Fin d → Int) → List (Fin d → Int)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.searchAux_eq_filter_append
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree d}, t.Valid → ∀ (query : Fin d → ℤ) (radius : ℕ) (acc : List (Fin d → ℤ)), t.searchAux query radius acc = List.filter (fun p ↦ Decidable.decide (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq query p ≤ radius)) t.toList ++ acc
statement:
theorem searchAux_eq_filter_append {t : BallTree d} (h : t.Valid)
    (query : Fin d → Int) (radius : Nat) (acc : List (Fin d → Int)) :
    t.searchAux query radius acc =
      t.toList.filter (fun p => distSq query p ≤ radius) ++ acc

docstring:
The search of a built tree is its point list filtered by the distance
predicate.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.search_build
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} (pts : List (Fin d → ℤ)) (query : Fin d → ℤ) (radius : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.build pts).search query radius = List.filter (fun p ↦ Decidable.decide (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq query p ≤ radius)) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.build pts).toList
statement:
theorem search_build (pts : List (Fin d → Int)) (query : Fin d → Int)
    (radius : Nat) :
    (build pts).search query radius =
      (build pts).toList.filter (fun p => distSq query p ≤ radius)

docstring:
The search of a built tree permutes the input filtered by the
distance predicate.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.search_build_perm
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} (pts : List (Fin d → ℤ)) (query : Fin d → ℤ) (radius : ℕ), ((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.build pts).search query radius).Perm (List.filter (fun p ↦ Decidable.decide (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq query p ≤ radius)) pts)
statement:
theorem search_build_perm (pts : List (Fin d → Int)) (query : Fin d → Int)
    (radius : Nat) :
    ((build pts).search query radius).Perm
      (pts.filter (fun p => distSq query p ≤ radius))

docstring:
The search of a valid tree is its point list filtered by the distance
predicate; pruning against the bounding spheres loses no point.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.search_eq_filter
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree d}, t.Valid → ∀ (query : Fin d → ℤ) (radius : ℕ), t.search query radius = List.filter (fun p ↦ Decidable.decide (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.distSq query p ≤ radius)) t.toList
statement:
theorem search_eq_filter {t : BallTree d} (h : t.Valid)
    (query : Fin d → Int) (radius : Nat) :
    t.search query radius =
      t.toList.filter (fun p => distSq query p ≤ radius)

docstring: The number of points stored in a tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.size
signature: {d : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree d → ℕ
statement: def size : BallTree d → Nat

docstring: The size of a built tree is the number of input points.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.size_build
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} (pts : List (Fin d → ℤ)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.build pts).size = pts.length
statement:
theorem size_build (pts : List (Fin d → Int)) :
    (build pts).size = pts.length

docstring: The points stored in a tree, from left to right.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.toList
signature: {d : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree d → List (Fin d → ℤ)
statement: def toList (t : BallTree d) : List (Fin d → Int)

docstring:
Accumulator traversal collecting the points of a tree in front of
`acc`, from left to right, in linear time.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.toListAux
signature: {d : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree d → List (Fin d → ℤ) → List (Fin d → ℤ)
statement: def toListAux : BallTree d → List (Fin d → Int) → List (Fin d → Int)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.toListAux_append
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree d) (acc : List (Fin d → ℤ)), t.toListAux acc = t.toListAux [] ++ acc
statement:
theorem toListAux_append (t : BallTree d) (acc : List (Fin d → Int)) :
    t.toListAux acc = t.toListAux [] ++ acc

docstring: The point list of a built tree is a permutation of the input.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.toList_build_perm
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} (pts : List (Fin d → ℤ)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.build pts).toList.Perm pts
statement:
theorem toList_build_perm (pts : List (Fin d → Int)) :
    (build pts).toList.Perm pts

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.toList_empty
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.empty.toList = []
statement: theorem toList_empty : (BallTree.empty : BallTree d).toList = []

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.toList_leaf
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} (p : Fin d → ℤ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.leaf p).toList = [p]
statement: theorem toList_leaf (p : Fin d → Int) : (BallTree.leaf p).toList = [p]

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.toList_node
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} (center : Fin d → ℤ) (bound : ℕ) (left right : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree d), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.node center bound left right).toList = left.toList ++ right.toList
statement:
theorem toList_node (center : Fin d → Int) (bound : Nat)
    (left right : BallTree d) :
    (BallTree.node center bound left right).toList =
      left.toList ++ right.toList

docstring: A tree built by halving satisfies the bounding-sphere invariant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.valid_build
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} (pts : List (Fin d → ℤ)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BallTree.build pts).Valid
statement: theorem valid_build (pts : List (Fin d → Int)) : (build pts).Valid

docstring: Increment a low-first fixed-width counter, charging one tick per changed existing bit.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.increment
signature: {k : ℕ} → Vector Bool k → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (Vector Bool k)
statement: public def increment {k : Nat} (bits : Vector Bool k) : TimeM Nat (Vector Bool k)

docstring: The exact increment cost is the initial one-prefix plus a first zero when present.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.increment_time
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.increment bits).time = (List.takeWhile id bits.toList).length + if (List.takeWhile id bits.toList).length < k then 1 else 0

docstring: Increment changes at most the fixed number of existing bits.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.increment_time_le
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.increment bits).time ≤ k
statement:
public theorem increment_time_le {k : Nat} (bits : Vector Bool k) :
    (increment bits).time ≤ k

docstring: All-one input realizes the worst-case cost of one flip per existing bit.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.increment_time_replicate_true
signature: ∀ (k : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.increment (Vector.replicate k Bool.true)).time = k
statement:
public theorem increment_time_replicate_true (k : Nat) :
    (increment (Vector.replicate k true)).time = k

docstring: Increment adds one to the unsigned value modulo the fixed width.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.increment_value
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k), (BitVec.ofBoolListLE (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.increment bits).ret.toList).toNat = ((BitVec.ofBoolListLE bits.toList).toNat + 1) % 2 ^ k

docstring: Reset every set bit to false, charging one tick for each changed existing bit.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset
signature: {k : ℕ} → Vector Bool k → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (Vector Bool k)
statement: public def reset {k : Nat} (bits : Vector Bool k) : TimeM Nat (Vector Bool k)

docstring: Reset charge plus final one-bit potential equals the initial potential.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset_potential
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset bits).time + (List.map Bool.toNat (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset bits).ret.toList).sum = (List.map Bool.toNat bits.toList).sum

docstring: Resetting a reset counter preserves the complete returned vector.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset_ret_idempotent
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset bits).ret).ret = (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset bits).ret
statement:
public theorem reset_ret_idempotent {k : Nat} (bits : Vector Bool k) :
    (reset (reset bits).ret).ret = (reset bits).ret

docstring: The exact reset charge is the number of set input bits.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset_time
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset bits).time = (List.map Bool.toNat bits.toList).sum
statement:
public theorem reset_time {k : Nat} (bits : Vector Bool k) :
    (reset bits).time = (bits.toList.map Bool.toNat).sum

docstring: A second reset has zero flip charge.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset_time_after_reset
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset bits).ret).time = 0
statement:
public theorem reset_time_after_reset {k : Nat} (bits : Vector Bool k) :
    (reset (reset bits).ret).time = 0

docstring: The exact reset charge is the indexed Hamming difference of input and output.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset_time_changes
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset bits).time = (List.map (fun i ↦ if bits.toList.getD i Bool.false ≠ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset bits).ret.toList.getD i Bool.false then 1 else 0) (List.range k)).sum
statement:
public theorem reset_time_changes {k : Nat} (bits : Vector Bool k) :
    (reset bits).time = ((List.range k).map fun i =>
      if bits.toList.getD i false ≠ (reset bits).ret.toList.getD i false
      then 1 else 0).sum

docstring: Reset changes at most the fixed number of existing bits.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset_time_le
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset bits).time ≤ k
statement:
public theorem reset_time_le {k : Nat} (bits : Vector Bool k) :
    (reset bits).time ≤ k

docstring: Resetting an all-false counter has zero flip charge.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset_time_replicate_false
signature: ∀ (k : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset (Vector.replicate k Bool.false)).time = 0
statement:
public theorem reset_time_replicate_false (k : Nat) :
    (reset (Vector.replicate k false)).time = 0

docstring: Reset at width zero has zero flip charge.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset_time_zero_width
signature: ∀ (bits : Vector Bool 0), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset bits).time = 0
statement:
public theorem reset_time_zero_width (bits : Vector Bool 0) :
    (reset bits).time = 0

docstring: Reset returns the all-false bit list at the original width.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset_toList
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset bits).ret.toList = List.replicate k Bool.false
statement:
public theorem reset_toList {k : Nat} (bits : Vector Bool k) :
    (reset bits).ret.toList = List.replicate k false

docstring: Reset refines the unsigned numeric constant zero.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset_value
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k), (BitVec.ofBoolListLE (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.reset bits).ret.toList).toNat = 0
statement:
public theorem reset_value {k : Nat} (bits : Vector Bool k) :
    (BitVec.ofBoolListLE (reset bits).ret.toList).toNat = 0

docstring: Execute successive increments, each consuming the actual previous returned counter.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run
signature: {k : ℕ} → Vector Bool k → ℕ → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (Vector Bool k)
statement: public def run {k : Nat} (bits : Vector Bool k) : Nat → TimeM Nat (Vector Bool k)

docstring: Bit `i` changes exactly `n / 2 ^ i` times in an actual zero-start run.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run_bit_flips
signature: ∀ (k i n : ℕ), i < k → (List.map (fun t ↦ if (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run (Vector.replicate k Bool.false) t).ret.toList.getD i Bool.false ≠ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run (Vector.replicate k Bool.false) (t + 1)).ret.toList.getD i Bool.false then 1 else 0) (List.range n)).sum = n / 2 ^ i
statement:
public theorem run_bit_flips (k i n : Nat) (hi : i < k) :
    ((List.range n).map fun t =>
      if (run (Vector.replicate k false) t).ret.toList.getD i false ≠
          (run (Vector.replicate k false) (t + 1)).ret.toList.getD i false
        then 1 else 0).sum = n / 2 ^ i

docstring: A successor run returns the increment of its actual predecessor state.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run_ret_succ
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k) (n : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run bits (n + 1)).ret = (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.increment (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run bits n).ret).ret
statement:
public theorem run_ret_succ {k : Nat} (bits : Vector Bool k) (n : Nat) :
    (run bits (n + 1)).ret = (increment (run bits n).ret).ret

docstring: The actual zero-start run cost is the sum of its existing bits' exact flip counts.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run_time_eq
signature: ∀ (k n : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run (Vector.replicate k Bool.false) n).time = (List.map (fun i ↦ n / 2 ^ i) (List.range k)).sum

docstring: A positive-width zero-start run costs at least its length.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run_time_ge
signature: ∀ (k n : ℕ), 0 < k → n ≤ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run (Vector.replicate k Bool.false) n).time
statement:
public theorem run_time_ge (k n : Nat) (hk : 0 < k) :
    n ≤ (run (Vector.replicate k false) n).time

docstring: A positive-length zero-start run costs strictly fewer than twice its length.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run_time_lt
signature: ∀ (k n : ℕ), 0 < n → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run (Vector.replicate k Bool.false) n).time < 2 * n
statement:
public theorem run_time_lt (k n : Nat) (hn : 0 < n) :
    (run (Vector.replicate k false) n).time < 2 * n

docstring: A successor run adds the next increment cost to the actual accumulated cost.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run_time_succ
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k) (n : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run bits (n + 1)).time = (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run bits n).time + (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.increment (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run bits n).ret).time

docstring: An arbitrary initial unsigned value advances by the run length modulo the fixed width.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run_value
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k) (n : ℕ), (BitVec.ofBoolListLE (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run bits n).ret.toList).toNat = ((BitVec.ofBoolListLE bits.toList).toNat + n) % 2 ^ k

docstring: A zero-step run returns the full pure input, with zero accumulated cost.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run_zero
signature: ∀ {k : ℕ} (bits : Vector Bool k), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinaryCounter.run bits 0 = Pure.pure bits
statement:
public theorem run_zero {k : Nat} (bits : Vector Bool k) :
    run bits 0 = pure bits

docstring: `All p tree` states that every key in `tree` satisfies `p`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.All
signature: {α : Type u} → (α → Prop) → BinaryTree α → Prop
statement: public def All {α : Type u} (p : α → Prop) : BinaryTree α → Prop

docstring: Structural membership, independent of the search-tree invariant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.Mem
signature: {α : Type u} → α → BinaryTree α → Prop
statement: public def Mem {α : Type u} (x : α) : BinaryTree α → Prop

docstring: Every left key is smaller and every right key is larger, recursively.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.Ordered
signature: {α : Type u} → [LT α] → BinaryTree α → Prop
statement: public def Ordered {α : Type u} [LT α] : BinaryTree α → Prop

docstring: `All` is equivalent to universal quantification over structural membership.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.all_iff_forall_mem
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {tree : BinaryTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.All p tree ↔ ∀ x ∈ tree, p x

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.contains
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → α → BinaryTree α → Bool
statement: public def contains {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] (x : α) : BinaryTree α → Bool

docstring: Search is equivalent to structural membership for an ordered tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.contains_eq_true_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {x : α} {tree : BinaryTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.Ordered tree → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.contains x tree = Bool.true ↔ x ∈ tree)

docstring: Delete a key, splicing the subtrees of a deleted node together with `join`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.delete

docstring: Remove the first tree whose root is minimal, preferring earlier trees on ties.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinomialForest.removeMinTree
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinomialTree α) → Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinomialTree α × List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinomialTree α))

public def removeMinTree [LinearOrder α] :

docstring: Removing a minimum tree partitions the forest and returns a globally minimal root.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinomialForest.removeMinTree_spec
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {trees : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinomialTree α)} {minimum : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinomialTree α} {rest : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinomialTree α)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinomialForest.removeMinTree trees = Option.some (minimum, rest) → minimum.elements + Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinomialForest.elements rest = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinomialForest.elements trees ∧ minimum ∈ trees ∧ rest.Sublist trees ∧ ∀ tree ∈ trees, minimum.root ≤ tree.root
statement:
public theorem removeMinTree_spec [LinearOrder α]
    {trees : List (BinomialTree α)} {minimum : BinomialTree α}
    {rest : List (BinomialTree α)} (result : removeMinTree trees = some (minimum, rest)) :
    minimum.elements + elements rest = elements trees ∧
      minimum ∈ trees ∧ rest.Sublist trees ∧
      ∀ tree ∈ trees, minimum.root ≤ tree.root

docstring:
A Bloom filter over `α` with `m` bits: a list of hash functions into `Fin m` and the bit vector.
No false-positive rate is claimed because the model supplies no probability distribution.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter
signature: Type u → ℕ → Type u
statement: public structure BloomFilter (α : Type u) (m : Nat)

docstring:
Bit-set characterization of insertion: after inserting `x`, bit `i` is set exactly when it was
already set or some hash function sends `x` to `i`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter.bit_insert_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {m : ℕ} (filter : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter α m) (x : α) (i : Fin m), (filter.insert x).bits[i] = Bool.true ↔ filter.bits[i] = Bool.true ∨ ∃ h ∈ filter.hashes, h x = i
statement:
public theorem bit_insert_iff {α : Type u} {m : Nat} (filter : BloomFilter α m)
    (x : α) (i : Fin m) :
    (filter.insert x).bits[i] = true ↔
      filter.bits[i] = true ∨ ∃ h ∈ filter.hashes, h x = i

docstring: The empty Bloom filter for the given hash functions: every bit is unset.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter.empty
signature: {α : Type u} → {m : ℕ} → List (α → Fin m) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter α m
statement: public def empty {α : Type u} {m : Nat} (hashes : List (α → Fin m)) : BloomFilter α m

docstring: Inserts an element by setting the bit selected by each hash function.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter.insert
signature: {α : Type u} → {m : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter α m → α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter α m
statement:
public def insert {α : Type u} {m : Nat} (filter : BloomFilter α m) (x : α) :
    BloomFilter α m

docstring: Whether every bit selected for `x` is set, so `x` may have been inserted.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter.mayContain
signature: {α : Type u} → {m : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter α m → α → Bool
statement: public def mayContain {α : Type u} {m : Nat} (filter : BloomFilter α m) (x : α) : Bool

docstring: With at least one hash function, the empty filter reports every element absent.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter.mayContain_empty
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {m : ℕ} {hashes : List (α → Fin m)}, hashes ≠ [] → ∀ (x : α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter.empty hashes).mayContain x = Bool.false

docstring: `mayContain` holds exactly when every hash-selected bit is set.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter.mayContain_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {m : ℕ} (filter : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter α m) (x : α), filter.mayContain x = Bool.true ↔ ∀ h ∈ filter.hashes, filter.bits[h x] = Bool.true
statement:
public theorem mayContain_iff {α : Type u} {m : Nat} (filter : BloomFilter α m) (x : α) :
    filter.mayContain x = true ↔ ∀ h ∈ filter.hashes, filter.bits[h x] = true

docstring:
No false negatives under further inserts: insertion never clears a bit, so an element reported
present stays reported present after any later insertion.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter.mayContain_insert_mono
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {m : ℕ} (filter : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter α m) (x y : α), filter.mayContain x = Bool.true → (filter.insert y).mayContain x = Bool.true

docstring: No false negatives: an element is reported present immediately after its own insertion.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter.mayContain_insert_self
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {m : ℕ} (filter : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BloomFilter α m) (x : α), (filter.insert x).mayContain x = Bool.true
statement:
public theorem mayContain_insert_self {α : Type u} {m : Nat} (filter : BloomFilter α m)
    (x : α) : (filter.insert x).mayContain x = true

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.build
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → List α → BinaryTree α
statement: public def build (xs : List α) : BinaryTree α

docstring:
Build a Cartesian tree with an explicit fuel bound: the recursion splits at
the minimum, so a fuel of at least the input length never runs out.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.buildFuel
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → ℕ → List α → BinaryTree α
statement: public def buildFuel : Nat → List α → BinaryTree α

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.buildFuel_cons
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (n : ℕ) (a : α) (as : List α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.buildFuel (n + 1) (a :: as) = BinaryTree.node (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.listMin a as) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.buildFuel n (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.splitAtFirst (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.listMin a as) (a :: as)).1) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.buildFuel n (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.splitAtFirst (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.listMin a as) (a :: as)).2)
statement:
public theorem buildFuel_cons (n : Nat) (a : α) (as : List α) :
    buildFuel (n + 1) (a :: as) =
      .node (listMin a as)
        (buildFuel n (splitAtFirst (listMin a as) (a :: as)).1)
        (buildFuel n (splitAtFirst (listMin a as) (a :: as)).2)

docstring: The Cartesian tree of a list is heap-ordered.

statement: public theorem heapOrdered_build (xs : List α) : HeapOrdered (build xs)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.heapOrdered_buildFuel
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (n : ℕ) (xs : List α), xs.length ≤ n → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.HeapOrdered (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.buildFuel n xs)
statement:
public theorem heapOrdered_buildFuel :
    ∀ (n : Nat) (xs : List α), xs.length ≤ n → HeapOrdered (buildFuel n xs)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.inorder_buildFuel

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.listMin

statement: public def listMin (a : α) : List α → α

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.listMin_le
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (a : α) (as : List α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.listMin a as ≤ a ∧ ∀ y ∈ as, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.listMin a as ≤ y

docstring:
Split a list at the first occurrence of `m`, dropping that occurrence.
Only equality on `α` is needed, so this helper and its specification are
generalized over `[DecidableEq α]` rather than the `[LinearOrder α]`
required to build Cartesian trees.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.splitAtFirst
signature: {α : Type u} → [DecidableEq α] → α → List α → List α × List α
statement: public def splitAtFirst (m : α) : List α → List α × List α

docstring:
Splitting at the *first* occurrence: the split value does not occur in
the left part. Together with the reconstruction equation in
`splitAtFirst_spec`, this characterizes the split point (including the
duplicate tie-breaking behavior used by `build`) without unfolding the
definition: reconstruction alone would hold for a split at any
occurrence.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.splitAtFirst_not_mem_fst
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq α] (m : α) (xs : List α), m ∈ xs → m ∉ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.splitAtFirst m xs).1
statement:
public theorem splitAtFirst_not_mem_fst (m : α) :
    ∀ (xs : List α), m ∈ xs → m ∉ (splitAtFirst m xs).1

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.splitAtFirst_spec
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq α] (m : α) (xs : List α), m ∈ xs → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.splitAtFirst m xs).1 ++ m :: (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.splitAtFirst m xs).2 = xs ∧ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.splitAtFirst m xs).1.length < xs.length ∧ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CartesianTree.splitAtFirst m xs).2.length < xs.length
statement:
public theorem splitAtFirst_spec (m : α) :
    ∀ (xs : List α), m ∈ xs →
      (splitAtFirst m xs).1 ++ m :: (splitAtFirst m xs).2 = xs ∧
        (splitAtFirst m xs).1.length < xs.length ∧
        (splitAtFirst m xs).2.length < xs.length

docstring:
A cuckoo hash table with two tables of `m` slots and hash functions `h1` and `h2`. No
expected constant-time bound is claimed because the model supplies neither a probability
distribution nor an independence assumption about the hashes.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing
signature: (K : Type u) → Type v → (m : ℕ) → (K → Fin m) → (K → Fin m) → Type (max u v)
statement:
public structure CuckooHashing (K : Type u) (V : Type v) (m : Nat)
    (h1 h2 : K → Fin m)

docstring: Each key is stored with at most one value (duplicate copies of a pair are allowed).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.KeyDet
signature: {K : Type u} → {V : Type v} → {m : ℕ} → {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2 → Prop
statement: public def KeyDet (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) : Prop

docstring: The binding `key ↦ value` is held in some slot of either table.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.Stored
signature: {K : Type u} → {V : Type v} → {m : ℕ} → {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2 → K → V → Prop
statement: public def Stored (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (key : K) (value : V) : Prop

docstring:
The placement invariant: an entry in the first table sits at `h1` of its key, and an entry
in the second table sits at `h2` of its key. This is what lets `lookup` check only two
slots.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.Valid
signature: {K : Type u} → {V : Type v} → {m : ℕ} → {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2 → Prop
statement: public def Valid (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) : Prop

docstring: The empty table, with every slot of both tables vacant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.empty
signature: {K : Type u} → {V : Type v} → {m : ℕ} → {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2
statement: public def empty : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2

docstring:
Inserts a binding or replaces the existing binding for the key. An existing binding in
either of the key's slots is overwritten in place; a replacement in the first table also
clears a duplicate copy of the key in its second slot, so no stale competing value
remains. Otherwise the eviction loop runs with the given fuel. Returns `none` when the
loop exhausts its fuel, which models the rehash trigger of the classical algorithm.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.insert
signature: {K : Type u} → {V : Type v} → {m : ℕ} → {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} → [DecidableEq K] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2 → K → V → ℕ → Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)
statement:
public def insert (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (key : K) (value : V) (fuel : Nat) :
    Option (CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)

docstring:
The eviction loop: place `cur` in the first table (if `first`) or the second table at its
hash slot, evicting any occupant to its other table in turn. Returns `none` when the fuel
runs out.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.insertAux
signature: {K : Type u} → {V : Type v} → {m : ℕ} → {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2 → K × V → Bool → ℕ → Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)
statement:
def insertAux (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (cur : K × V) (first : Bool) :
    Nat → Option (CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)

docstring: No key is stored with two values in the empty table, vacuously.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.keyDet_empty
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [DecidableEq K], Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.empty.KeyDet
statement: public theorem keyDet_empty : KeyDet (empty : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)

docstring:
A successful insertion or replacement preserves key determinism: replacement leaves no
stale copy of the key with a different value in the other slot.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.keyDet_insert
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [inst : DecidableEq K] (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (key : K) (value : V) (fuel : ℕ) (updated : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2), table.insert key value fuel = Option.some updated → table.Valid → table.KeyDet → updated.KeyDet
statement:
public theorem keyDet_insert (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (key : K) (value : V)
    (fuel : Nat) (updated : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)
    (inserted : insert table key value fuel = some updated)
    (valid : Valid table) (det : KeyDet table) :
    KeyDet updated

docstring: Looks up a key in its two possible slots: `table1[h1 key]` first, then `table2[h2 key]`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.lookup
signature: {K : Type u} → {V : Type v} → {m : ℕ} → {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} → [DecidableEq K] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2 → K → Option V
statement: public def lookup (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (key : K) : Option V

docstring: Looking up any key in the empty table returns `none`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.lookup_empty
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [inst : DecidableEq K] (key : K), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.empty.lookup key = Option.none
statement:
public theorem lookup_empty (key : K) :
    lookup (empty : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) key = none

docstring: Under `Valid` and `KeyDet`, lookup agrees exactly with `Stored`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.lookup_eq_some_iff_stored
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [inst : DecidableEq K] (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2), table.Valid → table.KeyDet → ∀ (key : K) (value : V), table.lookup key = Option.some value ↔ table.Stored key value

docstring: Under `Valid` and `KeyDet`, a stored binding is found by `lookup` with its value.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.lookup_eq_some_of_stored
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [inst : DecidableEq K] (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2), table.Valid → table.KeyDet → ∀ (key : K) (value : V), table.Stored key value → table.lookup key = Option.some value
statement:
public theorem lookup_eq_some_of_stored (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)
    (valid : Valid table) (det : KeyDet table) (key : K) (value : V)
    (stored : Stored table key value) :
    lookup table key = some value

docstring: A binding in the first table at its hash slot is found by `lookup` with its value.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.lookup_eq_some_of_table1
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [inst : DecidableEq K] (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (key : K) (value : V), table.table1.get (h1 key) = Option.some (key, value) → table.lookup key = Option.some value

docstring:
A binding in the second table at its hash slot is found by `lookup` with its value when
the first slot does not hold the key.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.lookup_eq_some_of_table2
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [inst : DecidableEq K] (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (key : K) (value : V), table.table2.get (h2 key) = Option.some (key, value) → (∀ (v₁ : V), table.table1.get (h1 key) ≠ Option.some (key, v₁)) → table.lookup key = Option.some value
statement:
public theorem lookup_eq_some_of_table2 (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (key : K)
    (value : V) (atSlot : table.table2.get (h2 key) = some (key, value))
    (notFirst : ∀ v₁, table.table1.get (h1 key) ≠ some (key, v₁)) :
    lookup table key = some value

docstring:
Looking up a successfully inserted key returns the inserted value, for tables satisfying
`Valid` and `KeyDet`. The inserted pair sits in one of the key's two slots in the result
(`stored_insert`), and the two invariants rule out a competing value in the other slot.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.lookup_insert
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [inst : DecidableEq K] (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2), table.Valid → table.KeyDet → ∀ (key : K) (value : V) (fuel : ℕ) (updated : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2), table.insert key value fuel = Option.some updated → updated.lookup key = Option.some value
statement:
public theorem lookup_insert (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (valid : Valid table)
    (det : KeyDet table) (key : K) (value : V) (fuel : Nat)
    (updated : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)
    (inserted : insert table key value fuel = some updated) :
    lookup updated key = some value

docstring:
A successful insertion or replacement does not change the lookup result for
any other key, the cuckoo analogue of `HashTable.lookup_insert_of_ne`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.lookup_insert_of_ne
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [inst : DecidableEq K] (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2), table.Valid → table.KeyDet → ∀ (key : K) (value : V) (fuel : ℕ) (updated : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2), table.insert key value fuel = Option.some updated → ∀ {other : K}, other ≠ key → updated.lookup other = table.lookup other
statement:
public theorem lookup_insert_of_ne (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)
    (valid : Valid table) (det : KeyDet table) (key : K) (value : V)
    (fuel : Nat) (updated : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)
    (inserted : insert table key value fuel = some updated)
    {other : K} (different : other ≠ key) :
    lookup updated other = lookup table other

docstring:
Lookup is complete under `Valid` in the weak sense: a stored key is found. The found value
may differ from the given one if the key is stored with two values; see
`lookup_eq_some_of_stored` for the value-exact form under `KeyDet`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.lookup_isSome_of_stored
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [inst : DecidableEq K] (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2), table.Valid → ∀ (key : K) (value : V), table.Stored key value → (table.lookup key).isSome = Bool.true

docstring: Lookup is sound: a found value is stored in one of the two tables.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.lookup_sound
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [inst : DecidableEq K] (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (key : K) (value : V), table.lookup key = Option.some value → table.Stored key value
statement:
public theorem lookup_sound (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (key : K) (value : V)
    (found : lookup table key = some value) : Stored table key value

docstring: Whether a slot holds a binding for `key`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.slotHasKey
signature: {K : Type u} → {V : Type v} → [DecidableEq K] → Option (K × V) → K → Bool
statement: def slotHasKey (slot : Option (K × V)) (key : K) : Bool

docstring: A successfully inserted binding is stored in the resulting table.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.stored_insert
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [inst : DecidableEq K] (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (key : K) (value : V) (fuel : ℕ) (updated : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2), table.insert key value fuel = Option.some updated → updated.Stored key value
statement:
public theorem stored_insert (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (key : K) (value : V)
    (fuel : Nat) (updated : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)
    (inserted : insert table key value fuel = some updated) :
    Stored updated key value

docstring:
A successful insertion or replacement preserves exactly the bindings of
every other key: for `other ≠ key`, a binding is stored after the operation
if and only if it was stored before. The forward direction covers both
replacement paths and the eviction loop; the backward direction rules out
new unrelated bindings.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.stored_insert_iff_of_ne
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [inst : DecidableEq K] (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2), table.Valid → ∀ (key : K) (value : V) (fuel : ℕ) (updated : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2), table.insert key value fuel = Option.some updated → ∀ {other : K} {otherValue : V}, other ≠ key → (updated.Stored other otherValue ↔ table.Stored other otherValue)
statement:
public theorem stored_insert_iff_of_ne (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)
    (valid : Valid table) (key : K) (value : V) (fuel : Nat)
    (updated : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)
    (inserted : insert table key value fuel = some updated)
    {other : K} {otherValue : V} (different : other ≠ key) :
    Stored updated other otherValue ↔ Stored table other otherValue

docstring: The empty table satisfies the placement invariant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.valid_empty
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [DecidableEq K], Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.empty.Valid
statement: public theorem valid_empty : Valid (empty : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)

docstring: A successful insertion or replacement preserves the placement invariant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing.valid_insert
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {m : ℕ} {h1 h2 : K → Fin m} [inst : DecidableEq K] (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (key : K) (value : V) (fuel : ℕ) (updated : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2), table.insert key value fuel = Option.some updated → table.Valid → updated.Valid
statement:
public theorem valid_insert (table : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2) (key : K) (value : V)
    (fuel : Nat) (updated : CuckooHashing K V m h1 h2)
    (inserted : insert table key value fuel = some updated) (valid : Valid table) :
    Valid updated

docstring: Every valid nonroot node is no smaller than its immediate `d`-ary parent.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryHeapOrdered
signature: {α : Type u} → [LE α] → ℕ → Array α → Prop
statement: structure DaryHeapOrdered {α : Type u} [LE α] (d : Nat) (a : Array α) : Prop

docstring: Local heap order implies that the root is no greater than any valid entry.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryHeapOrdered.root_le
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {d : ℕ}, 2 ≤ d → ∀ {a : Array α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryHeapOrdered d a → ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < a.size), a[0] ≤ a[i]
statement:
theorem DaryHeapOrdered.root_le {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    {d : Nat} (hd : 2 ≤ d) {a : Array α} (h : DaryHeapOrdered d a)
    (i : Nat) (hi : i < a.size) : a[0]'(by omega) ≤ a[i]

docstring: A configurable-arity min-heap with a contiguous level-order representation.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap
signature: (α : Type u) → [LinearOrder α] → Type u
statement: structure DaryMinHeap (α : Type u) [LinearOrder α]

docstring: Building from a list uses the normalized requested arity.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.arity_ofList
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (requestedArity : ℕ) (xs : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.ofList requestedArity xs).arity = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.normalizedArity requestedArity
statement:
theorem DaryMinHeap.arity_ofList {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    (requestedArity : Nat) (xs : List α) :
    (DaryMinHeap.ofList requestedArity xs).arity = normalizedArity requestedArity

docstring: The backing array stores exactly one entry per represented occurrence.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.card_elements
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (h : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α), h.elements.card = h.data.size
statement:
theorem DaryMinHeap.card_elements {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    (h : DaryMinHeap α) : h.elements.card = h.data.size

docstring: Insertion preserves every different value's multiplicity.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.count_push_of_ne
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (h : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α) {x y : α}, y ≠ x → Multiset.count y (h.push x).elements = Multiset.count y h.elements
statement:
theorem DaryMinHeap.count_push_of_ne {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    (h : DaryMinHeap α) {x y : α} (hyx : y ≠ x) :
    Multiset.count y (h.push x).elements = Multiset.count y h.elements

docstring: Inserting a value raises its multiplicity by one.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.count_push_self
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (h : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α) (x : α), Multiset.count x (h.push x).elements = Multiset.count x h.elements + 1
statement:
theorem DaryMinHeap.count_push_self {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    (h : DaryMinHeap α) (x : α) :
    Multiset.count x (h.push x).elements = Multiset.count x h.elements + 1

docstring: The multiset represented by a heap.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.elements
signature: {α : Type u} → [inst : LinearOrder α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α → Multiset α
statement:
def DaryMinHeap.elements {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    (h : DaryMinHeap α) : Multiset α

docstring: Building from a list preserves every occurrence.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.elements_ofList
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (requestedArity : ℕ) (xs : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.ofList requestedArity xs).elements = ↑xs
statement:
theorem DaryMinHeap.elements_ofList {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    (requestedArity : Nat) (xs : List α) :
    (DaryMinHeap.ofList requestedArity xs).elements = (↑xs : Multiset α)

docstring: Insertion adds exactly one multiset occurrence.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.elements_push
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (h : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α) (x : α), (h.push x).elements = x ::ₘ h.elements
statement:
theorem DaryMinHeap.elements_push {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    (h : DaryMinHeap α) (x : α) :
    (h.push x).elements = x ::ₘ h.elements

docstring: The empty heap, normalizing a requested arity below two to two.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.empty
signature: {α : Type u} → [inst : LinearOrder α] → ℕ → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α
statement:
def DaryMinHeap.empty {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    (requestedArity : Nat) : DaryMinHeap α

docstring:
Remove and return the minimum. The last entry moves to the root and
sifts down, so extraction follows one `d`-ary child path.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.extractMin
signature: {α : Type u} → [inst : LinearOrder α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α → Option (α × Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α)
statement:
def DaryMinHeap.extractMin {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    (h : DaryMinHeap α) : Option (α × DaryMinHeap α)

docstring: A successful extraction preserves the heap arity.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.extractMin_arity
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {h : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α} {x : α} {rest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α}, h.extractMin = Option.some (x, rest) → rest.arity = h.arity

docstring: A successful extraction partitions the represented multiset exactly.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.extractMin_cons_elements
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {h : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α} {x : α} {rest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α}, h.extractMin = Option.some (x, rest) → x ::ₘ rest.elements = h.elements
statement:
theorem DaryMinHeap.extractMin_cons_elements {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    {h : DaryMinHeap α} {x : α} {rest : DaryMinHeap α}
    (hx : h.extractMin = some (x, rest)) :
    x ::ₘ rest.elements = h.elements

docstring: Successful extraction decreases the result's multiplicity by one.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.extractMin_count
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {h : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α} {x : α} {rest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α}, h.extractMin = Option.some (x, rest) → Multiset.count x rest.elements = Multiset.count x h.elements - 1
statement:
theorem DaryMinHeap.extractMin_count {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    {h : DaryMinHeap α} {x : α} {rest : DaryMinHeap α}
    (hx : h.extractMin = some (x, rest)) :
    Multiset.count x rest.elements = Multiset.count x h.elements - 1

docstring: A successful extraction erases exactly one occurrence of its result.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.extractMin_elements
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {h : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α} {x : α} {rest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α}, h.extractMin = Option.some (x, rest) → rest.elements = h.elements.erase x
statement:
theorem DaryMinHeap.extractMin_elements {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    {h : DaryMinHeap α} {x : α} {rest : DaryMinHeap α}
    (hx : h.extractMin = some (x, rest)) :
    rest.elements = h.elements.erase x

docstring: Extraction fails exactly for the empty representation.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.extractMin_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (h : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α), h.extractMin = Option.none ↔ h.data.size = 0
statement:
theorem DaryMinHeap.extractMin_eq_none_iff {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    (h : DaryMinHeap α) : h.extractMin = none ↔ h.data.size = 0

docstring: A successful extraction returns a globally minimal stored value.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.extractMin_le
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {h : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α} {x y : α} {rest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α}, h.extractMin = Option.some (x, rest) → y ∈ h.elements → x ≤ y

docstring: A successful extraction returns a stored value.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.extractMin_mem
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {h : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α} {x : α} {rest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α}, h.extractMin = Option.some (x, rest) → x ∈ h.elements

docstring: Every returned heap satisfies its local heap-order invariant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap.extractMin_ordered
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {h : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α} {x : α} {rest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryMinHeap α}, h.extractMin = Option.some (x, rest) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DaryHeapOrdered rest.arity rest.data
statement:
theorem DaryMinHeap.extractMin_ordered {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    {h : DaryMinHeap α} {x : α} {rest : DaryMinHeap α}
    (_hx : h.extractMin = some (x, rest)) :
    DaryHeapOrdered rest.arity rest.data

docstring:

docstring: The pointwise store update, applying the predecessor write before the successor write.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.listDelete_get
statement:
public theorem listDelete_get {α : Type u} {capacity : Nat}
    (store : Vector (Option (Node α (Fin capacity))) capacity)
    (head : Option (Fin capacity)) (x : Fin capacity)
    (hx : (store.get x).isSome)
    (hp : ∀ p, ((store.get x).get hx).prev = some p → (store.get p).isSome)
    (hn : ∀ n, ((store.get x).get hx).next = some n → (store.get n).isSome)
    (z : Fin capacity) :
    (listDelete store head x hx hp hn).ret.1.get z =
      let originalX := (store.get x).get hx
      let carried := if originalX.prev = some z then
        (store.get z).map fun node => { node with next := originalX.next } else store.get z
      if originalX.next = some z then
        carried.map fun node => { node with prev := originalX.prev } else carried

docstring: The header changes to the original successor exactly when the predecessor is NIL.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.listDelete_head

statement:
public theorem listDelete_head {α : Type u} {capacity : Nat}
    (store : Vector (Option (Node α (Fin capacity))) capacity)
    (head : Option (Fin capacity)) (x : Fin capacity)
    (hx : (store.get x).isSome)

    (hn : ∀ n, ((store.get x).get hx).next = some n → (store.get n).isSome) :
    (listDelete store head x hx hp hn).ret.2 =
      if ((store.get x).get hx).prev.isSome then head else ((store.get x).get hx).next
