docstring: The complete returned store and header, with the successor read from the carried store.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.listDelete_ret
signature:
∀ {α : Type u} {capacity : ℕ} (store : Vector (Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.Node α (Fin capacity))) capacity) (head : Option (Fin capacity)) (x : Fin capacity) (hx : (store.get x).isSome = Bool.true) (hp : ∀ (p : Fin capacity), ((store.get x).get hx).prev = Option.some p → (store.get p).isSome = Bool.true) (hn : ∀ (n : Fin capacity), ((store.get x).get hx).next = Option.some n → (store.get n).isSome = Bool.true),
  have originalX := (store.get x).get hx;
  have carried :=
    match originalX.prev with
    | Option.none => store
    | Option.some p => store.set (↑p) (Option.map (fun node ↦ { payload := node.payload, next := originalX.next, prev := node.prev }) (store.get p)) ⋯;
  (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.listDelete store head x hx hp hn).ret =
    (match originalX.next with
      | Option.none => carried
      | Option.some n => carried.set (↑n) (Option.map (fun node ↦ { payload := node.payload, next := node.next, prev := originalX.prev }) (carried.get n)) ⋯,
      if originalX.prev.isSome = Bool.true then head else originalX.next)

docstring: The whole-store characteristic reduced at one index, preserving all aliases.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.listInsert_get
statement:
public theorem listInsert_get {α : Type u} {n : Nat}
    (store : Vector (Option (Node α (Fin n))) n) (x y z : Fin n)
    (hx : (store.get x).isSome) (hy : (store.get y).isSome)
    (hs : ∀ w, ((store.get y).get hy).next = some w → (store.get w).isSome) :
    let first := if x = z then some { (store.get x).get hx with
      next := ((store.get y).get hy).next, prev := some y } else store.get z
    let second := if ((store.get y).get hy).next = some z then
      first.map (fun (node : Node α (Fin n)) => { node with prev := some x }) else first
    (listInsert store x y hx hy hs).ret.get z =
      if y = z then second.map (fun (node : Node α (Fin n)) =>
        { node with next := some x }) else second

docstring: Complete source update, including an aliased supplied node and old head.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.listPrepend_ret
signature:
∀ {α : Type u} {capacity : ℕ} (store : Vector (Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.Node α (Fin capacity))) capacity) (head : Option (Fin capacity)) (x : Fin capacity) (hx : (store.get x).isSome = Bool.true) (hh : ∀ (h : Fin capacity), head = Option.some h → (store.get h).isSome = Bool.true),
  have updated :=
    store.set (↑x)
      (Option.some
        (have __src := (store.get x).get hx;
        { payload := __src.payload, next := head, prev := Option.none }))
      ⋯;
  (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.listPrepend store head x hx hh).ret =
    (match head, hh with
      | Option.none, hh => updated
      | Option.some h, hh => updated.set (↑h) (Option.map (fun node ↦ { payload := node.payload, next := node.next, prev := Option.some x }) (updated.get h)) ⋯,
      Option.some x)
statement:
public theorem listPrepend_ret {α : Type u} {capacity : Nat}
    (store : Vector (Option (Node α (Fin capacity))) capacity)
    (head : Option (Fin capacity)) (x : Fin capacity)
    (hx : (store.get x).isSome)
    (hh : ∀ h, head = some h → (store.get h).isSome) :
    let updated := store.set x.val
      (some { (store.get x).get hx with next := head, prev := none }) x.isLt
    (listPrepend store head x hx hh).ret =
      (match head with
       | none => updated
       | some h => updated.set h.val
           ((updated.get h).map fun node => { node with prev := some x }) h.isLt,
       some x)

docstring:
The complete returned pool differs only in the sentinel key; all other cells and
all next/prev links and satellite payloads are unchanged.

docstring:
The returned identity is the first pre-run data-node key match in circle order.
The sentinel is a stopping device, never a successful returned data identity.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.listSearchSentinel_ret
signature: ∀ {Key : Type u} {Satellite : Type v} {capacity : ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq Key] (store : Vector (Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.Node (Key × Satellite) (Fin capacity))) capacity) (s : Fin capacity) (key : Key) (ids : List (Fin capacity)) (rep : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.CircularRepresents store s ids), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.listSearchSentinel store s key ⋯).ret.2 = List.find? (fun x ↦ Decidable.decide (Option.map (fun node ↦ node.payload.1) (store.get x) = Option.some key)) ids
statement:
public theorem listSearchSentinel_ret {Key : Type u} {Satellite : Type v} {capacity : Nat}

    (rep : CircularRepresents store s ids) :
    (listSearchSentinel store s key ⟨ids, rep⟩).ret.2 =
      ids.find? (fun x => decide
        ((store.get x).map (fun node => node.payload.1) = some key))

docstring:

four fixed events. An absent query scans the complete data circle.

(fun x ↦ Decidable.decide (Option.map (fun node ↦ node.payload.1) (store.get x) = Option.some key)) ids).getD ids.length + 4
statement:

docstring: Every returned cell follows the predecessor write and then the carried successor write.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.sentinelDelete_get
statement:
public theorem sentinelDelete_get (z : Fin capacity) :
    (sentinelDelete store x hx hp hn hprev hnext).ret.get z =
      let nx := (store.get x).get hx
      let carried := if nx.prev = some z then
        (store.get z).map fun node => { node with next := nx.next } else store.get z
      if nx.next = some z then
        carried.map fun node => { node with prev := nx.prev } else carried

docstring: The two carried record updates determine the complete returned store.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.sentinelDelete_ret
statement:
public theorem sentinelDelete_ret {α : Type u} {capacity : Nat}
    (store : Vector (Option (Node α (Fin capacity))) capacity) (x : Fin capacity)
    (hx : (store.get x).isSome)
    (hp : ((store.get x).get hx).prev.isSome)
    (hn : ((store.get x).get hx).next.isSome)
    (hprev : ∀ p, ((store.get x).get hx).prev = some p → (store.get p).isSome)
    (hnext : ∀ n, ((store.get x).get hx).next = some n → (store.get n).isSome) :
    let nx := (store.get x).get hx
    let p := nx.prev.get hp
    let n := nx.next.get hn
    let carried := store.set p.val
      ((store.get p).map fun node => { node with next := nx.next }) p.isLt
    (sentinelDelete store x hx hp hn hprev hnext).ret =
      carried.set n.val ((carried.get n).map fun node => { node with prev := nx.prev }) n.isLt

docstring: The source-ordered update at every cell, including aliased write targets.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.sentinelInsert_get
statement:
public theorem sentinelInsert_get {α : Type u} {n : Nat}
    (store : Vector (Option (Node α (Fin n))) n) (x y z : Fin n)
    (hx : (store.get x).isSome) (hy : (store.get y).isSome)
    (hn : ((store.get y).get hy).next.isSome)
    (hs : ∀ w, ((store.get y).get hy).next = some w → (store.get w).isSome) :
    let first := if x = z then some { (store.get x).get hx with
      next := ((store.get y).get hy).next, prev := some y } else store.get z
    let second := if ((store.get y).get hy).next = some z then
      first.map (fun (node : Node α (Fin n)) => { node with prev := some x }) else first
    (sentinelInsert store x y hx hy hn hs).ret.get z =
      if y = z then second.map (fun (node : Node α (Fin n)) =>
        { node with next := some x }) else second

docstring: Every payload, including keys and satellite data, is preserved.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.sentinelInsert_payload
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {n : ℕ} (store : Vector (Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.Node α (Fin n))) n) (x y z : Fin n) (hx : (store.get x).isSome = Bool.true) (hy : (store.get y).isSome = Bool.true) (hn : ((store.get y).get hy).next.isSome = Bool.true) (hs : ∀ (w : Fin n), ((store.get y).get hy).next = Option.some w → (store.get w).isSome = Bool.true), Option.map Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.Node.payload ((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.sentinelInsert store x y hx hy hn hs).ret.get z) = Option.map Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.Node.payload (store.get z)

    (hs : ∀ w, ((store.get y).get hy).next = some w → (store.get w).isSome) :

      (store.get z).map Node.payload

docstring: Complete carried-store characteristic, without freshness.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DoublyLinkedList.sentinelInsert_ret
statement:
public theorem sentinelInsert_ret {α : Type u} {n : Nat}
    (store : Vector (Option (Node α (Fin n))) n) (x y : Fin n)
    (hx : (store.get x).isSome) (hy : (store.get y).isSome)
    (hn : ((store.get y).get hy).next.isSome)
    (hs : ∀ z, ((store.get y).get hy).next = some z → (store.get z).isSome) :
    let updated := store.set x.val (some { (store.get x).get hx with
      next := ((store.get y).get hy).next, prev := some y }) x.isLt
    let z := ((store.get y).get hy).next.get hn
    let backlinked := updated.set z.val
      ((updated.get z).map fun (node : Node α (Fin n)) =>
        { node with prev := some x }) z.isLt
    (sentinelInsert store x y hx hy hn hs).ret = backlinked.set y.val
      ((backlinked.get y).map fun (node : Node α (Fin n)) =>
        { node with next := some x }) y.isLt

docstring:
After deleting from a nonempty well-formed table, the slots are the
retained occupied prefix followed by empty slots.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableDelete_slots
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (T : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.Table α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.WellFormed T → T.num ≠ 0 → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableDelete T).slots = T.slots.extract 0 (T.num - 1) ++ Array.replicate ((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableDelete T).slots.size - (T.num - 1)) Option.none
statement:
public theorem tableDelete_slots {α : Type u} (T : Table α) (hT : WellFormed T)

    (tableDelete T).slots =
      T.slots.extract 0 (T.num - 1) ++
        Array.replicate ((tableDelete T).slots.size - (T.num - 1)) none

signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (xs : Array α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsertMany Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.empty xs).ret.slots.size ≤ 2 * xs.size
statement:
public theorem tableInsertMany_size_le {α : Type u} (xs : Array α) :
    (tableInsertMany empty xs).ret.slots.size ≤ 2 * xs.size

docstring: From empty, the actual total copied-item and insertion writes are at most three per item.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsertMany_time_le
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (xs : Array α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsertMany Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.empty xs).time ≤ 3 * xs.size
statement:
public theorem tableInsertMany_time_le {α : Type u} (xs : Array α) :
    (tableInsertMany empty xs).time ≤ 3 * xs.size

docstring: The first allocation has charge two, giving a strict bound for every nonempty input.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsertMany_time_lt
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (xs : Array α), xs.size > 0 → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsertMany Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.empty xs).time < 3 * xs.size
statement:
public theorem tableInsertMany_time_lt {α : Type u} (xs : Array α) :
    xs.size > 0 → (tableInsertMany empty xs).time < 3 * xs.size

docstring: The canonical insertion fold preserves compact-prefix occupancy.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsertMany_wellFormed
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (T : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.Table α) (xs : Array α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.WellFormed T → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.WellFormed (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsertMany T xs).ret
statement:
public theorem tableInsertMany_wellFormed {α : Type u} (T : Table α) (xs : Array α) :
    WellFormed T → WellFormed (tableInsertMany T xs).ret

docstring: The signed source potential bounds the amortized copy/write charge by three.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert_amortized
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (T : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.Table α) (x : α), ↑(Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert T x).time + (2 * ↑(Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert T x).ret.num - ↑(Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert T x).ret.slots.size) - (2 * ↑T.num - ↑T.slots.size) ≤ 3
statement:
public theorem tableInsert_amortized {α : Type u} (T : Table α) (x : α) :
    ((tableInsert T x).time : Int) +
      (2 * ((tableInsert T x).ret.num : Int) - ((tableInsert T x).ret.slots.size : Int)) -
      (2 * (T.num : Int) - (T.slots.size : Int)) ≤ 3

docstring: The actual inserted payload is appended to the saved logical contents.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert_contents
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (T : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.Table α) (x : α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.WellFormed T → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.contents (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert T x).ret = (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.contents T).push x
statement:
public theorem tableInsert_contents {α : Type u} (T : Table α) (x : α) :
    WellFormed T → contents (tableInsert T x).ret = (contents T).push x

docstring: The actual insertion increases the saved item count by one.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert_num
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (T : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.Table α) (x : α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert T x).ret.num = T.num + 1
statement:
public theorem tableInsert_num {α : Type u} (T : Table α) (x : α) :
    (tableInsert T x).ret.num = T.num + 1

docstring: The actual first allocation and full-table doubling determine the returned capacity.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert_size
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (T : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.Table α) (x : α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert T x).ret.slots.size = if T.slots.size = 0 then 1 else if T.num = T.slots.size then 2 * T.slots.size else T.slots.size
statement:
public theorem tableInsert_size {α : Type u} (T : Table α) (x : α) :
    (tableInsert T x).ret.slots.size =
      if T.slots.size = 0 then 1
      else if T.num = T.slots.size then 2 * T.slots.size else T.slots.size

docstring: Preserve the complete occupied prefix and all unused returned slots.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert_slots
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (T : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.Table α) (x : α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.WellFormed T → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert T x).ret.slots = T.slots.extract 0 T.num ++ #[Option.some x] ++ Array.replicate ((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert T x).ret.slots.size - (T.num + 1)) Option.none
statement:
public theorem tableInsert_slots {α : Type u} (T : Table α) (x : α) :
    WellFormed T → (tableInsert T x).ret.slots =
      T.slots.extract 0 T.num ++ #[some x] ++
        Array.replicate ((tableInsert T x).ret.slots.size - (T.num + 1)) none

docstring: Count the new payload write and exactly the old-item writes on a full resize.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert_time
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (T : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.Table α) (x : α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert T x).time = 1 + if T.slots.size > 0 ∧ T.num = T.slots.size then T.num else 0

docstring: Insertion preserves exact compact-prefix occupancy for arbitrary payload types.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert_wellFormed
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (T : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.Table α) (x : α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.WellFormed T → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.WellFormed (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.tableInsert T x).ret
statement:
public theorem tableInsert_wellFormed {α : Type u} (T : Table α) (x : α) :
    WellFormed T → WellFormed (tableInsert T x).ret

docstring: Well-formedness means exactly that the compact logical prefix is occupied.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.wellFormed_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (T : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.Table α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.DynamicTable.WellFormed T ↔ ∀ (i : ℕ) (h : i < T.slots.size), T.slots[i].isSome = Bool.true ↔ i < T.num

docstring: A rooted ordered tree: a root vertex with an ordered list of child subtrees.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree
signature: Type u → Type u
statement: inductive Tree (V : Type u)

docstring:
Forest validity: every vertex occurs at most once in the tree. Raw
`Tree`s may repeat vertex labels; the dynamic-forest interpretation of
`link` requires `Valid` inputs with disjoint vertex sets.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.Valid
signature: {V : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → Prop
statement: def Valid (t : Tree V) : Prop

docstring:
The arc sequence of the Euler tour: consecutive vertex pairs. Each tree edge
occurs once in each direction.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.arcTour
signature: {V : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → List (V × V)
statement: def arcTour (t : Tree V) : List (V × V)

docstring: `arcTour` computed from the single shared tour list.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.arcTour_eq_zip
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), t.arcTour = t.tour.zip t.tour.tail
statement:
theorem arcTour_eq_zip (t : Tree V) :
    arcTour t = (tour t).zip (tour t).tail

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.arcTour_length
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), t.arcTour.length = 2 * (t.size - 1)
statement: theorem arcTour_length (t : Tree V) : (arcTour t).length = 2 * (size t - 1)

docstring: The child subtrees of the root, in order.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.children
signature: {V : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)
statement: def children : Tree V → List (Tree V)

docstring:
Induction on a tree from the statement for every child subtree. The built-in
`induction` tactic does not support the nested recursion through `List`, so this
principle is derived from `Tree.rec` and used with `induction … using`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.children_ind
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} {motive : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → Prop}, (∀ (r : V) (cs : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)), (∀ c ∈ cs, motive c) → motive (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.node r cs)) → ∀ (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), motive t
statement:
theorem children_ind {motive : Tree V → Prop}
    (node : ∀ (r : V) (cs : List (Tree V)), (∀ c ∈ cs, motive c) →
      motive (.node r cs))
    (t : Tree V) : motive t

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.children_node
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (r : V) (cs : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.node r cs).children = cs
statement:
theorem children_node (r : V) (cs : List (Tree V)) :
    children (.node r cs) = cs

docstring:
Removes the last child subtree of the root, returning the remaining tree and the
removed subtree, or `none` when the root has no children.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.cutLast
signature: {V : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V × Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)
statement: def cutLast : Tree V → Option (Tree V × Tree V)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.cutLast_link
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t₁ t₂ : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), (t₁.link t₂).cutLast = Option.some (t₁, t₂)
statement: theorem cutLast_link (t₁ t₂ : Tree V) : cutLast (link t₁ t₂) = some (t₁, t₂)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.exists_cons_tour
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), ∃ l, t.tour = t.root :: l
statement: theorem exists_cons_tour (t : Tree V) : ∃ l, tour t = t.root :: l

docstring: Records `t₂` as a new last child subtree of the root of `t₁`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.link
signature: {V : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V
statement: def link : Tree V → Tree V → Tree V

docstring: A vertex occurs in the Euler tour exactly when it is a vertex of the tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.mem_tour_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V) (v : V), v ∈ t.tour ↔ v ∈ t.vertices
statement: theorem mem_tour_iff (t : Tree V) (v : V) : v ∈ tour t ↔ v ∈ vertices t

docstring:
Without disjointness, `link` need not be valid: linking two singleton
trees with the same root duplicates that vertex.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.not_valid_link_same_root
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (r : V), ¬((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.node r []).link (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.node r [])).Valid
statement:
theorem not_valid_link_same_root (r : V) :
    ¬ Valid (link (.node r []) (.node r []))

docstring: The root vertex of a tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.root
signature: {V : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → V
statement: def root : Tree V → V

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.root_link
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t₁ t₂ : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), (t₁.link t₂).root = t₁.root
statement: theorem root_link (t₁ t₂ : Tree V) : (link t₁ t₂).root = t₁.root

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.root_mem_tour
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), t.root ∈ t.tour
statement: theorem root_mem_tour (t : Tree V) : t.root ∈ tour t

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.root_node
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (r : V) (cs : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.node r cs).root = r
statement: theorem root_node (r : V) (cs : List (Tree V)) : root (.node r cs) = r

docstring: The number of vertices of a tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.size
signature: {V : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → ℕ
statement: def size : Tree V → Nat

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.size_link
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t₁ t₂ : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), (t₁.link t₂).size = t₁.size + t₂.size
statement: theorem size_link (t₁ t₂ : Tree V) : size (link t₁ t₂) = size t₁ + size t₂

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.size_pos
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), 0 < t.size
statement: theorem size_pos (t : Tree V) : 0 < size t

docstring:
The splice of two tours at the root `r` of the first tree: walk the first tour,
then the second tree's tour, then return to `r`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.spliceLink
signature: {V : Type u} → List V → List V → V → List V
statement: def spliceLink (tour₁ tour₂ : List V) (r : V) : List V

docstring:
The Euler tour of a tree: the vertex sequence of the depth-first walk that
returns to the parent vertex after each child subtree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.tour
signature: {V : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → List V
statement: def tour (t : Tree V) : List V

docstring:
Accumulator Euler tour: `tourAux t acc = tour t ++ acc` (see
`tourAux_eq`), so `tour` is linear rather than repeatedly appending child
tours.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.tourAux
signature: {V : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → List V → List V
statement: def tourAux : Tree V → List V → List V

docstring: The accumulator tour appends the tour onto its accumulator.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.tourAux_eq
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V) (acc : List V), t.tourAux acc = t.tour ++ acc
statement:
theorem tourAux_eq (t : Tree V) (acc : List V) :
    tourAux t acc = tour t ++ acc

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.tour_infix_link
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t₁ t₂ : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), ∃ pre post, (t₁.link t₂).tour = pre ++ t₂.tour ++ post
statement:
theorem tour_infix_link (t₁ t₂ : Tree V) :
    ∃ pre post, tour (link t₁ t₂) = pre ++ tour t₂ ++ post

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.tour_length
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), t.tour.length = 2 * t.size - 1
statement: theorem tour_length (t : Tree V) : (tour t).length = 2 * size t - 1

docstring:
The tour of a linked tree is the splice of the two tours: the first tour is a
prefix, and the second tour is inserted whole before the final return to the root.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.tour_link
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t₁ t₂ : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), (t₁.link t₂).tour = t₁.tour ++ (t₂.tour ++ [t₁.root])
statement:
theorem tour_link (t₁ t₂ : Tree V) :
    tour (link t₁ t₂) = tour t₁ ++ (tour t₂ ++ [t₁.root])

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.tour_link_splice
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t₁ t₂ : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), (t₁.link t₂).tour = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.spliceLink t₁.tour t₂.tour t₁.root
statement:
theorem tour_link_splice (t₁ t₂ : Tree V) :
    tour (link t₁ t₂) = spliceLink (tour t₁) (tour t₂) t₁.root

docstring: Characteristic node equation for `tour` (the former definition).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.tour_node
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (r : V) (cs : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.node r cs).tour = r :: List.flatMap (fun c ↦ c.tour ++ [r]) cs
statement:
theorem tour_node (r : V) (cs : List (Tree V)) :
    tour (.node r cs) = r :: cs.flatMap (fun c => tour c ++ [r])

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.tour_prefix_link
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t₁ t₂ : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), ∃ rest, (t₁.link t₂).tour = t₁.tour ++ rest
statement:
theorem tour_prefix_link (t₁ t₂ : Tree V) :
    ∃ rest, tour (link t₁ t₂) = tour t₁ ++ rest

docstring: Validity is exactly duplicate-freeness of the preorder vertex list.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.valid_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), t.Valid ↔ t.vertices.Nodup
statement: theorem valid_iff (t : Tree V) : Valid t ↔ (vertices t).Nodup

docstring:
Linking two valid trees with disjoint vertex sets stays valid: the
forest precondition for reading `link` as a dynamic-forest link.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.valid_link
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} {t₁ t₂ : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, t₁.Valid → t₂.Valid → t₁.vertices.Disjoint t₂.vertices → (t₁.link t₂).Valid
statement:
theorem valid_link {t₁ t₂ : Tree V} (h₁ : Valid t₁) (h₂ : Valid t₂)
    (hd : List.Disjoint (vertices t₁) (vertices t₂)) :
    Valid (link t₁ t₂)

docstring: A single-vertex tree is valid.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.valid_singleton
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (r : V), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.node r []).Valid
statement: theorem valid_singleton (r : V) : Valid (.node r [])

docstring: The vertices of a tree in preorder.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.vertices
signature: {V : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → List V
statement: def vertices (t : Tree V) : List V

docstring:
Accumulator preorder traversal: `verticesAux t acc = vertices t ++ acc`
(see `verticesAux_eq`), so `vertices` is linear rather than repeatedly
appending child lists.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.verticesAux
signature: {V : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → List V → List V
statement: def verticesAux : Tree V → List V → List V

docstring: The accumulator traversal appends the preorder list onto its accumulator.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.verticesAux_eq
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V) (acc : List V), t.verticesAux acc = t.vertices ++ acc
statement:
theorem verticesAux_eq (t : Tree V) (acc : List V) :
    verticesAux t acc = vertices t ++ acc

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.vertices_length
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), t.vertices.length = t.size
statement: theorem vertices_length (t : Tree V) : (vertices t).length = size t

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.vertices_link
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (t₁ t₂ : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), (t₁.link t₂).vertices = t₁.vertices ++ t₂.vertices
statement:
theorem vertices_link (t₁ t₂ : Tree V) :
    vertices (link t₁ t₂) = vertices t₁ ++ vertices t₂

docstring: Characteristic node equation for `vertices` (the former definition).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.vertices_node
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (r : V) (cs : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.node r cs).vertices = r :: List.flatMap Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.vertices cs
statement:
theorem vertices_node (r : V) (cs : List (Tree V)) :
    vertices (.node r cs) = r :: cs.flatMap vertices

docstring: Compute the largest feasible sum by scanning the sole traversal's actual result.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum
signature: List ℕ → ℕ → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ ℕ
statement: public def exactSubsetSum (xs : List Nat) (target : Nat) : TimeM Nat Nat

docstring: The sole saved-list exact-subset-sum traversal, returning all distinct feasible sums.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSumSums
signature: List ℕ → ℕ → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (List ℕ)
statement:
public def exactSubsetSumSums (xs : List Nat) (target : Nat) :
    TimeM Nat (List Nat)

docstring: The distinct computed sums are bounded by the number of positional sublists.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSumSums_length_le_pow

signature: ∀ (xs : List ℕ) (target : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSumSums xs target).ret.length ≤ target + 1

docstring: The returned value is optimal for positional Nat inputs, including zero and repeated values.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum_optimal
signature: ∀ (xs : List ℕ) (target : ℕ), (∃ ys, ys.Sublist xs ∧ ys.sum = (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum xs target).ret) ∧ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum xs target).ret ≤ target ∧ ∀ (ys : List ℕ), ys.Sublist xs → ys.sum ≤ target → ys.sum ≤ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum xs target).ret
statement:
public theorem exactSubsetSum_optimal (xs : List Nat) (target : Nat) :
    (∃ ys : List Nat, ys.Sublist xs ∧ ys.sum = (exactSubsetSum xs target).ret) ∧
      (exactSubsetSum xs target).ret ≤ target ∧
      ∀ ys : List Nat, ys.Sublist xs → ys.sum ≤ target →
        ys.sum ≤ (exactSubsetSum xs target).ret

docstring:
CLRS's optimum corollary, retaining its distinct positive-set and positive-target premises.
The positional Nat generalization is `exactSubsetSum_optimal`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum_optimal_of_positive
signature: ∀ (xs : List ℕ) (target : ℕ), xs.Nodup → (∀ x ∈ xs, 0 < x) → 0 < target → (∃ ys, ys.Sublist xs ∧ ys.sum = (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum xs target).ret) ∧ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum xs target).ret ≤ target ∧ ∀ (ys : List ℕ), ys.Sublist xs → ys.sum ≤ target → ys.sum ≤ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum xs target).ret
statement:
public theorem exactSubsetSum_optimal_of_positive (xs : List Nat) (target : Nat)
    (_hd : xs.Nodup) (_hp : ∀ x ∈ xs, 0 < x) (_ht : 0 < target) :
    (∃ ys : List Nat, ys.Sublist xs ∧ ys.sum = (exactSubsetSum xs target).ret) ∧
      (exactSubsetSum xs target).ret ≤ target ∧
      ∀ ys : List Nat, ys.Sublist xs → ys.sum ≤ target →
        ys.sum ≤ (exactSubsetSum xs target).ret

docstring: The returned maximum scans exactly the actual saved-list traversal's result.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum_ret
signature: ∀ (xs : List ℕ) (target : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum xs target).ret = List.foldl Max.max 0 (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSumSums xs target).ret

docstring: Exact selected-event cost, with every phase reading the actual public prefix result.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum_time
signature:
∀ (xs : List ℕ) (target : ℕ),
  (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum xs target).time =
    1 + xs.length +
        (List.map
            (fun i ↦
              have saved := (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSumSums (List.take i xs) target).ret;
              have merged := Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.merge saved (List.map (fun z ↦ z + xs.getD i 0) saved);
              saved.length + merged.time + (merged.ret.length - 1) + (List.destutter (fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 ≠ x2) merged.ret).length)
            (List.range xs.length)).sum +
      (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSumSums xs target).ret.length
statement:
public theorem exactSubsetSum_time (xs : List Nat) (target : Nat) :
    (exactSubsetSum xs target).time = 1 + xs.length +
      ((List.range xs.length).map fun i =>
        let saved := (exactSubsetSumSums (xs.take i) target).ret
        let merged := TimeM.merge saved (saved.map (fun z => z + xs.getD i 0))
        saved.length + merged.time + (merged.ret.length - 1) +
          (merged.ret.destutter (· ≠ ·)).length).sum +
      (exactSubsetSumSums xs target).ret.length

docstring: The actual shifted additions alone establish exponential growth on powers-of-two inputs.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum_time_ge_powers_of_two
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ^ n - 1 ≤ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum (List.map (fun j ↦ 2 ^ j) (List.range n)) (2 ^ n - 1)).time

docstring: Exponential upper bound on the actual selected-event count, including the final scan.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum_time_le_exponential
signature: ∀ (xs : List ℕ) (target : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum xs target).time ≤ 1 + xs.length + 7 * (2 ^ xs.length - 1) + 2 ^ xs.length

docstring: Numeric upper bound on the same run, using both target and total-value cardinalities.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum_time_le_numeric
signature: ∀ (xs : List ℕ) (target : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum xs target).time ≤ 1 + xs.length + (7 * xs.length + 1) * Min.min (target + 1) (xs.sum + 1)

docstring: A numeric polynomial target gives the source's selected-event polynomial bound.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum_time_le_of_target_le_pow
signature: ∀ (xs : List ℕ) (target d : ℕ), target ≤ xs.length ^ d → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum xs target).time ≤ 1 + xs.length + (7 * xs.length + 1) * (xs.length ^ d + 1)
statement:
public theorem exactSubsetSum_time_le_of_target_le_pow (xs : List Nat) (target d : Nat)
    (ht : target ≤ xs.length ^ d) :
    (exactSubsetSum xs target).time ≤ 1 + xs.length +
      (7 * xs.length + 1) * (xs.length ^ d + 1)

docstring: Bounded numeric input values give the source's selected-event polynomial bound.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum_time_le_of_values_le_pow
signature: ∀ (xs : List ℕ) (target d : ℕ), (∀ x ∈ xs, x ≤ xs.length ^ d) → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.ExactSubsetSum.exactSubsetSum xs target).time ≤ 1 + xs.length + (7 * xs.length + 1) * (xs.length * xs.length ^ d + 1)
statement:
public theorem exactSubsetSum_time_le_of_values_le_pow (xs : List Nat) (target d : Nat)
    (hx : ∀ x ∈ xs, x ≤ xs.length ^ d) :
    (exactSubsetSum xs target).time ≤ 1 + xs.length +
      (7 * xs.length + 1) * (xs.length * xs.length ^ d + 1)

docstring:
A Fenwick tree over `α`: the one-indexed interval-sum array, with an unused
dummy entry at index `0`. The represented underlying array is not stored; see
`FenwickTree.Valid`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree
signature: (α : Type u) → [AddCommMonoid α] → Type u
statement: public structure FenwickTree (α : Type u) [AddCommMonoid α]

docstring:
The tree represents `arr`: the stored array has one dummy entry plus one
entry per underlying element, and every stored entry equals its interval sum.
The underlying array itself is not stored at runtime; it appears only in this
specification relation.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.Valid
signature: {α : Type u} → [inst : AddCommMonoid α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree α → List α → Prop
statement:
public def Valid {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α] (t : FenwickTree α)
    (arr : List α) : Prop

docstring:
Add `δ` to underlying entry `i` by walking `i + 1, j + lowbit j, …` and adding
`δ` to exactly those stored entries; each write is constant-time only when
the stored array is uniquely referenced, since a shared array is copied by
the first persistent `Array.set`. An out-of-range
`i` visits no index and leaves the tree unchanged. The walk is fuelled by the
size, which always suffices because visited indices strictly increase.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.add
signature: {α : Type u} → [inst : AddCommMonoid α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree α → ℕ → α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree α
statement:
public def add {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α] (t : FenwickTree α) (i : Nat)
    (δ : α) : FenwickTree α

docstring: A point update at an out-of-range position is the identity.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.add_eq_self_of_le
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : AddCommMonoid α] (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree α) {i : ℕ}, t.size ≤ i → ∀ (δ : α), t.add i δ = t
statement:
public theorem add_eq_self_of_le {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α]
    (t : FenwickTree α) {i : Nat} (hi : t.size ≤ i) (δ : α) :
    add t i δ = t

docstring:
The interval sum stored at one-indexed position `j`: the sum of the
`lowbit j` entries of `arr` ending at position `j - 1`, with entries past the end
reading as `0`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.blockSum
signature: {α : Type u} → [AddCommMonoid α] → List α → ℕ → α
statement: public def blockSum {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α] (arr : List α) (j : Nat) : α

docstring:
Array-backed interval sum: like `blockSum`, but reads through an `Array`
in constant time per entry instead of traversing a `List` per lookup. This
is the version used by `build`, so construction takes `O(n log n)` reads
rather than quadratic list indexing.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.blockSumArray
signature: {α : Type u} → [AddCommMonoid α] → Array α → ℕ → α
statement:
public def blockSumArray {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α]
    (arr : Array α) (j : Nat) : α

docstring:
Build a Fenwick tree representing the given array by computing every
interval sum. The input is converted to an `Array` once, so each entry read
is constant-time and construction is `O(n log n)`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.build
signature: {α : Type u} → [inst : AddCommMonoid α] → List α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree α
statement: public def build {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α] (arr : List α) : FenwickTree α

docstring: The largest power of two dividing `n`, with `lowbit 0 = 0`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.lowbit
signature: ℕ → ℕ
statement: public def lowbit (n : Nat) : Nat

docstring:
The quotient `n / lowbit n` is odd, so `lowbit n` is the largest power of two
dividing `n`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.lowbit_div_odd
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → n / Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.lowbit n % 2 = 1
statement: public theorem lowbit_div_odd {n : Nat} (hn : 0 < n) : (n / lowbit n) % 2 = 1

docstring: `lowbit n` divides `n`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.lowbit_dvd
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.lowbit n ∣ n
statement: public theorem lowbit_dvd {n : Nat} (hn : 0 < n) : lowbit n ∣ n

docstring: `lowbit n` is at most `n`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.lowbit_le
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.lowbit n ≤ n
statement: public theorem lowbit_le (n : Nat) : lowbit n ≤ n

docstring: `lowbit` is positive on positive inputs.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.lowbit_pos
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → 0 < Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.lowbit n
statement: public theorem lowbit_pos {n : Nat} (hn : 0 < n) : 0 < lowbit n

docstring: `lowbit n` is a power of two.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.lowbit_two_pow
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → ∃ k, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.lowbit n = 2 ^ k
statement: public theorem lowbit_two_pow {n : Nat} (hn : 0 < n) : ∃ k, lowbit n = 2 ^ k

docstring: `lowbit 0` is `0`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.lowbit_zero
signature: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.lowbit 0 = 0
statement: public theorem lowbit_zero : lowbit 0 = 0

docstring:
The sum of the first `k` underlying entries, computed by walking the stored
entries at `k, k - lowbit k, …` down to `0`. Indices past the end are clamped:
querying at `k` greater than the size sums the whole represented array, just
like `List.take`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.prefixSum
signature: {α : Type u} → [inst : AddCommMonoid α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree α → ℕ → α
statement:
public def prefixSum {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α] (t : FenwickTree α) (k : Nat) :
    α

docstring:
A point update changes exactly the prefix sums past the updated position,
at every query index including past-the-end ones.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.prefixSum_add
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : AddCommMonoid α] {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree α} {arr : List α}, t.Valid arr → ∀ {i : ℕ}, i < arr.length → ∀ (δ : α) (k : ℕ), (t.add i δ).prefixSum k = t.prefixSum k + if i < k then δ else 0
statement:
public theorem prefixSum_add {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α] {t : FenwickTree α}
    {arr : List α} (hv : Valid t arr) {i : Nat} (hi : i < arr.length) (δ : α)
    (k : Nat) :
    prefixSum (add t i δ) k = prefixSum t k + (if i < k then δ else 0)

docstring:
Prefix sums of a freshly built tree agree with the input array's prefix
sums at every index.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.prefixSum_build
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : AddCommMonoid α] (arr : List α) (k : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.build arr).prefixSum k = (List.take k arr).sum
statement:
public theorem prefixSum_build {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α] (arr : List α)
    (k : Nat) : prefixSum (build arr) k = (arr.take k).sum

docstring:
For every `k`, including values past the end, `prefixSum` agrees with the
sum of the corresponding `List.take` of the represented array.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.prefixSum_eq_take_sum
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : AddCommMonoid α] (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree α) {arr : List α}, t.Valid arr → ∀ (k : ℕ), t.prefixSum k = (List.take k arr).sum
statement:
public theorem prefixSum_eq_take_sum {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α]
    (t : FenwickTree α) {arr : List α} (hv : Valid t arr) (k : Nat) :
    prefixSum t k = (arr.take k).sum

docstring: The empty prefix sums to zero.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.prefixSum_zero
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : AddCommMonoid α] (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree α), t.prefixSum 0 = 0
statement:
public theorem prefixSum_zero {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α] (t : FenwickTree α) :
    prefixSum t 0 = 0

docstring:
The sum of the underlying entries with indices in `[lo, hi)`, as a
difference of prefix sums. This is the one operation that needs additive
inverses. Reversed or empty ranges (`hi ≤ lo`) return `0`, matching the sum
over the empty list interval `((arr.take hi).drop lo)`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.rangeSum
signature: {α : Type u} → [inst : AddCommGroup α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree α → ℕ → ℕ → α
statement:
public def rangeSum {α : Type u} [AddCommGroup α] (t : FenwickTree α)
    (lo hi : Nat) : α

docstring:
`rangeSum` agrees with the sum of the represented array over `[lo, hi)`,
with both ends clamped through `List.take`. This holds for every `lo` and
`hi`: when `hi ≤ lo` both sides are `0`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.rangeSum_eq
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : AddCommGroup α] {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree α} {arr : List α}, t.Valid arr → ∀ (lo hi : ℕ), t.rangeSum lo hi = (List.drop lo (List.take hi arr)).sum

docstring:
The number of underlying elements, read off the stored array in constant
time.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.size
signature: {α : Type u} → [inst : AddCommMonoid α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree α → ℕ
statement: public def size {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α] (t : FenwickTree α) : Nat

docstring: The size of a built tree is the length of its input.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.size_build
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : AddCommMonoid α] (arr : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.build arr).size = arr.length
statement:
public theorem size_build {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α] (arr : List α) :

docstring: A tree representing `arr` has size `arr.length`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.size_eq_length_of_valid
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : AddCommMonoid α] {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree α} {arr : List α}, t.Valid arr → t.size = arr.length
statement:

docstring:
Point update at an in-range position moves the representation to the

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree.valid_add
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : AddCommMonoid α] {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FenwickTree α} {arr : List α}, t.Valid arr → ∀ {i : ℕ}, i < arr.length → ∀ (δ : α), (t.add i δ).Valid (arr.set i (arr.getD i 0 + δ))

docstring:
Cut the subtree at path `p` inside the `i`-th tree of a forest: returns the
extracted subtree together with the forest in which that tree is replaced by the cut
remainder (or removed when the whole tree was extracted).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.cutTreeAt
signature: {α : Type u} → List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α) → ℕ → List ℕ → Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α × List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α))
statement:
public def cutTreeAt (trees : List (FibonacciTree α)) (i : Nat) (p : List Nat) :
    Option (FibonacciTree α × List (FibonacciTree α))

docstring:
Cutting a subtree out of a forest partitions the represented multiset into the
remaining forest and the extracted subtree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.cutTreeAt_elements
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {trees : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)} {i : ℕ} {p : List ℕ} {sub : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α} {rest : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.cutTreeAt trees i p = Option.some (sub, rest) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.elements trees = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.elements rest + sub.elements

docstring:
A subtree addressed by an index into the root list and a path inside that tree can
be cut out of the forest.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.cutTreeAt_of_subtreeAt
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {trees : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)} {i : ℕ} {p : List ℕ} {t sub : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α}, trees[i]? = Option.some t → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.subtreeAt p t = Option.some sub → ∃ rest, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.cutTreeAt trees i p = Option.some (sub, rest)
statement:
public theorem cutTreeAt_of_subtreeAt {trees : List (FibonacciTree α)} {i : Nat}
    {p : List Nat} {t sub : FibonacciTree α} (htree : trees[i]? = some t)
    (hpath : t.subtreeAt p = some sub) :
    ∃ rest, cutTreeAt trees i p = some (sub, rest)

docstring: Both parts of a forest cut from a valid forest are valid.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.cutTreeAt_valid
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LE α] {trees : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)} {i : ℕ} {p : List ℕ} {sub : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α} {rest : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.Valid trees → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.cutTreeAt trees i p = Option.some (sub, rest) → sub.Valid ∧ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.Valid rest

docstring: The multiset represented by a forest.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.elements
signature: {α : Type u} → List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α) → Multiset α
statement: public def elements (trees : List (FibonacciTree α)) : Multiset α

docstring: The elements of a concatenated forest are the sum of the elements of its parts.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.elements_append
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (left right : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.elements (left ++ right) = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.elements left + Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.elements right
statement:
public theorem elements_append (left right : List (FibonacciTree α)) :
    elements (left ++ right) = elements left + elements right

docstring: Consolidation preserves every occurrence in the forest.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.elements_consolidate
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (trees : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.elements (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.consolidate trees) = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.elements trees
statement:
public theorem elements_consolidate [LinearOrder α] (trees : List (FibonacciTree α)) :
    elements (consolidate trees) = elements trees

docstring:
A valid forest with distinct degrees has at most as many roots as elements, since
every degree is smaller than the total count.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.length_le_card_of_sorted
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LE α] {trees : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.Valid trees → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.SortedDegrees trees → trees.length ≤ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.elements trees).card

docstring: Combine two optional minima.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.minOption
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → Option α → Option α → Option α
statement: public def minOption [LinearOrder α] (left right : Option α) : Option α

docstring: The minimum root value in a forest, or `none` for the empty forest.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.minRoot
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α) → Option α
statement: public def minRoot [LinearOrder α] : List (FibonacciTree α) → Option α

docstring: The minimum root of a concatenated forest combines the minima of its parts.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.minRoot_append
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (left right : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.minRoot (left ++ right) = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.minOption (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.minRoot left) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.minRoot right)
statement:
public theorem minRoot_append [LinearOrder α] (left right : List (FibonacciTree α)) :
    minRoot (left ++ right) = minOption (minRoot left) (minRoot right)

docstring: A forest has no minimum root exactly when it is empty.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.minRoot_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (trees : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.minRoot trees = Option.none ↔ trees = []
statement:
public theorem minRoot_eq_none_iff [LinearOrder α] (trees : List (FibonacciTree α)) :
    minRoot trees = none ↔ trees = []

docstring:
The minimum root is the root of some tree in the forest and is no greater than
every root in the forest.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.minRoot_spec
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {trees : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)} {minimum : α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.minRoot trees = Option.some minimum → (∃ tree ∈ trees, tree.root = minimum) ∧ ∀ tree ∈ trees, minimum ≤ tree.root

docstring: Remove the first tree whose root is minimal, preferring earlier trees on ties.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.removeMinTree
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α) → Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α × List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α))
statement:
public def removeMinTree [LinearOrder α] :
    List (FibonacciTree α) → Option (FibonacciTree α × List (FibonacciTree α))

docstring: Removing a minimum tree partitions the forest and returns a globally minimal root.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.removeMinTree_spec
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {trees : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)} {minimum : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α} {rest : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.removeMinTree trees = Option.some (minimum, rest) → minimum.elements + Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.elements rest = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.elements trees ∧ minimum ∈ trees ∧ rest.Sublist trees ∧ ∀ tree ∈ trees, minimum.root ≤ tree.root
statement:
public theorem removeMinTree_spec [LinearOrder α]
    {trees : List (FibonacciTree α)} {minimum : FibonacciTree α}
    {rest : List (FibonacciTree α)} (result : removeMinTree trees = some (minimum, rest)) :
    minimum.elements + elements rest = elements trees ∧
      minimum ∈ trees ∧ rest.Sublist trees ∧
      ∀ tree ∈ trees, minimum.root ≤ tree.root

docstring: The concatenation of valid forests is valid.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.valid_append
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LE α] {left right : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.Valid left → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.Valid right → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.Valid (left ++ right)
statement:
public theorem valid_append [LE α] {left right : List (FibonacciTree α)}
    (left_valid : Valid left) (right_valid : Valid right) : Valid (left ++ right)

docstring: Consolidation preserves forest validity.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.valid_consolidate
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {trees : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.Valid trees → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.Valid (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.consolidate trees)
statement:
public theorem valid_consolidate [LinearOrder α] {trees : List (FibonacciTree α)}
    (valid : Valid trees) : Valid (consolidate trees)

docstring: The empty forest is valid.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.valid_nil
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LE α], Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.Valid []
statement: public theorem valid_nil [LE α] : Valid ([] : List (FibonacciTree α))

docstring: A Fibonacci min-heap: a valid forest together with a cached minimum root value.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap
signature: (α : Type u) → [LinearOrder α] → Type u
statement: public structure FibonacciHeap (α : Type u) [LinearOrder α]

docstring: Insertion increments the element count.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.card_elements_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α) (value : α), (heap.insert value).elements.card = heap.elements.card + 1
statement:
public theorem card_elements_insert [LinearOrder α] (heap : FibonacciHeap α) (value : α) :
    (heap.insert value).elements.card = heap.elements.card + 1

docstring: Meld adds the element counts of both heaps.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.card_elements_meld
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (left right : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α), (left.meld right).elements.card = left.elements.card + right.elements.card
statement:
public theorem card_elements_meld [LinearOrder α] (left right : FibonacciHeap α) :
    (left.meld right).elements.card = left.elements.card + right.elements.card

docstring:
Decrease the key of the node addressed by root index `i` and path `p` to
`newKey`: cut the addressed subtree out of its tree, lower its root, and put it back
as a new tree in the root list. The cached minimum of the result is the smaller of
`newKey` and the previous cached minimum, computed without rescanning the root
list. When the address does not resolve or `newKey` is larger than the addressed
root (so the operation would be an increase), the heap is returned unchanged.
Unlike CLRS decrease-key this performs no cascading cuts: the trees carry no mark
field (see the module documentation).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.decreaseKey
signature: {α : Type u} → [inst : LinearOrder α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α → ℕ → List ℕ → α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α
statement:
public def decreaseKey [LinearOrder α] (heap : FibonacciHeap α) (i : Nat) (p : List Nat)
    (newKey : α) : FibonacciHeap α

docstring: A successful decrease-key preserves the number of represented elements.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.decreaseKey_card_elements
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α} {i : ℕ} {p : List ℕ} {newKey : α} {sub : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α} {rest : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.cutTreeAt heap.trees i p = Option.some (sub, rest) → newKey ≤ sub.root → (heap.decreaseKey i p newKey).elements.card = heap.elements.card

docstring:
A successful decrease-key replaces exactly one occurrence of the old key (the
addressed subtree's root) by the new key in the represented multiset.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.decreaseKey_elements
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α} {i : ℕ} {p : List ℕ} {newKey : α} {sub : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α} {rest : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.cutTreeAt heap.trees i p = Option.some (sub, rest) → newKey ≤ sub.root → (heap.decreaseKey i p newKey).elements = newKey ::ₘ heap.elements.erase sub.root

docstring:
`decreaseKey_elements` stated through the addressing view: the caller names the
root tree and the addressed subtree instead of the cut remainder.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.decreaseKey_elements_of_subtreeAt
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α} {i : ℕ} {p : List ℕ} {newKey : α} {t sub : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α}, heap.trees[i]? = Option.some t → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.subtreeAt p t = Option.some sub → newKey ≤ sub.root → (heap.decreaseKey i p newKey).elements = newKey ::ₘ heap.elements.erase sub.root
statement:
public theorem decreaseKey_elements_of_subtreeAt [LinearOrder α]
    {heap : FibonacciHeap α} {i : Nat} {p : List Nat} {newKey : α}
    {t sub : FibonacciTree α} (htree : heap.trees[i]? = some t)
    (hpath : t.subtreeAt p = some sub) (hle : newKey ≤ sub.root) :
    (heap.decreaseKey i p newKey).elements =
      newKey ::ₘ heap.elements.erase sub.root

docstring: Decrease-key with an address that does not resolve is the identity.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.decreaseKey_eq_self_of_cut_none
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α} {i : ℕ} {p : List ℕ} {newKey : α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.cutTreeAt heap.trees i p = Option.none → heap.decreaseKey i p newKey = heap

docstring: Decrease-key with a key larger than the addressed root is the identity.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.decreaseKey_eq_self_of_not_le
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α} {i : ℕ} {p : List ℕ} {newKey : α} {sub : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α} {rest : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.cutTreeAt heap.trees i p = Option.some (sub, rest) → ¬newKey ≤ sub.root → heap.decreaseKey i p newKey = heap

docstring:
After a successful decrease-key, minimum inspection returns the smaller of the
new key and the old minimum.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.decreaseKey_findMin
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α} {i : ℕ} {p : List ℕ} {newKey m : α} {sub : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α} {rest : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.cutTreeAt heap.trees i p = Option.some (sub, rest) → newKey ≤ sub.root → heap.findMin = Option.some m → (heap.decreaseKey i p newKey).findMin = Option.some (Min.min newKey m)

docstring:
On a successful cut with a genuine decrease, the new root list is the decreased
subtree in front of the cut remainder forest.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.decreaseKey_trees_of_cut
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α} {i : ℕ} {p : List ℕ} {newKey : α} {sub : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α} {rest : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.cutTreeAt heap.trees i p = Option.some (sub, rest) → newKey ≤ sub.root → (heap.decreaseKey i p newKey).trees = sub.decreaseRoot newKey :: rest

docstring:
The forest after decrease-key is valid: heap order is restored. This is the
validity field of the resulting heap, exposed as a theorem for convenience.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.decreaseKey_valid
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α) (i : ℕ) (p : List ℕ) (newKey : α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.Valid (heap.decreaseKey i p newKey).trees

docstring:
Remove and return the minimum value. The children of the minimum tree become roots
and the root list is consolidated; the new cached minimum is the minimum root of the
consolidated forest.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.deleteMin
signature: {α : Type u} → [inst : LinearOrder α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α → Option (α × Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α)
statement:
public def deleteMin [LinearOrder α]
    (heap : FibonacciHeap α) : Option (α × FibonacciHeap α)

docstring:
The computational forest projection of minimum deletion: remove a minimum tree,
promote its children, and consolidate.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.deleteMinTrees
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α) → Option (α × List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α))
statement:
public def deleteMinTrees [LinearOrder α]
    (trees : List (FibonacciTree α)) : Option (α × List (FibonacciTree α))

docstring: Successful deletion partitions the original multiset into its minimum and remainder.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.deleteMin_cons_elements
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α} {minimum : α} {rest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α}, heap.deleteMin = Option.some (minimum, rest) → minimum ::ₘ rest.elements = heap.elements

docstring: Successful deletion erases exactly one occurrence of the returned minimum.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.deleteMin_elements
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α} {minimum : α} {rest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α}, heap.deleteMin = Option.some (minimum, rest) → rest.elements = heap.elements.erase minimum

docstring: Deletion fails exactly for the empty heap.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.deleteMin_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α), heap.deleteMin = Option.none ↔ heap.trees = []
statement:
public theorem deleteMin_eq_none_iff [LinearOrder α] (heap : FibonacciHeap α) :
    heap.deleteMin = none ↔ heap.trees = []

docstring: Successful deletion returns a represented globally minimal value.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.deleteMin_le
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α} {minimum value : α} {rest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α}, heap.deleteMin = Option.some (minimum, rest) → value ∈ heap.elements → minimum ≤ value

docstring: After a successful deletion, the heap has at most as many roots as elements.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.deleteMin_length_le_card
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α} {minimum : α} {rest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α}, heap.deleteMin = Option.some (minimum, rest) → rest.trees.length ≤ rest.elements.card

docstring:
After a successful deletion, consolidation has made the root degrees strictly
increasing.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.deleteMin_sortedDegrees
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α} {minimum : α} {rest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α}, heap.deleteMin = Option.some (minimum, rest) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciForest.SortedDegrees rest.trees

docstring: Projecting away the validity proofs from deletion gives `deleteMinTrees`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.deleteMin_trees
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α), Option.map (fun result ↦ (result.1, result.2.trees)) heap.deleteMin = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.deleteMinTrees heap.trees

docstring: The multiset represented by a Fibonacci heap.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.elements
signature: {α : Type u} → [inst : LinearOrder α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α → Multiset α
statement: public def elements [LinearOrder α] (heap : FibonacciHeap α) : Multiset α

docstring: The empty heap represents the empty multiset.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.elements_empty
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α], Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.empty.elements = 0
statement: public theorem elements_empty [LinearOrder α] : (empty : FibonacciHeap α).elements = 0

docstring: Insertion adds exactly one occurrence.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.elements_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α) (value : α), (heap.insert value).elements = value ::ₘ heap.elements
statement:
public theorem elements_insert [LinearOrder α] (heap : FibonacciHeap α) (value : α) :
    (heap.insert value).elements = value ::ₘ heap.elements

docstring: Meld preserves every occurrence from both heaps.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.elements_meld
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (left right : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α), (left.meld right).elements = left.elements + right.elements
statement:
public theorem elements_meld [LinearOrder α] (left right : FibonacciHeap α) :
    (left.meld right).elements = left.elements + right.elements

docstring: A singleton heap represents a singleton multiset.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.elements_singleton
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (value : α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.singleton value).elements = {value}
statement:
public theorem elements_singleton [LinearOrder α] (value : α) :
    (singleton value).elements = {value}

docstring: Union preserves every occurrence from both heaps.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.elements_union
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (left right : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α), (left.union right).elements = left.elements + right.elements
statement:
public theorem elements_union [LinearOrder α] (left right : FibonacciHeap α) :
    (left.union right).elements = left.elements + right.elements

docstring: The empty Fibonacci heap.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.empty
signature: {α : Type u} → [inst : LinearOrder α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α
statement: public def empty [LinearOrder α] : FibonacciHeap α

docstring: Inspect the minimum value (the cached minimum) without removing it.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.findMin
signature: {α : Type u} → [inst : LinearOrder α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α → Option α
statement: public def findMin [LinearOrder α] (heap : FibonacciHeap α) : Option α

docstring: Minimum inspection fails exactly for the empty heap.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.findMin_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap α), heap.findMin = Option.none ↔ heap.trees = []
statement:
public theorem findMin_eq_none_iff [LinearOrder α] (heap : FibonacciHeap α) :
    heap.findMin = none ↔ heap.trees = []

docstring: Minimum inspection returns a value no greater than every represented value.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciHeap.findMin_le

docstring:
Cut out the subtree at a path: returns the extracted subtree together with the

`none` exactly for the empty path, where the whole tree is extracted.

statement:
public def cutAt : List Nat → FibonacciTree α →
    Option (FibonacciTree α × Option (FibonacciTree α))

docstring:
Cutting partitions the represented multiset into the remainder and the extracted
subtree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.cutAt_elements
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {p : List ℕ} {t sub t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.cutAt p t = Option.some (sub, Option.some t') → t.elements = t'.elements + sub.elements

docstring: A cut with no remainder extracted the whole tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.cutAt_eq_self
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {p : List ℕ} {t sub : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.cutAt p t = Option.some (sub, Option.none) → sub = t
statement:
public theorem cutAt_eq_self {p : List Nat} {t sub : FibonacciTree α}
    (h : cutAt p t = some (sub, none)) : sub = t

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.cutAt_nil
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.cutAt [] t = Option.some (t, Option.none)
statement: public theorem cutAt_nil (t : FibonacciTree α) : cutAt [] t = some (t, none)

docstring:
The remainder left by a cut from a valid tree is valid: its children are valid,
its stored degree is corrected, and its root still bounds every remaining element.

signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LE α] {p : List ℕ} {t sub t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α}, t.Valid → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.cutAt p t = Option.some (sub, Option.some t') → t'.Valid
statement:
public theorem cutAt_remainder_valid [LE α] {p : List Nat} {t sub t' : FibonacciTree α}
    (hv : Valid t) (h : cutAt p t = some (sub, some t')) : Valid t'

docstring: The subtree extracted by a cut from a valid tree is valid.

docstring: Cutting at a path extracts exactly the subtree that the path addresses.

docstring:
Decreasing a root replaces one occurrence of the old root in the represented
multiset by the new key.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.elements_decreaseRoot
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq α] (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α) (newKey : α), (t.decreaseRoot newKey).elements = newKey ::ₘ t.elements.erase t.root

public theorem elements_decreaseRoot [DecidableEq α] (t : FibonacciTree α) (newKey : α) :
    (t.decreaseRoot newKey).elements = newKey ::ₘ t.elements.erase t.root

docstring: Linking preserves the disjoint multiset union of both input trees.

    (link left right).elements = left.elements + right.elements

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.elements_singleton

docstring: Every addressed subtree can be cut out.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.subtreeAt_cutAt
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {p : List ℕ} {t sub : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.subtreeAt p t = Option.some sub → ∃ rem, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.cutAt p t = Option.some (sub, rem)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.subtreeAt_nil
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FibonacciTree.subtreeAt [] t = Option.some t

docstring:
`distance` is a lower bound for every weighted path with at most `r`
edges, and is either infinity or the weight of an attaining such path.
Paths may repeat vertices; no absence-of-negative-cycles hypothesis is needed.

signature: {n : ℕ} → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (WithTop ℤ) → ℕ → Fin n → Fin n → WithTop ℤ → Prop

signature: {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Fin n → WithTop ℤ) → List (Fin n) → Prop
statement:
def IsNegativeCycle {n : Nat} (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop Int)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.IsStageShortestPathWeight
signature: {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Fin n → WithTop ℤ) → ℕ → Fin n → Fin n → WithTop ℤ → Prop
statement:
def IsStageShortestPathWeight {n : Nat} (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop Int)
    (k : Nat) (source target : Fin n) (distance : WithTop Int) : Prop

signature: {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Fin n → WithTop ℤ) → Fin n → Fin n → List (Fin n) → Prop
statement:
def IsWeightedPath {n : Nat} (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop Int)
    (source target : Fin n) (path : List (Fin n)) : Prop

docstring: The direct-weight matrix contains no negative cycle.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.NoNegativeCycle
signature: {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Fin n → WithTop ℤ) → Prop
statement: def NoNegativeCycle {n : Nat} (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop Int) : Prop

docstring: Compute the all-pairs distance matrix by the bottom-up Floyd-Warshall recurrence.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.floydWarshall
signature: {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Fin n → WithTop ℤ) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.Cost (Fin n → Fin n → WithTop ℤ)
statement:
def floydWarshall {n : Nat} (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop Int) :
    TimeM Cost (Fin n → Fin n → WithTop Int)

docstring: An output cell is infinite exactly when no weighted path connects its endpoints.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.floydWarshall_distance_eq_top_iff
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop ℤ) (source target : Fin n), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.floydWarshall weight).ret source target = ⊤ ↔ ¬∃ path, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.IsWeightedPath weight source target path
statement:
theorem floydWarshall_distance_eq_top_iff {n : Nat}
    (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop Int) (source target : Fin n) :
    (floydWarshall weight).ret source target = ⊤ ↔
      ¬∃ path, IsWeightedPath weight source target path

docstring: Under the no-negative-cycle hypothesis, no concrete path is cheaper than the output.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.floydWarshall_distance_minimal
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop ℤ) (source target : Fin n) (path : List (Fin n)), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.NoNegativeCycle weight → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.IsWeightedPath weight source target path → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.floydWarshall weight).ret source target ≤ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.pathWeight weight path
statement:
theorem floydWarshall_distance_minimal {n : Nat}
    (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop Int) (source target : Fin n)
    (path : List (Fin n)) (hNoCycle : NoNegativeCycle weight)
    (hPath : IsWeightedPath weight source target path) :
    (floydWarshall weight).ret source target ≤ pathWeight weight path

docstring: Every finite output distance is realized by a concrete weighted path.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.floydWarshall_distance_realized
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop ℤ) (source target : Fin n) (distance : ℤ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.floydWarshall weight).ret source target = ↑distance → ∃ path, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.IsWeightedPath weight source target path ∧ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.pathWeight weight path = ↑distance
statement:
theorem floydWarshall_distance_realized {n : Nat}
    (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop Int) (source target : Fin n) (distance : Int)
    (hDistance : (floydWarshall weight).ret source target = (distance : WithTop Int)) :
    ∃ path, IsWeightedPath weight source target path ∧
      pathWeight weight path = (distance : WithTop Int)

docstring: Under the no-negative-cycle hypothesis, the final cell is the minimum over all paths.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.floydWarshall_distance_spec
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop ℤ) (source target : Fin n), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.NoNegativeCycle weight → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.IsStageShortestPathWeight weight n source target ((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.floydWarshall weight).ret source target)
statement:
theorem floydWarshall_distance_spec {n : Nat}
    (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop Int) (source target : Fin n)
    (hNoCycle : NoNegativeCycle weight) :
    IsStageShortestPathWeight weight n source target
      ((floydWarshall weight).ret source target)

docstring: No negative cycle implies that the diagonal detector is false.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.floydWarshall_hasNegativeDiagonal_eq_false
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop ℤ), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.NoNegativeCycle weight → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.hasNegativeDiagonal (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.floydWarshall weight).ret = Bool.false

docstring: A negative diagonal entry in the computed matrix implies a simple negative cycle.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.floydWarshall_hasNegativeDiagonal_sound
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (weight : Fin n → Fin n → WithTop ℤ), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.hasNegativeDiagonal (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.floydWarshall weight).ret = Bool.true → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.HasNegativeCycle weight
statement:
theorem floydWarshall_hasNegativeDiagonal_sound {n : Nat}

docstring:
Characterize an edge-bounded shortest weight by universal lower bounds
and finite attainment, without unfolding the path specification.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.isEdgeBoundedShortestPathWeight_iff
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (weight : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (WithTop ℤ)) (r : ℕ) (i j : Fin n) (distance : WithTop ℤ), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.IsEdgeBoundedShortestPathWeight weight r i j distance ↔ (∀ (path : List (Fin n)), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.IsWeightedPath weight i j path → path.length - 1 ≤ r → distance ≤ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.pathWeight weight path) ∧ (distance = ⊤ ∨ ∃ path, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.IsWeightedPath weight i j path ∧ path.length - 1 ≤ r ∧ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.pathWeight weight path = distance)
statement:
public theorem isEdgeBoundedShortestPathWeight_iff {n : Nat}
    (weight : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (WithTop Int))
    (r : Nat) (i j : Fin n) (distance : WithTop Int) :
    IsEdgeBoundedShortestPathWeight weight r i j distance ↔
      (∀ path, IsWeightedPath weight i j path → path.length - 1 ≤ r →
        distance ≤ pathWeight weight path) ∧
      (distance = ⊤ ∨ ∃ path, IsWeightedPath weight i j path ∧
        path.length - 1 ≤ r ∧ pathWeight weight path = distance)
