docstring: Negates each adjacency bit, charging one read and one write per bit.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.hamiltonianCycleToTsp
signature: Array Bool → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (Array Bool)
statement: def hamiltonianCycleToTsp (x : Array Bool) : TimeM Nat (Array Bool)

docstring:
An encoded simple graph yields zero on edges, one on nonedges and the diagonal,
and symmetric cells.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.hamiltonianCycleToTsp_costs
signature: ∀ (x : Array Bool) (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [inst : DecidableRel G.Adj], x.size = n * n → (∀ (i j : Fin n), x[↑i * n + ↑j]? = Option.some (Decidable.decide (G.Adj i j))) → (∀ (i j : Fin n), Option.map Bool.toNat (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.hamiltonianCycleToTsp x).ret[↑i * n + ↑j]? = Option.some (if G.Adj i j then 0 else 1)) ∧ (∀ (i : Fin n), Option.map Bool.toNat (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.hamiltonianCycleToTsp x).ret[↑i * n + ↑i]? = Option.some 1) ∧ ∀ (i j : Fin n), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.hamiltonianCycleToTsp x).ret[↑i * n + ↑j]? = (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.hamiltonianCycleToTsp x).ret[↑j * n + ↑i]?
statement:
theorem hamiltonianCycleToTsp_costs (x : Array Bool) (n : Nat)
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (_hsize : x.size = n * n)
    (henc : ∀ i j : Fin n, x[i.val * n + j.val]? = some (decide (G.Adj i j))) :
    (∀ i j : Fin n,
      ((hamiltonianCycleToTsp x).ret[i.val * n + j.val]?).map Bool.toNat =
        some (if G.Adj i j then 0 else 1)) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin n,
      ((hamiltonianCycleToTsp x).ret[i.val * n + i.val]?).map Bool.toNat = some 1) ∧
    (∀ i j : Fin n,
      (hamiltonianCycleToTsp x).ret[i.val * n + j.val]? =
        (hamiltonianCycleToTsp x).ret[j.val * n + i.val]?)

docstring:
Every source Hamiltonian cycle maps to the complete graph with the same support
and zero actual cost.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.hamiltonianCycleToTsp_forward
signature: ∀ (x : Array Bool) (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [inst : DecidableRel G.Adj], x.size = n * n → (∀ (i j : Fin n), x[↑i * n + ↑j]? = Option.some (Decidable.decide (G.Adj i j))) → ∀ (a : Fin n) (p : G.Walk a a), p.IsHamiltonianCycle → (SimpleGraph.Walk.mapLe ⋯ p).IsHamiltonianCycle ∧ (SimpleGraph.Walk.mapLe ⋯ p).support = p.support ∧ ∃ costs, List.mapM (fun d ↦ Option.map Bool.toNat (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.hamiltonianCycleToTsp x).ret[↑d.toProd.1 * n + ↑d.toProd.2]?) (SimpleGraph.Walk.mapLe ⋯ p).darts = Option.some costs ∧ costs.sum = 0
statement:
theorem hamiltonianCycleToTsp_forward (x : Array Bool) (n : Nat)
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hsize : x.size = n * n)
    (henc : ∀ i j : Fin n, x[i.val * n + j.val]? = some (decide (G.Adj i j)))
    (a : Fin n) (p : G.Walk a a) (hp : p.IsHamiltonianCycle) :
    (p.mapLe (show G ≤ SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n) from le_top)).IsHamiltonianCycle ∧
    (p.mapLe (show G ≤ SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n) from le_top)).support = p.support ∧
    ∃ costs : List Nat,
      (p.mapLe (show G ≤ SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n) from le_top)).darts.mapM
          (fun d => ((hamiltonianCycleToTsp x).ret[d.fst.val * n + d.snd.val]?).map
            Bool.toNat) = some costs ∧ costs.sum = 0

docstring:
A source graph has a strict Hamiltonian cycle exactly when the transformed instance
has a nonpositive-cost strict tour.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.hamiltonianCycleToTsp_iff
signature: ∀ (x : Array Bool) (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [inst : DecidableRel G.Adj], x.size = n * n → (∀ (i j : Fin n), x[↑i * n + ↑j]? = Option.some (Decidable.decide (G.Adj i j))) → ((∃ a p, p.IsHamiltonianCycle) ↔ ∃ a p, p.IsHamiltonianCycle ∧ ∃ costs, List.mapM (fun d ↦ Option.map Bool.toNat (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.hamiltonianCycleToTsp x).ret[↑d.toProd.1 * n + ↑d.toProd.2]?) p.darts = Option.some costs ∧ costs.sum ≤ 0)
statement:
theorem hamiltonianCycleToTsp_iff (x : Array Bool) (n : Nat)
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hsize : x.size = n * n)
    (henc : ∀ i j : Fin n, x[i.val * n + j.val]? = some (decide (G.Adj i j))) :
    ((∃ (a : Fin n) (p : G.Walk a a), p.IsHamiltonianCycle) ↔
      ∃ (a : Fin n) (p : (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)).Walk a a),
        p.IsHamiltonianCycle ∧ ∃ costs : List Nat,
          p.darts.mapM
            (fun d => ((hamiltonianCycleToTsp x).ret[d.fst.val * n + d.snd.val]?).map
              Bool.toNat) = some costs ∧ costs.sum ≤ 0)

docstring:
Every complete-graph Hamiltonian cycle of nonpositive actual cost transfers to
the source graph with unchanged support.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.hamiltonianCycleToTsp_reverse
signature: ∀ (x : Array Bool) (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [inst : DecidableRel G.Adj], x.size = n * n → (∀ (i j : Fin n), x[↑i * n + ↑j]? = Option.some (Decidable.decide (G.Adj i j))) → ∀ (a : Fin n) (p : (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)).Walk a a), p.IsHamiltonianCycle → (∃ costs, List.mapM (fun d ↦ Option.map Bool.toNat (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.hamiltonianCycleToTsp x).ret[↑d.toProd.1 * n + ↑d.toProd.2]?) p.darts = Option.some costs ∧ costs.sum ≤ 0) → ∃ q, q.IsHamiltonianCycle ∧ q.support = p.support
statement:
theorem hamiltonianCycleToTsp_reverse (x : Array Bool) (n : Nat)
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hsize : x.size = n * n)
    (henc : ∀ i j : Fin n, x[i.val * n + j.val]? = some (decide (G.Adj i j)))
    (a : Fin n) (p : (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)).Walk a a)
    (hp : p.IsHamiltonianCycle)
    (hcost : ∃ costs : List Nat,
      p.darts.mapM
        (fun d => ((hamiltonianCycleToTsp x).ret[d.fst.val * n + d.snd.val]?).map
          Bool.toNat) = some costs ∧ costs.sum ≤ 0) :
    ∃ q : G.Walk a a, q.IsHamiltonianCycle ∧ q.support = p.support

docstring: Checks a fixed-width binary Hamiltonian-cycle certificate against a row-major graph.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.verifyHamiltonianCycle
signature: Array Bool → Array Bool → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ Bool
statement: public def verifyHamiltonianCycle (x y : Array Bool) : TimeM Nat Bool

docstring: An accepted certificate has the exact fixed-word size and is no longer than the graph.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.verifyHamiltonianCycle_certificate_size
signature: ∀ (x y : Array Bool), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.verifyHamiltonianCycle x y).ret = Bool.true → y.size = x.size.sqrt * Nat.clog 2 x.size.sqrt ∧ y.size ≤ x.size

docstring: Every canonical Hamiltonian cycle has an accepted exact fixed-width certificate.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.verifyHamiltonianCycle_complete
statement:
public theorem verifyHamiltonianCycle_complete (x : Array Bool) :
    let m := Nat.sqrt x.size
    ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin m), m * m = x.size →
      (∀ i j, G.Adj i j ↔ x[i.val * m + j.val]? = some true) →
      ∀ (v : Fin m) (p : G.Walk v v), p.IsHamiltonianCycle →
        ∃ y : Array Bool, y.size = m * Nat.clog 2 m ∧
          (verifyHamiltonianCycle x y).ret = true

docstring: The actual verifier accepts exactly its graph encoding and ordered-cycle checks.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.verifyHamiltonianCycle_iff
statement:
public theorem verifyHamiltonianCycle_iff (x y : Array Bool) :
    let m := Nat.sqrt x.size
    let w := Nat.clog 2 m
    let decode := fun i : Nat => Nat.ofDigits 2
      ((y.toList.drop (i * w)).take w |>.map fun bit => if bit then 1 else 0)
    (verifyHamiltonianCycle x y).ret = true ↔
      m * m = x.size ∧ 3 ≤ m ∧ y.size = m * w ∧
      (∀ i < m, x[i * m + i]? = some false) ∧
      (∀ i < m, ∀ j < m, x[i * m + j]? = x[j * m + i]?) ∧
      (∀ i < m, decode i < m) ∧
      (∀ i < m, ∀ j < m, decode i = decode j → i = j) ∧
      (∀ i < m, x[decode i * m + decode ((i + 1) % m)]? = some true)

docstring: Certificate existence is exactly strict canonical Hamiltonian-cycle existence.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.verifyHamiltonianCycle_language_iff
signature:
∀ (x : Array Bool),
  (∃ y, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.verifyHamiltonianCycle x y).ret = Bool.true) ↔
    have m := x.size.sqrt;
    m * m = x.size ∧ 3 ≤ m ∧ ∃ G, (∀ (i j : Fin m), G.Adj i j ↔ x[↑i * m + ↑j]? = Option.some Bool.true) ∧ ∃ v p, p.IsHamiltonianCycle
statement:
public theorem verifyHamiltonianCycle_language_iff (x : Array Bool) :
    (∃ y : Array Bool, (verifyHamiltonianCycle x y).ret = true) ↔
      let m := Nat.sqrt x.size
      m * m = x.size ∧ 3 ≤ m ∧
        ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin m),
          (∀ i j, G.Adj i j ↔ x[i.val * m + j.val]? = some true) ∧
          ∃ v : Fin m, ∃ p : G.Walk v v, p.IsHamiltonianCycle

docstring: Every accepted certificate gives a canonical Hamiltonian cycle in the encoded graph.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.verifyHamiltonianCycle_sound
signature:
∀ (x y : Array Bool),
  (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.verifyHamiltonianCycle x y).ret = Bool.true →
    have m := x.size.sqrt;
    m * m = x.size ∧ 3 ≤ m ∧ ∃ G, (∀ (i j : Fin m), G.Adj i j ↔ x[↑i * m + ↑j]? = Option.some Bool.true) ∧ ∃ v p, p.IsHamiltonianCycle
statement:
public theorem verifyHamiltonianCycle_sound (x y : Array Bool)
    (h : (verifyHamiltonianCycle x y).ret = true) :
    let m := Nat.sqrt x.size
    m * m = x.size ∧ 3 ≤ m ∧
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin m),
        (∀ i j, G.Adj i j ↔ x[i.val * m + j.val]? = some true) ∧
        ∃ v : Fin m, ∃ p : G.Walk v v, p.IsHamiltonianCycle

docstring: The actual verifier's selected events are polynomially bounded for every input.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.verifyHamiltonianCycle_time_le
signature: ∃ c, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (x y : Array Bool), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.verifyHamiltonianCycle x y).time ≤ c * (x.size + y.size + 1) ^ 2

docstring: Accepted certificates give a bound in the graph's encoded bit length alone.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.verifyHamiltonianCycle_time_le_of_accept
signature: ∃ c, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (x y : Array Bool), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.verifyHamiltonianCycle x y).ret = Bool.true → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Graph.verifyHamiltonianCycle x y).time ≤ c * (x.size + 1) ^ 2
statement:
public theorem verifyHamiltonianCycle_time_le_of_accept :
    ∃ c : Nat, 0 < c ∧ ∀ x y : Array Bool,
      (verifyHamiltonianCycle x y).ret = true →
        (verifyHamiltonianCycle x y).time ≤ c * (x.size + 1) ^ 2

public theorem mem_contents_iff {w B : Nat} (t : GroupedYFastTrie w B)
    (x : Fin (2 ^ w)) : x ∈ t.contents ↔ ∃ g ∈ t.groups, x ∈ g

docstring:
Under `Valid`, representative lookup plus group scan decides membership in
`contents` exactly.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.GroupedYFastTrie.member_iff

    (x : Fin (2 ^ w)) : t.member x = true ↔ x ∈ t.contents

docstring: Membership in the trie built from a list is membership in the list.

At `B = 0`, building from a nonempty list cannot be valid: the single

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.GroupedYFastTrie.not_valid_ofSortedList_zero

Build a grouped y-fast trie from a sorted list by cutting it into groups
of at most `B` keys. The bound and validity require `0 < B`

result is invalid for nonempty `l` (`not_valid_ofSortedList_zero`).

Successor: locate the least representative above `x` in the x-fast trie, then

public def successor {w B : Nat} (t : GroupedYFastTrie w B) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)) :

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.GroupedYFastTrie.successor_empty
signature: ∀ {w B : ℕ} (x : Fin (2 ^ w)), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.GroupedYFastTrie.empty.successor x = Option.none
statement:
public theorem successor_empty {w B : Nat} (x : Fin (2 ^ w)) :
    (empty : GroupedYFastTrie w B).successor x = none

docstring: The successor is `none` exactly when no stored key is greater than `x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.GroupedYFastTrie.successor_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {w B : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.GroupedYFastTrie w B}, t.Valid → ∀ (x : Fin (2 ^ w)), t.successor x = Option.none ↔ ∀ z ∈ t.contents, ¬x < z

docstring: The successor is `some y` exactly when `y` is the least stored key above `x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.GroupedYFastTrie.successor_eq_some_iff
signature: ∀ {w B : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.GroupedYFastTrie w B}, t.Valid → ∀ (x y : Fin (2 ^ w)), t.successor x = Option.some y ↔ y ∈ t.contents ∧ x < y ∧ ∀ z ∈ t.contents, x < z → y ≤ z
statement:
public theorem successor_eq_some_iff {w B : Nat} {t : GroupedYFastTrie w B}
    (hv : t.Valid) (x y : Fin (2 ^ w)) :
    t.successor x = some y ↔
      y ∈ t.contents ∧ x < y ∧ ∀ z ∈ t.contents, x < z → y ≤ z

docstring:
The successor in the trie built from a list is the least element of the list
above the query.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.GroupedYFastTrie.successor_ofSortedList_eq_some_iff
signature: ∀ {w B : ℕ}, 0 < B → ∀ {l : List (Fin (2 ^ w))}, List.Pairwise (fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 < x2) l → ∀ (x y : Fin (2 ^ w)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.GroupedYFastTrie.ofSortedList B l).successor x = Option.some y ↔ y ∈ l ∧ x < y ∧ ∀ z ∈ l, x < z → y ≤ z
statement:
public theorem successor_ofSortedList_eq_some_iff {w B : Nat} (hB : 0 < B)
    {l : List (Fin (2 ^ w))} (hsorted : l.Pairwise (· < ·)) (x y : Fin (2 ^ w)) :
    (ofSortedList B l).successor x = some y ↔
      y ∈ l ∧ x < y ∧ ∀ z ∈ l, x < z → y ≤ z

signature: ∀ {w B : ℕ}, 0 < B → ∀ {l : List (Fin (2 ^ w))}, List.Pairwise (fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 < x2) l → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.GroupedYFastTrie.ofSortedList B l).Valid

docstring:
A finite hash table with separate `AList` chains and a positive number of buckets. No expected
constant-time bound is claimed because the model supplies neither a probability distribution nor
a probabilistic assumption about `hash`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable
signature: (α : Type u) → Type v → (α → ℕ) → Type (max u v)
statement: public structure HashTable (α : Type u) (β : Type v) (hash : α → Nat)

docstring: Every binding lies in its hash-selected bucket; each `AList` chain has unique keys.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.Valid
signature: {α : Type u} → {β : Type v} → {hash : α → ℕ} → [DecidableEq α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable α β hash → Prop
statement:
public def Valid {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {hash : α → Nat} [DecidableEq α]
    (table : HashTable α β hash) : Prop

docstring: The bucket-independent finite map represented by the table.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.abstraction
signature: {α : Type u} → {β : Type v} → {hash : α → ℕ} → [DecidableEq α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable α β hash → Finmap fun x ↦ β
statement:
public def abstraction {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {hash : α → Nat} [DecidableEq α]
    (table : HashTable α β hash) : Finmap (fun _ : α => β)

docstring: The empty table abstracts to the empty finite map.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.abstraction_empty
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (hash : α → ℕ) [inst : DecidableEq α] (bucketCount : ℕ) (bucketCount_pos : 0 < bucketCount), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.empty hash bucketCount bucketCount_pos).abstraction = ∅
statement:
public theorem abstraction_empty {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (hash : α → Nat) [DecidableEq α]
    (bucketCount : Nat) (bucketCount_pos : 0 < bucketCount) :
    abstraction (empty hash bucketCount bucketCount_pos : HashTable α β hash) = ∅

docstring: Abstracting insertion is finite-map insertion, including replacement.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.abstraction_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {hash : α → ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq α] (key : α) (value : β) (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable α β hash), table.Valid → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.insert key value table).abstraction = Finmap.insert key value table.abstraction
statement:
public theorem abstraction_insert {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {hash : α → Nat}
    [DecidableEq α] (key : α) (value : β) (table : HashTable α β hash)
    (valid : Valid table) :
    abstraction (insert key value table) = Finmap.insert key value (abstraction table)

docstring: The empty hash table with the specified positive bucket count.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.empty
signature: {α : Type u} → {β : Type v} → (hash : α → ℕ) → (bucketCount : ℕ) → 0 < bucketCount → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable α β hash
statement:
public def empty {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (hash : α → Nat)
    (bucketCount : Nat) (bucketCount_pos : 0 < bucketCount) : HashTable α β hash

docstring: Inserts a new binding or replaces the existing binding for the key.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.insert
signature: {α : Type u} → {β : Type v} → {hash : α → ℕ} → [DecidableEq α] → α → β → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable α β hash → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable α β hash
statement:
public def insert {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {hash : α → Nat} [DecidableEq α]

docstring: Looks up a key in its hash-selected bucket.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.lookup
signature: {α : Type u} → {β : Type v} → {hash : α → ℕ} → [DecidableEq α] → α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable α β hash → Option β
statement:
public def lookup {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {hash : α → Nat} [DecidableEq α]
    (key : α) (table : HashTable α β hash) : Option β

docstring: Table lookup agrees with lookup in its bucket-independent finite-map abstraction.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.lookup_abstraction
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {hash : α → ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq α] (key : α) (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable α β hash), table.Valid → Finmap.lookup key table.abstraction = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.lookup key table

docstring: Looking up any key in the empty table returns `none`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.lookup_empty
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (hash : α → ℕ) [inst : DecidableEq α] (bucketCount : ℕ) (bucketCount_pos : 0 < bucketCount) (key : α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.lookup key (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.empty hash bucketCount bucketCount_pos) = Option.none
statement:
public theorem lookup_empty {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (hash : α → Nat) [DecidableEq α]
    (bucketCount : Nat) (bucketCount_pos : 0 < bucketCount) (key : α) :
    lookup key (empty hash bucketCount bucketCount_pos : HashTable α β hash) = none

docstring: Looking up an inserted key returns the newly supplied value.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.lookup_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {hash : α → ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq α] (key : α) (value : β) (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable α β hash), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.lookup key (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.insert key value table) = Option.some value
statement:
public theorem lookup_insert {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {hash : α → Nat} [DecidableEq α]
    (key : α) (value : β) (table : HashTable α β hash) :
    lookup key (insert key value table) = some value

docstring: Inserting one key leaves lookup of every distinct key unchanged, including collisions.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.lookup_insert_of_ne
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {hash : α → ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq α] (key other : α) (value : β) (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable α β hash), other ≠ key → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.lookup other (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.insert key value table) = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.lookup other table
statement:
public theorem lookup_insert_of_ne {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {hash : α → Nat}
    [DecidableEq α] (key other : α) (value : β) (table : HashTable α β hash)
    (different : other ≠ key) :
    lookup other (insert key value table) = lookup other table

docstring: The empty table satisfies the canonicality invariant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.valid_empty
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (hash : α → ℕ) [inst : DecidableEq α] (bucketCount : ℕ) (bucketCount_pos : 0 < bucketCount), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.empty hash bucketCount bucketCount_pos).Valid
statement:
public theorem valid_empty {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (hash : α → Nat) [DecidableEq α]
    (bucketCount : Nat) (bucketCount_pos : 0 < bucketCount) :
    Valid (empty hash bucketCount bucketCount_pos : HashTable α β hash)

docstring: Insertion or replacement preserves canonical bucket placement.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.valid_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {hash : α → ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq α] (key : α) (value : β) (table : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable α β hash), table.Valid → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HashTable.insert key value table).Valid

public theorem valid_insert {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {hash : α → Nat} [DecidableEq α]
    (key : α) (value : β) (table : HashTable α β hash) (valid : Valid table) :

docstring: A binary coding tree whose leaves retain their symbols and weights.

docstring:
A competitor is a full prefix-code tree with exactly the same weighted
symbols as the input.  Full binary structure is intrinsic to `HuffmanTree`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.Admissible
signature: {α : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α → List (α × ℕ) → Prop
statement:
def HuffmanTree.Admissible {α : Type u} (tree : HuffmanTree α)

docstring: The subtype of symbols occurring as leaves of a tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.LeafSymbol
signature: {α : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α → Type (max 0 u)
statement: abbrev HuffmanTree.LeafSymbol {α : Type u} (tree : HuffmanTree α)

docstring:
The codeword for a symbol, when the symbol occurs in the tree.

A singleton tree uses `[false]`; larger trees use `false` for a left edge and
`true` for a right edge.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.code?
signature: {α : Type u} → [DecidableEq α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α → α → Option (List Bool)
statement:
def HuffmanTree.code? {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α] :
    HuffmanTree α → α → Option (List Bool)

docstring: Looking up a leaf symbol returns its total codeword.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.code?_codeOfLeaf
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq α] (tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α) (symbol : tree.LeafSymbol), tree.code? ↑symbol = Option.some (tree.codeOfLeaf symbol)

theorem HuffmanTree.code?_codeOfLeaf {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α]
    (tree : HuffmanTree α) (symbol : tree.LeafSymbol) :
    tree.code? symbol.1 = some (tree.codeOfLeaf symbol)

docstring: Every leaf symbol has a codeword.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.code?_isSome_of_mem_symbols
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq α] {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α} {symbol : α}, symbol ∈ tree.symbols → (tree.code? symbol).isSome = Bool.true
statement:
theorem HuffmanTree.code?_isSome_of_mem_symbols {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α]
    {tree : HuffmanTree α} {symbol : α} (h : symbol ∈ tree.symbols) :
    (tree.code? symbol).isSome

docstring: The total code on the leaf-symbol subtype.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.codeOfLeaf
signature: {α : Type u} → [DecidableEq α] → (tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α) → tree.LeafSymbol → List Bool
statement:
def HuffmanTree.codeOfLeaf {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α]

docstring: Decode a complete bit string, rejecting an incomplete or invalid final codeword.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.decode?
signature: {α : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α → List Bool → Option (List α)
statement:
def HuffmanTree.decode? {α : Type u} (tree : HuffmanTree α) :
    List Bool → Option (List α)

docstring: Decode one nonempty codeword, leaving unconsumed bits.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.decodeOne?
signature: {α : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α → List Bool → Option (α × List Bool)
statement:
def HuffmanTree.decodeOne? {α : Type u} :
    HuffmanTree α → List Bool → Option (α × List Bool)

docstring: Decode one path after the root choice, leaving unconsumed bits.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.decodePath?
signature: {α : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α → List Bool → Option (α × List Bool)
statement:
def HuffmanTree.decodePath? {α : Type u} :
    HuffmanTree α → List Bool → Option (α × List Bool)

docstring: Decoding concatenated leaf codewords recovers their symbols.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.decode_codeOfLeaf
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq α] (tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α) (message : List tree.LeafSymbol), tree.decode? (List.flatMap tree.codeOfLeaf message) = Option.some (List.map Subtype.val message)
statement:
theorem HuffmanTree.decode_codeOfLeaf {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α]
    (tree : HuffmanTree α) (message : List tree.LeafSymbol) :
    tree.decode? (message.flatMap tree.codeOfLeaf) = some (message.map Subtype.val)

docstring: Encoding and then decoding any leaf-subtype message is a round trip.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.decode_encode_leafSymbols
signature:
∀ {α : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq α] (tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α) (message : List tree.LeafSymbol),
  (match tree.encode? (List.map Subtype.val message) with
    | Option.none => Option.none
    | Option.some bits => tree.decode? bits) =
    Option.some (List.map Subtype.val message)
statement:
theorem HuffmanTree.decode_encode_leafSymbols {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α]
    (tree : HuffmanTree α) (message : List tree.LeafSymbol) :
    (match tree.encode? (message.map Subtype.val) with
      | none => none
      | some bits => tree.decode? bits) =
      some (message.map Subtype.val)

docstring: Encode a message when every symbol occurs in the tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.encode?
signature: {α : Type u} → [DecidableEq α] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α → List α → Option (List Bool)
statement:
def HuffmanTree.encode? {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α] (tree : HuffmanTree α) :
    List α → Option (List Bool)

docstring: Encoding leaf-subtype messages concatenates their total codewords.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.encode_codeOfLeaf
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq α] (tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α) (message : List tree.LeafSymbol), tree.encode? (List.map Subtype.val message) = Option.some (List.flatMap tree.codeOfLeaf message)
statement:
theorem HuffmanTree.encode_codeOfLeaf {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α]
    (tree : HuffmanTree α) (message : List tree.LeafSymbol) :
    tree.encode? (message.map Subtype.val) =
      some (message.flatMap tree.codeOfLeaf)

docstring:
The structural encoded-length objective: weighted path length with a one-bit
convention at a lone leaf, so a singleton leaf of weight `w` costs `w`. This agrees
with the public encoder's emitted cost (weight times codeword length, summed over
the weighted leaves) whenever the leaf symbols are unique; see
`HuffmanTree.encodedLength_eq_sum_codeLengths`. For trees with repeated symbols the
encoder resolves each symbol to its first leaf, so on such trees this function is
the structural path cost rather than the emitted encoder cost.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.encodedLength
signature: {α : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α → ℕ
statement: def HuffmanTree.encodedLength {α : Type u} : HuffmanTree α → Nat

docstring:
With unique symbols, `encodedLength` is exactly the encoder's total cost:
the sum over the weighted leaves of weight times emitted codeword length.
Without unique symbols the encoder resolves repeated symbols to their first
leaf, and `encodedLength` remains the structural path cost.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.encodedLength_eq_sum_codeLengths
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq α] {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α}, tree.symbols.Nodup → (List.map (fun x ↦ x.2 * (Option.map List.length (tree.code? x.1)).getD 0) tree.weightedLeaves).sum = tree.encodedLength
statement:
theorem HuffmanTree.encodedLength_eq_sum_codeLengths {α : Type u}
    [DecidableEq α] {tree : HuffmanTree α} (hnd : tree.symbols.Nodup) :
    (tree.weightedLeaves.map
        (fun x => x.2 * ((tree.code? x.1).map List.length).getD 0)).sum =
      tree.encodedLength

docstring: At a fork, the encoded-length objective agrees with weighted path length.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.encodedLength_fork
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (left right : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α), (left.fork right).encodedLength = (left.fork right).weightedPathLength
statement:
theorem HuffmanTree.encodedLength_fork {α : Type u} (left right : HuffmanTree α) :
    (HuffmanTree.fork left right).encodedLength =
      (HuffmanTree.fork left right).weightedPathLength

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree.weightedPathLength_eq_sum_pathLengths
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq α] {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α}, tree.symbols.Nodup → (List.map (fun x ↦ x.2 * (Option.map List.length (tree.pathCode? x.1)).getD 0) tree.weightedLeaves).sum = tree.weightedPathLength

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree.ContainsAt
signature: ℝ → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree → ℕ → Prop
statement: inductive ContainsAt (value : Real) : HuffmanWeightTree → Nat → Prop

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree.ContainsAt.depth_le_height
signature: ∀ {value : ℝ} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree} {depth : ℕ}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree.ContainsAt value tree depth → depth ≤ tree.height

docstring: Change one specified leaf occurrence and record its exact cost change.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree.ContainsAt.reweight
signature: ∀ {value replacement : ℝ} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree} {depth : ℕ}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree.ContainsAt value tree depth → ∃ remainder result, tree.weights = value ::ₘ remainder ∧ result.weights = replacement ::ₘ remainder ∧ result.totalWeight = tree.totalWeight + (replacement - value) ∧ result.pathCost = tree.pathCost + ↑depth * (replacement - value) ∧ result.height = tree.height
statement:
theorem ContainsAt.reweight {value replacement : Real}
    {tree : HuffmanWeightTree} {depth : Nat}
    (h : ContainsAt value tree depth) :
    ∃ (remainder : Multiset Real) (result : HuffmanWeightTree),
      tree.weights = value ::ₘ remainder ∧
      result.weights = replacement ::ₘ remainder ∧
      result.totalWeight = tree.totalWeight + (replacement - value) ∧
      result.pathCost =
        tree.pathCost + (depth : Real) * (replacement - value) ∧
      result.height = tree.height

docstring: A certificate that a cost is produced by repeated two-minimum merges.

signature: Multiset ℝ → ℝ → Prop

docstring:
Repeated two-minimum merges lower-bound every full tree with the same

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree.MergeTrace.le_pathCost

docstring:
Contract the two least weights after an independently derived sibling
exchange argument on structural tree cost.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree.contractLeastPair
signature: ∀ (tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree) (least next : ℝ) (tail : Multiset ℝ), tree.weights = least ::ₘ next ::ₘ tail → least ≤ next → (∀ weight ∈ tail, next ≤ weight) → ∃ result, result.weights = (least + next) ::ₘ tail ∧ result.pathCost + least + next ≤ tree.pathCost
statement:
theorem contractLeastPair (tree : HuffmanWeightTree) (least next : Real)
    (tail : Multiset Real)
    (htree : tree.weights = least ::ₘ next ::ₘ tail)
    (hleastNext : least ≤ next)
    (htail : ∀ weight ∈ tail, next ≤ weight) :
    ∃ result : HuffmanWeightTree,
      result.weights = (least + next) ::ₘ tail ∧
      result.pathCost + least + next ≤ tree.pathCost

theorem eq_leaf_of_height_eq_zero {tree : HuffmanWeightTree}

docstring:
Expose a deepest sibling pair and describe contraction by structural cost
identities, without representing the whole tree as weight-depth pairs.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree.exists_cherry_contraction
signature: ∀ (tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree), 1 ≤ tree.height → ∃ first second remainder baseCost, tree.weights = first ::ₘ second ::ₘ remainder ∧ tree.pathCost = baseCost + ↑tree.height * first + ↑tree.height * second ∧ ∀ (combined : ℝ), ∃ result, result.weights = combined ::ₘ remainder ∧ result.height ≤ tree.height ∧ result.pathCost = baseCost + ↑(tree.height - 1) * combined
statement:
theorem exists_cherry_contraction (tree : HuffmanWeightTree)
    (hpositive : 1 ≤ tree.height) :
    ∃ (first second : Real) (remainder : Multiset Real) (baseCost : Real),
      tree.weights = first ::ₘ second ::ₘ remainder ∧
      tree.pathCost =
        baseCost + (tree.height : Real) * first +
          (tree.height : Real) * second ∧
      ∀ combined : Real, ∃ result : HuffmanWeightTree,
        result.weights = combined ::ₘ remainder ∧
        result.height ≤ tree.height ∧
        result.pathCost =
          baseCost + ((tree.height - 1 : Nat) : Real) * combined

docstring: Replace one smaller weight by a larger one, with a height-based cost bound.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree.raiseBounded
signature: ∀ {bound : ℕ} (tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree), tree.height ≤ bound → ∀ (target : Multiset ℝ) (replacement value : ℝ), replacement ::ₘ tree.weights = value ::ₘ target → value ≤ replacement → ∃ result, result.weights = target ∧ result.height ≤ bound ∧ result.pathCost ≤ tree.pathCost + ↑bound * (replacement - value)
statement:
theorem raiseBounded {bound : Nat} (tree : HuffmanWeightTree)
    (hheight : tree.height ≤ bound) (target : Multiset Real)
    (replacement value : Real)
    (hweights : replacement ::ₘ tree.weights = value ::ₘ target)
    (hle : value ≤ replacement) :
    ∃ result : HuffmanWeightTree,
      result.weights = target ∧ result.height ≤ bound ∧
      result.pathCost ≤
        tree.pathCost + (bound : Real) * (replacement - value)

docstring: Perform two occurrence-preserving weight exchanges.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree.raisePair
signature: ∀ {bound : ℕ} (tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree), tree.height ≤ bound → ∀ (target : Multiset ℝ) (first second least next : ℝ), first ::ₘ second ::ₘ tree.weights = least ::ₘ next ::ₘ target → least ≤ next → least ≤ first → next ≤ second → ∃ result, result.weights = target ∧ result.pathCost ≤ tree.pathCost + ↑bound * (first - least) + ↑bound * (second - next)
statement:
theorem raisePair {bound : Nat} (tree : HuffmanWeightTree)
    (hheight : tree.height ≤ bound) (target : Multiset Real)
    (first second least next : Real)
    (hweights : first ::ₘ second ::ₘ tree.weights =
      least ::ₘ next ::ₘ target)
    (hleastNext : least ≤ next) (hleastFirst : least ≤ first)
    (hnextSecond : next ≤ second) :
    ∃ result : HuffmanWeightTree,
      result.weights = target ∧
      result.pathCost ≤ tree.pathCost +
        (bound : Real) * (first - least) +
        (bound : Real) * (second - next)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue
signature: (W : Type u) → [LinearOrder W] → ℕ → Type u
statement: structure IndexedMinQueue (W : Type u) [LinearOrder W] (n : Nat)

docstring: Strictly lower the finite key of one present identity and sift it upward.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.decreaseKey
signature: {W : Type u} → [inst : LinearOrder W] → {n : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n → Fin n → W → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM (Fin 5 → ℕ) (Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n))

docstring: DECREASE-KEY rejects absent identities and non-strict decreases.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.decreaseKey_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {W : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder W] {n : ℕ} (q : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n) (v : Fin n) (key : W), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.decreaseKey q v key).ret = Option.none ↔ q.position[v] = Option.none ∨ ∃ i, ∃ (hi : ↑i < q.heap.data.size), q.position[v] = Option.some i ∧ ¬↑key < (ofLex q.heap.data[↑i]).1
statement:
theorem decreaseKey_eq_none_iff {W : Type u} [LinearOrder W] {n : Nat}
    (q : IndexedMinQueue W n) (v : Fin n) (key : W) :
    (decreaseKey q v key).ret = none ↔
      q.position[v] = none ∨
        ∃ (i : Fin n) (hi : i.val < q.heap.data.size),
          q.position[v] = some i ∧
            ¬ (↑key : WithTop W) < (ofLex (q.heap.data[i.val]'hi)).1

docstring: A successful decrease replaces its key and preserves every identity.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.decreaseKey_ret
signature: ∀ {W : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder W] {n : ℕ} (q q' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n) (v : Fin n) (key : W), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.decreaseKey q v key).ret = Option.some q' → (∃ i, ∃ (hi : ↑i < q.heap.data.size), q.position[v] = Option.some i ∧ ↑key < (ofLex q.heap.data[↑i]).1 ∧ q'.heap.data = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.siftUp (q.heap.data.set (↑i) (toLex (↑key, v)) hi) ↑i) ∧ ∀ (w : Fin n), q'.position[w].isSome = q.position[w].isSome
statement:
theorem decreaseKey_ret {W : Type u} [LinearOrder W] {n : Nat}
    (q q' : IndexedMinQueue W n) (v : Fin n) (key : W)
    (h : (decreaseKey q v key).ret = some q') :
    (∃ (i : Fin n) (hi : i.val < q.heap.data.size),
      q.position[v] = some i ∧
        (↑key : WithTop W) < (ofLex (q.heap.data[i.val]'hi)).1 ∧
        q'.heap.data = siftUp
          (q.heap.data.set i.val (toLex ((↑key : WithTop W), v)) hi) i.val) ∧
      ∀ w : Fin n, q'.position[w].isSome = q.position[w].isSome

docstring: Each selected DECREASE-KEY coordinate has the frozen logarithmic bound.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.decreaseKey_time
signature: ∀ {W : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder W] {n : ℕ} (q : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n) (v : Fin n) (key : W) (c : Fin 5), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.decreaseKey q v key).time c ≤ 20 * ((q.heap.data.size + 1).log2 + 1)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.extractMin
signature: {W : Type u} → [inst : LinearOrder W] → {n : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM (Fin 5 → ℕ) (Option (Lex (WithTop W × Fin n) × Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n))
statement:
def extractMin {W : Type u} [LinearOrder W] {n : Nat}
    (q : IndexedMinQueue W n) :
    TimeM (Fin 5 → Nat)
      (Option ((WithTop W ×ₗ Fin n) × IndexedMinQueue W n))

docstring: EXTRACT-MIN rejects exactly an empty heap.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.extractMin_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {W : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder W] {n : ℕ} (q : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.extractMin q).ret = Option.none ↔ q.heap.data.size = 0

docstring: Successful extraction refines canonical extraction and removes only its identity.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.extractMin_ret
signature: ∀ {W : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder W] {n : ℕ} (q q' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n) (entry : Lex (WithTop W × Fin n)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.extractMin q).ret = Option.some (entry, q') → q.heap.extractMin = Option.some (entry, q'.heap) ∧ q'.position[(ofLex entry).2] = Option.none ∧ ∀ (w : Fin n), w ≠ (ofLex entry).2 → q'.position[w].isSome = q.position[w].isSome
statement:
theorem extractMin_ret {W : Type u} [LinearOrder W] {n : Nat}
    (q q' : IndexedMinQueue W n) (entry : WithTop W ×ₗ Fin n)
    (h : (extractMin q).ret = some (entry, q')) :
    q.heap.extractMin = some (entry, q'.heap) ∧
      q'.position[(ofLex entry).2] = none ∧
      ∀ w : Fin n, w ≠ (ofLex entry).2 →
        q'.position[w].isSome = q.position[w].isSome

signature: {W : Type u} → [inst : LinearOrder W] → {n : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n → Fin n → WithTop W → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM (Fin 5 → ℕ) (Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n))

docstring: INSERT rejects exactly the identities already present.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.insert_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {W : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder W] {n : ℕ} (q : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n) (v : Fin n) (key : WithTop W), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.insert q v key).ret = Option.none ↔ q.position[v].isSome = Bool.true

docstring: Successful INSERT refines canonical push and preserves all other identities.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.insert_ret
signature: ∀ {W : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder W] {n : ℕ} (q q' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n) (v : Fin n) (key : WithTop W), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.insert q v key).ret = Option.some q' → q'.heap = q.heap.push (toLex (key, v)) ∧ (∃ i, ∃ (hi : ↑i < q'.heap.data.size), q'.position[v] = Option.some i ∧ q'.heap.data[↑i] = toLex (key, v)) ∧ ∀ (w : Fin n), w ≠ v → q'.position[w].isSome = q.position[w].isSome
statement:
theorem insert_ret {W : Type u} [LinearOrder W] {n : Nat}
    (q q' : IndexedMinQueue W n) (v : Fin n) (key : WithTop W)
    (h : (insert q v key).ret = some q') :
    q'.heap = q.heap.push (toLex (key, v)) ∧
      (∃ (i : Fin n) (hi : i.val < q'.heap.data.size),
        q'.position[v] = some i ∧ q'.heap.data[i.val]'hi = toLex (key, v)) ∧
      ∀ w : Fin n, w ≠ v → q'.position[w].isSome = q.position[w].isSome

signature: ∀ {W : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder W] {n : ℕ} (q : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n) (v : Fin n), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.member q v).time = fun c ↦ if c = 2 then 1 else 0

docstring: An identity is absent exactly when no heap entry carries it.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.position_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {W : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder W] {n : ℕ} (q : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n) (v : Fin n), q.position[v] = Option.none ↔ ¬∃ entry ∈ q.heap.data.toList, (ofLex entry).2 = v

docstring: Source-order repeated INSERT has the frozen summed event bound.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.repeated_insert_time
signature: ∀ {W : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder W] {n : ℕ} (qs : Fin (n + 1) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.IndexedMinQueue W n) (keys : Fin n → WithTop W), qs 0 = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.empty n → (∀ (i : Fin n), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.insert (qs i.castSucc) i (keys i)).ret = Option.some (qs i.succ)) → ∀ (c : Fin 5), ∑ i, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IndexedMinQueue.insert (qs i.castSucc) i (keys i)).time c ≤ 20 * n * ((n + 1).log2 + 1)
statement:
theorem repeated_insert_time {W : Type u} [LinearOrder W] {n : Nat}
    (qs : Fin (n + 1) → IndexedMinQueue W n) (keys : Fin n → WithTop W)
    (hstart : qs 0 = empty (W := W) n)
    (hsteps : ∀ i : Fin n,
      (insert (qs i.castSucc) i (keys i)).ret = some (qs i.succ))
    (c : Fin 5) :
    (∑ i : Fin n, (insert (qs i.castSucc) i (keys i)).time c) ≤
      20 * n * (Nat.log2 (n + 1) + 1)

docstring:
Counts performed by the executable branches of an operation.

The `maxCacheReads` field is deliberately narrow: it counts only the
cached-maximum reads performed by search pruning in `searchWithCost`, one
per visited node where the left subtree's cached maximum decides the
descent. Maintenance paths (`mkNode`, `rebalanceWithCost`, and the
rotations) read cached heights, sizes, and maxima through constructor
patterns while rebuilding nodes; those field projections are not
separately instrumented, and maintenance work is reported through
`cacheWrites`, `rotations`, and the remaining counters instead.

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IntervalTree.IndexedIntervalTree.insert_spec
signature: ∀ {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IntervalTree.IndexedIntervalTree}, tree.Invariant → ∀ {entry : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IntervalTree.Entry}, entry.interval.valid = Bool.true → ∀ {result : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IntervalTree.IndexedIntervalTree}, tree.insert entry = Option.some result → result.Invariant ∧ entry ∈ result.root.entries ∧ ∀ (e : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IntervalTree.Entry), e ∈ result.root.entries ↔ e = entry ∨ e ∈ tree.root.entries ∧ e.id ≠ entry.id
statement:

        e = entry ∨ (e ∈ tree.root.entries ∧ e.id ≠ entry.id)

docstring:
Rebalancing an `mkNode` whose children are balanced and whose child
heights differ by at most two restores AVL balance.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IntervalTree.Tree.balancedProp_rebalance_mkNode
signature: ∀ {l : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IntervalTree.Tree} {e : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IntervalTree.Entry} {r : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IntervalTree.Tree}, l.BalancedProp → r.BalancedProp → l.height ≤ r.height + 2 ∧ r.height ≤ l.height + 2 → (l.mkNode e r).rebalanceWithCost.1.BalancedProp ∧ ((l.mkNode e r).rebalanceWithCost.1.height = Max.max l.height r.height + 1 ∨ (l.mkNode e r).rebalanceWithCost.1.height + 1 = Max.max l.height r.height + 1) ∧ ((l.mkNode e r).rebalanceWithCost.1.height + 1 = Max.max l.height r.height + 1 → l.height = r.height + 2 ∨ r.height = l.height + 2)
statement:
theorem balancedProp_rebalance_mkNode {l : Tree} {e : Entry} {r : Tree}
    (hl : l.BalancedProp) (hr : r.BalancedProp)
    (hbal : l.height ≤ r.height + 2 ∧ r.height ≤ l.height + 2) :
    (rebalanceWithCost (mkNode l e r)).1.BalancedProp ∧
      ((rebalanceWithCost (mkNode l e r)).1.height =
          max l.height r.height + 1 ∨
        (rebalanceWithCost (mkNode l e r)).1.height + 1 =
          max l.height r.height + 1) ∧
      ((rebalanceWithCost (mkNode l e r)).1.height + 1 =
          max l.height r.height + 1 →
        l.height = r.height + 2 ∨ r.height = l.height + 2)

docstring:

docstring: A singleton search records its short-circuit endpoint count and any empty visit.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IntervalTree.Tree.searchWithCost_singleton
signature: ∀ (entry : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IntervalTree.Entry) (query : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IntervalTree.Interval), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IntervalTree.Tree.searchWithCost query (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.IntervalTree.Tree.singleton entry) = if entry.interval.overlaps query = Bool.true then (Option.some entry, { nodeVisits := 1, endpointComparisons := if entry.interval.low ≤ query.high then 2 else 1 }) else (Option.none, { nodeVisits := 2, endpointComparisons := if entry.interval.low ≤ query.high then 2 else 1 })
statement:
theorem searchWithCost_singleton (entry : Entry) (query : Interval) :
    searchWithCost query (singleton entry) =
      if entry.interval.overlaps query then
        (some entry,
          { nodeVisits := 1
            endpointComparisons := if entry.interval.low ≤ query.high then 2 else 1 })
      else
        (none,
          { nodeVisits := 2
            endpointComparisons := if entry.interval.low ≤ query.high then 2 else 1 })

docstring: The orthogonal range report for the box `[lo, hi]`; see `reportAux`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.KdTree.report
signature: {d : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.KdTree d → (Fin d → ℤ) → (Fin d → ℤ) → List (Fin d → ℤ)
statement: def report (t : KdTree d) (lo hi : Fin d → Int) : List (Fin d → Int)

docstring:
Accumulator form of the orthogonal range report: `reportAux t lo hi acc`
prepends the reported points (in left-to-right order) onto `acc`. The
accumulator avoids repeatedly appending left results, so constructing the
output list costs only work linear in the number of reported points; the
traversal itself still visits every node that pruning does not cut, which
can be the whole tree even for an empty report, and no complexity bound is
proved here. At a split node with axis `a` and value `s`, the left child is
pruned when `s < lo a` and the right child is pruned when `hi a < s`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.KdTree.reportAux
signature: {d : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.KdTree d → (Fin d → ℤ) → (Fin d → ℤ) → List (Fin d → ℤ) → List (Fin d → ℤ)
statement:
def reportAux : KdTree d → (Fin d → Int) → (Fin d → Int) →
    List (Fin d → Int) → List (Fin d → Int)

docstring: The accumulator report of a valid tree is its filtered point list on `acc`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.KdTree.reportAux_eq_filter_append
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.KdTree d}, t.Valid → ∀ (lo hi : Fin d → ℤ) (acc : List (Fin d → ℤ)), t.reportAux lo hi acc = List.filter (fun p ↦ Decidable.decide (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.KdTree.inBox lo hi p)) t.toList ++ acc
statement:
theorem reportAux_eq_filter_append {t : KdTree d} (h : t.Valid)
    (lo hi : Fin d → Int) (acc : List (Fin d → Int)) :
    t.reportAux lo hi acc =
      t.toList.filter (fun p => inBox lo hi p) ++ acc

theorem report_build [NeZero d] (a : Fin d) (pts : List (Fin d → Int))
    (lo hi : Fin d → Int) :
    (build a pts).report lo hi =
      (build a pts).toList.filter (fun p => inBox lo hi p)

docstring: Each accepted edge has minimum weight among all edges crossing the current partition.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Kruskal.kruskal_light_edge
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (graph : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Kruskal.Graph n) (before : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Kruskal.WeightedEdge n)) (edge : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Kruskal.WeightedEdge n) (after : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Kruskal.WeightedEdge n)), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Kruskal.orderedEdges graph = before ++ edge :: after → ¬Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Kruskal.scan { forest := Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Kruskal.initialForest n, chosenRev := [] } before).forest edge.source edge.target → ∀ candidate ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Kruskal.validEdges graph, ¬Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Kruskal.scan { forest := Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Kruskal.initialForest n, chosenRev := [] } before).forest candidate.source candidate.target → edge.weight ≤ candidate.weight
statement:
public theorem kruskal_light_edge {n : Nat} (graph : Graph n)
    (before : List (WeightedEdge n)) (edge : WeightedEdge n)
    (after : List (WeightedEdge n))
    (decomposition : orderedEdges graph = before ++ edge :: after)
    (separated :
      ¬Equivalent (scan ⟨initialForest n, []⟩ before).forest edge.source edge.target)
    (candidate : WeightedEdge n) (inValid : candidate ∈ validEdges graph)
    (crossing :
      ¬Equivalent (scan ⟨initialForest n, []⟩ before).forest
        candidate.source candidate.target) :
    edge.weight ≤ candidate.weight

docstring:
The state invariant bundle used below: the vertex lists of the represented
trees are collectively duplicate-free (so the trees are vertex-disjoint), and
the preferred edges are a functional set of represented directed edges: no
duplicates, every preferred edge is a parent-child edge of some represented
tree, and each vertex has at most one preferred child. The duplicate-free
vertex condition also pins down the parent of each vertex, so the maximal
solid chains (`treePaths`) are genuine disjoint paths.

signature: {V : Type u} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V → Prop
statement: public def Valid (s : State V) : Prop

docstring:
Access preserves the state invariant: the new preferred edges are the
retained off-path edges together with the edges of the accessed root path;
the two groups have disjoint parent endpoints (off versus on the path), so
duplicate-freeness and the at-most-one-preferred-child condition carry over.
