statement: public theorem Valid.access {x : V} (hs : s.Valid) : (State.access x s).Valid

docstring:
Cutting preserves the state invariant: pruning partitions the cut
tree's vertex list into remainder plus detached subtree up to permutation
(`perm_vertices_pruneAt`), the rest of the forest is untouched, and the
preferred edges are reset.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.Valid.cut
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x : V}, s.Valid → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cut x s).Valid
statement: public theorem Valid.cut {x : V} (hs : s.Valid) : (State.cut x s).Valid

docstring:
Edge cutting preserves the state invariant: on an adjacent pair it is
the composite of `makeRoot` and `cut`, and otherwise it only resets the
preferred path.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.Valid.cutEdge
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x y : V}, s.Valid → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cutEdge x y s).Valid
statement:
public theorem Valid.cutEdge {x y : V} (hs : s.Valid) :
    (State.cutEdge x y s).Valid

docstring:
Linking preserves the state invariant: the joined tree has the union
of the two old vertex lists up to permutation (rerooting and grafting both
permute), the rest of the forest is untouched, and the preferred path is
reset.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.Valid.link
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x y : V}, s.Valid → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.link x y s).Valid
statement:
public theorem Valid.link {x y : V} (hs : s.Valid) :
    (State.link x y s).Valid

docstring:
Rerooting preserves the state invariant: the new forest has the same
flat vertex list as the old one up to permutation (the rerooted tree
replaces its original), and the preferred edges are reset.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.Valid.makeRoot
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x : V}, s.Valid → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.makeRoot x s).Valid
statement:
public theorem Valid.makeRoot {x : V} (hs : s.Valid) :
    (State.makeRoot x s).Valid

docstring:
Make the path from the represented root to `x` preferred, as in the
textbook `access`. Every edge of the root-to-`x` path becomes solid, the
previously preferred child edge of each vertex on that path is dropped
(made dashed), and every preferred edge whose parent endpoint lies off the
path is retained: this is what keeps off-path preferred paths alive across
accesses (for example, with root `1`, children `2 → 4` and `3 → 5`,
`access 5` after `access 4` keeps the preferred path `[2, 4]`, since the
edge `2`-`4` has parent endpoint off the `1`-`3`-`5` path; see the
regression tests in `LinkCutTreeTests`). The represented forest is
unchanged. On a vertex outside the forest this is the identity.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.access
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V
statement: public def access (x : V) (s : State V) : State V

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.access_eq_of_findTree_rootPath
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V} {p : List V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree x s.forest = Option.some t → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath x t = Option.some p → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.access x s = { forest := s.forest, preferred := List.filter (fun e ↦ Decidable.decide (e.1 ∉ p)) s.preferred ++ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pathEdges p }
statement:
public theorem access_eq_of_findTree_rootPath {x : V} {t : Tree V} {p : List V}
    (hft : findTree x s.forest = some t) (hrp : rootPath x t = some p) :
    access x s =
      ⟨s.forest, (s.preferred.filter (fun e => e.1 ∉ p)) ++ pathEdges p⟩

docstring: Access changes only the preferred edges, never the represented forest.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.access_forest
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} (x : V), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.access x s).forest = s.forest
statement: public theorem access_forest (x : V) : (access x s).forest = s.forest

docstring:
After `access x` in a valid state, the root-to-`x` path of the tree
containing `x` is one of the preferred paths of the decomposition, and
`x` is its last (deepest) vertex: `p.getLast? = some x`. No auxiliary
splay tree is modeled, so no claim is made about a splay-tree root. This
is only the endpoint property of the accessed preferred path. Other
preferred paths off that root path are retained (`mem_preferred_access`).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.access_last
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x : V}, s.Valid → s.Mem x → ∃ p ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.access x s).paths, p.getLast? = Option.some x ∧ ∃ t ∈ s.forest, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath x t = Option.some p

docstring:
An edge cut retains every other edge: in a valid state, after
`cutEdge x y` on an adjacent pair, every represented edge other than
`x`-`y` itself is still an edge of some represented tree. Edges of other
trees pass through untouched; edges of the cut tree survive the
rerooting (`adjacent_rerootAt`) and then lie on one side of the prune,
where they are kept by `adjacent_pruneAt_of_mem_mem` (remainder side) or
`adjacent_findSubtree_of_mem_mem` (detached side); the only edge
crossing the prune is `x`-`y` (`adjacent_node_crossing`).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.adjacent_cutEdge
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x y a b : V}, s.Valid → (∃ t ∈ s.forest, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent x y t) → (∃ t ∈ s.forest, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b t) → ¬(a = x ∧ b = y ∨ a = y ∧ b = x) → ∃ t ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cutEdge x y s).forest, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b t
statement:
public theorem adjacent_cutEdge {x y a b : V} (hs : s.Valid)
    (hadj : ∃ t ∈ s.forest, Adjacent x y t)
    (hab : ∃ t ∈ s.forest, Adjacent a b t)
    (hxy : ¬ ((a = x ∧ b = y) ∨ (a = y ∧ b = x))) :
    ∃ t ∈ (cutEdge x y s).forest, Adjacent a b t

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.connected_access_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x y z : V}, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.access x s).Connected y z ↔ s.Connected y z
statement:
public theorem connected_access_iff {x y z : V} :
    (access x s).Connected y z ↔ s.Connected y z

docstring:
Connectivity can equally be read off the Euler tours of the represented
trees.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.connected_iff_tour
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x y : V}, s.Connected x y ↔ ∃ t ∈ s.forest, x ∈ t.tour ∧ y ∈ t.tour
statement:
public theorem connected_iff_tour {x y : V} :
    s.Connected x y ↔ ∃ t ∈ s.forest, x ∈ Tree.tour t ∧ y ∈ Tree.tour t

docstring:
A link connects its endpoints: after `link x y`, `x` and `y` lie in one
represented tree. No invariant on the state is needed.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.connected_link
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x y : V}, s.Mem x → s.Mem y → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.link x y s).Connected x y
statement:
public theorem connected_link {x y : V} (hx : s.Mem x) (hy : s.Mem y) :
    (link x y s).Connected x y

docstring:
`makeRoot x` keeps `x` connected to exactly the vertices it was
connected to: rerooting spans the same vertex set as the old tree (and,
by `rerootAt`, the same undirected edges). Vertex disjointness is the
side condition that pins down which tree that is.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.connected_makeRoot
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x y : V}, s.Valid → s.Connected x y → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.makeRoot x s).Connected x y
statement:
public theorem connected_makeRoot {x y : V} (hs : s.Valid)
    (h : s.Connected x y) : (makeRoot x s).Connected x y

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.connected_refl_of_mem
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x : V}, s.Mem x → s.Connected x x
statement: public theorem connected_refl_of_mem {x : V} (h : s.Mem x) : s.Connected x x

docstring:
Detach the subtree rooted at `x` from its represented tree (the rooted
`cut`): the result contains the detached subtree itself, rooted at `x`,
and the remainder of the old tree with that subtree pruned off
(`pruneAt`), keeping every remaining edge. When `x` is the root of its
tree the remainder is empty and only the detached tree remains. Preferred
edges are reset.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cut
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V
statement: public def cut (x : V) (s : State V) : State V

docstring:
Undirected edge cut, the textbook composite: reroot at `x`
(`makeRoot x`, which reverses only the root-to-`x` path and keeps every
undirected edge), then detach the subtree rooted at `y`. When `x` and `y`
are joined by an edge of a valid represented tree, the rerooting makes
`y` the root of a child subtree of `x`, so the rooted `cut y` splits the
component into the two sides of the edge `x`-`y`
(`not_connected_cutEdge`), and every other edge is retained
(`adjacent_cutEdge`); the branched-tree tests in `LinkCutTreeTests`
exhibit this on concrete forests.

The adjacency precondition is checked, not assumed: the composite runs
only when some represented tree has `x` and `y` adjacent
(`adjacentB_eq_true_iff`). Without that guard the bare composite would
cut at `y` regardless of `x` (for instance `cutEdge 99 2` on the chain
`1 → 2` would detach `2` although there is no `99`-`2` edge). When no
represented tree has the edge, `cutEdge x y` leaves the forest unchanged
(`cutEdge_eq_of_not_adjacent`); as with the other structural operations,
the preferred edges are reset either way.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cutEdge
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → V → V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V
statement: public def cutEdge (x y : V) (s : State V) : State V

docstring:
On an adjacent pair, `cutEdge` is the textbook composite `cut y`
after `makeRoot x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cutEdge_eq_cut_makeRoot_of_adjacent
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x y : V}, (∃ t ∈ s.forest, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent x y t) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cutEdge x y s = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cut y (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.makeRoot x s)

docstring:
On a non-adjacent pair, `cutEdge` does not touch the forest: there is
no `x`-`y` edge to remove, and in particular no other edge at `y` is cut.
Only the preferred edges are reset, as for every structural operation.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cutEdge_eq_of_not_adjacent
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x y : V}, (¬∃ t ∈ s.forest, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent x y t) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cutEdge x y s = { forest := s.forest, preferred := [] }

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cutEdge_preferred
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} (x y : V), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cutEdge x y s).preferred = []
statement:
public theorem cutEdge_preferred (x y : V) :
    (cutEdge x y s).preferred = []

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cut_forest_eq_none
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x : V} {t sub : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree x s.forest = Option.some t → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findSubtree x t = Option.some sub → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pruneAt x t = Option.none → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cut x s).forest = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.removeTree x s.forest ++ [sub]
statement:
public theorem cut_forest_eq_none {x : V} {t sub : Tree V}
    (hft : findTree x s.forest = some t) (hsub : findSubtree x t = some sub)
    (hprune : pruneAt x t = none) :
    (cut x s).forest = removeTree x s.forest ++ [sub]

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cut_forest_eq_some
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x : V} {t sub rem : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree x s.forest = Option.some t → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findSubtree x t = Option.some sub → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pruneAt x t = Option.some rem → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cut x s).forest = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.removeTree x s.forest ++ [rem, sub]
statement:
public theorem cut_forest_eq_some {x : V} {t sub rem : Tree V}
    (hft : findTree x s.forest = some t) (hsub : findSubtree x t = some sub)
    (hprune : pruneAt x t = some rem) :
    (cut x s).forest = removeTree x s.forest ++ [rem, sub]

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cut_preferred
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} (x : V), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cut x s).preferred = []
statement: public theorem cut_preferred (x : V) : (cut x s).preferred = []

docstring:
Every preferred path is a genuine path of the represented forest:
consecutive vertices are joined by a parent-child edge of one represented
tree (`isChain_of_mem_treePaths`). This holds for every state, with no
validity hypothesis.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.isChain_of_mem_paths
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {p : List V}, p ∈ s.paths → List.IsChain (fun a b ↦ ∃ t ∈ s.forest, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b t) p
statement:
public theorem isChain_of_mem_paths {p : List V} (hp : p ∈ paths s) :
    p.IsChain (fun a b => ∃ t ∈ s.forest, Adjacent a b t)

docstring:
Link the represented trees of `x` and `y` with the new edge `x`-`y`,
as in the textbook operation: the tree of `x` is first rerooted at `x`
(`rerootAt`, so `x` becomes its root with every old edge kept) and then
grafted as a new child subtree of `y` (`graftAt`), adding exactly the edge
from `y` to `x`. Linking two vertices of the same tree, or a vertex
outside the forest, leaves the forest unchanged. Preferred edges are
reset.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.link
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → V → V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V
statement: public def link (x y : V) (s : State V) : State V

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.link_forest_eq
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x y : V} {tx ty tx' tj : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree x s.forest = Option.some tx → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree y s.forest = Option.some ty → x ∉ ty.vertices → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rerootAt x tx = Option.some tx' → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.graftAt y tx' ty = Option.some tj → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.link x y s).forest = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.removeTree x (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.removeTree y s.forest) ++ [tj]
statement:
public theorem link_forest_eq {x y : V} {tx ty tx' tj : Tree V}
    (hftx : findTree x s.forest = some tx)
    (hfty : findTree y s.forest = some ty)
    (hxy : x ∉ Tree.vertices ty)
    (hreroot : rerootAt x tx = some tx')
    (hgraft : graftAt y tx' ty = some tj) :
    (link x y s).forest = removeTree x (removeTree y s.forest) ++ [tj]

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.link_preferred
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} (x y : V), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.link x y s).preferred = []
statement: public theorem link_preferred (x y : V) : (link x y s).preferred = []

docstring:
Reroot the represented tree containing `x` at `x` (`rerootAt`): the
edges on the path from the old root to `x` are reversed and every other
edge is kept, so the undirected represented tree is unchanged. Preferred
edges are reset (all dashed). On a vertex outside the forest this only
resets the preferred edges.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.makeRoot
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V
statement: public def makeRoot (x : V) (s : State V) : State V

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.makeRoot_forest_eq
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x : V} {t t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree x s.forest = Option.some t → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rerootAt x t = Option.some t' → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.makeRoot x s).forest = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.removeTree x s.forest ++ [t']

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.makeRoot_preferred
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} (x : V), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.makeRoot x s).preferred = []
statement: public theorem makeRoot_preferred (x : V) : (makeRoot x s).preferred = []

docstring:
After `makeRoot x`, some represented tree is rooted at `x` and has `x`
as a vertex: the rerooted old tree of `x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.makeRoot_root
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x : V}, s.Mem x → ∃ t ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.makeRoot x s).forest, t.root = x ∧ x ∈ t.vertices
statement:
public theorem makeRoot_root {x : V} (hx : s.Mem x) :
    ∃ t ∈ (makeRoot x s).forest, t.root = x ∧ x ∈ Tree.vertices t

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.mem_access_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x y : V}, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.access x s).Mem y ↔ s.Mem y
statement: public theorem mem_access_iff {x y : V} : (access x s).Mem y ↔ s.Mem y

docstring:
After `cut x`, the detached subtree occurs in the forest with root
`x`, so `x` itself remains a vertex, as does every vertex of its old tree
on the other side of the cut. The duplicate-free hypothesis is the
validity side condition under which pruning partitions the vertex set
(`mem_vertices_pruneAt_of_mem_not_mem`).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.mem_cut
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x y : V} {t sub : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, t.vertices.Nodup → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree x s.forest = Option.some t → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findSubtree x t = Option.some sub → y ∈ t.vertices → y ∉ sub.vertices → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cut x s).Mem x ∧ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cut x s).Mem y
statement:
public theorem mem_cut {x y : V} {t sub : Tree V}
    (hnodup : (Tree.vertices t).Nodup)
    (hft : findTree x s.forest = some t) (hsub : findSubtree x t = some sub)
    (hy : y ∈ Tree.vertices t) (hy' : y ∉ Tree.vertices sub) :
    (cut x s).Mem x ∧ (cut x s).Mem y

docstring:
The decomposition partitions the vertex set of the represented forest:
a vertex lies on some preferred path exactly when it is in the forest. This
holds for every state, with no validity hypothesis.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.mem_paths_flatMap
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {v : V}, v ∈ List.flatMap id s.paths ↔ v ∈ List.flatMap Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.vertices s.forest
statement:
public theorem mem_paths_flatMap {v : V} :
    v ∈ (paths s).flatMap id ↔ v ∈ s.forest.flatMap Tree.vertices

docstring:
An off-path preferred edge survives `access x`: an edge whose parent
endpoint does not lie on the root-to-`x` path is retained. This is the
edge-level statement behind retaining off-path preferred paths.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.mem_preferred_access
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x : V} {e : V × V}, e ∈ s.preferred → (∀ (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V) (p : List V), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree x s.forest = Option.some t → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath x t = Option.some p → e.1 ∉ p) → e ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.access x s).preferred
statement:
public theorem mem_preferred_access {x : V} {e : V × V}
    (he : e ∈ s.preferred)
    (h : ∀ t p, findTree x s.forest = some t → rootPath x t = some p →
      e.1 ∉ p) :
    e ∈ (access x s).preferred

docstring: Every edge of the accessed root path is preferred after `access x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.mem_preferred_access_of_mem_pathEdges
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V} {p : List V} {e : V × V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree x s.forest = Option.some t → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath x t = Option.some p → e ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pathEdges p → e ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.access x s).preferred
statement:
public theorem mem_preferred_access_of_mem_pathEdges {x : V} {t : Tree V}
    {p : List V} {e : V × V} (hft : findTree x s.forest = some t)
    (hrp : rootPath x t = some p) (he : e ∈ pathEdges p) :
    e ∈ (access x s).preferred

docstring: Every preferred path of a valid state has distinct vertices.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.nodup_of_mem_paths
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {p : List V}, s.Valid → p ∈ s.paths → p.Nodup
statement:
public theorem nodup_of_mem_paths {p : List V} (hs : s.Valid)
    (hp : p ∈ paths s) : p.Nodup

docstring:
The flattened decomposition is duplicate-free: every vertex of a valid
state lies on exactly one preferred path. With `mem_paths_flatMap`, the
paths partition the vertex set.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.nodup_paths_flatMap
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V}, s.Valid → (List.flatMap id s.paths).Nodup
statement:
public theorem nodup_paths_flatMap (hs : s.Valid) :
    ((paths s).flatMap id).Nodup

docstring:
A cut separates: after `cut x`, `x` is no longer connected to any
vertex of its old tree that lies outside the subtree rooted at `x`. No
invariant on the state is needed: `x` cannot occur in the pruned
remainder (`mem_vertices_pruneAt`).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.not_connected_cut
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x y : V} {t sub : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree x s.forest = Option.some t → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findSubtree x t = Option.some sub → y ∉ sub.vertices → ¬(Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cut x s).Connected x y
statement:
public theorem not_connected_cut {x y : V} {t sub : Tree V}
    (hft : findTree x s.forest = some t) (hsub : findSubtree x t = some sub)
    (hy : y ∉ Tree.vertices sub) :
    ¬ (cut x s).Connected x y

docstring:
An edge cut separates its endpoints: in a valid state, after
`cutEdge x y` on an adjacent pair, `x` and `y` lie in different
represented trees. Rerooting at `x` keeps the edge (`adjacent_rerootAt`)
and makes the subtree at `y` root-free of `x`, so the rooted separation
theorem `not_connected_cut` applies.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.not_connected_cutEdge
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V} {x y : V}, s.Valid → (∃ t ∈ s.forest, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent x y t) → ¬(Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.cutEdge x y s).Connected x y

docstring: Distinct preferred paths of a valid state are vertex-disjoint.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.pairwise_disjoint_paths
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V}, s.Valid → List.Pairwise List.Disjoint s.paths
statement:
public theorem pairwise_disjoint_paths (hs : s.Valid) :
    (paths s).Pairwise List.Disjoint

docstring:
The preferred-path decomposition of a state: in each represented tree,
the maximal chains of preferred edges (`treePaths`), deepest continuation
last within each path. Vertices incident to no preferred edge are singleton
paths. Unlike a single distinguished path, this retains the preferred paths
of every subtree: only edges incident to the latest accessed root path
change under `access`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.paths
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V → List (List V)
statement: public def paths (s : State V) : List (List V)

docstring:
A state with no preferred edges is valid exactly when its forest is
duplicate-free. This is the invariant after every structural operation,
which resets all edges to dashed.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State.valid_of_preferred_nil
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} {s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.State V}, s.preferred = [] → (List.flatMap Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.vertices s.forest).Nodup → s.Valid
statement:
public theorem valid_of_preferred_nil (hpre : s.preferred = [])
    (h : (s.forest.flatMap Tree.vertices).Nodup) : s.Valid

docstring:
Computable adjacency test: `adjacentB a b t = true` exactly when
`Adjacent a b t` (`adjacentB_eq_true_iff`). This is the guard evaluated by
`State.cutEdge` before it cuts.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.adjacentB
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → V → V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → Bool
statement: public def adjacentB (a b : V) : Tree V → Bool

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.adjacentB_eq_true_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {a b : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.adjacentB a b t = Bool.true ↔ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b t
statement:
public theorem adjacentB_eq_true_iff {a b : V} :
    ∀ {t : Tree V}, adjacentB a b t = true ↔ Adjacent a b t

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.adjacentList_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} {a b : V} {cs : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent.AdjacentList a b cs ↔ ∃ c ∈ cs, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b c

docstring:
Grafting keeps every old edge and every edge of the new child, and adds
exactly the edge from `y` to the root of `newChild`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.adjacent_graftAt
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {y a b : V} {newChild t t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.graftAt y newChild t = Option.some t' → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b t' ↔ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b t ∨ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b newChild ∨ a = y ∧ b = newChild.root ∨ a = newChild.root ∧ b = y)
statement:
public theorem adjacent_graftAt {y a b : V} {newChild : Tree V} :
    ∀ {t t' : Tree V}, graftAt y newChild t = some t' →
      (Adjacent a b t' ↔ Adjacent a b t ∨ Adjacent a b newChild ∨
        (a = y ∧ b = newChild.root) ∨ (a = newChild.root ∧ b = y))

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.adjacent_node
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} {a b r : V} {cs : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.node r cs) ↔ (r = a ∧ ∃ c ∈ cs, c.root = b) ∨ (r = b ∧ ∃ c ∈ cs, c.root = a) ∨ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent.AdjacentList a b cs
statement:
public theorem adjacent_node {a b r : V} {cs : List (Tree V)} :
    Adjacent a b (.node r cs) ↔
      (r = a ∧ ∃ c ∈ cs, c.root = b) ∨ (r = b ∧ ∃ c ∈ cs, c.root = a) ∨
        Adjacent.AdjacentList a b cs

docstring:
Pruning keeps every edge whose endpoints survive: in a duplicate-free
tree, an edge of the original tree with both endpoints in the pruned
remainder is an edge of the remainder. Together with
`mem_vertices_pruneAt` (which gives the converse inclusion of vertices)
this specifies `pruneAt` at edge level on the surviving vertices.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.adjacent_pruneAt_of_mem_mem
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {a b x : V} {t t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, t.vertices.Nodup → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pruneAt x t = Option.some t' → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b t → a ∈ t'.vertices → b ∈ t'.vertices → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b t'
statement:
public theorem adjacent_pruneAt_of_mem_mem {a b x : V} :
    ∀ {t t' : Tree V}, (Tree.vertices t).Nodup →
      pruneAt x t = some t' → Adjacent a b t →
      a ∈ Tree.vertices t' → b ∈ Tree.vertices t' →
      Adjacent a b t'

docstring:
Rerooting a duplicate-free tree keeps every undirected edge: the
rerooted tree has exactly the same adjacency relation as the original.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.adjacent_rerootAt
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x a b : V} {t t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, t.vertices.Nodup → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rerootAt x t = Option.some t' → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b t' ↔ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b t)

docstring:
The preferred-path decomposition of one represented tree, given a list
of preferred (solid) edges `edges` directed from parent to preferred child.
Returns `(down, rest)`: `down` is the preferred path starting at the root of
the tree and following preferred edges downward, and `rest` is the list of
all other preferred paths of the tree. When a node has several preferred
children in `edges` (excluded in valid states by the at-most-one condition),
the first one in child order extends the downward path and the others head
their own paths in `rest`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.decomp
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → List (V × V) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → List V × List (List V)
statement: public def decomp (edges : List (V × V)) : Tree V → List V × List (List V)

docstring:
The downward path installed by the access edge update: when the edge
list `E` contains exactly the edges of the root-to-`x` path at vertices of
that path, the decomposition of the tree has that whole root path as its
downward preferred path.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.decomp_fst_eq_rootPath
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {E : List (V × V)} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V} {p : List V}, t.vertices.Nodup → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath x t = Option.some p → (∀ e ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pathEdges p, e ∈ E) → (∀ e ∈ E, e.1 ∈ p → e ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pathEdges p) → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.decomp E t).1 = p
statement:
public theorem decomp_fst_eq_rootPath {x : V} {E : List (V × V)} :
    ∀ {t : Tree V} {p : List V}, (Tree.vertices t).Nodup →
      rootPath x t = some p →
      (∀ e ∈ pathEdges p, e ∈ E) →
      (∀ e ∈ E, e.1 ∈ p → e ∈ pathEdges p) →
      (decomp E t).1 = p

docstring: The downward preferred path of a tree starts at the root of the tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.decomp_fst_head?
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] (edges : List (V × V)) (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.decomp edges t).1.head? = Option.some t.root
statement:
public theorem decomp_fst_head? (edges : List (V × V)) (t : Tree V) :
    (decomp edges t).1.head? = some t.root

docstring:
Every path in the decomposition of a tree is a genuine path of the
tree: consecutive vertices are joined by a parent-child edge.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.decomp_isChain
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] (edges : List (V × V)) (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), List.IsChain (fun a b ↦ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b t) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.decomp edges t).1 ∧ ∀ p ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.decomp edges t).2, List.IsChain (fun a b ↦ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b t) p

docstring:
The decomposition of a tree partitions its vertices: the flattened
paths are a permutation of the vertex list, for every preferred-edge list.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.decomp_perm
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] (edges : List (V × V)) (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), ((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.decomp edges t).1 ++ List.flatMap id (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.decomp edges t).2).Perm t.vertices

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.exists_mem_ofVertexList
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} {l : List V}, l ≠ [] → ∃ t ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.ofVertexList l, t.vertices = l
statement:
public theorem exists_mem_ofVertexList {l : List V} (hl : l ≠ []) :
    ∃ t ∈ ofVertexList l, Tree.vertices t = l

docstring:
The subtree rooted at `x`, if `x` occurs in the tree: the first such
subtree in preorder.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findSubtree
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)
statement: public def findSubtree (x : V) : Tree V → Option (Tree V)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findSubtree_eq_none_of_not_mem
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, x ∉ t.vertices → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findSubtree x t = Option.none
statement:
public theorem findSubtree_eq_none_of_not_mem {x : V} {t : Tree V}
    (hx : x ∉ Tree.vertices t) : findSubtree x t = none

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findSubtree_eq_some_of_mem
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, x ∈ t.vertices → ∃ s, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findSubtree x t = Option.some s
statement:
public theorem findSubtree_eq_some_of_mem {x : V} {t : Tree V}
    (hx : x ∈ Tree.vertices t) : ∃ s, findSubtree x t = some s

docstring: The first tree of a forest whose vertices contain `x`, if any.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → V → List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V) → Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)
statement: public def findTree (x : V) : List (Tree V) → Option (Tree V)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree_eq_some_of_exists
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {f : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)}, (∃ t ∈ f, x ∈ t.vertices) → ∃ t, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree x f = Option.some t ∧ t ∈ f ∧ x ∈ t.vertices

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree_eq_some_spec
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {f : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree x f = Option.some t → t ∈ f ∧ x ∈ t.vertices

docstring: The deepest vertex of a root path (its last entry) is the target vertex.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.getLast?_rootPath
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V} {p : List V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath x t = Option.some p → p.getLast? = Option.some x
statement:
public theorem getLast?_rootPath {x : V} {t : Tree V} {p : List V}
    (h : rootPath x t = some p) : p.getLast? = some x

docstring:
Attach `newChild` as a new last child of the node labelled `y`, keeping
every existing node and edge. Returns `none` when `y` does not occur. This
is the tree surgery behind `State.link`: it adds exactly the edge from `y`
to the root of `newChild`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.graftAt
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)
statement: public def graftAt (y : V) (newChild : Tree V) : Tree V → Option (Tree V)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.graftAt_eq_some_of_mem
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {y : V} {newChild t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, y ∈ t.vertices → ∃ t', Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.graftAt y newChild t = Option.some t'
statement:
public theorem graftAt_eq_some_of_mem {y : V} {newChild t : Tree V}
    (hy : y ∈ Tree.vertices t) : ∃ t', graftAt y newChild t = some t'

docstring: The first vertex of a root path is the root of the tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.head?_rootPath
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V} {p : List V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath x t = Option.some p → p.head? = Option.some t.root
statement:
public theorem head?_rootPath {x : V} {t : Tree V} {p : List V}
    (h : rootPath x t = some p) : p.head? = some t.root

docstring:
Consecutive vertices of a root path are joined by a parent-child edge
of the tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.isChain_adjacent_rootPath
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V} {p : List V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath x t = Option.some p → List.IsChain (fun a b ↦ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b t) p

docstring: Every preferred path of a tree is a genuine path of the tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.isChain_of_mem_treePaths
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {edges : List (V × V)} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V} {p : List V}, p ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.treePaths edges t → List.IsChain (fun a b ↦ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.Adjacent a b t) p

docstring:
Consecutive vertices of a root path are joined by a directed
parent-child edge of the tree, from parent to child.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.isChain_parentChild_rootPath
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V} {p : List V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath x t = Option.some p → List.IsChain (fun a b ↦ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.ParentChild a b t) p

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.mem_removeTree
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {f : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, t ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.removeTree x f ↔ t ∈ f ∧ x ∉ t.vertices

docstring: Every vertex on a root path is a vertex of the tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.mem_rootPath
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x v : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V} {p : List V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath x t = Option.some p → v ∈ p → v ∈ t.vertices
statement:
public theorem mem_rootPath {x v : V} {t : Tree V} {p : List V}
    (h : rootPath x t = some p) (hv : v ∈ p) : v ∈ Tree.vertices t

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.mem_vertices_findSubtree
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x v : V} {t s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findSubtree x t = Option.some s → v ∈ s.vertices → v ∈ t.vertices
statement:
public theorem mem_vertices_findSubtree {x v : V} {t s : Tree V}
    (h : findSubtree x t = some s) (hv : v ∈ Tree.vertices s) : v ∈ Tree.vertices t

docstring:
Grafting keeps every old vertex and adds exactly the vertices of the
new child.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.mem_vertices_graftAt
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {y v : V} {newChild t t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.graftAt y newChild t = Option.some t' → (v ∈ t'.vertices ↔ v ∈ t.vertices ∨ v ∈ newChild.vertices)

docstring:
Every vertex of the pruned tree was already a vertex of the original
tree, and `x` itself is gone.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.mem_vertices_pruneAt
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x v : V} {t t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pruneAt x t = Option.some t' → v ∈ t'.vertices → v ∈ t.vertices ∧ v ≠ x

docstring:
The vertices on the other side of a prune survive: in a duplicate-free
(valid) tree, every vertex outside the detached subtree at `x` is a vertex
of the pruned remainder. Together with `mem_vertices_pruneAt` this says
pruning partitions the vertex set of a valid tree into the detached
subtree and the remainder, keeping all remaining edges.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.mem_vertices_pruneAt_of_mem_not_mem
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x v : V} {t sub t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, t.vertices.Nodup → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findSubtree x t = Option.some sub → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pruneAt x t = Option.some t' → v ∈ t.vertices → v ∉ sub.vertices → v ∈ t'.vertices
statement:
public theorem mem_vertices_pruneAt_of_mem_not_mem {x v : V} :
    ∀ {t sub t' : Tree V}, (Tree.vertices t).Nodup →
      findSubtree x t = some sub → pruneAt x t = some t' →
      v ∈ Tree.vertices t → v ∉ Tree.vertices sub →
      v ∈ Tree.vertices t'

docstring: Rerooting keeps exactly the same vertex set.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.mem_vertices_rerootAt
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x v : V} {t t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rerootAt x t = Option.some t' → (v ∈ t'.vertices ↔ v ∈ t.vertices)

docstring: A root path in a duplicate-free tree has distinct vertices.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.nodup_rootPath
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V} {p : List V}, t.vertices.Nodup → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath x t = Option.some p → p.Nodup

docstring:
The spine over a vertex list, as a one-element forest, or the empty forest
for the empty list.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.ofVertexList
signature: {V : Type u} → List V → List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)
statement: public def ofVertexList : List V → List (Tree V)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.parentChildList_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} {a b : V} {cs : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.ParentChild.ParentChildList a b cs ↔ ∃ c ∈ cs, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.ParentChild a b c

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.parentChild_node
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} {a b r : V} {cs : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.ParentChild a b (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.node r cs) ↔ (r = a ∧ ∃ c ∈ cs, c.root = b) ∨ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.ParentChild.ParentChildList a b cs

docstring:
The directed edges of a vertex path: consecutive pairs, parent first.
The preferred edges installed by `access x` are `pathEdges` of the
root-to-`x` path.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pathEdges
signature: {V : Type u} → List V → List (V × V)
statement: public def pathEdges : List V → List (V × V)

docstring:
Removing the (unique, by duplicate-freeness) tree containing `x` from a
forest splits its flat vertex list into the remainder plus that tree, up
to permutation.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.perm_flatMap_removeTree
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {f : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, (List.flatMap Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.vertices f).Nodup → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findTree x f = Option.some t → (List.flatMap Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.vertices (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.removeTree x f) ++ t.vertices).Perm (List.flatMap Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree.vertices f)
statement:
public theorem perm_flatMap_removeTree {x : V} :
    ∀ {f : List (Tree V)} {t : Tree V},
      (f.flatMap Tree.vertices).Nodup → findTree x f = some t →
      ((removeTree x f).flatMap Tree.vertices ++ Tree.vertices t).Perm
        (f.flatMap Tree.vertices)

docstring: The preferred paths of a tree partition its vertex set.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.perm_treePaths_flatMap
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] (edges : List (V × V)) (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V), (List.flatMap id (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.treePaths edges t)).Perm t.vertices
statement:
public theorem perm_treePaths_flatMap (edges : List (V × V)) (t : Tree V) :
    ((treePaths edges t).flatMap id).Perm (Tree.vertices t)

docstring:
The vertex list of a grafted tree is the old vertex list followed by
the new child's, up to permutation.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.perm_vertices_graftAt
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {y : V} {newChild t t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.graftAt y newChild t = Option.some t' → t'.vertices.Perm (t.vertices ++ newChild.vertices)

docstring:
In a duplicate-free tree, pruning at `x` partitions the vertex list
into the remainder and the detached subtree, up to permutation.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.perm_vertices_pruneAt
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t sub t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, t.vertices.Nodup → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findSubtree x t = Option.some sub → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pruneAt x t = Option.some t' → t.vertices.Perm (t'.vertices ++ sub.vertices)
statement:
public theorem perm_vertices_pruneAt {x : V} :
    ∀ {t sub t' : Tree V}, (Tree.vertices t).Nodup →
      findSubtree x t = some sub → pruneAt x t = some t' →
      (Tree.vertices t).Perm (Tree.vertices t' ++ Tree.vertices sub)

docstring: Rerooting permutes the vertex list: same vertices, new preorder.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.perm_vertices_rerootAt
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rerootAt x t = Option.some t' → t'.vertices.Perm t.vertices

docstring:
Remove every subtree rooted at `x`, keeping every other node and edge:
the original tree with the `x` subtrees pruned off. Returns `none` exactly
when the root itself is `x` (nothing remains). This is the tree surgery
behind the remainder side of `State.cut`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pruneAt
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)
statement: public def pruneAt (x : V) : Tree V → Option (Tree V)

docstring: Pruning at a vertex that does not occur is the identity.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pruneAt_eq_self_of_not_mem
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, x ∉ t.vertices → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pruneAt x t = Option.some t
statement:
public theorem pruneAt_eq_self_of_not_mem {x : V} :
    ∀ {t : Tree V}, x ∉ Tree.vertices t → pruneAt x t = some t

docstring: The forest obtained by removing every tree whose vertices contain `x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.removeTree
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → V → List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V) → List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)
statement: public def removeTree (x : V) : List (Tree V) → List (Tree V)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.removeTree_eq_self_of_forall_not_mem
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {f : List (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)}, (∀ t ∈ f, x ∉ t.vertices) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.removeTree x f = f

docstring:
Reroot a tree at `x`, reversing the edges on the path from the old root
to `x` and keeping every other edge: the undirected tree is unchanged, only
the choice of root changes. Returns `none` when `x` does not occur. This is
the tree surgery behind `State.makeRoot`.

The recursion reroots the child subtree `c` on the root-to-`x` path first,
then grafts the remainder of the current node (the old root `r` together
with the sibling subtrees off the path) back under the root of `c`, which
is the next vertex on the reversed path. Attaching the remainder under
that path vertex, rather than directly under `x`, is what keeps every
path edge intact at depth greater than one.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rerootAt
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V)
statement: public def rerootAt (x : V) : Tree V → Option (Tree V)

docstring: Rerooting at a vertex that does not occur fails.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rerootAt_eq_none_of_not_mem
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, x ∉ t.vertices → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rerootAt x t = Option.none
statement:
public theorem rerootAt_eq_none_of_not_mem {x : V} :
    ∀ {t : Tree V}, x ∉ Tree.vertices t → rerootAt x t = none

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rerootAt_eq_some_of_mem
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, x ∈ t.vertices → ∃ t', Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rerootAt x t = Option.some t' ∧ t'.root = x
statement:
public theorem rerootAt_eq_some_of_mem {x : V} {t : Tree V}
    (hx : x ∈ Tree.vertices t) : ∃ t', rerootAt x t = some t' ∧ t'.root = x

docstring:
The path from the root of a tree down to `x`, root first, if `x` occurs in
the tree. This is the preferred path installed by `access x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → Option (List V)
statement: public def rootPath (x : V) : Tree V → Option (List V)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath_eq_some_of_mem
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, x ∈ t.vertices → ∃ p, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath x t = Option.some p
statement:
public theorem rootPath_eq_some_of_mem {x : V} {t : Tree V}
    (hx : x ∈ Tree.vertices t) : ∃ p, rootPath x t = some p

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath_ne_nil
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V} {p : List V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rootPath x t = Option.some p → p ≠ []
statement:
public theorem rootPath_ne_nil {x : V} {t : Tree V} {p : List V}
    (h : rootPath x t = some p) : p ≠ []

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.root_findSubtree
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t s : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.findSubtree x t = Option.some s → s.root = x
statement:
public theorem root_findSubtree {x : V} {t s : Tree V} (h : findSubtree x t = some s) :
    s.root = x

docstring: Grafting does not change the root.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.root_graftAt
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {y : V} {newChild t t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.graftAt y newChild t = Option.some t' → t'.root = t.root
statement:
public theorem root_graftAt {y : V} {newChild : Tree V} :
    ∀ {t t' : Tree V}, graftAt y newChild t = some t' → t'.root = t.root

docstring: Pruning keeps the root of the tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.root_pruneAt
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.pruneAt x t = Option.some t' → t'.root = t.root
statement:
public theorem root_pruneAt {x : V} {t t' : Tree V}
    (h : pruneAt x t = some t') : t'.root = t.root

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.root_rerootAt
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {x : V} {t t' : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.rerootAt x t = Option.some t' → t'.root = x
statement:
public theorem root_rerootAt {x : V} :
    ∀ {t t' : Tree V}, rerootAt x t = some t' → t'.root = x

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.root_spine
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (r : V) (xs : List V), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.spine r xs).root = r
statement: public theorem root_spine (r : V) (xs : List V) : (spine r xs).root = r

docstring:
The chain `r → c₁ → c₂ → ⋯` as a rooted tree: each vertex has the next as
its only child. A convenience constructor for building represented trees
from vertex lists; the structural operations do not use it (they perform
adjacency-preserving surgery instead).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.spine
signature: {V : Type u} → V → List V → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V
statement: public def spine : V → List V → Tree V

docstring:
All preferred paths of one represented tree under the preferred-edge
list `edges`: the downward path from the root, then every other path.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.treePaths
signature: {V : Type u} → [DecidableEq V] → List (V × V) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V → List (List V)
statement: public def treePaths (edges : List (V × V)) (t : Tree V) : List (List V)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.vertices_of_mem_ofVertexList
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.EulerTourTree.Tree V} {l : List V}, t ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.ofVertexList l → t.vertices = l
statement:
public theorem vertices_of_mem_ofVertexList {t : Tree V} {l : List V}
    (h : t ∈ ofVertexList l) : Tree.vertices t = l

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.vertices_spine
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} (r : V) (xs : List V), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LinkCutTree.spine r xs).vertices = r :: xs
statement:
public theorem vertices_spine : ∀ (r : V) (xs : List V),
    Tree.vertices (spine r xs) = r :: xs

docstring:
An LRU cache of capacity `cap`: entries most-recent-first, with the bundled invariants that
keys are pairwise distinct and there are at most `cap` entries.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache
signature: Type u → Type v → ℕ → Type (max u v)
statement: public structure LruCache (K : Type u) (V : Type v) (cap : Nat)

docstring: The empty cache.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.empty
signature: {K : Type u} → {V : Type v} → {cap : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap
statement: public def empty {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} : LruCache K V cap

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.eq_of_mem_of_fst_eq
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {entries : List (K × V)}, (List.map Prod.fst entries).Nodup → ∀ {p q : K × V}, p ∈ entries → q ∈ entries → p.1 = q.1 → p = q
statement:
theorem eq_of_mem_of_fst_eq {K : Type u} {V : Type v} :
    ∀ {entries : List (K × V)}, (entries.map Prod.fst).Nodup →
      ∀ {p q : K × V}, p ∈ entries → q ∈ entries → p.1 = q.1 → p = q

docstring: Removes every entry whose key is `k` (at most one, under the uniqueness invariant).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.eraseKey
signature: {K : Type u} → {V : Type v} → [DecidableEq K] → K → List (K × V) → List (K × V)
statement:
def eraseKey {K : Type u} {V : Type v} [DecidableEq K] (k : K)
    (entries : List (K × V)) : List (K × V)

docstring:
The key evicted by inserting a new key is the least recently used one: if a stored key `k`
disappears after putting a key `k'` that was not in the cache, the cache was full and `k` was
the last (least recent) key.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.evicted_is_least_recent
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq K] {cache : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap} {k k' : K} {v : V}, k' ∉ cache.keys → k ∈ cache.keys → k ∉ (cache.put k' v).keys → cache.keys.getLast? = Option.some k ∧ cache.size = cap
statement:
public theorem evicted_is_least_recent {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} [DecidableEq K]
    {cache : LruCache K V cap} {k k' : K} {v : V}
    (hnew : k' ∉ cache.keys) (hk : k ∈ cache.keys)
    (hevicted : k ∉ (cache.put k' v).keys) :
    cache.keys.getLast? = some k ∧ cache.size = cap

docstring: Two caches with the same entries are equal; the bundled invariant proofs are irrelevant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.ext
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : ℕ} {a b : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap}, a.entries = b.entries → a = b
statement:
theorem ext {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} {a b : LruCache K V cap}
    (h : a.entries = b.entries) : a = b

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.find?_eq_none_of_not_mem_keys
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq K] {entries : List (K × V)} {k : K}, k ∉ List.map Prod.fst entries → List.find? (fun q ↦ Decidable.decide (q.1 = k)) entries = Option.none
statement:
theorem find?_eq_none_of_not_mem_keys {K : Type u} {V : Type v} [DecidableEq K]
    {entries : List (K × V)} {k : K} (hk : k ∉ entries.map Prod.fst) :
    entries.find? (fun q => decide (q.1 = k)) = none

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.find?_eq_some_of_mem
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq K] {entries : List (K × V)}, (List.map Prod.fst entries).Nodup → ∀ {k : K} {v : V}, (k, v) ∈ entries → List.find? (fun q ↦ Decidable.decide (q.1 = k)) entries = Option.some (k, v)
statement:
theorem find?_eq_some_of_mem {K : Type u} {V : Type v} [DecidableEq K]
    {entries : List (K × V)} (nodup : (entries.map Prod.fst).Nodup) {k : K} {v : V}
    (hmem : (k, v) ∈ entries) :
    entries.find? (fun q => decide (q.1 = k)) = some (k, v)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.fst_of_find?_eq_some
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq K] {k : K} {p : K × V} {entries : List (K × V)}, List.find? (fun q ↦ Decidable.decide (q.1 = k)) entries = Option.some p → p.1 = k

docstring:
Looks up `k`. On a hit, returns the stored value and the cache with that entry promoted to the
front; on a miss, returns `none` and the unchanged cache.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.get
signature: {K : Type u} → {V : Type v} → {cap : ℕ} → [DecidableEq K] → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap → K → Option V × Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap
statement:
public def get {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} [DecidableEq K]
    (cache : LruCache K V cap) (k : K) : Option V × LruCache K V cap

docstring: A lookup of a stored key returns its stored value.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.get_hit
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq K] {cache : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap} {k : K} {v : V}, (k, v) ∈ cache.entries → (cache.get k).1 = Option.some v
statement:
public theorem get_hit {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} [DecidableEq K]
    {cache : LruCache K V cap} {k : K} {v : V} (hmem : (k, v) ∈ cache.entries) :
    (cache.get k).1 = some v

docstring: `get` preserves key uniqueness.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.get_keys_nodup
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq K] (cache : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap) (k : K), (cache.get k).2.keys.Nodup
statement:
public theorem get_keys_nodup {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} [DecidableEq K]
    (cache : LruCache K V cap) (k : K) : (cache.get k).2.keys.Nodup

docstring: A lookup of an absent key misses and leaves the cache unchanged.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.get_miss
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq K] {cache : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap} {k : K}, k ∉ cache.keys → (cache.get k).1 = Option.none ∧ (cache.get k).2 = cache
statement:
public theorem get_miss {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} [DecidableEq K]
    {cache : LruCache K V cap} {k : K} (hk : k ∉ cache.keys) :
    (cache.get k).1 = none ∧ (cache.get k).2 = cache

docstring:
The entries after `get` are a permutation of the entries before: the only effect of a
lookup on the cache state is reordering by promotion.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.get_perm
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq K] (cache : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap) (k : K), (cache.get k).2.entries.Perm cache.entries
statement:
public theorem get_perm {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} [DecidableEq K]
    (cache : LruCache K V cap) (k : K) :
    (cache.get k).2.entries.Perm cache.entries

docstring: A successful lookup promotes the entry to the front of the cache.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.get_promotes
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq K] {cache : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap} {k : K} {v : V}, (k, v) ∈ cache.entries → (cache.get k).2.entries.head? = Option.some (k, v)
statement:
public theorem get_promotes {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} [DecidableEq K]
    {cache : LruCache K V cap} {k : K} {v : V} (hmem : (k, v) ∈ cache.entries) :
    (cache.get k).2.entries.head? = some (k, v)

docstring:
Looking up a key immediately after putting it returns the stored value, provided the capacity
is positive so the new entry is not itself evicted.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.get_put
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq K] (cache : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap) (k : K) (v : V), 0 < cap → ((cache.put k v).get k).1 = Option.some v
statement:
public theorem get_put {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} [DecidableEq K]
    (cache : LruCache K V cap) (k : K) (v : V) (hcap : 0 < cap) :
    ((cache.put k v).get k).1 = some v

docstring:
Looking up a different key after a `put` that evicts nothing returns exactly what the
lookup returned before the `put`: surviving bindings keep their values.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.get_put_of_ne
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq K] {cache : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap} {k k' : K} {v : V}, k' ≠ k → cache.size < cap ∨ k ∈ cache.keys → ((cache.put k v).get k').1 = (cache.get k').1
statement:
public theorem get_put_of_ne {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} [DecidableEq K]
    {cache : LruCache K V cap} {k k' : K} {v : V} (hne : k' ≠ k)
    (hroom : cache.size < cap ∨ k ∈ cache.keys) :
    ((cache.put k v).get k').1 = (cache.get k').1

docstring: `get` does not change the number of stored entries.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.get_size
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq K] (cache : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap) (k : K), (cache.get k).2.size = cache.size
statement:
public theorem get_size {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} [DecidableEq K]
    (cache : LruCache K V cap) (k : K) :
    (cache.get k).2.size = cache.size

docstring: `get` preserves the capacity bound.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.get_size_le
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq K] (cache : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap) (k : K), (cache.get k).2.size ≤ cap
statement:
public theorem get_size_le {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} [DecidableEq K]
    (cache : LruCache K V cap) (k : K) : (cache.get k).2.size ≤ cap

docstring: The cached keys, most recently used first.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.keys
signature: {K : Type u} → {V : Type v} → {cap : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap → List K
statement: public def keys {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} (cache : LruCache K V cap) : List K

docstring: The keys of any cache are pairwise distinct.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.keys_nodup
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : ℕ} (cache : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache K V cap), cache.keys.Nodup
statement:
public theorem keys_nodup {K : Type u} {V : Type v} {cap : Nat} (cache : LruCache K V cap) :
    cache.keys.Nodup

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.length_eraseKey_add_one
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq K] {entries : List (K × V)} {k : K} {v : V}, (k, v) ∈ entries → (List.map Prod.fst entries).Nodup → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.eraseKey k entries).length + 1 = entries.length
statement:
theorem length_eraseKey_add_one {K : Type u} {V : Type v} [DecidableEq K] :
    ∀ {entries : List (K × V)} {k : K} {v : V}, (k, v) ∈ entries →
      (entries.map Prod.fst).Nodup → (eraseKey k entries).length + 1 = entries.length

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.length_eraseKey_le
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} {V : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq K] {k : K} {entries : List (K × V)}, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.LruCache.eraseKey k entries).length ≤ entries.length

docstring: Every entry stored by `put` is either the new binding or was already in the cache.

docstring:

docstring:
Same-run copy/fill assignments, scalar additions, and scalar products of FASTER-APSP.
The first coordinate excludes the accumulator vector updates in `matrixAccumulate`.

docstring: The total selected event count of this execution family is Θ(n³ log n).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.fasterAPSP_time_isTheta
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : Add α] [inst_1 : Mul α] [inst_2 : Zero α] (W : (n : ℕ) → Vector (Vector α n) n), (fun n ↦ ↑(Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.fasterAPSP (W n)).time.1 + ↑(Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.fasterAPSP (W n)).time.2.1 + ↑(Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.fasterAPSP (W n)).time.2.2) =Θ[Filter.atTop] fun n ↦ ↑n ^ 3 * Real.log ↑n

docstring:
With a zero diagonal and a previous at-most-`r`-edge distance matrix,
the actual infinity-initialized min-plus run returns at-most-`r+1`-edge
shortest weights. This includes repeated walks and signed edge weights.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.matrixAccumulate_edgeBounded
signature: ∀ {n r : ℕ} (A B : Vector (Vector (MinTropical (WithTop ℤ)) n) n), (∀ (j : Fin n), MinTropical.untrop ((B.get j).get j) = 0) → (∀ (i j : Fin n), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.IsEdgeBoundedShortestPathWeight (Matrix.of fun x y ↦ MinTropical.untrop ((B.get x).get y)) r i j (MinTropical.untrop ((A.get i).get j))) → ∀ (i j : Fin n), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.IsEdgeBoundedShortestPathWeight (Matrix.of fun x y ↦ MinTropical.untrop ((B.get x).get y)) (r + 1) i j (MinTropical.untrop (((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.matrixAccumulate A B (Vector.replicate n (Vector.replicate n 0))).ret.get i).get j))
statement:
public theorem matrixAccumulate_edgeBounded {n r : Nat}
    (A B : _root_.Vector (_root_.Vector (MinTropical (WithTop Int)) n) n)
    (hdiag : ∀ j : Fin n, MinTropical.untrop ((B.get j).get j) = 0)
    (hprevious : ∀ i j : Fin n,
      FloydWarshall.IsEdgeBoundedShortestPathWeight
        (Matrix.of fun x y => MinTropical.untrop ((B.get x).get y))
        r i j (MinTropical.untrop ((A.get i).get j)))
    (i j : Fin n) :
    FloydWarshall.IsEdgeBoundedShortestPathWeight
      (Matrix.of fun x y => MinTropical.untrop ((B.get x).get y))
      (r + 1) i j

        (Vector.replicate n (Vector.replicate n 0))).ret.get i).get j))

docstring:
Each actual min-plus output entry is the minimum of its saved accumulator
and every ordered candidate from the two unchanged input matrices.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.matrixAccumulate_minPlus_apply
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (A B C : Vector (Vector (MinTropical (WithTop ℤ)) n) n) (i j : Fin n), MinTropical.untrop (((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.matrixAccumulate A B C).ret.get i).get j) = Min.min (MinTropical.untrop ((C.get i).get j)) (Finset.univ.inf fun k ↦ MinTropical.untrop ((A.get i).get k) + MinTropical.untrop ((B.get k).get j))
statement:
public theorem matrixAccumulate_minPlus_apply {n : Nat}
    (A B C : _root_.Vector (_root_.Vector (MinTropical (WithTop Int)) n) n)
    (i j : Fin n) :
    MinTropical.untrop (((matrixAccumulate A B C).ret.get i).get j) =
      min (MinTropical.untrop ((C.get i).get j))
        (Finset.univ.inf fun k : Fin n =>
          MinTropical.untrop ((A.get i).get k) +
            MinTropical.untrop ((B.get k).get j))

docstring: Square accumulation returns the incoming matrix plus its canonical square product.

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.rectangularMatrixAccumulate
signature: {α : Type u} → [Add α] → [Mul α] → {p q r : ℕ} → Vector (Vector α q) p → Vector (Vector α r) q → Vector (Vector α r) p → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM (ℕ × ℕ) (Vector (Vector α r) p)

public def rectangularMatrixAccumulate {α : Type u} [Add α] [Mul α]
    {p q r : Nat} (A : _root_.Vector (_root_.Vector α q) p)

docstring: Every output entry is its incoming accumulator plus the canonical finite product sum.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.rectangularMatrixAccumulate_apply
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : AddCommMonoid α] [inst_1 : Mul α] {p q r : ℕ} (A : Vector (Vector α q) p) (B : Vector (Vector α r) q) (C : Vector (Vector α r) p) (i : Fin p) (j : Fin r), ((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.rectangularMatrixAccumulate A B C).ret.get i).get j = (C.get i).get j + ∑ k, (A.get i).get k * (B.get k).get j
statement:
theorem rectangularMatrixAccumulate_apply {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α] [Mul α]
    {p q r : Nat} (A : _root_.Vector (_root_.Vector α q) p)
    (B : _root_.Vector (_root_.Vector α r) q) (C : _root_.Vector (_root_.Vector α r) p)
    (i : Fin p) (j : Fin r) :
    ((rectangularMatrixAccumulate A B C).ret.get i).get j =
      (C.get i).get j + ∑ k : Fin q, (A.get i).get k * (B.get k).get j

docstring: The saved vector output refines accumulation using canonical matrix multiplication.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.rectangularMatrixAccumulate_ret
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : AddCommMonoid α] [inst_1 : Mul α] {p q r : ℕ} (A : Vector (Vector α q) p) (B : Vector (Vector α r) q) (C : Vector (Vector α r) p), (Matrix.of fun i j ↦ ((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.rectangularMatrixAccumulate A B C).ret.get i).get j) = (Matrix.of fun i j ↦ (C.get i).get j) + (Matrix.of fun i k ↦ (A.get i).get k) * Matrix.of fun k j ↦ (B.get k).get j
statement:
theorem rectangularMatrixAccumulate_ret {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α] [Mul α]
    {p q r : Nat} (A : _root_.Vector (_root_.Vector α q) p)
    (B : _root_.Vector (_root_.Vector α r) q) (C : _root_.Vector (_root_.Vector α r) p) :
    Matrix.of (fun i j => ((rectangularMatrixAccumulate A B C).ret.get i).get j) =
      Matrix.of (fun i j => (C.get i).get j) +
        Matrix.of (fun i k => (A.get i).get k) * Matrix.of (fun k j => (B.get k).get j)

docstring: Exact multiplication and accumulator-addition counts of the actual rectangular run.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.rectangularMatrixAccumulate_time
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : Add α] [inst_1 : Mul α] {p q r : ℕ} (A : Vector (Vector α q) p) (B : Vector (Vector α r) q) (C : Vector (Vector α r) p), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.rectangularMatrixAccumulate A B C).time = (p * q * r, p * q * r)
statement:
theorem rectangularMatrixAccumulate_time {α : Type u} [Add α] [Mul α]
    {p q r : Nat} (A : _root_.Vector (_root_.Vector α q) p)

docstring:
Add the product to the saved square accumulator by the eight-call CLRS recursion.
The two counters charge scalar multiplications and accumulator additions only.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.recursiveMatrixAccumulate
signature: {α : Type u} → [Add α] → [Mul α] → (k : ℕ) → Vector (Vector α (2 ^ k)) (2 ^ k) → Vector (Vector α (2 ^ k)) (2 ^ k) → Vector (Vector α (2 ^ k)) (2 ^ k) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM (ℕ × ℕ) (Vector (Vector α (2 ^ k)) (2 ^ k))

docstring: Each actual returned entry is the saved entry plus its canonical finite dot product.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.recursiveMatrixAccumulate_apply
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : AddCommMonoid α] [inst_1 : Mul α] (k : ℕ) (A B C : Vector (Vector α (2 ^ k)) (2 ^ k)) (i j : Fin (2 ^ k)), ((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.recursiveMatrixAccumulate k A B C).ret.get i).get j = (C.get i).get j + ∑ t, (A.get i).get t * (B.get t).get j
statement:
theorem recursiveMatrixAccumulate_apply {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α] [Mul α] (k : Nat)
    (A B C : _root_.Vector (_root_.Vector α (2 ^ k)) (2 ^ k)) (i j : Fin (2 ^ k)) :
    ((recursiveMatrixAccumulate k A B C).ret.get i).get j =
      (C.get i).get j + ∑ t : Fin (2 ^ k), (A.get i).get t * (B.get t).get j

docstring: The canonical Matrix view of the materialized result is `C + A * B`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.recursiveMatrixAccumulate_ret
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : AddCommMonoid α] [inst_1 : Mul α] (k : ℕ) (A B C : Vector (Vector α (2 ^ k)) (2 ^ k)), (Matrix.of fun i j ↦ ((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.recursiveMatrixAccumulate k A B C).ret.get i).get j) = (Matrix.of fun i j ↦ (C.get i).get j) + (Matrix.of fun i j ↦ (A.get i).get j) * Matrix.of fun i j ↦ (B.get i).get j
statement:
theorem recursiveMatrixAccumulate_ret {α : Type u} [AddCommMonoid α] [Mul α] (k : Nat)
    (A B C : _root_.Vector (_root_.Vector α (2 ^ k)) (2 ^ k)) :
    _root_.Matrix.of (fun i j => ((recursiveMatrixAccumulate k A B C).ret.get i).get j) =
      _root_.Matrix.of (fun i j => (C.get i).get j) +
        _root_.Matrix.of (fun i j => (A.get i).get j) *
          _root_.Matrix.of (fun i j => (B.get i).get j)

docstring:
The actual run performs exactly `8 ^ k` scalar multiplications and additions.
For dimension `2 ^ k` this equals its cube. Calls, indexing and allocation are uncharged.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.recursiveMatrixAccumulate_time
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : Add α] [inst_1 : Mul α] (k : ℕ) (A B C : Vector (Vector α (2 ^ k)) (2 ^ k)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.recursiveMatrixAccumulate k A B C).time = (8 ^ k, 8 ^ k)
statement:
theorem recursiveMatrixAccumulate_time {α : Type u} [Add α] [Mul α] (k : Nat)
    (A B C : _root_.Vector (_root_.Vector α (2 ^ k)) (2 ^ k)) :
    (recursiveMatrixAccumulate k A B C).time = (8 ^ k, 8 ^ k)

docstring: Without a negative cycle, the same executed table is minimal over all paths.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.slowAPSP_distance_spec
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (W L0 : Vector (Vector (MinTropical (WithTop ℤ)) n) n), (∀ (i : Fin n), MinTropical.untrop ((W.get i).get i) = 0) → (∀ (i j : Fin n), MinTropical.untrop ((L0.get i).get j) = if i = j then 0 else ⊤) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.NoNegativeCycle (Matrix.of fun x y ↦ MinTropical.untrop ((W.get x).get y)) → ∀ (i j : Fin n), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.IsStageShortestPathWeight (Matrix.of fun x y ↦ MinTropical.untrop ((W.get x).get y)) n i j (MinTropical.untrop (((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Matrix.slowAPSP W L0).ret.get i).get j))
statement:
public theorem slowAPSP_distance_spec {n : Nat}
    (W L0 : _root_.Vector (_root_.Vector (MinTropical (WithTop Int)) n) n)

docstring: The source identity initialization gives the minimum over at most `n-1` edges.
