docstring: Exact cost of the accepted saved-bucket executor on every valid array.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.bucketSort_time
signature: ∀ {R : Type} [inst : Field R] [inst_1 : LinearOrder R] [inst_2 : IsStrictOrderedRing R] [inst_3 : FloorRing R] (xs : Array R) (hx : ∀ x ∈ xs.toList, x ∈ Set.Ico 0 1), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.bucketSort xs hx).time = 5 * xs.size + ∑ i, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.insertionSort (List.filter (fun x ↦ Decidable.decide (⌊↑xs.size * x⌋₊ = ↑i)) xs.toList).reverse).time
statement:
public theorem bucketSort_time {R : Type} [Field R] [LinearOrder R]
    [IsStrictOrderedRing R] [FloorRing R] (xs : Array R)
    (hx : ∀ x ∈ xs.toList, x ∈ Ico (0 : R) 1) :
    (bucketSort xs hx).time = 5 * xs.size +
      ∑ i : Fin xs.size, (insertionSort
        ((xs.toList.filter
          (fun x => decide (Nat.floor ((xs.size : R) * x) = i.val))).reverse)).time

docstring: The actual continuous expected saved-bucket execution time is Theta of input size.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.bucketSort_time_expected_isTheta
signature: (fun n ↦ ∫ (ω : Fin n → ℝ), if hx : ∀ x ∈ (Array.ofFn ω).toList, x ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 then ↑(Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.bucketSort (Array.ofFn ω) hx).time else 0 ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x ↦ MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume[|Set.Ico 0 1]) =Θ[Filter.atTop] fun n ↦ ↑n
statement:
public theorem bucketSort_time_expected_isTheta :
    Asymptotics.IsTheta atTop
      (fun n : ℕ => ∫ ω : Fin n → ℝ,
        (if hx : ∀ x ∈ (Array.ofFn ω).toList, x ∈ Ico 0 1 then
          ((bucketSort (Array.ofFn ω) hx).time : ℝ) else 0)
        ∂Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin n => cond (volume : Measure ℝ) (Ico 0 1)))
      (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ))

signature: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → (∫ (ω : Fin n → ℝ), if hx : ∀ x ∈ (Array.ofFn ω).toList, x ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 then ↑(Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.bucketSort (Array.ofFn ω) hx).time else 0 ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x ↦ MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume[|Set.Ico 0 1]) ≤ 5 * ↑n + (↑n - 1) / 2

docstring: Squared actual bucket occupancies bound the cost for arbitrary valid arrays.

statement: abbrev compareLE (x y : α) : TimeM Nat Bool

docstring: Every sift-up executes at most one value comparison per level above its index.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.comparisons_siftUp_le_log2

docstring: Stable counting sort for records whose keys lie in `Fin k`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.countingSort
signature: {α : Type u} → {k : ℕ} → (α → Fin k) → Array α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (Array α)
statement:
def countingSort {α : Type u} {k : Nat} (key : α → Fin k)
    (input : Array α) : TimeM Nat (Array α)

docstring: Counting sort returns a sorted, stable permutation of the input records.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.countingSort_correct
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {k : ℕ} (key : α → Fin k) (input : Array α), List.Pairwise (fun x y ↦ key x ≤ key y) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.countingSort key input).ret.toList ∧ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.countingSort key input).ret.toList.Perm input.toList ∧ ∀ (q : Fin k), List.filter (fun x ↦ key x == q) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.countingSort key input).ret.toList = List.filter (fun x ↦ key x == q) input.toList
statement:
theorem countingSort_correct {α : Type u} {k : Nat} (key : α → Fin k)
    (input : Array α) :
    List.Pairwise (fun x y => key x ≤ key y) (countingSort key input).ret.toList ∧
      List.Perm (countingSort key input).ret.toList input.toList ∧
      ∀ q : Fin k,
        (countingSort key input).ret.toList.filter (fun x => key x == q) =
          input.toList.filter fun x => key x == q

docstring: Counting sort uses at most `7 * n + 3 * k` charged operations.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.countingSort_time
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {k : ℕ} (key : α → Fin k) (input : Array α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.countingSort key input).time ≤ 7 * input.size + 3 * k
statement:
theorem countingSort_time {α : Type u} {k : Nat} (key : α → Fin k)
    (input : Array α) :
    (countingSort key input).time ≤ 7 * input.size + 3 * k

docstring: The sum of counted comparisons and swaps is at most twice the index depth.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.events_siftUp_le_log2
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (a : Array α) (i : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.siftUp a i).time.1 + (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.siftUp a i).time.2 ≤ 2 * (i + 1).log2

docstring: Extract one minimum and return the remaining elements, charging once per comparison.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.extractMin
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → α → List α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (α × List α)
statement: def extractMin (candidate : α) : List α → TimeM Nat (α × List α)

docstring: Minimum extraction returns one minimum together with exactly the other input occurrences.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.extractMin_correct
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (candidate : α) (xs : List α), ((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.extractMin candidate xs).ret.1 :: (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.extractMin candidate xs).ret.2).Perm (candidate :: xs) ∧ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.extractMin candidate xs).ret.1 ≤ candidate ∧ ∀ x ∈ xs, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.extractMin candidate xs).ret.1 ≤ x
statement:
theorem extractMin_correct (candidate : α) (xs : List α) :
    List.Perm
        ((extractMin candidate xs).ret.1 :: (extractMin candidate xs).ret.2)
        (candidate :: xs) ∧
      (extractMin candidate xs).ret.1 ≤ candidate ∧
      ∀ x ∈ xs, (extractMin candidate xs).ret.1 ≤ x

docstring: Minimum extraction compares the candidate with every remaining element exactly once.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.extractMin_time

    (extractMin candidate xs).time = xs.length

docstring:
Interview candidates in order and hire only strict improvements.
The manager and chronological hire indices are zero-based; the fee pair counts
interviews and hires in the same indexed fold.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hireAssistant
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → List α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM (ℕ × ℕ) (Option ℕ × List ℕ)
statement:
public def hireAssistant {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] (xs : List α) :
    TimeM (Nat × Nat) (Option Nat × List Nat)

docstring: A nonempty input makes at least one hire and at most one per interview.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hireAssistant_hire_bounds
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (xs : List α), xs ≠ [] → 1 ≤ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hireAssistant xs).time.2 ∧ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hireAssistant xs).time.2 ≤ xs.length

docstring: The actual chronological history consists exactly of strict prefix records.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hireAssistant_hires
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (xs : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hireAssistant xs).ret.2 = List.map Prod.snd (List.filter (fun p ↦ (List.take p.2 xs).all fun a ↦ Decidable.decide (a < p.1)) xs.zipIdx)
statement:
public theorem hireAssistant_hires {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] (xs : List α) :
    (hireAssistant xs).ret.2 =
      (xs.zipIdx.filter (fun p => (xs.take p.2).all (fun a => decide (a < p.1)))).map
        Prod.snd

docstring: Every candidate in a strictly increasing input is hired, including empty input.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hireAssistant_increasing
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (xs : List α), List.Pairwise (fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 < x2) xs → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hireAssistant xs).ret.2 = List.range xs.length ∧ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hireAssistant xs).time = (xs.length, xs.length)
statement:
public theorem hireAssistant_increasing {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] (xs : List α)
    (h : xs.Pairwise (· < ·)) :
    (hireAssistant xs).ret.2 = List.range xs.length ∧
      (hireAssistant xs).time = (xs.length, xs.length)

docstring: Empty input interviews and hires nobody and returns no manager.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hireAssistant_nil
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α], Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hireAssistant [] = { ret := (Option.none, []), time := (0, 0) }
statement:
public theorem hireAssistant_nil {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] :

docstring: Execute Horner's nested evaluation on all coefficients, retaining their operation cost.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hornerEval
signature: {R : Type u} → [CommSemiring R] → {n : ℕ} → R → (Fin n → R) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ R
statement: def hornerEval {n : Nat} (x : R) (coefficients : Fin n → R) : TimeM Nat R

docstring: The total extension to no coefficients computes zero without arithmetic.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hornerEval_empty
signature: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] (x : R) (coefficients : Fin 0 → R), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hornerEval x coefficients = { ret := 0, time := 0 }
statement:
theorem hornerEval_empty (x : R) (coefficients : Fin 0 → R) :
    hornerEval x coefficients = ⟨0, 0⟩

docstring: Erasing the executed cost gives evaluation of the canonical coefficient polynomial.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hornerEval_ret_eq_eval
signature: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : DecidableEq R] {n : ℕ} (x : R) (coefficients : Fin n → R), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hornerEval x coefficients).ret = Polynomial.eval x ((Polynomial.ofFn n) coefficients)
statement:
theorem hornerEval_ret_eq_eval [DecidableEq R] {n : Nat} (x : R)
    (coefficients : Fin n → R) :
    (hornerEval x coefficients).ret = (Polynomial.ofFn n coefficients).eval x

docstring: The actual fold returns the complete coefficient/power sum in the source order.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hornerEval_ret_eq_sum
signature: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} (x : R) (coefficients : Fin n → R), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hornerEval x coefficients).ret = ∑ i, coefficients i * x ^ ↑i
statement:
theorem hornerEval_ret_eq_sum {n : Nat} (x : R) (coefficients : Fin n → R) :
    (hornerEval x coefficients).ret = ∑ i : Fin n, coefficients i * x ^ i.val

docstring: Zero initialization retains the two executed operations for a constant polynomial.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hornerEval_singleton
signature: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] (x : R) (coefficients : Fin 1 → R), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hornerEval x coefficients = { ret := coefficients 0, time := 2 }
statement:
theorem hornerEval_singleton (x : R) (coefficients : Fin 1 → R) :
    hornerEval x coefficients = ⟨coefficients 0, 2⟩

docstring: Every coefficient executes exactly one multiplication and one addition.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hornerEval_time
signature: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} (x : R) (coefficients : Fin n → R), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hornerEval x coefficients).time = 2 * n
statement:
theorem hornerEval_time {n : Nat} (x : R) (coefficients : Fin n → R) :
    (hornerEval x coefficients).time = 2 * n

docstring: At zero a nonempty coefficient vector returns its constant coefficient.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hornerEval_zero
signature: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} (coefficients : Fin (n + 1) → R), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.hornerEval 0 coefficients).ret = coefficients 0
statement:
theorem hornerEval_zero {n : Nat} (coefficients : Fin (n + 1) → R) :

docstring: Insertion sort with one unit of time charged for every order comparison.

statement: def insertionSort : List α → TimeM Nat (List α)

statement: def insertionSortInsert (a : α) : List α → TimeM Nat (List α)

docstring: Inserting one element charges at most one comparison per existing element.

signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (a : α) (xs : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.insertionSortInsert a xs).time ≤ xs.length

docstring: Insertion sort returns a sorted permutation of its input.

signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (xs : List α), List.Pairwise (fun x y ↦ x ≤ y) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.insertionSort xs).ret ∧ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.insertionSort xs).ret.Perm xs

signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (xs : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.insertionSort xs).ret.Perm xs

docstring: Insertion sort returns a nondecreasing list.

signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (xs : List α), List.Pairwise (fun x y ↦ x ≤ y) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.insertionSort xs).ret

docstring: An earliest-finish schedule, obtained by sorting by finish time and scanning once.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.intervalSchedule
signature: {ι : Type u} → {τ : Type v} → [LinearOrder τ] → (ι → τ) → (ι → τ) → List ι → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (List ι)
statement: def intervalSchedule (start finish : ι → τ) (xs : List ι) : TimeM Nat (List ι)

docstring:
The output preserves input occurrences, is feasible, and has maximum cardinality
among all feasible subpermutations of the input. Strictly positive durations are required.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.intervalSchedule_correct
signature: ∀ {ι : Type u} {τ : Type v} [inst : LinearOrder τ] (start finish : ι → τ) (xs : List ι), (∀ a ∈ xs, start a < finish a) → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.intervalSchedule start finish xs).ret.Subperm xs ∧ List.Pairwise (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.IntervalCompatible start finish) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.intervalSchedule start finish xs).ret ∧ ∀ (ys : List ι), ys.Subperm xs → List.Pairwise (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.IntervalCompatible start finish) ys → ys.length ≤ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.intervalSchedule start finish xs).ret.length
statement:
theorem intervalSchedule_correct (start finish : ι → τ) (xs : List ι)
    (hproper : ∀ a ∈ xs, start a < finish a) :
    (intervalSchedule start finish xs).ret.Subperm xs ∧
      List.Pairwise (IntervalCompatible start finish) (intervalSchedule start finish xs).ret ∧
      ∀ ys, ys.Subperm xs → List.Pairwise (IntervalCompatible start finish) ys →
        ys.length ≤ (intervalSchedule start finish xs).ret.length

docstring: At most `n * ⌈log₂ n⌉ + (n - 1)` comparisons are charged for `n` input occurrences.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.intervalSchedule_time
signature: ∀ {ι : Type u} {τ : Type v} [inst : LinearOrder τ] (start finish : ι → τ) (xs : List ι), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.intervalSchedule start finish xs).time ≤ xs.length * Nat.clog 2 xs.length + (xs.length - 1)
statement:
theorem intervalSchedule_time (start finish : ι → τ) (xs : List ι) :
    (intervalSchedule start finish xs).time ≤
      xs.length * Nat.clog 2 xs.length + (xs.length - 1)

docstring:
Returns the first zero-based occurrence of `pattern` in `text`, charging only symbol
comparisons. The empty pattern occurs at offset zero with cost zero.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.kmpSearch
signature: {α : Type u} → [BEq α] → List α → List α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (Option ℕ)
statement: public def kmpSearch [BEq α] (pattern text : List α) : TimeM Nat (Option Nat)

docstring: For a nonempty pattern, KMP agrees with the start-offset projection of `List.dropInfix?`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.kmpSearch_eq_dropInfix?_map_length
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] (pattern text : List α), pattern ≠ [] → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.kmpSearch pattern text).ret = Option.map (fun result ↦ result.1.length) (text.dropInfix? pattern)
statement:
theorem kmpSearch_eq_dropInfix?_map_length [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α]
    (pattern text : List α) (hpattern : pattern ≠ []) :
    (kmpSearch pattern text).ret =
      (List.dropInfix? text pattern).map fun result => result.1.length

docstring: KMP returns no offset exactly when no bounded offset matches the pattern.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.kmpSearch_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] (pattern text : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.kmpSearch pattern text).ret = Option.none ↔ ∀ (offset : ℕ), ¬Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.StringMatching.MatchAt pattern text offset
statement:
theorem kmpSearch_eq_none_iff [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α]
    (pattern text : List α) :
    (kmpSearch pattern text).ret = none ↔
      ∀ offset, ¬Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.StringMatching.MatchAt pattern text offset

docstring: KMP returns no offset exactly when the pattern is not an infix of the text.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.kmpSearch_eq_none_iff_not_isInfix
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] (pattern text : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.kmpSearch pattern text).ret = Option.none ↔ ¬pattern <:+: text
statement:
theorem kmpSearch_eq_none_iff_not_isInfix [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α]
    (pattern text : List α) :
    (kmpSearch pattern text).ret = none ↔ ¬pattern.IsInfix text

docstring: KMP returns an offset exactly when it is the least offset matching the pattern.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.kmpSearch_eq_some_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] (pattern text : List α) (offset : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.kmpSearch pattern text).ret = Option.some offset ↔ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.StringMatching.MatchAt pattern text offset ∧ ∀ earlier < offset, ¬Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.StringMatching.MatchAt pattern text earlier
statement:
theorem kmpSearch_eq_some_iff [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α]
    (pattern text : List α) (offset : Nat) :
    (kmpSearch pattern text).ret = some offset ↔
      Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.StringMatching.MatchAt pattern text offset ∧
        ∀ earlier < offset,
          ¬Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.StringMatching.MatchAt pattern text earlier

docstring: The empty pattern occurs at offset zero without any symbol comparisons.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.kmpSearch_nil_pattern
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : BEq α] (text : List α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.kmpSearch [] text = Pure.pure (Option.some 0)
statement:
theorem kmpSearch_nil_pattern [BEq α] (text : List α) :
    kmpSearch [] text = pure (some 0)

docstring: KMP uses at most twice the combined pattern and text lengths in symbol comparisons.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.kmpSearch_time_le
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : BEq α] (pattern text : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.kmpSearch pattern text).time ≤ 2 * pattern.length + 2 * text.length
statement:
theorem kmpSearch_time_le [BEq α] (pattern text : List α) :
    (kmpSearch pattern text).time ≤ 2 * pattern.length + 2 * text.length

docstring:
Returns the index of the first element satisfying `p`, charging one unit per evaluation of
`p`. No cost is charged for list operations, index arithmetic, or control flow.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch
signature: {α : Type u} → (α → Bool) → List α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (Option ℕ)
statement: def linearSearch (p : α → Bool) : List α → TimeM Nat (Option Nat)

docstring: Search fails exactly when no list element satisfies the predicate.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch p xs).ret = Option.none ↔ ∀ x ∈ xs, p x = Bool.false
statement:
theorem linearSearch_eq_none_iff (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α) :
    (linearSearch p xs).ret = none ↔ ∀ x ∈ xs, p x = false

docstring: A successful search returns exactly the first satisfying index.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch_eq_some_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α) (i : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch p xs).ret = Option.some i ↔ ∃ (h : i < xs.length), p xs[i] = Bool.true ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ) (hji : j < i), p xs[j] = Bool.false
statement:
theorem linearSearch_eq_some_iff (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α) (i : Nat) :
    (linearSearch p xs).ret = some i ↔
      ∃ h : i < xs.length,
        p xs[i] = true ∧
          ∀ j (hji : j < i), p (xs[j]'(Nat.lt_trans hji h)) = false

docstring:
The explicit unit-cost recurrence: the head predicate costs one unit, and the tail is searched
only when the head fails.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch_time_cons
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (p : α → Bool) (x : α) (xs : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch p (x :: xs)).time = if p x = Bool.true then 1 else 1 + (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch p xs).time
statement:
theorem linearSearch_time_cons (p : α → Bool) (x : α) (xs : List α) :
    (linearSearch p (x :: xs)).time =
      if p x then 1 else 1 + (linearSearch p xs).time

docstring: An unsuccessful search evaluates the predicate once for every list element.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch_time_eq_of_ret_eq_none
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch p xs).ret = Option.none → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch p xs).time = xs.length
statement:
theorem linearSearch_time_eq_of_ret_eq_none (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α)
    (h : (linearSearch p xs).ret = none) :
    (linearSearch p xs).time = xs.length

docstring: A successful search at index `i` performs exactly `i + 1` predicate evaluations.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch_time_eq_of_ret_eq_some
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α) (i : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch p xs).ret = Option.some i → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch p xs).time = i + 1
statement:
theorem linearSearch_time_eq_of_ret_eq_some (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α) (i : Nat)
    (h : (linearSearch p xs).ret = some i) :
    (linearSearch p xs).time = i + 1

docstring: Linear search evaluates the predicate at most once for every list element.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch_time_le
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch p xs).time ≤ xs.length
statement:
theorem linearSearch_time_le (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α) :
    (linearSearch p xs).time ≤ xs.length

docstring: Searching an empty list evaluates the predicate zero times.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch_time_nil
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (p : α → Bool), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.linearSearch p []).time = 0
statement: theorem linearSearch_time_nil (p : α → Bool) : (linearSearch p []).time = 0

docstring:
Returns the first index containing a value at least `key`, charging one tick for each element
comparison. If every value is below `key`, it returns `xs.size`.

Precondition: `xs` must be sorted (or at least partitioned at `key`: every element below the
returned index is `< key` and every element from that index on is `≥ key`). On an unsorted array
the result is unspecified: for example, `lowerBound #[2, 1] 2` returns `2`, not the first
qualifying index `0`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.lowerBound
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → Array α → α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ ℕ
statement: def lowerBound (xs : Array α) (key : α) : TimeM Nat Nat

docstring: On a sorted array, the returned index separates values below `key` from values at least `key`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.lowerBound_spec
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (xs : Array α) (key : α), Array.Pairwise (fun x y ↦ x ≤ y) xs → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.lowerBound xs key).ret ≤ xs.size ∧ (∀ j < (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.lowerBound xs key).ret, ∀ (_hjs : j < xs.size), xs[j] < key) ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.lowerBound xs key).ret ≤ j → ∀ (_hjs : j < xs.size), key ≤ xs[j]
statement:
theorem lowerBound_spec (xs : Array α) (key : α)
    (hs : xs.Pairwise (fun x y => x ≤ y)) :
    (lowerBound xs key).ret ≤ xs.size ∧
      (∀ j (_hj : j < (lowerBound xs key).ret) (_hjs : j < xs.size), xs[j] < key) ∧
      (∀ j (_hj : (lowerBound xs key).ret ≤ j) (_hjs : j < xs.size), key ≤ xs[j])

docstring: Lower-bound search uses at most `clog₂(n + 1)` element comparisons.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.lowerBound_time_le
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (xs : Array α) (key : α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.lowerBound xs key).time ≤ Nat.clog 2 (xs.size + 1)
statement:
theorem lowerBound_time_le (xs : Array α) (key : α) :
    (lowerBound xs key).time ≤ Nat.clog 2 (xs.size + 1)

docstring: The matcher returns exactly the canonical occurrences, including overlaps.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.mem_boyerMooreMatches_iff
signature: ∀ {σ : ℕ} (pattern text : List (Fin σ)) (offset : ℕ), offset ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.boyerMooreMatches pattern text).ret ↔ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.StringMatching.MatchAt pattern text offset

docstring: An offset is reported exactly when the pattern matches there, including empty patterns.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.mem_naiveMatches_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] (pattern text : List α) (offset : ℕ), offset ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.naiveMatches pattern text).ret ↔ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.StringMatching.MatchAt pattern text offset
statement:
theorem mem_naiveMatches_iff [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] (pattern text : List α) (offset : Nat) :
    offset ∈ (naiveMatches pattern text).ret ↔
      Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.StringMatching.MatchAt pattern text offset

docstring: An offset is reported exactly when the canonical pattern match holds there.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.mem_rabinKarpMatches_iff
signature: ∀ (d q : ℕ) (pattern text : List ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (offset : ℕ), offset ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.rabinKarpMatches d q pattern text hq).ret ↔ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.StringMatching.MatchAt pattern text offset
statement:
theorem mem_rabinKarpMatches_iff (d q : Nat) (pattern text : List Nat) (hq : 0 < q) (offset : Nat) :
    offset ∈ (rabinKarpMatches d q pattern text hq).ret ↔
      Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.StringMatching.MatchAt pattern text offset

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.minMax
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → List α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (Option (α × α))
statement:
public def minMax {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] (xs : List α) :
    TimeM Nat (Option (α × α))

docstring: Empty input is exactly the case without extrema.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.minMax_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (xs : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.minMax xs).ret = Option.none ↔ xs = []
statement:
theorem minMax_eq_none_iff {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] (xs : List α) :
    (minMax xs).ret = none ↔ xs = []

docstring: Both returned extrema occur in the input and bound all its members.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.minMax_eq_some_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (xs : List α) (lo hi : α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.minMax xs).ret = Option.some (lo, hi) ↔ lo ∈ xs ∧ hi ∈ xs ∧ (∀ x ∈ xs, lo ≤ x) ∧ ∀ x ∈ xs, x ≤ hi
statement:
theorem minMax_eq_some_iff {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] (xs : List α) (lo hi : α) :
    (minMax xs).ret = some (lo, hi) ↔
      lo ∈ xs ∧ hi ∈ xs ∧ (∀ x ∈ xs, lo ≤ x) ∧ (∀ x ∈ xs, x ≤ hi)

docstring: Empty input performs no element comparisons.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.minMax_nil
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α], Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.minMax [] = Pure.pure Option.none
statement:
theorem minMax_nil {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] :
    minMax ([] : List α) = pure none

docstring: The paired scan returns the canonical minimum and maximum of the original list.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.minMax_ret
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (xs : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.minMax xs).ret = xs.min?.bind fun lo ↦ Option.map (fun hi ↦ (lo, hi)) xs.max?
statement:
theorem minMax_ret {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] (xs : List α) :
    (minMax xs).ret = xs.min?.bind (fun lo => xs.max?.map (fun hi => (lo, hi)))

docstring: One element seeds both extrema without comparing elements.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.minMax_singleton

docstring: Erasing cost gives the canonical index filter on the candidate suffixes.

docstring: The exact sum of left-to-right comparison counts at every candidate alignment.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.naiveMatches_time_eq
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : BEq α] (pattern text : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.naiveMatches pattern text).time = if pattern.length ≤ text.length then (List.map (fun suffix ↦ Min.min pattern.length (List.findIdx (fun pair ↦ !pair.1 == pair.2) (pattern.zip suffix) + 1)) (List.take (text.length - pattern.length + 1) text.tails)).sum else 0
statement:
theorem naiveMatches_time_eq [BEq α] (pattern text : List α) :
    (naiveMatches pattern text).time =
      if pattern.length ≤ text.length then
        ((text.tails.take (text.length - pattern.length + 1)).map fun suffix =>
          min pattern.length
            ((pattern.zip suffix).findIdx (fun pair => !(pair.1 == pair.2)) + 1)).sum
      else 0

docstring: Three-way partition preserves occurrences and classifies every output field.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3_correct
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (pivot : α) (xs : List α), ((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3 pivot xs).ret.below ++ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3 pivot xs).ret.equal ++ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3 pivot xs).ret.above).Perm xs ∧ (∀ x ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3 pivot xs).ret.below, x < pivot) ∧ (∀ x ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3 pivot xs).ret.equal, x = pivot) ∧ ∀ x ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3 pivot xs).ret.above, pivot < x
statement:
theorem partition3_correct (pivot : α) (xs : List α) :
    List.Perm
        ((partition3 pivot xs).ret.below ++
          (partition3 pivot xs).ret.equal ++
          (partition3 pivot xs).ret.above)
        xs ∧
      (∀ x ∈ (partition3 pivot xs).ret.below, x < pivot) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ (partition3 pivot xs).ret.equal, x = pivot) ∧
      ∀ x ∈ (partition3 pivot xs).ret.above, pivot < x

docstring: Predicate counts survive partitioning when both other parts contribute zero.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3_countP_eq_below
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (pivot : α) (xs : List α) (p : α → Bool), (∀ x ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3 pivot xs).ret.equal, p x = Bool.false) → (∀ x ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3 pivot xs).ret.above, p x = Bool.false) → List.countP p xs = List.countP p (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3 pivot xs).ret.below

theorem partition3_countP_eq_below {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    (pivot : α) (xs : List α) (p : α → Bool)
    (hequal : ∀ x ∈ (partition3 pivot xs).ret.equal, p x = false)
    (habove : ∀ x ∈ (partition3 pivot xs).ret.above, p x = false) :
    xs.countP p = (partition3 pivot xs).ret.below.countP p

docstring: Filled below and equal blocks contribute their lengths to an above-part count.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3_countP_eq_block_add_above
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (pivot : α) (xs : List α) (p : α → Bool), (∀ x ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3 pivot xs).ret.below, p x = Bool.true) → (∀ x ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3 pivot xs).ret.equal, p x = Bool.true) → List.countP p xs = (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3 pivot xs).ret.below.length + (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3 pivot xs).ret.equal.length + List.countP p (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3 pivot xs).ret.above
statement:
theorem partition3_countP_eq_block_add_above {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α]
    (pivot : α) (xs : List α) (p : α → Bool)

    xs.countP p = (partition3 pivot xs).ret.below.length +
      (partition3 pivot xs).ret.equal.length + (partition3 pivot xs).ret.above.countP p

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.partition3_count_le

docstring: Exact setup, hash tests, rolling work, borrow additions, and hit-verification cost.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.rabinKarpMatches_time_eq
statement:
theorem rabinKarpMatches_time_eq (d q : Nat) (pattern text : List Nat) (hq : 0 < q)
    (hpos : 0 < pattern.length) (hlen : pattern.length ≤ text.length) :
    let m := pattern.length
    let r := text.length - m
    let residue := fun suffix : List Nat => Nat.ofDigits d (suffix.take m).reverse % q
    let borrows := ((text.tails.take r).map fun suffix =>
      if residue suffix < suffix.head! * (d ^ (m - 1) % q) % q then 1 else 0).sum
    let verification := ((text.tails.take (r + 1)).map fun suffix =>
      if Nat.ofDigits d pattern.reverse % q = residue suffix then
        min m ((pattern.zip suffix).findIdx (fun pair => !(pair.1 == pair.2)) + 1) else 0).sum
    (rabinKarpMatches d q pattern text hq).time =
      (8 * m - 1) + (r + 1) + 7 * r + borrows + verification

docstring: Setup plus matching work is bounded by the candidate count and the number of hash hits.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.rabinKarpMatches_time_le
statement:
theorem rabinKarpMatches_time_le (d q : Nat) (pattern text : List Nat) (hq : 0 < q)
    (hpos : 0 < pattern.length) (hlen : pattern.length ≤ text.length) :
    let m := pattern.length
    let r := text.length - m
    let hashHits := (text.tails.take (r + 1)).countP fun suffix =>
      Nat.ofDigits d pattern.reverse % q == Nat.ofDigits d (suffix.take m).reverse % q
    (rabinKarpMatches d q pattern text hq).time ≤
      (8 * m - 1) + (9 * (r + 1) - 8) + m * hashHits

docstring: Repeated-symbol words execute exactly m comparisons at every alignment, plus setup and rolls.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.rabinKarpMatches_time_replicate
statement:
theorem rabinKarpMatches_time_replicate (d q a m n : Nat) (hq : 0 < q) (hpos : 0 < m)
    (hlen : m ≤ n) :
    let t := Nat.ofDigits d (List.replicate m a).reverse % q
    let borrow := if t < a * (d ^ (m - 1) % q) % q then 1 else 0
    (rabinKarpMatches d q (List.replicate m a) (List.replicate n a) hq).time =
      (8 * m - 1) + (n - m + 1) + 7 * (n - m) +
        (n - m) * borrow + m * (n - m + 1)

docstring: Stable least-significant-digit radix sort for fixed-width most-significant-first digits.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.radixSort
signature: {α : Type u} → {b d : ℕ} → (α → Vector (Fin b) d) → Array α → 2 ≤ b → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (Array α)
statement:
def radixSort {α : Type u} {b d : Nat} (digits : α → Vector (Fin b) d)
    (input : Array α) (_hb : 2 ≤ b) : TimeM Nat (Array α)

docstring: Radix sort returns a lexicographically and numerically sorted stable permutation.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.radixSort_correct
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {b d : ℕ} (digits : α → Vector (Fin b) d) (input : Array α) (hb : 2 ≤ b), List.Pairwise (fun x y ↦ digits x ≤ digits y) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.radixSort digits input hb).ret.toList ∧ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.radixSort digits input hb).ret.toList.Perm input.toList ∧ (∀ (v : Vector (Fin b) d), List.filter (fun x ↦ digits x == v) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.radixSort digits input hb).ret.toList = List.filter (fun x ↦ digits x == v) input.toList) ∧ List.Pairwise (fun x y ↦ Nat.ofDigits b (List.map Fin.val (digits x).toList.reverse) ≤ Nat.ofDigits b (List.map Fin.val (digits y).toList.reverse)) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.radixSort digits input hb).ret.toList
statement:
theorem radixSort_correct {α : Type u} {b d : Nat} (digits : α → Vector (Fin b) d)
    (input : Array α) (hb : 2 ≤ b) :
    List.Pairwise (fun x y => digits x ≤ digits y) (radixSort digits input hb).ret.toList ∧
      List.Perm (radixSort digits input hb).ret.toList input.toList ∧
      (∀ v : Vector (Fin b) d,
        (radixSort digits input hb).ret.toList.filter (fun x => digits x == v) =
          input.toList.filter fun x => digits x == v) ∧
      List.Pairwise
        (fun x y =>
          Nat.ofDigits b ((digits x).toList.reverse.map Fin.val) ≤
            Nat.ofDigits b ((digits y).toList.reverse.map Fin.val))
        (radixSort digits input hb).ret.toList

docstring: Radix sort uses at most `d * (7 * n + 3 * b)` charged operations.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.radixSort_time
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {b d : ℕ} (digits : α → Vector (Fin b) d) (input : Array α) (hb : 2 ≤ b), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.radixSort digits input hb).time ≤ d * (7 * input.size + 3 * b)
statement:
theorem radixSort_time {α : Type u} {b d : Nat} (digits : α → Vector (Fin b) d)
    (input : Array α) (hb : 2 ≤ b) :
    (radixSort digits input hb).time ≤ d * (7 * input.size + 3 * b)

docstring:
Execute the increasing-position Fisher–Yates swaps using legal supplied
suffix draws. The two counters record actual draw and swap calls.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermute
signature: {α : Type u} → {n : ℕ} → Vector α n → ((i : Fin n) → Fin (n - ↑i)) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM (ℕ × ℕ) (Vector α n)

docstring:
The ideal-oracle distribution of the actual Fisher–Yates computation,
obtained from uniform complete legal suffix-draw histories.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermuteDistribution
signature: {α : Type u} → {n : ℕ} → Vector α n → PMF (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM (ℕ × ℕ) (Vector α n))
statement:
public def randomlyPermuteDistribution {α : Type u} {n : Nat}
    (xs : Vector α n) : PMF (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM (Nat × Nat) (Vector α n))

docstring:
The mass of a full actual output is the sum of its independent suffix-draw
history weights. Repeated values coalesce, and impossible event counts receive no mass.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermuteDistribution_apply
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {n : ℕ} (xs : Vector α n) (out : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM (ℕ × ℕ) (Vector α n)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermuteDistribution xs) out = ∑ draws, if out = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermute xs draws then ∏ i, (↑(n - ↑i))⁻¹ else 0
statement:
public theorem randomlyPermuteDistribution_apply {α : Type u} {n : Nat} (xs : Vector α n)
    (out : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM (Nat × Nat) (Vector α n)) :
    randomlyPermuteDistribution xs out =
      ∑ draws : (i : Fin n) → Fin (n - i.val),
        if out = randomlyPermute xs draws
        then ∏ i : Fin n, ((n - i.val : Nat) : ENNReal)⁻¹ else 0

docstring:
The actual ideal-oracle computation is the pushforward of the canonical uniform
position permutation. This equation retains the saved vector and the exact same-run cost.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermuteDistribution_eq_map_uniform
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {n : ℕ} (xs : Vector α n), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermuteDistribution xs = PMF.map (fun σ ↦ { ret := Vector.ofFn fun p ↦ xs[↑(σ p)], time := (n, n) }) (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)))
statement:
public theorem randomlyPermuteDistribution_eq_map_uniform {α : Type u} {n : Nat}
    (xs : Vector α n) :
    randomlyPermuteDistribution xs =
      (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))).map
        (fun σ => (⟨Vector.ofFn (fun p => xs[(σ p).val]), (n, n)⟩ :
          Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM (Nat × Nat) (Vector α n)))

docstring: Empty Fisher–Yates execution retrieves no choices and performs no swaps.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermute_empty
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (xs : Vector α 0) (draws : (i : Fin 0) → Fin (0 - ↑i)), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermute xs draws = { ret := xs, time := (0, 0) }

docstring:
Every occurrence is preserved by the saved Fisher–Yates swaps, even when
input values repeat.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermute_perm
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {n : ℕ} (xs : Vector α n) (draws : (i : Fin n) → Fin (n - ↑i)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermute xs draws).ret.toList.Perm xs.toList

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermute_prefix_probability
signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ} (hkn : k ≤ n) (a : Fin k → Fin n), Function.Injective a → (∑ draws, if ∀ (p : Fin k), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermute (Vector.ofFn fun q ↦ q) draws).ret[↑(Fin.castLE hkn p)] = a p then (↑n.factorial)⁻¹ else 0) = ↑(n - k).factorial / ↑n.factorial
statement:
public theorem randomlyPermute_prefix_probability {n k : Nat} (hkn : k ≤ n)
    (a : Fin k → Fin n) (hinj : Function.Injective a) :
    (∑ draws : (i : Fin n) → Fin (n - i.val),
      if ∀ p : Fin k,
        (randomlyPermute (Vector.ofFn fun q : Fin n => q) draws).ret[(Fin.castLE hkn p).val] = a p
      then (n.factorial : ENNReal)⁻¹ else 0) =
        ((n - k).factorial : ENNReal) / n.factorial

docstring:
Singleton execution retains its element but still retrieves the final
unique draw and executes its self-swap.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermute_singleton
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (xs : Vector α 1) (draws : (i : Fin 1) → Fin (1 - ↑i)), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermute xs draws = { ret := xs, time := (1, 1) }

docstring:
Fisher–Yates executes exactly one draw and one swap at every position,
including the final singleton draw and self-swap.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermute_time
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {n : ℕ} (xs : Vector α n) (draws : (i : Fin n) → Fin (n - ↑i)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.randomlyPermute xs draws).time = (n, n)

signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (xs : List α), List.Pairwise (fun x y ↦ x ≤ y) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.selectionSort xs).ret ∧ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.selectionSort xs).ret.Perm xs

Sift-down with `(value comparisons, array swaps)` as its event cost.

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.siftDown
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → Array α → ℕ → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM (ℕ × ℕ) (Array α)
statement:

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.siftDown_comparisons_le
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (a : Array α) (i : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.siftDown a i).time.1 ≤ 2 * (a.size.log2 - (i + 1).log2)

signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (a : Array α) (i : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.siftDown a i).time.2 ≤ a.size.log2 - (i + 1).log2

docstring: Total event count is at most three per remaining binary-tree level.

signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (a : Array α) (i : ℕ), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.siftDown a i).time.1 + (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM.siftDown a i).time.2 ≤ 3 * (a.size.log2 - (i + 1).log2)

docstring: Compute reflexive transitive closure by the CLRS saved-matrix recurrence.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosure
signature: {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Fin n → Bool) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (Fin n → Fin n → Bool)
statement:
def transitiveClosure {n : Nat} (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) :
    TimeM Nat (Fin n → Fin n → Bool)

docstring: Execute initialization followed by the first `pivots` saved-matrix stages.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosureStages
signature: {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Fin n → Bool) → (pivots : ℕ) → pivots ≤ n → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (Vector (Vector Bool n) n)
statement:
def transitiveClosureStages {n : Nat} (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool)
    (pivots : Nat) (hpivots : pivots ≤ n) : TimeM Nat (Vector (Vector Bool n) n)

docstring:
A saved-stage cell is true exactly when a canonical path exists whose internal vertices are
among the admitted pivots.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosureStages_cell_eq_true_iff
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (pivots : ℕ) (hpivots : pivots ≤ n) (i j : Fin n), ((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosureStages adjacency pivots hpivots).ret.get i).get j = Bool.true ↔ ∃ path, List.IsChainFromTo (fun a b ↦ adjacency a b = Bool.true) path i j ∧ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.FloydWarshall.InternalVerticesBelow pivots path
statement:
theorem transitiveClosureStages_cell_eq_true_iff {n : Nat}
    (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (pivots : Nat) (hpivots : pivots ≤ n)
    (i j : Fin n) :
    ((transitiveClosureStages adjacency pivots hpivots).ret.get i).get j = true ↔
      ∃ path, path.IsChainFromTo (fun a b => adjacency a b = true) i j ∧
        FloydWarshall.InternalVerticesBelow pivots path

docstring: Stage `k + 1` reads every operand from the complete saved result of stage `k`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosureStages_succ_cell
statement:
theorem transitiveClosureStages_succ_cell {n : Nat} (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool)
    (k : Nat) (hk : k < n) (i j : Fin n) :
    let previous := (transitiveClosureStages adjacency k (by omega)).ret
    ((transitiveClosureStages adjacency (k + 1) (by omega)).ret.get i).get j =
      ((previous.get i).get j ||
        ((previous.get i).get ⟨k, hk⟩ && (previous.get ⟨k, hk⟩).get j))

docstring: Before any pivot, a cell is the diagonal test or the corresponding input edge.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosureStages_zero_cell
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (i j : Fin n), ((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosureStages adjacency 0 ⋯).ret.get i).get j = (Decidable.decide (i = j) || adjacency i j)
statement:
theorem transitiveClosureStages_zero_cell {n : Nat} (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool)
    (i j : Fin n) :
    ((transitiveClosureStages adjacency 0 (by omega)).ret.get i).get j =
      (decide (i = j) || adjacency i j)

docstring: The returned Boolean is true exactly for canonical reflexive-transitive reachability.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosure_cell_eq_true_iff
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (i j : Fin n), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosure adjacency).ret i j = Bool.true ↔ Relation.ReflTransGen (fun a b ↦ adjacency a b = Bool.true) i j
statement:
theorem transitiveClosure_cell_eq_true_iff {n : Nat}
    (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (i j : Fin n) :
    (transitiveClosure adjacency).ret i j = true ↔
      Relation.ReflTransGen (fun a b => adjacency a b = true) i j

docstring: Initialization performs exactly `n²` cell assignments.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosure_initializations
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosureStages adjacency 0 ⋯).time = n ^ 2
statement:
theorem transitiveClosure_initializations {n : Nat} (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) :
    (transitiveClosureStages adjacency 0 (by omega)).time = n ^ 2

docstring: Each saved transition stage performs exactly `n²` new-cell assignments.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosure_stage_assignments
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (k : ℕ) (hk : k < n), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosureStages adjacency (k + 1) ⋯).time - (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosureStages adjacency k ⋯).time = n ^ 2
statement:
theorem transitiveClosure_stage_assignments {n : Nat} (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool)
    (k : Nat) (hk : k < n) :
    (transitiveClosureStages adjacency (k + 1) (by omega)).time -
        (transitiveClosureStages adjacency k (by omega)).time = n ^ 2

docstring: The same run performs `n²` initialization assignments and `n³` transition assignments.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosure_time
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosure adjacency).time = n ^ 2 + n ^ 3
statement:
theorem transitiveClosure_time {n : Nat} (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) :
    (transitiveClosure adjacency).time = n ^ 2 + n ^ 3

docstring: A singleton graph performs one initialization and one transition assignment.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosure_time_one
signature: ∀ (adjacency : Fin 1 → Fin 1 → Bool), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosure adjacency).time = 2
statement:
theorem transitiveClosure_time_one (adjacency : Fin 1 → Fin 1 → Bool) :
    (transitiveClosure adjacency).time = 2

docstring: The empty graph performs no cell assignments.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosure_time_zero
signature: ∀ (adjacency : Fin 0 → Fin 0 → Bool), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosure adjacency).time = 0
statement:
theorem transitiveClosure_time_zero (adjacency : Fin 0 → Fin 0 → Bool) :
    (transitiveClosure adjacency).time = 0

docstring: All `n` transition stages together perform exactly `n³` cell assignments.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosure_transition_assignments
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosureStages adjacency n ⋯).time - (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TransitiveClosure.transitiveClosureStages adjacency 0 ⋯).time = n ^ 3
statement:
theorem transitiveClosure_transition_assignments {n : Nat}
    (adjacency : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) :
    (transitiveClosureStages adjacency n (by omega)).time -
        (transitiveClosureStages adjacency 0 (by omega)).time = n ^ 3

docstring: `AllNodes` is universal quantification over complete structural membership.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.allNodes_iff_forall_mem
signature: ∀ {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} {p : κ → ν → ℕ → Prop} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.AllNodes p tree ↔ ∀ (key : κ) (value : ν) (priority : ℕ), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.MemNode key value priority tree → p key value priority

public theorem allNodes_iff_forall_mem {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v}
    {p : κ → ν → Nat → Prop} {tree : Tree κ ν} :
    AllNodes p tree ↔ ∀ key value priority, MemNode key value priority tree →
      p key value priority

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.allNodes_key_iff

docstring:
The inorder key-value refinement of a tree, computed by the linear
accumulating traversal `contentsAux`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.contents
signature: {κ : Type u} → {ν : Type v} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν → List (κ × ν)
statement: public def contents {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} (tree : Tree κ ν) : List (κ × ν)

docstring:
Append the inorder key-value traversal of a tree to a suffix in linear
time: the left traversal is accumulated onto the node entry and the already
traversed right suffix, so no ancestor recopies a completed traversal.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.contentsAux
signature: {κ : Type u} → {ν : Type v} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν → List (κ × ν) → List (κ × ν)
statement:
public def contentsAux {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} :
    Tree κ ν → List (κ × ν) → List (κ × ν)

docstring: Erased contents are exactly the two non-pivot split sides.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.contents_erase
signature: ∀ {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [inst : LinearOrder κ] (key : κ) (tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.erase key tree).contents = (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.split key tree).less.contents ++ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.split key tree).greater.contents
statement:
public theorem contents_erase {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [LinearOrder κ]
    (key : κ) (tree : Tree κ ν) :
    contents (erase key tree) =
      contents (split key tree).less ++ contents (split key tree).greater

docstring: Inserted contents are the split sides with the new key-value pair between them.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.contents_insert
signature: ∀ {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [inst : LinearOrder κ] (key : κ) (value : ν) (priority : ℕ) (tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.insert key value priority tree).contents = (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.split key tree).less.contents ++ (key, value) :: (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.split key tree).greater.contents
statement:
public theorem contents_insert {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [LinearOrder κ]
    (key : κ) (value : ν) (priority : Nat) (tree : Tree κ ν) :
    contents (insert key value priority tree) =
      contents (split key tree).less ++ (key, value) :: contents (split key tree).greater

docstring: Merging concatenates the two inorder key-value refinements.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.contents_merge
signature: ∀ {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} (left right : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν), (left.merge right).contents = left.contents ++ right.contents
statement:
public theorem contents_merge {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} (left right : Tree κ ν) :
    contents (merge left right) = contents left ++ contents right

docstring: Characteristic node equation for the linear inorder traversal.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.contents_node
signature: ∀ {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} (left : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν) (key : κ) (value : ν) (priority : ℕ) (right : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν), (left.node key value priority right).contents = left.contents ++ (key, value) :: right.contents
statement:
public theorem contents_node {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v}
    (left : Tree κ ν) (key : κ) (value : ν) (priority : Nat) (right : Tree κ ν) :
    contents (.node left key value priority right) =
      contents left ++ (key, value) :: contents right

docstring: Splitting decomposes inorder contents around the optional pivot entry.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.contents_split
signature: ∀ {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [inst : LinearOrder κ] (pivot : κ) (tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν), tree.contents = (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.split pivot tree).less.contents ++ (Option.map (fun result ↦ (pivot, result.1)) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.split pivot tree).found).toList ++ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.split pivot tree).greater.contents
statement:
public theorem contents_split {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [LinearOrder κ]
    (pivot : κ) (tree : Tree κ ν) :
    contents tree = contents (split pivot tree).less ++
      ((split pivot tree).found.map fun result => (pivot, result.1)).toList ++
      contents (split pivot tree).greater

docstring: Delete a key by splitting around it and merging the two remaining trees.

docstring: Splitting preserves min-heap priority order in both output trees.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.heapOrdered_split
signature: ∀ {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [inst : LinearOrder κ] {pivot : κ} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν}, tree.HeapOrdered → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.split pivot tree).less.HeapOrdered ∧ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.split pivot tree).greater.HeapOrdered

statement:

The inorder list of keys, used to state uniqueness independently of

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.keys
signature: {κ : Type u} → {ν : Type v} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν → List κ
statement: public def keys {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} (tree : Tree κ ν) : List κ

docstring: Characteristic node equation for the inorder key list.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.keys_node
signature: ∀ {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} (left : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν) (key : κ) (value : ν) (priority : ℕ) (right : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν), (left.node key value priority right).keys = left.keys ++ key :: right.keys

public theorem keys_node {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v}
    (left : Tree κ ν) (key : κ) (value : ν) (priority : Nat) (right : Tree κ ν) :

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.lookup_eq_some_iff
signature: ∀ {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [inst : LinearOrder κ] {query : κ} {value : ν} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν}, tree.Ordered → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.lookup query tree = Option.some value ↔ ∃ priority, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.MemNode query value priority tree)
statement:
public theorem lookup_eq_some_iff {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [LinearOrder κ]
    {query : κ} {value : ν} {tree : Tree κ ν} (hOrdered : Ordered tree) :

docstring: Looking up an erased key returns no value.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.lookup_erase_eq_none
signature: ∀ {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [inst : LinearOrder κ] {key : κ} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν}, tree.Valid → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.lookup key (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.erase key tree) = Option.none

docstring: Inorder contents contain exactly the tree's key-value pairs.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.mem_contents
signature: ∀ {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} {key : κ} {value : ν} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν}, (key, value) ∈ tree.contents ↔ ∃ priority, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.MemNode key value priority tree

docstring: The key list contains exactly the structurally present keys.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.mem_keys

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.merge
signature: {κ : Type u} → {ν : Type v} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν

docstring: The inorder keys of an ordered tree are strictly increasing.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.ordered_keys
signature: ∀ {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [inst : LinearOrder κ] {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν}, tree.Ordered → List.Pairwise (fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 < x2) tree.keys
statement:
public theorem ordered_keys {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [LinearOrder κ]

docstring: Splitting preserves strict BST ordering in both output trees.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.ordered_split
signature: ∀ {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [inst : LinearOrder κ] {pivot : κ} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν}, tree.Ordered → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.split pivot tree).less.Ordered ∧ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.split pivot tree).greater.Ordered
statement:
public theorem ordered_split {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [LinearOrder κ]
    {pivot : κ} {tree : Tree κ ν} (hOrdered : Ordered tree) :
    Ordered (split pivot tree).less ∧ Ordered (split pivot tree).greater

statement: public def rootPriority {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} : Tree κ ν → Option Nat

docstring: The recursively computed number of nodes.

docstring: Split outputs contain only keys respectively below and above the pivot.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.split_bounds
signature: ∀ {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [inst : LinearOrder κ] {pivot : κ} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree κ ν}, tree.Ordered → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.AllNodes (fun key x x_1 ↦ key < pivot) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.split pivot tree).less ∧ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.AllNodes (fun key x x_1 ↦ pivot < key) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Treap.Tree.split pivot tree).greater
statement:
public theorem split_bounds {κ : Type u} {ν : Type v} [LinearOrder κ]
    {pivot : κ} {tree : Tree κ ν} (hOrdered : Ordered tree) :
    AllNodes (fun key _ _ => key < pivot) (split pivot tree).less ∧
      AllNodes (fun key _ _ => pivot < key) (split pivot tree).greater

docstring: Inserting two distinct keys commutes up to lookup equivalence.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.LookupEquiv.insert_comm
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq α] (trie : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β) {firstKeys secondKeys : List α}, firstKeys ≠ secondKeys → ∀ (firstValue secondValue : β), ((trie.insert firstKeys firstValue).insert secondKeys secondValue).LookupEquiv ((trie.insert secondKeys secondValue).insert firstKeys firstValue)

      ((trie.insert secondKeys secondValue).insert firstKeys firstValue)

docstring: Lookup-equivalent valid tries enumerate the same entries, disregarding list order.

signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq α] {left right : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β}, left.LookupEquiv right → left.Valid → right.Valid → ∀ (keys : List α) (value : β), (keys, value) ∈ left.entries ↔ (keys, value) ∈ right.entries

    (keys, value) ∈ left.entries ↔ (keys, value) ∈ right.entries

docstring:
Whether a trie node carries no value and no children, so its parent
may prune it.

statement: def isEmptyNode {α : Type u} {β : Type v} : Trie α β → Bool

A trie is a childless non-terminal node exactly when it is the empty

theorem isEmptyNode_eq_true_iff {α : Type u} {β : Type v}
    {t : Trie α β} : isEmptyNode t = true ↔ t = .node none []

statement:
def lookup {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [DecidableEq α]

docstring:
Deleting one key does not change the lookup result for a distinct
key.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.lookup_delete_of_ne
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq α] (trie : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β) {deletedKeys keys : List α}, keys ≠ deletedKeys → (trie.delete deletedKeys).lookup keys = trie.lookup keys
statement:
theorem lookup_delete_of_ne {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [DecidableEq α]
    (trie : Trie α β) {deletedKeys keys : List α}
    (h : keys ≠ deletedKeys) :
    (trie.delete deletedKeys).lookup keys = trie.lookup keys

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.lookup_delete_self
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq α] (trie : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β) (keys : List α), (trie.delete keys).lookup keys = Option.none
statement:
theorem lookup_delete_self {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [DecidableEq α]

docstring: Every lookup in the empty trie fails.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.lookup_empty
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq α] (keys : List α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.empty.lookup keys = Option.none
statement:
theorem lookup_empty {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [DecidableEq α]
    (keys : List α) : (empty : Trie α β).lookup keys = none

docstring: Lookup succeeds with a value exactly when the corresponding pair occurs in `entries`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.lookup_eq_some_iff_mem_entries
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq α] {trie : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β}, trie.Valid → ∀ (keys : List α) (value : β), trie.lookup keys = Option.some value ↔ (keys, value) ∈ trie.entries
statement:
theorem lookup_eq_some_iff_mem_entries {α : Type u} {β : Type v}
    [DecidableEq α] {trie : Trie α β} (h : Valid trie)
    (keys : List α) (value : β) :
    trie.lookup keys = some value ↔ (keys, value) ∈ trie.entries

docstring: Inserting one key does not change the lookup result for a distinct key.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.lookup_insert_of_ne
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq α] (trie : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β) {insertedKeys keys : List α} (value : β), keys ≠ insertedKeys → (trie.insert insertedKeys value).lookup keys = trie.lookup keys
statement:
theorem lookup_insert_of_ne {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [DecidableEq α]
    (trie : Trie α β) {insertedKeys keys : List α} (value : β)
    (h : keys ≠ insertedKeys) :
    (trie.insert insertedKeys value).lookup keys = trie.lookup keys

docstring: Looking up an inserted key returns its new value.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.lookup_insert_same
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq α] (trie : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β) (keys : List α) (value : β), (trie.insert keys value).lookup keys = Option.some value
statement:
theorem lookup_insert_same {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [DecidableEq α]
    (trie : Trie α β) (keys : List α) (value : β) :
    (trie.insert keys value).lookup keys = some value

docstring: Lookup at any other key is unchanged by `setChild`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.lookup_setChild_of_ne
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq α] {k key : α}, k ≠ key → ∀ (child : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β) (children : List (α × Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β)), List.lookup k (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.setChild key child children) = List.lookup k children
statement:
theorem lookup_setChild_of_ne {α : Type u} {β : Type v}
    [DecidableEq α] {k key : α} (hk : k ≠ key) (child : Trie α β)
    (children : List (α × Trie α β)) :
    (setChild key child children).lookup k = children.lookup k

docstring:
Lookup at the updated key after `setChild`: the new child, or `none`
when the child was pruned as an empty node.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.lookup_setChild_self
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq α] (key : α) (child : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β) (children : List (α × Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β)), List.lookup key (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.setChild key child children) = if child.isEmptyNode = Bool.true then Option.none else Option.some child
statement:
theorem lookup_setChild_self {α : Type u} {β : Type v}
    [DecidableEq α] (key : α) (child : Trie α β)
    (children : List (α × Trie α β)) :
    (setChild key child children).lookup key =
      if isEmptyNode child then none else some child

docstring:
Replace the child stored at `key` by `child`, dropping the entry entirely
when `child` is a childless non-terminal node. The first entry at `key` is
replaced in place (or dropped, when pruning) and any later entries at `key`
are removed, so the order of the surviving entries is preserved and at
most one entry for `key` remains even in a trie that does not satisfy
`Valid`. In `delete`, `key` is always present; for an absent key a
non-empty child is appended at the end. Its public specification is
`lookup_setChild_self`, `lookup_setChild_of_ne`, and `setChild_valid`
below.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.setChild
signature: {α : Type u} → {β : Type v} → [DecidableEq α] → α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β → List (α × Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β) → List (α × Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β)

docstring:
`setChild` preserves the child-list half of trie validity: the child
keys stay duplicate-free and every surviving child stays valid.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.setChild_valid
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq α] {key : α} {child : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β} {children : List (α × Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie α β)}, (List.map Prod.fst children).Nodup → (∀ entry ∈ children, entry.2.Valid) → child.Valid → (List.map Prod.fst (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.setChild key child children)).Nodup ∧ ∀ entry ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.Trie.setChild key child children, entry.2.Valid

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root.height_insert_le
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (x : α) (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root.insert x t).height ≤ t.height + 1
statement:

docstring: The computed height of a root's tree agrees with its stored height.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root.height_tree
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.height t.tree = t.height
statement:
public theorem Root.height_tree (t : Root α) :
    TwoThreeTree.height t.tree = t.height

docstring:
Insert a key into a root, growing the height by one exactly when the root
splits. Insertion ignores an already-present key.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root.insert
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root α
statement: public def Root.insert [LinearOrder α] (x : α) (t : Root α) : Root α

docstring: Root insertion adds exactly the inserted key to the flattening.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root.mem_flatten_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {x y : α} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root α}, t.Ordered → (y ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root.insert x t).flatten ↔ y = x ∨ y ∈ t.flatten)

public theorem Root.mem_flatten_insert [LinearOrder α] {x y : α} {t : Root α}
