docstring:
A key is in the flattening of a tree built from a list exactly when it is
in the list.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root.mem_fromList
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {x : α} {xs : List α}, x ∈ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root.fromList xs).flatten ↔ x ∈ xs
statement:
public theorem Root.mem_fromList [LinearOrder α] {x : α} {xs : List α} :
    x ∈ (Root.fromList xs).flatten ↔ x ∈ xs

docstring: The empty tree is ordered.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root.ordered_empty
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LT α], Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root.empty.Ordered
statement: public theorem Root.ordered_empty [LT α] : (Root.empty : Root α).Ordered

docstring: A tree built from a list is ordered.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root.ordered_fromList
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (xs : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root.fromList xs).Ordered
statement:
public theorem Root.ordered_fromList [LinearOrder α] (xs : List α) :
    (Root.fromList xs).Ordered

docstring: Insertion preserves the ordering invariant at the root.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root.ordered_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {x : α} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root α}, t.Ordered → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Root.insert x t).Ordered
statement:
public theorem Root.ordered_insert [LinearOrder α] {x : α} {t : Root α}
    (hOrd : t.Ordered) : (t.insert x).Ordered

docstring:
A 2-3 tree indexed by height: all leaves of `Tree α h` are at depth `h`.
A `node2` stores one separator key with two children, and a `node3` stores two
separator keys with three children.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree
signature: Type u → ℕ → Type u
statement: public inductive Tree (α : Type u) : Nat → Type u

docstring: `All` is equivalent to universal quantification over the flattening.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.all_iff_forall_flatten
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {h : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.All p t ↔ ∀ y ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten t, p y
statement:
public theorem all_iff_forall_flatten {p : α → Prop} {h : Nat} {t : Tree α h} :
    All p t ↔ ∀ y ∈ flatten t, p y

docstring: `All` is equivalent to universal quantification over structural membership.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.all_iff_forall_mem
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {h : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.All p t ↔ ∀ x ∈ t, p x
statement:
public theorem all_iff_forall_mem {p : α → Prop} {h : Nat} {t : Tree α h} :
    All p t ↔ ∀ x, x ∈ t → p x

docstring: Every height-indexed tree is balanced.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.balanced
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {h : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Balanced t
statement: public theorem balanced {h : Nat} (t : Tree α h) : Balanced t

docstring: Search a tree by comparing the query against separator keys.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.contains
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → α → {h : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h → Bool
statement: public def contains [LinearOrder α] (x : α) : {h : Nat} → Tree α h → Bool

docstring: Search succeeds exactly on the keys of the flattening, for ordered trees.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.contains_eq_true_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {x : α} {h : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Ordered t → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.contains x t = Bool.true ↔ x ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten t)
statement:
public theorem contains_eq_true_iff [LinearOrder α] {x : α} {h : Nat} {t : Tree α h}
    (hOrd : Ordered t) : contains x t = true ↔ x ∈ flatten t

docstring:
The linear-time inorder traversal of a tree: subtrees interleaved with
separator keys.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten
signature: {α : Type u} → {h : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h → List α
statement: public def flatten {h : Nat} (t : Tree α h) : List α

docstring:
Append the inorder traversal of a tree to an existing suffix in linear
time: subtrees interleaved with separator keys, accumulated without
recopying left results.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flattenAux
signature: {α : Type u} → {h : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h → List α → List α
statement: public def flattenAux : {h : Nat} → Tree α h → List α → List α

docstring: `flattenAux` prepends the flattening of its tree to the suffix.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flattenAux_eq
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {h : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h) (suffix : List α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flattenAux t suffix = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten t ++ suffix
statement:
public theorem flattenAux_eq {h : Nat} (t : Tree α h) (suffix : List α) :
    flattenAux t suffix = flatten t ++ suffix

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten_leaf
signature: ∀ {α : Type u}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree.leaf = []
statement: public theorem flatten_leaf : flatten (Tree.leaf : Tree α 0) = []

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten_node2
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {h : ℕ} {a : α} {l r : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree.node2 a l r) = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten l ++ a :: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten r
statement:
public theorem flatten_node2 {h : Nat} {a : α} {l r : Tree α h} :
    flatten (Tree.node2 a l r) = flatten l ++ a :: flatten r

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten_node3
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {h : ℕ} {a b : α} {l m r : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree.node3 a b l m r) = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten l ++ a :: (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten m ++ b :: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten r)

docstring: The flattening of an ordered tree has no duplicate keys.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten_nodup
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {h : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Ordered t → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten t).Nodup
statement:
public theorem flatten_nodup [LinearOrder α] {h : Nat} {t : Tree α h}
    (hOrd : Ordered t) : (flatten t).Nodup

docstring: The height of a tree, computed from its leftmost spine.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.height
signature: {α : Type u} → {h : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h → ℕ
statement: public def height : {h : Nat} → Tree α h → Nat

docstring: The computed height of a tree agrees with its height index.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.height_eq
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {h : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.height t = h
statement: public theorem height_eq {h : Nat} (t : Tree α h) : height t = h

docstring:
Insert a key into a height-indexed tree, returning an `Overflow`. A leaf
always splits; a 2-node absorbs a split child by becoming a 3-node; a 3-node
with a split child splits in turn, promoting the appropriate separator. Inserting
a key equal to a separator leaves the tree unchanged.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.ins
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → α → {h : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Overflow α h
statement: public def ins [LinearOrder α] (x : α) : {h : Nat} → Tree α h → Overflow α h

docstring:
Insertion into an ordered tree satisfies `InsSpec`: it preserves the
ordering invariant and its flattening is `orderedInsert` of the old flattening.
Balance is automatic from the height index.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.ins_spec
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] (x : α) {h : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Ordered t → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.InsSpec x t (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.ins x t)
statement:
public theorem ins_spec [LinearOrder α] (x : α) :
    ∀ {h : Nat} (t : Tree α h), Ordered t → InsSpec x t (ins x t)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.instMembershipTree
signature: {α : Type u} → {h : ℕ} → Membership α (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h)
statement: public instance {h : Nat} : Membership α (Tree α h)

docstring: The flattening contains exactly the structurally present keys.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.mem_flatten
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {x : α} {h : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h}, x ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten t ↔ x ∈ t
statement:
public theorem mem_flatten {x : α} {h : Nat} {t : Tree α h} :
    x ∈ flatten t ↔ x ∈ t

docstring: Deprecated forwarder for the shared `Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.mem_orderedInsert`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.mem_orderedInsert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {x y : α} {xs : List α}, y ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.orderedInsert x xs ↔ y = x ∨ y ∈ xs
statement:
public theorem mem_orderedInsert [LinearOrder α] {x y : α} {xs : List α} :
    y ∈ orderedInsert x xs ↔ y = x ∨ y ∈ xs

docstring:
Deprecated forwarder for the shared `Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.orderedInsert`.
Kept so existing fully qualified references to `TwoThreeTree.orderedInsert`
keep elaborating; new code should use the shared name.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.orderedInsert
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → α → List α → List α
statement: public def orderedInsert [LinearOrder α] (x : α) : List α → List α

docstring: The flattening of an ordered tree is strictly increasing.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.ordered_flatten_pairwise
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {h : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Tree α h}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.Ordered t → List.Pairwise (fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 < x2) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TwoThreeTree.flatten t)
statement:
public theorem ordered_flatten_pairwise [LinearOrder α] {h : Nat} {t : Tree α h}
    (hOrd : Ordered t) : List.Pairwise (· < ·) (flatten t)

docstring: Two vertices are equivalent when `find` returns the same representative.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent
signature: {n : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n → Fin n → Fin n → Prop
statement: public def Equivalent {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x y : Fin n) : Prop

docstring: A finite parent forest with a strictly decreasing certificate on non-root edges.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest
signature: ℕ → Type
statement: public structure Forest (n : Nat)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.equivalentDecidable
signature: {n : ℕ} → (forest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n) → (x y : Fin n) → Decidable (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent forest x y)
statement:
public instance equivalentDecidable {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x y : Fin n) :
    Decidable (Equivalent forest x y)

docstring: Exact partition semantics: only the two selected old classes are merged.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.equivalent_union_iff
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (forest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n) (x y a b : Fin n), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.union forest x y) a b ↔ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent forest a b ∨ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent forest a x ∧ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent forest b y ∨ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent forest a y ∧ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent forest b x
statement:
public theorem equivalent_union_iff {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x y a b : Fin n) :
    Equivalent (union forest x y) a b ↔
      Equivalent forest a b ∨
        (Equivalent forest a x ∧ Equivalent forest b y) ∨
        (Equivalent forest a y ∧ Equivalent forest b x)

docstring: Follow parent pointers to the unique root reached from `x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find
signature: {n : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n → Fin n → Fin n
statement: public def find {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x : Fin n) : Fin n

docstring: Run `find`, charging one unit for every visited vertex, including the root.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.findWithCost
signature: {n : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n → Fin n → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (Fin n)
statement: public def findWithCost {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x : Fin n) : TimeM Nat (Fin n)

docstring: The cost annotation is exactly the traversed edge count plus the root visit.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.findWithCost_time
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (forest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n) (x : Fin n), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.findWithCost forest x).time = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.pathLength forest x + 1
statement:
public theorem findWithCost_time {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x : Fin n) :
    (findWithCost forest x).time = pathLength forest x + 1

docstring: One `find` costs at most the certified input depth plus one root visit.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.findWithCost_time_le_depth
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (forest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n) (x : Fin n), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.findWithCost forest x).time ≤ forest.depth x + 1
statement:
public theorem findWithCost_time_le_depth {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x : Fin n) :
  (findWithCost forest x).time ≤ forest.depth x + 1

docstring: Every queried vertex is equivalent to its representative.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find_in_class
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (forest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n) (x : Fin n), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent forest x (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find forest x)
statement:
public theorem find_in_class {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x : Fin n) :
    Equivalent forest x (find forest x)

docstring: The result of `find` is a root.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find_isRoot
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (forest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n) (x : Fin n), forest.parent (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find forest x) = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find forest x
statement:
public theorem find_isRoot {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x : Fin n) :
    forest.parent (find forest x) = find forest x

docstring: Starting from a parent pointer reaches the same root.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find_parent
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (forest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n) (x : Fin n), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find forest (forest.parent x) = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find forest x
statement:
public theorem find_parent {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x : Fin n) :
    find forest (forest.parent x) = find forest x

docstring: `union` redirects exactly the first selected representative to the second one.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find_union
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (forest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n) (x y z : Fin n), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.union forest x y) z = if Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent forest z x then Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find forest y else Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find forest z

docstring:
Every class outside the first selected class keeps its representative:
if `z` is not equivalent to `x`, then `union` with any `y` preserves the
representative of `z` (no hypothesis on `y` is needed).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find_union_of_unrelated
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (forest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n) (x y z : Fin n), ¬Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent forest z x → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.union forest x y) z = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.find forest z

docstring: Link two distinct certified roots, preserving the parent-forest invariant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.link
signature: {n : ℕ} → (forest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n) → (fromRoot toRoot : Fin n) → forest.parent fromRoot = fromRoot → forest.parent toRoot = toRoot → fromRoot ≠ toRoot → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n

docstring: Depth certificate used after redirecting `fromRoot` to `toRoot`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.linkDepth
signature: {n : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n → Fin n → Fin n → Fin n → ℕ
statement:
public def linkDepth {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (fromRoot toRoot : Fin n) :
    Fin n → Nat

docstring: Parent map obtained by redirecting `fromRoot` to `toRoot`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.linkParent
signature: {n : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n → Fin n → Fin n → Fin n → Fin n
statement:
public def linkParent {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (fromRoot toRoot : Fin n) :
    Fin n → Fin n

docstring: The number of non-root parent edges traversed by `find`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.pathLength
signature: {n : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n → Fin n → ℕ
statement: public def pathLength {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x : Fin n) : Nat

docstring: Persistently merge the classes of `x` and `y` by linking the first root to the second.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.union
signature: {n : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n → Fin n → Fin n → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n
statement: public def union {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x y : Fin n) : Forest n

docstring:
Run `union`, charging its two root searches and, only when the two
representatives are distinct, one root-link operation; when they already
coincide, `union` performs no link and none is charged.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.unionWithCost
signature: {n : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n → Fin n → Fin n → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n)
statement:
public def unionWithCost {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x y : Fin n) :
    TimeM Nat (Forest n)

docstring: One `union` costs at most the two certified input depths plus three visits/links.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.unionWithCost_time_le_depth
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (forest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n) (x y : Fin n), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.unionWithCost forest x y).time ≤ forest.depth x + forest.depth y + 3
statement:
public theorem unionWithCost_time_le_depth {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x y : Fin n) :
    (unionWithCost forest x y).time ≤ forest.depth x + forest.depth y + 3

docstring: Unioning two already equivalent vertices leaves the persistent forest unchanged.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.union_eq_self_of_equivalent
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} {forest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n} {x y : Fin n}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent forest x y → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.union forest x y = forest
statement:
public theorem union_eq_self_of_equivalent {n : Nat} {forest : Forest n} {x y : Fin n}
    (h : Equivalent forest x y) : union forest x y = forest

docstring: `union` makes its two selected vertices equivalent.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.union_equivalent
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (forest : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Forest n) (x y : Fin n), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.Equivalent (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UnionFind.union forest x y) x y
statement:
public theorem union_equivalent {n : Nat} (forest : Forest n) (x y : Fin n) :
    Equivalent (union forest x y) x y

docstring:
A finite hash family is universal if it is nonempty (so that choosing a member
uniformly at random, the reading behind the bound, makes sense) and every two
distinct keys collide under at most a `1 / m` fraction of its members, stated
without division as `collisionCount H x y * m ≤ H.card`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.IsUniversal
signature: {α : Type u} → {m : ℕ} → Finset (α → Fin m) → Prop
statement: public def IsUniversal (H : Finset (α → Fin m)) : Prop

docstring:
Indexed universality: the family `h` ranges over the nonempty finite index set `s`,
counting each index separately even when two indices give the same function. This is
the form in which the classical counting arguments, including the mod-prime family
below, are carried out. Nonemptiness is part of the predicate for the same reason as
in `IsUniversal`: there is no uniform random choice from an empty family.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.IsUniversalOn
signature: {α : Type u} → {m : ℕ} → {ι : Type v} → Finset ι → (ι → α → Fin m) → Prop
statement: public def IsUniversalOn {ι : Type v} (s : Finset ι) (h : ι → α → Fin m) : Prop

docstring: The index set of the mod-prime family: pairs `(a, b)` with `a ≠ 0`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.ModPrimeIndex
signature: ℕ → Type
statement: public abbrev ModPrimeIndex (p : Nat) : Type

docstring: The number of functions in the family `H` under which `x` and `y` collide.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.collisionCount
signature: {α : Type u} → {m : ℕ} → Finset (α → Fin m) → α → α → ℕ
statement: public def collisionCount (H : Finset (α → Fin m)) (x y : α) : Nat

docstring: The collision count never exceeds the size of the family.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.collisionCount_le_card
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {m : ℕ} (H : Finset (α → Fin m)) (x y : α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.collisionCount H x y ≤ H.card
statement:
public theorem collisionCount_le_card (H : Finset (α → Fin m)) (x y : α) :
    collisionCount H x y ≤ H.card

docstring: A key collides with itself under every function in the family.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.collisionCount_self
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {m : ℕ} (H : Finset (α → Fin m)) (x : α), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.collisionCount H x x = H.card
statement:
public theorem collisionCount_self (H : Finset (α → Fin m)) (x : α) :
    collisionCount H x x = H.card

docstring:
The collision bound part of universality, without nonemptiness. The empty
family satisfies this bound vacuously; `IsUniversal` is this bound together with
`H.Nonempty` and a positive range size `0 < m`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.isUniversal_bound_empty
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {m : ℕ} (x y : α), x ≠ y → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.collisionCount ∅ x y * m ≤ ∅.card
statement:
public theorem isUniversal_bound_empty :
    ∀ x y : α, x ≠ y →
      collisionCount (∅ : Finset (α → Fin m)) x y * m ≤
        (∅ : Finset (α → Fin m)).card

docstring: Membership in the `Finset` of distinct mod-prime functions.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.mem_modPrimeFamily
signature: ∀ {p m : ℕ} [inst : NeZero p] (hm : 0 < m) (h : ZMod p → Fin m), h ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrimeFamily p m hm ↔ ∃ ab, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrimeHashes p m hm ab = h

docstring:
The mod-prime family as a `Finset` of distinct functions. The universality result
below is proved for the indexed family `modPrimeHashes`, matching the `p * (p - 1)`
count of indices in CLRS; the image here can be smaller, since distinct index pairs
may agree as functions after the final reduction modulo `m`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrimeFamily
signature: (p m : ℕ) → [NeZero p] → 0 < m → Finset (ZMod p → Fin m)
statement:
public def modPrimeFamily (p m : Nat) [NeZero p] (hm : 0 < m) :
    Finset (ZMod p → Fin m)

docstring:
The mod-prime hash function `h_{a,b}(x) = ((a * x + b) mod p) mod m` of CLRS
Section 11.3.3: the inner reduction modulo `p` is the arithmetic of `ZMod p`, and the
outer reduction is `Nat` remainder of the canonical representative.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrimeHash
signature: (p m : ℕ) → 0 < m → ZMod p → ZMod p → ZMod p → Fin m
statement: public def modPrimeHash (p m : Nat) (hm : 0 < m) (a b x : ZMod p) : Fin m

docstring: Two keys collide under `h_{a,b}` exactly when the inner values agree modulo `m`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrimeHash_eq_iff
signature: ∀ (p m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (a b x y : ZMod p), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrimeHash p m hm a b x = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrimeHash p m hm a b y ↔ (a * x + b).val % m = (a * y + b).val % m

docstring: The value of a mod-prime hash is the displayed double remainder.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrimeHash_val
signature: ∀ (p m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (a b x : ZMod p), ↑(Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrimeHash p m hm a b x) = (a * x + b).val % m
statement:
public theorem modPrimeHash_val (p m : Nat) (hm : 0 < m) (a b x : ZMod p) :
    (modPrimeHash p m hm a b x).val = (a * x + b).val % m

docstring: The mod-prime family as functions indexed by pairs `(a, b)` with `a ≠ 0`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrimeHashes
signature: (p m : ℕ) → 0 < m → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.ModPrimeIndex p → ZMod p → Fin m
statement:
public def modPrimeHashes (p m : Nat) (hm : 0 < m) (ab : ModPrimeIndex p) :
    ZMod p → Fin m

docstring: The mod-prime family has `p * (p - 1)` indices.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrimeIndex_card
signature: ∀ {p : ℕ} [inst : NeZero p], Fintype.card (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.ModPrimeIndex p) = p * (p - 1)
statement:
public theorem modPrimeIndex_card {p : Nat} [NeZero p] :
    Fintype.card (ModPrimeIndex p) = p * (p - 1)

docstring:
The key counting lemma (CLRS Theorem 11.5, counting step): for distinct keys `x ≠ y`,
the number of indices `(a, b)`, `a ≠ 0`, for which `h_{a,b}` collides on `x` and `y`,
multiplied by `m`, is at most `p * (p - 1)`, the total number of indices. The
bijection `pairEquiv` identifies colliding indices with the colliding pairs counted
in `collidingPairs_mul_le`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrime_collision_mul_le
signature: ∀ {p m : ℕ} [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hm : 0 < m) {x y : ZMod p}, x ≠ y → {ab | Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrimeHashes p m hm ab x = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrimeHashes p m hm ab y}.card * m ≤ p * (p - 1)
statement:
public theorem modPrime_collision_mul_le {p m : Nat} [Fact p.Prime]
    (hm : 0 < m) {x y : ZMod p} (hxy : x ≠ y) :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : ModPrimeIndex p =>
      modPrimeHashes p m hm ab x = modPrimeHashes p m hm ab y).card * m ≤
      p * (p - 1)

docstring:
Universality of the mod-prime family (CLRS Theorem 11.5): the indexed family
`modPrimeHashes` over all `(a, b)` with `a ≠ 0` is universal. A uniformly random
index therefore collides on any two distinct keys with probability at most `1 / m`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrime_isUniversalOn
signature: ∀ {p m : ℕ} [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hm : 0 < m), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.IsUniversalOn Finset.univ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.modPrimeHashes p m hm)
statement:
public theorem modPrime_isUniversalOn {p m : Nat} [Fact p.Prime]
    (hm : 0 < m) :
    IsUniversalOn Finset.univ (modPrimeHashes p m hm)

docstring: The empty indexed family is not universal, for the same reason.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.not_isUniversalOn_empty
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {m : ℕ} {ι : Type v} (h : ι → α → Fin m), ¬Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.IsUniversalOn ∅ h
statement:
public theorem not_isUniversalOn_empty {ι : Type v} (h : ι → α → Fin m) :
    ¬ IsUniversalOn (∅ : Finset ι) h

docstring:
The empty family is not universal: universality includes nonemptiness, since
its meaning is a bound on the collision probability for a uniformly chosen member.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.not_isUniversal_empty
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {m : ℕ}, ¬Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.IsUniversal ∅
statement: public theorem not_isUniversal_empty : ¬ IsUniversal (∅ : Finset (α → Fin m))

docstring:
The core bijection of the CLRS counting argument. For fixed distinct keys `x ≠ y` in
the field `ZMod p`, solving the linear system `a * x + b = r`, `a * y + b = s` gives
`a = (r - s) / (x - y)` and `b = r - a * x`; this inverts `pairMap`. Hence the indices
`(a, b)` with `a ≠ 0` are in bijection with the ordered pairs `(r, s)` with `r ≠ s`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.pairEquiv
signature: {p : ℕ} → [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] → {x y : ZMod p} → x ≠ y → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.ModPrimeIndex p ≃ { rs // rs.1 ≠ rs.2 }
statement:
public def pairEquiv {p : Nat} [Fact p.Prime] {x y : ZMod p} (hxy : x ≠ y) :
    ModPrimeIndex p ≃ { rs : ZMod p × ZMod p // rs.1 ≠ rs.2 }

docstring: The forward direction of `pairEquiv` is `pairMap` on first components.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.pairEquiv_apply_fst
signature: ∀ {p : ℕ} [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {x y : ZMod p} (hxy : x ≠ y) (ab : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.ModPrimeIndex p), ↑((Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.pairEquiv hxy) ab) = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.pairMap x y ab

docstring:
The pair map of the CLRS counting argument: it sends an index `(a, b)` to the pair of
inner values `(a * x + b, a * y + b)` at two fixed keys.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.pairMap
signature: {p : ℕ} → ZMod p → ZMod p → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.ModPrimeIndex p → ZMod p × ZMod p
statement: public def pairMap {p : Nat} (x y : ZMod p) (ab : ModPrimeIndex p) : ZMod p × ZMod p

docstring: Extensionality form of `pairMap`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.pairMap_apply
signature: ∀ {p : ℕ} (x y : ZMod p) (ab : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.ModPrimeIndex p), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.pairMap x y ab = (↑ab.1 * x + ab.2, ↑ab.1 * y + ab.2)
statement:
public theorem pairMap_apply {p : Nat} (x y : ZMod p) (ab : ModPrimeIndex p) :
    pairMap x y ab = (ab.1.1 * x + ab.2, ab.1.1 * y + ab.2)

docstring:
For distinct keys `x ≠ y` in the field `ZMod p`, the two components of `pairMap`
differ: their difference is `a * (x - y)` with both factors nonzero.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.pairMap_fst_ne_snd
signature: ∀ {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {x y : ZMod p}, x ≠ y → ∀ (ab : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.ModPrimeIndex p), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.pairMap x y ab).1 ≠ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.pairMap x y ab).2

docstring: In particular `pairMap` is injective for distinct keys.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.pairMap_injective
signature: ∀ {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {x y : ZMod p}, x ≠ y → Function.Injective (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.UniversalHashing.pairMap x y)
statement:
public theorem pairMap_injective {p : Nat} [Fact p.Prime] {x y : ZMod p}
    (hxy : x ≠ y) : Function.Injective (pairMap x y)

docstring:
A two-level van Emde Boas tree over the universe `Fin (m * m)`: a summary
bit vector of length `m` and `m` cluster bit vectors of length `m`. This is
the two-level proto-van Emde Boas layout, not the fully recursive tree over
universes `2 ^ 2 ^ k`; see the file documentation.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas
signature: ℕ → Type
statement: public structure VanEmdeBoas (m : Nat)

docstring: The summary bit of a cluster is set exactly when the cluster is nonempty.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.Valid
signature: {m : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m → Prop
statement: public def Valid {m : Nat} (t : VanEmdeBoas m) : Prop

docstring: The finite set of stored elements.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.contents
signature: {m : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m → Finset (Fin (m * m))
statement: public def contents {m : Nat} (t : VanEmdeBoas m) : Finset (Fin (m * m))

docstring: The empty tree abstracts to the empty finite set.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.contents_empty
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.empty.contents = ∅
statement:
public theorem contents_empty {m : Nat} :
    (empty : VanEmdeBoas m).contents = ∅

docstring: Abstracting insertion is finite-set insertion.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.contents_insert
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} (x : Fin (m * m)) (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.insert x t).contents = Insert.insert x t.contents

docstring: The empty tree: every summary and cluster bit is unset.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.empty
signature: {m : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m
statement: public def empty {m : Nat} : VanEmdeBoas m

docstring: Inserts `x` by setting its cluster bit and the summary bit of its cluster.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.insert
signature: {m : ℕ} → Fin (m * m) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m
statement:
public def insert {m : Nat} (x : Fin (m * m)) (t : VanEmdeBoas m) :
    VanEmdeBoas m

docstring:
The greatest stored element: the greatest element of the last
summary-selected nonempty cluster, or `none` if no cluster is selected.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.max?
signature: {m : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m → Option (Fin (m * m))
statement: public def max? {m : Nat} (t : VanEmdeBoas m) : Option (Fin (m * m))

docstring: The empty tree has no greatest element.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.max?_empty
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.empty.max? = Option.none
statement: public theorem max?_empty {m : Nat} : (empty : VanEmdeBoas m).max? = none

docstring: In a valid tree, `max?` returns `none` exactly when nothing is stored.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.max?_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m}, t.Valid → (t.max? = Option.none ↔ ∀ (y : Fin (m * m)), t.member y = Bool.false)

docstring: In a valid tree, `max?` returns the greatest stored element.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.max?_eq_some_iff_of_valid
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m}, t.Valid → ∀ {x : Fin (m * m)}, t.max? = Option.some x ↔ t.member x = Bool.true ∧ ∀ (y : Fin (m * m)), t.member y = Bool.true → ↑y ≤ ↑x
statement:
public theorem max?_eq_some_iff_of_valid {m : Nat} {t : VanEmdeBoas m}
    (hv : t.Valid) {x : Fin (m * m)} :
    t.max? = some x ↔
      t.member x = true ∧
        ∀ y : Fin (m * m), t.member y = true → y.val ≤ x.val

docstring: In a valid tree, the element returned by `max?` follows every member.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.max?_greatest
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m}, t.Valid → ∀ {x y : Fin (m * m)}, t.max? = Option.some x → t.member y = Bool.true → ↑y ≤ ↑x

docstring: The greatest element of a singleton tree is its element.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.max?_insert_empty
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} (x : Fin (m * m)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.insert x Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.empty).max? = Option.some x
statement:
public theorem max?_insert_empty {m : Nat} (x : Fin (m * m)) :
    (insert x empty).max? = some x

docstring: The element returned by `max?` is stored in the tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.max?_mem
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m} {x : Fin (m * m)}, t.max? = Option.some x → t.member x = Bool.true
statement:
public theorem max?_mem {m : Nat} {t : VanEmdeBoas m} {x : Fin (m * m)}
    (h : t.max? = some x) : t.member x = true

docstring: The abstraction contains exactly the members of the tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.mem_contents
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m} {x : Fin (m * m)}, x ∈ t.contents ↔ t.member x = Bool.true
statement:
public theorem mem_contents {m : Nat} {t : VanEmdeBoas m} {x : Fin (m * m)} :
    x ∈ t.contents ↔ t.member x = true

docstring: Whether `x` is stored in the tree, checked in its own cluster.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.member
signature: {m : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m → Fin (m * m) → Bool
statement: public def member {m : Nat} (t : VanEmdeBoas m) (x : Fin (m * m)) : Bool

docstring: No element is a member of the empty tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.member_empty
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} (x : Fin (m * m)), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.empty.member x = Bool.false
statement:
public theorem member_empty {m : Nat} (x : Fin (m * m)) :
    (empty : VanEmdeBoas m).member x = false

docstring: Membership after insertion: the new element, or a previous member.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.member_insert
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m) (x y : Fin (m * m)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.insert x t).member y = Bool.true ↔ y = x ∨ t.member y = Bool.true

docstring: Membership is preserved by insertion of any element.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.member_insert_of_member
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m) (x y : Fin (m * m)), t.member y = Bool.true → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.insert x t).member y = Bool.true

docstring: Inserting `x` does not change membership of any other element.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.member_insert_of_ne
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {x y : Fin (m * m)}, y ≠ x → ∀ (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.insert x t).member y = t.member y

docstring: An inserted element is a member of the resulting tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.member_insert_self
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} (x : Fin (m * m)) (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.insert x t).member x = Bool.true
statement:
public theorem member_insert_self {m : Nat} (x : Fin (m * m))
    (t : VanEmdeBoas m) : (insert x t).member x = true

docstring:
The least stored element: the least element of the first summary-selected
nonempty cluster, or `none` if no cluster is selected.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.min?
signature: {m : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m → Option (Fin (m * m))
statement: public def min? {m : Nat} (t : VanEmdeBoas m) : Option (Fin (m * m))

docstring: The empty tree has no least element.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.min?_empty
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.empty.min? = Option.none
statement: public theorem min?_empty {m : Nat} : (empty : VanEmdeBoas m).min? = none

docstring: In a valid tree, `min?` returns `none` exactly when nothing is stored.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.min?_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m}, t.Valid → (t.min? = Option.none ↔ ∀ (y : Fin (m * m)), t.member y = Bool.false)

docstring: In a valid tree, `min?` returns the least stored element.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.min?_eq_some_iff_of_valid
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m}, t.Valid → ∀ {x : Fin (m * m)}, t.min? = Option.some x ↔ t.member x = Bool.true ∧ ∀ (y : Fin (m * m)), t.member y = Bool.true → ↑x ≤ ↑y
statement:
public theorem min?_eq_some_iff_of_valid {m : Nat} {t : VanEmdeBoas m}
    (hv : t.Valid) {x : Fin (m * m)} :
    t.min? = some x ↔
      t.member x = true ∧
        ∀ y : Fin (m * m), t.member y = true → x.val ≤ y.val

docstring: The least element of a singleton tree is its element.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.min?_insert_empty
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} (x : Fin (m * m)), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.insert x Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.empty).min? = Option.some x
statement:
public theorem min?_insert_empty {m : Nat} (x : Fin (m * m)) :
    (insert x empty).min? = some x

docstring: In a valid tree, the element returned by `min?` precedes every member.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.min?_least
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m}, t.Valid → ∀ {x y : Fin (m * m)}, t.min? = Option.some x → t.member y = Bool.true → ↑x ≤ ↑y

docstring: The element returned by `min?` is stored in the tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.min?_mem
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m} {x : Fin (m * m)}, t.min? = Option.some x → t.member x = Bool.true
statement:
public theorem min?_mem {m : Nat} {t : VanEmdeBoas m} {x : Fin (m * m)}
    (h : t.min? = some x) : t.member x = true

docstring:
The greatest stored element strictly below `x`: the last set position
in the cluster of `x`, else the greatest element of the previous
summary-selected nonempty cluster, else `none`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.predecessor
signature: {m : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m → Fin (m * m) → Option (Fin (m * m))
statement:
public def predecessor {m : Nat} (t : VanEmdeBoas m) (x : Fin (m * m)) :
    Option (Fin (m * m))

docstring: The empty tree has no predecessor for any element.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.predecessor_empty
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} (x : Fin (m * m)), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.empty.predecessor x = Option.none
statement:
public theorem predecessor_empty {m : Nat} (x : Fin (m * m)) :
    (empty : VanEmdeBoas m).predecessor x = none

docstring:
In a valid tree, `predecessor` returns `none` exactly when no stored
element is below `x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.predecessor_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m}, t.Valid → ∀ {x : Fin (m * m)}, t.predecessor x = Option.none ↔ ∀ (z : Fin (m * m)), t.member z = Bool.true → ↑x ≤ ↑z
statement:
public theorem predecessor_eq_none_iff {m : Nat} {t : VanEmdeBoas m}
    (hv : t.Valid) {x : Fin (m * m)} :
    t.predecessor x = none ↔
      ∀ z : Fin (m * m), t.member z = true → x.val ≤ z.val

docstring:
In a valid tree, `predecessor` returns the greatest stored element
below `x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.predecessor_eq_some_iff_of_valid
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m}, t.Valid → ∀ {x y : Fin (m * m)}, t.predecessor x = Option.some y ↔ t.member y = Bool.true ∧ ↑y < ↑x ∧ ∀ (z : Fin (m * m)), t.member z = Bool.true → ↑z < ↑x → ↑z ≤ ↑y
statement:
public theorem predecessor_eq_some_iff_of_valid {m : Nat} {t : VanEmdeBoas m}
    (hv : t.Valid) {x y : Fin (m * m)} :
    t.predecessor x = some y ↔
      t.member y = true ∧ y.val < x.val ∧
        ∀ z : Fin (m * m), t.member z = true → z.val < x.val →
          z.val ≤ y.val

docstring: In a valid tree, no member below `x` follows the returned predecessor.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.predecessor_greatest
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m}, t.Valid → ∀ {x y z : Fin (m * m)}, t.predecessor x = Option.some y → t.member z = Bool.true → ↑z < ↑x → ↑z ≤ ↑y
statement:
public theorem predecessor_greatest {m : Nat} {t : VanEmdeBoas m}
    (hv : t.Valid) {x y z : Fin (m * m)} (h : t.predecessor x = some y)
    (hz : t.member z = true) (hxz : z.val < x.val) :
    z.val ≤ y.val

docstring: The element returned by `predecessor` is strictly below `x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.predecessor_lt
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m} {x y : Fin (m * m)}, t.predecessor x = Option.some y → ↑y < ↑x

docstring: The element returned by `predecessor` is stored in the tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.predecessor_mem
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m} {x y : Fin (m * m)}, t.predecessor x = Option.some y → t.member y = Bool.true

docstring:
The least stored element strictly above `x`: the next set position in
the cluster of `x`, else the least element of the next summary-selected
nonempty cluster, else `none`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.successor
signature: {m : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m → Fin (m * m) → Option (Fin (m * m))
statement:
public def successor {m : Nat} (t : VanEmdeBoas m) (x : Fin (m * m)) :
    Option (Fin (m * m))

docstring: The empty tree has no successor for any element.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.successor_empty
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} (x : Fin (m * m)), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.empty.successor x = Option.none
statement:
public theorem successor_empty {m : Nat} (x : Fin (m * m)) :
    (empty : VanEmdeBoas m).successor x = none

docstring:
In a valid tree, `successor` returns `none` exactly when no stored
element is above `x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.successor_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m}, t.Valid → ∀ {x : Fin (m * m)}, t.successor x = Option.none ↔ ∀ (z : Fin (m * m)), t.member z = Bool.true → ↑z ≤ ↑x
statement:
public theorem successor_eq_none_iff {m : Nat} {t : VanEmdeBoas m}
    (hv : t.Valid) {x : Fin (m * m)} :
    t.successor x = none ↔
      ∀ z : Fin (m * m), t.member z = true → z.val ≤ x.val

docstring: In a valid tree, `successor` returns the least stored element above `x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.successor_eq_some_iff_of_valid
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m}, t.Valid → ∀ {x y : Fin (m * m)}, t.successor x = Option.some y ↔ t.member y = Bool.true ∧ ↑x < ↑y ∧ ∀ (z : Fin (m * m)), t.member z = Bool.true → ↑x < ↑z → ↑y ≤ ↑z
statement:
public theorem successor_eq_some_iff_of_valid {m : Nat} {t : VanEmdeBoas m}
    (hv : t.Valid) {x y : Fin (m * m)} :
    t.successor x = some y ↔
      t.member y = true ∧ x.val < y.val ∧
        ∀ z : Fin (m * m), t.member z = true → x.val < z.val →
          y.val ≤ z.val

docstring: The element returned by `successor` is strictly above `x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.successor_gt
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m} {x y : Fin (m * m)}, t.successor x = Option.some y → ↑x < ↑y

docstring: In a valid tree, no member above `x` precedes the returned successor.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.successor_least
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m}, t.Valid → ∀ {x y z : Fin (m * m)}, t.successor x = Option.some y → t.member z = Bool.true → ↑x < ↑z → ↑y ≤ ↑z
statement:
public theorem successor_least {m : Nat} {t : VanEmdeBoas m} (hv : t.Valid)
    {x y z : Fin (m * m)} (h : t.successor x = some y)
    (hz : t.member z = true) (hxz : x.val < z.val) :
    y.val ≤ z.val

docstring: The element returned by `successor` is stored in the tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.successor_mem
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m} {x y : Fin (m * m)}, t.successor x = Option.some y → t.member y = Bool.true

docstring: The empty tree satisfies the summary invariant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.valid_empty
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.empty.Valid
statement: public theorem valid_empty {m : Nat} : (empty : VanEmdeBoas m).Valid

docstring: Insertion preserves the summary invariant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.valid_insert
signature: ∀ {m : ℕ} (x : Fin (m * m)) (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas m), t.Valid → (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.VanEmdeBoas.insert x t).Valid
statement:
public theorem valid_insert {m : Nat} (x : Fin (m * m))
    (t : VanEmdeBoas m) (hv : t.Valid) : (insert x t).Valid

docstring:
The weight-balance invariant `BB[1/4]`: at every node, each child has
weight at most three quarters of the weight of the node,
`4 * weight child ≤ 3 * weight node`, written out in key counts as
`4 * (child.numNodes + 1) ≤ 3 * (left.numNodes + right.numNodes + 2)`.
See `balanced_node_iff_weight` for the same statement using `weight`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced
signature: {α : Type u} → BinaryTree α → Prop
statement: public def Balanced : BinaryTree α → Prop

docstring:
Rebuild a node from children that violate the weight invariant by at most
one inserted key, restoring balance. When the left child is too heavy, a
single right rotation is performed if the left-right grandchild is at most
twice as large as the left-left one, and a double left-right rotation
otherwise; the right-heavy case is symmetric. Children that already satisfy
the invariant are rebuilt without rotation.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.balance
signature: {α : Type u} → BinaryTree α → α → BinaryTree α → BinaryTree α
statement: public def balance (left : BinaryTree α) (key : α) (right : BinaryTree α) : BinaryTree α

docstring:
Rebalancing children that violate the weight invariant by at most the
one-key weight slack
`4 * (child.numNodes + 1) ≤ 3 * (left.numNodes + right.numNodes + 2) + 1`
produces a balanced tree. This is the precondition that one insertion
step maintains.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.balanced_balance
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {key : α} {left right : BinaryTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced left → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced right → 4 * (left.numNodes + 1) ≤ 3 * (left.numNodes + right.numNodes + 2) + 1 → 4 * (right.numNodes + 1) ≤ 3 * (left.numNodes + right.numNodes + 2) + 1 → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.balance left key right)
statement:
public theorem balanced_balance {key : α} {left right : BinaryTree α}
    (hBalLeft : Balanced left) (hBalRight : Balanced right)
    (hDiffLeft : 4 * (left.numNodes + 1) ≤ 3 * (left.numNodes + right.numNodes + 2) + 1)
    (hDiffRight : 4 * (right.numNodes + 1) ≤ 3 * (left.numNodes + right.numNodes + 2) + 1) :
    Balanced (balance left key right)

docstring: Trees built by insertion are balanced.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.balanced_fromList
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {xs : List α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.fromList xs)
statement:
public theorem balanced_fromList [LinearOrder α] {xs : List α} :
    Balanced (fromList xs)

docstring: Insertion preserves the weight-balance invariant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.balanced_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {x : α} {tree : BinaryTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced tree → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.insert x tree)
statement:
public theorem balanced_insert [LinearOrder α] {x : α} {tree : BinaryTree α}
    (hBal : Balanced tree) : Balanced (insert x tree)

docstring:
A node whose children are balanced and satisfy the weight inequalities
is balanced.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.balanced_node
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {key : α} {left right : BinaryTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced left → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced right → 4 * (left.numNodes + 1) ≤ 3 * (left.numNodes + right.numNodes + 2) → 4 * (right.numNodes + 1) ≤ 3 * (left.numNodes + right.numNodes + 2) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced (BinaryTree.node key left right)
statement:
public theorem balanced_node {key : α} {left right : BinaryTree α}
    (hLeft : Balanced left) (hRight : Balanced right)
    (hWeightLeft :
      4 * (left.numNodes + 1) ≤ 3 * (left.numNodes + right.numNodes + 2))
    (hWeightRight :
      4 * (right.numNodes + 1) ≤ 3 * (left.numNodes + right.numNodes + 2)) :
    Balanced (.node key left right)

docstring:
The node case of `Balanced`, stated with `weight`: a node is balanced
exactly when its children are balanced and each child has weight at most
three quarters of the weight of the node. This is the classical
`BB[1/4]` invariant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.balanced_node_iff_weight
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {key : α} {left right : BinaryTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced (BinaryTree.node key left right) ↔ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced left ∧ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced right ∧ 4 * Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.weight left ≤ 3 * Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.weight (BinaryTree.node key left right) ∧ 4 * Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.weight right ≤ 3 * Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.weight (BinaryTree.node key left right)
statement:
public theorem balanced_node_iff_weight {key : α} {left right : BinaryTree α} :
    Balanced (.node key left right) ↔
      Balanced left ∧ Balanced right ∧
        4 * weight left ≤ 3 * weight (.node key left right) ∧
          4 * weight right ≤ 3 * weight (.node key left right)

docstring: Build a tree by inserting the list from right to left.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.fromList
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → List α → BinaryTree α
statement: public def fromList [LinearOrder α] : List α → BinaryTree α

docstring:
The height of a balanced tree is logarithmic in its number of keys:
`BinaryTree.height tree ≤ Nat.log2 ((tree.numNodes + 1) ^ 3) + 1`. This is the
`Nat.log2` form of `pow_height_le`, using `(4 / 3) ^ 3 > 2` to pass from
base `4 / 3` to base `2`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.height_le_log2
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {tree : BinaryTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced tree → tree.height ≤ ((tree.numNodes + 1) ^ 3).log2 + 1
statement:
public theorem height_le_log2 {tree : BinaryTree α} (hBal : Balanced tree) :
    BinaryTree.height tree ≤ Nat.log2 ((tree.numNodes + 1) ^ 3) + 1

docstring:
Insert a key, leaving an existing equal key unchanged and rebalancing
every node on the search path.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.insert
signature: {α : Type u} → [LinearOrder α] → α → BinaryTree α → BinaryTree α
statement: public def insert [LinearOrder α] (x : α) : BinaryTree α → BinaryTree α

docstring: Insertion never decreases the size.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.le_numNodes_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {x : α} {tree : BinaryTree α}, tree.numNodes ≤ (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.insert x tree).numNodes
statement:
public theorem le_numNodes_insert [LinearOrder α] {x : α} {tree : BinaryTree α} :
    tree.numNodes ≤ (insert x tree).numNodes

docstring: Rebalancing preserves structural membership.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.mem_balance
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {x key : α} {left right : BinaryTree α}, x ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.balance left key right ↔ x ∈ left ∨ x = key ∨ x ∈ right
statement:
public theorem mem_balance {x key : α} {left right : BinaryTree α} :
    x ∈ balance left key right ↔ x ∈ left ∨ x = key ∨ x ∈ right

docstring: A key is in a tree built from a list exactly when it is in the list.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.mem_fromList
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {x : α} {xs : List α}, x ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.fromList xs ↔ x ∈ xs
statement:
public theorem mem_fromList [LinearOrder α] {x : α} {xs : List α} :
    x ∈ fromList xs ↔ x ∈ xs

docstring: Inserting a key adds exactly that key to structural membership.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.mem_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {x y : α} {tree : BinaryTree α}, y ∈ Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.insert x tree ↔ y = x ∨ y ∈ tree
statement:
public theorem mem_insert [LinearOrder α] {x y : α} {tree : BinaryTree α} :
    y ∈ insert x tree ↔ y = x ∨ y ∈ tree

docstring: Rebalancing does not change the number of keys.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.numNodes_balance
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {key : α} {left right : BinaryTree α}, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.balance left key right).numNodes = left.numNodes + right.numNodes + 1
statement:
public theorem numNodes_balance {key : α} {left right : BinaryTree α} :
    (balance left key right).numNodes = left.numNodes + right.numNodes + 1

docstring: The number of keys of the empty tree, for `BinaryTree.numNodes`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.numNodes_empty
signature: ∀ {α : Type u}, BinaryTree.nil.numNodes = 0
statement:
public theorem numNodes_empty :
    (BinaryTree.nil : BinaryTree α).numNodes = 0

docstring: Insertion increases the number of keys by at most one.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.numNodes_insert_le
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {x : α} {tree : BinaryTree α}, (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.insert x tree).numNodes ≤ tree.numNodes + 1
statement:
public theorem numNodes_insert_le [LinearOrder α] {x : α} {tree : BinaryTree α} :
    (insert x tree).numNodes ≤ tree.numNodes + 1

docstring: The number of keys of a node, for `BinaryTree.numNodes`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.numNodes_node
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {left right : BinaryTree α} {key : α}, (BinaryTree.node key left right).numNodes = left.numNodes + right.numNodes + 1

docstring: Rebalancing preserves the search-tree ordering invariant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.ordered_balance
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {key : α} {left right : BinaryTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.Ordered left → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.Ordered right → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.All (fun x ↦ x < key) left → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.All (fun x ↦ key < x) right → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.Ordered (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.balance left key right)
statement:
public theorem ordered_balance [LinearOrder α] {key : α} {left right : BinaryTree α}
    (hOrdLeft : BinarySearchTree.Ordered left) (hOrdRight : BinarySearchTree.Ordered right)
    (hAllLeft : BinarySearchTree.All (· < key) left) (hAllRight : BinarySearchTree.All (key < ·) right) :
    BinarySearchTree.Ordered (balance left key right)

docstring: Building a tree by insertion always produces an ordered tree.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.ordered_fromList
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {xs : List α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.Ordered (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.fromList xs)
statement:
public theorem ordered_fromList [LinearOrder α] {xs : List α} :
    BinarySearchTree.Ordered (fromList xs)

docstring: Insertion preserves the strict search-tree invariant.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.ordered_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : LinearOrder α] {x : α} {tree : BinaryTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.Ordered tree → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.BinarySearchTree.Ordered (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.insert x tree)
statement:
public theorem ordered_insert [LinearOrder α] {x : α} {tree : BinaryTree α}
    (hTree : BinarySearchTree.Ordered tree) : BinarySearchTree.Ordered (insert x tree)

docstring:
The weight of a balanced tree grows at least geometrically in its
height with ratio `4 / 3`: a balanced tree of height `k + 1` has weight
at least `(4 / 3) ^ k`, in integer form `4 ^ k ≤ 3 ^ k * weight tree`.
This is where the weight form of the invariant is used: the taller child
has weight at most three quarters of the weight of the node.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.pow_height_le
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {tree : BinaryTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.Balanced tree → ∀ (k : ℕ), tree.height = k + 1 → 4 ^ k ≤ 3 ^ k * Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.weight tree
statement:
public theorem pow_height_le {tree : BinaryTree α} (hBal : Balanced tree) :
    ∀ k : Nat, BinaryTree.height tree = k + 1 → 4 ^ k ≤ 3 ^ k * weight tree

docstring:
The Nievergelt-Reingold weight of a tree: external leaves count, so the
empty tree has weight `1` and any tree has weight one more than its number
of keys. The weight of a node is the sum of the weights of its children
(`weight_node`).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.weight
signature: {α : Type u} → BinaryTree α → ℕ
statement: public def weight (t : BinaryTree α) : Nat

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.weight_empty
signature: ∀ {α : Type u}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.weight BinaryTree.nil = 1
statement: public theorem weight_empty : weight (.nil : BinaryTree α) = 1

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.weight_node
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {left right : BinaryTree α} {key : α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.weight (BinaryTree.node key left right) = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.weight left + Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.WeightBalancedTree.weight right
statement:
public theorem weight_node {left right : BinaryTree α} {key : α} :
    weight (.node key left right) = weight left + weight right

docstring:
An x-fast trie over `w`-bit keys: the stored key set together with one prefix set per
level. The classical per-level hash tables are modeled as `Finset`s, so no O(log w)
successor bound (or any other running-time bound) is claimed.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie
signature: ℕ → Type
statement: public structure XFastTrie (w : Nat)

docstring: Every level holds exactly the prefixes of the stored keys at that length.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.Valid
signature: {w : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie w → Prop
statement: public def Valid {w : Nat} (t : XFastTrie w) : Prop

docstring: The key set after insertion is the key set with the new key inserted.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.contents_insert
signature: ∀ {w : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie w) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)), (t.insert x).contents = Insert.insert x t.contents
statement:
public theorem contents_insert {w : Nat} (t : XFastTrie w) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)) :
    (t.insert x).contents = Insert.insert x t.contents

docstring: The empty x-fast trie: no keys, every level empty.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.empty
signature: {w : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie w
statement: public def empty {w : Nat} : XFastTrie w

docstring: Whether some stored key shares the length-`l` prefix of `x`: the level-`l` probe.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.hasPrefix
signature: {w : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie w → Fin (w + 1) → Fin (2 ^ w) → Bool
statement:
public def hasPrefix {w : Nat} (t : XFastTrie w) (l : Fin (w + 1)) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)) :
    Bool

docstring: Under `Valid`, the level-`l` probe succeeds exactly on shared prefixes.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.hasPrefix_iff
signature: ∀ {w : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie w), t.Valid → ∀ (l : Fin (w + 1)) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)), t.hasPrefix l x = Bool.true ↔ ∃ y ∈ t.contents, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.prefixOf (↑l) y = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.prefixOf (↑l) x

docstring: Inserts a key and adds its prefix to every level.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.insert
signature: {w : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie w → Fin (2 ^ w) → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie w
statement: public def insert {w : Nat} (t : XFastTrie w) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)) : XFastTrie w

docstring: Membership by a single probe of the deepest level, as in the classical structure.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.member
signature: {w : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie w → Fin (2 ^ w) → Bool
statement: public def member {w : Nat} (t : XFastTrie w) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)) : Bool

docstring: Under `Valid`, the deepest-level probe decides membership exactly.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.member_iff
signature: ∀ {w : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie w), t.Valid → ∀ (x : Fin (2 ^ w)), t.member x = Bool.true ↔ x ∈ t.contents
statement:
public theorem member_iff {w : Nat} (t : XFastTrie w) (hv : t.Valid) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)) :
    t.member x = true ↔ x ∈ t.contents

docstring:
A key is a member immediately after its own insertion, with no
validity assumption on `t`: insertion puts the full-length prefix of `x`
directly into the deepest level that `member` probes.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.member_insert_self
signature: ∀ {w : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie w) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)), (t.insert x).member x = Bool.true
statement:
public theorem member_insert_self {w : Nat} (t : XFastTrie w)
    (x : Fin (2 ^ w)) : (t.insert x).member x = true

docstring: The predecessor of `x`: the greatest stored key smaller than `x`, if one exists.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.predecessor
signature: {w : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie w → Fin (2 ^ w) → Option (Fin (2 ^ w))
statement:
public def predecessor {w : Nat} (t : XFastTrie w) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)) :
    Option (Fin (2 ^ w))

docstring: The predecessor is `none` exactly when no stored key is smaller than `x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.predecessor_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {w : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie w) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)), t.predecessor x = Option.none ↔ ∀ z ∈ t.contents, ¬z < x
statement:
public theorem predecessor_eq_none_iff {w : Nat} (t : XFastTrie w) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)) :
    t.predecessor x = none ↔ ∀ z ∈ t.contents, ¬ z < x

docstring: The predecessor is `some y` exactly when `y` is the greatest stored key below `x`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.predecessor_eq_some_iff
signature: ∀ {w : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie w) (x y : Fin (2 ^ w)), t.predecessor x = Option.some y ↔ y ∈ t.contents ∧ y < x ∧ ∀ z ∈ t.contents, z < x → z ≤ y

docstring: The top `l` bits of a `w`-bit key, as a number below `2 ^ l` (for `l ≤ w`).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.XFastTrie.prefixOf
signature: {w : ℕ} → ℕ → Fin (2 ^ w) → ℕ
statement: public def prefixOf {w : Nat} (l : Nat) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)) : Nat

The successor of `x`: the least stored key greater than `x`, if one exists. Defined from

bound is claimed.

docstring:
The y-fast skeleton: an x-fast trie of representative keys, with a bucket of keys per
potential representative. In the classical structure each bucket is a balanced search
tree of Θ(w) keys; here buckets are `Finset`s, and the ordering invariant and split/merge
maintenance are deferred (see the module documentation). No complexity bound is claimed.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.YFastTrie
signature: ℕ → Type
statement: public structure YFastTrie (w : Nat)

docstring:
The representative trie is a valid x-fast trie whose keys are exactly the
owners of nonempty buckets, stated pointwise (no universe-wide filter),
and every representative is itself a stored key, in its own bucket:
representatives are sampled from the stored keys, so a representative `0`
whose bucket is `{1}` (with `contents = {1}`) is not valid. The classical
bucket ordering invariant (keys of bucket `r` lie in the interval ending
at `r`) is deferred, so this is the y-fast skeleton only.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.YFastTrie.Valid
signature: {w : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.YFastTrie w → Prop
statement: public def Valid {w : Nat} (t : YFastTrie w) : Prop

docstring:
All stored keys: the union of the representatives' buckets. Computed
from `reps.contents` (sparse), not by filtering the `2 ^ w`-element key
universe against an existential over all potential owners.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.YFastTrie.contents
signature: {w : ℕ} → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.YFastTrie w → Finset (Fin (2 ^ w))
statement: public def contents {w : Nat} (t : YFastTrie w) : Finset (Fin (2 ^ w))

docstring: A key is stored exactly when it lies in some representative's bucket.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.YFastTrie.mem_contents_iff
signature: ∀ {w : ℕ} (t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.YFastTrie w) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)), x ∈ t.contents ↔ ∃ r ∈ t.reps.contents, x ∈ t.buckets r
statement:
public theorem mem_contents_iff {w : Nat} (t : YFastTrie w) (x : Fin (2 ^ w)) :
    x ∈ t.contents ↔ ∃ r ∈ t.reps.contents, x ∈ t.buckets r

docstring:
Under validity, a key is stored exactly when it lies in some bucket
(the bucket's owner is then necessarily a representative).
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.YFastTrie.mem_contents_iff_exists_of_valid
signature: ∀ {w : ℕ} {t : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.YFastTrie w}, t.Valid → ∀ (x : Fin (2 ^ w)), x ∈ t.contents ↔ ∃ r, x ∈ t.buckets r

docstring: Under validity, every representative is a stored key.

docstring: `binSearchContains` is the Boolean view of `binSearch`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.binSearchContains_eq_isSome
signature: ∀ {α : Type} (as : Array α) (k : α) (lt : α → α → Bool) (lo hi : ℕ), as.binSearchContains k lt lo hi = (as.binSearch k lt lo hi).isSome
statement:
theorem binSearchContains_eq_isSome {α : Type} (as : Array α) (k : α)
    (lt : α → α → Bool) (lo hi : Nat) :
    as.binSearchContains k lt lo hi = (as.binSearch k lt lo hi).isSome

docstring:
On a sorted array, bounded `binSearchContains` is true exactly when the key occurs at a valid
index between the inclusive raw bounds.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.binSearchContains_eq_true_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type} [inst : LinearOrder α] {as : Array α}, Array.Pairwise (fun a b ↦ a ≤ b) as → ∀ {k : α} {lo hi : ℕ}, as.binSearchContains k (fun x y ↦ Decidable.decide (x < y)) lo hi = Bool.true ↔ ∃ i, ∃ (h : i < as.size), lo ≤ i ∧ i ≤ hi ∧ as[i] = k
statement:
theorem binSearchContains_eq_true_iff {α : Type} [LinearOrder α] {as : Array α}
    (hs : as.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≤ b)) {k : α} {lo hi : Nat} :
    as.binSearchContains k (fun x y => decide (x < y)) lo hi = true ↔
      ∃ i, ∃ h : i < as.size, lo ≤ i ∧ i ≤ hi ∧ as[i] = k

docstring: Full-range `binSearchContains` is true exactly when the key belongs to the array.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.binSearchContains_eq_true_iff_mem
signature: ∀ {α : Type} [inst : LinearOrder α] {as : Array α}, Array.Pairwise (fun a b ↦ a ≤ b) as → ∀ {k : α}, (as.binSearchContains k fun x y ↦ Decidable.decide (x < y)) = Bool.true ↔ k ∈ as

docstring:
On a sorted array, bounded binary search returns `none` exactly when the key has no occurrence
at a valid index between the inclusive raw bounds.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.binSearch_eq_none_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type} [inst : LinearOrder α] {as : Array α}, Array.Pairwise (fun a b ↦ a ≤ b) as → ∀ {k : α} {lo hi : ℕ}, as.binSearch k (fun x y ↦ Decidable.decide (x < y)) lo hi = Option.none ↔ ¬∃ i, ∃ (h : i < as.size), lo ≤ i ∧ i ≤ hi ∧ as[i] = k
statement:
theorem binSearch_eq_none_iff {α : Type} [LinearOrder α] {as : Array α}
    (hs : as.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≤ b)) {k : α} {lo hi : Nat} :
    as.binSearch k (fun x y => decide (x < y)) lo hi = none ↔
      ¬∃ i, ∃ h : i < as.size, lo ≤ i ∧ i ≤ hi ∧ as[i] = k

docstring: Full-range binary search returns `none` exactly when the key is absent.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.binSearch_eq_none_iff_not_mem
signature: ∀ {α : Type} [inst : LinearOrder α] {as : Array α}, Array.Pairwise (fun a b ↦ a ≤ b) as → ∀ {k : α}, (as.binSearch k fun x y ↦ Decidable.decide (x < y)) = Option.none ↔ k ∉ as

docstring:
On a sorted array, bounded binary search returns `a` exactly when `a` is the key and the key
occurs at a valid index between the inclusive raw bounds. The validity condition on the index
expresses the implementation's clamping of an oversized upper bound.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.binSearch_eq_some_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type} [inst : LinearOrder α] {as : Array α}, Array.Pairwise (fun a b ↦ a ≤ b) as → ∀ {k a : α} {lo hi : ℕ}, as.binSearch k (fun x y ↦ Decidable.decide (x < y)) lo hi = Option.some a ↔ a = k ∧ ∃ i, ∃ (h : i < as.size), lo ≤ i ∧ i ≤ hi ∧ as[i] = k
statement:
theorem binSearch_eq_some_iff {α : Type} [LinearOrder α] {as : Array α}
    (hs : as.Pairwise (fun a b => a ≤ b)) {k a : α} {lo hi : Nat} :
    as.binSearch k (fun x y => decide (x < y)) lo hi = some a ↔
      a = k ∧ ∃ i, ∃ h : i < as.size, lo ≤ i ∧ i ≤ hi ∧ as[i] = k

docstring:
Full-range binary search returns `a` exactly when `a` is the key and the key belongs to the
array.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.binSearch_eq_some_iff_mem
signature: ∀ {α : Type} [inst : LinearOrder α] {as : Array α}, Array.Pairwise (fun a b ↦ a ≤ b) as → ∀ {k a : α}, (as.binSearch k fun x y ↦ Decidable.decide (x < y)) = Option.some a ↔ a = k ∧ k ∈ as

signature: ∀ {heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.MinHeap Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanPriority} {choice : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTwoMin}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.extractTwoMin? heap = Option.some choice → (∀ item ∈ heap.elements, choice.first ≤ item) ∧ ∀ item ∈ choice.second ::ₘ choice.rest.elements, choice.second ≤ item

      (∀ item ∈ choice.second ::ₘ choice.rest.elements, choice.second ≤ item)

signature: {α : Type u} → ℕ → ℕ → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.MinHeap Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanPriority → Array (Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWorkItem α)) → Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α)

docstring:
Instrumented Huffman execution that reports indexed payload-table reads on
successful runs. Each call to `takeSerial?` performs one `table[serial]?` read.
The count excludes heap operations, table writes (cell clearing and merged-item
insertion), and the terminal `huffmanTableForest` scan.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffmanLoopWithLookupCount
signature: {α : Type u} → ℕ → ℕ → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.MinHeap Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanPriority → Array (Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWorkItem α)) → Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α × ℕ)

docstring:
Accumulator form of `huffmanLoopWithLookupCount`: `count` is the number
of indexed reads already performed, threaded through the recursion so a
successful run uses constant stack in `fuel` just like `huffmanLoop`.
`huffmanLoopWithLookupCount` is the `count = 0` special case, and
`huffmanLoopWithLookupCountAux_eq` is its characteristic equation.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffmanLoopWithLookupCountAux
signature: {α : Type u} → ℕ → ℕ → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.MinHeap Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanPriority → Array (Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWorkItem α)) → ℕ → Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α × ℕ)

name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffmanLoopWithLookupCountAux_eq
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (fuel nextSerial : ℕ) (heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.MinHeap Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanPriority) (table : Array (Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWorkItem α))) (count : ℕ), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffmanLoopWithLookupCountAux fuel nextSerial heap table count = Option.map (fun tree ↦ (tree, 2 * fuel + 1 + count)) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffmanLoop fuel nextSerial heap table)
statement:
theorem huffmanLoopWithLookupCountAux_eq {α : Type u} (fuel nextSerial : Nat)
    (heap : MinHeap HuffmanPriority) (table : Array (Option (HuffmanWorkItem α)))
    (count : Nat) :
    huffmanLoopWithLookupCountAux fuel nextSerial heap table count =
      (huffmanLoop fuel nextSerial heap table).map fun tree => (tree, 2 * fuel + 1 + count)

docstring:
Instrumenting the loop preserves its result and, on success, reports two
indexed payload reads per merge followed by one final indexed read.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffmanLoopWithLookupCount_eq
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (fuel nextSerial : ℕ) (heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.MinHeap Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanPriority) (table : Array (Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWorkItem α))), Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffmanLoopWithLookupCount fuel nextSerial heap table = Option.map (fun tree ↦ (tree, 2 * fuel + 1)) (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffmanLoop fuel nextSerial heap table)
statement:
theorem huffmanLoopWithLookupCount_eq {α : Type u} (fuel nextSerial : Nat)
    (heap : MinHeap HuffmanPriority) (table : Array (Option (HuffmanWorkItem α))) :
    huffmanLoopWithLookupCount fuel nextSerial heap table =
      (huffmanLoop fuel nextSerial heap table).map fun tree => (tree, 2 * fuel + 1)

docstring: Forgetting the instrumentation yields exactly the existing loop result.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffmanLoopWithLookupCount_map_fst
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} (fuel nextSerial : ℕ) (heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.MinHeap Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanPriority) (table : Array (Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWorkItem α))), Option.map Prod.fst (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffmanLoopWithLookupCount fuel nextSerial heap table) = Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffmanLoop fuel nextSerial heap table
statement:
theorem huffmanLoopWithLookupCount_map_fst {α : Type u} (fuel nextSerial : Nat)
    (heap : MinHeap HuffmanPriority) (table : Array (Option (HuffmanWorkItem α))) :
    (huffmanLoopWithLookupCount fuel nextSerial heap table).map Prod.fst =
      huffmanLoop fuel nextSerial heap table

docstring: A successful loop performs exactly `2 * fuel + 1` indexed payload reads.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffmanLoop_lookupCount
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {fuel nextSerial : ℕ} {heap : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.MinHeap Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanPriority} {table : Array (Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWorkItem α))} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffmanLoop fuel nextSerial heap table = Option.some tree → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffmanLoopWithLookupCount fuel nextSerial heap table = Option.some (tree, 2 * fuel + 1)

docstring:
The tree returned by `huffman` also minimizes the structural
encoded-length objective, including the one-bit singleton code; by

cost whenever the leaf symbols are unique.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffman_encodedLength_optimal
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq α] {input : List (α × ℕ)} {tree competitor : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.huffman input = Option.some tree → competitor.Admissible input → tree.encodedLength ≤ competitor.encodedLength

    (hresult : huffman input = some tree)
    (hcompetitor : competitor.Admissible input) :
    tree.encodedLength ≤ competitor.encodedLength

signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {input : List (α × ℕ)} {tree competitor : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWeightTree.MergeTrace ↑(List.map (fun pair ↦ ↑pair.2) input) ↑tree.weightedPathLength → competitor.Admissible input → tree.weightedPathLength ≤ competitor.weightedPathLength

docstring:
Return the optimum common-subsequence length and one witness, using prefix dynamic programming.
The abstract time counts interior table transitions and nonterminal reconstruction transitions.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.longestCommonSubsequence
signature: {α : Type u} → [BEq α] → List α → List α → Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM ℕ (ℕ × List α)
statement:
def longestCommonSubsequence {α : Type u} [BEq α] (xs ys : List α) :
    TimeM Nat (Nat × List α)

docstring: The reported length equals the witness length, and the witness is a longest common sublist.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.longestCommonSubsequence_correct
statement:
theorem longestCommonSubsequence_correct {α : Type u} [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α]
    (xs ys : List α) :
    let result := (longestCommonSubsequence xs ys).ret
    result.2.length = result.1 ∧ result.2 <+ xs ∧ result.2 <+ ys ∧
      (∀ zs, zs <+ xs → zs <+ ys → zs.length ≤ result.2.length)

docstring: The number of table and reconstruction transitions is at most `m*n + (m+n)`.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.longestCommonSubsequence_time
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : BEq α] (xs ys : List α), (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.longestCommonSubsequence xs ys).time ≤ xs.length * ys.length + (xs.length + ys.length)
statement:
theorem longestCommonSubsequence_time {α : Type u} [BEq α] (xs ys : List α) :
    (longestCommonSubsequence xs ys).time ≤ xs.length * ys.length + (xs.length + ys.length)

docstring: Taking one serial leaves every other table cell unchanged.
name: Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.takeSerial?_getElem?_of_ne
signature: ∀ {α : Type u} {serial : ℕ} {table remaining : Array (Option (Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanWorkItem α))} {tree : Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.HuffmanTree α}, Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.takeSerial? serial table = Option.some (tree, remaining) → ∀ {j : ℕ}, j ≠ serial → remaining[j]? = table[j]?

docstring: A work item stored at its own serial can always be taken from the table.

docstring: Taking a serial removes exactly the work item stored at that index.
