docstring:
For a Banach space `E` over `𝕜 = ℝ` or `ℂ`, finite-dimensional `M ↪ E**` via `iM`, `N ↪ E*` via
`iN`, and `ε > 0`, there exists `T : M →L[𝕜] E` that is `(1+ε)`-almost isometric, preserves dual
pairings `(iN n)(T m) = (iM m)(iN n)`, and fixes `J(E)`: `iM m = J x → T m = x`. Source: J.
Lindenstrauss and H. Rosenthal, Israel J. Math. 7 (1969) 325-349, principle of local reflexivity;
Johnson-Rosenthal-Zippin 1971 refinements; Albiac and Kalton, Topics in Banach Space Theory; Lean
states `RCLike` Banach finite- dimensional `M, N` version with `(1+ε)`-isometry and pairing
preservation.

Proves `Wanted` entry `principle_of_local_reflexivity`.

Proof: Helly's lemma applied to finitely many linear conditions plus one norm bound, then a finite
δ-net of the unit sphere of `range iM` turns net-point bounds into the `(1+ε)` bounds (the
elementary proof in Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*).
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.FunctionalAnalysis.LocalReflexivityWanted.principle_of_local_reflexivity
signature: ∀ {𝕜 : Type u_2} [inst : RCLike 𝕜] {E : Type u_3} [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_2 : NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] {M : Type u_4} [inst_4 : NormedAddCommGroup M] [inst_5 : NormedSpace 𝕜 M] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 M] {N : Type u_5} [inst_7 : NormedAddCommGroup N] [inst_8 : NormedSpace 𝕜 N] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 N] (iM : M →L[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E)) (iN : N →L[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 E), Function.Injective ⇑iM → Function.Injective ⇑iN → ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∃ T, (∀ (m : M), (1 + ε)⁻¹ * ‖iM m‖ ≤ ‖T m‖ ∧ ‖T m‖ ≤ (1 + ε) * ‖iM m‖) ∧ (∀ (m : M) (n : N), (iN n) (T m) = (iM m) (iN n)) ∧ ∀ (m : M) (x : E), iM m = (NormedSpace.inclusionInDoubleDual 𝕜 E) x → T m = x
statement:
public theorem principle_of_local_reflexivity
    {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜]
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E]
    {M : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace 𝕜 M] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 M]
    {N : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup N] [NormedSpace 𝕜 N] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 N]
    (iM : M →L[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E))
    (iN : N →L[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 E)
    (hM_inj : Function.Injective iM)
    (hN_inj : Function.Injective iN)
    (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ (T : M →L[𝕜] E),
      (∀ m : M, (1 + ε)⁻¹ * ‖iM m‖ ≤ ‖T m‖ ∧ ‖T m‖ ≤ (1 + ε) * ‖iM m‖)
      ∧ (∀ (m : M) (n : N), (iN n) (T m) = (iM m) (iN n))
      ∧ (∀ (m : M) (x : E), iM m = NormedSpace.inclusionInDoubleDual 𝕜 E x → T m = x)

docstring:
In an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space `E`, if `K ≠ 0` is compact and `T : E →L[ℂ] E`
commutes with `K`, then `T` has a nontrivial proper closed `ℂ`-invariant subspace `M` with `M ≠
⊥`, `M ≠ ⊤`, `IsClosed M`, `T '' M ⊆ M`. Source: V. Lomonosov, Functional Anal. Appl. 7 (1973)
and J. Hilden elementary proof, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.; Aronszajn-Smith 1954 precursor;
Radjavi-Rosenthal invariant subspace book, 1973; Lean states complex Banach infinite-dimensional
case `K≠0` compact commuting with `T` yields nontrivial closed invariant subspace.

docstring:
A commuting family of continuous affine self-maps preserving a nonempty compact convex set in a
real normed space has a common fixed point in the set; commutation is required globally on `E`.
Source: A. Markov, C. R. Acad. Sci. URSS 1936 and S. Kakutani, Proc. Imp. Acad. Tokyo 14 (1938)
242-245, Markov-Kakutani fixed-point theorem; Lean states real normed nonempty compact convex case
with globally commuting `E →ᴬ[ℝ] E` family.

docstring:
If `E` is a uniformly convex Banach space over `𝕜 = ℝ` or `ℂ`, then every continuous linear
functional on the dual `E →L[𝕜] 𝕜` is evaluation at some `x : E`, i.e. `∃ x, ∀ f, Φ f = f x`.
Source: D. Milman, C. R. (Doklady) Acad. Sci. URSS 18 (1938) and B. Pettis, Duke Math. J. 1939,
Milman-Pettis theorem that uniformly convex Banach spaces are reflexive; Clarkson uniform
convexity 1936; Lean states `RCLike` uniformly convex complete case via double-dual evaluation
surjectivity.

docstring:
For strictly increasing `Λ : ℕ → ℕ` with `Λ 0 = 0`, the real span of monomials `x ↦ x^(Λ n)` is
dense in `C(I, ℝ)` (`I = [0, 1]`) for the sup norm iff the reciprocal sum of positive exponents
diverges, i.e. `¬Summable (fun n => (Λ (n+1) : ℝ)⁻¹)`. Source: C. Müntz, Festschrift H. A. Schwarz
1914 303-312 and O. Szász, Math. Ann. 77 (1916) 482-496, Müntz-Szász theorem; Rudin Real &
Complex; Lean states integer-exponent `ℕ→ℕ` `StrictMono` with `0∈range` case as closure `= ⊤` iff
non-summable reciprocals.

docstring:
For `1 ≤ q < p < ∞` and `𝕜 = ℝ` or `ℂ`, every bounded linear operator `T : lp (fun _ : ℕ => 𝕜) p
→L[𝕜] lp (fun _ : ℕ => 𝕜) q` from `ℓ^p(ℕ, 𝕜)` to `ℓ^q(ℕ, 𝕜)` is compact. Source: H. R. Pitt,
A Note on Bilinear Forms, J. London Math. Soc. s1-11 (1936), 174–180,
DOI 10.1112/JLMS/S1-11.3.174, compactness of operators `ℓ^p → ℓ^q` for `q<p`; textbook Albiac
and Kalton, Topics in Banach Space Theory Prop 2.1.6; Lean states `RCLike` `lp _ p →L[𝕜] lp _ q`
with `q<p<∞` compact specialization via `IsCompactOperator`.

docstring:
For finite `ι, κ` with counting measure, if `T : (ι → ℂ) →ₗ[ℂ] (κ → ℂ)` has `ℓ^{p₀} → ℓ^{q₀}`
bound `M₀` and `ℓ^{p₁} → ℓ^{q₁}` bound `M₁` and `1/p = (1-θ)/p₀ + θ/p₁`, `1/q = (1-θ)/q₀ + θ/q₁`
with `θ ∈ [0, 1]`, then `eLpNorm (T f) q ≤ (M₀^(1-θ) * M₁^θ) * eLpNorm f p` for all `f`. Source:
M. Riesz, Sur les maxima des formes bilinéaires et sur les fonctionnelles linéaires,
Acta Math. 49 (1927), 465–497, DOI 10.1007/BF02564121; and G. O. Thorin, Convexity theorems
generalizing those of M. Riesz and Hadamard with some applications,
Comm. Sem. Math. Univ. Lund 9 (1948), 1–58, Riesz-Thorin interpolation theorem; Stein-Shakarchi
Complex interpolation; Lean states finite counting-measure complex `→ₗ[ℂ]` form with explicit
interpolation identities `p⁻¹=(1-θ)p₀⁻¹+θp₁⁻¹` and bound `M₀^(1-θ)M₁^θ`.

Proves `Wanted` entry `riesz_thorin`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.FunctionalAnalysis.RieszThorinWanted.riesz_thorin
signature: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [inst : MeasurableSpace ι] [inst_1 : MeasurableSpace κ] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass κ] {p₀ p₁ q₀ q₁ p q : ENNReal} {θ : ℝ}, 0 ≤ θ → θ ≤ 1 → 1 ≤ p₀ → 1 ≤ p₁ → 1 ≤ p → 1 ≤ q₀ → 1 ≤ q₁ → 1 ≤ q → p⁻¹ = ENNReal.ofReal (1 - θ) * p₀⁻¹ + ENNReal.ofReal θ * p₁⁻¹ → q⁻¹ = ENNReal.ofReal (1 - θ) * q₀⁻¹ + ENNReal.ofReal θ * q₁⁻¹ → ∀ {M₀ M₁ : ENNReal} (T : (ι → ℂ) →ₗ[ℂ] κ → ℂ), (∀ (f : ι → ℂ), MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (T f) q₀ MeasureTheory.Measure.count ≤ M₀ * MeasureTheory.eLpNorm f p₀ MeasureTheory.Measure.count) → (∀ (f : ι → ℂ), MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (T f) q₁ MeasureTheory.Measure.count ≤ M₁ * MeasureTheory.eLpNorm f p₁ MeasureTheory.Measure.count) → ∀ (f : ι → ℂ), MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (T f) q MeasureTheory.Measure.count ≤ M₀ ^ (1 - θ) * M₁ ^ θ * MeasureTheory.eLpNorm f p MeasureTheory.Measure.count
statement:
theorem riesz_thorin
    {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]
    [MeasurableSpace ι] [MeasurableSpace κ]
    [MeasurableSingletonClass ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass κ]
    {p₀ p₁ q₀ q₁ p q : ENNReal}
    {θ : ℝ} (hθ₀ : 0 ≤ θ) (hθ₁ : θ ≤ 1)
    (hp₀ : 1 ≤ p₀) (hp₁ : 1 ≤ p₁) (hp : 1 ≤ p)
    (hq₀ : 1 ≤ q₀) (hq₁ : 1 ≤ q₁) (hq : 1 ≤ q)
    (hp_eq : p⁻¹ = ENNReal.ofReal (1 - θ) * p₀⁻¹ + ENNReal.ofReal θ * p₁⁻¹)
    (hq_eq : q⁻¹ = ENNReal.ofReal (1 - θ) * q₀⁻¹ + ENNReal.ofReal θ * q₁⁻¹)
    {M₀ M₁ : ENNReal}
    (T : (ι → Complex) →ₗ[Complex] (κ → Complex))
    (h₀ : ∀ f : ι → Complex,
      eLpNorm (T f) q₀ (Measure.count : Measure κ) ≤
        M₀ * eLpNorm f p₀ (Measure.count : Measure ι))
    (h₁ : ∀ f : ι → Complex,
      eLpNorm (T f) q₁ (Measure.count : Measure κ) ≤
        M₁ * eLpNorm f p₁ (Measure.count : Measure ι)) :
    ∀ f : ι → Complex,
      eLpNorm (T f) q (Measure.count : Measure κ) ≤
        (M₀ ^ (1 - θ) * M₁ ^ θ) * eLpNorm f p (Measure.count : Measure ι)

docstring:
Finite-hypothesis form of `riesz_thorin` below: the same interpolation bound
under `[Finite ι] [Finite κ]`, installing `Fintype.ofFinite` locally where finite
sums require it. `riesz_thorin` is the `Fintype` specialization, proved from this.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.FunctionalAnalysis.RieszThorinWanted.riesz_thorin_finite

    {ι κ : Type*} [Finite ι] [Finite κ]

    {θ : ℝ} (hθ₀ : 0 ≤ θ) (hθ₁ : θ ≤ 1)

docstring:
Every bounded sequence `x` in a Banach space over `𝕜 = ℝ` or `ℂ` has a strictly increasing
subsequence `φ` such that `x ∘ φ` is either weakly Cauchy (`f (x (φ n))` Cauchy for every `f : E
→L[𝕜] 𝕜`) or has a uniform `ℓ¹` lower bound. Source: H. P. Rosenthal,
A Characterization of Banach Spaces Containing l1, PNAS 71 (1974), 2411–2413,
DOI 10.1073/pnas.71.6.2411, ℓ¹ dichotomy theorem; Bourgain et al., extensions; Lean states
`RCLike` Banach bounded `Set.range` dichotomy with `StrictMono φ` and `HasUniformL1LowerBound`
defined via `ℕ →₀ 𝕜` finitely supported coefficients.

Proves `Wanted` entry `rosenthal_l1`.

Proof: We use the Nash-Williams/Galvin-Prikry Ramsey route, following Rosenthal's 1974 theorem,
Albiac and Kalton, Sections 10.1–10.2, and Farahat's 1974 proof.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.FunctionalAnalysis.RosenthalL1Wanted.rosenthal_l1
signature: ∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} [inst : RCLike 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_2 : NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] (x : ℕ → E), Bornology.IsBounded (Set.range x) → ∃ φ, ∃ (_ : StrictMono φ), (∀ (f : E →L[𝕜] 𝕜) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∃ N, ∀ (m n : ℕ), N ≤ m → N ≤ n → ‖f (x (φ m)) - f (x (φ n))‖ < ε) ∨ MathlibExt.Analysis.FunctionalAnalysis.RosenthalL1Wanted.HasUniformL1LowerBound (x ∘ φ)
statement:
public theorem rosenthal_l1
    {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜]
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E]
    (x : ℕ → E) (hx : Bornology.IsBounded (Set.range x)) :
    ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (_ : StrictMono φ),
      (∀ (f : E →L[𝕜] 𝕜) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
        ∃ N, ∀ m n, N ≤ m → N ≤ n → ‖f (x (φ m)) - f (x (φ n))‖ < ε) ∨
      HasUniformL1LowerBound (𝕜 := 𝕜) (x ∘ φ)

docstring: Source: A. M. Gleason, Measures on the closed subspaces of a Hilbert space, J. Math. Mech. 6 (1957), 885-893. Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `gleason_theorem_finite`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.GleasonWanted.Analysis.gleason_theorem_finite
signature: ∀ {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : FiniteDimensional ℂ H], 3 ≤ Module.finrank ℂ H → ∀ (f : MathlibExt.Analysis.GleasonWanted.Analysis.FrameFunction H), ∃! ρ, ρ.IsPositive ∧ MathlibExt.Analysis.GleasonWanted.Analysis.reTr ρ = 1 ∧ ∀ (P : H →L[ℂ] H), MathlibExt.Analysis.GleasonWanted.Analysis.IsOrthProj P → f.μ P = MathlibExt.Analysis.GleasonWanted.Analysis.reTr (ρ * P)
statement:
public theorem_wanted gleason_theorem_finite
    {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
      [CompleteSpace H] [FiniteDimensional ℂ H]
    (hdim : 3 ≤ Module.finrank ℂ H)
    (f : FrameFunction H) :
    ∃! ρ : H →L[ℂ] H,
      ContinuousLinearMap.IsPositive ρ ∧
      reTr ρ = 1 ∧
      ∀ P : H →L[ℂ] H, IsOrthProj P → f.μ P = reTr (ρ * P)

name: MathlibExt.Analysis.GleasonWanted.Analysis.gleason_theorem_separable
signature: ∀ {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace H], 3 ≤ Module.rank ℂ H → ∀ (f : MathlibExt.Analysis.GleasonWanted.Analysis.SphereFrameFunction H), ∃ ρ, ρ.IsPositive ∧ ∀ (x : ↑(Metric.sphere 0 1)), f.f x = (Inner.inner ℂ (↑x) (ρ ↑x)).re
statement:
public theorem_wanted gleason_theorem_separable
    {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
      [CompleteSpace H] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace H]
    (hdim : 3 ≤ Module.rank ℂ H)

docstring:
Resolved false: Miles and Williamson (J. London Math. Soc. (2) 33 (1986) 110-116) proved that a
transcendental entire f with positive coefficients and int_0^inf a_n x^n/f(x) dx = 1 for all n

exists. Source: Antonio Greco and Andrea Loi, Radial balanced metrics on the unit disk,
arXiv:0803.3711 (2008), https://arxiv.org/abs/0803.3711. Moved from

are two points at which `f` is differentiable (analytic points of the
meromorphic germ) with different values. This excludes pointwise-modified
constant representatives (for example `f 0 = 1`, `f z = 0` elsewhere),
which are meromorphic with zero derivative density but represent the
constant-zero germ.

docstring:
[AMR-022-1016] Hayman's question: is
`liminf_{r → ∞} n(r)/A(r) = 1` for every globally meromorphic,
nonconstant `f` with bounded root counts at each radius?
The known bounds `1 ≤ liminf n(r)/A(r) ≤ e` are not formalized here.

signature: Prop

docstring:
Resolved false: Toppila constructed a nonconstant meromorphic function with liminf n(r)/A(r) >=
80/79, and Hinkkanen and Miles (arXiv:2401.13808, 2024, Theorem 1.1) give one with liminf
n(r)/A(r) >= 1.07328, so the universal claim liminf = 1 is false. Source: A. Hinkkanen and J.
Miles, Maximum and Average Valence of Meromorphic Functions, arXiv preprint (2024),
arXiv:2401.13808, https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.13808. Moved from
`OpenConjectures/Analysis/HaymanSphericalAreaRatio`.

docstring: Source: Classical heat-equation theory. Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `heat_kernel_solves_heat_equation`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.HeatKernelWanted.Analysis.ODE.heat_kernel_solves_heat_equation
signature: ∀ (f : ℝ → ℝ), Continuous f → (∃ M, ∀ (x : ℝ), |f x| ≤ M) → (∀ (t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∀ (x : ℝ), ∃ ux uxx, (∀ (y : ℝ), HasDerivAt (fun z ↦ MathlibExt.Analysis.HeatKernelWanted.Analysis.ODE.heatSolution f t z) (ux y) y) ∧ HasDerivAt ux uxx x ∧ HasDerivAt (fun s ↦ MathlibExt.Analysis.HeatKernelWanted.Analysis.ODE.heatSolution f s x) uxx t) ∧ ∀ (x : ℝ), Filter.Tendsto (fun t ↦ MathlibExt.Analysis.HeatKernelWanted.Analysis.ODE.heatSolution f t x) (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds (f x))
statement:
public theorem_wanted heat_kernel_solves_heat_equation
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf_cont : Continuous f) (hf_bdd : ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ M) :
    -- The PDE on (0, ∞) × ℝ.
    (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ∀ x : ℝ, ∃ ux : ℝ → ℝ, ∃ uxx : ℝ,
        (∀ y : ℝ, HasDerivAt (fun z => heatSolution f t z) (ux y) y) ∧
        HasDerivAt ux uxx x ∧
        HasDerivAt (fun s => heatSolution f s x) uxx t) ∧
    -- Initial condition recovered as a one-sided limit at t = 0.
    (∀ x : ℝ,
        Filter.Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => heatSolution f t x)
          (nhdsWithin (0 : ℝ) (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds (f x)))

docstring:
Real-analytic orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the circle,
modeled by its degree-one lift F : ℝ → ℝ to the universal cover.
Characteristic properties: analyticity of the lift and of the inverse lift,
degree-one periodicity F (x + 1) = F x + 1 (circle map), two-sided inverse
(diffeomorphism), and strict monotonicity (orientation-preserving).
Cites: Hayman (2018), Problem 2.90; https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

Poincaré rotation number of a circle-map lift F : ℝ → ℝ: the mean motion

Cites: Hayman (2018), Problem 2.90; https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

there exists an analytic orientation-preserving circle diffeomorphism H whose

Diophantine condition on a real number, in the standard inhomogeneous
approximation sense: some margin γ > 0 and exponent τ ≥ 0 bound
|α - p / q| from below by γ / q ^ (2 + τ) for all integers p and all
positive integers q.
Cites: Hayman (2018), Problem 2.90; https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

docstring:
Hayman Problem 2.90 (M. R. Herman): does there exist an irrational number
α satisfying no diophantine condition such that every ℝ-analytic
orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the circle with rotation number α
is ℝ-analytically conjugated to a rotation?
Cites: Hayman (2018), Problem 2.90; https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

Resolved true: Yoccoz (Analytic linearization of circle diffeomorphisms, LNM 1784, 2002)
characterized the Herman class H of rotation numbers for which every analytic circle
diffeomorphism is analytically linearizable and proved CD strictly contained in H; any alpha in
H minus CD is the required non-Diophantine number. Source: H. Eliasson, B. Fayad and R.
Krikorian, Jean-Christophe Yoccoz and the theory of circle diffeomorphisms (2018),
arXiv:1810.07107 (account of J.-C. Yoccoz, Analytic linearization of circle diffeomorphisms,
Lecture Notes in Math. 1784, Springer (2002), 125-173), https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.07107. Moved
from `OpenConjectures/Analysis/HermanProblem290`.

linear map from `E` to `E` defined by the identity:

`⟨Hf(x) u, v⟩ = D²f(x) (u,v)`.

where `D²f(x)` is the second Frechet derivative of `f` within `s` at `x` as a bilinear operator.

docstring:
Statement of Theorem 1.1:

There exists a function `C : ℝ≥0∞ → ℝ` such that if `u : ℝ⁴ → ℝ` satisfies the following properties:
* `u` is smooth on `B₁(0)`,
* `‖u‖_{C¹(B₁(0))} < ∞` (the definition of this norm is given above), and
* for all `x ∈ B₁(0)`, `(Δ u) x > 0` and `(σ₂ D²u) x = 1`,
then `‖D² u 0‖_F ≤ C(‖u‖_{C¹})`.
Source: R. Shankar and Y. Yuan, `Hessian estimates for the sigma-2 equation in dimension four`, Annals of Math, 201 (2) 2025. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2025-201-2-HessianEstimates.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_hessian_estimates`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.HessianEstimatesWanted.HessianEstimates.theorem_1_1
signature: ∃ C, ∀ (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4) → ℝ), ContDiffOn ℝ (↑⊤) u (Metric.ball 0 1) → MathlibExt.Analysis.HessianEstimatesWanted.HessianEstimates.eC1NormOn u (Metric.ball 0 1) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume < ⊤ → (∀ x ∈ Metric.ball 0 1, Laplacian.laplacian u x > 0) → (∀ x ∈ Metric.ball 0 1, MathlibExt.Analysis.HessianEstimatesWanted.HessianEstimates.σ₂ (MathlibExt.Analysis.HessianEstimatesWanted.HessianEstimates.H u (Metric.ball 0 1) x) = 1) → MathlibExt.Analysis.HessianEstimatesWanted.HessianEstimates.frobeniusNorm (MathlibExt.Analysis.HessianEstimatesWanted.HessianEstimates.H u (Metric.ball 0 1) 0) ≤ C (MathlibExt.Analysis.HessianEstimatesWanted.HessianEstimates.eC1NormOn u (Metric.ball 0 1) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume)
statement:
public theorem_wanted theorem_1_1 : ∃ C : ℝ≥0∞ → ℝ, ∀ (u : ℝ⁴ → ℝ)
    (_smooth : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ u B₁(0))
    (_bounded : ‖u‖_C¹(B₁(0)) < (∞ : ℝ≥0∞))
    (_positive_branch : ∀ x ∈ B₁(0), (Δ u) x > 0)
    (_solution : ∀ x ∈ B₁(0), σ₂ (H u B₁(0) x) = 1),
    ‖H u B₁(0) 0‖_F ≤ C (‖u‖_C¹(B₁(0)))

docstring:
Spectral theorem for bounded self-adjoint operators, multiplication-operator form: a
self-adjoint `T : E →L[ℂ] E` is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by a real-valued
measurable function on some `L²`. Sources: Mathlib
`Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Spectrum.lean` TODO (spectral theory for bounded
self-adjoint operators); W. Rudin, Functional Analysis, 2nd ed., Ch. 12.

Proves `Wanted` entry `boundedSelfAdjoint_spectral_multiplication`.

Proof: Scalar measures from the continuous functional calculus identify each cyclic subspace with an
`L²` space. A maximal orthogonal family of cyclic subspaces is then assembled over a disjoint-union
measure, where the spectral coordinate acts by multiplication.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.BoundedSelfAdjointSpectralWanted.boundedSelfAdjoint_spectral_multiplication
signature: ∀ {E : Type u} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ E] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace E] (T : E →L[ℂ] E), IsSelfAdjoint T → ∃ X x μ φ, ∃ (_ : Measurable φ), ∃ U, ∀ (x_2 : E), ∀ᵐ (a : X) ∂μ, ↑↑(U (T x_2)) a = ↑(φ a) * ↑↑(U x_2) a
statement:
theorem boundedSelfAdjoint_spectral_multiplication
    {E : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    (T : E →L[ℂ] E) (hT : IsSelfAdjoint T) :
    ∃ (X : Type u) (_ : MeasurableSpace X) (μ : Measure X) (φ : X → ℝ) (_ : Measurable φ)
      (U : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] Lp ℂ 2 μ),
      ∀ x, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, U (T x) a = (φ a : ℂ) * U x a

docstring:
A compact normal `T : E →L[ℂ] E` on a complex Hilbert space admits a Hilbert basis `b` with
eigenvalues `μ` vanishing at infinity and `T (b i) = μ i • b i`, with index type in the same
universe as `E`. Source: Compact normal spectral theorem, Hilbert-Schmidt and Riesz 1910s;
Reed-Simon I; Rudin Functional Analysis; Lean states complex Hilbert compact `IsStarNormal` case
with same finite-level-set vanishing condition and same-universe index.

Proves `Wanted` entry `compactNormal_hilbertBasis`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.CompactSpectralWanted.compactNormal_hilbertBasis
signature: ∀ {E : Type uE} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ E] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace E] (T : E →L[ℂ] E), IsCompactOperator ⇑T → IsStarNormal T → ∃ ι b μ, (∀ ε > 0, {i | ε ≤ ‖μ i‖}.Finite) ∧ ∀ (i : ι), T (b i) = μ i • b i
statement:
theorem compactNormal_hilbertBasis
    {E : Type uE} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    (T : E →L[ℂ] E) (hT_compact : IsCompactOperator T)
    (hT_normal : IsStarNormal T) :
    ∃ (ι : Type uE) (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ E) (μ : ι → ℂ),
      (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), Set.Finite { i | ε ≤ ‖μ i‖ }) ∧
      (∀ i, T (b i) = μ i • b i)

docstring:
Eckart-Young best rank-`k` approximation in operator norm: the infimum operator-norm distance from
`T` to linear maps `S` of `finrank` at most `k` equals `T.singularValues k`.
Source: C. Eckart and G. Young, The Approximation of One Matrix by Another of Lower Rank,
Psychometrika 1 (1936), 211-218, DOI 10.1007/BF02288367; unitary-invariant extension L. Mirsky, QJM
11 (1960), DOI 10.1093/qmath/11.1.50.

Proves `Wanted` entry `eckartYoung_best_rank_approx_operator_norm`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.EckartYoungWanted.eckartYoung_best_rank_approx_operator_norm
signature: ∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} [inst : RCLike 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_2 : InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [inst_3 : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] {F : Type u_3} [inst_4 : NormedAddCommGroup F] [inst_5 : InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F] [inst_6 : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 F] (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) (k : ℕ), InfSet.sInf {r | ∃ S, Module.finrank 𝕜 ↥S.range ≤ k ∧ r = ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (T - S)‖} = T.singularValues k
statement:
theorem eckartYoung_best_rank_approx_operator_norm
    (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) (k : ℕ) :
    sInf
        { r : ℝ |
          ∃ S : E →ₗ[𝕜] F,
            Module.finrank 𝕜 S.range ≤ k ∧
              r = ‖(T - S).toContinuousLinearMap‖ } =
      T.singularValues k

docstring:
Hoffman-Wielandt for Hermitian matrices: `∑ (λ_A i - λ_B i)^2 ≤ ‖A - B‖_F^2`.
Source: A. J. Hoffman and H. W. Wielandt, Duke Math. J. 20 (1953), DOI
10.1215/S0012-7094-53-02004-3.

Proves `Wanted` entry `hoffman_wielandt_hermitian`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.HoffmanWielandtWanted.hoffman_wielandt_hermitian
statement:
theorem hoffman_wielandt_hermitian
    {n : ℕ} (A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ)
    (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) :
    let hA_sym := (Matrix.isSymmetric_toEuclideanLin_iff.mpr hA)
    let hB_sym := (Matrix.isSymmetric_toEuclideanLin_iff.mpr hB)
    ∑ i : Fin n, (hA_sym.eigenvalues finrank_euclideanSpace_fin i -
        hB_sym.eigenvalues finrank_euclideanSpace_fin i) ^ 2 ≤
      ∑ i : Fin n, ∑ j : Fin n, Complex.normSq (A i j - B i j)

docstring:
For a real inner-product space `E` (not necessarily complete) and a complete real inner-product
space `F`, every `K`-Lipschitz map `f : E → F` on a set `s` extends to a globally `K`-Lipschitz
map `g : E → F` with `EqOn f g s` and the same constant `K`. Source: M. Kirszbraun, Fund. Math.
22 (1934) 77-108 thesis; Valentine 1945 extension to Hilbert; Federer, Geometric Measure Theory,
2.10.43; the Lean theorem takes a real inner-product-space domain `E` and a complete real
inner-product-space target `F`, with the same Lipschitz constant `LipschitzWith K`.

docstring:
The sum of the first `k` entries of `eig : Fin n → ℝ`. Applied to the eigenvalues of a
Hermitian matrix, listed in decreasing order, it is the sum of the `k` largest ones.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.KyFanWanted.eigPrefSum
signature: {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → ℝ) → (k : ℕ) → k ≤ n → ℝ

    (hk : k ≤ n) : ℝ

name: MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.KyFanWanted.eigPrefSum_eq_sum
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (eig : Fin n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n), MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.KyFanWanted.eigPrefSum eig k hk = ∑ i, eig (Fin.castLE hk i)
statement:
theorem eigPrefSum_eq_sum {n : ℕ} (eig : Fin n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) :
    eigPrefSum eig k hk = ∑ i : Fin k, eig (Fin.castLE hk i)

name: MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.KyFanWanted.eigPrefSum_succ
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (eig : Fin n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k + 1 ≤ n), MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.KyFanWanted.eigPrefSum eig (k + 1) hk = MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.KyFanWanted.eigPrefSum eig k ⋯ + eig ⟨k, hk⟩
statement:
theorem eigPrefSum_succ {n : ℕ} (eig : Fin n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k + 1 ≤ n) :
    eigPrefSum eig (k + 1) hk = eigPrefSum eig k (Nat.le_of_succ_le hk) + eig ⟨k, hk⟩

docstring:
Schur's theorem (Schur–Horn direction): the real diagonal of a self-adjoint operator in any
orthonormal basis is a doubly-stochastic image of its eigenvalues, hence majorized by the
eigenvalues.
Source: I. Schur, 1923, Über eine Klasse von Mittelbildungen mit Anwendungen auf die
Determinantentheorie; A. Horn, Doubly Stochastic Matrices and the Diagonal of a Rotation Matrix,
Amer. J. Math. 76 (1954), 620–630, DOI 10.2307/2372705.
Proves `Wanted` entry `schur_diagonal_eigenvalues_doublyStochastic`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.SchurHorn.schur_diagonal_eigenvalues_doublyStochastic
signature: ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ E] [inst_2 : FiniteDimensional ℂ E] {n : ℕ} (T : E →ₗ[ℂ] E) (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : Module.finrank ℂ E = n) (b : OrthonormalBasis (Fin n) ℂ E), ∃ D ∈ doublyStochastic ℝ (Fin n), (fun i ↦ RCLike.re (Inner.inner ℂ (b i) (T (b i)))) = D.mulVec (hT.eigenvalues hn)
statement:
theorem schur_diagonal_eigenvalues_doublyStochastic
    {n : ℕ} (T : E →ₗ[ℂ] E) (hT : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hn : Module.finrank ℂ E = n)
    (b : OrthonormalBasis (Fin n) ℂ E) :
    ∃ D : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ,
      D ∈ doublyStochastic ℝ (Fin n) ∧
        (fun i => RCLike.re (inner (𝕜 := ℂ) (b i) (T (b i))) : Fin n → ℝ) =
          D.mulVec (hT.eigenvalues hn)

DOI 10.1007/BF01292610.

signature: ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] (f : E → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 f → MathlibExt.Analysis.MountainPassWanted.Analysis.MountainPassProblem.PalaisSmale f → ∀ {a b : E} {ε r : ℝ}, MathlibExt.Analysis.MountainPassWanted.Analysis.MountainPassProblem.MountainRange f a b ε r → ∃ x, MathlibExt.Analysis.MountainPassWanted.Analysis.MountainPassProblem.IsCriticalPoint f x ∧ f x = MathlibExt.Analysis.MountainPassWanted.Analysis.MountainPassProblem.mountainPassLevel f a b ∧ ε ≤ MathlibExt.Analysis.MountainPassWanted.Analysis.MountainPassProblem.mountainPassLevel f a b
statement:
public theorem_wanted mountain_pass (f : E → ℝ) (_hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f) (_hps : PalaisSmale f)
    {a b : E} {ε r : ℝ} (_hmr : MountainRange f a b ε r) :
    ∃ x : E, IsCriticalPoint f x ∧
      f x = mountainPassLevel f a b ∧ ε ≤ mountainPassLevel f a b

docstring:
**Nyquist--Shannon sampling theorem / Whittaker--Shannon interpolation
formula** for Schwartz functions with Fourier support in the mathlib-convention
Nyquist band `[-1/2, 1/2]`.

The explicit `Summable` conjunct records the convergence content of the
cardinal series, rather than relying only on Lean's total `tsum`.
Source: C. E. Shannon, *Communication in the presence of noise*, Proc. IRE 37 (1949); H. Nyquist (1928); E. T. Whittaker (1915). Knill, *Some fundamental theorems in mathematics*, §179. Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `nyquist_shannon_sampling`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.NyquistShannonWanted.Analysis.NyquistShannon.nyquist_shannon_sampling
signature: ∀ (f : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ), MathlibExt.Analysis.NyquistShannonWanted.Analysis.NyquistShannon.FourierSupportedInNyquist f → ∀ (t : ℝ), (Summable fun n ↦ f ↑n * MathlibExt.Analysis.NyquistShannonWanted.Analysis.NyquistShannon.sinc (Real.pi * (↑n - t))) ∧ f t = ∑' (n : ℤ), f ↑n * MathlibExt.Analysis.NyquistShannonWanted.Analysis.NyquistShannon.sinc (Real.pi * (↑n - t))
statement:
public theorem_wanted nyquist_shannon_sampling (f : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (hf : FourierSupportedInNyquist f) :
    ∀ t : ℝ,
      Summable (fun n : ℤ ↦ f (n : ℝ) * sinc (Real.pi * ((n : ℝ) - t))) ∧
        f t =
          ∑' n : ℤ, f (n : ℝ) * sinc (Real.pi * ((n : ℝ) - t))

docstring:
Duhamel's formula (variation of constants): for a bounded linear operator
`A` and continuous forcing `b`, the function built from the operator
exponential solves `x' = A x + b` from `x₀`, and it is the unique solution.
Sources: `Mathlib/docs/undergrad.yaml`, section `Multivariable calculus` /
`Differential equations`, entry `method of constant variation
(Duhamel's formula)` (unmapped);
G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems, Section 3.2;
stable ref https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duhamel%27s_principle.

Proves `Wanted` entry `duhamel_variation_of_constants`.

Proof: Factor the propagator by the commuting exponential group law, differentiate the
integrating-factor primitive, and apply global Lipschitz uniqueness. This follows Teschl,
Sections 3.2 and 3.4, formula (3.48) and Theorem 3.12 / (3.97).
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.ODE.DuhamelWanted.duhamel_variation_of_constants
signature: ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] (A : E →L[ℝ] E) (b : ℝ → E) (t₀ : ℝ) (x₀ : E), Continuous b → ∃ x, x t₀ = x₀ ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ), x t = (NormedSpace.exp ((t - t₀) • A)) x₀ + ∫ (s : ℝ) in t₀..t, (NormedSpace.exp ((t - s) • A)) (b s)) ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ), HasDerivAt x (A (x t) + b t) t) ∧ ∀ (y : ℝ → E), y t₀ = x₀ → (∀ (t : ℝ), HasDerivAt y (A (y t) + b t) t) → y = x

theorem duhamel_variation_of_constants
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    (A : E →L[ℝ] E) (b : ℝ → E) (t₀ : ℝ) (x₀ : E)

docstring:
Explicit Euler is first-order convergent: for a `C^2` right-hand side,
Lipschitz in the state, a true solution exists on `[t₀, T]` and the Euler
polygonal approximations have global error `O(h)` with a uniform constant.
Sources: `Mathlib/docs/undergrad.yaml`, section `Numerical Analysis` /
`Ordinary differential equations`, entries `explicit Euler method`,
`convergence` and `order` (unmapped);
E. Hairer, S. P. Nørsett and G. Wanner, Solving Ordinary Differential
Equations I, 2nd ed., Theorem I.7.3;
stable ref https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_method.

Proves `Wanted` entry `explicit_euler_first_order_convergence`.

Proof: clamp the time variable and use global Picard--Lindelöf for existence.  The local bound
above and Mathlib's discrete Grönwall inequality then give the first-order global estimate.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.ODE.ExplicitEulerWanted.explicit_euler_first_order_convergence
signature: ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] (f : ℝ → E → E) (t₀ T : ℝ) (x₀ : E) (L : NNReal), t₀ < T → ContDiff ℝ 2 (Function.uncurry f) → (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc t₀ T, LipschitzWith L (f t)) → ∃ x, x t₀ = x₀ ∧ (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc t₀ T, HasDerivAt x (f t (x t)) t) ∧ ∃ C, ∀ h ∈ Set.Ioc 0 (T - t₀), ∀ (X : ℕ → E), X 0 = x₀ → (∀ (n : ℕ), X (n + 1) = X n + h • f (t₀ + ↑n * h) (X n)) → ∀ (n : ℕ), ↑n * h ≤ T - t₀ → ‖X n - x (t₀ + ↑n * h)‖ ≤ C * h
statement:
theorem explicit_euler_first_order_convergence
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    (f : ℝ → E → E) (t₀ T : ℝ) (x₀ : E) (L : NNReal)
    (hT : t₀ < T)
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 (Function.uncurry f))
    (hlip : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc t₀ T, LipschitzWith L (f t)) :
    ∃ x : ℝ → E, x t₀ = x₀ ∧ (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc t₀ T, HasDerivAt x (f t (x t)) t) ∧
      ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ h ∈ Set.Ioc 0 (T - t₀), ∀ X : ℕ → E, X 0 = x₀ →
        (∀ n, X (n + 1) = X n + h • f (t₀ + (n : ℝ) * h) (X n)) →
        ∀ n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) * h ≤ T - t₀ →
          ‖X n - x (t₀ + (n : ℝ) * h)‖ ≤ C * h

docstring:
Explicit Euler consistency: one step from the exact solution has local
truncation error `O(h^2)`.
Sources: `Mathlib/docs/undergrad.yaml`, section `Numerical Analysis` /
`Ordinary differential equations`, entry `consistency` (unmapped);
E. Hairer, S. P. Nørsett and G. Wanner, Solving Ordinary Differential
Equations I, 2nd ed., Section I.7.

Proves `Wanted` entry `explicit_euler_local_truncation_error`.

Proof: differentiate the velocity by the chain rule, bound that derivative on the compact time
interval, and apply the mean value inequality twice.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.ODE.ExplicitEulerWanted.explicit_euler_local_truncation_error
signature: ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] (f : ℝ → E → E) (t₀ T : ℝ) (x₀ : E), t₀ < T → ContDiff ℝ 2 (Function.uncurry f) → ∀ (x : ℝ → E), x t₀ = x₀ → (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc t₀ T, HasDerivAt x (f t (x t)) t) → ∃ C, ∀ h ∈ Set.Ioc 0 (T - t₀), ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc t₀ T, t + h ≤ T → ‖x (t + h) - (x t + h • f t (x t))‖ ≤ C * h ^ 2
statement:
theorem explicit_euler_local_truncation_error
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    (f : ℝ → E → E) (t₀ T : ℝ) (x₀ : E)
    (hT : t₀ < T)
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 (Function.uncurry f))
    (x : ℝ → E) (hx0 : x t₀ = x₀)
    (hx : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc t₀ T, HasDerivAt x (f t (x t)) t) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ h ∈ Set.Ioc 0 (T - t₀), ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc t₀ T, t + h ≤ T →
      ‖x (t + h) - (x t + h • f t (x t))‖ ≤ C * h ^ 2

docstring:
Fundamental matrix of a linear ODE system: for continuous `A`, there is a
matrix solution `Φ` of `Φ' = A Φ` with `Φ t₀ = 1`, everywhere invertible,
and every solution of `x' = A x` is a `Φ`-multiple of its initial value.
Sources: `Mathlib/docs/undergrad.yaml`, section `Multivariable calculus` /
`Differential equations`, entry `linear differential systems` (unmapped);
G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems, Section 3.4;
stable ref https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamental_matrix_(linear_differential_equation).

Proves `Wanted` entry `fundamental_matrix_linear_system`.

Proof: Global solutions are patched from clamped-time systems using Teschl, Theorem 3.9, then
assembled into the principal matrix solution of (3.83) and Theorem 3.10. Liouville's formula gives
invertibility as in (3.88)-(3.89).
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.ODE.LinearSystemFundamentalMatrixWanted.fundamental_matrix_linear_system
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (A : ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (t₀ : ℝ), Continuous A → ∃ Φ, Φ t₀ = 1 ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ), HasDerivAt Φ (A t * Φ t) t) ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ), IsUnit (Φ t).det) ∧ ∀ (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ), ∃ x, x t₀ = x₀ ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ), HasDerivAt x ((A t).mulVec (x t)) t) ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ), x t = (Φ t).mulVec x₀) ∧ ∀ (y : ℝ → Fin n → ℝ), y t₀ = x₀ → (∀ (t : ℝ), HasDerivAt y ((A t).mulVec (y t)) t) → y = x
statement:
theorem fundamental_matrix_linear_system
    {n : ℕ} (A : ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (t₀ : ℝ)
    (hA : Continuous A) :
    ∃ Φ : ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ, Φ t₀ = 1 ∧
      (∀ t, HasDerivAt Φ (A t * Φ t) t) ∧
      (∀ t, IsUnit (Φ t).det) ∧
      ∀ x₀ : Fin n → ℝ, ∃ x : ℝ → (Fin n → ℝ),
        x t₀ = x₀ ∧ (∀ t, HasDerivAt x ((A t).mulVec (x t)) t) ∧
        (∀ t, x t = (Φ t).mulVec x₀) ∧
        ∀ y : ℝ → (Fin n → ℝ), y t₀ = x₀ →
          (∀ t, HasDerivAt y ((A t).mulVec (y t)) t) → y = x

docstring:
Liouville (Abel) formula: the Wronskian determinant of a fundamental
matrix grows by the exponential of the integrated trace.
Sources: `Mathlib/docs/undergrad.yaml`, section `Multivariable calculus` /
`Differential equations`, entry `linear differential systems` (unmapped);
G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems, Section 3.4;
stable ref https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel%27s_identity.

Proves `Wanted` entry `fundamental_matrix_liouville_det`.

Proof: Jacobi's formula follows from the determinant's first-order term; an integrating factor then
gives Teschl, Lemma 3.11, formula (3.91).
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.ODE.LinearSystemFundamentalMatrixWanted.fundamental_matrix_liouville_det
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (A : ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (t₀ : ℝ), Continuous A → ∀ (Φ : ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), Φ t₀ = 1 → (∀ (t : ℝ), HasDerivAt Φ (A t * Φ t) t) → ∀ (t : ℝ), (Φ t).det = (Φ t₀).det * Real.exp (∫ (s : ℝ) in t₀..t, (A s).trace)
statement:
theorem fundamental_matrix_liouville_det
    {n : ℕ} (A : ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (t₀ : ℝ)
    (hA : Continuous A)
    (Φ : ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
    (hΦ0 : Φ t₀ = 1) (hΦ : ∀ t, HasDerivAt Φ (A t * Φ t) t) :
    ∀ t, (Φ t).det = (Φ t₀).det * Real.exp (∫ s in t₀..t, (A s).trace)

docstring:
Global existence and uniqueness for globally Lipschitz right-hand sides.
Sources: `Mathlib/docs/undergrad.yaml`, section `Multivariable calculus` /
`Differential equations`, entry `maximal solutions` (unmapped);
G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems, Section 2.2;
stable ref https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picard%E2%80%93Lindel%C3%B6f_theorem.

Proves `Wanted` entry `ode_global_exists_of_global_lipschitz`.

Proof: local Picard--Lindelöf solutions are continued using the Gronwall bound of Teschl's
Theorem 2.17 and the extension criterion of Lemma 2.14.  Time reversal supplies the
negative-time solution, and global Gronwall uniqueness identifies every solution with the glued
one.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.ODE.MaximalSolutionWanted.ode_global_exists_of_global_lipschitz
signature: ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] (f : ℝ → E → E) (t₀ : ℝ) (x₀ : E) (L : NNReal), Continuous (Function.uncurry f) → (∀ (t : ℝ), LipschitzWith L (f t)) → ∃! x, x t₀ = x₀ ∧ ∀ (t : ℝ), HasDerivAt x (f t (x t)) t
statement:
theorem ode_global_exists_of_global_lipschitz
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    (f : ℝ → E → E) (t₀ : ℝ) (x₀ : E) (L : NNReal)
    (hfcont : Continuous (Function.uncurry f))
    (hlip : ∀ t, LipschitzWith L (f t)) :

docstring:
Maximal solutions exit compacts: an ODE whose right-hand side is locally
Lipschitz in the state variable, locally uniformly in time, on an open set
admits a solution on a maximal open interval which, at each end, eventually
leaves every compact subset of the domain.
Sources: `Mathlib/docs/undergrad.yaml`, section `Multivariable calculus` /
`Differential equations`, entries `maximal solutions` and
`exit theorem of a compact subspace` (unmapped);
G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems,
Section 2.4.

Proves `Wanted` entry `ode_maximal_solution_exit_compact`.

Proof: local Picard--Lindelöf solutions are glued by uniqueness into Teschl's maximal solution
(Theorem 2.13).  A compactly recurrent finite endpoint extends by Lemma 2.14, giving the two exit
statements of Corollaries 2.15--2.16.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.ODE.MaximalSolutionWanted.ode_maximal_solution_exit_compact
signature: ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] (U : Set (ℝ × E)) (f : ℝ × E → E) (t₀ : ℝ) (x₀ : E), IsOpen U → (t₀, x₀) ∈ U → ContinuousOn f U → (∀ p ∈ U, ∃ C, ∃ s ∈ nhds p, ∀ (t : ℝ) (x y : E), (t, x) ∈ s ∩ U → (t, y) ∈ s ∩ U → Dist.dist (f (t, x)) (f (t, y)) ≤ ↑C * Dist.dist x y) → ∃ I x, x t₀ = x₀ ∧ IsOpen I ∧ t₀ ∈ I ∧ (∀ t₁ ∈ I, ∀ t₂ ∈ I, Set.Icc t₁ t₂ ⊆ I) ∧ (∀ t ∈ I, (t, x t) ∈ U ∧ HasDerivAt x (f (t, x t)) t) ∧ ∀ (K : Set (ℝ × E)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → (∃ c ∈ I, ∀ t ∈ I, c ≤ t → (t, x t) ∉ K) ∧ ∃ c ∈ I, ∀ t ∈ I, t ≤ c → (t, x t) ∉ K
statement:
theorem ode_maximal_solution_exit_compact
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    (U : Set (ℝ × E)) (f : ℝ × E → E) (t₀ : ℝ) (x₀ : E)
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hmem : (t₀, x₀) ∈ U)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f U)
    (hlip : ∀ p ∈ U, ∃ C : NNReal, ∃ s ∈ nhds p,
      ∀ t : ℝ, ∀ x y : E, (t, x) ∈ s ∩ U → (t, y) ∈ s ∩ U →
        dist (f (t, x)) (f (t, y)) ≤ C * dist x y) :
    ∃ I : Set ℝ, ∃ x : ℝ → E, x t₀ = x₀ ∧ IsOpen I ∧ t₀ ∈ I ∧
      (∀ t₁ ∈ I, ∀ t₂ ∈ I, Set.Icc t₁ t₂ ⊆ I) ∧
      (∀ t ∈ I, (t, x t) ∈ U ∧ HasDerivAt x (f (t, x t)) t) ∧
      ∀ K : Set (ℝ × E), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U →
        (∃ c ∈ I, ∀ t ∈ I, c ≤ t → (t, x t) ∉ K) ∧
        ∃ c ∈ I, ∀ t ∈ I, t ≤ c → (t, x t) ∉ K

docstring:
Picard iteration converges: for a continuous right-hand side, globally
Lipschitz in the state, the Picard iterates from the constant map converge
pointwise to a global solution.
Sources: `Mathlib/docs/undergrad.yaml`, section `Numerical Analysis` /
`Iterative methods of solving systems of real and vector-valued equations`,
entry `Picard method` (unmapped);
G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems, Section 2.3;
stable ref https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picard%E2%80%93Lindel%C3%B6f_theorem.

Proves `Wanted` entry `picard_iterates_converge`.

Proof: Sum the factorially bounded successive differences, obtaining locally uniform convergence
on every compact time interval. Pass the recursion through the integral and apply the fundamental
theorem of calculus. This is the argument of Teschl, Theorem 2.5 and Corollary 2.6 (Section 2.3),
for the Picard iterates (2.13) of Section 2.2, with a constant global Lipschitz constant.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.ODE.PicardIterationWanted.picard_iterates_converge
signature: ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] (f : ℝ → E → E) (t₀ : ℝ) (x₀ : E) (L : NNReal), Continuous (Function.uncurry f) → (∀ (t : ℝ), LipschitzWith L (f t)) → ∀ (u : ℕ → ℝ → E), (u 0 = fun x ↦ x₀) → (∀ (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ), u (n + 1) t = x₀ + ∫ (s : ℝ) in t₀..t, f s (u n s)) → ∃ x, x t₀ = x₀ ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ), HasDerivAt x (f t (x t)) t) ∧ ∀ (t : ℝ), Filter.Tendsto (fun n ↦ u n t) Filter.atTop (nhds (x t))
statement:
theorem picard_iterates_converge
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    (f : ℝ → E → E) (t₀ : ℝ) (x₀ : E) (L : NNReal)
    (hfcont : Continuous (Function.uncurry f))
    (hlip : ∀ t, LipschitzWith L (f t))
    (u : ℕ → ℝ → E) (hu0 : u 0 = fun _ => x₀)
    (hu : ∀ n t, u (n + 1) t = x₀ + ∫ s in t₀..t, f s (u n s)) :
    ∃ x : ℝ → E, x t₀ = x₀ ∧ (∀ t, HasDerivAt x (f t (x t)) t) ∧
      ∀ t, Filter.Tendsto (fun n => u n t) Filter.atTop (nhds (x t))

docstring:
Picard step estimate: successive iterates differ by at most
`M * L^n * |t - t₀|^(n+1) / (n+1)!`.
Sources: `Mathlib/docs/undergrad.yaml`, section `Numerical Analysis` /
`Iterative methods of solving systems of real and vector-valued equations`,
entries `Picard method` and `rate of convergence and estimation of error`
(unmapped); G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems,
Section 2.3.

Proves `Wanted` entry `picard_iterates_step_estimate`.

Proof: Induct on the iterate index, apply the Lipschitz bound under the interval integral, and
integrate the absolute-power majorant exactly, as in the induction for estimate (2.29) in the proof
of Teschl, Theorem 2.5 (Section 2.3).
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.ODE.PicardIterationWanted.picard_iterates_step_estimate
signature: ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] (f : ℝ → E → E) (t₀ : ℝ) (x₀ : E) (L : NNReal), Continuous (Function.uncurry f) → (∀ (t : ℝ), LipschitzWith L (f t)) → ∀ (u : ℕ → ℝ → E), (u 0 = fun x ↦ x₀) → (∀ (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ), u (n + 1) t = x₀ + ∫ (s : ℝ) in t₀..t, f s (u n s)) → ∀ (M : ℝ), (∀ (s : ℝ), ‖f s x₀‖ ≤ M) → ∀ (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ), ‖u (n + 1) t - u n t‖ ≤ M * ↑L ^ n * |t - t₀| ^ (n + 1) / ↑(n + 1).factorial
statement:
theorem picard_iterates_step_estimate
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (f : ℝ → E → E) (t₀ : ℝ) (x₀ : E) (L : NNReal)
    (hfcont : Continuous (Function.uncurry f))
    (hlip : ∀ t, LipschitzWith L (f t))
    (u : ℕ → ℝ → E) (hu0 : u 0 = fun _ => x₀)
    (hu : ∀ n t, u (n + 1) t = x₀ + ∫ s in t₀..t, f s (u n s))
    (M : ℝ) (hM : ∀ s, ‖f s x₀‖ ≤ M) :
    ∀ n t, ‖u (n + 1) t - u n t‖ ≤
      M * (L : ℝ) ^ n * |t - t₀| ^ (n + 1) / (Nat.factorial (n + 1) : ℝ)

statement:
theorem picard_iterates_tendsto_of_hasDerivAt
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    (f : ℝ → E → E) (t₀ : ℝ) (x₀ : E) (L : NNReal)

docstring: Source: L. V. Kantorovich (1942), after G. Monge (1781). Listed as §73 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `monge_kantorovich`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.OptimalTransportWanted.Analysis.monge_kantorovich_exists
signature: ∀ {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2} [inst : TopologicalSpace X] [PolishSpace X] [inst_2 : MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [inst_4 : TopologicalSpace Y] [PolishSpace Y] [inst_6 : MeasurableSpace Y] [BorelSpace Y] (P : MeasureTheory.Measure X) (Q : MeasureTheory.Measure Y) [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure Q] (c : X × Y → ENNReal), Continuous c → ∃ π ∈ MathlibExt.Analysis.OptimalTransportWanted.Analysis.Couplings P Q, ∀ π' ∈ MathlibExt.Analysis.OptimalTransportWanted.Analysis.Couplings P Q, MathlibExt.Analysis.OptimalTransportWanted.Analysis.kantorovichCost c π ≤ MathlibExt.Analysis.OptimalTransportWanted.Analysis.kantorovichCost c π'
statement:
public theorem_wanted monge_kantorovich_exists
    {X Y : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace X] [PolishSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]
    [TopologicalSpace Y] [PolishSpace Y] [MeasurableSpace Y] [BorelSpace Y]
    (P : Measure X) (Q : Measure Y)
    [IsProbabilityMeasure P] [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]

docstring:
A real `α` is **Diophantine** if there are `C > 0` and `τ : ℝ` such
that `C / |q|^τ ≤ |α − p/q|` for all integers `p, q` with `q ≠ 0`. The
exponent τ is implicitly ≥ 2 by Dirichlet's theorem. This implies α is
irrational, so `e^{2πiα}` is not a root of unity.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.PoincareSiegelWanted.ComplexAnalysis.IsDiophantine
signature: ℝ → Prop
statement: def IsDiophantine (α : ℝ) : Prop

docstring: Source: C. L. Siegel, *Iteration of analytic functions*, Annals of Math. 43 (1942), 607-612. Earlier formal-power-series version: H. Poincaré thèse (1879). Listed as §83 (additional statement 1) in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `poincare_siegel_linearisation`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.PoincareSiegelWanted.ComplexAnalysis.poincare_siegel
signature: ∀ (α : ℝ), MathlibExt.Analysis.PoincareSiegelWanted.ComplexAnalysis.IsDiophantine α → ∀ (lam : ℂ), lam = Complex.exp (2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I * ↑α) → ∀ (f : ℂ → ℂ), AnalyticAt ℂ f 0 → f 0 = 0 → deriv f 0 = lam → ∃ u, AnalyticAt ℂ u 0 ∧ u 0 = 0 ∧ deriv u 0 = 1 ∧ ∀ᶠ (z : ℂ) in nhds 0, f (u z) = u (lam * z)
statement:
public theorem_wanted poincare_siegel
    (α : ℝ) (_hα : IsDiophantine α)
    (lam : ℂ) (_hlam : lam = Complex.exp (2 * Real.pi * Complex.I * (α : ℂ)))
    (f : ℂ → ℂ) (_hf : AnalyticAt ℂ f 0) (_hf0 : f 0 = 0)
    (_hmult : deriv f 0 = lam) :
    ∃ u : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ u 0 ∧ u 0 = 0 ∧ deriv u 0 = 1 ∧
      ∀ᶠ z in nhds (0 : ℂ), f (u z) = u (lam * z)

docstring:
The defining binomial recurrence for even Euler numbers:
`∑_{k = 0}^m (2m).choose (2k) * E_k` is `1` for `m = 0` and `0` otherwise.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry10bEuleriansymmetry.chapter5EulerEven_recurrence
signature: ∀ (m : ℕ), ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), ↑((2 * m).choose (2 * k)) * MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry10bEuleriansymmetry.chapter5EulerEven k = if m = 0 then 1 else 0
statement:
theorem chapter5EulerEven_recurrence (m : ℕ) :
    ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (m + 1),
      ((Nat.choose (2 * m) (2 * k) : ℕ) : ℤ) * chapter5EulerEven k =
      if m = 0 then 1 else 0

docstring: Unfolding of `E_m` for `m ≠ 0` as a signed binomial sum over earlier values.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry10bEuleriansymmetry.chapter5EulerEven_step
signature: ∀ (m : ℕ), m ≠ 0 → MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry10bEuleriansymmetry.chapter5EulerEven m = -∑ k, ↑((2 * m).choose (2 * ↑k)) * MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry10bEuleriansymmetry.chapter5EulerEven ↑k
statement:
theorem chapter5EulerEven_step (m : ℕ) (hm : m ≠ 0) :
    chapter5EulerEven m =
      -∑ k : Fin m, (Nat.choose (2 * m) (2 * k.val) : ℤ) * chapter5EulerEven k.val

name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry10bEuleriansymmetry.ramanujan_part1_ch5_entry10b_euleriansymmetry
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ^ (2 * n) * (2 ^ (2 * n) - 1) * bernoulli (2 * n) = ↑(2 * n) * ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, ↑((2 * n - 2).choose (2 * k)) * ↑(MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry10bEuleriansymmetry.chapter5EulerEven k) * ↑(MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry10bEuleriansymmetry.chapter5EulerEven (n - k - 1))
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch5_entry10b_euleriansymmetry (n : ℕ) :

            (chapter5EulerEven k : ℚ) *

signature: ∀ (p : ℂ), p ≠ -1 → (∀ (h : ℂ) (phi : Polynomial ℂ), (Polynomial.taylor h) (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry1Euleriangf.chapter5DerivativeExpansion (fun n ↦ MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry3.chapter5Entry3Coeff n p) h phi) + Polynomial.C p * MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry1Euleriangf.chapter5DerivativeExpansion (fun n ↦ MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry3.chapter5Entry3Coeff n p) h phi = phi) ∧ ∀ (a : ℕ → ℂ), (∀ (h : ℂ) (phi : Polynomial ℂ), (Polynomial.taylor h) (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry1Euleriangf.chapter5DerivativeExpansion a h phi) + Polynomial.C p * MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry1Euleriangf.chapter5DerivativeExpansion a h phi = phi) → ∀ (n : ℕ), a n = MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry3.chapter5Entry3Coeff n p

Entry 30, pp. 131–132.
Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch5_entry30_secondordereulerian`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry30Secondordereulerian.ramanujan_part1_ch5_entry30_secondordereulerian
signature: (∀ (a : ℕ → ℂ) (c : ℝ), 1 < c → (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ‖a p‖ ≤ (↑p).rpow (-c)) → (Summable fun j ↦ MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry30Secondordereulerian.chapter5Entry30Coeff a (j + 2)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ), n ≠ 0 → MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry30Secondordereulerian.chapter5Entry30Coeff a n = if Squarefree n then ∏ p ∈ n.primeFactors, a p else 0) ∧ HasProd (fun p ↦ 1 + a ↑p) (1 + ∑' (j : ℕ), MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry30Secondordereulerian.chapter5Entry30Coeff a (j + 2))) ∧ ∀ (s : ℂ), 1 < s.re → (∀ (n : ℕ), n ≠ 0 → MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry30Secondordereulerian.chapter5Entry30SignedCoeff s n = if Squarefree n then if Odd n.primeFactors.card then -↑n ^ (-s) else ↑n ^ (-s) else 0) ∧ riemannZeta s ≠ 0 ∧ riemannZeta (2 * s) ≠ 0 ∧ Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry30Secondordereulerian.chapter5Entry30SquarefreeTerm s) ∧ ∑' (j : ℕ), MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry30Secondordereulerian.chapter5Entry30SquarefreeTerm s j = riemannZeta s / riemannZeta (2 * s) ∧ Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry30Secondordereulerian.chapter5Entry30OddTerm s) ∧ ∑' (j : ℕ), MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry30Secondordereulerian.chapter5Entry30OddTerm s j = (riemannZeta s ^ 2 - riemannZeta (2 * s)) / (2 * riemannZeta s * riemannZeta (2 * s)) ∧ Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry30Secondordereulerian.chapter5Entry30NonSquarefreeTerm s) ∧ ∑' (j : ℕ), MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch5.Entry30Secondordereulerian.chapter5Entry30NonSquarefreeTerm s j = riemannZeta s * (riemannZeta (2 * s) - 1) / riemannZeta (2 * s)
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch5_entry30_secondordereulerian :
    (∀ (a : ℕ → ℂ) (c : ℝ), 1 < c →
      (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ‖a p‖ ≤ Real.rpow (p : ℝ) (-c)) →
        Summable (fun j : ℕ => chapter5Entry30Coeff a (j + 2)) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, n ≠ 0 →
          chapter5Entry30Coeff a n =
            if Squarefree n then ∏ p ∈ n.primeFactors, a p else 0) ∧
        HasProd (fun p : Nat.Primes => 1 + a p)
          (1 + ∑' j : ℕ, chapter5Entry30Coeff a (j + 2))) ∧
    (∀ s : ℂ, 1 < s.re →
      (∀ n : ℕ, n ≠ 0 →
        chapter5Entry30SignedCoeff s n =
          if Squarefree n then
            if Odd n.primeFactors.card then -((n : ℂ) ^ (-s))
            else (n : ℂ) ^ (-s)
          else 0) ∧
      riemannZeta s ≠ 0 ∧
      riemannZeta (2 * s) ≠ 0 ∧
      Summable (chapter5Entry30SquarefreeTerm s) ∧
      (∑' j : ℕ, chapter5Entry30SquarefreeTerm s j) =
        riemannZeta s / riemannZeta (2 * s) ∧
      Summable (chapter5Entry30OddTerm s) ∧
      (∑' j : ℕ, chapter5Entry30OddTerm s j) =
        (riemannZeta s ^ 2 - riemannZeta (2 * s)) /
          (2 * riemannZeta s * riemannZeta (2 * s)) ∧
      Summable (chapter5Entry30NonSquarefreeTerm s) ∧
      (∑' j : ℕ, chapter5Entry30NonSquarefreeTerm s j) =
        riemannZeta s * (riemannZeta (2 * s) - 1) /
          riemannZeta (2 * s))

docstring:
Source: Bruce C. Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks, Part I, Chapter 6.

Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch6_entry10_centralbinomialexpansion`.

Proof: Rewrite the plus series as the minus series at `x` minus twice the minus
series at `2 * x`, then apply the preceding Euler–Maclaurin remainder bound.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry10Centralbinomialexpansion.ramanujan_part1_ch6_entry10_centralbinomialexpansion
signature: ∀ (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ), 0 < x → 1 ≤ n → Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry10Centralbinomialexpansion.chapter6Entry14PlusTerm x) ∧ |MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry10Centralbinomialexpansion.chapter6Entry14PlusSum x - (Real.log 2 / x - 1 / 4 + MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry10Centralbinomialexpansion.chapter6Entry14PlusCorrection n x)| ≤ |↑(bernoulli (2 * n)) * ↑(bernoulli (2 * n + 2))| * x ^ (2 * n) / ↑(2 * n).factorial * (x ^ 2 / (4 * Real.pi ^ 2) + Real.pi ^ 2 / 6 + 2 ^ (2 * n + 1) * (x ^ 2 / Real.pi ^ 2 + Real.pi ^ 2 / 6))
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch6_entry10_centralbinomialexpansion (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (hx : 0 < x) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    Summable (chapter6Entry14PlusTerm x) ∧
      |chapter6Entry14PlusSum x -
          (Real.log 2 / x - 1 / 4 + chapter6Entry14PlusCorrection n x)| ≤
        |(bernoulli (2 * n) : ℝ) * (bernoulli (2 * n + 2) : ℝ)| *
          x ^ (2 * n) / ((2 * n).factorial : ℝ) *
          (x ^ 2 / (4 * Real.pi ^ 2) + Real.pi ^ 2 / 6 +
            (2 : ℝ) ^ (2 * n + 1) *
              (x ^ 2 / Real.pi ^ 2 + Real.pi ^ 2 / 6))

signature: ∀ (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ), 0 < x → 1 ≤ n → Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry10Centralbinomialfull.chapter6Entry14MinusTerm x) ∧ |MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry10Centralbinomialfull.chapter6Entry14MinusSum x - (Real.eulerMascheroniConstant / x - Real.log x / x + 1 / 4 - MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry10Centralbinomialfull.chapter6Entry14MinusCorrection n x)| ≤ |↑(bernoulli (2 * n)) * ↑(bernoulli (2 * n + 2))| * x ^ (2 * n) / ↑(2 * n).factorial * (x ^ 2 / (4 * Real.pi ^ 2) + Real.pi ^ 2 / 6)

docstring:
Source: Bruce C. Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks, Part I, Chapter 6.
Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch6_entry13_ramanujanfactorial`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry13Ramanujanfactorial.ramanujan_part1_ch6_entry13_ramanujanfactorial
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch6_entry13_ramanujanfactorial (x : ℝ) (hx : 1 < |x|) :
    let leftTerm := fun j : ℕ =>
      (-1 : ℝ) ^ (j + 2) / (x ^ (j + 1) - 1)
    let rightTerm := fun j : ℕ =>
      ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (j + 2) * (x ^ (2 * (j + 1)) + 1)) /
        (x ^ ((j + 1) ^ 2) * (x ^ (2 * (j + 1)) - 1))
    (∀ j : ℕ, x ^ (j + 1) - 1 ≠ 0) ∧
      (∀ j : ℕ,
        x ^ ((j + 1) ^ 2) * (x ^ (2 * (j + 1)) - 1) ≠ 0) ∧
      Summable leftTerm ∧ Summable rightTerm ∧
      ∑' j, leftTerm j = ∑' j, rightTerm j

docstring:
Source: Bruce C. Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks, Part I, Chapter 6.

hypothesis `hn` is unused and keeps the source's shape.
Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch6_entry16_harmonicasymptotic`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry16FiniteSum.ramanujan_part1_ch6_entry16_finite_sum
signature: ∀ (a r x : ℝ) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → (∀ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, 1 - a * x ^ k ≠ 0) → (∀ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, 1 - r * x ^ (k - 1) ≠ 0) → ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, r ^ k / (1 - a * x ^ k) = ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, (a * r * x ^ k) ^ k / (1 - a * x ^ k) + ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, a ^ (k - 1) * ((r * x ^ (k - 1)) ^ k - (r * x ^ (k - 1)) ^ (n + 1)) / (1 - r * x ^ (k - 1))
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch6_entry16_finite_sum
    (a r x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
    (hax : ∀ k ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 - a * x ^ k ≠ 0)
    (hrx : ∀ k ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 - r * x ^ (k - 1) ≠ 0) :
    ∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n, r ^ k / (1 - a * x ^ k) =
      (∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n,
        (a * r * x ^ k) ^ k / (1 - a * x ^ k)) +
      ∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n,
        a ^ (k - 1) *
          ((r * x ^ (k - 1)) ^ k - (r * x ^ (k - 1)) ^ (n + 1)) /
            (1 - r * x ^ (k - 1))

name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry16FiniteSum.ramanujan_part1_ch6_entry16_finite_sum_general
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] (a r x : K) (n : ℕ), (∀ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, 1 - a * x ^ k ≠ 0) → (∀ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, 1 - r * x ^ (k - 1) ≠ 0) → ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, r ^ k / (1 - a * x ^ k) = ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, (a * r * x ^ k) ^ k / (1 - a * x ^ k) + ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, a ^ (k - 1) * ((r * x ^ (k - 1)) ^ k - (r * x ^ (k - 1)) ^ (n + 1)) / (1 - r * x ^ (k - 1))
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch6_entry16_finite_sum_general
    {K : Type*} [Field K] (a r x : K) (n : ℕ)
    (hax : ∀ k ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 - a * x ^ k ≠ 0)
    (hrx : ∀ k ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 - r * x ^ (k - 1) ≠ 0) :
    ∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n, r ^ k / (1 - a * x ^ k) =
      (∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n,
        (a * r * x ^ k) ^ k / (1 - a * x ^ k)) +
      ∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n,
        a ^ (k - 1) *
          ((r * x ^ (k - 1)) ^ k - (r * x ^ (k - 1)) ^ (n + 1)) /
            (1 - r * x ^ (k - 1))

signature: ∀ (a r x : ℂ), ‖r‖ < 1 → ‖x‖ ≤ 1 → (‖x‖ = 1 → ‖a * r‖ < 1) → (∀ (k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → 1 - a * x ^ k ≠ 0) → (‖x‖ = 1 → ∃ delta, 0 < delta ∧ ∀ (k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → delta ≤ ‖1 - a * x ^ k‖) → (∀ (k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → 1 - r * x ^ (k - 1) ≠ 0) ∧ Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry16InfiniteSum.chapter6Entry16LeftTerm a r x) ∧ Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry16InfiniteSum.chapter6Entry16MiddleTerm a r x) ∧ Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry16InfiniteSum.chapter6Entry16RightTerm a r x) ∧ ∑' (j : ℕ), MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry16InfiniteSum.chapter6Entry16LeftTerm a r x j = ∑' (j : ℕ), MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry16InfiniteSum.chapter6Entry16MiddleTerm a r x j + ∑' (j : ℕ), MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry16InfiniteSum.chapter6Entry16RightTerm a r x j
statement:

    (a r x : ℂ)
    (hr : ‖r‖ < 1) (hx : ‖x‖ ≤ 1)
    (hboundary : ‖x‖ = 1 → ‖a * r‖ < 1)
    (hpoles : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → 1 - a * x ^ k ≠ 0)
    (hboundarySeparated : ‖x‖ = 1 →
      ∃ delta : ℝ, 0 < delta ∧
        ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → delta ≤ ‖1 - a * x ^ k‖) :
    (∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → 1 - r * x ^ (k - 1) ≠ 0) ∧
      Summable (chapter6Entry16LeftTerm a r x) ∧
      Summable (chapter6Entry16MiddleTerm a r x) ∧
      Summable (chapter6Entry16RightTerm a r x) ∧
      (∑' j : ℕ, chapter6Entry16LeftTerm a r x j) =
        (∑' j : ℕ, chapter6Entry16MiddleTerm a r x j) +
          ∑' j : ℕ, chapter6Entry16RightTerm a r x j

docstring:
Source: Bruce C. Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks, Part I, Chapter 6.

Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch6_entry17_stirlingcoeffs`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch6.Entry17Stirlingcoeffs.ramanujan_part1_ch6_entry17_stirlingcoeffs
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch6_entry17_stirlingcoeffs
    (a b m nu x : ℝ)
    (hx : |x| ≤ 1) (hnu : |nu| < 1)
    (hboundary : |x| = 1 → |m * nu| < 1)
    (hm : m ≠ 0)
    (hmx : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 - m * x ^ k ≠ 0) :
    let leftTerm := fun k : ℕ =>
      (a + (k : ℝ) * b) * nu ^ k / (1 - m * x ^ k)
    let firstTerm := fun k : ℕ =>
      ((a + (k : ℝ) * b) * (1 - m * nu * x ^ (2 * k)) *
          (m * nu * x ^ k) ^ k) /
        ((1 - m * x ^ k) * (1 - nu * x ^ k))
    let secondTerm := fun k : ℕ =>
      (m * nu * x ^ k) ^ (k + 1) / (1 - nu * x ^ k) ^ 2
    (∀ k : ℕ, 1 - nu * x ^ k ≠ 0) ∧
      Summable leftTerm ∧ Summable firstTerm ∧ Summable secondTerm ∧
      ∑' k, leftTerm k =
        ∑' k, firstTerm k + b / m * ∑' k, secondTerm k

docstring:
Source: Bruce C. Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks, Part I, Chapter 7.

Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch7_entry14_bernoulliasymptotic`.

Proof outline: the limits `c k` are the Stieltjes constants. For
`ζ(s) - 1/(s-1)`, the `k`th derivative at `s = 1` is `(-1)^k c k`, while the
normalized Taylor coefficient is `(-1)^k c k / k! = chapter7StieltjesA c k`.
The identity follows by termwise differentiation in `s` and evaluation at `s = 1`.

signature: ∀ (r : ℕ), 0 < r → ∀ (x : ℂ), (Polynomial.eval₂ (Algebra.algebraMap ℚ ℂ) (x + 1) (Polynomial.bernoulli (r + 1)) - Polynomial.eval₂ (Algebra.algebraMap ℚ ℂ) 1 (Polynomial.bernoulli (r + 1))) / (↑r + 1) = (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (r + 1), ↑((r + 1).choose k) * ↑(bernoulli k) * x ^ (r + 1 - k)) / (↑r + 1) + x ^ r

name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch7.Entry9Zetaeven.ramanujan_part1_ch7_entry9_zetaeven
signature: ∀ (phi psi : ℂ → ℂ → ℂ), (∀ (x : ℂ), MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch7.chapter7Admissible x → Differentiable ℂ fun r ↦ phi r x) → (∀ (x : ℂ), MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch7.chapter7Admissible x → Differentiable ℂ fun r ↦ psi r x) → (∀ (r x : ℂ), r.re < 0 → MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch7.chapter7Admissible x → HasSum (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch7.chapter7PowerDifferenceTerm r x) (phi r x)) → (∀ (r x : ℂ), r.re < 0 → MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch7.chapter7Admissible x → HasSum (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch7.chapter7PowerDifferenceTerm r x) (psi r x)) → (∀ (x : ℂ), MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch7.chapter7Admissible x → ∀ (r : ℂ), phi r x = psi r x) ∧ ∀ (m : ℕ) (x : ℂ), MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch7.chapter7Admissible x → phi (↑m) x = MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch7.Entry8Bernoullibound.chapter7IntegerPhi m x ∧ psi (↑m) x = MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch7.Entry8Bernoullibound.chapter7IntegerPhi m x
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch7_entry9_zetaeven
    (phi psi : ℂ → ℂ → ℂ)
    (hphi_entire : ∀ x, chapter7Admissible x →
      Differentiable ℂ (fun r : ℂ => phi r x))
    (hpsi_entire : ∀ x, chapter7Admissible x →
      Differentiable ℂ (fun r : ℂ => psi r x))
    (hphi_series : ∀ r x, r.re < 0 → chapter7Admissible x →
      HasSum (chapter7PowerDifferenceTerm r x) (phi r x))
    (hpsi_series : ∀ r x, r.re < 0 → chapter7Admissible x →
      HasSum (chapter7PowerDifferenceTerm r x) (psi r x)) :
    (∀ x, chapter7Admissible x → ∀ r, phi r x = psi r x) ∧
      (∀ m : ℕ, ∀ x, chapter7Admissible x →
        phi m x = chapter7IntegerPhi m x ∧
          psi m x = chapter7IntegerPhi m x)

name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry10Qgammalimit.ramanujan_part1_ch8_entry10_qgammalimit
signature: ∀ (x : ℂ), x.re < 0 → x ≠ 0 ∧ Complex.Gamma (1 - 1 / x) ≠ 0 ∧ MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry10Qgammalimit.chapter8Entry10Kernel x 0 = 0 ∧ MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry10Qgammalimit.chapter8Entry10Kernel x 1 = -1 / x ∧ (∀ u ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1, ↑u * (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry9Qgamma.chapter8UnitPow x u - 1) ≠ 0 ∧ MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry10Qgammalimit.chapter8Entry10Kernel x u = ↑(1 - u) / (↑u * (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry9Qgamma.chapter8UnitPow x u - 1))) ∧ IntervalIntegrable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry10Qgammalimit.chapter8Entry10Kernel x) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume 0 1 ∧ (1 - 1 / x).digamma + ↑Real.eulerMascheroniConstant = -x * ∫ (u : ℝ) in 0..1, MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry10Qgammalimit.chapter8Entry10Kernel x u
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch8_entry10_qgammalimit (x : ℂ) (hx : x.re < 0) :
    x ≠ 0 ∧
      Complex.Gamma (1 - 1 / x) ≠ 0 ∧
      chapter8Entry10Kernel x 0 = 0 ∧
      chapter8Entry10Kernel x 1 = -1 / x ∧
      (∀ u : ℝ, u ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1 →
        (u : ℂ) * (Entry9Qgamma.chapter8UnitPow x u - 1) ≠ 0 ∧
          chapter8Entry10Kernel x u =
            ((1 - u : ℝ) : ℂ) /
              ((u : ℂ) * (Entry9Qgamma.chapter8UnitPow x u - 1))) ∧
      IntervalIntegrable (chapter8Entry10Kernel x) volume 0 1 ∧
      Complex.digamma (1 - 1 / x) +
          (Real.eulerMascheroniConstant : ℂ) =
        -x * ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..1, chapter8Entry10Kernel x u

statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch8_entry12_qgammaintegers (x : ℂ) (hx : 1 < x.re) :
    (∀ j : ℕ,
      let k : ℂ := j + 1
      (k * x) ^ 3 - k * x ≠ 0) ∧
      Summable (chapter8PhiTerm x) ∧

statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch8_entry14_v_integral5 (x : ℝ) (hxLower : -1 < x)
    (hxUpper : x < 4 / (Real.sqrt 5 + 1)) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun u : ℝ => 1 / (1 + u ^ (5 : ℕ))) volume 0 x ∧
      0 < (1 + x) ^ 5 / (1 + x ^ 5) ∧
      0 <
        (1 + (1 / 2 : ℝ) * x * (Real.sqrt 5 - 1) + x ^ 2) /
          (1 - (1 / 2 : ℝ) * x * (Real.sqrt 5 + 1) + x ^ 2) ∧
      4 + x * (Real.sqrt 5 - 1) ≠ 0 ∧
      4 - x * (Real.sqrt 5 + 1) ≠ 0 ∧
      chapter8Entry14A 5 x =
        (1 / 20 : ℝ) * Real.log ((1 + x) ^ 5 / (1 + x ^ 5)) +
          1 / (4 * Real.sqrt 5) *
            Real.log
              ((1 + (1 / 2 : ℝ) * x * (Real.sqrt 5 - 1) + x ^ 2) /
                (1 - (1 / 2 : ℝ) * x * (Real.sqrt 5 + 1) + x ^ 2)) +
          (1 / 10 : ℝ) * Real.sqrt (10 + 2 * Real.sqrt 5) *
            Real.arctan
              (x * Real.sqrt (10 + 2 * Real.sqrt 5) /
                (4 + x * (Real.sqrt 5 - 1))) +
          (1 / 10 : ℝ) * Real.sqrt (10 - 2 * Real.sqrt 5) *
            Real.arctan
              (x * Real.sqrt (10 - 2 * Real.sqrt 5) /
                (4 - x * (Real.sqrt 5 + 1)))

signature: ∀ (x : ℝ), IntervalIntegrable (fun u ↦ 1 / (1 + u ^ 6)) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume 0 x ∧ 0 < 1 + x * √3 + x ^ 2 ∧ 0 < 1 - x * √3 + x ^ 2 ∧ MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry14ViIntegral6.chapter8Entry14A 6 x = 1 / 2 * Real.arctan x + 1 / 6 * Real.arctan (x ^ 3) + 1 / (4 * √3) * Real.log ((1 + x * √3 + x ^ 2) / (1 - x * √3 + x ^ 2))
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch8_entry14_vi_integral6 (x : ℝ) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun u : ℝ => 1 / (1 + u ^ (6 : ℕ))) volume 0 x ∧
      0 < 1 + x * Real.sqrt 3 + x ^ 2 ∧
      0 < 1 - x * Real.sqrt 3 + x ^ 2 ∧
      chapter8Entry14A 6 x =
        (1 / 2 : ℝ) * Real.arctan x +
          (1 / 6 : ℝ) * Real.arctan (x ^ 3) +

            Real.log
              ((1 + x * Real.sqrt 3 + x ^ 2) /
                (1 - x * Real.sqrt 3 + x ^ 2))

signature: ∀ (x : ℝ), |x| < 1 → IntervalIntegrable (fun u ↦ 1 / (1 + u ^ 8)) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume 0 x ∧ 0 < (1 + x * √(2 + √2) + x ^ 2) / (1 - x * √(2 + √2) + x ^ 2) ∧ 0 < (1 + x * √(2 - √2) + x ^ 2) / (1 - x * √(2 - √2) + x ^ 2) ∧ 1 - x ^ 2 ≠ 0 ∧ MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry14ViiIntegral8.chapter8Entry14A 8 x = √(2 + √2) / 16 * (Real.log ((1 + x * √(2 + √2) + x ^ 2) / (1 - x * √(2 + √2) + x ^ 2)) + 2 * Real.arctan (x * √(2 + √2) / (1 - x ^ 2))) + √(2 - √2) / 16 * (Real.log ((1 + x * √(2 - √2) + x ^ 2) / (1 - x * √(2 - √2) + x ^ 2)) + 2 * Real.arctan (x * √(2 - √2) / (1 - x ^ 2)))

theorem ramanujan_part1_ch8_entry14_vii_integral8 (x : ℝ) (hx : |x| < 1) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun u : ℝ => 1 / (1 + u ^ (8 : ℕ))) volume 0 x ∧
      0 <
        (1 + x * Real.sqrt (2 + Real.sqrt 2) + x ^ 2) /
          (1 - x * Real.sqrt (2 + Real.sqrt 2) + x ^ 2) ∧
      0 <
        (1 + x * Real.sqrt (2 - Real.sqrt 2) + x ^ 2) /
          (1 - x * Real.sqrt (2 - Real.sqrt 2) + x ^ 2) ∧
      1 - x ^ 2 ≠ 0 ∧
      chapter8Entry14A 8 x =
        Real.sqrt (2 + Real.sqrt 2) / 16 *
            (Real.log
                ((1 + x * Real.sqrt (2 + Real.sqrt 2) + x ^ 2) /
                  (1 - x * Real.sqrt (2 + Real.sqrt 2) + x ^ 2)) +
              2 * Real.arctan
                (x * Real.sqrt (2 + Real.sqrt 2) / (1 - x ^ 2))) +
          Real.sqrt (2 - Real.sqrt 2) / 16 *
            (Real.log
                ((1 + x * Real.sqrt (2 - Real.sqrt 2) + x ^ 2) /
                  (1 - x * Real.sqrt (2 - Real.sqrt 2) + x ^ 2)) +
              2 * Real.arctan
                (x * Real.sqrt (2 - Real.sqrt 2) / (1 - x ^ 2)))

docstring:

Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch8_entry15_doublegamma`.

Proof: Convexity of `log Γ` gives crude digamma bounds. A telescoped centered expansion and
Taylor's formula for the complex exponential then give the stated coefficients and remainder.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry15Doublegamma.ramanujan_part1_ch8_entry15_doublegamma
signature: ∀ (n : ℂ), Filter.Tendsto MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry15Doublegamma.chapter8Entry15A Filter.atTop Filter.atTop ∧ (fun x ↦ MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry15Doublegamma.chapter8Entry15Power n x - MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry15Doublegamma.chapter8Entry15Approx n x) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x ↦ 1 / ↑(MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry15Doublegamma.chapter8Entry15A x) ^ 8

      IsBigO atTop
        (fun x : ℝ => chapter8Entry15Power n x - chapter8Entry15Approx n x)
        (fun x : ℝ => (1 : ℂ) / (chapter8Entry15A x : ℂ) ^ 8)

docstring:
Source: Bruce C. Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks, Part I, Chapter 8, Entry 16.

Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch8_entry16_eulerconstantseries`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry16Eulerconstantseries.ramanujan_part1_ch8_entry16_eulerconstantseries
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch8_entry16_eulerconstantseries :
    let A : ℕ → ℕ := fun k => (3 ^ k - 1) / 2
    let term : ℕ → ℝ := fun k =>
      ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) *
        ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc (A k + 1) (A (k + 1)),
          (1 : ℝ) / ((3 * (j : ℝ)) ^ 3 - 3 * (j : ℝ))
    Summable term ∧
      Real.eulerMascheroniConstant = Real.log 2 - 2 * ∑' k : ℕ, term k

signature: ∀ (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ), -1 < x → 0 < n → (∀ (j : ℕ), 0 < ↑j + 1 + x) ∧ (∀ k ∈ Finset.range n, ∀ (j : ℕ), 0 < ↑j + 1 + (x - ↑k) / ↑n) ∧ Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry17Loggammaintegral.chapter8Entry17Term x) ∧ (∀ k ∈ Finset.range n, Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry17Loggammaintegral.chapter8Entry17Term ((x - ↑k) / ↑n))) ∧ 0 < Real.Gamma (x + 1) ∧ ↑n * MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry17Loggammaintegral.chapter8Entry17Phi x - ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry17Loggammaintegral.chapter8Entry17Phi ((x - ↑k) / ↑n) = ↑n * Real.log ↑n * MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry17Loggammaintegral.chapter8RealDigamma (x + 1) - ↑n * Real.log ↑n ^ 2 / 2
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch8_entry17_loggammaintegral (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (hx : -1 < x) (hn : 0 < n) :
    (∀ j : ℕ, 0 < (j + 1 : ℝ) + x) ∧
      (∀ k ∈ range n, ∀ j : ℕ,
        0 < (j + 1 : ℝ) + (x - k) / n) ∧
      Summable (chapter8Entry17Term x) ∧
      (∀ k ∈ range n,
        Summable (chapter8Entry17Term ((x - k) / n))) ∧
      0 < Real.Gamma (x + 1) ∧
      (n : ℝ) * chapter8Entry17Phi x -
          ∑ k ∈ range n, chapter8Entry17Phi ((x - k) / n) =
        (n : ℝ) * Real.log n * chapter8RealDigamma (x + 1) -

name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry19Gaussdigamma.ramanujan_part1_ch8_entry19_gaussdigamma
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ), (∀ m ≤ n, Filter.Tendsto (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry19Gaussdigamma.chapter8LogPowerConstantApprox m) Filter.atTop (nhds (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry19Gaussdigamma.chapter8LogPowerConstant m))) ∧ (fun x ↦ MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry19Gaussdigamma.chapter8Entry19Combination n x - MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch8.Entry19Gaussdigamma.chapter8Entry19Approx n x) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x ↦ 1 / ↑x ^ (n + 3)

Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch9_entry13_bernoulligen`.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry13Bernoulligen.ramanujan_part1_ch9_entry13_bernoulligen
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ), 1 ≤ n → x ≠ 0 → |x| < 2 * Real.pi → IntervalIntegrable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry13Bernoulligen.chapter9Entry13Integrand n) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume 0 x ∧ Filter.Tendsto (fun N ↦ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, Real.cos (↑(k + 1) * x) / ↑(k + 1)) Filter.atTop (nhds (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry13Bernoulligen.chapter9Clausen 1 x)) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ), 2 ≤ m → m ≤ n + 1 → Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry13Bernoulligen.chapter9ClausenTerm m x)) ∧ ∫ (u : ℝ) in 0..x, MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry13Bernoulligen.chapter9Entry13Integrand n u = Real.cos (↑n * Real.pi / 2) * ↑n.factorial * (riemannZeta ↑(n + 1)).re - ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (-1) ^ (j * (j + 1) / 2) * ↑n.factorial / ↑(n - j).factorial * x ^ (n - j) * MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry13Bernoulligen.chapter9Clausen (j + 1) x
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch9_entry13_bernoulligen (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ)
    (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hx0 : x ≠ 0) (hx : |x| < 2 * Real.pi) :
    IntervalIntegrable (chapter9Entry13Integrand n) volume 0 x ∧
      Tendsto
        (fun N : ℕ => ∑ k ∈ range N,
          Real.cos (((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * x) / ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ))
        atTop (𝓝 (chapter9Clausen 1 x)) ∧
      (∀ m : ℕ, 2 ≤ m → m ≤ n + 1 →
        Summable (chapter9ClausenTerm m x)) ∧
      (∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..x, chapter9Entry13Integrand n u) =
        Real.cos (n * Real.pi / 2) * n.factorial *
            (riemannZeta ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ)).re -
          ∑ j ∈ range (n + 1),
            (-1 : ℝ) ^ (j * (j + 1) / 2) *
              (n.factorial : ℝ) / ((n - j).factorial : ℝ) *
              x ^ (n - j) * chapter9Clausen (j + 1) x

docstring:
Source: Bruce C. Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks, Part I, Chapter 9.

Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch9_entry14_xoversin`.

Proof: Subtracts a scaled Entry 13 identity at `2x` from the identity at `x`, then
splits the zeta and Clausen series into even and odd frequencies, following Berndt
and Lewin, *Polylogarithms and Associated Functions*, Chapter 4.
name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry14Xoversin.ramanujan_part1_ch9_entry14_xoversin
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ), 1 ≤ n → x ≠ 0 → |x| < Real.pi → IntervalIntegrable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry14Xoversin.chapter9Entry14Integrand n) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume 0 x ∧ (Summable fun k ↦ 1 / ↑(2 * k + 1) ^ (n + 1)) ∧ Filter.Tendsto (fun N ↦ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, Real.cos (↑(2 * k + 1) * x) / ↑(2 * k + 1)) Filter.atTop (nhds (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry14Xoversin.chapter9OddClausen 1 x)) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ), 2 ≤ m → m ≤ n + 1 → Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry14Xoversin.chapter9OddClausenTerm m x)) ∧ ∫ (u : ℝ) in 0..x, MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry14Xoversin.chapter9Entry14Integrand n u = Real.cos (↑n * Real.pi / 2) * ↑n.factorial * MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry14Xoversin.chapter9ChiAtOne (n + 1) - ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (-1) ^ (j * (j + 1) / 2) * ↑n.factorial / ↑(n - j).factorial * x ^ (n - j) * MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry14Xoversin.chapter9OddClausen (j + 1) x
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch9_entry14_xoversin (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ)
    (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hx0 : x ≠ 0) (hx : |x| < Real.pi) :
    IntervalIntegrable (chapter9Entry14Integrand n) volume 0 x ∧
      Summable (fun k : ℕ =>
        1 / (((2 * k + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (n + 1))) ∧
      Tendsto
        (fun N : ℕ => ∑ k ∈ range N,
          Real.cos (((2 * k + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * x) /
            ((2 * k + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ))
        atTop (𝓝 (chapter9OddClausen 1 x)) ∧
      (∀ m : ℕ, 2 ≤ m → m ≤ n + 1 →
        Summable (chapter9OddClausenTerm m x)) ∧
      (∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..x, chapter9Entry14Integrand n u) =
        Real.cos (n * Real.pi / 2) * n.factorial *
            chapter9ChiAtOne (n + 1) -
          ∑ j ∈ range (n + 1),
            (-1 : ℝ) ^ (j * (j + 1) / 2) *
              (n.factorial : ℝ) / ((n - j).factorial : ℝ) *
              x ^ (n - j) * chapter9OddClausen (j + 1) x

name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry15Xcot.ramanujan_part1_ch9_entry15_xcot
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ), (∀ k ≤ n, ∀ (y : ℝ), 0 < y → y < Real.pi → IntervalIntegrable (fun u ↦ u ^ k * (Real.cos u / Real.sin u)) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume (Real.pi / 4) y) ∧ ∀ (x : ℝ), 0 < x → x < Real.pi / 2 → 2 ^ n * MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry15Xcot.chapter9CotPrimitive n (Real.pi / 2 - x) = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (-1) ^ k * ↑(n.choose k) * Real.pi ^ (n - k) * (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry15Xcot.chapter9CotPrimitive k (2 * x) - 2 ^ k * MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry15Xcot.chapter9CotPrimitive k x) - ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (-1) ^ k * ↑(n.choose k) * Real.pi ^ (n - k) * MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry15Xcot.chapter9CotPrimitive k (Real.pi / 2)

name: MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry1Logratio.ramanujan_part1_ch9_entry1_logratio
signature: ∀ (r : ℕ) (a x : ℝ), 0 < r → (∀ (z : ℤ), a ≠ ↑(2 * z + 1)) → |x| < Real.pi → Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry1Logratio.chapter9Entry1ConstantTerm r a) ∧ (Odd r ∧ (∀ k ∈ Finset.range ((r - 1) / 2 + 1), Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry1Logratio.chapter9Entry1ConstantTerm (r - 2 * k) a)) ∧ Filter.Tendsto (fun N ↦ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry1Logratio.chapter9Entry1CosineTerm r a x k) Filter.atTop (nhds (∑ k ∈ Finset.range ((r - 1) / 2 + 1), (-1) ^ k * MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry1Logratio.chapter9Entry1Constant (r - 2 * k) a * x ^ (2 * k) / ↑(2 * k).factorial)) ∨ Even r ∧ (∀ k ∈ Finset.range (r / 2), Summable (MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry1Logratio.chapter9Entry1ConstantTerm (r - 2 * k - 1) a)) ∧ Filter.Tendsto (fun N ↦ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry1Logratio.chapter9Entry1SineTerm r a x k) Filter.atTop (nhds (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (r / 2), (-1) ^ k * MathlibExt.Analysis.Ramanujan.Part1Ch9.Entry1Logratio.chapter9Entry1Constant (r - 2 * k - 1) a * x ^ (2 * k + 1) / ↑(2 * k + 1).factorial)))
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch9_entry1_logratio (r : ℕ) (a x : ℝ)
    (hr : 0 < r)
    (ha : ∀ z : ℤ, a ≠ ((2 * z + 1 : ℤ) : ℝ))
    (hx : |x| < Real.pi) :
    Summable (chapter9Entry1ConstantTerm r a) ∧
      ((Odd r ∧
          (∀ k ∈ range ((r - 1) / 2 + 1),
            Summable (chapter9Entry1ConstantTerm (r - 2 * k) a)) ∧
          Tendsto
            (fun N : ℕ =>
              ∑ k ∈ range N, chapter9Entry1CosineTerm r a x k)
            atTop
            (𝓝 (∑ k ∈ range ((r - 1) / 2 + 1),
              (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * chapter9Entry1Constant (r - 2 * k) a *
                x ^ (2 * k) / ((2 * k).factorial : ℝ)))) ∨
        (Even r ∧
          (∀ k ∈ range (r / 2),
            Summable (chapter9Entry1ConstantTerm (r - 2 * k - 1) a)) ∧
          Tendsto
            (fun N : ℕ =>
              ∑ k ∈ range N, chapter9Entry1SineTerm r a x k)
            atTop
            (𝓝 (∑ k ∈ range (r / 2),
              (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * chapter9Entry1Constant (r - 2 * k - 1) a *
                x ^ (2 * k + 1) / ((2 * k + 1).factorial : ℝ)))))
