docstring:
Gaussian elimination with arbitrary nonzero row pivots admits an endpoint factorization into a
row permutation and a list of unit lower-triangular row operations whose product reaches row
echelon form. This records the factorization, not the intermediate matrices of an algorithm trace.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Numerical Analysis / Solving systems of linear
inequalities / Gauss's pivot; L. N. Trefethen and D. Bau, Numerical Linear Algebra, SIAM (1997),
Lectures 20-21.

Proves `Wanted` entry `exists_gauss_elimination_opList`.

Proof: Induct on the columns after transporting the index orders to `Fin`; a nonzero first column
uses a row pivot and recurses on the lower-right block. Package the resulting single unit
lower-triangular matrix as a singleton list (forward elimination to row echelon form,
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaussian_elimination).
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.GaussPivotWanted.exists_gauss_elimination_opList
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [inst_1 : Fintype m] [inst_2 : DecidableEq m] [inst_3 : LinearOrder m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [inst_6 : LinearOrder n] (A : Matrix m n K), ∃ ops σ, (∀ M ∈ ops, M.IsLowerTriangular ∧ ∀ (i : m), M.diag i = 1) ∧ (ops.prod * A.submatrix (⇑σ) id).IsRowEchelon
statement:
theorem exists_gauss_elimination_opList (A : Matrix m n K) :
    ∃ (ops : List (Matrix m m K)) (σ : Equiv.Perm m),
      (∀ M ∈ ops, M.IsLowerTriangular ∧ ∀ i, M.diag i = 1) ∧
      (ops.prod * A.submatrix σ id).IsRowEchelon

docstring:
One row-pivot step of Gaussian elimination: given any nonzero entry in column `j`, swap its row
to the pivot row `r` and clear the entries below it by a unit lower-triangular row operation.
This is arbitrary nonzero pivot selection, not magnitude-maximizing partial pivoting.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Numerical Analysis / Solving systems of linear
inequalities / Gauss's pivot; L. N. Trefethen and D. Bau, Numerical Linear Algebra, SIAM (1997),
Lectures 20-21.

Proves `Wanted` entry `gauss_pivot_elim_step`.

Proof: Use an entrywise unit lower-triangular matrix whose pivot column contains the elimination
coefficients, then evaluate the matrix product as a finite sum (row operations of type 3,
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaussian_elimination).
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.GaussPivotWanted.gauss_pivot_elim_step
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [inst_1 : Fintype m] [inst_2 : DecidableEq m] [inst_3 : LinearOrder m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [LinearOrder n] (A : Matrix m n K) (r : m) (j : n) (i₀ : m), A i₀ j ≠ 0 → ∃ P, P.IsLowerTriangular ∧ (∀ (i : m), P.diag i = 1) ∧ ∀ i > r, (P * A.submatrix (⇑(Equiv.swap r i₀)) id) i j = 0
statement:
theorem gauss_pivot_elim_step (A : Matrix m n K) (r : m) (j : n)
    (i₀ : m) (h : A i₀ j ≠ 0) :
    ∃ P : Matrix m m K, P.IsLowerTriangular ∧ (∀ i, P.diag i = 1) ∧
      ∀ i > r, (P * A.submatrix (Equiv.swap r i₀) id) i j = 0

docstring:
Hadamard's determinant inequality for a complex `n × n` matrix:
`‖det A‖ ≤ ∏ i, √(∑ j, ‖A i j‖^2)` via `normSq`,
i.e. `‖det A‖ ≤ ∏ i, sqrt(∑ j, normSq(A i j))`.
Source: J. Hadamard, Résolution d'une question relative aux déterminants,
Bulletin des Sciences Mathématiques 17 (1893), 240–246.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.HadamardDeterminant.hadamard_determinant_inequality
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ), ‖A.det‖ ≤ ∏ i, √(∑ j, Complex.normSq (A i j))

docstring:
Jordan normal form: a square matrix whose characteristic polynomial splits is similar to a
block-diagonal matrix of Jordan blocks.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Linear algebra / Structure theory of endomorphisms /
Jordan normal form; R. A. Horn and C. R. Johnson, Matrix Analysis, 2nd ed., Cambridge University
Press (2013), Theorem 3.4.1.

Proves `Wanted` entry `exists_jordan_normal_form_of_splits`.

Proof: Decompose into the maximal generalized eigenspaces (Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right,
4th ed., 8.22), take a Jordan-chain basis of each nilpotent restriction, and collect them as in
the proof of Axler 8.46. The nilpotent case is proved by induction on the range, extending chains
by preimages and adding kernel vectors, as in Wikipedia, "Jordan normal form", section "A proof".
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.JordanNormalFormWanted.exists_jordan_normal_form_of_splits
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] {n : Type u_2} [inst_1 : Fintype n] [inst_2 : DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n K), A.charpoly.Splits → ∃ k s μ P e, (∀ (i : Fin k), 0 < s i) ∧ IsUnit P ∧ A = P * (Matrix.reindex e e) (Matrix.blockDiagonal' fun i ↦ MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.JordanNormalFormWanted.jordanBlock (s i) (μ i)) * P⁻¹
statement:
theorem exists_jordan_normal_form_of_splits
    {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (A : Matrix n n K) (h : A.charpoly.Splits) :
    ∃ (k : ℕ) (s : Fin k → ℕ) (μ : Fin k → K) (P : Matrix n n K)
      (e : (Σ i, Fin (s i)) ≃ n),
      (∀ i, 0 < s i) ∧ IsUnit P ∧
        A = P * Matrix.reindex e e
          (Matrix.blockDiagonal' (fun i => jordanBlock (s i) (μ i))) * P⁻¹

docstring:
A Jordan block of size `s` with eigenvalue `μ`: `μ` on the diagonal, `1` on the first
superdiagonal, `0` elsewhere.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Linear algebra / Structure theory of endomorphisms /
Jordan normal form; R. A. Horn and C. R. Johnson, Matrix Analysis, 2nd ed., Cambridge University
Press (2013), Section 3.4.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.JordanNormalFormWanted.jordanBlock
signature: {K : Type u_1} → [Field K] → (s : ℕ) → K → Matrix (Fin s) (Fin s) K
statement: def jordanBlock (s : ℕ) (μ : K) : Matrix (Fin s) (Fin s) K

docstring:
Characteristic entrywise description of a Jordan block.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Linear algebra / Structure theory of endomorphisms /
Jordan normal form; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_normal_form.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.JordanNormalFormWanted.jordanBlock_apply
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] (s : ℕ) (μ : K) (i j : Fin s), MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.JordanNormalFormWanted.jordanBlock s μ i j = if ↑i + 1 = ↑j then 1 else if i = j then μ else 0
statement:
theorem jordanBlock_apply (s : ℕ) (μ : K) (i j : Fin s) :
    jordanBlock s μ i j = (if i.val + 1 = j.val then 1 else if i = j then μ else 0)

docstring:
LU decomposition without pivoting: a square matrix whose leading principal minors are all
nonzero factors as a unit-diagonal lower-triangular matrix times an upper-triangular matrix.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Numerical Analysis / Solving systems of linear
inequalities / LU decomposition; L. N. Trefethen and D. Bau, Numerical Linear Algebra, SIAM
(1997), Lecture 20.

Proves `Wanted` entry `exists_lu_decomposition_of_minors_ne_zero`.

Proof: Induct on the dimension and extend the factorization of the leading principal block by a
bordered (Schur-complement) step. The statement is the existence half of Wikipedia, "LU
decomposition", section "Existence and uniqueness".
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.LUDecompositionWanted.exists_lu_decomposition_of_minors_ne_zero
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] (n : ℕ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K), (∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n), (A.submatrix (Fin.castLE hk) (Fin.castLE hk)).det ≠ 0) → ∃ L U, L.IsLowerTriangular ∧ U.IsUpperTriangular ∧ (∀ (i : Fin n), L i i = 1) ∧ A = L * U
statement:
theorem exists_lu_decomposition_of_minors_ne_zero (n : ℕ)
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)
    (h : ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n),
      Matrix.det (A.submatrix (Fin.castLE hk) (Fin.castLE hk)) ≠ 0) :
    ∃ L U : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K,
      L.IsLowerTriangular ∧ U.IsUpperTriangular ∧ (∀ i, L i i = 1) ∧ A = L * U

docstring:
Uniqueness of the LU decomposition with unit diagonal for an invertible matrix.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Numerical Analysis / Solving systems of linear
inequalities / LU decomposition; L. N. Trefethen and D. Bau, Numerical Linear Algebra, SIAM
(1997), Lecture 20.

Proves `Wanted` entry `lu_decomposition_unique`.

Proof: Move the invertible triangular factors across the equality, then use the triangular inverse
and diagonal formulas to show the resulting matrix is the identity. The statement is the
uniqueness half of Wikipedia, "LU decomposition", section "Existence and uniqueness".
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.LUDecompositionWanted.lu_decomposition_unique
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] (n : ℕ) (A L₁ L₂ U₁ U₂ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K), IsUnit A.det → L₁.IsLowerTriangular → U₁.IsUpperTriangular → (∀ (i : Fin n), L₁ i i = 1) → L₂.IsLowerTriangular → U₂.IsUpperTriangular → (∀ (i : Fin n), L₂ i i = 1) → A = L₁ * U₁ → A = L₂ * U₂ → L₁ = L₂ ∧ U₁ = U₂
statement:
theorem lu_decomposition_unique (n : ℕ)
    (A L₁ L₂ U₁ U₂ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)
    (hA : IsUnit A.det)
    (hL₁ : L₁.IsLowerTriangular) (hU₁ : U₁.IsUpperTriangular) (hd₁ : ∀ i, L₁ i i = 1)
    (hL₂ : L₂.IsLowerTriangular) (hU₂ : U₂.IsUpperTriangular) (hd₂ : ∀ i, L₂ i i = 1)
    (e₁ : A = L₁ * U₁) (e₂ : A = L₂ * U₂) :
    L₁ = L₂ ∧ U₁ = U₂

docstring:
Jacobi's formula: the determinant of the matrix exponential is the exponential of the trace.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Linear algebra / Exponential / matrix exponential;
B. C. Hall, Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations, 2nd ed., Springer (2015),
Proposition 2.23.

Proves `Wanted` entry `matrix_det_exp_eq_exp_trace`.

Proof: the three cases of B. C. Hall, An Elementary Introduction to Groups and Representations,
https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0005032, Theorem 3.10. The Jordan-Chevalley decomposition
(`Module.End.exists_isNilpotent_isSemisimple`) writes `A = N + S` with `N` nilpotent, `S`
semisimple and `N`, `S` commuting, so `exp A = exp N * exp S`. Diagonalizing `S` gives
`det (exp S) = exp (trace S)`. For the nilpotent part, where Hall uses a strictly upper-triangular
form, `exp N - 1` is nilpotent, so `det (exp N) = 1`, while `trace N = 0`.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.MatrixExpDetTraceWanted.matrix_det_exp_eq_exp_trace
signature: ∀ {n : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype n] [inst_1 : DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ), (NormedSpace.exp A).det = Complex.exp A.trace
statement:
theorem matrix_det_exp_eq_exp_trace (A : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    Matrix.det (NormedSpace.exp A) = Complex.exp (Matrix.trace A)

docstring:
The exponential of a nilpotent matrix is a finite partial sum of the exponential series.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Linear algebra / Exponential / matrix exponential;
R. A. Horn and C. R. Johnson, Matrix Analysis, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2013),
Section 3.2.

Proves `Wanted` entry `matrix_exp_eq_sum_of_isNilpotent`.

Proof: if `A ^ m = 0`, every term of the exponential series from index `m` on vanishes.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.MatrixExpDetTraceWanted.matrix_exp_eq_sum_of_isNilpotent
signature: ∀ {n : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype n] [inst_1 : DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ), IsNilpotent A → ∃ m, NormedSpace.exp A = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range m, (↑k.factorial)⁻¹ • A ^ k
statement:
theorem matrix_exp_eq_sum_of_isNilpotent (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (h : IsNilpotent A) :
    ∃ m : ℕ, NormedSpace.exp A = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range m, (Nat.factorial k : ℂ)⁻¹ • A ^ k

docstring:
Every nonzero irreducible nonnegative real matrix has a positive dominant eigenvalue.
Source: O. Perron, Math. Ann. 64 (1907), 248-263, DOI 10.1007/BF01449896; G. Frobenius, S.-Ber.
Preuss. Akad. Wiss. Berlin (1912), 456-477.

The nonzero hypothesis is not needed; see `Matrix.IsIrreducible.perron_frobenius`.

Proves `Wanted` entry `perron_frobenius`.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.PerronFrobeniusWanted.perron_frobenius
signature: ∀ {n : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype n] [inst_1 : DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ), A.IsIrreducible → A ≠ 0 → ∃ r v, 0 < r ∧ (∀ (i : n), 0 < v i) ∧ A.mulVec v = r • v ∧ ∀ (μ : ℂ), (μ • 1 - MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.PerronFrobeniusWanted.toComplexMatrix A).det = 0 → ‖μ‖ ≤ r
statement:
theorem perron_frobenius
    (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (hA : A.IsIrreducible) (hA0 : A ≠ 0) :
    ∃ (r : ℝ) (v : n → ℝ),
      0 < r ∧ (∀ i, 0 < v i) ∧ A.mulVec v = r • v ∧
        ∀ μ : ℂ, Matrix.det (μ • (1 : Matrix n n ℂ) - toComplexMatrix A) = 0 → ‖μ‖ ≤ r

docstring: Coercion of a real matrix to complex via `Complex.ofReal`.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.PerronFrobeniusWanted.toComplexMatrix
signature: {n : Type u_1} → Matrix n n ℝ → Matrix n n ℂ
statement: noncomputable def toComplexMatrix (A : Matrix n n ℝ) : Matrix n n ℂ

docstring:
Polar decomposition in `GL(n, ℂ)`: every invertible complex matrix is uniquely the product of
a unitary matrix and a positive-definite Hermitian matrix.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Bilinear and Quadratic Forms Over a Vector Space /
Endomorphisms / polar decompositions in GL(n, ℂ); R. A. Horn and C. R. Johnson, Matrix Analysis,
2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2013), Theorem 7.3.1.

Proves `Wanted` entry `polar_decomposition_gl_complex`.

Proof: Specialize `Matrix.exists_unique_unitaryGroup_posDef_of_isUnit_det` to `ℂ` and unbundle
its unitary witness. The generic proof takes `P` to be the CFC square root of `Aᴴ * A` and
`U = A * P⁻¹`, the construction in Wikipedia, "Polar decomposition".
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.PolarDecompositionGLWanted.polar_decomposition_gl_complex
signature: ∀ {n : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype n] [inst_1 : DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ), IsUnit A.det → ∃ U P, U ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ ∧ P.PosDef ∧ A = U * P ∧ ∀ (U' P' : Matrix n n ℂ), U' ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ → P'.PosDef → A = U' * P' → U' = U ∧ P' = P
statement:
theorem polar_decomposition_gl_complex (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (hA : IsUnit A.det) :
    ∃ U P : Matrix n n ℂ,
      U ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ ∧ P.PosDef ∧ A = U * P ∧
        ∀ U' P' : Matrix n n ℂ,
          U' ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ → P'.PosDef → A = U' * P' → U' = U ∧ P' = P

docstring:
Polar decomposition in `GL(n, ℝ)`: every invertible real matrix is uniquely the product of an
orthogonal matrix and a positive-definite symmetric matrix.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Bilinear and Quadratic Forms Over a Vector Space /
Endomorphisms / polar decompositions in GL(n, ℝ); R. A. Horn and C. R. Johnson, Matrix Analysis,
2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2013), Theorem 7.3.1.

Proves `Wanted` entry `polar_decomposition_gl_real`.

Proof: Specialize `Matrix.exists_unique_unitaryGroup_posDef_of_isUnit_det` to `ℝ`, where the
unitary group is the orthogonal group, and unbundle its unitary witness. The generic proof takes
`P` to be the CFC square root of `Aᴴ * A` and `U = A * P⁻¹`, the construction in Wikipedia,
"Polar decomposition".
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.PolarDecompositionGLWanted.polar_decomposition_gl_real
signature: ∀ {n : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype n] [inst_1 : DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ), IsUnit A.det → ∃ O S, O ∈ Matrix.orthogonalGroup n ℝ ∧ S.PosDef ∧ A = O * S ∧ ∀ (O' S' : Matrix n n ℝ), O' ∈ Matrix.orthogonalGroup n ℝ → S'.PosDef → A = O' * S' → O' = O ∧ S' = S
statement:
theorem polar_decomposition_gl_real (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (hA : IsUnit A.det) :
    ∃ O S : Matrix n n ℝ,
      O ∈ Matrix.orthogonalGroup n ℝ ∧ S.PosDef ∧ A = O * S ∧
        ∀ O' S' : Matrix n n ℝ,
          O' ∈ Matrix.orthogonalGroup n ℝ → S'.PosDef → A = O' * S' → O' = O ∧ S' = S

docstring:
Rectangular real singular value decomposition: every real `m × n` matrix factors as `U * Σ * Vᵀ`
with `U` and `V` orthogonal and `Σ` diagonal with nonnegative entries; the singular values
beyond the first `min m n` (indices `j` with `m ≤ j.val`) are zero.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Numerical Analysis / Iterative methods / singular value
decomposition; G. H. Golub and C. F. Van Loan, Matrix Computations, 4th ed., Johns Hopkins
University Press (2013), Theorem 2.4.1.

Proves `Wanted` entry `real_singular_value_decomposition`.

Proof: Apply the spectral theorem to `AᵀA`, normalize the images of the eigenvectors with positive
eigenvalues, and extend them to an orthonormal basis of the codomain, as in the proof of S. Axler,
Linear Algebra Done Right, 4th ed., 7.70, and the matrix form that follows it (Section 7E).
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.RealSVDWanted.real_singular_value_decomposition
signature: ∀ (m n : ℕ) (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ), ∃ U V σ, (∀ (j : Fin n), 0 ≤ σ j) ∧ (∀ (j : Fin n), m ≤ ↑j → σ j = 0) ∧ U ∈ Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin m) ℝ ∧ V ∈ Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ ∧ A = (U * Matrix.of fun i j ↦ if ↑i = ↑j then σ j else 0) * V.transpose
statement:
theorem real_singular_value_decomposition (m n : ℕ) (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) :
    ∃ (U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ) (V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ),
      (∀ j, 0 ≤ σ j) ∧ (∀ j, m ≤ j.val → σ j = 0) ∧
      U ∈ Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin m) ℝ ∧ V ∈ Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ ∧
      A = U * Matrix.of (fun i j => if i.val = j.val then σ j else 0) *
        Matrix.transpose V

docstring:
Every matrix over a field is row-equivalent to a matrix in reduced row echelon form.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Linear algebra / Matrices / row-reduced matrices;
G. Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra, 6th ed., Wellesley-Cambridge Press (2023),
Section 2.2.

Proves `Wanted` entry `exists_isReducedRowEchelon_rowEquivalent`.

Proof: Choose pivot columns greedily (columns outside the span of the earlier ones), extend them
to a basis of `m → K` whose order matches the rows, and take `R` to be the coordinate matrix of the
columns of `A` in that basis and `P` the matrix of the coordinate map.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.ReducedRowEchelonWanted.exists_isReducedRowEchelon_rowEquivalent
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [inst_1 : Fintype m] [inst_2 : DecidableEq m] [inst_3 : LinearOrder m] [Fintype n] [inst_5 : LinearOrder n] (A : Matrix m n K), ∃ R P, R.IsReducedRowEchelon ∧ IsUnit P ∧ R = P * A
statement:
theorem exists_isReducedRowEchelon_rowEquivalent
    (A : Matrix m n K) :
    ∃ (R : Matrix m n K) (P : Matrix m m K),
      R.IsReducedRowEchelon ∧ IsUnit P ∧ R = P * A

docstring:
The reduced row echelon form in a row-equivalence class is unique.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Linear algebra / Matrices / row-reduced matrices;
G. Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra, 6th ed., Wellesley-Cambridge Press (2023),
Section 2.2.

Proves `Wanted` entry `isReducedRowEchelon_unique_of_rowEquivalent`.

Proof: Reindex the columns along the order isomorphism with `Fin (Fintype.card n)`. For `Fin`
columns, induct on the number of columns: the matrices agree on all but the last column by
induction, and that forces their last columns to agree.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.ReducedRowEchelonWanted.isReducedRowEchelon_unique_of_rowEquivalent
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [inst_1 : Fintype m] [inst_2 : DecidableEq m] [inst_3 : LinearOrder m] [Fintype n] [inst_5 : LinearOrder n] (R₁ R₂ : Matrix m n K), R₁.IsReducedRowEchelon → R₂.IsReducedRowEchelon → ∀ (P : Matrix m m K), IsUnit P → R₂ = P * R₁ → R₁ = R₂
statement:
theorem isReducedRowEchelon_unique_of_rowEquivalent
    (R₁ R₂ : Matrix m n K)
    (h₁ : R₁.IsReducedRowEchelon) (h₂ : R₂.IsReducedRowEchelon)
    (P : Matrix m m K) (hP : IsUnit P) (h : R₂ = P * R₁) :
    R₁ = R₂

docstring:
Row operations by an invertible matrix preserve the solution set of the homogeneous system.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Linear algebra / Matrices / elementary row operations;
G. Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra, 6th ed., Wellesley-Cambridge Press (2023),
Section 2.2.

Proves `Wanted` entry `ker_mulVecLin_mul_left_isUnit`.

Proof: `Matrix.mulVec_mulVec` rewrites `(P * A) *ᵥ x` as `P *ᵥ (A *ᵥ x)`, and `P *ᵥ ·` is
injective because `P` is a unit.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.ReducedRowEchelonWanted.ker_mulVecLin_mul_left_isUnit
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [inst_1 : Fintype m] [inst_2 : DecidableEq m] [LinearOrder m] [inst_4 : Fintype n] [LinearOrder n] (P : Matrix m m K) (A : Matrix m n K), IsUnit P → (P * A).mulVecLin.ker = A.mulVecLin.ker
statement:
theorem ker_mulVecLin_mul_left_isUnit
    (P : Matrix m m K) (A : Matrix m n K) (hP : IsUnit P) :
    LinearMap.ker (Matrix.mulVecLin (P * A)) = LinearMap.ker (Matrix.mulVecLin A)

docstring:
Simultaneous diagonalization of two real quadratic forms with one positive-definite: for a
symmetric matrix `S` and a positive-definite matrix `P`, there is an invertible congruence
diagonalizing `S` while normalizing `P` to the identity.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Bilinear and Quadratic Forms Over a Vector Space /
Endomorphisms / simultaneous diagonalization of two real quadratic forms, with one
positive-definite; R. A. Horn and C. R. Johnson, Matrix Analysis, 2nd ed., Cambridge University
Press (2013), Theorem 4.5.15.

Proves `Wanted` entry `simultaneous_diagonalization_posDef`.

Proof: Normalize `P` to the identity by a congruence built from its orthonormal eigenbasis, scaled
by the inverse square roots of its eigenvalues, then orthogonally diagonalize the transformed
symmetric matrix. This is the argument of Wikipedia's "Definite matrix", section "Simultaneous
diagonalization", with the eigenbasis scaling in place of a Cholesky factor.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.SimultaneousDiagonalizationWanted.simultaneous_diagonalization_posDef
signature: ∀ {n : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype n] [inst_1 : DecidableEq n] (S P : Matrix n n ℝ), S.IsSymm → P.PosDef → ∃ C, IsUnit C ∧ (C.transpose * S * C).IsDiag ∧ C.transpose * P * C = 1
statement:
theorem simultaneous_diagonalization_posDef
    (S P : Matrix n n ℝ) (hS : S.IsSymm) (hP : P.PosDef) :
    ∃ C : Matrix n n ℝ,
      IsUnit C ∧ (Matrix.transpose C * S * C).IsDiag ∧ Matrix.transpose C * P * C = 1

docstring:
Every strictly positive square matrix can be scaled to doubly stochastic form.
Source: R. Sinkhorn, Ann. Math. Statist. 35 (1964), 876-879, DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177703591.
Proves `Wanted` entry `sinkhorn_scaling`.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.SinkhornWanted.sinkhorn_scaling
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → ∀ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), (∀ (i j : Fin n), 0 < A i j) → ∃ r c, (∀ (i : Fin n), 0 < r i) ∧ (∀ (j : Fin n), 0 < c j) ∧ (fun i j ↦ r i * A i j * c j) ∈ doublyStochastic ℝ (Fin n)
statement:
theorem sinkhorn_scaling {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
    (hA : ∀ i j, 0 < A i j) :
    ∃ (r c : Fin n → ℝ), (∀ i, 0 < r i) ∧ (∀ j, 0 < c j) ∧
      (fun i j => r i * A i j * c j) ∈ doublyStochastic ℝ (Fin n)

docstring:
The permanent of a doubly stochastic matrix is at least n! / n^n.
Source: G. P. Egorychev, Adv. Math. 42 (1981), 299-305, DOI 10.1016/0001-8708(81)90044-X; D. I.
Falikman, Math. Notes 29 (1981), 475-479, DOI 10.1007/BF01163285.

Proves `Wanted` entry `van_der_waerden_permanent`.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.VanDerWaerdenWanted.van_der_waerden_permanent
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → ∀ A ∈ doublyStochastic ℝ (Fin n), ↑n.factorial / ↑n ^ n ≤ A.permanent
statement:
public theorem van_der_waerden_permanent {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
    (hA : A ∈ doublyStochastic ℝ (Fin n)) :
    ((n.factorial : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ^ n) ≤ A.permanent

docstring:
Any submodule of a finite free module over a PID has a Smith normal form with invariant-factor
divisibility chain `a i ∣ a (i+1)`, the refinement beyond the existing Mathlib diagonal-basis
Smith-form API.
Source: H. J. S. Smith, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. 151 (1861), 293-326, DOI 10.1098/RSTL.1861.0016.
It is `Submodule.exists_smith_normal_form_dvd_chain`, kept under the source's name.
Proves `Wanted` entry `smithNormalForm`.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.SmithNormalFormWanted.smithNormalForm
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsPrincipalIdealRing R] [inst_3 : AddCommGroup M] [inst_4 : _root_.Module R M] [Module.Free R M] [Module.Finite R M] (N : Submodule R M), ∃ n m, ∃ (hnm : n ≤ m), ∃ bM bN a, (∀ (i : Fin n), ↑(bN i) = a i • bM (Fin.castLE hnm i)) ∧ (∀ (i : Fin n), a i ≠ 0) ∧ ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi1 : i < n) (hi2 : i + 1 < n), a ⟨i, hi1⟩ ∣ a ⟨i + 1, hi2⟩
statement:
theorem smithNormalForm
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsPrincipalIdealRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Free R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (N : Submodule R M) :
    ∃ (n m : ℕ) (hnm : n ≤ m) (bM : Module.Basis (Fin m) R M)
      (bN : Module.Basis (Fin n) R N) (a : Fin n → R),
      (∀ i, (bN i : M) = a i • bM (Fin.castLE hnm i)) ∧
      (∀ i, a i ≠ 0) ∧
      (∀ (i : ℕ) (hi1 : i < n) (hi2 : i + 1 < n), a ⟨i, hi1⟩ ∣ a ⟨i + 1, hi2⟩)

docstring: Source: Folklore (Pfaffian computation). Listed as §39 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Marked as an open TODO at the head of Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/SymplecticGroup.lean (rev 5450b53e5ddc). Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `symplectic_matrix_det`.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.SymplecticDetWanted.LinearAlgebra.symplectic_matrix_det
signature: ∀ {l : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq l] [inst_1 : Fintype l] [inst_2 : CommRing R] {A : Matrix (l ⊕ l) (l ⊕ l) R}, A ∈ Matrix.symplecticGroup l R → A.det = 1

public theorem_wanted symplectic_matrix_det
    {l R : Type*} [DecidableEq l] [Fintype l] [CommRing R]
    {A : Matrix (l ⊕ l) (l ⊕ l) R} (_hA : A ∈ Matrix.symplecticGroup l R) :
    A.det = 1

docstring:
The coefficient `c_k` in the usual monic characteristic-polynomial
expansion `χ_A(X) = X^N + c₁ X^(N-1) + ... + c_N`.

Mathlib's `Matrix.charpoly` is the monic characteristic polynomial
`det (X • 1 - A)`, so this is the coefficient of degree `N - k`.
For `k > N`, the coefficient is `0`, which lets the trace recurrence be
stated uniformly for all positive `k`.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TraceNewtonWanted.LinearAlgebra.TraceNewton.charpolyDescendingCoeff
signature: {n : Type u_1} → [Fintype n] → [DecidableEq n] → {R : Type u_2} → [CommRing R] → Matrix n n R → ℕ → R
statement:
noncomputable def charpolyDescendingCoeff {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (A : Matrix n n R) (k : ℕ) : R

docstring: Source: Knill, *Some fundamental theorems in mathematics*, §220. Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `trace_cayley_hamilton_newton`.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TraceNewtonWanted.LinearAlgebra.TraceNewton.trace_cayley_hamilton_newton
signature: ∀ {n : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype n] [inst_1 : DecidableEq n] {R : Type u_2} [inst_2 : CommRing R] (A : Matrix n n R) {k : ℕ}, 1 ≤ k → ↑k * MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TraceNewtonWanted.LinearAlgebra.TraceNewton.charpolyDescendingCoeff A k + ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (A ^ j).trace * MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TraceNewtonWanted.LinearAlgebra.TraceNewton.charpolyDescendingCoeff A (k - j) = 0
statement:
public theorem_wanted trace_cayley_hamilton_newton {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (A : Matrix n n R) {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    (k : R) * charpolyDescendingCoeff A k +
        ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k,
          trace (A ^ j) * charpolyDescendingCoeff A (k - j) = 0

docstring:
An endomorphism whose characteristic polynomial splits is triangularizable: there is a basis
in which its matrix is upper triangular.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Linear algebra / Structure theory of endomorphisms /
triangularization; S. Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right, 4th ed., Springer (2024), Theorem 5.41.

Proves `Wanted` entry `exists_basis_upperTriangular_toMatrix`.

Proof: induction on dimension. An eigenvector spans an invariant line, the induced map on the
quotient has split minimal polynomial (it divides that of `f`), and a triangularizing basis of the
quotient lifts, together with the eigenvector, to one of `V` (`Module.Basis.sumQuot`). This is the
eigenvector-deflation induction of the proof of Schur's theorem in R. A. Horn and C. R. Johnson,
Matrix Analysis, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2013), Theorem 2.3.1, without unitarity.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TriangularizationWanted.exists_basis_upperTriangular_toMatrix
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_2 : _root_.Module K V] [inst_3 : FiniteDimensional K V] {ι : Type u_3} [inst_4 : Fintype ι] [inst_5 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_6 : LinearOrder ι] (f : Module.End K V), (LinearMap.charpoly f).Splits → Module.finrank K V = Fintype.card ι → ∃ b, ((LinearMap.toMatrix b b) f).IsUpperTriangular
statement:
theorem exists_basis_upperTriangular_toMatrix
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [LinearOrder ι]
    (f : Module.End K V) (h : f.charpoly.Splits)
    (hdim : Module.finrank K V = Fintype.card ι) :
    ∃ b : Module.Basis ι K V, (LinearMap.toMatrix b b f).IsUpperTriangular

docstring:
A square matrix whose characteristic polynomial splits is similar to an upper-triangular
matrix.

Sources: Mathlib `docs/undergrad.yaml`, Linear algebra / Structure theory of endomorphisms /
triangularization; R. A. Horn and C. R. Johnson, Matrix Analysis, 2nd ed., Cambridge University
Press (2013), Theorem 2.3.1.

Proves `Wanted` entry `exists_upperTriangular_similar_of_splits`.

Proof: apply `exists_basis_upperTriangular_toMatrix` to `Matrix.toLin` of the matrix and
conjugate by the change-of-basis matrix from the standard basis.
name: MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TriangularizationWanted.exists_upperTriangular_similar_of_splits
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] {n : Type u_3} [inst_1 : Fintype n] [inst_2 : DecidableEq n] [inst_3 : LinearOrder n] (A : Matrix n n K), A.charpoly.Splits → ∃ P T, IsUnit P ∧ T.IsUpperTriangular ∧ A = P * T * P⁻¹
statement:
theorem exists_upperTriangular_similar_of_splits
    {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [LinearOrder n]

    ∃ P T : Matrix n n K, IsUnit P ∧ T.IsUpperTriangular ∧ A = P * T * P⁻¹

Math. 6 (1924) 244–277 original paradox; S. Wagon, The Banach–Tarski Paradox, Cambridge Univ.
Press (1993); Lean states closed unit ball duplication specialization in ℝ³ with ambient `≃ᵢ`
equidecomposability.

docstring:
There exists a measurable compact `K ⊆ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` with `volume K = 0` such that
every unit vector `v` has a translate `a + [0, 1]·v ⊆ K`. Source: A. S. Besicovitch, Math. Z. 27
(1928) 312–320 and S. Kakeya, Tohoku Rep. 6 (1917); Perron-tree gives compact measure-zero Kakeya
set; Lean states compact Lebesgue-null oriented version in ℝ² with segments `a+t•v`, `t∈[0, 1]`.

The proof here follows T. W. Körner, "Besicovitch via Baire", Studia Math. 158 (2003): a
Baire-category argument in the Hausdorff metric space of compact sets, not a Perron-tree
construction.

formulation R. J. Gardner, Bull. AMS 39 (2002), 355–406, DOI 10.1090/S0273-0979-02-00941-2.

For `0 < n`, every `n`-family of finite Borel measures on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` with `μ i ≪
volume` admits a unit vector `v` and `t : ℝ` bisecting each measure into two half-spaces of equal
mass `μ i univ / 2`. Source: A. H. Stone and J. W. Tukey, Duke Math. J. 9 (1942) 356–359 ham
sandwich theorem; J. Matoušek, Using the Borsuk–Ulam Theorem; Lean states measure-theoretic
Euclidean specialization with `μ i ≪ volume` making the bisecting hyperplane null.

22 (1976), 366–389, DOI 10.1016/0022-1236(76)90004-5.

docstring:
Take `λ_SSS` to be the greatest real number `λ` such that, for any `ε > 0`,
there are only finitely many totally positive algebraic integers α satisfying
`tr(α) < (λ − ε) * deg(α)`. Note that the paper said "least real number",
but this is clearly a typo, as this set does not have a lower bound. Defining
it as the greatest real number is consistent with how this constant is defined in
another paper by the same author, namely in Orloski, Sardari and Smith: "New
lower bounds for the Schur-Siegel-Smyth trace problem" (arXiv:2401.03252).
There, `λ_SSS` is defined as the limit inferior of `tr(α)/deg(α)` over all
totally positive `α`, which is exactly the *greatest* real number `λ` such that
for all `ε > 0`, only finitely many `α` have `tr(α)/deg(α) < λ - ε`.

docstring:
**Gronwall's theorem** (maximal order of the sum-of-divisors function): the `limsup`
at `Filter.atTop` of `σ(n) / (n * log (log n))` equals `Real.exp
Real.eulerMascheroniConstant`, i.e. `e ^ γ`. Source: S. Nazardonyavi and S. Yakubovich,
"Extremely Abundant Numbers and the Riemann Hypothesis," Journal of Integer Sequences 17
(2014), Article 14.2.8, lines 98–111,
https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL17/Nazar/nazar4.tex (live source SHA-256
`6854eacdc72e1e5a005b005552942d6d7cfa7a41d7892c0f61bb2b1886e1d7c5`); original
attribution: T. H. Gronwall, "Some asymptotic expressions in the theory of numbers,"
Transactions of the AMS 14 (1913), 113–122. Totalization note: `σ`, division, and the
logarithms are total Lean functions, so the finitely many small natural inputs where
`n * log (log n)` is nonpositive or zero merely contribute finitely many values and do
not affect the `limsup` at `Filter.atTop`.

Proves `Wanted` entry `gronwall_sigma_limsup`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ArithmeticFunction.GronwallSigmaLimsupWanted.gronwall_sigma_limsup
signature: Filter.limsup (fun n ↦ ↑((ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n) / (↑n * Real.log (Real.log ↑n))) Filter.atTop = Real.exp Real.eulerMascheroniConstant
statement:
theorem gronwall_sigma_limsup :
    Filter.limsup
      (fun n : ℕ => ((ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n : ℕ) : ℝ) /
        ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log n))) Filter.atTop =
      Real.exp Real.eulerMascheroniConstant

statement:
theorem isAsymptoticDobrowolskiCoefficient_iff_strict {c : ℝ} :
    IsAsymptoticDobrowolskiCoefficient c ↔
      ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ D : ℕ, 3 ≤ D ∧
        ∀ α : ℂ, IsAlgebraic ℚ α → α ≠ 0 → ¬IsOfFinOrder α →
          D ≤ (minpoly ℚ α).natDegree →
            1 + (c - ε) * dobrowolskiScale (minpoly ℚ α).natDegree <
              algebraicMahlerMeasure α

docstring:
Statement of Corollary 1.1 (Liouville does not correlate with polynomial phases on
short intervals on average):

Let `λ` denote the liouville function. Fix `k : ℕ` and `θ : ℝ` such that `0 < θ < 1`. Then

`∫ x ∈ [X, 2X], ‖λ‖_{uᵏ⁺¹[x, x + Xᶿ]}dx = o(X)`

as `X → ∞`.
Source: K. Matomäki, M. Radziwiłł, T. Tao, J. Teräväinen, and T. Ziegler, `Higher uniformity of bounded multiplicative functions in short intervals on average`, Annals of Math, 197 (2) 2023. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2023-197-2-BoundedMultiplicativeFunctions.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_bounded_multiplicative_functions`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BoundedMultiplicativeFunctionsWanted.BoundedMultiplicativeFunctions.corollary_1_1
signature: ∀ (k : ℕ) (θ : ℝ), 0 < θ → θ < 1 → (fun X ↦ ∫ (x : ℝ) in X..2 * X, MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BoundedMultiplicativeFunctionsWanted.BoundedMultiplicativeFunctions.weakGowersUniformityNorm k x (X ^ θ) fun n ↦ ↑(ArithmeticFunction.liouville ⌊n⌋₊)) =o[Filter.atTop] fun X ↦ X

docstring:
Statement of Theorem 1.3 (Non-pretentious multiplicative functions do not correlate
with polynomial phases on short intervals on average):

Let `k : ℕ`, `θ : ℝ` such that `0 < θ < 1/2` and `η : ℝ` such that `η > 0`. Then there exist
constants `Q : ℕ` such that `Q > 0`, `C : ℝ` such that `C > 0`, and `B : ℝ`, such that for any
multiplicative 1-bounded arithmetic function `f : ℕ → ℂ`, any `X : ℝ` such that `X ≥ 1` and any
`H : ℝ` such that `Xᶿ ≤ H ≤ X¹⁻ᶿ`, if

`∫ x ∈ [X, 2X], ‖f‖_{uᵏ⁺¹[x, x + H]}dx ≥ ηX`

then

`M(f;CXᵏ⁺¹/Hᵏ⁺¹,Q) ≤ B`.
Source: K. Matomäki, M. Radziwiłł, T. Tao, J. Teräväinen, and T. Ziegler, `Higher uniformity of bounded multiplicative functions in short intervals on average`, Annals of Math, 197 (2) 2023. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2023-197-2-BoundedMultiplicativeFunctions.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_bounded_multiplicative_functions`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BoundedMultiplicativeFunctionsWanted.BoundedMultiplicativeFunctions.theorem_1_3
signature: ∀ (k : ℕ) (θ : ℝ), 0 < θ → θ < 1 / 2 → ∀ η > 0, ∃ Q, ∃ (_ : 1 ≤ Q), ∃ C, ∃ (_ : 0 < C), ∃ B, ∀ (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ), f.IsMultiplicative → MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BoundedMultiplicativeFunctionsWanted.BoundedMultiplicativeFunctions.IsOneBounded ⇑f → ∀ X ≥ 1, ∀ (H : ℝ), X ^ θ ≤ H → H ≤ X ^ (1 - θ) → ∫ (x : ℝ) in X..2 * X, MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BoundedMultiplicativeFunctionsWanted.BoundedMultiplicativeFunctions.weakGowersUniformityNorm k x H f.intExtension ≥ η * X → MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BoundedMultiplicativeFunctionsWanted.BoundedMultiplicativeFunctions.M (⇑f) (C * X ^ (k + 1) / H ^ (k + 1)) Q ≤ B
statement:
public theorem_wanted theorem_1_3 (k : ℕ) (θ : ℝ) (hθ₀ : 0 < θ) (hθ₁ : θ < 1 / 2) (η : ℝ) (hη : η > 0) :
    ∃ (Q : ℕ+) (_hQ : 1 ≤ Q) (C : ℝ) (_hC : 0 < C) (B : ℝ),
      ∀ (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ) (_hf : f.IsMultiplicative) (_hf' : IsOneBounded f)
        (X : ℝ) (_hX : X ≥ 1) (H : ℝ) (_hXH : X ^ θ ≤ H) (_hHX : H ≤ X ^ (1 - θ)),
          ∫ x in X..(2 * X), weakGowersUniformityNorm k x H f.intExtension ≥ η * X →
            M f (C * X ^ (k + 1) / H ^ (k + 1)) Q ≤ B

docstring:
Given `k : ℕ`, `x H : ℝ` we define the weak Gowers uniformity norm of a function `f : ℤ → ℂ`
by the formula:

`‖f‖_{uᵏ⁺¹[x, x + H]} :=`
  `sup_{P ∈ ℝ[X] | degree(P) ≤ k} (1/H) |∑_{x ≤ n ≤ x + H} f(n)exp(2πi(-P(n)))|`.

docstring: Large-square prime contribution bounded by the `c_9` term.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.U9_B_le
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∑ p ∈ {p ∈ (2100 * n + 1).primesBelow | p ≤ 1890 * n} with 2100 * n < p ^ 2, ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.nu9 p n) * Real.log ↑p ≤ (18900 / 279 + 18900 / 657 + 18900 / 963) * ↑n * Real.log 3.4

lemma U9_B_le (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    ∑ p ∈ ((Nat.primesBelow (2100 * n + 1)).filter (fun p => p ≤ 1890 * n)).filter
      (fun p => 2100 * n < p ^ 2),
      ((nu9 p n : ℤ) : ℝ) * Real.log ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)
    ≤ (18900 / 279 + 18900 / 657 + 18900 / 963 : ℝ) * (n : ℝ) * Real.log 3.4

docstring: One level layer bounded via the primorial estimate.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.U9_Bi_le
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (B : Finset ℕ), (∀ p ∈ B, Nat.Prime p ∧ p ≤ 1890 * n) → ∀ (i : ℕ), 1 ≤ i → ∀ (jm : ℝ), 1 ≤ jm → (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ≤ 1890 * n → ↑i ≤ MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.G9r (↑n / ↑p) → ↑p ≤ 18900 * ↑n / jm) → 0 ≤ 18900 * ↑n / jm → ∑ p ∈ B with i ≤ (MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.G9r (↑n / ↑p)).toNat, Real.log ↑p ≤ 18900 * ↑n / jm * Real.log 3.4
statement:
lemma U9_Bi_le (n : ℕ) (_hn : 1 ≤ n) (B : Finset ℕ)
    (hBmem : ∀ p ∈ B, p.Prime ∧ p ≤ 1890 * n)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) (jm : ℝ) (_hjm : 1 ≤ jm)
    (hle_i : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ≤ 1890 * n → (i : ℤ) ≤ G9r ((n : ℝ) / ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) →
      ((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ 18900 * (n : ℝ) / jm)
    (hYnn : 0 ≤ 18900 * (n : ℝ) / jm) :
    ∑ p ∈ B.filter (fun p => i ≤ (G9r ((n : ℝ) / ((p : ℕ) : ℝ))).toNat),
        Real.log ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)
      ≤ 18900 * (n : ℝ) / jm * Real.log 3.4

docstring: Single-term lower bound for `logF9`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.logF9_term_lower
signature: ∀ q ∈ MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.w9, ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ↑q.2 * (Real.log ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.N10m q.1 n).factorial - Real.log ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.N9m q.1 n).factorial - Real.log ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.N1m q.1 n).factorial) ≥ ↑q.2 * (MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.fmain ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.N10m q.1 n) - MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.fmain ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.N9m q.1 n) - MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.fmain ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.N1m q.1 n)) - (1 + Real.log ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.N10m q.1 n) + Real.log ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.N9m q.1 n) + Real.log ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.N1m q.1 n))
statement:
lemma logF9_term_lower (q : ℕ × ℤ) (hq : q ∈ w9) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    (q.2 : ℝ) * (Real.log (((N10m q.1 n)!) : ℝ) - Real.log (((N9m q.1 n)!) : ℝ)
      - Real.log (((N1m q.1 n)!) : ℝ))
    ≥ (q.2 : ℝ) * (fmain ((N10m q.1 n : ℕ) : ℝ) - fmain ((N9m q.1 n : ℕ) : ℝ)
      - fmain ((N1m q.1 n : ℕ) : ℝ))
      - (1 + Real.log ((N10m q.1 n : ℕ) : ℝ) + Real.log ((N9m q.1 n : ℕ) : ℝ)
        + Real.log ((N1m q.1 n : ℕ) : ℝ))

docstring: Upper bound for `logF9 n` assuming no prime in `(1890 * n, 2100 * n]`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.logF9_upper
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → 1890 * n < p → p ≤ 2100 * n → False) → MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.Internal.logF9 n ≤ (18900 / 279 + 18900 / 657 + 18900 / 963) * ↑n * Real.log 3.4 + √(2100 * ↑n) * Real.log (2100 * ↑n)

docstring:
Every real `x ≥ 48` has a prime strictly between `x` and `(9 / 8) * x`.
Source: R. Breusch, *Zur Verallgemeinerung des Bertrandschen Postulates*,
Math. Z. 34 (1932), 505–526, conclusion on p. 515.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.breusch_prime_interval
signature: ∀ (x : ℝ), 48 ≤ x → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ x < ↑p ∧ ↑p < 9 / 8 * x
statement:
theorem breusch_prime_interval : ∀ x : ℝ, 48 ≤ x →
    ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ x < (p : ℝ) ∧ (p : ℝ) < (9 / 8 : ℝ) * x

docstring:
Ramanujan's two-primes refinement of Bertrand's postulate: for `n ≥ 6`
there are two distinct primes in the open interval `(n, 2 * n)`.

For `n ≥ 48`, this follows by applying `breusch_prime_interval` at `n` and
`9n/8`. The remaining finite range is checked by kernel reduction.

Source: Nathaniel Benjamin, Grant Fickes, Eugene Fiorini,
Edgar Jaramillo Rodriguez, Eric Jovinelly, and Tony W. H. Wong, "Primes
and Perfect Powers in the Catalan Triangle", Journal of Integer Sequences
22 (2019), Article 19.7.6, proof sentence at line 153 (inside the proof of
the theorem labeled `c_nn not power`), attributed there to Ramanujan,
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL22/Fiorini/fiorini3.tex>.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.BreuschWanted.ramanujan_two_primes_between
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ), 6 ≤ n → ∃ p q, Nat.Prime p ∧ Nat.Prime q ∧ n < p ∧ p < q ∧ q < 2 * n
statement:
theorem ramanujan_two_primes_between (n : ℕ) (hn : 6 ≤ n) :
    ∃ p q : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ n < p ∧ p < q ∧ q < 2 * n

docstring:
A length-`M` integer Büchi sequence: the second differences of the squared
terms are constantly `2`. Only the prefix `j < M` of the total function `u`
is observed.

docstring:
A length-`M` Büchi sequence is trivial when, up to independently changing
the signs of its terms, it is a run of consecutive increasing integers. Since
independent signs do not change squares, and equality of integer squares
supplies the necessary signs, this is encoded by requiring an integer `x`
with `u j ^ 2 = (x + j) ^ 2` for every `j < M`.

signature: ℕ → (ℕ → ℤ) → Prop
statement: def IsTrivial (M : ℕ) (u : ℕ → ℤ) : Prop

docstring:
Büchi's integer-square sequence conjecture in general existential-length
form: there exists a length `M ≥ 5` for which every length-`M` Büchi sequence
is trivial.

signature: Prop
statement: def conjecture : Prop

docstring:
Resolved true: Stanley Yao Xiao (arXiv:2412.16740v3, Jun 2025) proves unconditionally that five
integer squares with constant second difference 2 are consecutive (Theorem 1.3), so the
formalized existential-length claim holds with M = 5; the earlier length-8 bound was Vojta's
conditional result under Bombieri-Lang. Source: Stanley Yao Xiao, Hilbert's tenth problem for
systems of diagonal quadratic forms, and Büchi's problem, arXiv:2412.16740v3 (2025),
https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.16740v3. Moved from
`OpenConjectures/NumberTheory/BuchiSquareSequenceBound`.

statement: public theorem_wanted conjecture_holds : conjecture

signature: LinearIndependent ℚ ![1, riemannZeta 2, ZMod.LFunction ![0, 1, -1] 2] ∧ ∀ (m n : ℤ), m ≠ -1 → m ≠ 0 → n ≠ -1 → n ≠ 0 → 10 ^ 6 * |m - n| < |n| → Irrational (Real.log (1 + 1 / ↑m) * Real.log (1 + 1 / ↑n)) ∧ (m ≠ n → LinearIndependent ℚ ![1, Real.log (1 + 1 / ↑m), Real.log (1 + 1 / ↑n), Real.log (1 + 1 / ↑m) * Real.log (1 + 1 / ↑n)])

docstring:
Statement of Theorem 1.1:

For an odd prime number `p`, and a power `q` of `p` satisfying
`q > 685090 * p ^ 2`, the following holds. For any nonzero `h ∈ 𝔽_q[T]`, we have
`#{f ∈ 𝔽_q[T] : |f| = X, f and f + h are prime} ∼ 𝔖_q(h) X / log_q^2 (X)`
as `X → ∞` through the powers of `q`.

Moreover, we have a power saving (depending on q) in the asymptotic above.
Source: W. Sawin and M. Shusterman, `On the Chowla and twin primes conjectures over 𝔽_q[T]`, Annals of Math, 196 (2) 2022. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2022-196-2-ChowlaAndTwinPrimeOverFqT.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_chowla_and_twin_prime_over_fq_t`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ChowlaAndTwinPrimeOverFqTWanted.ChowlaAndTwinPrimeOverFqT.theorem_1_1
signature: ∀ {p : ℕ} [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {n : ℕ}, Odd p → p ^ n > 685090 * p ^ 2 → ∃ ε > 0, ∀ (h : Polynomial (GaloisField p n)), h ≠ 0 → (fun X ↦ ↑{f | ‖f‖ = ↑↑X ∧ f ∈ MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ChowlaAndTwinPrimeOverFqTWanted.ChowlaAndTwinPrimeOverFqT.primes (GaloisField p n) ∧ f + h ∈ MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ChowlaAndTwinPrimeOverFqTWanted.ChowlaAndTwinPrimeOverFqT.primes (GaloisField p n)}.ncard - MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ChowlaAndTwinPrimeOverFqTWanted.ChowlaAndTwinPrimeOverFqT.𝔖_q h * ↑↑X / Real.logb (↑p ^ n) ↑↑X ^ 2) =O[Filter.atTop] fun X ↦ ↑↑X ^ (1 - ε)
statement:
public theorem_wanted theorem_1_1 (hp : Odd p) (hq : q > 685090 * p ^ 2) :
    ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), -- there exists a power saving such that ...
      ∀ h ≠ 0, (fun X : powers q ↦ Set.ncard {f | ‖f‖ = X ∧ f ∈ primes 𝔽_q ∧ f + h ∈ primes 𝔽_q} -
        𝔖_q h * X / (Real.logb q X) ^ 2) =O[Filter.atTop] (fun X : powers q ↦ (X : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε))

docstring:
Statement of Theorem 1.3:

For an odd prime number `p`, an integer `k ≥ 1`, and a power `q` of `p` satisfying `q > p²k²e²`,
the following holds. For every fixed choice of `k` distinct polynomials `h₁,...,hₖ ∈ 𝔽_q[T]`,
we have `∑ (f ∈ 𝔽_q[T]⁺, |f| ≤ X), μ(f + h₁) μ(f + h₂) ... μ(f + hₖ) = o(X)`, `X → ∞`.
Source: W. Sawin and M. Shusterman, `On the Chowla and twin primes conjectures over 𝔽_q[T]`, Annals of Math, 196 (2) 2022. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2022-196-2-ChowlaAndTwinPrimeOverFqT.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_chowla_and_twin_prime_over_fq_t`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ChowlaAndTwinPrimeOverFqTWanted.ChowlaAndTwinPrimeOverFqT.theorem_1_3
signature: ∀ {p : ℕ} [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {n : ℕ}, Odd p → ∀ k ≥ 1, ↑p ^ n > ↑p ^ 2 * ↑k ^ 2 * Real.exp 1 ^ 2 → ∀ (h : Fin k → Polynomial (GaloisField p n)), Function.Injective h → (fun X ↦ ∑' (f : ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ChowlaAndTwinPrimeOverFqTWanted.ChowlaAndTwinPrimeOverFqT.monicBounded (GaloisField p n) X)), ∏ i, UniqueFactorizationMonoid.moebius (↑f + h i)) =o[Filter.atTop] id

docstring:
Grundman consecutive `b`-Niven bound: for base `b ≥ 2` and start `a > 0`,
some `i ≤ 2 * b` has `a + i` not divisible by its base-`b` digit sum, so no
`2 * b + 1` consecutive positive integers beginning at `a` are all `b`-Niven.
`Nat.digits b` supplies the base-`b` digits whose sum defines a `b`-Niven
number. Source: Michael Gohn, Joshua Harrington, Sophia Lebiere, Hani Samamah,
Kyla Shappell, and Tony W. H. Wong, "Arithmetic Progressions of b-Prodigious
Numbers," Journal of Integer Sequences 25 (2022), Article 22.8.7, line 149,
`https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL25/Wong/wong42.tex` (live source
SHA-256 `09b0ec8ea4e9539b3460be066b663952caef58777a25d79dca670beb5bd1381f`,
exact line-149 SHA-256
`93d551f5f24448b2ba0a54f1d28eadaa5c2ee800104778a7a18997c8b1980ef1`), citing as
the original result Heidi Grundman, "Sequences of consecutive n-Niven numbers,"
Fibonacci Quarterly 32 (1994), 174–175.

Proves `Wanted` entry `grundman_consecutive_niven_bound`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Digits.GrundmanNivenBoundWanted.grundman_consecutive_niven_bound
signature: ∀ (b a : ℕ), 2 ≤ b → 0 < a → ∃ i ≤ 2 * b, ¬(b.digits (a + i)).sum ∣ a + i
statement:
theorem grundman_consecutive_niven_bound
    (b a : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (ha : 0 < a) :
    ∃ i : ℕ, i ≤ 2 * b ∧
      ¬ ((Nat.digits b (a + i)).sum ∣ a + i)

docstring:
Statement of Theorem 1 (Number fields have small models):

There exists a positive constant `Q` such that the following is true. Let `K` be a number field
of degree `n ≥ Q` and root discriminant `δ` over `ℚ`. Then there exist integers `r ≤ Q log n` and
`d ≤ Q log n` such that `(d + r) choose r ≤ Q n log n`, and there exist `r` polynomials
`E₁, ..., Eᵣ` of degree `≤ d` in `ℤ[x₁, ..., xᵣ]` all having coefficients bounded in absolute value
by `(n δ) ^ (Q log n)` such that the (smooth and zero-dimensional affine) scheme with equations
`E₁ = ... = Eᵣ = 0` and `det (∂Eᵢ/∂xⱼ) ≠ 0` contains `Spec K` as one of its irreducible components.
Source: J.-M. Couveignes, `Enumerating number fields`, Annals of Math, 192 (2) 2020. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2020-192-2-EnumeratingNumberFields.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_enumerating_number_fields`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.EnumeratingNumberFieldsWanted.EnumeratingNumberFields.theorem_1
signature: ∃ Q > 0, ∀ n ≥ Q, ∀ (K : MathlibExt.NumberTheory.EnumeratingNumberFieldsWanted.EnumeratingNumberFields.NumberFieldOfDegree n), ∃ r d, ↑r ≤ ↑Q * Real.log ↑n ∧ ↑d ≤ ↑Q * Real.log ↑n ∧ ↑((d + r).choose r) ≤ ↑Q * ↑n * Real.log ↑n ∧ ∃ E, (∀ (i : Fin r), (E i).totalDegree ≤ d) ∧ (∀ (i : Fin r) (j : Fin r →₀ ℕ), ↑|(E i).coeff j| ≤ (↑n * NumberField.rootDiscr K.carrier) ^ (↑Q * Real.log ↑n)) ∧ ∃ Z, ∃ (hZ : Z ∈ irreducibleComponents ↥(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.EnumeratingNumberFieldsWanted.EnumeratingNumberFields.nonsingularOpen fun i ↦ (MvPolynomial.map (Algebra.algebraMap ℤ ℚ)) (E i))), Nonempty ((MathlibExt.NumberTheory.EnumeratingNumberFieldsWanted.EnumeratingNumberFields.nonsingularOpen fun i ↦ (MvPolynomial.map (Algebra.algebraMap ℤ ℚ)) (E i)).irreducibleComponent Z hZ ≅ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec ↧K.carrier)
statement:
public theorem_wanted theorem_1 : ∃ Q > 0, ∀ n ≥ Q, ∀ K : NumberFieldOfDegree n, ∃ (r d : ℕ),
    r ≤ Q * log n ∧ d ≤ Q * log n ∧ (d + r).choose r ≤ Q * n * log n ∧
      ∃ E : Fin r → MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ, (∀ i, (E i).totalDegree ≤ d) ∧
        (∀ i j, |(E i).coeff j| ≤ (n * rootDiscr K) ^ (Q * log n)) ∧
          letI X := nonsingularOpen fun i ↦ (E i).map (algebraMap ℤ ℚ)
          ∃ Z, ∃ hZ : Z ∈ irreducibleComponents X,

Statement of Theorem 2 (Number fields with bounded discriminant):

There exists a positive constant `Q` such that the following is true. Let `n ≥ Q` be an integer.
Let `H ≥ 1` be an integer. The number of isomorphism classes of number fields
with degree `n` and discriminant `≤ H` is `≤ n^(Q n log^3 n) H^(Q log^3 n)`.
Source: J.-M. Couveignes, `Enumerating number fields`, Annals of Math, 192 (2) 2020. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2020-192-2-EnumeratingNumberFields.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_enumerating_number_fields`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.EnumeratingNumberFieldsWanted.EnumeratingNumberFields.theorem_2
signature: ∃ Q > 0, ∀ n ≥ Q, ∀ H ≥ 1, Finite (MathlibExt.NumberTheory.EnumeratingNumberFieldsWanted.EnumeratingNumberFields.NumberFieldOfBoundedDiscriminantUpToIsomorphism n H) ∧ ↑(Nat.card (MathlibExt.NumberTheory.EnumeratingNumberFieldsWanted.EnumeratingNumberFields.NumberFieldOfBoundedDiscriminantUpToIsomorphism n H)) ≤ ↑n ^ (↑Q * ↑n * Real.log ↑n ^ 3) * ↑H ^ (↑Q * Real.log ↑n ^ 3)
statement:
public theorem_wanted theorem_2 : ∃ Q > 0, ∀ n ≥ Q, ∀ H ≥ 1,
    Finite (NumberFieldOfBoundedDiscriminantUpToIsomorphism n H) ∧
    (Nat.card (NumberFieldOfBoundedDiscriminantUpToIsomorphism n H) : ℝ) ≤
      n ^ (Q * n * log n ^ 3) * H ^ (Q * log n ^ 3)

: Fin g → ℕ, n = ∑ i, (x i) ^ k`. Source: D. Hilbert, Beweis für die Darstellbarkeit der ganzen
Zahlen durch eine feste Anzahl n-ter Potenzen (Waringsches Problem), Math. Ann. 67 (1909) 281–305;
textbook in Vaughan, The Hardy-Littlewood Method; general includes minimal g(k).

Proof: We follow Linnik's elementary route as presented in Tim Jameson's notes: a mean-value
estimate gives positive Schnirelmann density for a bounded power sumset, which is then an additive
basis of finite order by Schnirelmann's inequality.

docstring:
Statement of Theorem 1.1 (Large values estimate):

Suppose `(bₙ)` is a sequence of complex numbers with `|bₙ| ≤ 1`, and `(tᵣ)` for `r ≤ R` is a
sequence of `1`-separated points in `[0, T]` such that

`|∑_N^2N bₙ n^(itᵣ)| ≥ V`

for all `r ≤ R`. Then we have

`R ≤ T^(o(1)) * (N^2 V^(-2) + N^(18/5) V^(-4) + T N^(12/5) V^(-4))`.

Note: The inequality may be false at `T = 1`, so we must impose `T > 1`.
Source: L. Guth and J. Maynard, `New large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials`, Annals of Math, 203 (2) 2026. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2026-203-2-LargeValueEstimates.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_large_value_estimates`.

signature: ∃ o, o =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧ ∀ (b : ℕ → ℂ), (∀ (n : ℕ), ‖b n‖ ≤ 1) → ∀ (N : ℕ) (V T : ℝ) (R : ℕ) (t : Fin R → ℝ), N > 0 → V > 0 → T > 1 → (∀ (i j : Fin R), i ≠ j → |t i - t j| ≥ 1) → (∀ (i : Fin R), t i ∈ Set.Icc 0 T) → (∀ (r : Fin R), ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc N (2 * N), b n * ↑n ^ (Complex.I * ↑(t r))‖ ≥ V) → ↑R ≤ T ^ o T * MathlibExt.NumberTheory.LargeValueEstimatesWanted.LargeValueEstimates.bound N V T

docstring:

Source: C. Hermite, Sur la fonction exponentielle, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 77 (1873) for e; F. von
Lindemann, Über die Zahl π, Math. Ann. 20 (1882) 213–225 extension to π; textbook in Baker,
Transcendental Number Theory

docstring:
If `α : ι → ℂ` is injective over a `Fintype ι` with `∀ i, IsAlgebraic ℚ (α i)`, then for any
algebraic coefficients `β : ι → ℂ` not all zero, `∑ i, β i * Complex.exp (α i) ≠ 0`. Source: F.
von Lindemann 1882 and K. Weierstrass, Zu Lindemann's Abhandlung Über die Ludolph'sche Zahl, 1885;
textbook in Baker, Transcendental Number Theory

Proves `Wanted` entry `lindemann_weierstrass`.

A subspace `V ≤ ℝᵈ` is called rational, if `V ∩ ℤᵈ` is a full-rank lattice in `V`.

of rational subspaces below.

docstring:
For a subspace `x ≤ ℝᵈ` and `k : ℕ`, define the diophantine exponent of `x`
for approximation by `k`-dimensional rational subspaces by
`βₖ(x) = inf { β > 0 | ∃ c > 0 : ∀ v ∈ Xₖ(ℚ), d(v, x) ≥ c * H(v)^(−β) }.`

Then, if `x = x¹` is a line and `y = yᵏ` a k-dimensional subspace, we set

`d(xˡ, yᵏ) = max { d(y¹, xˡ) : y¹ ≤ yᵏ }`, if `k ≤ l`, and

docstring:
Statement of Theorem 1 (Dirichlet's principle in Grassmann varieties):

For all `l`-dimensional subspaces `x ≤ ℝᵈ` and all `k ∈ {1,...,l}`, we have
`βₖ(x) ≥ d / (k * (d - l))`, and this lower bound is optimal.
Source: N. de Saxcé, `Rational approximations to linear subspaces`, Annals of Math, 203 (3) 2026. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2026-203-3-LinearSubspaces.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_linear_subspaces`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.LinearSubspacesWanted.LinearSubspaces.theorem_1
signature: ∀ {d : ℕ}, 2 ≤ d → ∀ (l : ℕ), 0 < l → l < d → ∀ (k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → k ≤ l → (∀ (x : Submodule ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))), Module.finrank ℝ ↥x = l → MathlibExt.NumberTheory.LinearSubspacesWanted.LinearSubspaces.diophantineExponent k x ≥ ↑d / (↑k * (↑d - ↑l))) ∧ ∃ x, Module.finrank ℝ ↥x = l ∧ MathlibExt.NumberTheory.LinearSubspacesWanted.LinearSubspaces.diophantineExponent k x = ↑d / (↑k * (↑d - ↑l))
statement:
public theorem_wanted theorem_1
    (hd : 2 ≤ d) (l : ℕ) (hl0 : 0 < l) (hld : l < d) (k : ℕ) (hk1 : 1 ≤ k) (hkl : k ≤ l) :
    (∀ x : Submodule ℝ ℝᵈ, finrank ℝ x = l → diophantineExponent k x ≥ d / (k * (d - l))) ∧
    (∃ x : Submodule ℝ ℝᵈ, finrank ℝ x = l ∧ diophantineExponent k x = d / (k * (d - l)))

Source: A. Poëls, `On approximation to a real number by algebraic numbers of bounded degree`, Annals of Math, 201 (1) 2025. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2025-201-1-OnApproximationOfReals.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_on_approximation_of_reals`.

docstring:
For every exponent `β ∈ (0, 1)` there is a constant `ξ₁ > 0`, depending only
on `β`, such that the inclusive residue-class prime count satisfies
`π(X; k, ell) < ξ₁ X / (φ(k) log(X/k))` whenever `2 ≤ X`, `1 ≤ k`, and
`k ≤ X ^ β`.

Source: Jean-Marie De Koninck and Imre Kátai, "Some Remarks on a Paper of
L. Toth," Journal of Integer Sequences 13 (2010),
`https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL13/DeKoninck/dekoninck7.tex`,
Lemma `lem:pi`, lines 424–429. Both the live and bundled source have SHA-256
`a81e23b6e88f02c8bcad5f1b6e4d71d822e82e1725a9e8ba2708bd2bc0e4a57d`, and the
exact lines 424–429 joined by LF without a terminal LF have SHA-256
`bd645263ac19a24bf1b4ff3ac5baf13ec5ee8f59ae16945edd528cf4ac153828`. The source
cites E. C. Titchmarsh, "A divisor problem," Rend. Palermo 54 (1930), 414–429
and 57 (1933), 478–479. The bound `2 ≤ X` makes the source's implicit analytic
lower range explicit, and the source prints no coprimality hypothesis.

Proves `Wanted` entry `brun_titchmarsh_uniform`.

Proof: Selberg's `Λ²` upper-bound sieve on an arithmetic progression, with
optimized weights and a harmonic lower bound for the diagonal sum.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.PrimeCounting.BrunTitchmarshUniformWanted.brun_titchmarsh_uniform
signature: ∀ (β : ℝ), 0 < β → β < 1 → ∃ ξ₁, 0 < ξ₁ ∧ ∀ (X k ell : ℕ), 2 ≤ X → 1 ≤ k → ↑k ≤ (↑X).rpow β → ↑(X.primeCountingMod k ell) < ξ₁ * ↑X / (↑k.totient * Real.log (↑X / ↑k))
statement:
public theorem brun_titchmarsh_uniform (β : ℝ) (hβ0 : 0 < β)
    (hβ1 : β < 1) :
    ∃ ξ₁ : ℝ, 0 < ξ₁ ∧ ∀ X k ell : ℕ, 2 ≤ X → 1 ≤ k →
      (k : ℝ) ≤ Real.rpow (X : ℝ) β →
      (Nat.primeCountingMod X k ell : ℝ) <
        ξ₁ * (X : ℝ) / ((Nat.totient k : ℝ) * Real.log ((X : ℝ) / (k : ℝ)))

docstring:
For coprime `a` and `q`, with `1 ≤ q < X`, the inclusive residue-class
prime count satisfies
`π(X; q, a) ≤ 2X / (φ(q) log(X/q))`.

Source: H. Iwaniec and E. Kowalski, *Analytic Number Theory*, AMS Colloquium
Publications 53, 2004, Theorem 6.6; quoted as equation (1) in Y. Wang and
X. Zhang, arXiv:2608.19262v1.

Proof: An elementary Eratosthenes sieve handles `X ≤ 20000q`. Above that
range, the weighted arithmetic large sieve is combined with explicit lower
bounds for the squarefree-totient sum and the choice
`z = ⌊√(2N/3)⌋`, where `N = ⌊X/q⌋ + 1`.

Proves `Wanted` entry `brun_titchmarsh`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.PrimeCounting.BrunTitchmarshWanted.brun_titchmarsh
signature: ∀ (X q a : ℕ), a.Coprime q → 1 ≤ q → q < X → ↑(X.primeCountingMod q a) ≤ 2 * ↑X / (↑q.totient * Real.log (↑X / ↑q))
statement:
public theorem brun_titchmarsh (X q a : ℕ) (haq : Nat.Coprime a q)
    (hq : 1 ≤ q) (hqX : q < X) :
    (Nat.primeCountingMod X q a : ℝ) ≤
      2 * (X : ℝ) / ((Nat.totient q : ℝ) * Real.log ((X : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)))

docstring:
The sum of reciprocals over twin-prime pairs, indexed by the smaller prime
`p` of each pair `(p, p + 2)`, converges over `ℝ`; a shared prime such as `5`
is intentionally counted once in each of `(3, 5)` and `(5, 7)`, and a finite
collection of twin-prime pairs is already covered because a finitely supported
function is summable.

Source: Alexei Kourbatov and Marek Wolf, "On the First Occurrences of Gaps
Between Primes in a Residue Class," Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020),
`https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Wolf/wolf2.tex`, lines 684–705;
live and bundled source SHA-256
`f19705a8cece7b19aea01b0669774f24e42d49f9a262ff1c6ea0b4e6644e6d64` and exact
cited span SHA-256
`dd71eb411be0ec74f9b3599bfdc17309c68109e03167163b629ab5949415e8da`.
Corroboration: Prapanpong Pongsriiam and Kota Saito, "Palindromes and
Antipalindromes in Short Intervals," Journal of Integer Sequences 26 (2023),
`https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL26/Saito/saito1.tex`, lines 205–210;
live and bundled source SHA-256
`0c721e5603affcd1b7a1dfeb67dcc79ef6a28132308cb081a1ee39c12515fabc` and exact
cited span SHA-256
`b28ebf74254fb808313c73f910a0f7978dbae8e6987027c94e6924a6d81cc47f`.
The sources attribute the theorem to V. Brun's 1919 paper on convergence or
finiteness of the reciprocal twin-prime series.

Proves `Wanted` entry `brun_twin_prime_reciprocal_series_summable`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.PrimeCounting.BrunTwinPrimeReciprocalsWanted.brun_twin_prime_reciprocal_series_summable

      if p.Prime ∧ (p + 2).Prime then

      else 0)

docstring:
Gandhi's formula for the `n`th prime.

For one-indexed `n`, with `pᵢ` the `i`th prime and
`Pₙ₋₁ = p₁ * p₂ * ⋯ * pₙ₋₁` (the empty product `1` when `n = 1`),
`pₙ = ⌊1 - log₂(-1 / 2 + ∑_{d ∣ Pₙ₋₁} μ(d) / (2 ^ d - 1))⌋`.

Source: J. M. Gandhi, "Formulae for the nth prime," Proc. Washington State
University Conference on Number Theory (1971), 96--107. The displayed formula
and indexing follow the secondary source Eric S. Rowland, "A Natural
Prime-Generating Recurrence," Journal of Integer Sequences 11 (2008),
Article 08.2.8, lines 90--103 of the official TeX,
https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL11/Rowland/rowland21.tex,
where `f(n)` is the `n`th prime `pₙ` and `Pₙ = p₁ p₂ ⋯ pₙ`.
Proves `Wanted` entry `gandhi_nthPrimeFormula`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.PrimeCounting.GandhiNthPrimeFormulaWanted.gandhi_nthPrimeFormula
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ↑(Nat.nth Nat.Prime (n - 1)) = ⌊1 - Real.logb 2 (-1 / 2 + ∑ d ∈ (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n - 1), Nat.nth Nat.Prime (i - 1)).divisors, ↑(ArithmeticFunction.moebius d) / (2 ^ d - 1))⌋
statement:
theorem gandhi_nthPrimeFormula (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    ((Nat.nth Nat.Prime (n - 1) : ℕ) : ℤ) =
      ⌊1 - Real.logb 2 (-1 / 2 +
        ∑ d ∈ Nat.divisors
          (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n - 1), Nat.nth Nat.Prime (i - 1)),
          (((ArithmeticFunction.moebius d : ℤ) : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ d - 1)))⌋

docstring:
For each positive real exponent `N`, the Siegel–Walfisz estimate holds
uniformly for positive moduli `q ≤ (log x)^N` and reduced residue classes.

The constants may depend on `N`, but not on `x`, `q`, or `a`.

Source: P. Holdridge, *Random Diophantine Equations in the Primes*,
arXiv:2305.06306v2, Theorem 4.2, citing H. Davenport, *Multiplicative Number
Theory*, 2nd ed., revised by H. L. Montgomery, Springer, 1980, Chapter 22.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.PrimeCounting.SiegelWalfiszWanted.siegel_walfisz
signature: ∀ (N : ℝ), 0 < N → ∃ c C X₀, 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧ 1 < X₀ ∧ ∀ (x : ℝ), X₀ ≤ x → ∀ (q : ℕ), 0 < q → ∀ (a : ZMod q), IsUnit a → ↑q ≤ Real.log x ^ N → |Chebyshev.psiResidueClass a x - x / ↑q.totient| ≤ C * x * Real.exp (-c * √(Real.log x))
statement:
public theorem_wanted siegel_walfisz (N : ℝ) (hN : 0 < N) :
    ∃ (c C X₀ : ℝ), 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧ 1 < X₀ ∧
      ∀ x : ℝ, X₀ ≤ x →
        ∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q →
          ∀ a : ZMod q, IsUnit a →
            (q : ℝ) ≤ (Real.log x) ^ N →
              |Chebyshev.psiResidueClass a x - x / (Nat.totient q : ℝ)| ≤
                C * x * Real.exp (-c * Real.sqrt (Real.log x))

docstring:
Fix `B > 0`. Uniformly over positive moduli `q ≤ (log x) ^ B` and reduced
residue classes `b`, the number of primes `p ≤ x` congruent to `b` modulo `q`
differs from `li(x) / φ(q)` by at most `C * x * exp (-c * sqrt (log x))` for
sufficiently large `x`. The constants may depend on `B`, but not on `x`, `q`, or `b`.

The count uses `Nat.floor x` so its endpoint is inclusive. The logarithmic integral
is written explicitly as in the source, rather than using the principal-value
normalization `Real.logarithmicIntegral`.

Source: A. Guo, *Exceptional sets for compositions involving Euler's function, the
divisor-sum function and Dedekind's function*, arXiv:2608.19972v1, Lemma
`siegel`, `main.tex` lines 289–295. The official arXiv source file has SHA-256
`b4996cf07cc79703901e7313202c5a795b6e5313745490e0224d3589ff2a2d07`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.PrimeCounting.UniformPrimeCountingWanted.uniform_prime_counting_arithmetic_progression
signature: ∀ (B : ℝ), 0 < B → ∃ c C X₀, 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧ 2 ≤ X₀ ∧ ∀ (x : ℝ), X₀ ≤ x → ∀ (q b : ℕ), 0 < q → b.Coprime q → ↑q ≤ Real.log x ^ B → |↑{p ∈ Finset.range (⌊x⌋₊ + 1) | Nat.Prime p ∧ p ≡ b [MOD q]}.card - (∫ (u : ℝ) in 2..x, (Real.log u)⁻¹) / ↑q.totient| ≤ C * x * Real.exp (-c * √(Real.log x))
statement:
public theorem_wanted uniform_prime_counting_arithmetic_progression (B : ℝ) (hB : 0 < B) :
    ∃ (c C X₀ : ℝ), 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧ 2 ≤ X₀ ∧
      ∀ x : ℝ, X₀ ≤ x →
        ∀ q b : ℕ, 0 < q → Nat.Coprime b q →
          (q : ℝ) ≤ (Real.log x) ^ B →
            |(((Finset.range (Nat.floor x + 1)).filter fun p =>
                Nat.Prime p ∧ Nat.ModEq q p b).card : ℝ) -
              (∫ u in (2 : ℝ)..x, (Real.log u)⁻¹) / (Nat.totient q : ℝ)| ≤
                C * x * Real.exp (-c * Real.sqrt (Real.log x))

docstring:
The arithmetic large sieve for primes in one progression.

Source: Montgomery–Vaughan, *The large sieve* (1973), Corollary 1 and Lemma 3,
equations (2.7) and (3.2), lines 322–461. The Farey fractions are weighted by
the denominator-dependent spacing from `weightedLargeSieve`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.PrimeCounting.arithmeticLargeSieve_progression
signature: ∀ (N z q a : ℕ), 0 < z → 0 < q → ∀ S ⊆ Finset.range N, (∀ n ∈ S, Nat.Prime (q * n + a)) → (∀ n ∈ S, z < q * n + a) → (∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 z, (↑N + 3 * ↑r * ↑z / 2)⁻¹ * (↑(ArithmeticFunction.moebius r) ^ 2 / ↑r.totient)) * ↑S.card ^ 2 ≤ ↑q / ↑q.totient * ↑S.card
statement:
public theorem arithmeticLargeSieve_progression (N z q a : ℕ) (hz : 0 < z)

docstring:
The weighted Hilbert inequality in cosecant form.

This is Montgomery–Vaughan (1974), Theorem 1, in its weighted circle form. The
proof follows Yangjit, arXiv:2203.14950, lines 166–205, 209–462, and 596–640:
Selberg's eigenvector identity, the Hermitian spectral theorem, and convex circle
packing estimates for the one-pole and two-pole cosecant-square sums.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.PrimeCounting.weightedHilbertCosecant
signature: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] (x δ : ι → ℝ) (z : ι → ℂ), (∀ (r : ι), 0 < δ r) → (∀ (r s : ι), r ≠ s → δ r ≤ ‖↑(x r - x s)‖) → ‖∑ r, ∑ s ∈ Finset.univ.erase r, z r * (starRingEnd ℂ) (z s) / ↑(Real.sin (Real.pi * (x r - x s)))‖ ≤ 3 / 2 * ∑ r, ‖z r‖ ^ 2 / δ r
statement:
public theorem weightedHilbertCosecant {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (x δ : ι → ℝ) (z : ι → ℂ) (hδ : ∀ r, 0 < δ r)
    (hsep : ∀ r s, r ≠ s →
      δ r ≤ ‖((x r - x s : ℝ) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ))‖) :
    ‖∑ r, ∑ s ∈ Finset.univ.erase r,
        z r * conj (z s) / Real.sin (Real.pi * (x r - x s))‖ ≤
      3 / 2 * ∑ r, ‖z r‖ ^ 2 / δ r

docstring:
The weighted large sieve.

Source: Montgomery–Vaughan, *The large sieve* (1973), Theorem 1, equations
(1.5)–(1.6) and (2.4), lines 227–321. The proof uses duality, the exact
geometric sum, and `weightedHilbertCosecant`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.PrimeCounting.weightedLargeSieve
signature: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] (N : ℕ) (x δ : ι → ℝ) (a : ℕ → ℂ), (∀ (r : ι), 0 < δ r) → (∀ (r s : ι), r ≠ s → δ r ≤ ‖↑(x r - x s)‖) → ∑ r, (↑N + 3 / (2 * δ r))⁻¹ * ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, a n * Complex.exp (↑(2 * Real.pi * (↑n * x r)) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, ‖a n‖ ^ 2
statement:
public theorem weightedLargeSieve {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (N : ℕ) (x δ : ι → ℝ) (a : ℕ → ℂ) (hδ : ∀ r, 0 < δ r)
    (hsep : ∀ r s, r ≠ s →
      δ r ≤ ‖((x r - x s : ℝ) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ))‖) :
    ∑ r, (N + 3 / (2 * δ r))⁻¹ *
        ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, a n *
          Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n * x r) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2 ≤
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, ‖a n‖ ^ 2

docstring: The coefficient is the finite sum over positive factors whose product is `n`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.PrimeDistribution.convolution_apply
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (α β : ℕ →₀ R) (n : ℕ), (MathlibExt.NumberTheory.PrimeDistribution.convolution α β) n = (Finsupp.filter (fun a ↦ 0 < a) α).sum fun a u ↦ (Finsupp.filter (fun b ↦ 0 < b) β).sum fun b v ↦ if a * b = n then u * v else 0

    convolution α β n =
      (α.filter (fun a ↦ 0 < a)).sum (fun a u ↦
        (β.filter (fun b ↦ 0 < b)).sum (fun b v ↦ if a * b = n then u * v else 0))

docstring:
Signed residue discrepancy, normalized by the totient of a positive modulus over a
characteristic-zero field, so the normalizing cast is nonzero. Only positive indices
contribute. Modulus zero is unrepresentable: `q` ranges over `ℕ+`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.PrimeDistribution.discrepancy
signature: {𝕜 : Type u_1} → [inst : Field 𝕜] → [CharZero 𝕜] → (ℕ →₀ 𝕜) → ℕ+ → ℕ → 𝕜

docstring: A positive singleton contributes its residue value minus the coprime mean.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.PrimeDistribution.discrepancy_single
signature: ∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} [inst : Field 𝕜] [inst_1 : CharZero 𝕜] (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∀ (v : 𝕜) (q : ℕ+) (a : ℕ), MathlibExt.NumberTheory.PrimeDistribution.discrepancy (fun₀ | n => v) q a = (if n % ↑q = a % ↑q then v else 0) - (if n.Coprime ↑q then v else 0) / ↑(↑q).totient
statement:
theorem discrepancy_single {𝕜 : Type*} [Field 𝕜] [CharZero 𝕜] (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
    (v : 𝕜) (q : ℕ+) (a : ℕ) :
    discrepancy (Finsupp.single n v) q a =
      (if n % q = a % q then v else 0) -
        (if Nat.Coprime n q then v else 0) / (Nat.totient (q : ℕ) : 𝕜)

docstring: The extra index zero contributes nothing to discrepancy over any coefficient field.

docstring:
For `q ≥ 2` and `Nat.Coprime a q`, the count of primes `p ≤ n` with `p ≡ a [MOD q]` satisfies
`count * log n / n → 1 / φ(q)` as `n → ∞`, where `φ = Nat.totient`. Source: G. L. Dirichlet 1837
existence, PNT for AP by de la Vallée Poussin and Hadamard 1896-1899 extensions; textbook in
Montgomery-Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I, Multiplicative Number Theory

            Real.log (n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ))

docstring:

(arXiv:2608.21354, 2026) prove that a Rademacher random multiplicative function a.s. has
|Σ_{n≤x} f(n)| ≪ √x (log log x)^{1/4+ε}, so the normalized limsup is a.s. 0 and no constant c>0
works. Source: B. Durkan, A. Pearce-Crump, A sharp almost sure upper bound for partial sums of
random multiplicative functions, arXiv preprint (2026), arXiv:2607.29429,
https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29429; W. Verreault, Almost sure upper bound for sums of random
multiplicative functions and critical chaos, arXiv preprint (2026), arXiv:2608.21354,

docstring: Source: Bruce C. Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks, Part I (Springer, 1985), Chapter 1, Entry 1.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch1.Entry1Magicsquare3.ramanujan_part1_ch1_entry1_magicsquare3
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → ∀ (a b : Fin n → ℕ) (L R : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n), (∀ (i : Fin n), Function.Bijective (L i)) → (∀ (j : Fin n), Function.Bijective fun i ↦ L i j) → (Function.Bijective fun i ↦ L i i) → (Function.Bijective fun i ↦ L i ⟨n - 1 - ↑i, ⋯⟩) → (∀ (i : Fin n), Function.Bijective (R i)) → (∀ (j : Fin n), Function.Bijective fun i ↦ R i j) → (Function.Bijective fun i ↦ R i i) → (Function.Bijective fun i ↦ R i ⟨n - 1 - ↑i, ⋯⟩) → (Function.Bijective fun p ↦ (L p.1 p.2, R p.1 p.2)) → ∃ S, (∀ (i : Fin n), ∑ j, (a (L i j) + b (R i j)) = S) ∧ (∀ (j : Fin n), ∑ i, (a (L i j) + b (R i j)) = S) ∧ ∑ i, (a (L i i) + b (R i i)) = S ∧ ∑ i, (a (L i ⟨n - 1 - ↑i, ⋯⟩) + b (R i ⟨n - 1 - ↑i, ⋯⟩)) = S
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch1_entry1_magicsquare3
    {n : ℕ} (_hn : 0 < n)
    (a b : Fin n → ℕ)
    (L R : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n)
    (hL_row : ∀ i : Fin n, Function.Bijective (L i))
    (hL_col : ∀ j : Fin n, Function.Bijective (fun i : Fin n => L i j))
    (hL_diag : Function.Bijective (fun i : Fin n => L i i))
    (hL_anti : Function.Bijective (fun i : Fin n => L i ⟨n - 1 - i.val, by omega⟩))
    (hR_row : ∀ i : Fin n, Function.Bijective (R i))
    (hR_col : ∀ j : Fin n, Function.Bijective (fun i : Fin n => R i j))
    (hR_diag : Function.Bijective (fun i : Fin n => R i i))
    (hR_anti : Function.Bijective (fun i : Fin n => R i ⟨n - 1 - i.val, by omega⟩))
    (_hPair : Function.Bijective (fun p : Fin n × Fin n => (L p.1 p.2, R p.1 p.2))) :
    ∃ S : ℕ,
      (∀ i : Fin n, (∑ j : Fin n, (a (L i j) + b (R i j))) = S)
      ∧ (∀ j : Fin n, (∑ i : Fin n, (a (L i j) + b (R i j))) = S)
      ∧ ((∑ i : Fin n, (a (L i i) + b (R i i))) = S)
      ∧ ((∑ i : Fin n,
          (a (L i ⟨n - 1 - i.val, by omega⟩) + b (R i ⟨n - 1 - i.val, by omega⟩))) = S)

Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry10_poisson_asymptotic`.

Proof: Taylor expansion on the central Poisson range is combined with the associated-Stirling
central-moment identity from Comtet; Berndt's route and even-moment tails control the remainder.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry10PoissonAsymptotic.ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry10_poisson_asymptotic
signature: ∀ (M : ℕ), 0 < M → ∀ (φ : ℝ → ℂ) (G : ℝ → ℝ) (A : ℝ), 1 ≤ A → ∀ (F : Finset ℕ), (∃ C, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∃ p, ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, ‖φ x‖ ≤ C * x ^ p ∧ ‖G x‖ ≤ C * x ^ p) → (∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, 1 ≤ G x) → (∀ (m : ℕ), 0 < m → ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, (∀ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m, DifferentiableAt ℝ (iteratedDeriv (k - 1) φ) x) ∧ ‖iteratedDeriv m φ x / ↑m.factorial‖ ≤ G x * (A / x) ^ m) → (fun x ↦ (↑(Real.exp (-x)) * ∑' (j : ℕ), if j ∈ F then 0 else ↑(x ^ j / ↑j.factorial) * φ ↑j) - φ x - ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 M, ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc k (2 * k - 2), ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry10PoissonAsymptotic.twoAssocStirlingSecond n (n + 1 - k)) * ↑x ^ (n - k + 1) * (iteratedDeriv n φ x / ↑n.factorial)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x ↦ G x / x ^ M
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry10_poisson_asymptotic
  (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M)
  (φ : ℝ → ℂ) (G : ℝ → ℝ) (A : ℝ) (hA : 1 ≤ A)
  (F : Finset ℕ)
  (h_poly : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∃ p : ℕ, ∀ᶠ x in Filter.atTop, ‖φ x‖ ≤ C * x ^ p ∧ ‖G x‖ ≤ C * x ^ p)
  (hG_ge : ∀ᶠ x in Filter.atTop, (1 : ℝ) ≤ G x)
  (h_deriv : ∀ m : ℕ, 0 < m → ∀ᶠ x in Filter.atTop,
      (∀ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m, DifferentiableAt ℝ (iteratedDeriv (k - 1) φ) x) ∧
          ‖iteratedDeriv m φ x / (Nat.factorial m : ℂ)‖ ≤ G x * (A / x) ^ m) :
    Asymptotics.IsBigO Filter.atTop
    (fun x : ℝ =>
      ((Real.exp (-x) : ℂ)) *
          (∑' j : ℕ, if j ∈ F then (0 : ℂ) else
              (((x ^ j / (Nat.factorial j : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * φ (j : ℝ)))
      - φ x
      - ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 M, ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc k (2 * k - 2),
          (((twoAssocStirlingSecond n (n + 1 - k) : ℤ) : ℂ) * ((x : ℂ) ^ (n - k + 1)) *
              (iteratedDeriv n φ x / (Nat.factorial n : ℂ))))
    (fun x : ℝ => G x / (x : ℝ) ^ M)

`ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry12_summable_succ_n` without the hypothesis that `n + k ≠ 0` whenever
`0 ≤ k` and `r + k < 0`. This is a statement about Lean's totalized `zpow`: at an index where
`n + k = 0` and the exponent `r + 1 + k` is negative, the term is `0 ^ (r + 1 + k) = 0`, whereas
the source's term is undefined there. Summability depends only on the tail, where every exponent
is nonnegative.

docstring:
Source: Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks Part I, Chapter 3, Corollary to Entry 13, formula
    (13.8), printed p. 70 / PDF p. 80.

    `{w | ‖w‖ ≤ ‖exp (w - 1)‖}` has a bounded lobe containing `0` and an unbounded lobe, meeting
    only at `w = 1`. `hw1` selects the bounded lobe (given `hw`, it is equivalent to `w.re ≤ 1`);
    on the unbounded lobe the identity fails in general.

Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry13_corollary_schroder`.

Proof: Following Berndt's formula (13.8), we use Abel's binomial identity, a Cauchy product and a
holomorphic ODE; radial continuity selects the unit-disk branch of `u ↦ u * exp (-u)`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry13CorollarySchroder.ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry13_corollary_schroder
signature: ∀ (z w : ℂ), ‖w‖ ≤ ‖Complex.exp (w - 1)‖ → ‖w‖ ≤ 1 → HasSum (fun k ↦ if k = 0 then 1 else z * (z + ↑k * w) ^ (k - 1) * Complex.exp (-↑k * w) / ↑k.factorial) (Complex.exp z)
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry13_corollary_schroder
    (z w : ℂ) (hw : ‖w‖ ≤ ‖Complex.exp (w - 1)‖) (hw1 : ‖w‖ ≤ 1) :
    HasSum (fun k : ℕ => if k = 0 then 1 else z * (z + (k : ℂ) * w) ^ (k - 1) *
        Complex.exp (-(k : ℂ) * w) / (Nat.factorial k : ℂ)) (Complex.exp z)

docstring: Abel's binomial identity for the scaled Abel polynomials used in Schröder's series.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry13CorollarySchroder.schroder_abel_binomial
signature: ∀ (w x y : ℂ) (n : ℕ), (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (↑(n.choose j) * if j = 0 then 1 else x * (x + ↑j * w) ^ (j - 1)) * if n - j = 0 then 1 else y * (y + ↑(n - j) * w) ^ (n - j - 1)) = if n = 0 then 1 else (x + y) * (x + y + ↑n * w) ^ (n - 1)

signature:
∀ (n a : ℝ),
  |a| ≤ 1 / 4 →
    have term := fun k ↦ if k < 2 then 0 else (∏ j ∈ Finset.Ico (k + 1) (2 * k), (n + ↑j)) * a ^ k / ↑k.factorial;
    Summable term ∧ (2 / (1 + √(1 - 4 * a))).rpow n = 1 + n * a + n * ∑' (k : ℕ), term k
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry14_cor1_catalanpowerseries
    (n a : ℝ) (ha : |a| ≤ 1 / 4) :
    let term := fun k : ℕ => if k < 2 then 0 else
      (∏ j ∈ Finset.Ico (k + 1) (2 * k), (n + (j : ℝ))) * a ^ k / (Nat.factorial k : ℝ)
    Summable term ∧
      Real.rpow (2 / (1 + Real.sqrt (1 - 4 * a))) n = 1 + n * a + n * ∑' k, term k

docstring: Hagen–Rothe convolution for the coefficients in Ramanujan's Lagrange series.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry14LagrangeSeries.lagrangeSeriesCoefficient_add
signature: ∀ (p q r s : ℝ) (m : ℕ), MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry14LagrangeSeries.lagrangeSeriesCoefficient p q (r + s) m = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), ↑(m.choose k) * MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry14LagrangeSeries.lagrangeSeriesCoefficient p q r k * MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry14LagrangeSeries.lagrangeSeriesCoefficient p q s (m - k)
statement:
theorem lagrangeSeriesCoefficient_add (p q r s : ℝ) (m : ℕ) :
    lagrangeSeriesCoefficient p q (r + s) m =
      ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), (Nat.choose m k : ℝ) *
        lagrangeSeriesCoefficient p q r k * lagrangeSeriesCoefficient p q s (m - k)

docstring: The positive-degree Lagrange-series coefficient in product form.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry14LagrangeSeries.lagrangeSeriesCoefficient_of_ne_zero
signature: ∀ (p q n : ℝ) {k : ℕ}, k ≠ 0 → MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry14LagrangeSeries.lagrangeSeriesCoefficient p q n k = n * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (k - 1), (n + ↑k * p - ↑(j + 1) * q)

theorem lagrangeSeriesCoefficient_of_ne_zero (p q n : ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≠ 0) :
    lagrangeSeriesCoefficient p q n k =
      n * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (k - 1),
        (n + (k : ℝ) * p - ((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * q)
