docstring:
Source: Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks Part I, Chapter 3, Entry 14, formulas
    (14.1)--(14.5), printed pp. 70--71 / PDF pp. 80--81; attribution on printed p. 72 / PDF p.
    82.

Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry14_lagrange_series`.

Proof: The argument uses the Hagen--Rothe convolution, a Stirling-type coefficient bound uniform
through the boundary circle, and a continuous exponential lift.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry14LagrangeSeries.ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry14_lagrange_series
signature: ∀ (p q : ℝ), 0 < p → 0 < q → p ≠ q → ∀ (a : ℂ), ‖a‖ ≤ p ^ (-p / q) * |p - q| ^ ((p - q) / q) → ∃ L, a * ↑q * Complex.exp (↑p * L) - Complex.exp (↑q * L) + 1 = 0 ∧ ∀ (n : ℝ), HasSum (fun k ↦ if k = 0 then 1 else (↑n * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (k - 1), (↑n + ↑k * ↑p - (↑j + 1) * ↑q)) * a ^ k / ↑k.factorial) (Complex.exp (↑n * L))
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry14_lagrange_series (p q : ℝ)
    (hp : 0 < p)
        (hq : 0 < q) (hpq : p ≠ q) (a : ℂ) (ha : ‖a‖ ≤ p ^ (-p / q) * |p - q| ^ ((p - q) / q)) :
    ∃ L : ℂ, a * (↑q : ℂ) * Complex.exp (↑p * L) - Complex.exp (↑q * L) + 1 = 0 ∧ ∀ n : ℝ,
        HasSum (fun k : ℕ => if k = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else (↑n : ℂ) *
            Finset.prod (Finset.range (k - 1))
                (fun j => (↑n : ℂ) + (k : ℂ) * (↑p : ℂ) - ((j + 1 : ℂ) * (↑q : ℂ))) * a ^ k /
                    (↑(Nat.factorial k) : ℂ)) (Complex.exp ((↑n : ℂ) * L))

docstring:
Source: Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks Part I, Chapter 3, Entry 15, Example 1, printed pp.
    73-75 / PDF pp. 83-85.

Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry15_example1_exponential_series`.

Proof: Following Berndt and the generalized binomial series of Graham, Knuth, and Patashnik,
the series is realized as `B_n(z) ^ m` with `B_n = 1 + z * B_n ^ n`; root selection at
`z = 2 ^ (-n)`, with the endpoint supplied by Entry 14's Catalan-power series, gives `B_n = 2`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry15Example1ExponentialSeries.ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry15_example1_exponential_series
signature: ∀ (m n : ℝ), 0 < n → n ≤ 2 → HasSum (fun k ↦ if k = 0 then 1 else (m * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (k - 1), (m + ↑k * n - (↑j + 1))) / (2 ^ (↑k * n) * ↑k.factorial)) (2 ^ m)
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry15_example1_exponential_series (m n : ℝ)
    (hn_pos : 0 < n) (hn_le : n ≤ 2) :
    HasSum (fun k : ℕ =>
      if k = 0 then (1 : ℝ)
      else (m * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (k - 1), (m + (k : ℝ) * n - ((j : ℝ) + 1))) /
        ((2 : ℝ) ^ ((k : ℝ) * n) * (Nat.factorial k : ℝ))) ((2 : ℝ) ^ m)

name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry15InverseSeries.ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry15_inverse_series
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry15_inverse_series :
    ∃ (r : ℝ) (b : ℕ → ℝ),
      0 < r ∧ b 0 = 1 ∧ b 1 = -1 ∧ b 2 = (1 : ℝ) / 3 ∧ b 3 = -(1 : ℝ) / 36 ∧
        b 4 = -(1 : ℝ) / 270 ∧
        (∀ x : ℝ, |x| < r → ∃ u : ℝ, HasSum (fun k : ℕ => b k * x ^ k) u) ∧
        ∀ x : ℝ, 0 < x → x < r → ∀ u : ℝ, HasSum (fun k : ℕ => b k * x ^ k) u →
          0 < u ∧ u < 1 ∧ u - Real.log u = 1 + x ^ 2 / 2 ∧
            HasSum (fun j : ℕ => (1 - u) ^ (j + 2) / (↑(j + 2) : ℝ)) (x ^ 2 / 2)

Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry16`. The series is `Entry12.F`, and the
recurrence is `Entry12.ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry12` multiplied by `exp (-n * log x)`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry16.ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry16
signature: ∀ (a x n : ℂ) (r : ℤ), x ≠ 0 → x = a * Complex.log x → ‖a‖ > Real.exp 1 ∨ a = ↑(Real.exp 1) ∧ r ≤ -2 → (∀ (k : ℕ), r + ↑k < 0 → n + ↑k ≠ 0) → n * MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry16.varphi a x r n = MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry16.varphi a x (r + 1) n - Complex.log x * MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry16.varphi a x (r + 1) (n + 1)
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry16 (a x n : ℂ)
    (r : ℤ)
        (hx_ne : x ≠ 0)
            (hx_eq : x = a * Complex.log x)
                (ha : ‖a‖ > Real.exp 1 ∨ (a = (Real.exp 1 : ℂ) ∧ r ≤ -2))
                    (hn : ∀ k : ℕ, r + (k : ℤ) < 0 → n + (k : ℂ) ≠ 0) :
    n * varphi a x r n = varphi a x (r + 1) n - Complex.log x * varphi a x (r + 1) (n + 1)

signature: ∀ (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → ρ * Real.exp (ρ + 1) = 1 → ∀ (n : ℝ), -ρ < n ∧ n < 1 → ∀ (x : ℂ), HasSum (fun k ↦ (x + ↑k * ↑n) ^ k / (↑k.factorial * Complex.exp (↑k * ↑n))) (Complex.exp x / (1 - ↑n))

theorem ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry16_corollary1_jensen_series (ρ : ℝ)

Source: Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks Part I, Chapter 3, construction and formulas
    (16.4)-(16.5), printed pp. 78-79 / PDF pp. 88-89.

    `hu` selects the component of `{u | ‖u * exp (1 - u)‖ < 1}` containing `0` (given `h`,
    equivalent to `u.re < 1`); on the other component the series converges to a different
    value.

Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry16_psi_series`.

Proof: Entry 12 gives absolute and locally uniform convergence, and termwise
differentiation gives the recurrence in Berndt (16.4)-(16.5). The Jensen-series
base case from Berndt (16.6) extends to the star-convex domain by analytic uniqueness.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry16PsiSeries.ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry16_psi_series
signature: ∀ (r : ℕ) (n u : ℂ), ‖u * Complex.exp (1 - u)‖ < 1 → ‖u‖ < 1 → HasSum (fun j ↦ (n + ↑j) ^ (r + j) * Complex.exp (-u * (n + ↑j)) * u ^ j / ↑j.factorial) (∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (r + 1), MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry16PsiSeries.psi r k n / (1 - u) ^ (r + k))
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry16_psi_series (r : ℕ)
    (n u : ℂ) (h : ‖u * Complex.exp (1 - u)‖ < 1) (hu : ‖u‖ < 1) :
    HasSum (fun j : ℕ => (n + (↑j : ℂ)) ^ (r + j) * Complex.exp (-u * (n + (↑j : ℂ))) * u ^ j /
        (↑(Nat.factorial j) : ℂ)) (∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (r + 1), psi r k n / (1 - u) ^ (r + k))

name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry17.ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry17
signature: ∀ (a : ℝ), 1 / Real.exp 1 < a → ∃ R x, 0 < R ∧ AnalyticAt ℝ x 0 ∧ x 0 = a ∧ (∀ (h : ℝ), |h| < R → 0 < x h ∧ x h ^ x h = a ^ a * Real.exp h) ∧ ∀ (r : ℕ), 2 ≤ r → (-a) ^ (r - 1) * iteratedDeriv r x 0 = (1 + Real.log a)⁻¹ * (↑r - 2) * ((-a) ^ (r - 2) * iteratedDeriv (r - 1) x 0) + (1 + Real.log a)⁻¹ * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (r - 1), ↑((r - 1).choose k) * ((-a) ^ (k - 1) * iteratedDeriv k x 0) * ((-a) ^ (r - k - 1) * iteratedDeriv (r - k) x 0)
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry17 :
    ∀ (a : ℝ), 1 / Real.exp 1 < a →
        ∃ (R : ℝ) (x : ℝ → ℝ), 0 < R ∧ AnalyticAt ℝ x (0 : ℝ) ∧ x 0 = a ∧
            (∀ h : ℝ, |h| < R → 0 < x h ∧ x h ^ x h = a ^ a * Real.exp h) ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, 2 ≤ r →
                (-a) ^ (r - 1) * iteratedDeriv r x 0 = (1 + Real.log a)⁻¹ * ((r : ℝ) - 2) *
                    ((-a) ^ (r - 2) * iteratedDeriv (r - 1) x 0) + (1 + Real.log a)⁻¹ *
                        ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (r - 1), (Nat.choose (r - 1) k : ℝ) *
                            ((-a) ^ (k - 1) * iteratedDeriv k x 0) *
                                ((-a) ^ (r - k - 1) * iteratedDeriv (r - k) x 0)

signature: ∀ (R : ℝ), 1 < R → ∀ (f : ℂ → ℂ), AnalyticOn ℂ f (Metric.ball 0 R) → ∀ (z : ℂ), (∀ (n : ℕ), z + ↑n ≠ 0) → (Summable fun p ↦ ((-1) ^ p.1 / ∏ i ∈ Finset.range (p.1 + 1), (z + ↑i)) * (iteratedDeriv (p.1 + p.2) f 0 / ↑p.2.factorial)) → ∃ c, HasSum (fun k ↦ iteratedDeriv k f 0 / ((z + ↑k) * ↑k.factorial)) c ∧ HasSum (fun k ↦ (-1) ^ k * iteratedDeriv k f 1 / ∏ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), (z + ↑i)) c

docstring:
Ramanujan's Entry 9(i) product series `P(a, b, x; z)`: the `j`-th summand is
`(-b)^j * x^(j+1)` divided by `∏ r ∈ Finset.range (j + 1), (z + a + b * (r + 1))`.

This is a totalized extension of the source expression: Lean's division sends `c / 0` to `0`,
and `∑'` of a non-summable family to `0`. Hence at a pole of the source expression -- for
example `a = 0`, `b = 1`, `x = 1`, `z = -1`, where every product contains the vanishing
factor `z + a + b * (0 + 1) = 0` -- every quotient, and so `entry9_P` itself, evaluates to
`0`, whereas the source expression has a singularity there. Off the poles, with
`w = (z + a) / b` in the sector `|arg w| ≤ π - ε` and `‖w‖ > 0`, `entry9_P_closed` identifies
`entry9_P` with the source's closed form.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry9Odd.entry9_P
signature: ℂ → ℂ → ℂ → ℂ → ℂ
statement: noncomputable def entry9_P (a b x : ℂ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ

docstring:
Closed form of `entry9_P` off the poles: with `w = (z + a) / b` in the sector
`|arg w| ≤ π - ε`, `‖w‖ > 0`, and no vanishing factor `w + (r + 1)`, the defining product
series equals `Complex.exp (-x)` times the factorial-weighted series
`∑' m, x^(m+1) / (m! * (z + (a + b * (m + 1))))`. The two exponential series multiplied in
the proof are absolutely summable, so this is the source's value of the Entry 9(i)
expression on this domain.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry9Odd.entry9_P_closed
signature: ∀ (a b x z w : ℂ) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ε < Real.pi → b ≠ 0 → -Real.pi + ε ≤ w.arg → w.arg ≤ Real.pi - ε → 0 < ‖w‖ → (z + a) / b = w → (∀ (r : ℕ), w + (↑r + 1) ≠ 0) → MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry9Odd.entry9_P a b x z = Complex.exp (-x) * ∑' (m : ℕ), x ^ (m + 1) / (↑m.factorial * (z + (a + b * (↑m + 1))))
statement:
theorem entry9_P_closed (a b x z w : ℂ) (ε : ℝ)
    (hεpos : 0 < ε) (hεlt : ε < Real.pi)
    (hb : b ≠ 0)
    (h1 : -Real.pi + ε ≤ Complex.arg w) (h2 : Complex.arg w ≤ Real.pi - ε)
    (hwpos : 0 < ‖w‖) (hz : (z + a) / b = w)
    (hw : ∀ r : ℕ, w + ((r : ℂ) + 1) ≠ 0) :
    entry9_P a b x z = Complex.exp (-x) * ∑' (m : ℕ),
      (x ^ (m + 1) / ((Nat.factorial m : ℂ) * (z + (a + b * ((m : ℂ) + 1)))))

signature: ∀ (a b x : ℂ), b ≠ 0 → ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ε < Real.pi → ∀ (n : ℕ), (fun z ↦ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (-1) ^ k * MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry9IiGeneralizedbellgeneratingDefining.generalizedBellGenerating a b x k / z ^ (k + 1) - MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Entry9Odd.entry9_P a b x z) =O[Filter.comap (fun z ↦ (z + a) / b) (Filter.cocompact ℂ ⊓ Filter.principal {w | -Real.pi + ε ≤ w.arg ∧ w.arg ≤ Real.pi - ε})] fun z ↦ 1 / z ^ (n + 2)
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch3_entry9_odd (a b x : ℂ)
    (hb : b ≠ 0) (ε : ℝ) (hεpos : 0 < ε) (hεlt : ε < Real.pi) (n : ℕ) :
    Asymptotics.IsBigO
      (Filter.comap (fun z : ℂ => (z + a) / b)
        (Filter.cocompact ℂ ⊓ Filter.principal {w : ℂ | -Real.pi + ε ≤ Complex.arg w ∧
            Complex.arg w ≤ Real.pi - ε}))
      (fun z : ℂ =>
          (Finset.sum (Finset.range (n + 1))
              (fun k => ((-1 : ℂ) ^ k * generalizedBellGenerating a b x k) / z ^ (k + 1)) -
            entry9_P a b x z))
      (fun z : ℂ => (1 : ℂ) / z ^ (n + 2))

docstring:
Source: Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks Part I, Chapter 3, Section 8, Example 1, formula
    (8.1), printed p. 50 / PDF p. 60.

    For `lam = ⊥` the expansion is stated on the sector `|arg z| ≤ π / 2 - eps`, as for finite
    `lam`; on the wider sector `|arg z| ≤ π - eps` it fails, e.g. for `a j = j! (-2/3)^j`.

Proves `Wanted` entry `ramanujan_part1_ch3_section8_example1_asymptotic`.

Proof: Use convergence at one real point to obtain absolute convergence two units to the right,
then expand each `1 / ((z + 1)⋯(z + j + 1))` termwise in powers of `1 / z` and bound the tail.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.Ramanujan.Part1Ch3.Section8Example1Asymptotic.ramanujan_part1_ch3_section8_example1_asymptotic
signature: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℂ) (ψ : ℂ → ℂ) (lam : WithBot ℝ) (eps : ℝ), 0 < eps → (lam ≠ ⊥ → eps < Real.pi / 2) → (lam = ⊥ → eps < Real.pi / 2) → (∀ (z : ℂ), (∀ (n : ℕ), z ≠ -↑(n + 1)) → lam < ↑z.re → HasSum (fun j ↦ (-1) ^ j * a j / ∏ k ∈ Finset.range (j + 1), (z + ↑(k + 1))) (ψ z)) → ∀ (N : ℕ), ∃ C R, 0 < R ∧ 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (z : ℂ), (∀ (n : ℕ), z ≠ -↑(n + 1)) → lam < ↑z.re → ((lam = ⊥ → |z.arg| ≤ Real.pi / 2 - eps) ∧ ∀ (r : ℝ), lam = ↑r → |(z - ↑r).arg| ≤ Real.pi / 2 - eps) → R ≤ ‖z‖ → ‖ψ z - ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), ((-1) ^ j * ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (j + 1), a k * ↑((j + 1).stirlingSecond (k + 1))) / z ^ (j + 1)‖ ≤ C / ‖z‖ ^ (N + 2)
statement:
theorem ramanujan_part1_ch3_section8_example1_asymptotic
  (a : ℕ → ℂ)
  (ψ : ℂ → ℂ)
  (lam : WithBot ℝ)
  (eps : ℝ)
  (heps_pos : 0 < eps)
  (heps_lt_pi_div_two : lam ≠ (⊥ : WithBot ℝ) → eps < Real.pi / 2)
  (heps_lt_pi_div_two_bot : lam = (⊥ : WithBot ℝ) → eps < Real.pi / 2)
  (hsum : ∀ z : ℂ, (∀ n : ℕ, z ≠ -((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ)) → lam < (↑z.re : WithBot ℝ) →
      HasSum (fun j : ℕ => (-1 : ℂ) ^ j * a j / ∏ k ∈ Finset.range (j + 1), (z + ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ)))
          (ψ z)) :
    ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ C : ℝ, ∃ R : ℝ, 0 < R ∧ 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ z : ℂ, (∀ n : ℕ, z ≠ -((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ)) →
        lam < (↑z.re : WithBot ℝ) →
            ((lam = (⊥ : WithBot ℝ) → |Complex.arg z| ≤ Real.pi / 2 - eps) ∧
                (∀ r : ℝ, lam = (↑r : WithBot ℝ) → |Complex.arg (z - (r : ℂ))| ≤ Real.pi /
                    2 - eps)) →
                R ≤ ‖z‖ → ‖ψ z - ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1),
                    ((-1 : ℂ) ^ j *
                        (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (j + 1), a k *
                            ((Nat.stirlingSecond (j + 1) (k + 1) : ℕ) : ℂ)) / z ^ (j + 1))‖ ≤ C /
                            ‖z‖ ^ (N + 2)

    (a : ℕ → ℂ) (lam : Option ℝ) (eps : ℝ) (heps_pos : 0 < eps)

`z` off the poles (and right of `lam` when `lam = some l`), it converges on the part of `sector lam
eps z` beyond some radius, for every `eps > 0`; `ramanujan_part1_ch3_section8_example1_summable`
is the source-shaped form.

    (a : ℕ → ℂ) (lam : Option ℝ) (eps : ℝ) (heps_pos : 0 < eps)

docstring:
Roth's finiteness theorem with an abstract finite collection of divisibility places.

The functions `p`, `μ`, and `ν` encode lower bounds on powers dividing the numerator and
denominator. Taking `S` empty gives the usual archimedean approximation set.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.RothAuxiliary.finite_of_divisible_approximations
signature: ∀ (α : ℝ), IsAlgebraic ℚ α → ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 → ∀ {ι : Type u_1} (S : Finset ι) (p : ι → ℕ) (μ ν : ι → ℝ), (∀ l ∈ S, 0 ≤ μ l) → (∀ l ∈ S, 0 ≤ ν l) → ∑ l ∈ S, (μ l + ν l) < 2 + ε → {q | |α - ↑q| < 1 / (↑q.den).rpow (2 + ε - ∑ l ∈ S, (μ l + ν l)) ∧ ∃ a b, ↑(∏ l ∈ S, p l ^ a l) ∣ q.num ∧ ∏ l ∈ S, p l ^ b l ∣ q.den ∧ ∀ l ∈ S, (↑q.den).rpow (μ l) ≤ ↑(p l) ^ a l ∧ (↑q.den).rpow (ν l) ≤ ↑(p l) ^ b l}.Finite
statement:
public theorem finite_of_divisible_approximations
    (α : ℝ) (hα : IsAlgebraic ℚ α)
    (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hεone : ε ≤ 1)
    {ι : Type*} (S : Finset ι) (p : ι → ℕ) (μ ν : ι → ℝ)
    (hμ : ∀ l ∈ S, 0 ≤ μ l) (hν : ∀ l ∈ S, 0 ≤ ν l)
    (hσ : ∑ l ∈ S, (μ l + ν l) < 2 + ε) :
    Set.Finite {q : ℚ |
      |α - (q : ℝ)| <
          1 / Real.rpow (q.den : ℝ) (2 + ε - ∑ l ∈ S, (μ l + ν l)) ∧
        ∃ a b : ι → ℕ,
          ((∏ l ∈ S, p l ^ a l : ℕ) : ℤ) ∣ q.num ∧
          (∏ l ∈ S, p l ^ b l) ∣ q.den ∧
          ∀ l ∈ S,
            Real.rpow (q.den : ℝ) (μ l) ≤ (p l : ℝ) ^ a l ∧
            Real.rpow (q.den : ℝ) (ν l) ≤ (p l : ℝ) ^ b l}

docstring: Source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1004.0665 Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `cyclotomic_integer_house_between_two_and_76_33`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.SmallHouseWanted.NumberTheory.cyclotomic_integer_house_between_two_and_76_33
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] [inst_2 : Algebra ℚ K] (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] [IsCyclotomicExtension {n} ℚ K] {β : K}, IsIntegral ℤ β → β ∈ NumberField.maximalRealSubfield K → 2 < NumberField.house β ∧ NumberField.house β < 76 / 33 → NumberField.house β = (√7 + √3) / 2 ∨ NumberField.house β = √5 ∨ NumberField.house β = 1 + 2 * Real.cos (2 * Real.pi / 7) ∨ NumberField.house β = (1 + √5) / √2 ∨ NumberField.house β = (1 + √13) / 2
statement:
public theorem_wanted cyclotomic_integer_house_between_two_and_76_33
    {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K] [Algebra ℚ K]
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] [IsCyclotomicExtension {n} ℚ K] {β : K}
    (hβ_int : IsIntegral ℤ β)
    (hβ_real : β ∈ NumberField.maximalRealSubfield K) :
    (2 < house β ∧ house β < (76 : ℝ) / 33) →
      house β = (Real.sqrt 7 + Real.sqrt 3) / 2 ∨
      house β = Real.sqrt 5 ∨
      house β = 1 + 2 * Real.cos (2 * Real.pi / 7) ∨
      house β = (1 + Real.sqrt 5) / Real.sqrt 2 ∨
      house β = (1 + Real.sqrt 13) / 2

< 1 / (q.den : ℝ) ^ (2+ε)` via `Real.rpow`. Source: K. F. Roth, Rational approximations to
algebraic numbers, Mathematika 2 (1955) 1–20; predecessors Thue 1909 and Siegel 1921; textbook in
Schmidt, Diophantine Approximation

Proves `Wanted` entry `thue_siegel_roth`.

Proof: The proof constructs Siegel's auxiliary polynomial, bounds its index at rational
approximation points by a Taylor estimate, and contradicts the inductive Roth lemma.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ThueSiegelRothWanted.thue_siegel_roth
signature: ∀ (α : ℝ), IsAlgebraic ℚ α → Irrational α → ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → {q | |α - ↑q| < 1 / (↑q.den).rpow (2 + ε)}.Finite

docstring:
The every-value complex form of Gelfond–Schneider. If `a` and `b` are algebraic, `a ≠ 1`,
`b` is not rational, and `z` is any logarithm of `a`, then `exp (b * z)` is transcendental.
The hypothesis `exp z = a` already implies `a ≠ 0`. Taking
`z = log a + n * (2 * π * I)` recovers every integer-indexed logarithm branch.

Source: A. O. Gelfond, *Sur le septième problème de Hilbert* (1934), and T. Schneider,
*Transzendenzuntersuchungen periodischer Funktionen I. Transzendenz von Potenzen*, J. Reine
Angew. Math. 172 (1935), 65–69, DOI 10.1515/crll.1935.172.65. Explicit arbitrary- and
principal-branch applications occur in arXiv:2311.11127v1, arXiv:2607.23662v1, and
arXiv:2608.17545v1. The Lean formalization in arXiv:2603.24823v1 states only the principal
`Complex.cpow` value; this declaration records the arbitrary-logarithm form.

Proves `Wanted` entry `gelfondSchneider_complex_exp`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.TranscendenceWanted.gelfondSchneider_complex_exp
signature: ∀ {a b z : ℂ}, IsAlgebraic ℚ a → IsAlgebraic ℚ b → a ≠ 1 → b ∉ Set.range ⇑(Algebra.algebraMap ℚ ℂ) → Complex.exp z = a → Transcendental ℚ (Complex.exp (b * z))
statement:
theorem gelfondSchneider_complex_exp :
    ∀ {a b z : ℂ}, IsAlgebraic ℚ a → IsAlgebraic ℚ b → a ≠ 1 →
      b ∉ Set.range (algebraMap ℚ ℂ) → Complex.exp z = a →
        Transcendental ℚ (Complex.exp (b * z))

docstring:
`Real.rpow` specialization of Gelfond–Schneider: if `α β : ℝ` satisfy `0 < α`, `α ≠ 1`,
`IsAlgebraic ℚ α`, `IsAlgebraic ℚ β` and `Irrational β`, then `Real.rpow α β` is transcendental
over `ℚ`. Source: A. O. Gelfond, Sur le septième problème de Hilbert, Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 2
(1934) 1–6 and T. Schneider 1935 independent; textbook in Baker, Transcendental Number Theory

Proves `Wanted` entry `gelfondSchneider_real_rpow`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.TranscendenceWanted.gelfondSchneider_real_rpow
signature: ∀ (α β : ℝ), 0 < α → α ≠ 1 → IsAlgebraic ℚ α → IsAlgebraic ℚ β → Irrational β → Transcendental ℚ (α.rpow β)
statement:
theorem gelfondSchneider_real_rpow :
    ∀ (α β : ℝ), 0 < α → α ≠ 1 → IsAlgebraic ℚ α → IsAlgebraic ℚ β →
      Irrational β → Transcendental ℚ (Real.rpow α β)

docstring:
Statement of Theorem A (Brown's theorem in positive characteristic):

Let `w ∈ ℕ`, where `ℕ := {1,2,...}`. Then every MZV of weight `w` can be written as a `K`-linear
combination of MZV's in the set `𝒯_w`. In particular, `dim 𝒵_w ≤ d(w)`.
Note that `K` in the paper is `RatFunc F`.
Source: T. N. Dac, `On Zagier-Hoffman's conjectures in positive characteristic`, Annals of Math, 194 (1) 2021. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2021-194-1-ZagierHoffmanPositiveChar.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_zagier_hoffman_positive_char`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ZagierHoffmanPositiveCharWanted.ZagierHoffmanPositiveChar.theorem_A
signature: ∀ (F : Type u_1) [inst : Field F] [inst_1 : DecidableEq (RatFunc F)] (w : ℕ+), MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ZagierHoffmanPositiveCharWanted.ZagierHoffmanPositiveChar.𝒵 F ↑w = Submodule.span (RatFunc F) (MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ZagierHoffmanPositiveCharWanted.ZagierHoffmanPositiveChar.𝒯 F ↑w) ∧ Module.rank (RatFunc F) ↥(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ZagierHoffmanPositiveCharWanted.ZagierHoffmanPositiveChar.𝒵 F ↑w) ≤ ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ZagierHoffmanPositiveCharWanted.ZagierHoffmanPositiveChar.d F ↑w)

docstring:
Statement of Theorem B:

Let `w ∈ ℕ`, where `ℕ := {1,2,...}`. MZVs of weight `w` in `𝒯0 w` are all linearly independent over
`K`. In particular, `dim 𝒵 w ≥ |𝒯0 w|`. Note that `K` in the paper is `RatFunc F`.
Source: T. N. Dac, `On Zagier-Hoffman's conjectures in positive characteristic`, Annals of Math, 194 (1) 2021. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2021-194-1-ZagierHoffmanPositiveChar.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_zagier_hoffman_positive_char`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ZagierHoffmanPositiveCharWanted.ZagierHoffmanPositiveChar.theorem_B
signature: ∀ (F : Type u_1) [inst : Field F] [inst_1 : DecidableEq (RatFunc F)] (w : ℕ+), LinearIndependent (RatFunc F) Subtype.val ∧ Module.rank (RatFunc F) ↥(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ZagierHoffmanPositiveCharWanted.ZagierHoffmanPositiveChar.𝒵 F ↑w) ≥ ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ZagierHoffmanPositiveCharWanted.ZagierHoffmanPositiveChar.𝒯0 F ↑w).ncard

docstring:
Statement of Theorem D:

Let `w ∈ ℕ+` with `w ≤ 2q − 2`. Then `𝒯 w` is a `K`-basis for `𝒵 w`. In particular,
`dim_K (𝒵 w) = d(w)`. Note that `K` in the paper is `RatFunc F`.

Note: Theorem A establishes that `𝒯 w` spans `𝒵 w`. So to prove `𝒯 w` is a `K`-basis for `𝒵 w`, we
only need to show that `𝒯 w` are linearly independent in `𝒵 w`.
Source: T. N. Dac, `On Zagier-Hoffman's conjectures in positive characteristic`, Annals of Math, 194 (1) 2021. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2021-194-1-ZagierHoffmanPositiveChar.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_zagier_hoffman_positive_char`.
name: MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ZagierHoffmanPositiveCharWanted.ZagierHoffmanPositiveChar.theorem_D
signature: ∀ (F : Type u_1) [inst : Field F] [inst_1 : DecidableEq (RatFunc F)] (w : ℕ+), ↑w ≤ 2 * Nat.card F - 2 → LinearIndependent (RatFunc F) Subtype.val ∧ Module.rank (RatFunc F) ↥(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ZagierHoffmanPositiveCharWanted.ZagierHoffmanPositiveChar.𝒵 F ↑w) = ↑(MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ZagierHoffmanPositiveCharWanted.ZagierHoffmanPositiveChar.d F ↑w)

Every Boolean algebra `B` embeds via an injective `BoundedLatticeHom` into a powerset `Set X` for

algebras preserves `ᶜ` via `map_compl'`.

Proves `Wanted` entry `berry_esseen`.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.BerryEsseenWanted.berry_esseen
signature: ∃ C, 0 < C ∧ ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ), (∀ (n : ℕ), Measurable (X n)) → ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X P → (∀ (i : ℕ), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) P P) → MeasureTheory.Integrable (X 0) P → MeasureTheory.MemLp (X 0) 3 P → ∫ (x : Ω), X 0 x ∂P = 0 → 0 < ProbabilityTheory.variance (X 0) P → ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∀ (x : ℝ), |(MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun ω ↦ (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, X i ω) / √(↑n * ProbabilityTheory.variance (X 0) P)) P).real (Set.Iic x) - (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1).real (Set.Iic x)| ≤ (C * ∫ (x : Ω), (fun ω ↦ |X 0 ω| ^ 3) x ∂P) / (√(ProbabilityTheory.variance (X 0) P) ^ 3 * √↑n)
statement:
theorem berry_esseen
    : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      ∀ {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
        (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ),
        (∀ n, Measurable (X n)) →
        iIndepFun X P →
        (∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) P P) →
        Integrable (X 0) P →
        MemLp (X 0) 3 P →
        P[X 0] = 0 →
        0 < Var[X 0; P] →
        ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n →
          ∀ x : ℝ,
            |((P.map (fun ω => (∑ i ∈ range n, X i ω) / Real.sqrt (n * Var[X 0; P]))).real (Iic x)
              - (gaussianReal 0 1).real (Iic x))|
            ≤ C * (P[fun ω => |X 0 ω| ^ 3]) / (Real.sqrt (Var[X 0; P]) ^ 3 * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ))

docstring:
I.i.d. Berry–Esseen bound with explicit constant `42`.

Reusable public API for `berry_esseen`: the constant is stated explicitly, and
the redundant `Integrable (X 0) P` premise is omitted since it follows from
`hXmem` via `MemLp.integrable` on a probability space.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.BerryEsseenWanted.berry_esseen_explicit
signature: ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ), (∀ (n : ℕ), Measurable (X n)) → ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X P → (∀ (i : ℕ), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) P P) → MeasureTheory.MemLp (X 0) 3 P → ∫ (x : Ω), X 0 x ∂P = 0 → 0 < ProbabilityTheory.variance (X 0) P → ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∀ (x : ℝ), |(MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun ω ↦ (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, X i ω) / √(↑n * ProbabilityTheory.variance (X 0) P)) P).real (Set.Iic x) - (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1).real (Set.Iic x)| ≤ (42 * ∫ (x : Ω), (fun ω ↦ |X 0 ω| ^ 3) x ∂P) / (√(ProbabilityTheory.variance (X 0) P) ^ 3 * √↑n)
statement:
theorem berry_esseen_explicit
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    (hXmeas : ∀ n, Measurable (X n))
    (hXindep : iIndepFun X P)
    (hXid : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) P P)
    (hXmem : MemLp (X 0) 3 P)
    (hXmean : P[X 0] = 0)
    (hXvar : 0 < Var[X 0; P])
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (x : ℝ) :
    |((P.map (fun ω => (∑ i ∈ range n, X i ω) / Real.sqrt (n * Var[X 0; P]))).real (Iic x)
      - (gaussianReal 0 1).real (Iic x))|
      ≤ 42 * (P[fun ω => |X 0 ω| ^ 3])
        / (Real.sqrt (Var[X 0; P]) ^ 3 * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ))

docstring:
Finite-sum Berry–Esseen bound with explicit constant `42`, stated with
`gaussianReal` so it is usable from the public API.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.BerryEsseenWanted.berry_esseen_finsetSum_gaussian
signature: ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] {ξ : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}, (∀ (j : ℕ), Measurable (ξ j)) → ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun ξ P → ∀ {s : Finset ℕ}, (∀ j ∈ s, MeasureTheory.MemLp (ξ j) 3 P) → (∀ j ∈ s, ∫ (x : Ω), ξ j x ∂P = 0) → ∑ j ∈ s, ∫ (x : Ω), (fun ω ↦ ξ j ω ^ 2) x ∂P = 1 → ∀ {γ : ℝ}, 0 ≤ γ → ∑ j ∈ s, ∫ (x : Ω), (fun ω ↦ |ξ j ω| ^ 3) x ∂P ≤ γ → ∀ (z : ℝ), |P.real {ω | ∑ j ∈ s, ξ j ω ≤ z} - (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1).real (Set.Iic z)| ≤ 42 * γ
statement:
theorem berry_esseen_finsetSum_gaussian {Ω : Type*}
    [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    {ξ : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} (hmeas : ∀ j, Measurable (ξ j))
    (hindep : iIndepFun ξ P) {s : Finset ℕ}
    (hmem : ∀ j ∈ s, MemLp (ξ j) 3 P)
    (hmean : ∀ j ∈ s, P[ξ j] = 0)
    (hvar : ∑ j ∈ s, P[fun ω => (ξ j ω) ^ 2] = 1)
    {γ : ℝ} (hγ : 0 ≤ γ)
    (hγ3 : ∑ j ∈ s, P[fun ω => |ξ j ω| ^ 3] ≤ γ)
    (z : ℝ) :
    |P.real {ω | ∑ j ∈ s, ξ j ω ≤ z} - (gaussianReal 0 1).real (Iic z)|
      ≤ 42 * γ

docstring:
Symmetric Lovász Local Lemma: with bounded degree and small probabilities, there is positive
probability that no bad event occurs.
Source for the `Real.exp 1 * p * (d + 1) ≤ 1` criterion: N. Alon and J. H. Spencer,
The Probabilistic Method, third edition, Wiley, 2008, Corollary 5.1.2; the original local
lemma of P. Erdős and L. Lovász (1975) gives the earlier weaker `4 * p * d ≤ 1` form.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.Combinatorics.LovaszLocalLemma.lovasz_local_lemma_symmetric_finite
signature: ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {I : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype Ω] [inst_1 : Fintype I] [inst_2 : DecidableEq I] (pmf : Ω → ℝ), (∀ (ω : Ω), 0 ≤ pmf ω) → ∑ ω, pmf ω = 1 → ∀ (A : I → Set Ω) (G : SimpleGraph I) [inst_3 : DecidableRel G.Adj] (p : ℝ) (d : ℕ), 0 ≤ p → G.maxDegree ≤ d → (∀ (i : I), (∑ ω, if ω ∈ A i then pmf ω else 0) ≤ p) → (∀ (i : I) (S : Finset I), (∀ j ∈ S, j ∉ Insert.insert i (G.neighborSet i)) → (∑ ω, if ω ∈ A i ∧ ∀ j ∈ S, ω ∈ A j then pmf ω else 0) = (∑ ω, if ω ∈ A i then pmf ω else 0) * ∑ ω, if ∀ j ∈ S, ω ∈ A j then pmf ω else 0) → Real.exp 1 * p * (↑d + 1) ≤ 1 → 0 < ∑ ω, if ∀ (i : I), ω ∉ A i then pmf ω else 0
statement:
theorem lovasz_local_lemma_symmetric_finite
    [Fintype Ω] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (pmf : Ω → ℝ)
    (hpmf_nonneg : ∀ ω, 0 ≤ pmf ω)
    (hpmf_sum : ∑ ω : Ω, pmf ω = 1)
    (A : I → Set Ω)
    (G : SimpleGraph I) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (p : ℝ) (d : ℕ)
    (hp_nonneg : 0 ≤ p)
    (hmaxDeg : G.maxDegree ≤ d)
    (hp_le : ∀ i : I,
      ∑ ω : Ω, (if ω ∈ A i then pmf ω else 0) ≤ p)
    (hDep : ∀ (i : I) (S : Finset I),
      (∀ j ∈ S, j ∉ insert i (G.neighborSet i)) →
      ∑ ω : Ω,
        (if ω ∈ A i ∧ ∀ j ∈ S, ω ∈ A j then pmf ω else 0) =
      (∑ ω : Ω, (if ω ∈ A i then pmf ω else 0)) *
      (∑ ω : Ω, (if ∀ j ∈ S, ω ∈ A j then pmf ω else 0)))
    (hExp : Real.exp 1 * p * ((d : ℝ) + 1) ≤ 1) :
    0 < ∑ ω : Ω, (if ∀ i : I, ω ∉ A i then pmf ω else 0)

docstring:
If `μ : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → Bool)` is invariant under every finitely supported permutation of
`ℕ`, then there exists a mixing measure `ν : ProbabilityMeasure (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)` such that for
all disjoint `A B : Finset ℕ` the cylinder probability equals `ENNReal.ofReal (∫ p ^ |A| * (1-p) ^
|B| ∂ν)`. Source: B. de Finetti, Funzione caratteristica di un fenomeno aleatorio, Atti Accad.
Naz. Lincei 4 (1931) and La prévision: ses lois logiques (1937); textbook in Kallenberg,
Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles; also Durrett, Probability Theory and Examples

name: MathlibExt.Probability.DeFinettiWanted.deFinetti_binary
signature: ∀ (μ : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → Bool)), (∀ (σ : Equiv.Perm ℕ), {n | σ n ≠ n}.Finite → MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun ω ↦ ω ∘ ⇑σ) ↑μ = ↑μ) → ∃ ν, ∀ (A B : Finset ℕ), Disjoint A B → ↑μ {ω | (∀ i ∈ A, ω i = Bool.true) ∧ ∀ i ∈ B, ω i = Bool.false} = ENNReal.ofReal (∫ (p : ↑(Set.Icc 0 1)), ↑p ^ A.card * (1 - ↑p) ^ B.card ∂↑ν)
statement:
theorem deFinetti_binary
    (μ : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → Bool))
    (hμ : ∀ (σ : Equiv.Perm ℕ), Set.Finite {n : ℕ | σ n ≠ n} →
      Measure.map (fun ω : ℕ → Bool => ω ∘ ⇑σ) (μ : Measure (ℕ → Bool)) =
        (μ : Measure (ℕ → Bool))) :
    ∃ (ν : ProbabilityMeasure (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)),
      ∀ (A B : Finset ℕ), Disjoint A B →
        (μ : Measure (ℕ → Bool))
          {ω : ℕ → Bool | (∀ i ∈ A, ω i = true) ∧ (∀ i ∈ B, ω i = false)} =
          ENNReal.ofReal
            (MeasureTheory.integral (ν : Measure (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1))
              (fun p : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 =>
                (p.val : ℝ) ^ A.card * (1 - (p.val : ℝ)) ^ B.card))

docstring: Explicit partial-sum interpolation formula for `donskerProcess`.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.DonskerWanted.donskerProcess_apply_eq
signature: ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} (n : ℕ) (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (ω : Ω) (t : ↑(Set.Icc 0 1)), n ≠ 0 → (MathlibExt.Probability.DonskerWanted.donskerProcess n X ω) t = (∑ i ∈ Finset.range ⌊↑n * ↑t⌋₊, X i ω + if ⌊↑n * ↑t⌋₊ < n then X ⌊↑n * ↑t⌋₊ ω * (↑n * ↑t - ↑⌊↑n * ↑t⌋₊) else 0) / √↑n
statement:
public theorem donskerProcess_apply_eq {Ω : Type*} (n : ℕ) (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (ω : Ω)
    (t : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    donskerProcess n X ω t =
      ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range (Nat.floor ((n : ℝ) * t.1)), X i ω) +
        if Nat.floor ((n : ℝ) * t.1) < n then
          X (Nat.floor ((n : ℝ) * t.1)) ω *
            ((n : ℝ) * t.1 - Nat.floor ((n : ℝ) * t.1))
        else 0) / Real.sqrt (n : ℝ)

docstring:
If `X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ` is i.i.d. with mean `0`, variance `1` and `MemLp` `2`, then for any Brownian
motion `B` with `IsBrownianReal B P'` there exists `Y : Ω' → C([0, 1], ℝ)` restricting to `B` a.e.
on `[0, 1]` such that `donskerProcess n X` converges in distribution to `Y`. Source: M. D.
Donsker, An invariance principle for certain probability limit theorems, Mem. Amer. Math. Soc. 6
(1951); extension Prohorov 1956 to Polish; textbook in Billingsley, Convergence of Probability
Measures, 2nd ed., Kallenberg, Foundations of Modern Probability; Lean is `C(Icc 0 1, ℝ)`
polygonal process with `MemLp 2`, mean-zero variance-one standardization.

Proves `Wanted` entry `donsker_invariance_principle`.

Proof: The route combines finite-dimensional convergence from the central limit theorem,
tightness from a maximal inequality and a modulus-of-continuity criterion, Prokhorov's theorem,
and uniqueness of laws on `C([0,1])` from finite-dimensional distributions.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.DonskerWanted.donsker_invariance_principle
signature: ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] {Ω' : Type u_2} [inst_2 : MeasurableSpace Ω'] {P' : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω'} [inst_3 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P'] (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ), (∀ (n : ℕ), Measurable (X n)) → ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X P → (∀ (i : ℕ), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) P P) → MeasureTheory.Integrable (X 0) P → MeasureTheory.MemLp (X 0) 2 P → ∫ (x : Ω), X 0 x ∂P = 0 → ProbabilityTheory.variance (X 0) P = 1 → ∀ (B : NNReal → Ω' → ℝ), ProbabilityTheory.IsBrownianReal B P' → ∃ Y, (∀ᵐ (ω' : Ω') ∂P', ∀ (t : ↑(Set.Icc 0 1)), (Y ω') t = B (MathlibExt.Probability.DonskerWanted.iccToNNReal t) ω') ∧ MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution (fun n ω ↦ MathlibExt.Probability.DonskerWanted.donskerProcess n X ω) Filter.atTop Y (fun x ↦ P) P'
statement:
public theorem donsker_invariance_principle
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    {Ω' : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω'] {P' : Measure Ω'} [IsProbabilityMeasure P']
    (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    (hMeas : ∀ n, Measurable (X n))
    (hIndep : iIndepFun X P)
    (hIdent : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) P P)
    (hInt : Integrable (X 0) P)
    (hMemLp : MemLp (X 0) 2 P)
    (hMean : P[X 0] = 0)
    (hVar : Var[X 0; P] = 1)
    (B : ℝ≥0 → Ω' → ℝ) (hB : IsBrownianReal B P') :
    ∃ (Y : Ω' → C(Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ℝ)),
      (∀ᵐ ω' ∂P', ∀ t : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, (Y ω' t) = B (iccToNNReal t) ω') ∧
      TendstoInDistribution (fun n (ω : Ω) => donskerProcess n X ω) Filter.atTop Y
        (fun _ => P) P'

docstring:
Expected sum of squared differences under independent resampling of each coordinate.
Source: B. Efron and C. Stein, "The Jackknife Estimate of Variance", Annals of Statistics 9 (1981),
DOI 10.1214/aos/1176345462.
It follows from `efron_stein_finite_iid_general`; the instance `[DecidableEq α]` is
unused and keeps the source's shape.
Proves `Wanted` entry `efron_stein_finite_iid`.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.EfronStein.efron_stein_finite_iid
signature:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] {n : ℕ} (p : α → ℝ),
  (∀ (a : α), 0 ≤ p a) →
    ∑ a, p a = 1 →
      ∀ (f : (Fin n → α) → ℝ),
        have μ := ∑ x, (∏ i, p (x i)) * f x;
        have var_ := ∑ x, (∏ i, p (x i)) * (f x - μ) ^ 2;
        var_ ≤ 1 / 2 * ∑ i, ∑ x, ∑ a, (∏ j, p (x j)) * p a * (f x - f (Function.update x i a)) ^ 2
statement:
theorem efron_stein_finite_iid
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    {n : ℕ}
    (p : α → ℝ)
    (hp_nonneg : ∀ a, 0 ≤ p a)
    (hp_sum : ∑ a : α, p a = 1)
    (f : (Fin n → α) → ℝ) :
    let μ : ℝ := ∑ x : Fin n → α, (∏ i : Fin n, p (x i)) * f x
    let var_ : ℝ :=
      ∑ x : Fin n → α, (∏ i : Fin n, p (x i)) * (f x - μ) ^ 2
    var_ ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
      ∑ i : Fin n, ∑ x : Fin n → α, ∑ a : α,
        (∏ j : Fin n, p (x j)) * p a *
          (f x - f (Function.update x i a)) ^ 2

docstring:
Finite discrete Kolmogorov maximal inequality: `n` independent variables with finite
state `α`, coordinate pmfs `p`,
`P[∃ i, |∑_{j ≤ i} X_j(ω_j)| ≥ lam] ≤ (∑_i E[X_i²]) / lam²`.

Primary source: A. Kolmogoroff, "Über die Summen durch den Zufall bestimmter
unabhängiger Größen", Math. Ann. 99 (1928), 309–319, DOI 10.1007/BF01459098.

signature: ∀ {α : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype α] [Nonempty α] {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → α → ℝ), (∀ (i : Fin n) (a : α), 0 ≤ p i a) → (∀ (i : Fin n), ∑ a, p i a = 1) → ∀ (X : Fin n → α → ℝ), (∀ (i : Fin n), ∑ a, p i a * X i a = 0) → ∀ (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → ∑ ω with ∃ i, |∑ j with j ≤ i, X j (ω j)| ≥ lam, ∏ i, p i (ω i) ≤ (∑ i, ∑ a, p i a * X i a ^ 2) / lam ^ 2
statement:
public theorem kolmogorov_maximal_inequality
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [Nonempty α]
    {n : ℕ}
    (p : Fin n → α → ℝ)
    (hp_nonneg : ∀ i a, 0 ≤ p i a)
    (hp_sum : ∀ i, ∑ a : α, p i a = 1)
    (X : Fin n → α → ℝ)
    (h_mean : ∀ i, ∑ a : α, p i a * X i a = 0)
    (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam) :
    (∑ ω ∈ Finset.univ.filter
        (fun ω : Fin n → α =>
          ∃ i : Fin n,
            |∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.filter
                (fun j : Fin n => j ≤ i), X j (ω j)| ≥ lam),
      ∏ i : Fin n, p i (ω i))
    ≤ (∑ i : Fin n, ∑ a : α, p i a * (X i a) ^ 2) / lam ^ 2

docstring:
If `X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ` is i.i.d. with `Integrable`, `MemLp 2`, mean `0` and variance `1`, then a.s.
the normalized partial sums have `limsup = 1` and `liminf = -1` when divided by `√(2 n log log
n)`. Source: A. Y. Khinchin 1924, A. N. Kolmogorov 1929, P. Hartman and A. Wintner, On the law of
the iterated logarithm, Amer. J. Math. 63 (1941) 169–176; textbook in Durrett, Probability Theory
and Examples, 5th ed., Foundations of Modern Probability (Hartman-Wintner LIL). Lean i.i.d.
mean-zero variance-one normalized `√(2 n log log n)` form.

Proves `Wanted` entry `law_of_the_iterated_logarithm`.

Proof: Hartman–Wintner truncation and exponential maximal bounds give the upper half; a CLT block
argument and the second Borel–Cantelli lemma give the lower half.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.LawIteratedLogarithmWanted.law_of_the_iterated_logarithm
signature: ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ), (∀ (n : ℕ), Measurable (X n)) → ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ → (∀ (i : ℕ), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) → MeasureTheory.Integrable (X 0) μ → MeasureTheory.MemLp (X 0) 2 μ → ∫ (x : Ω), X 0 x ∂μ = 0 → ProbabilityTheory.variance (X 0) μ = 1 → ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, Filter.limsup (fun n ↦ (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, X i ω) / √(2 * ↑n * Real.log (Real.log ↑n))) Filter.atTop = 1 ∧ Filter.liminf (fun n ↦ (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, X i ω) / √(2 * ↑n * Real.log (Real.log ↑n))) Filter.atTop = -1
statement:
public theorem law_of_the_iterated_logarithm
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    (hMeas : ∀ n, Measurable (X n))
    (hIndep : iIndepFun X μ)
    (hIdent : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ)
    (hInt : Integrable (X 0) μ)
    (hMemLp : MemLp (X 0) 2 μ)
    (hMean : μ[X 0] = 0)
    (hVar : Var[X 0; μ] = 1) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ,
      Filter.limsup (fun n : ℕ =>
        (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, X i ω) /
          Real.sqrt (2 * (n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)))) Filter.atTop = (1 : ℝ)
      ∧ Filter.liminf (fun n : ℕ =>
        (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, X i ω) /
          Real.sqrt (2 * (n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)))) Filter.atTop = (-1 : ℝ)

docstring:
Finite iid McDiarmid inequality gives exponential tail bound above the mean.
Source: C. McDiarmid, Surveys in Combinatorics 1989, 148-188, DOI 10.1017/CBO9781107359949.008.
When every `c i` is `0` (including `n = 0`), the right-hand side is `Real.exp 0 = 1` by Lean's
convention `x / 0 = 0`; `mcdiarmid_one_sided_finite_iid_of_sum_sq_eq_zero` gives the sharp value
`prob = 0` there, and `mcdiarmid_one_sided_finite_iid_general` covers `0 < ∑ i, c i ^ 2`. The
instance `[DecidableEq α]` is unused and keeps the source's shape.
Proves `Wanted` entry `mcdiarmid_one_sided_finite_iid`.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.McDiarmid.mcdiarmid_one_sided_finite_iid
signature:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] {n : ℕ} (p : α → ℝ),
  (∀ (a : α), 0 ≤ p a) →
    ∑ a, p a = 1 →
      ∀ (f : (Fin n → α) → ℝ) (c : Fin n → ℝ),
        (∀ (i : Fin n), 0 ≤ c i) →
          ∀ (t : ℝ),
            0 < t →
              (∀ (i : Fin n) (x y : Fin n → α), (∀ (j : Fin n), j ≠ i → x j = y j) → |f x - f y| ≤ c i) →
                have mu := ∑ x, (∏ i, p (x i)) * f x;
                have prob := ∑ x with Decidable.decide (t ≤ f x - mu) = Bool.true, ∏ i, p (x i);
                prob ≤ Real.exp (-2 * t ^ 2 / ∑ i, c i ^ 2)
statement:
theorem mcdiarmid_one_sided_finite_iid
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    {n : ℕ}
    (p : α → ℝ)
    (hp_nonneg : ∀ a, 0 ≤ p a)
    (hp_sum : ∑ a : α, p a = 1)
    (f : (Fin n → α) → ℝ)
    (c : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hc_nonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ c i)
    (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t)
    (hbd : ∀ (i : Fin n) (x y : Fin n → α),
      (∀ j, j ≠ i → x j = y j) → |f x - f y| ≤ c i) :
    let mu : ℝ := ∑ x : Fin n → α, (∏ i : Fin n, p (x i)) * f x
    let prob : ℝ :=
      ∑ x ∈ (Finset.univ.filter fun x => decide (t ≤ f x - mu)),
        ∏ i : Fin n, p (x i)
    prob ≤ Real.exp (-2 * t ^ 2 / ∑ i : Fin n, c i ^ 2)

docstring:
Finite iid McDiarmid inequality without a `DecidableEq α` instance, for sensitivities with
`0 < ∑ i, c i ^ 2`. `mcdiarmid_one_sided_finite_iid` is the source-shaped form.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.McDiarmid.mcdiarmid_one_sided_finite_iid_general
signature:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype α] [Nonempty α] {n : ℕ} (p : α → ℝ),
  (∀ (a : α), 0 ≤ p a) →
    ∑ a, p a = 1 →
      ∀ (f : (Fin n → α) → ℝ) (c : Fin n → ℝ),
        (∀ (i : Fin n), 0 ≤ c i) →
          0 < ∑ i, c i ^ 2 →
            ∀ (t : ℝ),
              0 < t →
                (∀ (i : Fin n) (x y : Fin n → α), (∀ (j : Fin n), j ≠ i → x j = y j) → |f x - f y| ≤ c i) →
                  have mu := ∑ x, (∏ i, p (x i)) * f x;
                  have prob := ∑ x with Decidable.decide (t ≤ f x - mu) = Bool.true, ∏ i, p (x i);
                  prob ≤ Real.exp (-2 * t ^ 2 / ∑ i, c i ^ 2)
statement:
theorem mcdiarmid_one_sided_finite_iid_general
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [Nonempty α]
    {n : ℕ}
    (p : α → ℝ)
    (hp_nonneg : ∀ a, 0 ≤ p a)
    (hp_sum : ∑ a : α, p a = 1)
    (f : (Fin n → α) → ℝ)
    (c : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hc_nonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ c i)
    (hc_pos : 0 < ∑ i : Fin n, c i ^ 2)
    (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t)
    (hbd : ∀ (i : Fin n) (x y : Fin n → α),
      (∀ j, j ≠ i → x j = y j) → |f x - f y| ≤ c i) :
    let mu : ℝ := ∑ x : Fin n → α, (∏ i : Fin n, p (x i)) * f x
    let prob : ℝ :=
      ∑ x ∈ (Finset.univ.filter fun x => decide (t ≤ f x - mu)),
        ∏ i : Fin n, p (x i)
    prob ≤ Real.exp (-2 * t ^ 2 / ∑ i : Fin n, c i ^ 2)

docstring:
When `∑ i, c i ^ 2 = 0`, every coordinate change leaves `f` unchanged, so the upper tail
`t ≤ f x - mu` has probability `0` for every `t > 0`.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.McDiarmid.mcdiarmid_one_sided_finite_iid_of_sum_sq_eq_zero
signature:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype α] [Nonempty α] {n : ℕ} (p : α → ℝ),
  (∀ (a : α), 0 ≤ p a) →
    ∑ a, p a = 1 →
      ∀ (f : (Fin n → α) → ℝ) (c : Fin n → ℝ),
        (∀ (i : Fin n), 0 ≤ c i) →
          ∑ i, c i ^ 2 = 0 →
            ∀ (t : ℝ),
              0 < t →
                (∀ (i : Fin n) (x y : Fin n → α), (∀ (j : Fin n), j ≠ i → x j = y j) → |f x - f y| ≤ c i) →
                  have mu := ∑ x, (∏ i, p (x i)) * f x;
                  have prob := ∑ x with Decidable.decide (t ≤ f x - mu) = Bool.true, ∏ i, p (x i);
                  prob = 0
statement:
theorem mcdiarmid_one_sided_finite_iid_of_sum_sq_eq_zero
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [Nonempty α]
    {n : ℕ}
    (p : α → ℝ)
    (hp_nonneg : ∀ a, 0 ≤ p a)
    (hp_sum : ∑ a : α, p a = 1)
    (f : (Fin n → α) → ℝ)
    (c : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hc_nonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ c i)
    (hc_zero : ∑ i : Fin n, c i ^ 2 = 0)
    (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t)
    (hbd : ∀ (i : Fin n) (x y : Fin n → α),
      (∀ j, j ≠ i → x j = y j) → |f x - f y| ≤ c i) :
    let mu : ℝ := ∑ x : Fin n → α, (∏ i : Fin n, p (x i)) * f x
    let prob : ℝ :=
      ∑ x ∈ (Finset.univ.filter fun x => decide (t ≤ f x - mu)),
        ∏ i : Fin n, p (x i)
    prob = 0

This (unnamed) corollary appears directly below Theorem A in the paper:

For every `p ∈ (0, 1/2]` and any sequence `Bₙ` of `n × n` random matrices with mutually
independent `Bernoulli(p)` entries we have that

`P(Bₙ is singular) = (1 - p + oₙ(1))ⁿ`.
Source: K. Tikhomirov, `Singularity of random Bernoulli matrices`, Annals of Math, 191 (2) 2020. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2020-191-2-RandomBernoulliMatrices.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_random_bernoulli_matrices`.

docstring:
Statement of Theorem A:

For every `p ∈ (0, 1/2]` and `ε > 0` there exists `N, C > 0` such that for any `n ≥ N` and any
`n × n` random matrix `B` with mutually independent `Bernoulli(p)` entries,

`P(σ_min (B + sIIᵀ) ≤ t/√n) ≤ (1 - p + ε)ⁿ + Ct` for all `s ∈ [-1,0]` and `t > 0`.
Source: K. Tikhomirov, `Singularity of random Bernoulli matrices`, Annals of Math, 191 (2) 2020. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge (v1.0.0, e32eb14), AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2020-191-2-RandomBernoulliMatrices.lean Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `annals_random_bernoulli_matrices`.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.RandomBernoulliMatricesWanted.RandomBernoulliMatrices.theorem_A
signature: ∀ {p : ↑unitInterval} {ε : ℝ}, 0 < p → ↑p ≤ 1 / 2 → 0 < ε → ∃ N > 0, ∃ C > 0, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ (Ω : Type u_1) (_mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω) (P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω) (B : Ω → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun x x_1 ↦ B x_1 x.1 x.2) P → (∀ (i j : Fin n), ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw (fun x ↦ B x i j) (ProbabilityTheory.bernoulliMeasure 1 0 p) P) → ∀ (s : ℝ), -1 ≤ s ∧ s ≤ 0 → ∀ (t : ℝ), 0 < t → P.real {ω | MathlibExt.Probability.RandomBernoulliMatricesWanted.RandomBernoulliMatrices.σ_min (B ω + Matrix.of fun x x_1 ↦ s) ≤ t / √↑n} ≤ (1 - ↑p + ε) ^ n + C * t
statement:
public theorem_wanted theorem_A {p : I} {ε : ℝ} (hp₀ : 0 < p) (hp₁ : (p : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 2) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ N > 0, ∃ C > 0, ∀ n ≥ N,
      ∀ (Ω : Type*) (_mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω) (P : Measure Ω) (B : Ω → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
        (_B_indep : iIndepFun (fun x : Fin n × Fin n ↦ (B · x.1 x.2)) P)
        (_B_bernoulli : ∀ i j, HasLaw (B · i j) (bernoulliMeasure 1 0 p) P),
        ∀ s : ℝ, -1 ≤ s ∧ s ≤ 0 → ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t →
          P.real {ω : Ω | σ_min (B ω + of (fun _ _ ↦ s)) ≤ t / √n} ≤ (1 - p + ε) ^ n + C * t

docstring:
If `μₙ : ℕ → ProbabilityMeasure X` converges weakly to `μ₀` on a Polish space `X`, then there
exist measurable `Yₙ, Y₀ : ℝ → X` with `(volume.restrict (Icc 0 1)).map Yₙ = μₙ`,
`(volume.restrict (Icc 0 1)).map Y₀ = μ₀` and `Yₙ → Y₀` a.s. for `volume.restrict (Icc 0 1)`.
Source: A. V. Skorokhod, Limit theorems for stochastic processes, Theory Probab. Appl. 1 (1956)
261–290; textbook in Billingsley, Convergence of Probability Measures, 2nd ed., Foundations of
Modern Probability (Icc 0 1)` source, `Icc` Lebesgue base; standard version on `[0, 1]` with
Lebesgue.

signature: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : TopologicalSpace X] [PolishSpace X] [inst_2 : MeasurableSpace X] [inst_3 : BorelSpace X] (μ : ℕ → MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure X) (μ₀ : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure X), Filter.Tendsto (fun n ↦ μ n) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₀) → ∃ Y Y₀, (∀ (n : ℕ), Measurable (Y n)) ∧ Measurable Y₀ ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ), MeasureTheory.Measure.map (Y n) (MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.restrict (Set.Icc 0 1)) = ↑(μ n)) ∧ MeasureTheory.Measure.map Y₀ (MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.restrict (Set.Icc 0 1)) = ↑μ₀ ∧ ∀ᵐ (x : ℝ) ∂MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.restrict (Set.Icc 0 1), Filter.Tendsto (fun n ↦ Y n x) Filter.atTop (nhds (Y₀ x))

docstring:
In the unit-noise model with invertible `Xᵀ * X`, the least-squares matrix `B = (Xᵀ * X)⁻¹ * Xᵀ`
satisfies `B * X = 1` and `A * Aᵀ - B * Bᵀ` is `PosSemidef` for every `A` with `A * X = 1`.
Source: C. F. Gauss, *Theoria combinationis observationum erroribus minimis obnoxiae* (1823); A. C.
Aitken, “On Least Squares and Linear Combination of Observations,” *Proceedings of the Royal
Society of Edinburgh* 55 (1936), 42–48, DOI `10.1017/S0370164600014346`.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.Statistics.GaussMarkov.gaussMarkov_covariance_minimality
signature:
∀ {m n : ℕ} (X : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ),
  IsUnit (X.transpose * X) →
    have B := (X.transpose * X)⁻¹ * X.transpose;
    B * X = 1 ∧ ∀ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) ℝ), A * X = 1 → (A * A.transpose - B * B.transpose).PosSemidef
statement:
theorem gaussMarkov_covariance_minimality
    {m n : ℕ} (X : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ)
    (hX : IsUnit (Xᵀ * X)) :
    let B := (Xᵀ * X)⁻¹ * Xᵀ
    B * X = (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) ∧
      ∀ A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) ℝ,
        A * X = (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) →
          (A * Aᵀ - B * Bᵀ).PosSemidef

docstring:
Dominated Neyman–Pearson lemma (two simple hypotheses), strengthened form.

For `k ≥ 0`, a test `φ⋆` taking the value `1` where `q > k * p` and `0` where
`q < k * p` is most powerful among tests with no larger `p`-size. No normalization
of `p` or `q` and no tie-breaking condition on `{q = k * p}` are assumed.

Source: J. Neyman and E. S. Pearson, "On the problem of the most efficient tests of
statistical hypotheses", Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. A 231 (1933), 289–337,
DOI `10.1098/rsta.1933.0009`.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.Statistics.NeymanPearson.neyman_pearson_dominated_two_simple
signature: ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {p q : Ω → ℝ}, Measurable p → Measurable q → (∀ (x : Ω), 0 ≤ p x) → (∀ (x : Ω), 0 ≤ q x) → MeasureTheory.Integrable p μ → MeasureTheory.Integrable q μ → ∀ (k : ℝ), 0 ≤ k → ∀ (φstar : Ω → ↑(Set.Icc 0 1)), Measurable φstar → (∀ (x : Ω), k * p x < q x → ↑(φstar x) = 1) → (∀ (x : Ω), q x < k * p x → ↑(φstar x) = 0) → ∀ (φ : Ω → ↑(Set.Icc 0 1)), Measurable φ → ∫ (x : Ω), ↑(φ x) * p x ∂μ ≤ ∫ (x : Ω), ↑(φstar x) * p x ∂μ → ∫ (x : Ω), ↑(φ x) * q x ∂μ ≤ ∫ (x : Ω), ↑(φstar x) * q x ∂μ
statement:
theorem neyman_pearson_dominated_two_simple
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    {p q : Ω → ℝ}
    (hp_meas : Measurable p) (hq_meas : Measurable q)
    (hp_nonneg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ p x) (hq_nonneg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ q x)
    (hp_int : Integrable p μ) (hq_int : Integrable q μ)
    (k : ℝ) (hk : 0 ≤ k)
    (φstar : Ω → Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) (hφstar_meas : Measurable φstar)
    (hφstar_gt : ∀ x, k * p x < q x → (φstar x).val = 1)
    (hφstar_lt : ∀ x, q x < k * p x → (φstar x).val = 0) :
    ∀ (φ : Ω → Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1), Measurable φ →
      (∫ x, (φ x).val * p x ∂μ ≤ ∫ x, (φstar x).val * p x ∂μ) →
      (∫ x, (φ x).val * q x ∂μ ≤ ∫ x, (φstar x).val * q x ∂μ)

docstring:
Strassen's theorem on a finite poset, without decidability assumptions: for nonnegative
`p q : α → ℝ` of equal total mass, `p(U) ≤ q(U)` for every upward-closed `U` iff some nonnegative
coupling `π` of `p` and `q` is supported on pairs `x ≤ y`.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.StrassenCouplingWanted.forall_isUpperSet_sum_le_iff_exists_coupling
signature: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype α] [inst_1 : PartialOrder α] (p q : α → ℝ), (∀ (x : α), 0 ≤ p x) → (∀ (x : α), 0 ≤ q x) → ∑ x, p x = ∑ x, q x → ((∀ (U : Finset α), MathlibExt.Probability.StrassenCouplingWanted.IsUpperSet U → ∑ x ∈ U, p x ≤ ∑ x ∈ U, q x) ↔ ∃ π, (∀ (x y : α), 0 ≤ π x y) ∧ (∀ (x : α), ∑ y, π x y = p x) ∧ (∀ (y : α), ∑ x, π x y = q y) ∧ ∀ (x y : α), ¬x ≤ y → π x y = 0)
statement:
theorem forall_isUpperSet_sum_le_iff_exists_coupling
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [PartialOrder α]
    (p q : α → ℝ)
    (hp_nonneg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ p x)
    (hq_nonneg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ q x)
    (hsum : ∑ x : α, p x = ∑ x : α, q x) :
    (∀ U : Finset α, IsUpperSet U → ∑ x ∈ U, p x ≤ ∑ x ∈ U, q x) ↔
    ∃ π : α → α → ℝ,
      (∀ x y, 0 ≤ π x y) ∧
      (∀ x, ∑ y : α, π x y = p x) ∧
      (∀ y, ∑ x : α, π x y = q y) ∧
      (∀ x y, ¬ x ≤ y → π x y = 0)

docstring:
For nonnegative pmfs `p, q : α → ℝ` summing to 1, `p(U) ≤ q(U)` for every upward-closed `U` iff
there exists a nonnegative `π : α → α → ℝ` with row marginal `p`, column marginal `q`, and `π x y =
0` whenever `¬(x ≤ y)`.
Source: V. Strassen, "The Existence of Probability Measures with Given Marginals", Ann. Math.
Statist. 36 (1965), 423-439, DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177700153.

Proves `Wanted` entry `strassen_coupling_finite_poset`.
name: MathlibExt.Probability.StrassenCouplingWanted.strassen_coupling_finite_poset
signature: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype α] [inst_1 : PartialOrder α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableLE α] (p q : α → ℝ), (∀ (x : α), 0 ≤ p x) → (∀ (x : α), 0 ≤ q x) → ∑ x, p x = 1 → ∑ x, q x = 1 → ((∀ (U : Finset α), MathlibExt.Probability.StrassenCouplingWanted.IsUpperSet U → ∑ x ∈ U, p x ≤ ∑ x ∈ U, q x) ↔ ∃ π, (∀ (x y : α), 0 ≤ π x y) ∧ (∀ (x : α), ∑ y, π x y = p x) ∧ (∀ (y : α), ∑ x, π x y = q y) ∧ ∀ (x y : α), ¬x ≤ y → π x y = 0)
statement:
theorem strassen_coupling_finite_poset
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [PartialOrder α] [DecidableEq α]
    [DecidableLE α]
    (p q : α → ℝ)
    (hp_nonneg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ p x)
    (hq_nonneg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ q x)
    (hp_sum : ∑ x : α, p x = 1)
    (hq_sum : ∑ x : α, q x = 1) :
    (∀ U : Finset α, IsUpperSet U → ∑ x ∈ U, p x ≤ ∑ x ∈ U, q x) ↔
    ∃ π : α → α → ℝ,
      (∀ x y, 0 ≤ π x y) ∧
      (∀ x, ∑ y : α, π x y = p x) ∧
      (∀ y, ∑ x : α, π x y = q y) ∧
      (∀ x y, ¬ x ≤ y → π x y = 0)

docstring:
Finite Kochen-Specker in real dimension 3: there exists a finite set of unit vectors in `ℝ³` with no
`{0,1}`-valuation satisfying both orthogonal non-contextuality and completeness on triples from the
set.
Source: S. Kochen, E. P. Specker, The Problem of Hidden Variables in Quantum Mechanics, J. Math.
Mech. 17 (1967), 59-87, DOI 10.1512/iumj.1968.17.17004.

Proves `Wanted` entry `kochen_specker_finite_real_three`.
name: MathlibExt.QuantumInformation.Finite.KochenSpeckerWanted.kochen_specker_finite_real_three
signature: ∃ N v, (∀ (i : Fin N), ‖v i‖ = 1) ∧ ¬∃ c, (∀ (i j : Fin N), Inner.inner ℝ (v i) (v j) = 0 → ↑(c i) + ↑(c j) ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ (b : Fin 3 → Fin N), (Orthonormal ℝ fun r ↦ v (b r)) → ∑ r, ↑(c (b r)) = 1
statement:
theorem kochen_specker_finite_real_three :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (v : Fin N → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)),
      (∀ i, ‖v i‖ = 1) ∧
      ¬ ∃ (c : Fin N → Fin 2),
        (∀ i j : Fin N, inner (𝕜 := ℝ) (v i) (v j) = 0 →
          (c i).val + (c j).val ≤ 1) ∧
          ∀ (b : Fin 3 → Fin N),
            Orthonormal ℝ (fun r => v (b r)) →
              (∑ r : Fin 3, (c (b r)).val) = 1

docstring:
Two-state pure-state no-cloning obstruction: in a complex inner-product space,
non-orthogonal non-identical unit vectors cannot both be exactly cloned by a single
complex linear isometry `H ⊗ H ≃ₗᵢ H ⊗ H` with a fixed blank state.
Source: W. K. Wootters and W. H. Zurek, "A single quantum cannot be cloned",
Nature 299 (1982), 802-803, DOI 10.1038/299802a0.
name: MathlibExt.QuantumInformation.Finite.NoCloning.no_cloning_two_state
signature: ∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] (ψ φ b : H), ‖ψ‖ = 1 → ‖φ‖ = 1 → ‖b‖ = 1 → 0 < ‖Inner.inner ℂ ψ φ‖ → ‖Inner.inner ℂ ψ φ‖ < 1 → ¬∃ U, U (ψ ⊗ₜ[ℂ] b) = ψ ⊗ₜ[ℂ] ψ ∧ U (φ ⊗ₜ[ℂ] b) = φ ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ
statement:
public theorem no_cloning_two_state
    {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
    (ψ φ b : H) (_hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (_hφ : ‖φ‖ = 1) (hb : ‖b‖ = 1)
    (hpos : 0 < ‖⟪ψ, φ⟫_ℂ‖) (hlt : ‖⟪ψ, φ⟫_ℂ‖ < 1) :
    ¬ ∃ (U : (H ⊗[ℂ] H) ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] (H ⊗[ℂ] H)),
      U (ψ ⊗ₜ[ℂ] b) = ψ ⊗ₜ[ℂ] ψ ∧ U (φ ⊗ₜ[ℂ] b) = φ ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ

docstring:
Tightness of Tsirelson's bound `2√2`: there exist `4×4` complex matrices `A₀, A₁, B₀, B₁` forming an
`IsCHSHTuple` whose CHSH operator `A₀*B₀ + A₀*B₁ + A₁*B₀ - A₁*B₁` has eigenvalue `2√2` (cast to
`ℂ`), showing the upper bound `2√2` in `Mathlib.Algebra.Star.CHSH` is sharp.
Source: B. S. Cirel'son/Tsirelson, "Quantum generalizations of Bell's inequality", Lett. Math. Phys.
4 (1980), 93-100, DOI 10.1007/BF00417500.
name: MathlibExt.QuantumInformation.Finite.TsirelsonTight.tsirelson_bound_tight
signature: ∃ A₀ A₁ B₀ B₁, IsCHSHTuple A₀ A₁ B₀ B₁ ∧ Module.End.HasEigenvalue (Matrix.toLin' (A₀ * B₀ + A₀ * B₁ + A₁ * B₀ - A₁ * B₁)) ↑(2 * √2)
statement:
public theorem tsirelson_bound_tight :
    ∃ (A₀ A₁ B₀ B₁ : Matrix (Fin 4) (Fin 4) ℂ),
      IsCHSHTuple A₀ A₁ B₀ B₁ ∧
        Module.End.HasEigenvalue
          (Matrix.toLin' (A₀ * B₀ + A₀ * B₁ + A₁ * B₀ - A₁ * B₁))
          ((↑(2 * Real.sqrt 2) : ℂ))

docstring:
If `k` is a field and `M` is a finitely generated module over `MvPolynomial (Fin n) k`, then `M`
has projective dimension at most `n` in `ModuleCat`. Source: D. Hilbert, Math. Ann. 36 (1890)
473–534 finite free resolution length ≤n; Lang, Algebra; Lean states field case `k[X₁, …, Xₙ]`
with `HasProjectiveDimensionLE n` and n=0 field case.

    {k : Type*} [Field k]

docstring:
Under linear bounds for `s.nu` and the remainders, the level-weight error sum is at most
`R ^ 12`.
name: MathlibExt.SelbergSieve.levelWeights_errSum_le
signature: ∀ (s : BoundingSieve) (R : ℕ), 1 ≤ R → (∀ (d : ℕ), d ∣ s.prodPrimes → 1 ≤ ↑d * s.nu d) → (∀ (d : ℕ), d ∣ s.prodPrimes → |BoundingSieve.rem d| ≤ ↑d) → BoundingSieve.errSum (BoundingSieve.lambdaSquared (MathlibExt.SelbergSieve.levelWeights s R)) ≤ ↑R ^ 12
statement:
theorem levelWeights_errSum_le
    (s : BoundingSieve) (R : ℕ) (hR : 1 ≤ R)
    (hnu : ∀ d : ℕ, d ∣ s.prodPrimes → 1 ≤ (d : ℝ) * s.nu d)
    (hrem : ∀ d : ℕ, d ∣ s.prodPrimes → |s.rem d| ≤ (d : ℝ)) :
    s.errSum (BoundingSieve.lambdaSquared (levelWeights s R)) ≤
      (R : ℝ) ^ 12

docstring: The divisor sum of the level weights diagonalizes to the normalized `y`-coefficient.
name: MathlibExt.SelbergSieve.levelWeights_inner
signature: ∀ (s : BoundingSieve) (R l : ℕ), l ∣ s.prodPrimes → (∑ d ∈ s.prodPrimes.divisors, if l ∣ d then s.nu d * MathlibExt.SelbergSieve.levelWeights s R d else 0) = MathlibExt.SelbergSieve.levelY s R l
statement:
theorem levelWeights_inner (s : BoundingSieve) (R l : ℕ)
    (hl : l ∣ s.prodPrimes) :
    (∑ d ∈ s.prodPrimes.divisors,
      if l ∣ d then s.nu d * levelWeights s R d else 0) =
      levelY s R l

docstring: The main sum of the squared level weights is the reciprocal of the level sum.

signature: ∀ (s : BoundingSieve) (R : ℕ), 1 ≤ R → BoundingSieve.mainSum (BoundingSieve.lambdaSquared (MathlibExt.SelbergSieve.levelWeights s R)) = 1 / MathlibExt.SelbergSieve.levelSum s R

turn `arr` into a unimodal permutation.

name: MathlibExt.TheoryOfComputation.PermuteToUnimodalWanted.ProgramVerification.minRearrange_correct
signature: ∀ {arr : Array ℕ}, arr.Perm (1...=arr.size).toArray → (∃ x, ∃ (hx : x.Perm (1...=arr.size).toArray), MathlibExt.TheoryOfComputation.PermuteToUnimodalWanted.ProgramVerification.Unimodal x ∧ MathlibExt.TheoryOfComputation.PermuteToUnimodalWanted.ProgramVerification.differences (Vector.mk x ⋯) arr.toVector = MathlibExt.TheoryOfComputation.PermuteToUnimodalWanted.ProgramVerification.minRearrange arr) ∧ ∀ (x : Array ℕ) (hx : x.Perm (1...=arr.size).toArray), MathlibExt.TheoryOfComputation.PermuteToUnimodalWanted.ProgramVerification.Unimodal x → MathlibExt.TheoryOfComputation.PermuteToUnimodalWanted.ProgramVerification.minRearrange arr ≤ MathlibExt.TheoryOfComputation.PermuteToUnimodalWanted.ProgramVerification.differences (Vector.mk x ⋯) arr.toVector
statement:
public theorem_wanted minRearrange_correct {arr : Array Nat} :
    arr.Perm (1...=arr.size).toArray →
      (∃ (x : Array Nat) (hx : x.Perm (1...=arr.size).toArray), Unimodal x ∧ differences (Vector.mk x (by simpa using hx.size_eq)) arr.toVector = minRearrange arr) ∧
      (∀ (x : Array Nat) (hx : x.Perm (1...=arr.size).toArray), Unimodal x → minRearrange arr ≤ differences (Vector.mk x (by simpa using hx.size_eq)) arr.toVector)

docstring:
For a compact Hausdorff topological group and `x ≠ y`, there exist `n>0` and a continuous
homomorphism `ρ : G → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ` with `ρ g ∈ unitaryGroup` for all `g`, `ρ 1 = 1`,
and `ρ x ≠ ρ y`. Source: F. Peter and H. Weyl, Math. Ann. 97 (1927), 737–755; Folland, A Course in
Abstract Harmonic Analysis 2nd ed.; Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction 2nd ed.

Proves `Wanted` entry `peter_weyl_point_separation`.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.Algebra.PeterWeylWanted.peter_weyl_point_separation
signature: ∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] [T2Space G] {x y : G}, x ≠ y → ∃ n, ∃ (_ : 0 < n), ∃ ρ, Continuous ρ ∧ ρ 1 = 1 ∧ (∀ (g h : G), ρ (g * h) = ρ g * ρ h) ∧ (∀ (g : G), ρ g ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) ∧ ρ x ≠ ρ y
statement:
public theorem peter_weyl_point_separation
    {G : Type*} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
    [CompactSpace G] [T2Space G]
    {x y : G} (hxy : x ≠ y) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (_hn : 0 < n) (ρ : G → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ),
      Continuous ρ ∧
      ρ 1 = 1 ∧
      (∀ g h : G, ρ (g * h) = ρ g * ρ h) ∧
      (∀ g : G, ρ g ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) ∧
      ρ x ≠ ρ y

docstring:

docstring:
Resolved false: Kaluba-Nowak-Ozawa proved Aut(F5) has Kazhdan property (T) (Math. Ann. 375
(2019), 1169-1191). Property (T) passes to finite-index subgroups and forces finite
abelianization, so every finite-index subgroup of Aut(F5) has first Betti rank 0. The n = 5
instance is therefore false, refuting the universal claim over n > 3. Source: M. Kaluba, P. W.
Nowak, N. Ozawa, Aut(F5) has property (T), Math. Ann. 375 (2019), no. 3-4, 1169-1191,
https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.07167. Moved from
`OpenConjectures/Topology/AutFnFiniteIndexPositiveBetti`.

docstring:
Resolved true: Aut(F_n) has Kazhdan's property (T) for n >= 4: Kaluba–Kielak–Nowak (Ann. of

Aut(F_n) and SL_n(Z), Ann. of Math. 193 (2021), arXiv:1812.03456,
https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.03456; Martin Nitsche, Computer proofs for Property (T), and SDP
duality, arXiv:2009.05134v3 (2022), https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.05134. Moved from

    (x₀ : sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) 1) :
    ∃ e : ℕ → sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) 1 →
        sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) 1 ×

      (∀ n,

docstring: Source: Jean Gallier & Dianna Xu, *A Guide to the Classification Theorem for Compact Surfaces*, https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~jean/surfclassif-root.pdf Via leanprover/lean-eval@38361be, problem `topological_classification_of_surfaces`.

signature: ∀ (S : Type u_1) [inst : TopologicalSpace S] [T2Space S] [ConnectedSpace S] [CompactSpace S] [Nonempty S] [inst_5 : ChartedSpace (EuclideanHalfSpace 2) S] [IsManifold (modelWithCornersEuclideanHalfSpace 2) 0 S], Nonempty (S ≃ₜ ↑(Metric.sphere 0 1)) ∨ ∃ p n, (1 ≤ p ∨ 1 ≤ n) ∧ Nonempty (S ≃ₜ Quot (MathlibExt.Topology.ClassificationOfSurfacesWanted.Topology.ClassificationOfSurfaces.OrientableRel p n)) ∨ 1 ≤ p ∧ Nonempty (S ≃ₜ Quot (MathlibExt.Topology.ClassificationOfSurfacesWanted.Topology.ClassificationOfSurfaces.NonOrientableRel p n))

Apply one braid generator to the traversal state. The crossing
occupies the `z`-slab `[zBot, zTop]` (with `zBot < zTop`). The braid
generator is `w = ±i`; we cross strands at positions `i` and `i + 1`,
with `i = w.natAbs`.

half-space because `q.2 = 0` forces any open neighborhood of `q` to
escape the half-space), but it preserves the half-space and maps the
disk image onto the model half-plane in the half-space.

docstring:
An oriented smooth knot in `ℝ³`: a 2π-periodic, smooth, injective immersion.
The orientation is the one induced by the parametrization.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.Knot
signature: Type
statement: structure Knot

docstring:
A knot is *chiral* if it is not ambient-isotopic, in the
orientation-sensitive sense used in this benchmark, to its mirror image (the
reflection of the image through the `xy`-plane).
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.Knot.Chiral
signature: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.Knot → Prop
statement: def Knot.Chiral (K : Knot) : Prop

docstring:
Two oriented knots are ambient-isotopic if some ambient isotopy of `ℝ³`
carries the parametrized knot `K₁` to the parametrized knot `K₂`, up to an
orientation-preserving smooth reparametrization of the source circle.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.Knot.Isotopic
signature: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.Knot → MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.Knot → Prop
statement: def Knot.Isotopic (K₁ K₂ : Knot) : Prop

docstring: **Smoothly slice (smooth knot version).**
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.Knot.SmoothlySlice
signature: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.Knot → Prop
statement: def Knot.SmoothlySlice (K : Knot) : Prop

docstring:
**Topologically slice (smooth knot version).** A smooth knot is
topologically slice if its image bounds a *locally flat* topologically
embedded proper `2`-disk in the upper half-space, with interior and
boundary points using the matching local model.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.Knot.TopologicallySlice
signature: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.Knot → Prop
statement: def Knot.TopologicallySlice (K : Knot) : Prop

docstring:
A piecewise-linear closed polyline in `ℝ³` with at least three vertices.

Simplicity (being an embedded simple closed curve) is *not* bundled into the
structure; it is expressed separately as `PLKnot.IsSimple`. Keeping it out of
the structure lets named polylines such as `conwayKnot` be written down as
trusted, `sorry`-free data, with the finite-but-laborious simplicity proof
posed as its own benchmark obligation rather than carried as an unchecked
proof field.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.PLKnot
signature: Type
statement: structure PLKnot

docstring:
A smooth knot `J` is a *smooth representative* of the PL knot `K` if
their images are unoriented topologically ambient isotopic in `ℝ³`. For
tame curves (which both sides are by construction) this is equivalent to
the usual smooth/PL knot type relation.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.PLKnot.HasSmoothRepresentative
signature: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.PLKnot → MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.Knot → Prop
statement: def PLKnot.HasSmoothRepresentative (K : PLKnot) (J : Knot) : Prop

docstring:
The polyline is a *simple closed curve*: the periodic parametrization is
injective on a half-open fundamental domain `[0, vertices.length)`.
Equivalent to: all vertices distinct, non-adjacent edges disjoint, adjacent
edges meet only at their shared vertex.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.PLKnot.IsSimple
signature: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.PLKnot → Prop
statement: def PLKnot.IsSimple (K : PLKnot) : Prop

docstring:
**Smoothly slice (PL knot version).** A PL knot is smoothly slice if
some smooth knot of the same knot type is smoothly slice. This is
Piccirillo's theorem about the Conway knot in the form most natural for
a polyline witness.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.PLKnot.SmoothlySlice
signature: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.PLKnot → Prop
statement: def PLKnot.SmoothlySlice (K : PLKnot) : Prop

docstring:
**Topologically slice (PL knot version).** A PL knot is topologically
slice if some smooth knot of the same knot type is topologically slice.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.PLKnot.TopologicallySlice
signature: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.PLKnot → Prop
statement: def PLKnot.TopologicallySlice (K : PLKnot) : Prop

statement: def PLKnot.image (K : PLKnot) : Set R3

name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.R3
signature: Type
statement: abbrev R3 : Type

docstring:
Two subsets of `ℝ³` are *unoriented topologically ambient isotopic*
if some topological ambient isotopy of `ℝ³` carries one onto the other.
"Unoriented" because this is a set-level relation that forgets any
parametrization.

statement: def Set.UnorientedTopAmbIsotopic (A B : Set R3) : Prop

A topological ambient isotopy of `ℝ³`: a one-parameter family of self-
homeomorphisms of `ℝ³`, jointly continuous in `(t, x)`, with a jointly
continuous inverse family, starting at the identity. The time domain is
`ℝ` for consistency with `AmbientIsotopy` in `Prelude.lean`; only `H 0`
and `H 1` matter for the isotopy relation.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.TopAmbientIsotopy
signature: Type
statement: structure TopAmbientIsotopy

docstring:
An oriented two-component smooth link in `ℝ³`: a pair of oriented knots
with disjoint images.

Two oriented two-component links are ambient-isotopic if a single ambient

corresponding oriented component of the second.

The PL closure of a braid word on `n` strands, traced as one polyline
component starting at strand position `1`.

statement: noncomputable def braidClosure (n : ℕ) (word : List ℤ) : List R3

docstring:
The unit Euclidean circle `{(x, y) | x² + y² = 1}` in `ℝ²`, the source of
the slicing disk's boundary.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.circle1
signature: Set (ℝ × ℝ)
statement: abbrev circle1 : Set (ℝ × ℝ)

docstring:
A braid word for the Conway knot 11n34, on 4 strands, of length 11
and writhe `-1`. Each `±i` represents the braid generator `σ_i` (or its
inverse, for negative sign).

Source: KnotInfo's `11n_34` record, `braid_notation` field. The Knot Atlas
records a different but Markov-equivalent presentation for the same knot,
`[1, 1, 2, -3, 2, 1, -3, -2, -2, -3, -3]` (which it labels `K11n34`, the
mirror of the Conway knot); both representations agree on braid index 4,
braid length 11, and writhe `-1`. Sliceness is mirror-invariant, so either
braid word is a valid witness for `conway_knot_not_smoothly_slice`.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.conwayBraidWord
signature: List ℤ
statement: def conwayBraidWord : List ℤ

docstring:
The Conway knot 11n34 as a piecewise-linear closed polyline in `ℝ³`,
realized as the braid closure of `conwayBraidWord` on 4 strands.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.conwayKnot
signature: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.PLKnot
statement: noncomputable def conwayKnot : PLKnot

docstring:
The closed unit Euclidean `2`-disk `{(x, y) | x² + y² ≤ 1}`, the source
of a slicing disk's parametrization.

We spell the disk and its boundary out explicitly via `x² + y² ≤ 1` / `= 1`
rather than as `Metric.closedBall`/`Metric.sphere` on `ℝ × ℝ`: the product
norm on `ℝ × ℝ` is the *sup* norm, so `Metric.closedBall 0 1` would be the
*square* `[-1, 1]²` and `Metric.sphere 0 1` its cornered boundary. Smooth
slice-ness over a cornered domain is vacuously unsatisfiable — at a corner
no smooth immersion can match a corner-free smooth knot boundary while
keeping an injective derivative — which would make `Knot.SmoothlySlice`
false for *every* knot.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.disk2
signature: Set (ℝ × ℝ)
statement: abbrev disk2 : Set (ℝ × ℝ)

docstring:
Model boundary half-plane in the upper half-space. The disk sits in
the plane `q.1 1 = 0 ∧ q.1 2 = 0` (a copy of `ℝ × ℝ`, parametrized by
`q.1 0` and `q.2`) and is restricted to the half-space `q.2 ≥ 0`. Used
to express boundary local flatness of a proper embedded disk.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.modelHalfPlane2
signature: Set (MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.R3 × ℝ)
statement: def modelHalfPlane2 : Set (R3 × ℝ)

docstring:
Model interior `2`-plane in `ℝ³ × ℝ`: the locus where the last two
coordinates of `q.1` and `q.2` all vanish. Used to express interior local
flatness of an embedded `2`-disk.
name: MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.modelPlane2
signature: Set (MathlibExt.Topology.ConwayKnotShared.KnotTheory.R3 × ℝ)
statement: def modelPlane2 : Set (R3 × ℝ)

Every nonempty compact metrizable perfect totally disconnected space is homeomorphic to the Cantor

statement:
public theorem_wanted biLipschitz
    {X T : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [MetricSpace T] [CompactSpace X]
    {P : Set (Fin k → ℝ)} (_hP : IsPolyhedron P)
    {ι : Type*}
    (U : ι → Set X) (_hUopen : ∀ α, IsOpen (U α))
    (ρ : PartitionOfUnity ι X univ) (_hρ : ρ.IsSubordinate U)
    (f : C(P × X, T))
    (slice : P → (X ≃ₜ T))
    (_h_slice_eq : ∀ p : P, ∀ x : X, f (p, x) = slice p x)
    (L : NNReal)
    (_hf_joint     : LipschitzWith L f.toFun)
    (_hf_slice_inv : ∀ p : P, LipschitzWith L (slice p).symm) :
    ∃ F : C(I × P × X, T), ∃ L' : NNReal, ∃ Slice : I × P → (X ≃ₜ T),
      (∀ p : P, ∀ x : X, F (0, p, x) = f (p, x)) ∧
      (∀ t : I, ∀ p : P, ∀ x : X, F (t, p, x) = Slice (t, p) x) ∧
      (∃ K : Subdivision P,
         ∀ D ∈ K.complex.facets,
            AdaptedTo U k
              (fun q : closedCell P D × X => F (1, q.1.1, q.2))) ∧
      (∀ S : Set X, Supported (f := f.toFun) S →
          Supported (fun q : (I × P) × X => F (q.1.1, q.1.2, q.2)) S) ∧
      (∀ Q : Set P, IsBoundarySubpolyhedron Q →
        ∀ S' : Set X,
          Supported (fun q : Q × X => f (q.1.1, q.2)) S' →
            Supported (fun q : (I × Q) × X => F (q.1.1, q.1.2.1, q.2)) S') ∧
      (∀ tp : I × P, LipschitzWith L' (Slice tp)) ∧
      (∀ tp : I × P, LipschitzWith L' (Slice tp).symm)

statement:
public theorem_wanted smale_conjecture
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]
    (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [SecondCountableTopology X]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanHalfSpace n) X] [IsManifold (𝓡∂ n) ∞ X]
    [CompactSpace X]
    (F F' : X × sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) 1 →
            sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) 1)
    (hF  : ContMDiff ((𝓡∂ n).prod (𝓡 3)) (𝓡 3) ∞ F)
    (hF' : ContMDiff ((𝓡∂ n).prod (𝓡 3)) (𝓡 3) ∞ F')
    (hFinv₁ : ∀ x p, F  (x, F' (x, p)) = p)
    (hFinv₂ : ∀ x p, F' (x, F  (x, p)) = p)
    (ψ_bdry : (𝓡∂ n).boundary X → Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin 4) ℝ)
    (hψ_bdry_cont : Continuous ψ_bdry)
    (hF_bdry : ∀ (b : (𝓡∂ n).boundary X)
                 (p : sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) 1),
              (F ((b : X), p) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) =
                Matrix.UnitaryGroup.toLinearEquiv (ψ_bdry b)
                  (p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4))) :
    ∃ (ψ : X → Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin 4) ℝ)
      (H H' : X × unitInterval × sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) 1 →
              sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) 1),
      Continuous ψ ∧
      (∀ b : (𝓡∂ n).boundary X, ψ (b : X) = ψ_bdry b) ∧
      ContMDiff ((𝓡∂ n).prod ((𝓡∂ 1).prod (𝓡 3))) (𝓡 3) ∞ H ∧
      ContMDiff ((𝓡∂ n).prod ((𝓡∂ 1).prod (𝓡 3))) (𝓡 3) ∞ H' ∧
      (∀ x t p, H  (x, t, H' (x, t, p)) = p) ∧
      (∀ x t p, H' (x, t, H  (x, t, p)) = p) ∧
      (∀ x p, H (x, 0, p) = F (x, p)) ∧
      (∀ x (p : sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) 1),
              (H (x, 1, p) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) =
              Matrix.UnitaryGroup.toLinearEquiv (ψ x)
                (p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4))) ∧
      (∀ (b : (𝓡∂ n).boundary X)
         (t : unitInterval)
         (p : sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) 1),
              H ((b : X), t, p) = F ((b : X), p))

public theorem_wanted watanabe_four_dim_smale_disproof :

        (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [SecondCountableTopology X]

          (∀ x t p, H' (x, t, H  (x, t, p)) = p) ∧
          (∀ x p, H (x, 0, p) = F (x, p)) ∧
          (∀ x (p : sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 5)) 1),

Product formula: for `k ≤ M`,

statement:
theorem gaussBinom_mul_qPochFin_mul_qPochFin {R : Type*}

docstring:
Perron-Frobenius for irreducible nonnegative real matrices: there is a positive eigenvalue `r`
with a positive eigenvector, and `r` bounds the modulus of every complex eigenvalue.
name: Matrix.IsIrreducible.perron_frobenius
signature: ∀ {n : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype n] [inst_1 : DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}, A.IsIrreducible → ∃ r v, 0 < r ∧ (∀ (i : n), 0 < v i) ∧ A.mulVec v = r • v ∧ ∀ (μ : ℂ), (μ • 1 - A.map Complex.ofReal).det = 0 → ‖μ‖ ≤ r
statement:
theorem _root_.Matrix.IsIrreducible.perron_frobenius
    {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsIrreducible) :
    ∃ (r : ℝ) (v : n → ℝ),
      0 < r ∧ (∀ i, 0 < v i) ∧ A.mulVec v = r • v ∧
        ∀ μ : ℂ, Matrix.det (μ • (1 : Matrix n n ℂ) - A.map Complex.ofReal) = 0 → ‖μ‖ ≤ r

docstring:
Largest singular value divided by the smallest of the first `n` singular
values; a zero smallest singular value gives infinity. Zero order is outside
the optimization domain.
name: Matrix.SignConditionNumber.conditionNumber
signature: {n : ℕ} → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → ENNReal
statement: noncomputable def conditionNumber {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : ENNReal

docstring: On the nonsingular branch, the definition is exactly the singular-value ratio.
name: Matrix.SignConditionNumber.conditionNumber_eq_ratio_of_smallest_ne_zero
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).singularValues (n - 1) ≠ 0 → Matrix.SignConditionNumber.conditionNumber A = ENNReal.ofReal ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).singularValues 0 / (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).singularValues (n - 1))
statement:
theorem conditionNumber_eq_ratio_of_smallest_ne_zero {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
    (h : (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).singularValues (n - 1) ≠ 0) :
    conditionNumber A = ENNReal.ofReal
      ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).singularValues 0 /
        (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).singularValues (n - 1))

docstring: A vanishing smallest singular value selects the infinite branch.
name: Matrix.SignConditionNumber.conditionNumber_eq_top_of_smallest_eq_zero
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).singularValues (n - 1) = 0 → Matrix.SignConditionNumber.conditionNumber A = ⊤
statement:
theorem conditionNumber_eq_top_of_smallest_eq_zero {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
    (h : (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).singularValues (n - 1) = 0) :
    conditionNumber A = ⊤
