docstring:
Uspensky's theorem on partitions into Beatty sequences: there exists no
partition of the positive integers into three or more Beatty sequences.

Source: A. J. Hildebrand, Xiaomin Li, Junxian Li, and Yun Xie, *Almost Beatty
Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 22 (2019), Article 19.4.6, Theorem B
(Uspensky's theorem), lines 234–236,
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL22/Hildebrand/hilde2.tex>;
first proved by Uspensky in 1927 (lines 238–244).

Beatty-sequence and partition conventions from the same source, lines 183–200:
`B_α = (⌊n/α⌋)` with `0 < α < 1`, `ℕ = {1, 2, ...}`, and a partition means
every element belongs to exactly one subset. The source statement carries no
irrationality hypothesis. The complement version (Theorem B*, lines 260–263)
is a source-declared equivalent and is not stated separately.
Proves `Wanted` entry `uspensky_no_partition_into_three_or_more_beatty_sequences`.
name: MetaMathlibExt.uspensky_no_partition_into_three_or_more_beatty_sequences
signature: ∀ (k : ℕ), 3 ≤ k → ∀ (α : Fin k → ℝ), (∀ (i : Fin k), 0 < α i) → (∀ (i : Fin k), α i < 1) → ¬((Set.univ.PairwiseDisjoint fun i ↦ {x | ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ beattySeq (1 / α i) n = x}) ∧ ⋃ i, {x | ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ beattySeq (1 / α i) n = x} = {x | 0 < x})
statement:
theorem uspensky_no_partition_into_three_or_more_beatty_sequences
    (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (α : Fin k → ℝ)
    (hαpos : ∀ i, 0 < α i) (hαlt : ∀ i, α i < 1) :
    ¬ ((Set.univ : Set (Fin k)).PairwiseDisjoint
        (fun i => {x : ℤ | ∃ n : ℤ, 0 < n ∧ beattySeq (1 / α i) n = x}) ∧
      (⋃ i, {x : ℤ | ∃ n : ℤ, 0 < n ∧ beattySeq (1 / α i) n = x}) =
        {x : ℤ | 0 < x})

docstring:
Van Aubel's theorem (statement `vanaubel-s1` from
    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Aubel%27s_theorem):
    for a quadrilateral with ordered vertices `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, erect a square
    on each directed side `A → B`, `B → C`, `C → D`, `D → A`; the segments joining
    the centers of opposite squares are equal in length and perpendicular.

    Here every square lies to the left of its directed side: its center is the
    side midpoint plus half the side vector rotated counterclockwise by 90 degrees,
    `(x, y) ↦ (-y, x)`. The identity needs no orientation hypothesis. When the
    vertices are listed clockwise these are the outward squares of the source;
    when they are listed counterclockwise they are the inward squares, and
    `vanAubel_right` gives the outward version.
Proves `Wanted` entry `vanAubel`.
name: MetaMathlibExt.vanAubel
signature: ∀ (A B C D Oab Obc Ocd Oda : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), Oab = 2⁻¹ • (A + B) + 2⁻¹ • !₂[-(B - A).ofLp 1, (B - A).ofLp 0] → Obc = 2⁻¹ • (B + C) + 2⁻¹ • !₂[-(C - B).ofLp 1, (C - B).ofLp 0] → Ocd = 2⁻¹ • (C + D) + 2⁻¹ • !₂[-(D - C).ofLp 1, (D - C).ofLp 0] → Oda = 2⁻¹ • (D + A) + 2⁻¹ • !₂[-(A - D).ofLp 1, (A - D).ofLp 0] → ‖Oab - Ocd‖ = ‖Obc - Oda‖ ∧ Inner.inner ℝ (Oab - Ocd) (Obc - Oda) = 0
statement:
theorem vanAubel :
    ∀ (A B C D : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))
      (Oab Obc Ocd Oda : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
      Oab = (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • (A + B) +
        (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • WithLp.toLp 2 (![-((B - A).ofLp 1), ((B - A).ofLp 0)]) →
      Obc = (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • (B + C) +
        (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • WithLp.toLp 2 (![-((C - B).ofLp 1), ((C - B).ofLp 0)]) →
      Ocd = (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • (C + D) +
        (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • WithLp.toLp 2 (![-((D - C).ofLp 1), ((D - C).ofLp 0)]) →
      Oda = (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • (D + A) +
        (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • WithLp.toLp 2 (![-((A - D).ofLp 1), ((A - D).ofLp 0)]) →
      ‖Oab - Ocd‖ = ‖Obc - Oda‖ ∧ ⟪Oab - Ocd, Obc - Oda⟫_ℝ = 0

docstring:
Van Aubel's theorem with every square to the right of its directed side:
each center is the side midpoint plus half the side vector rotated clockwise
by 90 degrees, `(x, y) ↦ (y, -x)`. When the vertices `A`, `B`, `C`, `D` are
listed counterclockwise these are the outward squares; together with
`vanAubel` this covers the outward construction for both orientations.
name: MetaMathlibExt.vanAubel_right
signature: ∀ (A B C D Oab Obc Ocd Oda : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), Oab = 2⁻¹ • (A + B) + 2⁻¹ • !₂[(B - A).ofLp 1, -(B - A).ofLp 0] → Obc = 2⁻¹ • (B + C) + 2⁻¹ • !₂[(C - B).ofLp 1, -(C - B).ofLp 0] → Ocd = 2⁻¹ • (C + D) + 2⁻¹ • !₂[(D - C).ofLp 1, -(D - C).ofLp 0] → Oda = 2⁻¹ • (D + A) + 2⁻¹ • !₂[(A - D).ofLp 1, -(A - D).ofLp 0] → ‖Oab - Ocd‖ = ‖Obc - Oda‖ ∧ Inner.inner ℝ (Oab - Ocd) (Obc - Oda) = 0
statement:
theorem vanAubel_right :
    ∀ (A B C D : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))
      (Oab Obc Ocd Oda : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
      Oab = (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • (A + B) +
        (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • WithLp.toLp 2 (![((B - A).ofLp 1), -((B - A).ofLp 0)]) →
      Obc = (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • (B + C) +
        (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • WithLp.toLp 2 (![((C - B).ofLp 1), -((C - B).ofLp 0)]) →
      Ocd = (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • (C + D) +
        (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • WithLp.toLp 2 (![((D - C).ofLp 1), -((D - C).ofLp 0)]) →
      Oda = (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • (D + A) +
        (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • WithLp.toLp 2 (![((A - D).ofLp 1), -((A - D).ofLp 0)]) →
      ‖Oab - Ocd‖ = ‖Obc - Oda‖ ∧ ⟪Oab - Ocd, Obc - Oda⟫_ℝ = 0

docstring:
Van der Waerden's theorem: for positive integers `r` (colors) and `k`
(progression length), there exists `N = W(r, k)` such that every `r`-coloring
of `{1, ..., N}` contains a monochromatic `k`-term arithmetic progression
`a, a + d, ..., a + (k - 1) * d` with `d ≥ 1`.
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_der_Waerden%27s_theorem

Proves `Wanted` entry `vanDerWaerden`.

Proof: Apply the Hales-Jewett theorem to digit-sum encodings of words over `Fin k`, so a
combinatorial line becomes an arithmetic progression. This follows the standard derivation in
Graham, Rothschild, and Spencer, *Ramsey Theory*, Section 2.3, from van der Waerden (1927).
name: MetaMathlibExt.vanDerWaerden
statement:
theorem vanDerWaerden : ∀ (r k : Nat), 0 < r → 0 < k →
    ∃ N : Nat, ∀ c : {m : Nat // 1 ≤ m ∧ m ≤ N} → Fin r, ∃ a d : Nat,
      1 ≤ a ∧ 1 ≤ d ∧ a + (k - 1) * d ≤ N ∧
        ∀ i : Nat, i < k → ∀ (h₁ : 1 ≤ a + i * d) (h₂ : a + i * d ≤ N)
          (h₀ : 1 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ N), c ⟨a + i * d, h₁, h₂⟩ = c ⟨a, h₀⟩

docstring:
Van Schooten's theorem: an equilateral triangle `ABC` with a point `P` on the
circumcircle on arc `AB` not containing `C` satisfies `PA + PB = PC`.
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Schooten%27s_theorem.
It follows from `vanSchooten_general`; the hypotheses `P ≠ A`, `P ≠ B` and `P ≠ C` are unused
and keep the source's shape.
Proves `Wanted` entry `vanSchooten`.
name: MetaMathlibExt.vanSchooten
signature: ∀ (A B C P O : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → Dist.dist A B = Dist.dist B C → Dist.dist B C = Dist.dist C A → A ∈ Metric.sphere O r → B ∈ Metric.sphere O r → C ∈ Metric.sphere O r → P ∈ Metric.sphere O r → P ≠ A → P ≠ B → P ≠ C → Dist.dist C P > Dist.dist A P → Dist.dist C P > Dist.dist B P → Dist.dist P A + Dist.dist P B = Dist.dist P C
statement:
theorem vanSchooten : ∀ (A B C P O : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) (r : ℝ),
  0 < r →
  dist A B = dist B C →
  dist B C = dist C A →
  A ∈ Metric.sphere O r →
  B ∈ Metric.sphere O r →
  C ∈ Metric.sphere O r →
  P ∈ Metric.sphere O r →
  P ≠ A → P ≠ B → P ≠ C →
  dist C P > dist A P →
  dist C P > dist B P →
  dist P A + dist P B = dist P C

docstring:
Van Schooten's theorem without point-disequality hypotheses: if `ABC` is equilateral,
inscribed in the circle of radius `r > 0` about `O`, and `P` on that circle is strictly closer
to `A` and to `B` than to `C`, then `PA + PB = PC`. `vanSchooten` is the source-shaped form.
name: MetaMathlibExt.vanSchooten_general
signature: ∀ (A B C P O : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → Dist.dist A B = Dist.dist B C → Dist.dist B C = Dist.dist C A → A ∈ Metric.sphere O r → B ∈ Metric.sphere O r → C ∈ Metric.sphere O r → P ∈ Metric.sphere O r → Dist.dist C P > Dist.dist A P → Dist.dist C P > Dist.dist B P → Dist.dist P A + Dist.dist P B = Dist.dist P C
statement:
theorem vanSchooten_general (A B C P O : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r)
    (he1 : dist A B = dist B C) (he2 : dist B C = dist C A)
    (hA : A ∈ Metric.sphere O r) (hB : B ∈ Metric.sphere O r)
    (hC : C ∈ Metric.sphere O r) (hP : P ∈ Metric.sphere O r)
    (h1 : dist C P > dist A P) (h2 : dist C P > dist B P) :
    dist P A + dist P B = dist P C

docstring:
Variant of Klamkin's identity as an infinite series.

Source: Ulrich Abel, "A Short Proof of the Binomial Identities of Frisch and
Klamkin," Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), Article 20.7.1, Theorem
(label theorem-variant-Klamkin), equation (Identity-variant-Klamkin),
lines 210–218,
https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Abel/abel12.tex

The generalized binomial `C(a, b+k)` is rendered with Gamma functions. Abel assumes only
`a - b + 1 ∉ ℕ`; here `h_ab` excludes every integer value of `a - b`, since otherwise some
`Gamma (a - (b + k) + 1)` sits at a pole (value `0` in Lean) and the rendered summands vanish.

Proves `Wanted` entry `variant_Klamkin`.

Proof: Rewrite the summand as an ordinary hypergeometric coefficient and apply Abel's
specialization of Gauss's formula (Abramowitz-Stegun 15.1.20), then simplify by Gamma recurrence.
name: MetaMathlibExt.variant_Klamkin
signature: ∀ (a b : ℝ) (n : ℕ), (∀ (m : ℕ), -a ≠ ↑m) → (∀ (m : ℕ), -b ≠ ↑m) → 1 ≤ n → ↑n < -a - 1 → (∀ (m : ℤ), a - b ≠ ↑m) → HasSum (fun k ↦ (-1) ^ k * ↑((n + k - 1).choose k) * (Real.Gamma (a + 1) / (Real.Gamma (b + ↑k + 1) * Real.Gamma (a - (b + ↑k) + 1)))⁻¹) ((a + 1) / (a + ↑n + 1) * (Real.Gamma (a + ↑n + 1) / (Real.Gamma (b + 1) * Real.Gamma (a + ↑n - b + 1)))⁻¹)
statement:
public theorem variant_Klamkin (a b : ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (h_neg_a : ∀ m : ℕ, -a ≠ (m : ℝ))
    (h_neg_b : ∀ m : ℕ, -b ≠ (m : ℝ))
    (h_n_pos : 1 ≤ n)
    (h_n_bound : (n : ℝ) < -a - 1)
    (h_ab : ∀ m : ℤ, a - b ≠ (m : ℝ)) :
    HasSum (fun k : ℕ => (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * (Nat.choose (n + k - 1) k : ℝ) *
      (Real.Gamma (a + 1) /
        (Real.Gamma (b + (k : ℝ) + 1) *
          Real.Gamma (a - (b + (k : ℝ)) + 1)))⁻¹)
      ((a + 1) / (a + (n : ℝ) + 1) *
        ((Real.Gamma (a + (n : ℝ) + 1) /
          (Real.Gamma (b + 1) * Real.Gamma (a + (n : ℝ) - b + 1)))⁻¹))

docstring:
Varignon's theorem (statement varignon-s1): side-midpoints of any quadrilateral form
a parallelogram of half the area.
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varignon%27s_theorem.
`A B C D` are arbitrary points in the Euclidean plane, including degenerate or
self-crossing configurations.
`P Q R S` are the midpoints of sides AB, BC, CD, DA (`2 • P = A + B`, etc.).
Conclusion: `P + R = Q + S` (the diagonals of PQRS bisect each other, i.e. PQRS is a
parallelogram via parallel opposite sides / bisecting diagonals), and twice the signed area of
PQRS, expressed through `EuclideanGeometry.orientedTriangleArea`, equals the signed area of ABCD.

Proves `Wanted` entry `varignon`.
name: MetaMathlibExt.varignon
signature: ∀ (A B C D P Q R S : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), 2 • P = A + B → 2 • Q = B + C → 2 • R = C + D → 2 • S = D + A → P + R = Q + S ∧ 2 * (EuclideanGeometry.orientedTriangleArea P Q R + EuclideanGeometry.orientedTriangleArea P R S) = EuclideanGeometry.orientedTriangleArea A B C + EuclideanGeometry.orientedTriangleArea A C D
statement:
theorem varignon :
  ∀ (A B C D P Q R S : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
    2 • P = A + B → 2 • Q = B + C → 2 • R = C + D → 2 • S = D + A →
    P + R = Q + S ∧
    2 * (EuclideanGeometry.orientedTriangleArea P Q R +
      EuclideanGeometry.orientedTriangleArea P R S) =
      EuclideanGeometry.orientedTriangleArea A B C +
        EuclideanGeometry.orientedTriangleArea A C D

docstring:
Vaughan's identity, statement id `vaughan-identity-s1`: the von Mangoldt function `Λ`,
characterized by the Dirichlet convolution `Λ = μ * log` (`hLambda`) with `μ`
the Möbius function (Dirichlet inverse of `1`, `hMu`) and `logW` the logarithm,
at `n > V` with parameters `U`, `V ≥ 1` decomposes into the type-I truncated
`μ * log` sum minus the type-II `μ_{≤U} * Λ_{≤V} * 1` double sum plus the
type-II `μ_{>U} * Λ_{>V} * 1` double sum.
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaughan%27s_identity
It follows from `vaughan_identity_general`; the hypotheses `hU` and `hV` are unused and keep the
source's shape.
Proves `Wanted` entry `vaughan_identity`.
name: MetaMathlibExt.vaughan_identity
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (μ Λ : ArithmeticFunction R) (logW : ℕ → R) (U V n : ℕ), 1 ≤ U → 1 ≤ V → V < n → (∀ (m : ℕ), Λ m = ∑ d ∈ Finset.range (m + 1) with d ∣ m, μ d * logW (m / d)) → (∀ (m : ℕ), ∑ d ∈ Finset.range (m + 1) with d ∣ m, μ d = if m = 1 then 1 else 0) → Λ n = ∑ b ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) with b ∣ n ∧ b ≤ U, μ b * logW (n / b) - ∑ b ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) with b ∣ n ∧ b ≤ U, ∑ c ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) with c ≤ V ∧ b * c ∣ n, μ b * Λ c + ∑ b ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) with b ∣ n ∧ U < b, ∑ c ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) with V < c ∧ b * c ∣ n, μ b * Λ c
statement:
theorem vaughan_identity {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (μ Λ : ArithmeticFunction R) (logW : ℕ → R)
    (U V n : ℕ) (hU : 1 ≤ U) (hV : 1 ≤ V) (hn : V < n)
    (hLambda : ∀ m, Λ m =
      ∑ d ∈ (Finset.range (m + 1)).filter (fun d => d ∣ m), μ d * logW (m / d))
    (hMu : ∀ m, ∑ d ∈ (Finset.range (m + 1)).filter (fun d => d ∣ m), μ d =
      if m = 1 then 1 else 0) :
    Λ n = (∑ b ∈ (Finset.range (n + 1)).filter (fun b => b ∣ n ∧ b ≤ U),
        μ b * logW (n / b))
      - (∑ b ∈ (Finset.range (n + 1)).filter (fun b => b ∣ n ∧ b ≤ U),
          ∑ c ∈ (Finset.range (n + 1)).filter (fun c => c ≤ V ∧ b * c ∣ n),
            μ b * Λ c)
      + (∑ b ∈ (Finset.range (n + 1)).filter (fun b => b ∣ n ∧ U < b),
          ∑ c ∈ (Finset.range (n + 1)).filter (fun c => V < c ∧ b * c ∣ n),
            μ b * Λ c)

docstring:
Vaughan's identity with only the hypotheses the argument uses: for any `U` and any `V < n`,
with `Λ = μ * logW` (`hLambda`) and `μ` the Dirichlet inverse of `1` (`hMu`), `Λ n` is the
truncated `μ * log` sum minus the `μ_{≤U} * Λ_{≤V} * 1` double sum plus the
`μ_{>U} * Λ_{>V} * 1` double sum. `vaughan_identity` is the source-shaped form.
name: MetaMathlibExt.vaughan_identity_general
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (μ Λ : ArithmeticFunction R) (logW : ℕ → R) (U V n : ℕ), V < n → (∀ (m : ℕ), Λ m = ∑ d ∈ Finset.range (m + 1) with d ∣ m, μ d * logW (m / d)) → (∀ (m : ℕ), ∑ d ∈ Finset.range (m + 1) with d ∣ m, μ d = if m = 1 then 1 else 0) → Λ n = ∑ b ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) with b ∣ n ∧ b ≤ U, μ b * logW (n / b) - ∑ b ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) with b ∣ n ∧ b ≤ U, ∑ c ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) with c ≤ V ∧ b * c ∣ n, μ b * Λ c + ∑ b ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) with b ∣ n ∧ U < b, ∑ c ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) with V < c ∧ b * c ∣ n, μ b * Λ c
statement:
theorem vaughan_identity_general {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (μ Λ : ArithmeticFunction R) (logW : ℕ → R)
    (U V n : ℕ) (hn : V < n)
    (hLambda : ∀ m, Λ m =
      ∑ d ∈ (Finset.range (m + 1)).filter (fun d => d ∣ m), μ d * logW (m / d))
    (hMu : ∀ m, ∑ d ∈ (Finset.range (m + 1)).filter (fun d => d ∣ m), μ d =
      if m = 1 then 1 else 0) :
    Λ n = (∑ b ∈ (Finset.range (n + 1)).filter (fun b => b ∣ n ∧ b ≤ U),
        μ b * logW (n / b))
      - (∑ b ∈ (Finset.range (n + 1)).filter (fun b => b ∣ n ∧ b ≤ U),
          ∑ c ∈ (Finset.range (n + 1)).filter (fun c => c ≤ V ∧ b * c ∣ n),
            μ b * Λ c)
      + (∑ b ∈ (Finset.range (n + 1)).filter (fun b => b ∣ n ∧ U < b),
          ∑ c ∈ (Finset.range (n + 1)).filter (fun c => V < c ∧ b * c ∣ n),
            μ b * Λ c)

docstring:
Viviani's theorem, source-shaped form (statement `viviani-s1`): thin
wrapper over `viviani_general` retaining the frozen Wanted signature,
including its (unused) positivity hypothesis `0 < dist A B`, for exact
compatibility with the former `Wanted` entry. New callers should prefer
`viviani_general`, which needs no positivity hypothesis.
name: MetaMathlibExt.viviani
signature: ∀ (A B C P : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), Dist.dist A B = Dist.dist B C → Dist.dist B C = Dist.dist C A → 0 < Dist.dist A B → P ∈ interior ((convexHull ℝ) {A, B, C}) → Metric.infDist P ↑line[ℝ, A, B] + Metric.infDist P ↑line[ℝ, B, C] + Metric.infDist P ↑line[ℝ, C, A] = Metric.infDist A ↑line[ℝ, B, C]
statement:
theorem viviani : ∀ (A B C P : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
  dist A B = dist B C → dist B C = dist C A → 0 < dist A B →
  P ∈ interior (convexHull ℝ {A, B, C}) →
  Metric.infDist P ↑(affineSpan ℝ {A, B}) +
    Metric.infDist P ↑(affineSpan ℝ {B, C}) +
    Metric.infDist P ↑(affineSpan ℝ {C, A}) =

docstring:
Viviani's theorem, general form (statement `viviani-s1`): an
equilateral triangle in the Euclidean plane and an interior point `P`;
the sum of the perpendicular distances from `P` to the three sides
equals the altitude of the triangle. No positivity hypothesis on the
side length is needed: membership of `P` in the ambient interior already
yields affine independence, hence nondegeneracy.
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viviani%27s_theorem.

Proves `Wanted` entry `viviani` (via the source-shaped wrapper `viviani`
below).

Proof: Following the barycentric-coordinate area decomposition in Wikipedia, "Viviani's theorem"
(Proof section), we express the three distances as barycentric weights times a common height.
name: MetaMathlibExt.viviani_general
signature: ∀ (A B C P : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), Dist.dist A B = Dist.dist B C → Dist.dist B C = Dist.dist C A → P ∈ interior ((convexHull ℝ) {A, B, C}) → Metric.infDist P ↑line[ℝ, A, B] + Metric.infDist P ↑line[ℝ, B, C] + Metric.infDist P ↑line[ℝ, C, A] = Metric.infDist A ↑line[ℝ, B, C]
statement:
theorem viviani_general : ∀ (A B C P : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
  dist A B = dist B C → dist B C = dist C A →
  P ∈ interior (convexHull ℝ {A, B, C}) →
  Metric.infDist P ↑(affineSpan ℝ {A, B}) +
    Metric.infDist P ↑(affineSpan ℝ {B, C}) +
    Metric.infDist P ↑(affineSpan ℝ {C, A}) =
    Metric.infDist A ↑(affineSpan ℝ {B, C})

docstring:
Von Szily identity for the super Catalan numbers `S(m, n)`: the source
normalization `(2 * m)! * (2 * n)! / (m! * n! * (m + n)!)` equals the
all-integer alternating sum with plus-plus indices `choose (2 * m) (m + k)`
and `choose (2 * n) (n + k)`, summed over exactly its simultaneous finite
binomial support.

Source: Kendra Killpatrick, *Super FiboCatalan Numbers and Their Lucas
Analogues*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.5.8, von
Szily identity quoted in the Open problems section, lines 671–674,
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL28/Killpatrick/killp6.tex>,
citing I. Gessel, *Super ballot numbers*, J. Symbolic Comput. 14 (1992),
p. 11.

Math notes: the source sums over `k ∈ ℤ`; only finitely many terms are
nonzero, represented here by the `Finset.Icc` of the common support.

Proves `Wanted` entry `von_szily_super_catalan_identity`.
name: MetaMathlibExt.von_szily_super_catalan_identity
signature: ∀ (m n : ℕ), ↑((2 * m).factorial * (2 * n).factorial / (m.factorial * n.factorial * (m + n).factorial)) = ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc (Max.max (-↑m) (-↑n)) (Min.min ↑m ↑n), (-1) ^ k.natAbs * ↑((2 * m).choose (↑m + k).toNat) * ↑((2 * n).choose (↑n + k).toNat)
statement:
theorem von_szily_super_catalan_identity (m n : ℕ) :
    (((2 * m).factorial * (2 * n).factorial /
        (m.factorial * n.factorial * (m + n).factorial) : ℕ) : ℤ) =
      ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc (max (-(m : ℤ)) (-(n : ℤ))) (min (m : ℤ) (n : ℤ)),
        (-1 : ℤ) ^ k.natAbs *
          (Nat.choose (2 * m) (Int.toNat ((m : ℤ) + k)) : ℤ) *
          (Nat.choose (2 * n) (Int.toNat ((n : ℤ) + k)) : ℤ)

docstring:
Vosper equality characterization: for prime `p` and nonempty
`A B : Finset (ZMod p)` with `A + B ≠ Finset.univ`,
`(A + B).card = A.card + B.card - 1` iff (i) `min A.card B.card = 1`, or
(ii) `(A + B).card = p - 1` with the complement of `A + B` equal to `{c}`
for some `c : ZMod p` and `B` the complement of the image `c - A`, or
(iii) `AreFiniteArithmeticProgressionsWithCommonDifference A B`.

Source: Fabián Arias, Jerson Borja, and Samuel Anaya, *Counting Integers
Representable as Sums of k-th Powers Modulo n*, Journal of Integer Sequences
26 (2023), Article 23.8.1, Theorem [Vosper] `theo_Vosper`, lines 256–267,
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL26/Borja/borja4.tex>.

Proves `Wanted` entry `vosper_eq_iff`.
name: MetaMathlibExt.vosper_eq_iff
signature: ∀ {p : ℕ} [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (A B : Finset (ZMod p)), A.Nonempty → B.Nonempty → A + B ≠ Finset.univ → ((A + B).card = A.card + B.card - 1 ↔ Min.min A.card B.card = 1 ∨ ((A + B).card = p - 1 ∧ ∃ c, {x | x ∉ A + B} = {c} ∧ B = {x | x ∉ Finset.image (fun a ↦ c - a) A}) ∨ MetaMathlibExt.AreFiniteArithmeticProgressionsWithCommonDifference A B)
statement:
theorem vosper_eq_iff {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)]
    (A B : Finset (ZMod p)) (hA : A.Nonempty) (hB : B.Nonempty)
    (hAB : A + B ≠ Finset.univ) :
    (A + B).card = A.card + B.card - 1 ↔
      (min A.card B.card = 1 ∨
        ((A + B).card = p - 1 ∧
          ∃ c : ZMod p,
            Finset.filter (fun x => x ∉ (A + B)) Finset.univ = {c} ∧
              B = Finset.filter
                (fun x => x ∉ Finset.image (fun a => c - a) A) Finset.univ) ∨
        AreFiniteArithmeticProgressionsWithCommonDifference A B)

docstring:
Ward's product definition of a generalized binomial coefficient:
`{{n+m} choose n}_s = ∏_{b>1} s_b ^ ε₀^{b,n,m}`.

Only bases at most `n + m` can carry in the units place, so this is a finite product.
The source explicitly uses the product as a definition over arbitrary coefficient
sequences, including sequences with zero terms.

docstring:
Generalized Ward identity for `f`-binomial coefficients via ones-position carries.

Source: Tom Edgar and Michael Z. Spivey,
"Multiplicative Functions, Generalized Binomial Coefficients, and Generalized Catalan Numbers,"
Journal of Integer Sequences 19 (2016), Article 16.1.6,
Theorem [Ward] `thmward` (equation `wardeqn`), lines 475–482,
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL19/Edgar/edgar3.tex>;
attributed there to M. Ward.

Math notes: `(n % b + m % b) / b` is the carry in the ones position when adding `n`
and `m` in base `b`; for the classical case this recovers Kummer's carry-count theorem.
It follows from `ward_sbinomial_carry_product_general` and
`wardGeneralizedBinomialCoefficient_eq_prod_Icc`; the hypotheses `hs` and `hf` are used only at
positive indices.
Proves `Wanted` entry `ward_sbinomial_carry_product`.
name: MetaMathlibExt.ward_sbinomial_carry_product
signature:
∀ (s : ℕ → ℤ),
  (∀ (b : ℕ), s b ≠ 0) →
    ∀ (f : ℕ → ℤ),
      (∀ (k : ℕ), f k = ∏ d ∈ k.divisors, s d) →
        ∀ (n m : ℕ),
          have fFactorial := fun t ↦ ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 t, f i;
          ↑(fFactorial (n + m)) / (↑(fFactorial n) * ↑(fFactorial m)) = ∏ b ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n + m), ↑(s b) ^ ((n % b + m % b) / b)
statement:
theorem ward_sbinomial_carry_product
    (s : Nat → Int) (hs : ∀ b, s b ≠ 0)
    (f : Nat → Int) (hf : ∀ k, f k = ∏ d ∈ Nat.divisors k, s d)
    (n m : Nat) :
    let fFactorial : Nat → Int := fun t => ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 t, f i;
    (fFactorial (n + m) : ℚ) / ((fFactorial n : ℚ) * (fFactorial m : ℚ)) =
      ∏ b ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n + m), (s b : ℚ) ^ ((n % b + m % b) / b)

docstring:
Ward's identity with hypotheses only on positive indices: if `f k = ∏_{d ∣ k} s d` and
`s b ≠ 0` for all positive `k` and `b`, then the `f`-factorial quotient

`ward_sbinomial_carry_product` is the source-shaped form.
name: MetaMathlibExt.ward_sbinomial_carry_product_general
signature: ∀ (s : ℕ → ℤ), (∀ (b : ℕ), 0 < b → s b ≠ 0) → ∀ (f : ℕ → ℤ), (∀ (k : ℕ), 0 < k → f k = ∏ d ∈ k.divisors, s d) → ∀ (n m : ℕ), ↑(∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + m), f i) / (↑(∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, f i) * ↑(∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m, f i)) = ↑(MetaMathlibExt.wardGeneralizedBinomialCoefficient s n m)
statement:
theorem ward_sbinomial_carry_product_general
    (s : ℕ → ℤ) (hs : ∀ b, 0 < b → s b ≠ 0)
    (f : ℕ → ℤ) (hf : ∀ k, 0 < k → f k = ∏ d ∈ Nat.divisors k, s d)
    (n m : ℕ) :
    ((∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + m), f i : ℤ) : ℚ) /
        (((∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, f i : ℤ) : ℚ) * ((∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m, f i : ℤ) : ℚ)) =
      ((wardGeneralizedBinomialCoefficient s n m : ℤ) : ℚ)

            Real.exp (-Real.cos α / (ρ * x)) + 1 - p ^ 2 = 0} M₀) :
    ∀ M : ℝ, 0 < M → M ≤ M₀ → ∀ w : ℂ, 0 ≤ w.re →
      ∃ b : ℕ → ℂ, ∀ z : ℂ, 0 < z.re →
        Summable (fun k : ℕ =>
          ‖b (k + 1) /
            ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (k + 1),
              ((M : ℂ) * z + w + ((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ))‖) ∧
        HasSum
          (fun k : ℕ =>
            b (k + 1) /
              ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (k + 1),
                ((M : ℂ) * z + w + ((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ)))
          (f z - b 0)

Watson's lemma for real Laplace integrals: an all-orders right-hand expansion of `g`
at zero with coefficients `c` integrates termwise against `Real.exp (-m * ·)` over
`(0, ∞)`, leaving a `1 / m ^ (N + 2)` remainder for every truncation order `N`.

Grounded record: `jis_grounded_f44808e9542400b9602c4bfc`
Concept: `jis_dep_4b8d33719e173348274b207f`
Source: `https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL14/Nemes/nemes4.tex`, lines 142-151
File SHA-256: `4420f4c929622a46f0e5623054b7cc4a699802cfb111b4dce5d1922af1e4c1d7`
Span SHA-256: `30a175909268f0c6c372ad6dba97f6edb373a35cf7eb26ecb5a0c0212eec8ee6`
Counts: 2 mentions / 1 paper / 1 proof use.

signature: ∀ (g : ℝ → ℝ) (c : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ (N : ℕ), (fun s ↦ g s - ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, c (k + 1) * s ^ (k + 1)) =O[nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)] fun s ↦ s ^ (N + 1)) → (∃ m₀, ∀ m ≥ m₀, MeasureTheory.IntegrableOn (fun s ↦ g s * Real.exp (-m * s)) (Set.Ioi 0) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume) → ∀ (N : ℕ), (fun m ↦ (∫ (s : ℝ) in Set.Ioi 0, g s * Real.exp (-m * s)) - ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, ↑(k + 1).factorial * c (k + 1) / m ^ (k + 2)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun m ↦ 1 / m ^ (N + 2)

  (g : ℝ → ℝ) (c : ℕ → ℝ)
  (hlocal : ∀ N : ℕ, Asymptotics.IsBigO (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0))

Weyl's equidistribution criterion (statement `weyl-criterion-s1`):
a real sequence `x` is equidistributed mod 1 iff every nontrivial Fourier mean
vanishes. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equidistribution_theorem.

signature: ∀ (x : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ (a b : ℝ), 0 ≤ a → a < b → b ≤ 1 → Filter.Tendsto (fun N ↦ ↑{n ∈ Finset.range N | a ≤ Int.fract (x n) ∧ Int.fract (x n) < b}.card / ↑N) Filter.atTop (nhds (b - a))) ↔ ∀ (h : ℤ), h ≠ 0 → Filter.Tendsto (fun N ↦ 1 / ↑N * ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, Complex.exp (↑(2 * Real.pi * ↑h * x n) * Complex.I)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
statement:
public theorem weyl_criterion (x : ℕ → ℝ) :
    (∀ a b : ℝ, 0 ≤ a → a < b → b ≤ 1 →
      Tendsto (fun N : ℕ =>
        ((Finset.filter (fun n => a ≤ Int.fract (x n) ∧ Int.fract (x n) < b)
          (Finset.range N)).card : ℝ) / (N : ℝ))

docstring:
Wintner mean-value theorem for arithmetic functions, one-variable case:
under absolute convergence of `Σ |(μ * f) n| / n`, the Cesàro mean
`x⁻¹ * Σ_{n ∈ [1, x]} f n` tends to `Σ' (μ * f) n / n`, where `μ * f` is the
Dirichlet convolution of the Möbius function with `f`.

Source: László Tóth, *On the Asymptotic Density of k-tuples of Positive
Integers with Pairwise Non-Coprime Components*, Journal of Integer Sequences
27 (2024), Article 24.8.5, mean-value definition and Theorem `Th_Wintner_gen`,
lines 292–310 (the `k = 1` case identified at lines 297–298 as Wintner's
classical theorem; the source theorem itself is Ushiroya's multivariable
generalization),
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL27/Toth/toth27.tex>.

Math notes: no multiplicativity, Euler product, quantitative error term, or
alternating mean is assumed or concluded.
Proves `Wanted` entry `wintner_mean_value`.

signature: ∀ (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ), (Summable fun n ↦ ‖(↑ArithmeticFunction.moebius * f) n‖ / ↑n) → Filter.Tendsto (fun x ↦ (↑x)⁻¹ * ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 x, f n) Filter.atTop (nhds (∑' (n : ℕ), (↑ArithmeticFunction.moebius * f) n / ↑n))
statement:
theorem wintner_mean_value (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ)
    (hsum : Summable
      (fun n : ℕ => ‖((↑ArithmeticFunction.moebius : ArithmeticFunction ℂ) * f) n‖ /
        (n : ℝ))) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => ((x : ℂ)⁻¹) * ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 x, f n) Filter.atTop
    (nhds (∑' n : ℕ, ((↑ArithmeticFunction.moebius : ArithmeticFunction ℂ) * f) n /
      (n : ℂ)))

docstring:
Wintner's mean-value theorem for arithmetic functions of several variables.

Source: László Tóth,
"On the Asymptotic Density of k-tuples of Positive Integers with Pairwise Non-Coprime Components,"
Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.8.5,
Theorem `Th_Wintner_gen`, lines 300–311,
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL27/Toth/toth27.tex>.
Proved by H. Ushiroya (2012) as a generalization of Wintner's classical one-variable theorem.

Math notes: `mobiusConvolution` is the Dirichlet convolution `μ * f` over divisor tuples;
the hypothesis is absolute convergence of `Σ |(μ*f)(m)| / (m_1 ⋯ m_k)`, and the conclusion
is convergence of the rectangular mean to the corresponding infinite sum.

Proves `Wanted` entry `wintner_mean_value_multivariable`.
name: MetaMathlibExt.wintner_mean_value_multivariable
signature:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  0 < k →
    ∀ (f : (Fin k → ℕ) → ℂ),
      have mobiusConvolution := fun n ↦ ∑ d, if ∀ (i : Fin k), ↑(d i) + 1 ∣ n i then (∏ i, ↑(ArithmeticFunction.moebius (↑(d i) + 1))) * f fun i ↦ n i / (↑(d i) + 1) else 0;
      (Summable fun m ↦ ‖mobiusConvolution fun i ↦ m i + 1‖ / ∏ i, (↑(m i) + 1)) → Filter.Tendsto (fun x ↦ (∑ n, f fun i ↦ ↑(n i) + 1) / ∏ i, ↑(x i)) Filter.atTop (nhds (∑' (m : Fin k → ℕ), (mobiusConvolution fun i ↦ m i + 1) / ∏ i, (↑(m i) + 1)))
statement:
theorem wintner_mean_value_multivariable
    (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) (f : (Fin k → ℕ) → ℂ) :
    let mobiusConvolution : (Fin k → ℕ) → ℂ := (fun n =>
      ∑ d : (i : Fin k) → Fin (n i),
        if ∀ i, (d i : ℕ) + 1 ∣ n i then
          (∏ i, (ArithmeticFunction.moebius ((d i : ℕ) + 1) : ℂ)) *
            f (fun i => n i / ((d i : ℕ) + 1))
        else 0);
    Summable (fun m : Fin k → ℕ =>
      ‖mobiusConvolution (fun i => m i + 1)‖ /
        ∏ i, (m i + 1 : ℝ)) →
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun x : Fin k → ℕ =>
          (∑ n : (i : Fin k) → Fin (x i), f (fun i => (n i : ℕ) + 1)) /
            ∏ i, (x i : ℂ))
        Filter.atTop
        (nhds (∑' m : Fin k → ℕ,
          mobiusConvolution (fun i => m i + 1) /
            ∏ i, (m i + 1 : ℂ)))

docstring:
Wirtinger's inequality for functions: a C1 function on `[0, π]` vanishing at the endpoints
satisfies `∫₀^π f² ≤ ∫₀^π (f')²`.

Source: G. H. Hardy, J. E. Littlewood, and G. Pólya, *Inequalities*, second edition,
Cambridge University Press, 1952, §7.7 (the endpoint-zero form on `[0, L]`).

Proves `Wanted` entry `wirtinger_inequality`.

Proof: A Picone-type comparison. For `0 < c < 1` the weight `h x = -c * tan (c * (x - π / 2))` is
smooth on `[0, π]` with `h' + h ^ 2 = -c ^ 2`, so integrating
`f' ^ 2 = (f' - h * f) ^ 2 + (h * f ^ 2)' + c ^ 2 * f ^ 2` gives `c ^ 2 * ∫ f ^ 2 ≤ ∫ f' ^ 2`;
then let `c` tend to one.
name: MetaMathlibExt.wirtinger_inequality
signature: ∀ (f f' : ℝ → ℝ), (∀ x ∈ Set.Icc 0 Real.pi, HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (Set.Icc 0 Real.pi) x) → ContinuousOn f' (Set.Icc 0 Real.pi) → f 0 = 0 → f Real.pi = 0 → ∫ (x : ℝ) in 0..Real.pi, f x ^ 2 ≤ ∫ (x : ℝ) in 0..Real.pi, f' x ^ 2
statement:
public theorem wirtinger_inequality (f f' : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hf_deriv : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) Real.pi,
      HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (Set.Icc 0 Real.pi) x)
    (hf_deriv_cont : ContinuousOn f' (Set.Icc 0 Real.pi))
    (h0 : f 0 = 0) (hpi : f Real.pi = 0) :
    intervalIntegral (fun x => (f x) ^ 2) 0 Real.pi MeasureTheory.volume ≤
      intervalIntegral (fun x => (f' x) ^ 2) 0 Real.pi MeasureTheory.volume

docstring:
Witt's multigraded value `M(n₁, …, nᵣ)`: let `n` be the sum of all entries
of `degree` and `g` their finite gcd; `M` is `(1/n)` times the sum over
positive `d` dividing `g` of `μ(d)` times the multinomial coefficient for
`i ↦ degree i / d` (`ArithmeticFunction.moebius` and `Nat.multinomial`,
coerced into `ℚ`); the `n = 0` boundary is `0`.

Source: Pieter Moree, *Convoluted Convolved Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of
Integer Sequences 7 (2004), Article 04.2.2, equations `witty`/`basaal`,
lines 598–613 (Möbius inversion of the circular-word count; context
*Circular words and Witt's dimension formula*, lines 574–597),
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL7/Moree/moree12.tex>.

lines 621–628,

docstring:
For odd `ν ≥ 1` and prime `p ≥ ν + 4`, the `ν`-th harmonic power sum through
`p - 1` vanishes modulo `p²`. Inverses are taken in `ZMod (p ^ 2)`, where every
`t < p` is a unit.

Source: Christian Ballot, "On a Congruence of Kimball and Webb Involving Lucas
Sequences," Journal of Integer Sequences 17 (2014), Article 14.1.3,
Theorem (label thm:L), lines 94–99,
https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL17/Ballot/ballot7.tex

The source notes there (lines 108–111) that this is Theorem 131 of Hardy and
Wright, a generalization of the 1862 Wolstenholme congruence, first studied by
Leudesdorf.

docstring:
Factor complexity of an infinite word `w` over a finite alphabet:
the complexity function `p_w(n)`, the number of distinct contiguous factors
of `w` of length `n`, where a length-`n` factor starting at `i` is
`fun j : Fin n => w (i + j)`. The image set collapses repeated occurrences,
so `Set.ncard` of the range counts distinct factors rather than occurrences.

Source: Fabien Durand, Julien Leroy, and Gwenaël Richomme, *Do the
Properties of an S-adic Representation Determine Factor Complexity?*,
Journal of Integer Sequences 16 (2013), Article 13.2.6, complexity-function
definition, lines 117–128,
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL16/Durand/durand2.tex>.

docstring:
Worpitzky identity for multiset Eulerian numbers: for nonnegative integers
`k` over `Fin m` with total `K`, `∏ i, C (x + k i - 1) (k i)` equals
`∑ p, C (x + K - p) K * a p` where `a p` counts permutations of the multiset
`1 ^ (k 1) ⋯ m ^ (k m)` with `p - 1` descents (summed over
`Finset.Icc 1 (max 1 K)`).

Source: A. Dzhumadil'daev and D. Yeliussizov, *Power Sums of Binomial
Coefficients*, Journal of Integer Sequences 16 (2013), Article 13.1.4, Theorem
Worpitzky, lines 212-217,
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL16/Yeliussizov/dzhuma6.tex>, quoting
A. S. Dzhumadil'daev, *Worpitzky identity for multipermutations*, Mat. Zametki
90 (2011), 464-466.

Proves `Wanted` entry `worpitzky_identity_multiset`.
name: MetaMathlibExt.worpitzky_identity_multiset
signature: ∀ (m : ℕ) (k : Fin m → ℕ) (x : ℕ), ∏ i, (x + k i - 1).choose (k i) = ∑ p ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Max.max 1 (∑ a, k a)), (x + ∑ a, k a - p).choose (∑ a, k a) * Nat.card { w // (∀ (i : Fin m), Fintype.card { j // w j = i } = k i) ∧ {j | ∃ (h : ↑j + 1 < ∑ a, k a), w j > w ⟨↑j + 1, h⟩}.card + 1 = p }
statement:
theorem worpitzky_identity_multiset (m : ℕ) (k : Fin m → ℕ) (x : ℕ) :
    Finset.prod Finset.univ (fun i => Nat.choose (x + k i - 1) (k i)) =
      Finset.sum (Finset.Icc 1 (max 1 (Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun a => k a)))) (fun p =>
        Nat.choose (x + Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun a => k a) - p)
            (Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun a => k a)) *
          Nat.card { w : Fin (Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun a => k a)) → Fin m //
            (∀ i,
              Fintype.card
                  { j : Fin (Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun a => k a)) // w j = i } = k i) ∧
            (Finset.univ.filter
                (fun j : Fin (Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun a => k a)) =>
                  ∃ h : j.val + 1 < Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun a => k a),
                    w j > w ⟨j.val + 1, h⟩)).card + 1 = p })

docstring:
Carry recurrence for reverse multiples: a `(g, k)` reverse multiple in
little-endian base-`g` digits holds exactly when there is a unique carry
sequence `r` with `r 0 = 0`, `r n = 0`, every carry below `k`, and the column
equations `k * a i + r i = a (n - 1 - i) + r (i + 1) * g`; `r (i + 1)` is the
source's `r_i`. The Young graph `H(g, k)`, its paths and the even/odd pivot-node
correspondence of Young's theorem (`thm:youngsthm`, lines 192–196) are not
formalized here.

Source: L. H. Kendrick, *Young Graphs: 1089 et al.*, Journal of Integer
Sequences 18 (2015), Article 15.9.7, subsection `subsec:eqtns`, lines 128–154
(the column equations for `kN = Reverse_g(N)`, Young's bound `r_i ≤ k - 1`,
and equation `eq:rmdig`),
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL18/Kendrick/ken1.tex>.
It follows from `young_reverse_multiple_carry_path_iff_general`; the hypotheses `hfirst` and `hlast`
(and `hn`, which only serves to state them) are unused and keep the source's shape.
Proves `Wanted` entry `young_reverse_multiple_carry_path_iff`.
name: MetaMathlibExt.young_reverse_multiple_carry_path_iff
signature: ∀ (g k n : ℕ), 2 ≤ k → k < g → ∀ (hn : 0 < n) (a : Fin n → ℕ), (∀ (i : Fin n), a i < g) → a ⟨0, hn⟩.rev ≠ 0 → a ⟨0, hn⟩ ≠ 0 → (k * ∑ i, a i * g ^ ↑i = ∑ i, a i.rev * g ^ ↑i ↔ ∃! r, r ⟨0, ⋯⟩ = 0 ∧ r (Fin.last n) = 0 ∧ ∀ (i : Fin n), r i.succ < k ∧ k * a i + r i.castSucc = a i.rev + r i.succ * g)
statement:
theorem young_reverse_multiple_carry_path_iff
    (g k n : ℕ) (hgk : 2 ≤ k) (hkg : k < g) (hn : 0 < n)
    (a : Fin n → ℕ) (hdigit : ∀ i, a i < g)
    (hfirst : a (Fin.rev ⟨0, hn⟩) ≠ 0) (hlast : a ⟨0, hn⟩ ≠ 0) :
    k * (∑ i, a i * g ^ i.val) = ∑ i, a (Fin.rev i) * g ^ i.val ↔
      ∃! r : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ,
        r ⟨0, Nat.succ_pos n⟩ = 0 ∧ r (Fin.last n) = 0 ∧
          ∀ i : Fin n, r i.succ < k ∧
            k * a i + r i.castSucc = a (Fin.rev i) + r i.succ * g

docstring:
Carry recurrence for reverse multiples, with only the hypotheses the
argument uses: for `2 ≤ k < g` and little-endian base-`g` digits `a`, `k` times the number equals
its digit reversal exactly when there is a unique carry sequence `r` with `r 0 = 0`, `r n = 0`,
every carry below `k`, and the column equations. The digit length may be `0` and the end digits
may vanish. `young_reverse_multiple_carry_path_iff` is the source-shaped form.
name: MetaMathlibExt.young_reverse_multiple_carry_path_iff_general
signature: ∀ (g k n : ℕ), 2 ≤ k → k < g → ∀ (a : Fin n → ℕ), (∀ (i : Fin n), a i < g) → (k * ∑ i, a i * g ^ ↑i = ∑ i, a i.rev * g ^ ↑i ↔ ∃! r, r ⟨0, ⋯⟩ = 0 ∧ r (Fin.last n) = 0 ∧ ∀ (i : Fin n), r i.succ < k ∧ k * a i + r i.castSucc = a i.rev + r i.succ * g)
statement:
theorem young_reverse_multiple_carry_path_iff_general
    (g k n : ℕ) (hgk : 2 ≤ k) (hkg : k < g)
    (a : Fin n → ℕ) (hdigit : ∀ i, a i < g) :
    k * (∑ i, a i * g ^ i.val) = ∑ i, a (Fin.rev i) * g ^ i.val ↔
      ∃! r : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ,
        r ⟨0, Nat.succ_pos n⟩ = 0 ∧ r (Fin.last n) = 0 ∧
          ∀ i : Fin n, r i.succ < k ∧
            k * a i + r i.castSucc = a (Fin.rev i) + r i.succ * g

docstring:
Young's correspondence between reverse multiples and paths in the associated Young graph,
including the edge-label reconstruction of the digits in the even- and odd-length cases:
`(g, k)` reverse multiples with an even (respectively odd) number of base-`g` digits
correspond bijectively to paths from the starting node to even (respectively odd) pivot
nodes, with digits read off edge labels.

Source: L. H. Kendrick, *Young Graphs: 1089 et al.*, Journal of Integer Sequences 18
(2015), Article 15.9.7, Theorem [Young's Theorem], lines 192-197,
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL18/Kendrick/ken1.tex>, after Theorems 1 and 2
of Young's first paper on reverse multiples.

Proves `Wanted` entry `young_reverse_multiples_equiv_pivot_paths`.
name: MetaMathlibExt.young_reverse_multiples_equiv_pivot_paths
statement:
theorem young_reverse_multiples_equiv_pivot_paths
    (g k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hkg : k < g) :
    let digitValue := fun digits : List ℕ =>
      digits.foldl (fun value digit => value * g + digit) 0
    let IsReverseMultiple := fun digits : List ℕ =>
      (∃ first middle last,
          digits = first :: middle ++ [last] ∧ first ≠ 0 ∧ last ≠ 0) ∧
        (∀ digit ∈ digits, digit < g) ∧
        k * digitValue digits = digitValue digits.reverse
    let Transition := fun (source : ℕ × ℕ) (label : ℕ × ℕ) (target : ℕ × ℕ) =>
      k * label.2 + source.2 = label.1 + target.2 * g ∧
        k * label.1 + target.1 = label.2 + source.1 * g
    let IsPath := fun path : List (ℕ × ℕ) × List (ℕ × ℕ) =>
      path.2.length = path.1.length + 1 ∧
        path.2.head? = some (0, 0) ∧
        (∀ node ∈ path.2, node.1 < k ∧ node.2 < k) ∧
        (∀ label ∈ path.1, label.1 < g ∧ label.2 < g) ∧
        (∃ first rest,
          path.1 = first :: rest ∧ first.1 ≠ 0 ∧ first.2 ≠ 0) ∧
        List.Forall₂
          (fun label endpoints => Transition endpoints.1 label endpoints.2)
          path.1 (path.2.zip path.2.tail)
    let EvenReverseMultiples :=
      {digits : List ℕ // IsReverseMultiple digits ∧ Even digits.length}
    let OddReverseMultiples :=
      {digits : List ℕ // IsReverseMultiple digits ∧ Odd digits.length}
    let PathsToEvenPivots :=
      {path : List (ℕ × ℕ) × List (ℕ × ℕ) //
        IsPath path ∧ ∃ r, path.2.getLast? = some (r, r)}
    let PathsToOddPivots :=
      {path : List (ℕ × ℕ) × List (ℕ × ℕ) //
        IsPath path ∧
          ∃ r s middle,
            path.2.getLast? = some (r, s) ∧ middle < g ∧
              Transition (r, s) (middle, middle) (s, r)}
    ∃ evenCorrespondence : EvenReverseMultiples ≃ PathsToEvenPivots,
      ∃ oddCorrespondence : OddReverseMultiples ≃ PathsToOddPivots,
        (∀ reverseMultiple,
          (evenCorrespondence reverseMultiple).1.1 =
            List.zip
              (reverseMultiple.1.take (reverseMultiple.1.length / 2))
              (reverseMultiple.1.reverse.take (reverseMultiple.1.length / 2))) ∧
        (∀ reverseMultiple,
          (oddCorrespondence reverseMultiple).1.1 =
              List.zip
                (reverseMultiple.1.take (reverseMultiple.1.length / 2))
                (reverseMultiple.1.reverse.take (reverseMultiple.1.length / 2)) ∧
            ∃ middle r s,
              (reverseMultiple.1.drop (reverseMultiple.1.length / 2)).head? =
                some middle ∧
              (oddCorrespondence reverseMultiple).1.2.getLast? = some (r, s) ∧
              Transition (r, s) (middle, middle) (s, r))

name: MetaMathlibExt.zagier_matrix_inverse
statement:
public theorem zagier_matrix_inverse (K : ℕ) (hK : 1 < K) :
    (Matrix.of (fun i j : Fin (K - 1) =>
        (2 : ℚ) / (2 * (↑(i.val + 1) : ℚ) - 1) *
          ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (2 * K - 2 * (i.val + 1) + 1),
            (↑(Nat.choose (2 * (j.val + 1) - 1)
              (2 * K - 2 * (i.val + 1) - n + 1)) : ℚ) *
              (↑(Nat.choose (n + 2 * (i.val + 1) - 2) n) : ℚ) * bernoulli n) :
      Matrix (Fin (K - 1)) (Fin (K - 1)) ℚ)
    =
    (Matrix.of (fun i j : Fin (K - 1) =>
        (-2 : ℚ) / (2 * (↑(i.val + 1) : ℚ) - 1) *
          ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (2 * K - 2 * (i.val + 1) + 1),
            (↑(Nat.choose (2 * K - 2 * (j.val + 1))
              (2 * K - 2 * (i.val + 1) - n + 1)) : ℚ) *
              (↑(Nat.choose (n + 2 * (i.val + 1) - 2) n) : ℚ) * bernoulli n) :
      Matrix (Fin (K - 1)) (Fin (K - 1)) ℚ)
    ∧ (Matrix.of (fun i j : Fin (K - 1) =>
        (↑(Nat.choose (2 * K - 2 * (j.val + 1)) (2 * (i.val + 1) - 1)) : ℚ) +
          (↑(Nat.choose (2 * K - 2 * (j.val + 1)) (2 * K - 2 * (i.val + 1))) : ℚ)) :
      Matrix (Fin (K - 1)) (Fin (K - 1)) ℚ)
    * (Matrix.of (fun i j : Fin (K - 1) =>
        (2 : ℚ) / (2 * (↑(i.val + 1) : ℚ) - 1) *
          ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (2 * K - 2 * (i.val + 1) + 1),
            (↑(Nat.choose (2 * (j.val + 1) - 1)
              (2 * K - 2 * (i.val + 1) - n + 1)) : ℚ) *
              (↑(Nat.choose (n + 2 * (i.val + 1) - 2) n) : ℚ) * bernoulli n) :
      Matrix (Fin (K - 1)) (Fin (K - 1)) ℚ)
    = 1
    ∧ (Matrix.of (fun i j : Fin (K - 1) =>
        (2 : ℚ) / (2 * (↑(i.val + 1) : ℚ) - 1) *
          ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (2 * K - 2 * (i.val + 1) + 1),
            (↑(Nat.choose (2 * (j.val + 1) - 1)
              (2 * K - 2 * (i.val + 1) - n + 1)) : ℚ) *
              (↑(Nat.choose (n + 2 * (i.val + 1) - 2) n) : ℚ) * bernoulli n) :
      Matrix (Fin (K - 1)) (Fin (K - 1)) ℚ)
    * (Matrix.of (fun i j : Fin (K - 1) =>
        (↑(Nat.choose (2 * K - 2 * (j.val + 1)) (2 * (i.val + 1) - 1)) : ℚ) +
          (↑(Nat.choose (2 * K - 2 * (j.val + 1)) (2 * K - 2 * (i.val + 1))) : ℚ)) :
      Matrix (Fin (K - 1)) (Fin (K - 1)) ℚ)
    = 1

docstring:
Zagier's formula for the probability that the product of two uniformly chosen cyclic
permutations of `Fin n` has exactly `k` cycles:
`(1 + (-1) ^ (n - k)) / Nat.factorial (n + 1) * Nat.stirlingFirst (n + 1) k`.
Cyclicity is encoded as cycle-type-plus-fixed-points count equal to one.

Source: R. Cori and G. Hetyei, *On Reduced Unicellular Hypermonopoles*, Journal of
Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.3.3, Theorem [Zagier], lines 351-359,
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL28/Hetyei/hetyei2.tex>, quoting D. Zagier.

Proof: We formalize the plane-permutation transposition and reflection bijections of
Chen and Reidys, arXiv:1502.07674, lines 786-1074, and their specialization to Zagier's
recurrence, lines 1167-1370. A generating-polynomial coefficient identity supplies the
matching Stirling recurrence; descending induction on the cycle count finishes.

name: MetaMathlibExt.zagier_probability_product_two_cyclic_permutations
signature: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 0 < n → 0 < k → k ≤ n → ↑(Fintype.card { p // p.1.cycleType.card + Fintype.card ↑(Function.fixedPoints ⇑p.1) = 1 ∧ p.2.cycleType.card + Fintype.card ↑(Function.fixedPoints ⇑p.2) = 1 ∧ (p.1 * p.2).cycleType.card + Fintype.card ↑(Function.fixedPoints ⇑(p.1 * p.2)) = k }) / ↑(Fintype.card { σ // σ.cycleType.card + Fintype.card ↑(Function.fixedPoints ⇑σ) = 1 }) ^ 2 = (1 + (-1) ^ (n - k)) / ↑(n + 1).factorial * ↑((n + 1).stirlingFirst k)
statement:
public theorem zagier_probability_product_two_cyclic_permutations
    (n k : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hk : 0 < k) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    ((Fintype.card {p : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) × Equiv.Perm (Fin n) //
        Multiset.card p.1.cycleType + Fintype.card (Function.fixedPoints p.1) = 1 ∧
        Multiset.card p.2.cycleType + Fintype.card (Function.fixedPoints p.2) = 1 ∧
        Multiset.card (p.1 * p.2).cycleType +
            Fintype.card (Function.fixedPoints (p.1 * p.2)) = k}) : ℚ) /
      ((Fintype.card {σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) //
          Multiset.card σ.cycleType + Fintype.card (Function.fixedPoints σ) = 1}) : ℚ) ^ 2 =
      (1 + (-1 : ℚ) ^ (n - k)) / Nat.factorial (n + 1) *
        Nat.stirlingFirst (n + 1) k

docstring:
Zeilberger's lemma: extraction of `gamma k` from `h_n (x * c(x)^2) / c(x)^n`,
where `c` is the Catalan generating function.

Provenance: Paul Barry, "The γ-Vectors of Pascal-like Triangles Defined by
Riordan Arrays", Journal of Integer Sequences 22 (2019), Article 19.1.4,
Zeilberger's Lemma proposition lines 281–283,
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL22/Barry2/barry402.tex>.
The gamma-matrix setup and `h` notation use supporting lines 110–120; the
Catalan generating function `c(x) = (1 - sqrt (1 - 4 * x)) / (2 * x)` has
coefficients `C_n = (1 / (n + 1)) * choose (2 * n) n` (A000108).
The malformed recalled display at source line 275 printing `gamma_n` on both
sides is excluded; the correctly printed proposition with `h_n` on the left
is formalized.

name: MetaMathlibExt.zeilberger_gamma_coefficient
signature:
∀ (n k : ℕ) (h : Polynomial ℚ) (gamma : ℕ → ℚ),
  k ≤ n / 2 →
    h = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n / 2 + 1), Polynomial.C (gamma j) * Polynomial.X ^ j * (1 + Polynomial.X) ^ (n - 2 * j) →
      have C := (PowerSeries.map (Nat.castRingHom ℚ)) PowerSeries.catalanSeries;
      gamma k = (PowerSeries.coeff k) ((Polynomial.aeval (PowerSeries.X * C ^ 2)) h * (C ^ n)⁻¹)
statement:
theorem zeilberger_gamma_coefficient
    (n k : ℕ) (h : Polynomial ℚ) (gamma : ℕ → ℚ)
    (hk : k ≤ n / 2)
    (hgamma :
      h = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n / 2 + 1),
        Polynomial.C (gamma j) * Polynomial.X ^ j *
          (1 + Polynomial.X) ^ (n - 2 * j)) :
    let C : PowerSeries ℚ :=
      PowerSeries.map (Nat.castRingHom ℚ) PowerSeries.catalanSeries
    gamma k =
      PowerSeries.coeff k
        ((Polynomial.aeval (PowerSeries.X * C ^ 2) h) * (C ^ n)⁻¹)

statement:
public theorem zeta_three_infinite_product_formulas :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun m : ℕ =>
        ∏ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (2 * m + 1),
          (1 / Real.rpow (Real.exp 1) (1 / 4)) *
            (1 - 1 / ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) ^
              (((n * (n + 1) / 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) * (-1 : ℤ) ^ n))
      Filter.atTop
      (nhds (Real.exp (7 * (riemannZeta (3 : ℂ)).re / (4 * Real.pi ^ 2) + 1 / 4))) ∧
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun m : ℕ =>
        ∏ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (2 * m),
          Real.rpow (Real.exp 1) (1 / 4) *
            (1 - 1 / ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) ^
              (((n * (n + 1) / 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) * (-1 : ℤ) ^ n))
      Filter.atTop
      (nhds (Real.exp (7 * (riemannZeta (3 : ℂ)).re / (4 * Real.pi ^ 2) - 1 / 4))) ∧
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun m : ℕ =>
        ((∏ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m,
            (((2 * n : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ ((2 * n : ℕ) ^ 2))) /
          (∏ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m,
            (((2 * n - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ ((2 * n - 1 : ℕ) ^ 2)))) ^ 4 *
        ((((2 * m + 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (4 * m + 5)) /
          (((2 * m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (12 * m + 9))) ^ m)
      Filter.atTop

docstring: An endomorphism with split characteristic polynomial has a Jordan-chain basis.
name: Module.End.exists_jordanBasis_of_charpoly_splits
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] {V : Type v} [inst_1 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_2 : _root_.Module K V] [inst_3 : FiniteDimensional K V] (f : Module.End K V), (LinearMap.charpoly f).Splits → ∃ k d μ b, (∀ (i : Fin k), f (b ⟨i, 0⟩) = μ i • b ⟨i, 0⟩) ∧ (∀ (i : Fin k) (j : Fin (d i)), f (b ⟨i, j.succ⟩) = μ i • b ⟨i, j.succ⟩ + b ⟨i, j.castSucc⟩) ∧ (LinearMap.toMatrix b b) f = Matrix.blockDiagonal' fun i ↦ MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.JordanNormalFormWanted.jordanBlock (d i + 1) (μ i)
statement:
theorem exists_jordanBasis_of_charpoly_splits
    {V : Type v} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V]
    (f : Module.End K V) (hf : f.charpoly.Splits) :
    ∃ (k : ℕ) (d : Fin k → ℕ) (μ : Fin k → K)
      (b : Basis (Σ i, Fin (d i + 1)) K V),
      (∀ i, f (b ⟨i, 0⟩) = μ i • b ⟨i, 0⟩) ∧
      (∀ i (j : Fin (d i)),
        f (b ⟨i, j.succ⟩) = μ i • b ⟨i, j.succ⟩ + b ⟨i, j.castSucc⟩) ∧
      LinearMap.toMatrix b b f =
        Matrix.blockDiagonal' (fun i ↦ jordanBlock (d i + 1) (μ i))

docstring: A nilpotent endomorphism has a basis made of Jordan chains.
name: Module.End.exists_jordanBasis_of_isNilpotent
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] {V : Type v} [inst_1 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_2 : _root_.Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (f : Module.End K V), IsNilpotent f → ∃ k d b, (∀ (i : Fin k), f (b ⟨i, 0⟩) = 0) ∧ (∀ (i : Fin k) (j : Fin (d i)), f (b ⟨i, j.succ⟩) = b ⟨i, j.castSucc⟩) ∧ (LinearMap.toMatrix b b) f = Matrix.blockDiagonal' fun i ↦ MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.JordanNormalFormWanted.jordanBlock (d i + 1) 0
statement:
theorem exists_jordanBasis_of_isNilpotent
    {V : Type v} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V]
    (f : Module.End K V) (hf : IsNilpotent f) :
    ∃ (k : ℕ) (d : Fin k → ℕ) (b : Basis (Σ i, Fin (d i + 1)) K V),
      (∀ i, f (b ⟨i, 0⟩) = 0) ∧
      (∀ i (j : Fin (d i)), f (b ⟨i, j.succ⟩) = b ⟨i, j.castSucc⟩) ∧
      LinearMap.toMatrix b b f =
        Matrix.blockDiagonal' (fun i ↦ jordanBlock (d i + 1) 0)

docstring:
`χ` is a Dirichlet character of modulus `q`: it is `q`-periodic and its
nonvanishing locus is exactly the set of integers coprime to `q`.
name: MonoidHom.IsDirichletCharacterModulus
signature: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : MonoidWithZero R] → (ℤ →* R) → ℕ → Prop
statement: def IsDirichletCharacterModulus (χ : ℤ →* R) (q : ℕ) : Prop

docstring:
ATLAS `NumberTheoryI` Lemma 18.8: `χ` with least positive period `m` is a
Dirichlet character of modulus `m'` iff `m ∣ m'` and `m' ∣ m ^ k` for some `k`.
Forward: minimality gives the divisibility, and a prime divisor of `m'` divides
`m` (else `χ p` is simultaneously zero and nonzero).  Backward: periodicity
lifts along `m ∣ m'`, and the nonvanishing locus transfers via the two lemmas
above.  The `Nontrivial R` hypothesis is sharp: the subsingleton monoid with zero
satisfies the remaining typeclasses while forcing every `χ n = 0`, which
falsifies the claimed nonvanishing locus.
name: MonoidHom.isDirichletCharacterModulus_iff
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : MonoidWithZero R] {χ : ℤ →* R} [Nontrivial R] [IsCancelMulZero R] {m m' : ℕ}, 0 < m → Function.Periodic ⇑χ ↑m → (∀ (d : ℕ), 0 < d → Function.Periodic ⇑χ ↑d → m ≤ d) → 0 < m' → (χ.IsDirichletCharacterModulus m' ↔ m ∣ m' ∧ ∃ k, m' ∣ m ^ k)
statement:
theorem isDirichletCharacterModulus_iff {χ : ℤ →* R} [Nontrivial R]
    [IsCancelMulZero R] {m m' : ℕ}
    (hm : 0 < m)
    (hper : Function.Periodic χ (m : ℤ))
    (hmin : ∀ d : ℕ, 0 < d → Function.Periodic χ (d : ℤ) → m ≤ d)
    (hm' : 0 < m') :
    χ.IsDirichletCharacterModulus m' ↔ m ∣ m' ∧ ∃ k : ℕ, m' ∣ m ^ k

docstring: `χ` is a Dirichlet character of its own least period `m`.
name: MonoidHom.isDirichletCharacterModulus_self
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : MonoidWithZero R] {χ : ℤ →* R} [Nontrivial R] [IsCancelMulZero R] {m : ℕ}, 0 < m → Function.Periodic ⇑χ ↑m → (∀ (d : ℕ), 0 < d → Function.Periodic ⇑χ ↑d → m ≤ d) → χ.IsDirichletCharacterModulus m
statement:
theorem isDirichletCharacterModulus_self {χ : ℤ →* R} [Nontrivial R]
    [IsCancelMulZero R] {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m)
    (hper : Function.Periodic χ (m : ℤ))
    (hmin : ∀ d : ℕ, 0 < d → Function.Periodic χ (d : ℤ) → m ≤ d) :
    χ.IsDirichletCharacterModulus m

docstring:
Burnside's orbit count when every nonidentity group element has the same
finite number of fixed points.
name: MulAction.card_add_mul_card_sub_one_eq_card_orbits_mul_card
signature: ∀ (G : Type u_1) (X : Type u_2) [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : MulAction G X] [Finite G] [Finite X] (c : ℕ), (∀ (g : G), g ≠ 1 → Nat.card ↑(MulAction.fixedBy X g) = c) → Nat.card X + c * (Nat.card G - 1) = Nat.card (MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient G X) * Nat.card G
statement:
theorem _root_.MulAction.card_add_mul_card_sub_one_eq_card_orbits_mul_card
    (G X : Type*) [Group G] [MulAction G X] [Finite G] [Finite X]
    (c : ℕ) (hfixed : ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → Nat.card (MulAction.fixedBy X g) = c) :
    Nat.card X + c * (Nat.card G - 1) =
      Nat.card (MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient G X) * Nat.card G

docstring: A multigraph described by a symmetric edge-multiplicity function. Loops are permitted.
name: Multigraph
signature: Type u_1 → Type u_1
statement: structure Multigraph (V : Type*)

docstring: Adjacency in a multigraph means positive edge multiplicity.
name: Multigraph.Adj
signature: {V : Type u_1} → Multigraph V → V → V → Prop
statement: def Adj (G : Multigraph V) (v w : V) : Prop

docstring: Connectivity via reflexive-transitive closure.
name: Multigraph.Connected
signature: {V : Type u_1} → Multigraph V → V → V → Prop
statement: def Connected (G : Multigraph V) (v w : V) : Prop

docstring: A multigraph is connected when all pairs connect.
name: Multigraph.IsConnected
signature: {V : Type u_1} → Multigraph V → Prop
statement: def IsConnected (G : Multigraph V) : Prop

docstring: Adjacency is symmetric.
name: Multigraph.adj_comm
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} (G : Multigraph V) (v w : V), G.Adj v w ↔ G.Adj w v
statement:
theorem adj_comm (G : Multigraph V) (v w : V) :
    G.Adj v w ↔ G.Adj w v

docstring: Every vertex connects to itself.
name: Multigraph.connected_refl
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} (G : Multigraph V) (v : V), G.Connected v v
statement:
theorem connected_refl (G : Multigraph V) (v : V) :
    G.Connected v v

docstring:
The outgoing degree of a vertex. A loop contributes its multiplicity once, matching the
outgoing-isogeny convention.
name: Multigraph.degree
signature: {V : Type u_1} → Multigraph V → [Fintype V] → V → ℕ
statement: def degree (G : Multigraph V) [Fintype V] (v : V) : ℕ

docstring: Degree restricted to vertices satisfying `P`.
name: Multigraph.degreeOn
signature: {V : Type u_1} → Multigraph V → [Fintype V] → V → (P : V → Prop) → [DecidablePred P] → ℕ
statement:
def degreeOn (G : Multigraph V) [Fintype V] (v : V)
    (P : V → Prop) [DecidablePred P] : ℕ

docstring: Degree splits over a predicate and its complement.
name: Multigraph.degreeOn_compl
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} (G : Multigraph V) [inst : Fintype V] (v : V) (P : V → Prop) [inst_1 : DecidablePred P], G.degree v = G.degreeOn v P + G.degreeOn v fun w ↦ ¬P w
statement:
theorem degreeOn_compl (G : Multigraph V) [Fintype V]
    (v : V) (P : V → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
    G.degree v = G.degreeOn v P + G.degreeOn v (fun w => ¬ P w)

docstring: `degreeOn` depends only on predicate values on support.
name: Multigraph.degreeOn_congr
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} (G : Multigraph V) [inst : Fintype V] (v : V) {P Q : V → Prop} [inst_1 : DecidablePred P] [inst_2 : DecidablePred Q], (∀ (w : V), G.edgeMult v w > 0 → (P w ↔ Q w)) → G.degreeOn v P = G.degreeOn v Q
statement:
theorem degreeOn_congr (G : Multigraph V) [Fintype V]
    (v : V) {P Q : V → Prop}
    [DecidablePred P] [DecidablePred Q]
    (h : ∀ w, G.edgeMult v w > 0 → (P w ↔ Q w)) :
    G.degreeOn v P = G.degreeOn v Q

statement: abbrev AffineCoordinateRing (X : Set (σ → K))

docstring:
A rational function on an affine set is regular at a point when a denominator that
does not vanish there clears the function.
name: MvPolynomial.AffineCoordinateRing.IsRegularAt
signature: {K : Type u_1} → {σ : Type u_2} → [inst : Field K] → (X : Set (σ → K)) → [IsDomain (MvPolynomial.AffineCoordinateRing X)] → FractionRing (MvPolynomial.AffineCoordinateRing X) → ↑X → Prop
statement:
def IsRegularAt (X : Set (σ → K)) [IsDomain (AffineCoordinateRing X)]
    (r : FractionRing (AffineCoordinateRing X)) (P : X) : Prop

docstring: Evaluation of an affine coordinate-ring element at a point of the underlying set.
name: MvPolynomial.AffineCoordinateRing.evalAt
signature: {K : Type u_1} → {σ : Type u_2} → [inst : Field K] → (X : Set (σ → K)) → ↑X → MvPolynomial.AffineCoordinateRing X →+* K
statement: noncomputable def evalAt (X : Set (σ → K)) (P : X) : AffineCoordinateRing X →+* K

docstring: Evaluation of a residue class agrees with evaluation of its representative.
name: MvPolynomial.AffineCoordinateRing.evalAt_mk
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_2} [inst : Field K] (X : Set (σ → K)) (P : ↑X) (f : MvPolynomial σ K), (MvPolynomial.AffineCoordinateRing.evalAt X P) ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal K X)) f) = (MvPolynomial.aeval ↑P) f
statement:
theorem evalAt_mk (X : Set (σ → K)) (P : X) (f : MvPolynomial σ K) :
    evalAt X P (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ f) = MvPolynomial.aeval P.1 f

docstring: Coordinate-ring elements define rational functions regular at every point.
name: MvPolynomial.AffineCoordinateRing.isRegularAt_algebraMap
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_2} [inst : Field K] (X : Set (σ → K)) [inst_1 : IsDomain (MvPolynomial.AffineCoordinateRing X)] (a : MvPolynomial.AffineCoordinateRing X) (P : ↑X), MvPolynomial.AffineCoordinateRing.IsRegularAt X ((Algebra.algebraMap (MvPolynomial.AffineCoordinateRing X) (FractionRing (MvPolynomial.AffineCoordinateRing X))) a) P
statement:
theorem isRegularAt_algebraMap (X : Set (σ → K)) [IsDomain (AffineCoordinateRing X)]
    (a : AffineCoordinateRing X) (P : X) :
    IsRegularAt X (algebraMap (AffineCoordinateRing X)
      (FractionRing (AffineCoordinateRing X)) a) P

docstring:
Specializing all but one variable of a stable polynomial to the closed upper half-plane
leaves every root of a nonzero specialization in the closed lower half-plane.
name: MvPolynomial.IsStable.roots_im_nonpos_univariateSpecialization
signature: ∀ {σ : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq σ] {p : MvPolynomial σ ℂ}, p.IsStable → ∀ (i : σ) (a : σ → ℂ), (∀ (j : σ), j ≠ i → 0 ≤ (a j).im) → MvPolynomial.univariateSpecialization i a p ≠ 0 → ∀ w ∈ (MvPolynomial.univariateSpecialization i a p).roots, w.im ≤ 0

    (i : σ) (a : σ → ℂ) (ha : ∀ j, j ≠ i → 0 ≤ (a j).im)
    (hq : univariateSpecialization i a p ≠ 0) :

docstring: The type of regular functions from $k^σ$ to $k^τ$.
name: MvPolynomial.RegularFunction
signature: (k : Type u_1) → [CommSemiring k] → Type u_2 → Type u_3 → Type (max (max u_3 u_1) u_2)
statement: abbrev RegularFunction

docstring:
The Jacobian of a vector valued polynomial function, viewed as a polynomial.

The matrix is indexed as codomain by domain, following Mathlib's matrix
convention: entry `(j, i)` is the partial derivative of the `j`-th component
with respect to the `i`-th variable, so the Jacobian supports `Matrix.mulVec`
and the standard chain-rule multiplication order.
name: MvPolynomial.RegularFunction.Jacobian
signature: {k : Type u_1} → [inst : CommSemiring k] → {σ : Type u_2} → {τ : Type u_3} → MvPolynomial.RegularFunction k σ τ → Matrix τ σ (MvPolynomial σ k)
statement:
noncomputable def Jacobian (F : RegularFunction k σ τ) :
    Matrix τ σ (MvPolynomial σ k)

name: MvPolynomial.RegularFunction.Jacobian_apply
signature: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring k] {σ : Type u_2} {τ : Type u_3} (F : MvPolynomial.RegularFunction k σ τ) (j : τ) (i : σ), F.Jacobian j i = (MvPolynomial.pderiv i) (F j)
statement:
lemma Jacobian_apply (F : RegularFunction k σ τ) (j : τ) (i : σ) :
    F.Jacobian j i = MvPolynomial.pderiv i (F j)

docstring:
The evaluation of a regular function `f` over `k` at some point `a`
with coordinates in some algebra over `k`.
name: MvPolynomial.RegularFunction.aeval
signature: {k : Type u_1} → [inst : CommSemiring k] → {σ : Type u_6} → {τ : Type u_7} → {S₁ : Type u_8} → [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁] → [Algebra k S₁] → MvPolynomial.RegularFunction k σ τ → (σ → S₁) → τ → S₁
statement:
noncomputable def aeval {σ τ : Type*} {S₁ : Type*} [CommSemiring S₁] [Algebra k S₁]
    (F : RegularFunction k σ τ) : (σ → S₁) → τ → S₁

docstring: The composition of two vector valued polynomial functions.
name: MvPolynomial.RegularFunction.comp
signature: {k : Type u_1} → [inst : CommSemiring k] → {σ : Type u_2} → {τ : Type u_3} → {ι : Type u_4} → MvPolynomial.RegularFunction k τ ι → MvPolynomial.RegularFunction k σ τ → MvPolynomial.RegularFunction k σ ι
statement:
noncomputable def comp
    (G : RegularFunction k τ ι) (F : RegularFunction k σ τ) :
    RegularFunction k σ ι

docstring: `aeval` is compatible with composition of regular functions.
name: MvPolynomial.RegularFunction.comp_aeval
signature: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring k] {σ : Type u_6} {τ : Type u_7} {ι : Type u_8} {S₁ : Type u_9} [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁] [inst_2 : Algebra k S₁] (G : MvPolynomial.RegularFunction k τ ι) (F : MvPolynomial.RegularFunction k σ τ) (a : σ → S₁), (G.comp F).aeval a = G.aeval (F.aeval a)
statement:
lemma comp_aeval
    {σ τ ι S₁ : Type*} [CommSemiring S₁] [Algebra k S₁]
    (G : RegularFunction k τ ι) (F : RegularFunction k σ τ)
    (a : σ → S₁) : (G.comp F).aeval a = G.aeval (F.aeval a)

name: MvPolynomial.RegularFunction.comp_apply
signature: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring k] {σ : Type u_2} {τ : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_4} (G : MvPolynomial.RegularFunction k τ ι) (F : MvPolynomial.RegularFunction k σ τ) (i : ι), G.comp F i = (MvPolynomial.bind₁ F) (G i)
statement:
lemma comp_apply (G : RegularFunction k τ ι) (F : RegularFunction k σ τ) (i : ι) :
    (G.comp F) i = MvPolynomial.bind₁ F (G i)

docstring: Composition of regular functions is associative.
name: MvPolynomial.RegularFunction.comp_assoc
signature: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring k] {σ : Type u_2} {τ : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_4} {κ : Type u_5} (H : MvPolynomial.RegularFunction k ι κ) (G : MvPolynomial.RegularFunction k τ ι) (F : MvPolynomial.RegularFunction k σ τ), (H.comp G).comp F = H.comp (G.comp F)
statement:
lemma comp_assoc (H : RegularFunction k ι κ) (G : RegularFunction k τ ι)
    (F : RegularFunction k σ τ) :
    (H.comp G).comp F = H.comp (G.comp F)

docstring: Evaluating a univariate specialization amounts to updating the selected variable.

docstring: Membership in the ideal tangent space is simultaneous vanishing on all of `I`.

signature: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : Field k] {n : ℕ} (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) (P v : Fin n → k), v ∈ MvPolynomial.tangentSpaceIdeal I P ↔ ∀ f ∈ I, f.totalDerivativeAt P v = 0

theorem mem_tangentSpaceIdeal (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) (P : Fin n → k)

signature: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : Field k] {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) (P v : Fin n → k), v ∈ f.tangentSpacePoly P ↔ f.totalDerivativeAt P v = 0

signature: ∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] {is js : List σ}, is.Perm js → ∀ (p : MvPolynomial σ R), MvPolynomial.mixedDifferential is p = MvPolynomial.mixedDifferential js p

docstring: Partial differentiation commutes with every mixed differential operator.
name: MvPolynomial.pderiv_mixedDifferential
signature: ∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] (i : σ) (is : List σ) (p : MvPolynomial σ R), (MvPolynomial.pderiv i) (MvPolynomial.mixedDifferential is p) = MvPolynomial.mixedDifferential is ((MvPolynomial.pderiv i) p)

public theorem pderiv_mixedDifferential {σ R : Type*} [CommRing R]

    pderiv i (mixedDifferential is p) = mixedDifferential is (pderiv i p)

docstring:
Frobenius probable prime (pseudo1.tex lines 713-741).
`f` is monic over the integers; degree and discriminant are `f.natDegree`
and `f.discr`. `n` is odd, greater than one, and coprime to the natural
absolute value of `f.eval 0 * f.discr`. All algorithm polynomials live over
`ZMod n`: `fs 0` is the coefficientwise reduction of `f`; each `F i` is a
greatest common monic divisor of `X ^ (n ^ i) - X` and `fs (i - 1)` with exact
factorization `fs (i - 1) = F i * fs i`; the stage ends with `fs f.natDegree = 1`.
The Frobenius step asks `F i ∣ (F i).comp (X ^ n)` for `2 ≤ i ≤ d`.
With quotient witnesses `q`, each even `i` satisfies `natDegree (F i) = i * q i`,
and the Jacobi step asks `(-1) ^ S = jacobiSym f.discr n` where `S` sums
`q i` over the even indices, zero elsewhere.
name: Nat.IsFrobeniusProbablePrime
signature: ℕ → Polynomial ℤ → Prop
statement: public def IsFrobeniusProbablePrime (n : ℕ) (f : _root_.Polynomial ℤ) : Prop

docstring: Unfolding of `Nat.IsFrobeniusProbablePrime`.
name: Nat.IsFrobeniusProbablePrime.unfold
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Polynomial ℤ), n.IsFrobeniusProbablePrime f ↔ f.Monic ∧ Odd n ∧ 1 < n ∧ n.Coprime (Polynomial.eval 0 f * f.discr).natAbs ∧ ∃ F fs q, fs 0 = Polynomial.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod n)) f ∧ fs f.natDegree = 1 ∧ (∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 f.natDegree, (F i).IsGreatestCommonMonicDivisor (Polynomial.X ^ n ^ i - Polynomial.X) (fs (i - 1)) ∧ fs (i - 1) = F i * fs i) ∧ (∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 2 f.natDegree, F i ∣ (F i).comp (Polynomial.X ^ n)) ∧ (∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 f.natDegree, Even i → (F i).natDegree = i * q i) ∧ ((-1) ^ ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 f.natDegree, if i % 2 = 0 then q i else 0) = jacobiSym f.discr n
statement:
public theorem IsFrobeniusProbablePrime.unfold (n : ℕ) (f : _root_.Polynomial ℤ) :
    IsFrobeniusProbablePrime n f ↔
      (f.Monic ∧ Odd n ∧ 1 < n ∧
        _root_.Nat.Coprime n (Int.natAbs (f.eval 0 * f.discr)) ∧
        ∃ F fs : ℕ → _root_.Polynomial (ZMod n),
          ∃ q : ℕ → ℕ,
            fs 0 = f.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod n)) ∧
            fs f.natDegree = 1 ∧
            (∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 f.natDegree,
              Polynomial.IsGreatestCommonMonicDivisor (F i)
                (Polynomial.X ^ (n ^ i) - Polynomial.X : _root_.Polynomial (ZMod n))
                (fs (i - 1)) ∧ fs (i - 1) = F i * fs i) ∧
            (∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 2 f.natDegree,
              F i ∣ (F i).comp (Polynomial.X ^ n : _root_.Polynomial (ZMod n))) ∧
            (∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 f.natDegree, Even i → (F i).natDegree = i * q i) ∧
            (-1 : ℤ) ^
                Finset.sum (Finset.Icc 1 f.natDegree)
                  (fun i => if i % 2 = 0 then q i else 0) =
              jacobiSym f.discr n)

docstring:
Frobenius pseudoprime (pseudo1.tex lines 763-768): a composite `n`
that is a Frobenius probable prime with respect to the monic polynomial `f`.
Composite is `¬ n.Prime` conjoined with the probable-prime `1 < n` clause.
name: Nat.IsFrobeniusPseudoprime

All later starts are handled by the consolidated hard-case estimate above.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.erdos_choose_prime_factor_gt
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (k : ℕ), n < k → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ (k + n - 1).choose n
statement:
lemma erdos_choose_prime_factor_gt (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (k : ℕ) (hk : n < k) :
    ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ Nat.choose (k + n - 1) n

docstring:
If `s = n + 2` does not divide the two terms immediately before the block, then
it divides some term in the block.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.exists_dvd_block_of_succ_succ_prime_not_dvd_pred
statement:
lemma exists_dvd_block_of_succ_succ_prime_not_dvd_pred {n k s : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (hsn : s = n + 2) (hnot_one : ¬ s ∣ k - 1) (hnot_two : ¬ s ∣ k - 2) :
    ∃ i < n, s ∣ k + i

docstring:
In the central residual range, the offset central-binomial lower bound contradicts
the `N / 3` first-layer estimate unless a large prime divides `Nat.choose N r`.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_central_offset_erdos_div_three_layers_bound
signature: ∀ {N r i : ℕ}, 4 ≤ r → i ≤ r → N = 2 * r + i → 6 ≤ N → r * (2 ^ i * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 N), if j = 0 then primorial (N / 3) else primorial ((j + 1).nthRoot N)) < 3 ^ i * 4 ^ r → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ r < p ∧ p ∣ N.choose r
statement:
lemma exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_central_offset_erdos_div_three_layers_bound
    {N r i : ℕ} (hr : 4 ≤ r) (hi : i ≤ r) (hN : N = 2 * r + i) (hN6 : 6 ≤ N)
    (hbound :
      r * (2 ^ i *
        (∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 N),
          if j = 0 then primorial (N / 3) else primorial (Nat.nthRoot (j + 1) N))) <
        3 ^ i * 4 ^ r) :
    ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ r < p ∧ p ∣ Nat.choose N r

docstring: Erdős layer estimate with first layer `N / 3`, in binomial form.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_erdos_div_three_layers_bound
signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, n < k → 6 ≤ k + n - 1 → (n.factorial * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 (k + n - 1)), if j = 0 then primorial ((k + n - 1) / 3) else primorial ((j + 1).nthRoot (k + n - 1))) < k ^ n → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ (k + n - 1).choose n
statement:
lemma exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_erdos_div_three_layers_bound {n k : ℕ}
    (hk : n < k) (hN6 : 6 ≤ k + n - 1)
    (hbound :
      n ! *
          (∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 (k + n - 1)),

docstring: Full Erdős layer conditional estimate in binomial form.

signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, 1 ≤ n → n < k → (n.factorial * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 (k + n - 1)), if j = 0 then primorial n else primorial ((j + 1).nthRoot (k + n - 1))) < k ^ n → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ (k + n - 1).choose n

docstring: Three-layer power-of-four Erdős estimate in binomial form.

docstring:

name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_half_bound
signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, 1 ≤ n → n < k → n.factorial * (k + n - 1) ^ (n / 2 + 1) < k ^ n → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ (k + n - 1).choose n

docstring:
A large prime divisor of any term in the block gives a large prime divisor of the
corresponding binomial coefficient.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_large_prime_dvd_block
signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, (∃ i < n, ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ k + i) → ∃ q, Nat.Prime q ∧ n < q ∧ q ∣ (k + n - 1).choose n

docstring:
A large-start consecutive-block estimate gives the corresponding binomial
large-prime criterion.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_large_start
signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, 2 ≤ n → n < k → n.factorial * 2 ^ (n - 1) < k → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ (k + n - 1).choose n

lemma exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_large_start {n k : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hk : n < k)

docstring: Prime-counting conditional estimate in binomial form.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_primeCounting_bound
signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, 1 ≤ n → n < k → n.factorial * (k + n - 1) ^ n.primeCounting < k ^ n → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ (k + n - 1).choose n
statement:
lemma exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_primeCounting_bound {n k : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (hk : n < k) (hbound : n ! * (k + n - 1) ^ Nat.primeCounting n < k ^ n) :
    ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ Nat.choose (k + n - 1) n

docstring:
In the first residual range, the scaled ternary lower bound contradicts the
three-layer Erdős upper bound unless `Nat.choose N r` has a prime divisor above `r`.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_scaled_ternary_erdos_layers_bound
signature: ∀ {N r : ℕ}, 4 ≤ r → 3 * r ≤ N → r * (2 ^ r * ((3 * r) ^ r * 4 ^ (r + N.sqrt + Nat.nthRoot 3 N * Nat.log 2 N))) < 3 ^ r * 4 ^ r * N ^ r → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ r < p ∧ p ∣ N.choose r
statement:
lemma exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_scaled_ternary_erdos_layers_bound {N r : ℕ}
    (hr : 4 ≤ r) (hrN : 3 * r ≤ N)
    (hbound :
      r * (2 ^ r * ((3 * r) ^ r *
        4 ^ (r + Nat.sqrt N + Nat.nthRoot 3 N * Nat.log 2 N))) <
        3 ^ r * 4 ^ r * N ^ r) :
    ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ r < p ∧ p ∣ Nat.choose N r

docstring:
The smooth-number count contradiction gives a large prime divisor of the block
binomial coefficient.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_smooth_count_bound
signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, 2 ^ n.primeCounting * (k + n - 1).sqrt < n → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ (k + n - 1).choose n

docstring: Split `sqrt/primorial` conditional estimate in binomial form.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_sqrt_primorial_bound
signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, 1 ≤ n → n < k → n.factorial * ((k + n - 1) ^ ((k + n - 1).sqrt + 1) * primorial n) < k ^ n → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ (k + n - 1).choose n
statement:
lemma exists_prime_dvd_choose_of_sqrt_primorial_bound {n k : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (hk : n < k)
    (hbound :
      n ! * ((k + n - 1) ^ (Nat.sqrt (k + n - 1) + 1) * primorial n) < k ^ n) :
    ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ Nat.choose (k + n - 1) n

docstring:
Small central-offset cases for `Nat.choose (2 * n + 2) n`, handled by an
explicit short prime-gap certificate.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.exists_prime_dvd_choose_two_mul_add_two_small
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 7 ≤ n → n < 512 → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ (2 * n + 2).choose n

lemma exists_prime_dvd_choose_two_mul_add_two_small {n : ℕ} (hn7 : 7 ≤ n)
    (hnlt : n < 512) :
    ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ Nat.choose (2 * n + 2) n

docstring:
Large-`n` first residual estimate: after scaling to the ternary lower bound,
the Erdős three-layer upper bound is too small throughout `3 * n ≤ N ≤ n ^ 2 + n`.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.first_residual_large_scaled_ternary_bound
signature: ∀ {n N : ℕ}, 945 ≤ n → 3 * n ≤ N → N ≤ n ^ 2 + n → n * (2 ^ n * ((3 * n) ^ n * 4 ^ (n + N.sqrt + Nat.nthRoot 3 N * Nat.log 2 N))) < 3 ^ n * 4 ^ n * N ^ n
statement:
lemma first_residual_large_scaled_ternary_bound {n N : ℕ}
    (hn : 945 ≤ n) (hNlo : 3 * n ≤ N) (hNhi : N ≤ n ^ 2 + n) :
    n * (2 ^ n * ((3 * n) ^ n *
      4 ^ (n + Nat.sqrt N + Nat.nthRoot 3 N * Nat.log 2 N))) <
      3 ^ n * 4 ^ n * N ^ n

docstring:
The power comparison used after the central-offset residual estimate has been reduced to
exponents.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.four_pow_mul_two_pow_mul_four_pow_lt_three_pow_mul_four_pow
statement:
lemma four_pow_mul_two_pow_mul_four_pow_lt_three_pow_mul_four_pow
    {D E i n : ℕ} (hexp : 2 * D + i + 2 * E < 19 * (i / 12) + 2 * n) :
    4 ^ D * (2 ^ i * 4 ^ E) < 3 ^ i * 4 ^ n

docstring:
In the range `N ≤ 4 * n`, the `Nat.nthRoot 3 N * Nat.log 2 N` contribution is at
most `n / 5`.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.nthRoot_three_mul_log_le_one_fifth_of_le_four_mul
signature: ∀ {n N : ℕ}, 945 ≤ n → N ≤ 4 * n → Nat.nthRoot 3 N * Nat.log 2 N ≤ n / 5

docstring:
A prime in the interval `[k, k + n - 1]`, and larger than `n`, divides the
corresponding block binomial coefficient.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.prime_dvd_choose_of_mem_interval
signature: ∀ {n k p : ℕ}, Nat.Prime p → n < p → k ≤ p → p ≤ k + n - 1 → p ∣ (k + n - 1).choose n
statement:
lemma prime_dvd_choose_of_mem_interval {n k p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hp_gt : n < p)
    (hp_ge : k ≤ p) (hp_le : p ≤ k + n - 1) :
    p ∣ Nat.choose (k + n - 1) n

docstring:
If a prime `n < r` divides `k + j` for some `j < n`, then it divides
`Nat.choose (k + n - 1) n`.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.prime_dvd_seq_implies_choose
signature: ∀ {n k r : ℕ}, Nat.Prime r → n < r → ∀ j < n, r ∣ k + j → r ∣ (k + n - 1).choose n
statement:
lemma prime_dvd_seq_implies_choose {n k r : ℕ} (hr : r.Prime) (hr_gt : n < r)
    (j : ℕ) (hj : j < n) (hdvd : r ∣ k + j) :
    r ∣ Nat.choose (k + n - 1) n

docstring: Large-`n` residual estimate in the central-offset range `k + n - 1 < 3 * n`.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.second_residual_large_central_offset_bound
signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, 945 ≤ n → n < k → k + n - 1 < 3 * n → n * (2 ^ (k - n - 1) * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 (k + n - 1)), if j = 0 then primorial ((k + n - 1) / 3) else primorial ((j + 1).nthRoot (k + n - 1))) < 3 ^ (k - n - 1) * 4 ^ n
statement:
lemma second_residual_large_central_offset_bound {n k : ℕ}
    (hn : 945 ≤ n) (hk : n < k) (hcentral : k + n - 1 < 3 * n) :
    n * (2 ^ (k - n - 1) *
      (∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 (k + n - 1)),
        if j = 0 then primorial ((k + n - 1) / 3)
        else primorial (Nat.nthRoot (j + 1) (k + n - 1)))) <
      3 ^ (k - n - 1) * 4 ^ n

docstring:
For `38 ≤ n < 945` and `k < 1291`, a prime-gap table supplies a block term
with a prime divisor greater than `n`.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.second_residual_mid_has_large_prime_factor
signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, 38 ≤ n → n < 945 → n + 3 ≤ k → k < 1291 → ∃ i < n, ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ k + i

docstring:
The mid residual range `38 ≤ n < 945` satisfies the prime-counting conditional
estimate once `1291 ≤ k`, using the finite certificates in this file.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.second_residual_mid_primeCounting_lt_start_pow
signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, 38 ≤ n → n < 945 → 1291 ≤ k → n.factorial * (k + n - 1) ^ n.primeCounting < k ^ n

docstring:
For `7 ≤ n < 38` and `k < 100`, a small prime-gap table supplies a block term

name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.second_residual_tiny_has_large_prime_factor
signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, 7 ≤ n → n < 38 → n + 3 ≤ k → k < 100 → ∃ i < n, ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ k + i

docstring:
The small residual range `7 ≤ n < 38` satisfies the prime-counting conditional
estimate once `100 ≤ k`.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.second_residual_tiny_primeCounting_lt_start_pow
signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, 7 ≤ n → n < 38 → 100 ≤ k → n.factorial * (k + n - 1) ^ n.primeCounting < k ^ n

docstring:

estimates.

statement:
lemma self_le_four_pow_div_one_twenty_eight_add_one {n : ℕ} (hn : 512 ≤ n) :

docstring: If `N ≤ 4 * n` and `n` is large enough, then `sqrt N` is at most `n / 15`.

statement:
lemma sqrt_le_div_fifteen_of_le_four_mul {n N : ℕ} (hn : 900 ≤ n)
    (hNhi : N ≤ 4 * n) :
