docstring:
If no block term has a prime divisor larger than `n`, the quadratic-start
consecutive estimate forces `k ≤ n ^ 2`.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.start_le_quadratic_of_no_large_prime_dvd_block
signature: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, 38 ≤ n → (¬∃ i < n, ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ k + i) → k ≤ n ^ 2
statement:
lemma start_le_quadratic_of_no_large_prime_dvd_block {n k : ℕ} (hn : 38 ≤ n)
    (hblock : ¬ ∃ i < n, ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ n < p ∧ p ∣ k + i) :
    k ≤ n ^ 2

docstring: A binary-to-ternary comparison used to convert powers of `2` into powers of `3`.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.Internal.two_pow_nineteen_mul_div_twelve_le_three_pow
statement:
lemma two_pow_nineteen_mul_div_twelve_le_three_pow (n : ℕ) :
    2 ^ (19 * (n / 12)) ≤ 3 ^ n

docstring: Explicit large-`n` estimate for the central Erdős layer product at `N = 2 * n + 2`.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.central_erdos_layers_two_mul_add_two_lt_four_pow
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 512 ≤ n → (n * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 (2 * n + 2)), if j = 0 then primorial ((2 * n + 2) / 3) else primorial ((j + 1).nthRoot (2 * n + 2))) < 4 ^ n
statement:
theorem central_erdos_layers_two_mul_add_two_lt_four_pow {n : ℕ} (hn : 512 ≤ n) :
    n * (∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 (2 * n + 2)),
        if j = 0 then primorial ((2 * n + 2) / 3)
        else primorial (Nat.nthRoot (j + 1) (2 * n + 2))) < 4 ^ n

docstring:
If every prime divisor of `Nat.choose N r` is at most `r`, then the product formula for
`Nat.choose N r` can be truncated from primes up to `N` to candidates up to `r`.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.choose_eq_prod_small_prime_powers_of_no_large
signature: ∀ {N r : ℕ}, r ≤ N → (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ∣ N.choose r → p ≤ r) → ∏ p ∈ Finset.range (r + 1), p ^ (N.choose r).factorization p = N.choose r
statement:
theorem choose_eq_prod_small_prime_powers_of_no_large {N r : ℕ} (hrN : r ≤ N)
    (hsmall : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ Nat.choose N r → p ≤ r) :
    (∏ p ∈ Finset.range (r + 1), p ^ (Nat.choose N r).factorization p) =
      Nat.choose N r

docstring:
Sharpened Erdős layer bound with the `N / 3` first layer. The first-layer cutoff follows
from `Nat.factorization_choose_of_lt_three_mul`.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.choose_le_prod_erdos_div_three_layers_of_no_large
signature: ∀ {N r : ℕ}, 0 < N → r ≤ N → 2 * r ≤ N → 6 ≤ N → (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ∣ N.choose r → p ≤ r) → N.choose r ≤ ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 N), if j = 0 then primorial (N / 3) else primorial ((j + 1).nthRoot N)
statement:
theorem choose_le_prod_erdos_div_three_layers_of_no_large {N r : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N)
    (hrN : r ≤ N) (h2rN : 2 * r ≤ N) (hN6 : 6 ≤ N)
    (hsmall : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ Nat.choose N r → p ≤ r) :
    Nat.choose N r ≤
      ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 N),
        if j = 0 then primorial (N / 3) else primorial (Nat.nthRoot (j + 1) N)

docstring:
Sharpened full Erdős layer bound.  The first layer uses the no-large-prime cutoff `r`;
subsequent layers use the root bounds.  This matches the product estimate in Erdős's proof.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.choose_le_prod_erdos_layers_of_no_large
signature: ∀ {N r : ℕ}, 0 < N → r ≤ N → (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ∣ N.choose r → p ≤ r) → N.choose r ≤ ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 N), if j = 0 then primorial r else primorial ((j + 1).nthRoot N)
statement:
theorem choose_le_prod_erdos_layers_of_no_large {N r : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N)
    (hrN : r ≤ N) (hsmall : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ Nat.choose N r → p ≤ r) :
    Nat.choose N r ≤
      ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 N),
        if j = 0 then primorial r else primorial (Nat.nthRoot (j + 1) N)

docstring:
Full Erdős prime-power layer bound. Under the no-large-prime hypothesis, the binomial
coefficient is bounded by the product of primorials at successive roots of `N`.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.choose_le_prod_primorial_nthRoot_of_no_large
signature: ∀ {N r : ℕ}, 0 < N → r ≤ N → (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ∣ N.choose r → p ≤ r) → N.choose r ≤ ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 N), primorial ((j + 1).nthRoot N)
statement:
theorem choose_le_prod_primorial_nthRoot_of_no_large {N r : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N)
    (hrN : r ≤ N) (hsmall : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ Nat.choose N r → p ≤ r) :
    Nat.choose N r ≤
      ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (Nat.log 2 N), primorial (Nat.nthRoot (j + 1) N)

docstring:
Using the already-formalized prime-counting bound `π(r) ≤ r / 2 + 1` gives a sharper
no-large-prime estimate.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.choose_le_top_pow_half_add_one_of_no_large
signature: ∀ {N r : ℕ}, 0 < N → r ≤ N → (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ∣ N.choose r → p ≤ r) → N.choose r ≤ N ^ (r / 2 + 1)
statement:
theorem choose_le_top_pow_half_add_one_of_no_large {N r : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (hrN : r ≤ N)
    (hsmall : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ Nat.choose N r → p ≤ r) :
    Nat.choose N r ≤ N ^ (r / 2 + 1)

docstring:
The same no-large-prime hypothesis gives the sharper Erdős factorization bound with exponent
`Nat.primeCounting r`. The remaining hard part of the classical proof is to contradict this bound
using lower estimates for the relevant binomial coefficient.
name: Nat.SylvesterSchur.choose_le_top_pow_primeCounting_of_no_large
signature: ∀ {N r : ℕ}, 0 < N → r ≤ N → (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ∣ N.choose r → p ≤ r) → N.choose r ≤ N ^ r.primeCounting
statement:
theorem choose_le_top_pow_primeCounting_of_no_large {N r : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (hrN : r ≤ N)
    (hsmall : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ Nat.choose N r → p ≤ r) :
    Nat.choose N r ≤ N ^ Nat.primeCounting r

docstring:
Replacing `Nat.primeCounting r` by the elementary bound `r - 1` gives a slightly coarser

docstring:
Coarse generic power-of-four bound for the Erdős product with first layer `r`.

      4 ^ (r + Nat.sqrt N * Nat.log 2 N)

docstring:

      4 ^ (r + Nat.sqrt N + Nat.nthRoot 3 N * Nat.log 2 N)

docstring:
Exact preperiod and primitive period of Fermat-number residues modulo an odd prime.

This is the exact-preperiod/primitive-period expansion of Theorem `thm:5` in the section
"A simpler formulation of Aigner's theorem": for an odd prime `p` with
`orderOf (2 : ZMod p) = 2 ^ v * w` and `w` odd, writing `k := orderOf (2 : ZMod w)`, the
shifted residue sequence `n ↦ (Nat.fermatNumber (v + n) : ZMod p)` is periodic with period
`k`, no shift `h < v` admits any positive tail period, and every positive period of the
tail from `v` is divisible by `k`.

Source: `https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL28/Klaska/klaska22.tex`,
Theorem `thm:5`, lines 593--606 of
`56ede62e8bb2abc2c9097317bce881d696be23082f48fa2822d297f0f11e65af.tex`
(source SHA-256 `56ede62e8bb2abc2c9097317bce881d696be23082f48fa2822d297f0f11e65af`,
excerpt SHA-256 `e4893c51946a5353f9ac51df8a431d7a4374170b122bfcb5befb12ae3d342bd7`).
Concept `jis_dep_f3be3eca42e403215ccd3864` (grounded `jis_grounded_b5fc700e81e8282d5e992c5d`);
accounting: 7 mentions / 3 papers / 2 proof uses.
This is the complete selected theorem statement, not a prerequisite stage.
Proves `Wanted` entry `fermatNumber_mod_prime_exact_preperiod_period`.
name: Nat.fermatNumber_mod_prime_exact_preperiod_period
signature:
∀ (p v w : ℕ),
  Nat.Prime p →
    p ≠ 2 →
      orderOf 2 = 2 ^ v * w →
        Odd w →
          have k := orderOf 2;
          Function.Periodic (fun n ↦ ↑(v + n).fermatNumber) k ∧ (∀ h < v, ¬∃ kp, 0 < kp ∧ Function.Periodic (fun n ↦ ↑(h + n).fermatNumber) kp) ∧ ∀ (kp : ℕ), 0 < kp → Function.Periodic (fun n ↦ ↑(v + n).fermatNumber) kp → k ∣ kp
statement:
theorem fermatNumber_mod_prime_exact_preperiod_period (p v w : ℕ)
    (hp : p.Prime) (hp2 : p ≠ 2)
    (hord : orderOf (2 : ZMod p) = 2 ^ v * w) (hw : Odd w) :
    let k := orderOf (2 : ZMod w);
      Function.Periodic (fun n : ℕ => (Nat.fermatNumber (v + n) : ZMod p)) k ∧
        (∀ h < v, ¬ ∃ kp : ℕ, 0 < kp ∧
          Function.Periodic (fun n : ℕ => (Nat.fermatNumber (h + n) : ZMod p)) kp) ∧
        (∀ kp : ℕ, 0 < kp →
          Function.Periodic (fun n : ℕ => (Nat.fermatNumber (v + n) : ZMod p)) kp → k ∣ kp)

docstring:
Hurwitz class number `H`. Source: arXiv:2307.05244 `main.tex` lines 359-365
    (span SHA-256 `b04cba9e14e90ed1b64100eda01d08dd3de6e1d2b2ea9ec9b1a56cfc467f6622`):
    `H(N) = 0` if `N ≡ 1` or `2 mod 4`; `H(0) = -1 / 12`; otherwise `N > 0`
    and `N ≡ 0` or `3 mod 4`, `H(N)` is the class number of not necessarily
    primitive positive-definite quadratic forms of discriminant `-N`, with
    weight `1 / 2` for forms equivalent to `a * (x ^ 2 + y ^ 2)` and weight
    `1 / 3` for forms equivalent to `a * (x ^ 2 + x * y + y ^ 2)`.

docstring:
**Korselt's criterion**: a positive composite natural number is a Carmichael number iff it is
squarefree and `p - 1 ∣ n - 1` for every prime divisor `p` of `n`.
name: Nat.isCarmichaelNumber_iff_korselt
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 < n → (n.IsCarmichaelNumber ↔ Squarefree n ∧ (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ∣ n → p - 1 ∣ n - 1) ∧ ¬Nat.Prime n)
statement:
theorem Nat.isCarmichaelNumber_iff_korselt (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) :
    Nat.IsCarmichaelNumber n ↔
      Squarefree n ∧
        (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ n → (p - 1) ∣ (n - 1)) ∧ ¬n.Prime

docstring:

statement:
theorem Nat.isCarmichaelNumber_iff_zmod (n : ℕ) :
    Nat.IsCarmichaelNumber n ↔
      1 < n ∧ ¬n.Prime ∧ ∀ x : ZMod n, x ^ n = x

docstring:
`threeSquareRepresentationCount n` counts ordered triples `(x, y, z)` with
`x, y, z ∈ [-(n : ℤ), n]` and `x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 + z ^ 2 = n`. The interval
`[-(n : ℤ), n]` contains every integer solution and handles `n = 0`, so
this realizes the exact source count `r₃(n)`.
Primary source: E. T. Mortenson, arXiv:1702.01627v2,
`Mortenson-AC-Gauss-arxiv-v2.tex` lines 127-131 (span SHA-256
`2f2704bfc2f61e5fc50b27df3e14542a0ef19ddd4c7580c7f589f23d38ccff12`,
file SHA-256 `13bccb58b9397a2bf3fb713779f0d76623513aec5c0f313a3cf95cf8466b5cf3`)
defining `rₛ` by `Rₛ(q) = ∑ₙ rₛ(n) (-q) ^ n = (∑_{m ∈ ℤ} (-1) ^ m q ^ (m ^ 2)) ^ s`
(ordered signed integer tuples). Ranked source arXiv:2307.05244 `main.tex`
lines 78-82 (span SHA-256 `08a4b80a1e84386e7dc97f8d87e1a4f84945d55022722618d59beca2382f9942`)
identifies the equation `x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 + z ^ 2 = n`.

Membership in a section set unfolds to the ideal membership plus the
archimedean bounds.
name: NumberField.ArakelovDivisor.mem_sectionSet
signature: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [NumberField K] (D : NumberField.ArakelovDivisor K) (x : K), x ∈ NumberField.ArakelovDivisor.sectionSet K D ↔ x ∈ ↑D.1 ∧ ∀ (w : NumberField.InfinitePlace K), w x ≤ ↑(D.2 w)

        ∀ w : InfinitePlace K, w x ≤ (D.2 w : ℝ)

docstring:

`NumberField.Embeddings.finite_of_norm_le` applies.

noncomputable def ArakelovDivisor.sizeHom :

docstring: The size homomorphism unfolds to the quotient of its two factors.
name: NumberField.ArakelovDivisor.sizeHom_apply
signature: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (D : NumberField.ArakelovDivisor K), (NumberField.ArakelovDivisor.sizeHom K) D = (NumberField.ArakelovDivisor.archHom K) D / (NumberField.ArakelovDivisor.idealHom K) D
statement:
theorem ArakelovDivisor.sizeHom_apply (D : ArakelovDivisor K) :
    ArakelovDivisor.sizeHom K D =

docstring: Coercion of the size homomorphism to the reals.
name: NumberField.ArakelovDivisor.sizeHom_coe
signature: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (D : NumberField.ArakelovDivisor K), ↑((NumberField.ArakelovDivisor.sizeHom K) D) = (∏ w, ↑(D.2 w) ^ w.mult) / ↑(FractionalIdeal.absNorm ↑D.1)

    Nat.card {I : Ideal (𝓞 K) // I ≠ ⊥ ∧ Ideal.absNorm I ≤ M} ≤

docstring:
Derived real-threshold floor bridge: the same bound with `⌊M⌋₊` in place of `M`.
For `M < 1` the subtype is empty since every nonzero ideal has norm at

docstring:
Exact formalization of ATLAS `NumberTheoryI:295`, *Number Theory I*,
Section 14.5, Lemma 14.21: the positive-real threshold, real exponentiation,
and `log₂` exponent are represented by `hM`, `Real.rpow`, and `Real.logb 2 M`,
respectively. The proof derives this literal source endpoint from the stronger
integer/floor variants above.

      I ≠ ⊥ ∧ (Ideal.absNorm I : ℝ) ≤ M} : ℝ) ≤
      ((Module.finrank ℚ K : ℝ) * M) ^ (Real.logb 2 M)

docstring:
Finite number-field characterization of the Hilbert class field of `K`.

`L` is the Hilbert class field of `K` if `L / K` is finite-dimensional abelian Galois,
unramified at every finite height-one prime of `𝓞 K` and at infinite places, and maximal
among such extensions: every other finite-dimensional abelian Galois number field `M / K`
unramified at all finite and infinite places embeds into `L` over `K`.
name: NumberField.IsHilbertClassField
signature: (K L : Type u) → [inst : Field K] → [inst_1 : Field L] → [NumberField K] → [NumberField L] → [Algebra K L] → Prop
statement:
structure IsHilbertClassField (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [NumberField K]
    [NumberField L] [Algebra K L] : Prop

docstring: Maximality applied: an admissible competitor `M / K` embeds into `L` over `K`.
name: NumberField.IsHilbertClassField.apply_maximal
signature: ∀ {K L : Type u} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : Field L] [inst_2 : NumberField K] [inst_3 : NumberField L] [inst_4 : Algebra K L] {M : Type u} [inst_5 : Field M] [NumberField M] [inst_7 : Algebra K M], NumberField.IsHilbertClassField K L → FiniteDimensional K M → IsAbelianGalois K M → (∀ (𝔭 : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)), Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (NumberField.RingOfIntegers M) 𝔭.asIdeal) → IsUnramifiedAtInfinitePlaces K M → Nonempty (M →ₐ[K] L)
statement:
theorem IsHilbertClassField.apply_maximal {M : Type u} [Field M] [NumberField M]
    [Algebra K M] (h : IsHilbertClassField K L)
    (hfin : FiniteDimensional K M)
    (hgal : IsAbelianGalois K M)
    (hfinU : ∀ 𝔭 : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K),
      Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (𝓞 M) 𝔭.asIdeal)
    (hinfU : IsUnramifiedAtInfinitePlaces K M) : Nonempty (M →ₐ[K] L)

docstring:
Semilocal étaleness above an unramified prime: localizing the whole finite
algebra `𝓞 K` at the prime-complement of `p` (inverting everything outside `p`,
keeping all local factors above `p` simultaneously) is étale over the local
base `Localization.AtPrime p`.

This packages the primewise unramified hypothesis used by
`isUnramifiedAtPrime_sup` in the primary Lean source for ATLAS `NumberTheoryI`
target N390, Proposition 19.14. It is the semilocal algebra, not a single local
factor `Localization.AtPrime Q`.
name: NumberField.IsUnramifiedIn.etale_localization
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_2} [inst : Field K] [NumberField K] (p : Ideal ℤ) [inst_2 : p.IsPrime], Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) p → Algebra.Etale (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) p.primeCompl))
statement:
theorem IsUnramifiedIn.etale_localization {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    (p : Ideal ℤ) [p.IsPrime] (h : Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (𝓞 K) p) :
    Algebra.Etale (Localization.AtPrime p)
      (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (𝓞 K) p.primeCompl))

docstring:
Contracted maximal prime: the correct prime of the normalized tensor algebra
at which to localize to obtain the local factor `Localization.AtPrime Q`.

Let `g := normalizedTensorToCompositumAtPrime E F p h Q` and
`T := Localization.AtPrime Q`. This is the comap of the maximal ideal of the
local ring `T` under `g`. It contains the prime kernel of `g` (see
`normalizedTensorToCompositumAtPrime_ker_le`), but it is in general strictly
larger: for a nonzero prime below `Q`, a nonzero uniformizer lies outside
`RingHom.ker g` yet maps to a nonunit of `T`.

This is a named alternative-normalization prerequisite stage for the missing
`cyclotomic_ramIdx_eq_of_unramified` and
[`baseChange_ramificationIdx_eq_one`, lines 1549--1586](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/e8b31c5cb0bec89b487ce33fe525a2c0b0f8b9c6/v1/Atlas/NumberTheoryI/code/AnalyticClassNumber.lean#L1549-L1586)
in the primary Lean source for ATLAS `NumberTheoryI` target N390,
Proposition 19.14. It does not prove
compositum unramifiedness, any `IsLocalization` identification, or the final
maximality theorem.
name: NumberField.IsUnramifiedIn.normalizedTensorCompositumPrime
signature: {L : Type u_1} → [inst : Field L] → [inst_1 : NumberField L] → (E F : IntermediateField ℚ L) → (p : Ideal ℤ) → [inst_2 : p.IsPrime] → Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥F) p → (Q : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥(E ⊔ F))) → [Q.IsPrime] → [Q.LiesOver p] → Ideal ↥(integralClosure (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥F) p.primeCompl)) (TensorProduct (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥F) p.primeCompl)) (FractionRing (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥E))))
statement:
noncomputable def normalizedTensorCompositumPrime
    (E F : IntermediateField ℚ L)
    (p : Ideal ℤ) [p.IsPrime] (h : Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (𝓞 F) p)
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 (E ⊔ F : IntermediateField ℚ L)))
    [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver p] :
    Ideal (integralClosure

docstring:
Canonical localization map: the universal property of
`Localization.AtPrime` applied at the contracted maximal prime. An element
outside the contracted prime maps outside the maximal ideal of the local target
`T`, hence to a unit.

This is a plain `RingHom`, not an `AlgHom`: no `Algebra A S` or
`IsScalarTower A C S` data is installed, since that instance search is fragile.
No `IsLocalization` or `AlgEquiv` claim is made here: the missing
bijection/local-factor identification remains a later infrastructure problem,
and localization at `RingHom.ker g` is in general false.
name: NumberField.IsUnramifiedIn.normalizedTensorLocalizationToCompositumAtPrime

            (h : Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥F) p) →
              (Q : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥(E ⊔ F))) →
                [inst_3 : Q.IsPrime] →
                  [inst_4 : Q.LiesOver p] →
                    let qC := NumberField.IsUnramifiedIn.normalizedTensorCompositumPrime E F p h Q;
                    let S := Localization.AtPrime qC;
                    let T := Localization.AtPrime Q;
                    S →+* T

    let qC := normalizedTensorCompositumPrime E F p h Q
    let S := Localization.AtPrime qC
    let T := Localization.AtPrime Q

name: NumberField.IsUnramifiedIn.normalizedTensorLocalizationToCompositumAtPrime_mk'_spec
signature: ∀ {L : Type u_1} [inst : Field L] [inst_1 : NumberField L] (E F : IntermediateField ℚ L) (p : Ideal ℤ) [inst_2 : p.IsPrime] (h : Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥F) p) (Q : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥(E ⊔ F))) [inst_3 : Q.IsPrime] [inst_4 : Q.LiesOver p] (x : ↥(integralClosure (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥F) p.primeCompl)) (TensorProduct (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥F) p.primeCompl)) (FractionRing (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥E))))) (y : ↥(NumberField.IsUnramifiedIn.normalizedTensorCompositumPrime E F p h Q).primeCompl) (v : Localization.AtPrime Q), (NumberField.IsUnramifiedIn.normalizedTensorLocalizationToCompositumAtPrime E F p h Q) (IsLocalization.mk' (Localization.AtPrime (NumberField.IsUnramifiedIn.normalizedTensorCompositumPrime E F p h Q)) x y) = v ↔ (NumberField.IsUnramifiedIn.normalizedTensorToCompositumAtPrime E F p h Q) x = (NumberField.IsUnramifiedIn.normalizedTensorToCompositumAtPrime E F p h Q) ↑y * v

    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 (E ⊔ F : IntermediateField ℚ L)))
    [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver p]
    (x : integralClosure
      (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (𝓞 F) p.primeCompl))
      (TensorProduct (Localization.AtPrime p)
        (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (𝓞 F) p.primeCompl))
        (FractionRing (𝓞 E))))
    (y : (normalizedTensorCompositumPrime E F p h Q).primeCompl)

docstring:
This maps the normalized tensor algebra to the local ring at `Q` and
selects the compositum component, but does NOT yet claim the induced
localization is an equivalence.

It is the normalized, prime-selected map corresponding to the fixed-`Q` stage
of `baseChange_ramificationIdx_eq_one` in the primary Lean source for ATLAS
N390.
name: NumberField.IsUnramifiedIn.normalizedTensorToCompositumAtPrime
signature:
{L : Type u_1} →
  [inst : Field L] →
    [inst_1 : NumberField L] →
      (E F : IntermediateField ℚ L) →
        (p : Ideal ℤ) →
          [inst_2 : p.IsPrime] →
            Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥F) p →
              (Q : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥(E ⊔ F))) →
                [inst_3 : Q.IsPrime] →
                  [inst_4 : Q.LiesOver p] →
                    let R := Localization.AtPrime p;
                    let S_F := Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥F) p.primeCompl);
                    have C := integralClosure S_F (TensorProduct R S_F (FractionRing (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ↥E)));
                    let T := Localization.AtPrime Q;
                    ↥C →ₐ[R] T
statement:
noncomputable def normalizedTensorToCompositumAtPrime
    (E F : IntermediateField ℚ L)
    (p : Ideal ℤ) [p.IsPrime] (h : Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (𝓞 F) p)
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 (E ⊔ F : IntermediateField ℚ L)))
    [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver p] :
    let R := Localization.AtPrime p
    let S_F := Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (𝓞 F) p.primeCompl)
    let C := integralClosure S_F
      (TensorProduct R S_F (FractionRing (𝓞 E)))
    let T := Localization.AtPrime Q
    letI : Algebra R T := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver p Q
    C →ₐ[R] T

docstring:
Characteristic formula on normalized simple tensors: after transporting a
tensor generator through the normalization equivalence, the selected component
is the product of its two semilocal images.
name: NumberField.IsUnramifiedIn.normalizedTensorToCompositumAtPrime_equiv_tmul
statement:
theorem normalizedTensorToCompositumAtPrime_equiv_tmul
    (E F : IntermediateField ℚ L)
    (p : Ideal ℤ) [p.IsPrime] (h : Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (𝓞 F) p)
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 (E ⊔ F : IntermediateField ℚ L)))
    [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver p]
    (x : Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (𝓞 F) p.primeCompl))
    (y : Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (𝓞 E) p.primeCompl)) :
    let R := Localization.AtPrime p
    let S_F := Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (𝓞 F) p.primeCompl)
    let S_E := Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (𝓞 E) p.primeCompl)
    let M := (E ⊔ F : IntermediateField ℚ L)
    letI _algE : Algebra E M := (IntermediateField.inclusion le_sup_left).toAlgebra
    letI _algF : Algebra F M := (IntermediateField.inclusion le_sup_right).toAlgebra
    let T := Localization.AtPrime Q
    letI : Algebra R T := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver p Q
    let fF : S_F →ₐ[𝓞 F] T := Localization.semilocalizationToAtPrime p Q
    let fE : S_E →ₐ[𝓞 E] T := Localization.semilocalizationToAtPrime p Q
    let e := tensorProductLocalizationEquivIntegralClosure (E := E) (F := F) p h
    normalizedTensorToCompositumAtPrime E F p h Q (e (x ⊗ₜ[R] y)) =
      fF x * fE y

docstring:
Global normalization base-change bridge above an unramified prime: for number
fields `E` and `F` and `p` unramified in `𝓞 F`, tensoring the semilocal
integral-closure identification of `E` with the semilocal ring of `F` identifies
`S_F ⊗[R] S_E` with the integral closure of `S_F` in the base-changed fraction
ring.

This is the normalization-under-étale-base-change route toward the compositum
step `baseChange_ramificationIdx_eq_one` and `isUnramifiedAtPrime_sup` in the
primary Lean source for ATLAS N390. The local-factor/compositum identification
needed to recover those source theorems is not claimed here.
name: NumberField.IsUnramifiedIn.tensorProductLocalizationEquivIntegralClosure
signature:
{E : Type u_2} →
  {F : Type u_3} →
    [inst : Field E] →
      [inst_1 : NumberField E] →
        [inst_2 : Field F] →
          [NumberField F] →
            (p : Ideal ℤ) →
              [inst_4 : p.IsPrime] →
                Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (NumberField.RingOfIntegers F) p →
                  let R := Localization.AtPrime p;
                  let S_F := Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (NumberField.RingOfIntegers F) p.primeCompl);
                  let S_E := Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (NumberField.RingOfIntegers E) p.primeCompl);
                  TensorProduct R S_F S_E ≃ₐ[S_F] ↥(integralClosure S_F (TensorProduct R S_F (FractionRing (NumberField.RingOfIntegers E))))
statement:
noncomputable def IsUnramifiedIn.tensorProductLocalizationEquivIntegralClosure
    {E F : Type*} [Field E] [NumberField E] [Field F] [NumberField F]
    (p : Ideal ℤ) [p.IsPrime] (h : Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (𝓞 F) p) :
    let R := Localization.AtPrime p
    let S_F := Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (𝓞 F) p.primeCompl)
    let S_E := Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (𝓞 E) p.primeCompl)
    TensorProduct R S_F S_E ≃ₐ[S_F]
      integralClosure S_F (TensorProduct R S_F (FractionRing (𝓞 E)))

docstring: Equivalence of pairs is reflexive.

docstring: Equivalence of pairs is symmetric.

theorem IsEquivalent.symm {P Q : CongruenceSubgroupPair K} :

docstring: Unfolding of `IsEquivalent` to the intersection formula.
name: NumberField.Modulus.CongruenceSubgroupPair.isEquivalent_iff
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (P Q : NumberField.Modulus.CongruenceSubgroupPair K), P.IsEquivalent Q ↔ P.modulus.coprimeFractionalIdeals ⊓ Q.subgroup.toAmbientSubgroup = Q.modulus.coprimeFractionalIdeals ⊓ P.subgroup.toAmbientSubgroup

theorem isEquivalent_iff (P Q : CongruenceSubgroupPair K) :
    IsEquivalent P Q ↔
      coprimeFractionalIdeals P.modulus ⊓ Q.subgroup.toAmbientSubgroup =
        coprimeFractionalIdeals Q.modulus ⊓ P.subgroup.toAmbientSubgroup

name: NumberField.Modulus.IsUnramifiedOutside
signature: {K : Type u_1} → [inst : Field K] → [inst_1 : NumberField K] → NumberField.Modulus K → (L : Type u_2) → [inst_2 : Field L] → [NumberField L] → [Algebra K L] → Prop

def IsUnramifiedOutside (L : Type*) [Field L] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L] :

docstring: A ray class character: homomorphism from the ray class group to `Circle`.
name: NumberField.Modulus.RayClassCharacter
signature: {K : Type u_1} → [inst : Field K] → [inst_1 : NumberField K] → NumberField.Modulus K → Type (max u_1 0)
statement: abbrev RayClassCharacter (m : Modulus K)

docstring: A character at `m2` induced by one at `m1` via level change.
name: NumberField.Modulus.RayClassCharacter.IsInducedBy
signature: {K : Type u_1} → [inst : Field K] → [inst_1 : NumberField K] → {m1 m2 : NumberField.Modulus K} → m2.RayClassCharacter → m1.RayClassCharacter → m1 ∣ m2 → Prop
statement:
def RayClassCharacter.IsInducedBy (chi2 : RayClassCharacter m2)
    (chi1 : RayClassCharacter m1) (h : m1 ∣ m2) : Prop

docstring: A character is primitive if induced only from the same modulus.
name: NumberField.Modulus.RayClassCharacter.IsPrimitive
signature: {K : Type u_1} → [inst : Field K] → [inst_1 : NumberField K] → {m2 : NumberField.Modulus K} → m2.RayClassCharacter → Prop
statement: def RayClassCharacter.IsPrimitive (chi : RayClassCharacter m2) : Prop

docstring: Induction holds iff pullbacks agree on all ideals coprime to `m2`.
name: NumberField.Modulus.RayClassCharacter.isInducedBy_iff
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {m1 m2 : NumberField.Modulus K} (chi2 : m2.RayClassCharacter) (chi1 : m1.RayClassCharacter) (h : m1 ∣ m2), chi2.IsInducedBy chi1 h ↔ ∀ (x : ↥m2.coprimeFractionalIdeals), (NumberField.Modulus.pullback chi2) x = (NumberField.Modulus.pullback chi1) ((NumberField.Modulus.coprimeInclusion h) x)
statement:
theorem RayClassCharacter.isInducedBy_iff (chi2 : RayClassCharacter m2)
    (chi1 : RayClassCharacter m1) (h : m1 ∣ m2) :
    chi2.IsInducedBy chi1 h ↔ ∀ x : coprimeFractionalIdeals m2,
      pullback chi2 x = pullback chi1 (coprimeInclusion h x)

docstring: Unfolding of primitivity to an explicit induction equation.
name: NumberField.Modulus.RayClassCharacter.isPrimitive_iff
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {m2 : NumberField.Modulus K} (chi : m2.RayClassCharacter), chi.IsPrimitive ↔ ∀ (m0 : NumberField.Modulus K) (chi0 : m0.RayClassCharacter) (h : m0 ∣ m2), chi = MonoidHom.comp chi0 (NumberField.Modulus.RayClassGroup.mapOfDvd h) → m0 = m2
statement:
theorem RayClassCharacter.isPrimitive_iff (chi : RayClassCharacter m2) :
    chi.IsPrimitive ↔ ∀ (m0 : Modulus K) (chi0 : RayClassCharacter m0)
      (h : m0 ∣ m2), chi = chi0.comp (RayClassGroup.mapOfDvd h) → m0 = m2

name: NumberField.Modulus.RayClassCharacter_apply_mul
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {m : NumberField.Modulus K} (chi : m.RayClassCharacter) (a b : m.RayClassGroup), chi (a * b) = chi a * chi b
statement:
theorem RayClassCharacter_apply_mul (chi : RayClassCharacter m)
    (a b : RayClassGroup m) :
    chi (a * b) = chi a * chi b

name: NumberField.Modulus.RayClassCharacter_apply_one
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {m : NumberField.Modulus K} (chi : m.RayClassCharacter), chi 1 = 1
statement:
theorem RayClassCharacter_apply_one (chi : RayClassCharacter m) :
    chi 1 = 1

docstring: Ray class group of a modulus: coprime ideals modulo the ray group.
name: NumberField.Modulus.RayClassGroup
signature: {K : Type u_1} → [inst : Field K] → [inst_1 : NumberField K] → NumberField.Modulus K → Type u_1
statement: abbrev RayClassGroup (m : Modulus K)

docstring: Level-change map on ray class groups.
name: NumberField.Modulus.RayClassGroup.mapOfDvd
signature: {K : Type u_1} → [inst : Field K] → [inst_1 : NumberField K] → {m1 m2 : NumberField.Modulus K} → m1 ∣ m2 → m2.RayClassGroup →* m1.RayClassGroup
statement: def RayClassGroup.mapOfDvd (h : m1 ∣ m2) : RayClassGroup m2 →* RayClassGroup m1

docstring: `mapOfDvd` on canonical representatives.
name: NumberField.Modulus.RayClassGroup.mapOfDvd_rayClassMap
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {m1 m2 : NumberField.Modulus K} (h : m1 ∣ m2) (x : ↥m2.coprimeFractionalIdeals), (NumberField.Modulus.RayClassGroup.mapOfDvd h) (m2.rayClassMap x) = m1.rayClassMap ((NumberField.Modulus.coprimeInclusion h) x)
statement:
theorem RayClassGroup.mapOfDvd_rayClassMap (h : m1 ∣ m2)
    (x : coprimeFractionalIdeals m2) :
    mapOfDvd h (rayClassMap m2 x) = rayClassMap m1 (coprimeInclusion h x)

docstring:
The Artin map on fractional ideals coprime to `m`, descended directly with
Mathlib's quotient universal property `MonoidHom.liftOfSurjective`.
name: NumberField.Modulus.artinMap
signature: {K : Type u_1} → [inst : Field K] → [inst_1 : NumberField K] → {L : Type u_2} → [inst_2 : Field L] → [inst_3 : NumberField L] → [inst_4 : Algebra K L] → [IsAbelianGalois K L] → (m : NumberField.Modulus K) → m.IsUnramifiedOutside L → ↥m.coprimeFractionalIdeals →* Gal(L/K)
statement:
noncomputable def artinMap (h : m.IsUnramifiedOutside L) :
    m.coprimeFractionalIdeals →* (L ≃ₐ[K] L)

docstring:
Exact factorization identity: the Artin map composed with the free-group
presentation is the free-group Frobenius map. Proved through the public
`liftOfRightInverse` simp API, keeping `Function.surjInv` opaque.
name: NumberField.Modulus.artinMap_comp_freeGroupToCoprime
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {L : Type u_2} [inst_2 : Field L] [inst_3 : NumberField L] [inst_4 : Algebra K L] [inst_5 : IsAbelianGalois K L] (m : NumberField.Modulus K) (h : m.IsUnramifiedOutside L), (m.artinMap h).comp m.freeGroupToCoprime = m.freeGroupToGal h
statement:
theorem artinMap_comp_freeGroupToCoprime (h : m.IsUnramifiedOutside L) :
    (m.artinMap (L := L) h).comp m.freeGroupToCoprime =
      m.freeGroupToGal (L := L) h

docstring: The Artin map evaluates on a prime generator as the unramified Frobenius.
name: NumberField.Modulus.artinMap_primeCoprimeUnit
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {L : Type u_2} [inst_2 : Field L] [inst_3 : NumberField L] [inst_4 : Algebra K L] [inst_5 : IsAbelianGalois K L] (m : NumberField.Modulus K) (h : m.IsUnramifiedOutside L) (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)) (hvm : ¬m.finiteSupported v), (m.artinMap h) (m.primeCoprimeUnit v hvm) = m.frobeniusAtCoprimePrime h ⟨v, hvm⟩
statement:
theorem artinMap_primeCoprimeUnit (h : m.IsUnramifiedOutside L)
    (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) (hvm : ¬ m.finiteSupported v) :
    m.artinMap (L := L) h (m.primeCoprimeUnit v hvm) =
      m.frobeniusAtCoprimePrime (L := L) h ⟨v, hvm⟩

docstring: Change of modulus by pullback joined with the ray group.
name: NumberField.Modulus.changeModulus
signature: {K : Type u_1} → [inst : Field K] → [inst_1 : NumberField K] → {m1 : NumberField.Modulus K} → m1.CongruenceSubgroup → (m2 : NumberField.Modulus K) → m2.CongruenceSubgroup
statement:
def changeModulus {m1 : Modulus K} (C1 : CongruenceSubgroup m1)
    (m2 : Modulus K) : CongruenceSubgroup m2

docstring: The canonical change of modulus is equivalent to the original pair.
name: NumberField.Modulus.changeModulus_isEquivalent
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {m1 m2 : NumberField.Modulus K} (C1 : m1.CongruenceSubgroup), m2 ∣ m1 → m1.coprimeFractionalIdeals ⊓ m2.rayGroupAmbient ≤ C1.toAmbientSubgroup → { modulus := m1, subgroup := C1 }.IsEquivalent { modulus := m2, subgroup := NumberField.Modulus.changeModulus C1 m2 }

docstring:
Ambient subgroup of `changeModulus`: pullback of `C1` joined
with the ambient ray group.
name: NumberField.Modulus.changeModulus_toAmbientSubgroup
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {m1 m2 : NumberField.Modulus K} (C1 : m1.CongruenceSubgroup), (NumberField.Modulus.changeModulus C1 m2).toAmbientSubgroup = C1.toAmbientSubgroup ⊓ m2.coprimeFractionalIdeals ⊔ m2.rayGroupAmbient
statement:
theorem changeModulus_toAmbientSubgroup {m1 m2 : Modulus K}
    (C1 : CongruenceSubgroup m1) :
    (changeModulus C1 m2).toAmbientSubgroup =
      (C1.toAmbientSubgroup ⊓ coprimeFractionalIdeals m2) ⊔
        rayGroupAmbient m2

docstring:
Simplified ambient form when `m2 ∣ m1`: `C1` already lies
in the coprime ideals for `m2`.
name: NumberField.Modulus.changeModulus_toAmbientSubgroup_of_dvd
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {m1 m2 : NumberField.Modulus K} (C1 : m1.CongruenceSubgroup), m2 ∣ m1 → (NumberField.Modulus.changeModulus C1 m2).toAmbientSubgroup = C1.toAmbientSubgroup ⊔ m2.rayGroupAmbient
statement:
theorem changeModulus_toAmbientSubgroup_of_dvd {m1 m2 : Modulus K}
    (C1 : CongruenceSubgroup m1) (hdiv : m2 ∣ m1) :
    (changeModulus C1 m2).toAmbientSubgroup =
      C1.toAmbientSubgroup ⊔ rayGroupAmbient m2

docstring:
Count bound for a sum of two generators with nonzero sum.

Only the nonzero-sum guard is required publicly; zero summands are handled
by reduction to the other summand.
name: NumberField.Modulus.count_spanSingleton_add_ge_of_ne_zero
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)) {x y : K} {n : ℤ}, x + y ≠ 0 → n ≤ FractionalIdeal.count K v (FractionalIdeal.spanSingleton (nonZeroDivisors (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)) x) → n ≤ FractionalIdeal.count K v (FractionalIdeal.spanSingleton (nonZeroDivisors (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)) y) → n ≤ FractionalIdeal.count K v (FractionalIdeal.spanSingleton (nonZeroDivisors (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)) (x + y))
statement:
theorem count_spanSingleton_add_ge_of_ne_zero
    (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))
    {x y : K} {n : ℤ} (hxy : x + y ≠ 0)
    (hx : n ≤ FractionalIdeal.count K v
      (FractionalIdeal.spanSingleton (𝓞 K)⁰ x))
    (hy : n ≤ FractionalIdeal.count K v
      (FractionalIdeal.spanSingleton (𝓞 K)⁰ y)) :
    n ≤ FractionalIdeal.count K v
      (FractionalIdeal.spanSingleton (𝓞 K)⁰ (x + y))

docstring:
Exact N422 criterion: an equivalent pair at `m2` exists iff the ray
condition holds at `m1`.
name: NumberField.Modulus.exists_equivalent_iff_changeModulus
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {m1 : NumberField.Modulus K} (C1 : m1.CongruenceSubgroup) {m2 : NumberField.Modulus K}, m2 ∣ m1 → ((∃ C2, { modulus := m1, subgroup := C1 }.IsEquivalent { modulus := m2, subgroup := C2 }) ↔ m1.coprimeFractionalIdeals ⊓ m2.rayGroupAmbient ≤ C1.toAmbientSubgroup)
statement:
theorem exists_equivalent_iff_changeModulus {m1 : Modulus K}
    (C1 : CongruenceSubgroup m1) {m2 : Modulus K} (hdiv : m2 ∣ m1) :
    (∃ C2 : CongruenceSubgroup m2,
      CongruenceSubgroupPair.IsEquivalent

        { modulus := m2, subgroup := C2 }) ↔
      coprimeFractionalIdeals m1 ⊓ rayGroupAmbient m2 ≤

docstring:

[`coprime_rep_exists`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/e8b31c5cb0bec89b487ce33fe525a2c0b0f8b9c6/v1/Atlas/NumberTheoryI/code/RayClassFields.lean#L1553-L1747)

signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (m : NumberField.Modulus K) (x : ↥m.rayElements), ∃ a b, IsUnit ((Ideal.Quotient.mk ↑m.finitePart) a) ∧ IsUnit ((Ideal.Quotient.mk ↑m.finitePart) b) ∧ (Algebra.algebraMap (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) a / (Algebra.algebraMap (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) b = ↑↑x

theorem exists_isUnit_mod_finitePart_div_eq
    (m : Modulus K) (x : rayElements m) :

      IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk (m.finitePart : Ideal (𝓞 K)) b) ∧
      algebraMap (𝓞 K) K a / algebraMap (𝓞 K) K b = ((x : Kˣ) : K)

docstring:
Finite-target weak approximation at the finite and real places of a modulus.

Source mapping toward ATLAS N406, Theorem 21.8, Section 21.3
(`weak_approx_coprime_sign_finitePart`, lines 2255--2568): the finite target `a`
is lifted at source lines 2267--2275 with supported valuation-one hypothesis at
2277--2292; the finite/infinite index family below is at 2314--2385;
modulus-dependent tolerances at 2388--2404; nonzero witness at 2406--2412;
valuation preservation at 2414--2451; sign control at 2458--2477; and the strict
absolute-value-to-discrete-valuation residue comparison at 2480--2568.
name: NumberField.Modulus.exists_ne_zero_with_target_and_sign
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_3} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (m : NumberField.Modulus K) (a : K) (pos : ↥m.infinitePart → Prop), a ≠ 0 → (∀ (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)), m.finiteSupported v → (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation K v) a = 1) → ∃ x, x ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)), m.finiteSupported v → (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation K v) x = 1 ∧ (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation K v) (x - a) ≤ WithZero.exp (-m.finiteExponent v)) ∧ ∀ (w : NumberField.RealPlace K) (hw : w ∈ m.infinitePart), (pos ⟨w, hw⟩ → 0 < (NumberField.InfinitePlace.embedding_of_isReal ⋯) x) ∧ (¬pos ⟨w, hw⟩ → (NumberField.InfinitePlace.embedding_of_isReal ⋯) x < 0)
statement:
theorem exists_ne_zero_with_target_and_sign
    (m : Modulus K) (a : K)
    (pos : {w : RealPlace K // w ∈ m.infinitePart} → Prop)
    (ha0 : a ≠ 0)
    (haval : ∀ v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K),
      finiteSupported m v → v.valuation K a = 1) :
    ∃ x : K, x ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K),
        finiteSupported m v →
          v.valuation K x = 1 ∧
          v.valuation K (x - a) ≤ WithZero.exp (-(finiteExponent m v))) ∧
      ∀ (w : RealPlace K) (hw : w ∈ m.infinitePart),
        (pos ⟨w, hw⟩ → 0 < InfinitePlace.embedding_of_isReal w.property x) ∧
        (¬ pos ⟨w, hw⟩ → InfinitePlace.embedding_of_isReal w.property x < 0)

docstring:
Simultaneous weak approximation at the finite and real places of a modulus.

Retained API: the `a = 1` specialization of
`exists_ne_zero_with_target_and_sign`.
name: NumberField.Modulus.exists_ne_zero_with_valuation_one_and_sign
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_3} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (m : NumberField.Modulus K) (pos : ↥m.infinitePart → Prop), ∃ x, x ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)), m.finiteSupported v → (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation K v) x = 1) ∧ ∀ (w : NumberField.RealPlace K) (hw : w ∈ m.infinitePart), (pos ⟨w, hw⟩ → 0 < (NumberField.InfinitePlace.embedding_of_isReal ⋯) x) ∧ (¬pos ⟨w, hw⟩ → (NumberField.InfinitePlace.embedding_of_isReal ⋯) x < 0)
statement:
theorem exists_ne_zero_with_valuation_one_and_sign
    (m : Modulus K)
    (pos : {w : RealPlace K // w ∈ m.infinitePart} → Prop) :
    ∃ x : K, x ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K),
        finiteSupported m v → v.valuation K x = 1) ∧
      ∀ (w : RealPlace K) (hw : w ∈ m.infinitePart),
        (pos ⟨w, hw⟩ → 0 < InfinitePlace.embedding_of_isReal w.property x) ∧
        (¬ pos ⟨w, hw⟩ → InfinitePlace.embedding_of_isReal w.property x < 0)

docstring:
Valuation criterion for triviality of the finite residue map: a valuation bound
on `z - 1` at every supported finite place forces `finiteResidueMap m z = 1`.

Source mapping (N406, Theorem 21.8, Section 21.3; ATLAS NumberTheoryI item N406):
the native-API finite-congruence step corresponding to
[`finitePartMapHom_ker_iff`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/e8b31c5cb0bec89b487ce33fe525a2c0b0f8b9c6/v1/Atlas/NumberTheoryI/code/RayClassFields.lean#L1996-L2011),
used by the weak-approximation argument before residue/sign surjectivity and by
[`theorem_21_8_quotient_iso`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/e8b31c5cb0bec89b487ce33fe525a2c0b0f8b9c6/v1/Atlas/NumberTheoryI/code/RayClassFields.lean#L2607-L2647).
It is not the generalized weak-approximation theorem and not the final N406
result.
name: NumberField.Modulus.finiteResidueMap_eq_one_of_valuation_le
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (m : NumberField.Modulus K) (z : ↥m.rayElements), (∀ (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)), m.finiteSupported v → (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation K v) (↑↑z - 1) ≤ WithZero.exp (-m.finiteExponent v)) → m.finiteResidueMap z = 1
statement:
theorem finiteResidueMap_eq_one_of_valuation_le
    (m : Modulus K) (z : rayElements m)
    (h : ∀ v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K),
      finiteSupported m v →
        v.valuation K (((z : Kˣ) : K) - 1) ≤
          WithZero.exp (-(finiteExponent m v))) :
    finiteResidueMap m z = 1

`Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt` conjunct).

signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (m : NumberField.Modulus K) {L : Type u_2} [inst_2 : Field L] [inst_3 : NumberField L] [inst_4 : Algebra K L] [inst_5 : IsGalois K L] (h : m.IsUnramifiedOutside L) (p : m.CoprimePrimes), ∃ Q, Finite (NumberField.RingOfIntegers L ⧸ ↑Q) ∧ (↑Q).LiesOver (↑p).asIdeal ∧ Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) ↑Q ∧ IsArithFrobAt (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) (m.frobeniusAtCoprimePrime h p) ↑Q
statement:
theorem frobeniusAtCoprimePrime_spec (h : m.IsUnramifiedOutside L)
    (p : m.CoprimePrimes) :
    ∃ Q : Ideal.primesOver p.val.asIdeal (𝓞 L),
      Finite (𝓞 L ⧸ Q.1) ∧ Q.1.LiesOver p.val.asIdeal ∧
        Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (𝓞 K) Q.1 ∧
        IsArithFrobAt (𝓞 K) (m.frobeniusAtCoprimePrime (L := L) h p) Q.1

docstring:
Valuation-one criterion for ray elements: if the normalized valuation of `a`
is one at every finite prime supported by `m`, then the principal fractional
ideal `(a)` has count zero at each such prime, so `a ∈ rayElements m`.

This is the converse of `rayElement_valuation_eq_one`: the converse valuation
criterion used to turn the controlled approximation witness into a ray element.
It is a reusable bridge toward N406, not itself the full source theorem.
name: NumberField.Modulus.mem_rayElements_of_valuation_eq_one
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (m : NumberField.Modulus K) (a : Kˣ), (∀ (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)), m.finiteSupported v → (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation K v) ↑a = 1) → a ∈ m.rayElements
statement:
theorem mem_rayElements_of_valuation_eq_one
    (m : Modulus K) (a : Kˣ)
    (h : ∀ v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K),
      finiteSupported m v → v.valuation K ((a : K)) = 1) :
    a ∈ rayElements m

statement:

      Subgroup.mem_comap.mp hx.1⟩ :
      coprimeFractionalIdeals m) ∈ rayGroup m

signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (m : NumberField.Modulus K) (a b c d : NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) (ha : IsUnit ((Ideal.Quotient.mk ↑m.finitePart) a)) (hb : IsUnit ((Ideal.Quotient.mk ↑m.finitePart) b)) (hc : IsUnit ((Ideal.Quotient.mk ↑m.finitePart) c)) (hd : IsUnit ((Ideal.Quotient.mk ↑m.finitePart) d)), (Algebra.algebraMap (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) a / (Algebra.algebraMap (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) b = (Algebra.algebraMap (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) c / (Algebra.algebraMap (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) d → ha.unit * hb.unit⁻¹ = hc.unit * hd.unit⁻¹

theorem quotientUnits_div_eq_of_div_eq
    (m : Modulus K) (a b c d : 𝓞 K)

    (hb : IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk (m.finitePart : Ideal (𝓞 K)) b))
    (hc : IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk (m.finitePart : Ideal (𝓞 K)) c))
    (hd : IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk (m.finitePart : Ideal (𝓞 K)) d))
    (h : algebraMap (𝓞 K) K a / algebraMap (𝓞 K) K b =
      algebraMap (𝓞 K) K c / algebraMap (𝓞 K) K d) :
    ha.unit * hb.unit⁻¹ = hc.unit * hd.unit⁻¹

docstring:
Six-term exact sequence, residue-sign form: aggregation of the separately
source-backed map/exactness/surjectivity declarations from ATLAS lines
1012--1480 (not a direct declaration port), additionally transported through
the quotient equivalence backed by lines 2607--2647.
name: NumberField.Modulus.rayClass_residueSign_six_term_exact
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (m : NumberField.Modulus K), Function.Injective ⇑m.integralRayOneUnitsInclusion ∧ Function.MulExact ⇑m.integralRayOneUnitsInclusion ⇑m.integralUnitsToResidueSign ∧ Function.MulExact ⇑m.integralUnitsToResidueSign ⇑m.residueSignToRayClassGroup ∧ Function.MulExact ⇑m.residueSignToRayClassGroup ⇑m.rayClassToClassGroup ∧ Function.Surjective ⇑m.rayClassToClassGroup
statement:

    Function.Injective (integralRayOneUnitsInclusion m) ∧
    Function.MulExact (integralRayOneUnitsInclusion m)
      (integralUnitsToResidueSign m) ∧
    Function.MulExact (integralUnitsToResidueSign m)
      (residueSignToRayClassGroup m) ∧
    Function.MulExact (residueSignToRayClassGroup m)
      (rayClassToClassGroup m) ∧
    Function.Surjective (rayClassToClassGroup m)

docstring:

signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (m : NumberField.Modulus K), Function.Injective ⇑m.integralRayOneUnitsInclusion ∧ Function.MulExact ⇑m.integralRayOneUnitsInclusion ⇑m.integralUnitsToRayQuotient ∧ Function.MulExact ⇑m.integralUnitsToRayQuotient ⇑m.rayQuotientToRayClassGroup ∧ Function.MulExact ⇑m.rayQuotientToRayClassGroup ⇑m.rayClassToClassGroup ∧ Function.Surjective ⇑m.rayClassToClassGroup

      (rayClassToClassGroup m) ∧

A ray element has valuation one at every finite prime supported by the modulus.
Source (N406 §21.3): the supported-finite-place fact; compare
[`valuation_eq_one_of_spanSingleton_coprime'`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/e8b31c5cb0bec89b487ce33fe525a2c0b0f8b9c6/v1/Atlas/NumberTheoryI/code/RayClassFields.lean#L1206-L1248)

docstring:
Restriction of the `M`-Artin map at a prime generator agrees with the
`L`-Artin map at the same generator.
name: NumberField.Modulus.restrictNormalHom_artinMap_primeCoprimeUnit
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : Field L] [inst_2 : Field M] [inst_3 : NumberField K] [inst_4 : NumberField L] [inst_5 : NumberField M] [inst_6 : Algebra K L] [inst_7 : Algebra K M] [inst_8 : Algebra L M] [inst_9 : IsScalarTower K L M] [inst_10 : IsAbelianGalois K L] [inst_11 : IsAbelianGalois K M] (m : NumberField.Modulus K) (hL : m.IsUnramifiedOutside L) (hM : m.IsUnramifiedOutside M) (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)) (hvm : ¬m.finiteSupported v), (AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom L) ((m.artinMap hM) (m.primeCoprimeUnit v hvm)) = (m.artinMap hL) (m.primeCoprimeUnit v hvm)
statement:
theorem restrictNormalHom_artinMap_primeCoprimeUnit
    (m : Modulus K) (hL : m.IsUnramifiedOutside L)
    (hM : m.IsUnramifiedOutside M)
    (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K))
    (hvm : ¬ m.finiteSupported v) :
    AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom L
        (m.artinMap (L := M) hM (m.primeCoprimeUnit v hvm)) =
      m.artinMap (L := L) hL (m.primeCoprimeUnit v hvm)

docstring:
Restriction of the `M`-Artin map agrees with the `L`-Artin map as bundled
homomorphisms.
name: NumberField.Modulus.restrictNormalHom_comp_artinMap
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : Field L] [inst_2 : Field M] [inst_3 : NumberField K] [inst_4 : NumberField L] [inst_5 : NumberField M] [inst_6 : Algebra K L] [inst_7 : Algebra K M] [inst_8 : Algebra L M] [inst_9 : IsScalarTower K L M] [inst_10 : IsAbelianGalois K L] [inst_11 : IsAbelianGalois K M] (m : NumberField.Modulus K) (hL : m.IsUnramifiedOutside L) (hM : m.IsUnramifiedOutside M), (AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom L).comp (m.artinMap hM) = m.artinMap hL
statement:
theorem restrictNormalHom_comp_artinMap
    (m : Modulus K) (hL : m.IsUnramifiedOutside L)
    (hM : m.IsUnramifiedOutside M) :
    (AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom L).comp (m.artinMap (L := M) hM) =
      m.artinMap (L := L) hL

docstring:
Restriction of the chosen Frobenius at `p` from `M` agrees with the chosen
Frobenius at `p` on the abelian subextension `L`. The lower abelianity is used
only to trivialize conjugation of the lower Frobenius value.
name: NumberField.Modulus.restrictNormalHom_frobeniusAtCoprimePrime
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : Field L] [inst_2 : Field M] [inst_3 : NumberField K] [inst_4 : NumberField L] [inst_5 : NumberField M] [inst_6 : Algebra K L] [inst_7 : Algebra K M] [inst_8 : Algebra L M] [inst_9 : IsScalarTower K L M] [inst_10 : IsAbelianGalois K L] [inst_11 : IsGalois K M] (m : NumberField.Modulus K) (hL : m.IsUnramifiedOutside L) (hM : m.IsUnramifiedOutside M) (p : m.CoprimePrimes), (AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom L) (m.frobeniusAtCoprimePrime hM p) = m.frobeniusAtCoprimePrime hL p
statement:
theorem restrictNormalHom_frobeniusAtCoprimePrime
    (m : Modulus K) (hL : m.IsUnramifiedOutside L)
    (hM : m.IsUnramifiedOutside M) (p : m.CoprimePrimes) :
    AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom L
        (m.frobeniusAtCoprimePrime (L := M) hM p) =
      m.frobeniusAtCoprimePrime (L := L) hL p

docstring: Sign of a unit at a real place, valued in `Multiplicative (ZMod 2)`.

signature: {K : Type u_1} → [inst : Field K] → [inst_1 : NumberField K] → NumberField.RealPlace K → Kˣ →* Multiplicative (ZMod 2)

name: NumberField.Modulus.signAtRealPlace_apply_eq_one_iff
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (w : NumberField.RealPlace K) (x : Kˣ), (NumberField.Modulus.signAtRealPlace w) x = 1 ↔ 0 < (NumberField.InfinitePlace.embedding_of_isReal ⋯) ↑x
statement:
theorem signAtRealPlace_apply_eq_one_iff (w : RealPlace K) (x : Kˣ) :
    signAtRealPlace w x = 1 ↔

docstring: Equality of principal ideals is equality up to an integral unit.
name: NumberField.Modulus.toPrincipalIdeal_eq_iff_exists_integralUnit_mul
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (x y : Kˣ), (toPrincipalIdeal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) x = (toPrincipalIdeal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) y ↔ ∃ u, x = (Units.map ↑(Algebra.algebraMap (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K)) u * y

theorem toPrincipalIdeal_eq_iff_exists_integralUnit_mul (x y : Kˣ) :
    toPrincipalIdeal (𝓞 K) K x = toPrincipalIdeal (𝓞 K) K y ↔

docstring:
Polar density of a set of height-one primes, via a meromorphic continuation.

`HasPolarDensity S ρ` asserts the existence of a positive exponent `n : ℕ+`, a
pole order `m : ℤ`, and an actual meromorphic continuation `F : ℂ → ℂ` such that
`F` is meromorphic at `1`, agrees with the pointwise `n`-th power of the partial
Dedekind zeta function on the right-half-plane germ at `1`, has
`meromorphicOrderAt F 1 = -m`, and `ρ = m / n`.
name: NumberField.Set.HasPolarDensity
signature: {K : Type u_1} → [inst : Field K] → [NumberField K] → Set (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)) → ℚ → Prop
statement: def HasPolarDensity (S : Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))) (ρ : ℚ) : Prop

docstring:
Uniqueness of the polar density: the `NeBot`/closure argument above is
essential, without it side equality could be vacuous.
name: NumberField.Set.HasPolarDensity.unique
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {S : Set (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K))} {ρ₁ ρ₂ : ℚ}, NumberField.Set.HasPolarDensity S ρ₁ → NumberField.Set.HasPolarDensity S ρ₂ → ρ₁ = ρ₂
statement:
theorem HasPolarDensity.unique {S : Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))} {ρ₁ ρ₂ : ℚ}
    (h₁ : S.HasPolarDensity ρ₁) (h₂ : S.HasPolarDensity ρ₂) : ρ₁ = ρ₂

docstring:
The empty set of height-one primes has polar density `0`, witnessed by the
constant continuation `F = fun _ => 1` with `n = 1` and `m = 0`.
name: NumberField.Set.hasPolarDensity_empty
signature: ∀ (K : Type u_2) [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K], NumberField.Set.HasPolarDensity ∅ 0
statement:
theorem hasPolarDensity_empty (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] :
    (∅ : Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))).HasPolarDensity 0

docstring:
The topological idele class group, namely the quotient of the topological idele
group by principal ideles. Upstream `NumberField.IdeleClassGroup` (the quotient of
`𝔸[R, K]ˣ`) is a distinct type.
name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleClassGroup
signature: (R : Type u_1) → (K : Type u_2) → [inst : CommRing R] → [IsDedekindDomain R] → [inst_2 : Field K] → [inst_3 : Algebra R K] → [IsFractionRing R K] → Type (max (max u_2 u_1) u_1 u_2)
statement: abbrev TopologicalIdeleClassGroup

docstring:
The topological idele group, with the standard product/restricted-product topology.

This is the product of the infinite ideles and the finite ideles. It carries the
product of the infinite-place product topology and the finite restricted-product
topology, which differs from the subspace topology on the units of the adele ring.
Upstream `NumberField.IdeleGroup` (`𝔸[R, K]ˣ`) is a distinct type.
name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup
signature: (R : Type u_1) → (K : Type u_2) → [inst : CommRing R] → [IsDedekindDomain R] → [inst_2 : Field K] → [inst_3 : Algebra R K] → [IsFractionRing R K] → Type (max u_2 u_2 u_1)
statement: def TopologicalIdeleGroup

docstring: The norm-one idele class group `C_K^1 := I_K^1 / K^×`.
name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.NormOneIdeleClassGroup
signature: (K : Type u_1) → [inst : Field K] → [NumberField K] → Type u_1
statement: public abbrev NormOneIdeleClassGroup

docstring: The adelic norm of an idele: archimedean factor times finite finprod factor.
name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.adelicNorm
signature: (K : Type u_1) → [inst : Field K] → [inst_1 : NumberField K] → NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K →* ℝ
statement: public noncomputable def adelicNorm : TopologicalIdeleGroup (𝓞 K) K →* ℝ

docstring: Evaluation of the adelic norm of an idele.
name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.adelicNorm_apply
signature: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (a : NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K), (NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.adelicNorm K) a = (∏ w, ‖↑(a.1 w)‖ ^ w.mult) * ∏ᶠ (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)), ‖↑(a.2 v)‖
statement:
public theorem adelicNorm_apply (a : TopologicalIdeleGroup (𝓞 K) K) :
    adelicNorm K a =
      (∏ w : InfinitePlace K, ‖(a.1 w : w.Completion)‖ ^ w.mult) *
        ∏ᶠ v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K),
          ‖(a.2 v : v.adicCompletion K)‖

docstring: The adelic norm of a principal idele is one (product formula).
name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.adelicNorm_principalEmbedding
signature: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (x : Kˣ), (NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.adelicNorm K) ((NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.principalEmbedding (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) x) = 1
statement:
public theorem adelicNorm_principalEmbedding (x : Kˣ) :
    adelicNorm K (principalEmbedding (𝓞 K) K x) = 1

docstring: The diagonal embedding of global units into the finite ideles.
name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.finitePrincipalEmbedding
signature: (R : Type u_1) → (K : Type u_2) → [inst : CommRing R] → [inst_1 : IsDedekindDomain R] → [inst_2 : Field K] → [inst_3 : Algebra R K] → [inst_4 : IsFractionRing R K] → Kˣ →* NumberField.FiniteIdeleGroup R K
statement: def finitePrincipalEmbedding : Kˣ →* FiniteIdeleGroup R K

name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.finitePrincipalEmbedding_apply
signature: ∀ (R : Type u_1) (K : Type u_2) [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : IsDedekindDomain R] [inst_2 : Field K] [inst_3 : Algebra R K] [inst_4 : IsFractionRing R K] (x : Kˣ) (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum R), ((NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.finitePrincipalEmbedding R K) x) v = (Units.map ↑(Algebra.algebraMap K (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.adicCompletion K v))) x
statement:
theorem finitePrincipalEmbedding_apply (x : Kˣ) (v : HeightOneSpectrum R) :
    finitePrincipalEmbedding R K x v =
      Units.map (algebraMap K (v.adicCompletion K)).toMonoidHom x

docstring: The diagonal embedding of global units into the infinite ideles.
name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.infinitePrincipalEmbedding
signature: (K : Type u_2) → [inst : Field K] → Kˣ →* NumberField.InfiniteIdeleGroup K
statement: def infinitePrincipalEmbedding : Kˣ →* InfiniteIdeleGroup K

name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.infinitePrincipalEmbedding_apply
signature: ∀ (K : Type u_2) [inst : Field K] (x : Kˣ) (v : NumberField.InfinitePlace K), (NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.infinitePrincipalEmbedding K) x v = (Units.map ↑(Algebra.algebraMap K v.Completion)) x
statement:
theorem infinitePrincipalEmbedding_apply (x : Kˣ) (v : InfinitePlace K) :
    infinitePrincipalEmbedding K x v =
      Units.map (algebraMap K v.Completion).toMonoidHom x

signature: (R : Type u_1) → (K : Type u_2) → [inst : CommRing R] → [inst_1 : IsDedekindDomain R] → [inst_2 : Field K] → [inst_3 : Algebra R K] → [inst_4 : IsFractionRing R K] → CommGroup (NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup R K)

docstring: Membership in the norm-one ideles.
name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.mem_normOneIdeles
signature: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {a : NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K}, a ∈ NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.normOneIdeles K ↔ (NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.adelicNorm K) a = 1
statement:
public theorem mem_normOneIdeles {a : TopologicalIdeleGroup (𝓞 K) K} :
    a ∈ normOneIdeles K ↔ adelicNorm K a = 1

docstring: Norm-one ideles: kernel of the adelic norm.
name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.normOneIdeles
signature: (K : Type u_1) → [inst : Field K] → [inst_1 : NumberField K] → Subgroup (NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K)

docstring: Principal ideles viewed inside the norm-one ideles.
name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.normOnePrincipalIdeles
signature: (K : Type u_1) → [inst : Field K] → [inst_1 : NumberField K] → Subgroup ↥(NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.normOneIdeles K)
statement: public def normOnePrincipalIdeles : Subgroup (normOneIdeles K)

docstring: The class of a principal idele in the norm-one idele class group is trivial.
name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.normOne_mk_principalEmbedding
signature: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] (x : Kˣ), ↑⟨(NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.principalEmbedding (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) x, ⋯⟩ = 1
statement:
public theorem normOne_mk_principalEmbedding (x : Kˣ) :
    QuotientGroup.mk (s := normOnePrincipalIdeles K)
        ⟨principalEmbedding (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K x,
          principalIdeles_le_normOneIdeles K ⟨x, rfl⟩⟩ = 1

name: NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup.principalEmbedding
signature: (R : Type u_1) → (K : Type u_2) → [inst : CommRing R] → [inst_1 : IsDedekindDomain R] → [inst_2 : Field K] → [inst_3 : Algebra R K] → [inst_4 : IsFractionRing R K] → Kˣ →* NumberField.TopologicalIdeleGroup R K

docstring:
A family of units that is `< 1` off the diagonal generates a subgroup of finite
index: if `w (u v) < 1` whenever `w ≠ v`, then the subgroup generated by the range
of `u` has finite index in `(𝓞 F)ˣ`.

The logarithmic images form a column strictly diagonally dominant system — the
off-diagonal components are negative while each column sum is positive — hence
are linearly independent by `det_ne_zero_of_sum_col_lt_diag`. Maximal rank is
transported along `equivFinRank` and concluded with
`isMaxRank_iff_closure_finiteIndex` and `Subgroup.finiteIndex_of_le`.

docstring:
A solution of a `C²` ODE has a uniform quadratic explicit-Euler local error on a compact
time interval.

signature: ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] (f : ℝ → E → E) (t₀ T : ℝ), t₀ < T → ContDiff ℝ 2 (Function.uncurry f) → ∀ (x : ℝ → E), (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc t₀ T, HasDerivAt x (f t (x t)) t) → ∃ C, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ h ∈ Set.Ioc 0 (T - t₀), ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc t₀ T, t + h ≤ T → ‖x (t + h) - (x t + h • f t (x t))‖ ≤ C * h ^ 2
statement:
theorem _root_.ODE.exists_explicitEuler_localTruncationError_le
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]

docstring:
Pointwise pole multiplicity of `f` at `z`, defined locally from
`meromorphicOrderAt f z`.

The multiplicity is the negation of the order, truncated to `ℕ`: a pole of order
`-n` contributes `n`, while zeros, nonzero values, and points where `f` is not
locally meromorphic (junk order `0`) contribute `0`. Since only the local order is
used, the value at `z` never depends on the behavior of `f` far away from `z`.

docstring:
Flexible Hamming distance between a small permutation `σ` of `Fin n` and a
large permutation `τ` of `Fin m` (with `h : n ≤ m`): the disagreement count on
the embedded copy plus the `m - n` unmatched points, normalized by `n`.

Kourovka 21.84 is internally inconsistent about the argument order: it first
defines the distance with the small permutation first, `d_n^flex(σ, τ)` for
`σ ∈ S_n`, `τ ∈ S_m`, but later writes the convergence expression with
`ρ_n(g)` first. This formalization follows the definition site (small first),
which is also the type-correct order for the embedding `Fin n → Fin m`.

As above, the `n = 0` denominator is harmless for `Filter.atTop`
convergence.
name: PermutationStability.flexibleHammingDistance
signature: {n m : ℕ} → n ≤ m → Equiv.Perm (Fin n) → Equiv.Perm (Fin m) → ℝ
statement:
noncomputable def flexibleHammingDistance {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m)
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m)) : ℝ

name: PermutationStability.flexibleHammingDistance_diagonal
signature: ∀ {n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ n) (σ τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)), PermutationStability.flexibleHammingDistance h σ τ = PermutationStability.normalizedHammingDistance n σ τ
statement:
theorem flexibleHammingDistance_diagonal {n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ n)
    (σ τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    flexibleHammingDistance h σ τ = normalizedHammingDistance n σ τ

name: PermutationStability.flexibleHammingDistance_self
signature: ∀ {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m)), (∀ (i : Fin n), τ (Fin.castLE h i) = Fin.castLE h (σ i)) → PermutationStability.flexibleHammingDistance h σ τ = ↑(m - n) / ↑n
statement:
theorem flexibleHammingDistance_self {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m)
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m))
    (hτ : ∀ i, τ (Fin.castLE h i) = Fin.castLE h (σ i)) :
    flexibleHammingDistance h σ τ = ((m - n : ℕ) : ℝ) / n

name: PerronKernel.boundary_rect_one_div
signature: ∀ {a b T : ℝ}, a < 0 → 0 < b → 0 < T → ((∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, 1 / (↑x + -↑T * Complex.I)) - ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, 1 / (↑x + ↑T * Complex.I)) + Complex.I * ((∫ (y : ℝ) in -T..T, 1 / (↑b + ↑y * Complex.I)) - ∫ (y : ℝ) in -T..T, 1 / (↑a + ↑y * Complex.I)) = 2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I
statement:
theorem boundary_rect_one_div {a b T : ℝ} (ha : a < 0) (hb : 0 < b) (hT : 0 < T) :
    (∫ x : ℝ in a..b, (1 : ℂ) / (x + -T * Complex.I))
      - (∫ x : ℝ in a..b, (1 : ℂ) / (x + T * Complex.I))

        - (∫ y : ℝ in (-T)..T, (1 : ℂ) / (a + y * Complex.I))) =
        2 * Real.pi * Complex.I

name: PerronKernel.boundary_rect_one_div_outside

statement:
theorem boundary_rect_one_div_outside {a b T : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a ≤ b)

name: PerronKernel.horiz_diff_one_div
signature: ∀ {a b T : ℝ}, T ≠ 0 → a ≤ b → (∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, 1 / (↑x + -↑T * Complex.I)) - ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, 1 / (↑x + ↑T * Complex.I) = 2 * Complex.I * (↑(Real.arctan (b / T)) - ↑(Real.arctan (a / T)))

docstring: Horizontal side bound over `[c, U]`, exact value (no sign hypothesis on `L`).
name: PerronKernel.horiz_side_bound_exact
signature: ∀ {y U c T e : ℝ}, 0 < y → c ≤ U → 0 < T → e = T ∨ e = -T → Real.log y ≠ 0 → ‖∫ (x : ℝ) in c..U, ↑y ^ (↑x + ↑e * Complex.I) / (↑x + ↑e * Complex.I)‖ ≤ (Real.exp (Real.log y * U) - Real.exp (Real.log y * c)) / Real.log y / T
statement:
theorem horiz_side_bound_exact {y U c T e : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y)

    ‖∫ x : ℝ in c..U, (y : ℂ) ^ ((x : ℂ) + (e : ℂ) * Complex.I)

        / Real.log y / T

statement:
theorem horiz_side_bound_gt_one {y U c T e : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) (hy1 : 1 < y)

name: PerronKernel.integral_div_add_sq

docstring: Slope of the remainder at `0`, in integral form.

docstring: Rectangle identity for `y^s/s` with the pole inside (`y > 1` case).
name: PerronKernel.rect_identity_gt_one
signature: ∀ {y U c T : ℝ}, 0 < y → 0 < U → 0 < c → 0 < T → ((∫ (x : ℝ) in -U..c, ↑y ^ (↑x + ↑(-T) * Complex.I) / (↑x + ↑(-T) * Complex.I)) - ∫ (x : ℝ) in -U..c, ↑y ^ (↑x + ↑T * Complex.I) / (↑x + ↑T * Complex.I)) + Complex.I * ((∫ (t : ℝ) in -T..T, ↑y ^ (↑c + ↑t * Complex.I) / (↑c + ↑t * Complex.I)) - ∫ (t : ℝ) in -T..T, ↑y ^ (↑(-U) + ↑t * Complex.I) / (↑(-U) + ↑t * Complex.I)) = 2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I
statement:
theorem rect_identity_gt_one {y U c T : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) (hU : 0 < U) (hc : 0 < c)
    (hT : 0 < T) :
    (∫ x : ℝ in (-U)..c, (y : ℂ) ^ ((x : ℂ) + ((-T : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
        / ((x : ℂ) + ((-T : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I))

        / ((x : ℂ) + ((T : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I))
      + Complex.I * ((∫ t : ℝ in (-T)..T, (y : ℂ) ^ ((c : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * Complex.I)
          / ((c : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * Complex.I))
        - (∫ t : ℝ in (-T)..T, (y : ℂ) ^ (((-U : ℝ) : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * Complex.I)
          / (((-U : ℝ) : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * Complex.I)))

docstring: Rectangle identity for `y^s/s` with the pole outside (`y < 1` case).
name: PerronKernel.rect_identity_lt_one
signature: ∀ {y U c T : ℝ}, 0 < y → c < U → 0 < c → 0 < T → ((∫ (x : ℝ) in c..U, ↑y ^ (↑x + ↑(-T) * Complex.I) / (↑x + ↑(-T) * Complex.I)) - ∫ (x : ℝ) in c..U, ↑y ^ (↑x + ↑T * Complex.I) / (↑x + ↑T * Complex.I)) + Complex.I * ((∫ (t : ℝ) in -T..T, ↑y ^ (↑U + ↑t * Complex.I) / (↑U + ↑t * Complex.I)) - ∫ (t : ℝ) in -T..T, ↑y ^ (↑c + ↑t * Complex.I) / (↑c + ↑t * Complex.I)) = 0

theorem rect_identity_lt_one {y U c T : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) (hcU : c < U) (hc : 0 < c)

name: PerronKernel.vertical_side_one_div
signature: ∀ {c T : ℝ}, c ≠ 0 → 0 ≤ T → ∫ (y : ℝ) in -T..T, 1 / (↑c + ↑y * Complex.I) = 2 * ↑(Real.arctan (T / c))

docstring: Weaker corollary: only the existence of the subfamily and the equivalence.
name: PiFieldQuotient.exists_algEquiv
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} [inst : Field K] {ι : Type u_1} {F : ι → Type v} [inst_1 : (i : ι) → Field (F i)] [inst_2 : (i : ι) → Algebra K (F i)] {B : Type w} [inst_3 : CommRing B] [inst_4 : Algebra K B] [Finite ι] (φ : ((i : ι) → F i) →ₐ[K] B), Function.Surjective ⇑φ → ∃ S, Nonempty (B ≃ₐ[K] (i : ↥S) → F ↑i)
statement:
public theorem exists_algEquiv
    (φ : (∀ i, F i) →ₐ[K] B) (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) :
    ∃ S : Finset ι, Nonempty (B ≃ₐ[K] (∀ i : S, F i))

docstring:
A surjective algebra map out of a finite product of fields exhibits its target as
coordinate restriction to a subfamily, up to `K`-algebra equivalence.
name: PiFieldQuotient.exists_algEquiv_restrict
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} [inst : Field K] {ι : Type u_1} {F : ι → Type v} [inst_1 : (i : ι) → Field (F i)] [inst_2 : (i : ι) → Algebra K (F i)] {B : Type w} [inst_3 : CommRing B] [inst_4 : Algebra K B] [Finite ι] (φ : ((i : ι) → F i) →ₐ[K] B), Function.Surjective ⇑φ → ∃ S e, (↑e).comp φ = AlgHom.pi fun i ↦ Pi.evalAlgHom K F ↑i
statement:
public theorem exists_algEquiv_restrict
    (φ : (∀ i, F i) →ₐ[K] B) (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) :
    ∃ S : Finset ι, ∃ e : B ≃ₐ[K] (∀ i : S, F i),
      e.toAlgHom.comp φ = AlgHom.pi (fun i : S => Pi.evalAlgHom K F i)

docstring:
A product algebra equivalence induces a permutation of the factors together
with factorwise algebra equivalences. In particular the decomposition of a
finite product of fields into fields is unique up to permutation and
factorwise `K`-algebra equivalence.

This is the multiplicity-preserving correction of
`EtaleAlgebra.etale_decomposition_unique` from the primary Lean source for
ATLAS N83, Corollary 4.33.
name: PiFieldQuotient.exists_indexEquiv_algEquiv
signature: ∀ {K : Type u} [inst : Field K] {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] {κ : Type w} [Finite κ] {F : ι → Type x} [inst_3 : (i : ι) → Field (F i)] [inst_4 : (i : ι) → Algebra K (F i)] {G : κ → Type y} [inst_5 : (j : κ) → Field (G j)] [inst_6 : (j : κ) → Algebra K (G j)] (e : ((i : ι) → F i) ≃ₐ[K] (j : κ) → G j), ∃ σ, ∀ (i : ι), Nonempty (F i ≃ₐ[K] G (σ i))
statement:
public theorem exists_indexEquiv_algEquiv
    {K : Type u} [Field K]
    {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] {κ : Type w} [Finite κ]
    {F : ι → Type x} [∀ i, Field (F i)] [∀ i, Algebra K (F i)]
    {G : κ → Type y} [∀ j, Field (G j)] [∀ j, Algebra K (G j)]

    ∃ σ : ι ≃ κ, ∀ i, Nonempty (F i ≃ₐ[K] G (σ i))

docstring:

docstring:
Greatest common monic divisor (pseudo1.tex lines 617-624).
`IsGreatestCommonMonicDivisor h g1 g2` holds when `h`, `g1` and `g2` are monic
polynomials over a commutative ring and the ideal generated by `g1` and `g2`
equals the principal ideal generated by `h`. Existence is not automatic.
name: Polynomial.IsGreatestCommonMonicDivisor
signature: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : CommRing R] → Polynomial R → Polynomial R → Polynomial R → Prop
statement:
public def IsGreatestCommonMonicDivisor {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (h g₁ g₂ : _root_.Polynomial R) : Prop

docstring: Unfolding of `Polynomial.IsGreatestCommonMonicDivisor`.
name: Polynomial.IsGreatestCommonMonicDivisor.unfold
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (h g₁ g₂ : Polynomial R), h.IsGreatestCommonMonicDivisor g₁ g₂ ↔ h.Monic ∧ g₁.Monic ∧ g₂.Monic ∧ Ideal.span {g₁, g₂} = Ideal.span {h}
statement:
public theorem IsGreatestCommonMonicDivisor.unfold {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (h g₁ g₂ : _root_.Polynomial R) :
    IsGreatestCommonMonicDivisor h g₁ g₂ ↔
      (h.Monic ∧ g₁.Monic ∧ g₂.Monic ∧
        Ideal.span ({g₁, g₂} : Set (_root_.Polynomial R)) =
          Ideal.span ({h} : Set (_root_.Polynomial R)))

docstring:

index `i ≤ k`, with `i` cast into `F`. The source assumes positive `k`; the
predicate is stated for all natural levels, with the positive-level
characterization `isKComplete_succ_iff` and the zero-level boundary
`isKComplete_zero` below.

    (k : ℕ) : Prop

signature: ∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : IsDomain A] [inst_2 : IsDiscreteValuationRing A] (f : Polynomial A) (a a₀ : A), (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval a₀ (Polynomial.derivative f)) < (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (a - a₀) → (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval a (Polynomial.derivative f)) = (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval a₀ (Polynomial.derivative f))

name: Polynomial.eq_of_isRoot_of_addVal_derivative_lt_addVal_sub
signature: ∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : IsDomain A] [inst_2 : IsDiscreteValuationRing A] (f : Polynomial A) (a a' a₀ : A), f.IsRoot a → f.IsRoot a' → (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval a₀ (Polynomial.derivative f)) < (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (a - a₀) → (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval a₀ (Polynomial.derivative f)) < (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (a' - a₀) → a = a'

docstring:
First-order Taylor expansion with unique quadratic remainder, over an
arbitrary commutative ring.
name: Polynomial.existsUnique_taylor_remainder
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (f : Polynomial R) (a : R), ∃! g, f = Polynomial.C (Polynomial.eval a f) + Polynomial.C (Polynomial.eval a (Polynomial.derivative f)) * (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) + g * (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ 2
statement:
theorem existsUnique_taylor_remainder (f : R[X]) (a : R) :
    ∃! g : R[X],
      f = C (f.eval a) + C (f.derivative.eval a) * (X - C a) +
        g * (X - C a) ^ 2

docstring:
Roots of a sufficiently small monic coefficient perturbation generate the same local
extension as a closest root of an irreducible separable polynomial.
name: Polynomial.exists_isClosestConjugate_root_of_l1Norm_sub_lt
signature: ∀ (K : Type u_3) [inst : NontriviallyNormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] (f : Polynomial K), f.Monic → Irreducible f → f.Separable → ∃ δ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ (g : Polynomial K), g.Monic → Polynomial.l1Norm (NormedField.toAbsoluteValue K) (f - g) < δ → ∀ (β : AlgebraicClosure K), (Polynomial.aeval β) g = 0 → ∃ α, (Polynomial.aeval α) f = 0 ∧ AlgebraicClosure.IsClosestConjugate K α β ∧ K⟮α⟯ = K⟮β⟯
statement:
theorem exists_isClosestConjugate_root_of_l1Norm_sub_lt
    (K : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K]
    (f : K[X]) (hf : f.Monic) (hirr : Irreducible f) (hsep : f.Separable) :
    ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ g : K[X], g.Monic →
      l1Norm (NormedField.toAbsoluteValue K) (f - g) < δ →
      ∀ β : AlgebraicClosure K, aeval β g = 0 →
        ∃ α : AlgebraicClosure K, aeval α f = 0 ∧
          AlgebraicClosure.IsClosestConjugate K α β ∧
          IntermediateField.adjoin K {α} = IntermediateField.adjoin K {β}

docstring:
Strong complete-DVR Hensel endpoint: an approximate root with
`2 * addVal (derivative) < addVal (value)` refines to an exact root `a`
with a valuation bound, uniqueness in the strict ball, and derivative
valuation stability. The strict-ball witness fact is kept (the ATLAS
published statement dropped it), which is what makes uniqueness usable.
This is an existence/uniqueness/stability statement only; it claims
nothing about Newton sequences or convergence rates.
name: Polynomial.exists_isRoot_of_two_mul_addVal_derivative_lt_addVal
signature: ∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : IsDomain A] [inst_2 : IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A] (f : Polynomial A) (a₀ : A), 2 * (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval a₀ (Polynomial.derivative f)) < (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval a₀ f) → ∃ a, f.IsRoot a ∧ a - a₀ ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A ∧ (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval a₀ (Polynomial.derivative f)) < (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (a - a₀) ∧ (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval a₀ f) ≤ (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (a - a₀) + 2 * (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval a₀ (Polynomial.derivative f)) ∧ (∀ (a' : A), f.IsRoot a' → (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval a₀ (Polynomial.derivative f)) < (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (a' - a₀) → a' = a) ∧ (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval a (Polynomial.derivative f)) = (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval a₀ (Polynomial.derivative f))
statement:
theorem Polynomial.exists_isRoot_of_two_mul_addVal_derivative_lt_addVal
    (f : A[X]) (a₀ : A)
    (hval : 2 * addVal A (f.derivative.eval a₀) < addVal A (f.eval a₀)) :
    ∃ a : A,
    f.IsRoot a ∧
    a - a₀ ∈ maximalIdeal A ∧
    addVal A (f.derivative.eval a₀) < addVal A (a - a₀) ∧
    addVal A (f.eval a₀) ≤
      addVal A (a - a₀) + 2 * addVal A (f.derivative.eval a₀) ∧
    (∀ a' : A, f.IsRoot a' →
      addVal A (f.derivative.eval a₀) < addVal A (a' - a₀) → a' = a) ∧
    addVal A (f.derivative.eval a) = addVal A (f.derivative.eval a₀)

docstring:
Newton-iteration Hensel lift for a complete DVR: an approximate root whose derivative
is a unit refines to an exact root congruent to the approximation mod the maximal ideal.

signature: ∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : IsDomain A] [inst_2 : IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A] (f : Polynomial A) (a₀ : A), Polynomial.eval a₀ f ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A → IsUnit (Polynomial.eval a₀ (Polynomial.derivative f)) → ∃ a, f.IsRoot a ∧ a - a₀ ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A
