docstring:
In a finite family with a common upper interlacing point, one member has largest root no
larger than the largest root of any real-rooted monic nonnegative weighted sum.
name: Polynomial.exists_maxRealRoot_le_weightedSum_of_commonUpperInterlacing
signature: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (w : ι → ℝ) (P : ι → Polynomial ℂ), (∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ w i) → (∀ (i : ι), (P i).Monic) → (∀ (i : ι), (P i).IsRealRooted) → (∀ (i : ι), 0 < (P i).natDegree) → Polynomial.HasCommonUpperInterlacing P → (∑ i, ↑(w i) • P i).Monic → (∑ i, ↑(w i) • P i).IsRealRooted → ∃ i, (P i).maxRealRoot ≤ (∑ j, ↑(w j) • P j).maxRealRoot
statement:
public theorem exists_maxRealRoot_le_weightedSum_of_commonUpperInterlacing
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (w : ι → ℝ) (P : ι → Polynomial ℂ)
    (hw : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (hmonic : ∀ i, (P i).Monic)
    (hrooted : ∀ i, (P i).IsRealRooted) (hdegree : ∀ i, 0 < (P i).natDegree)
    (hcommon : Polynomial.HasCommonUpperInterlacing P)
    (hsumMonic : (∑ i, (w i : ℂ) • P i).Monic)
    (hsumRooted : (∑ i, (w i : ℂ) • P i).IsRealRooted) :
    ∃ i, (P i).maxRealRoot ≤ (∑ j, (w j : ℂ) • P j).maxRealRoot

docstring:
If the segment from a weighted sum to every member of a finite monic family stays
real-rooted, some member has largest root no larger than that of the weighted sum.
name: Polynomial.exists_maxRealRoot_le_weightedSum_of_segment_realRooted
signature: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι], Nonempty ι → ∀ (w : ι → ℝ) (P : ι → Polynomial ℂ) {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → (∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ w i) → (∀ (i : ι), (P i).IsMonicOfDegree n) → (∑ i, ↑(w i) • P i).IsMonicOfDegree n → (∀ (i : ι), ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 1, ((1 - ↑t) • ∑ j, ↑(w j) • P j + ↑t • P i).IsRealRooted) → ∃ i, (P i).maxRealRoot ≤ (∑ j, ↑(w j) • P j).maxRealRoot
statement:
public theorem exists_maxRealRoot_le_weightedSum_of_segment_realRooted
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (hne : Nonempty ι) (w : ι → ℝ) (P : ι → Polynomial ℂ)
    {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hw : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i)
    (hfamily : ∀ i, (P i).IsMonicOfDegree n)
    (hsum : (∑ i, (w i : ℂ) • P i).IsMonicOfDegree n)
    (hsegments : ∀ i t, t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 →
      ((1 - (t : ℂ)) • (∑ j, (w j : ℂ) • P j) + (t : ℂ) • P i).IsRealRooted) :
    ∃ i, (P i).maxRealRoot ≤ (∑ j, (w j : ℂ) • P j).maxRealRoot

docstring:
Dense scalar coefficients approximate a monic irreducible separable polynomial in `l1Norm`
while preserving irreducibility and separability after mapping to the complete field.
name: Polynomial.exists_monic_and_natDegree_eq_and_l1Norm_sub_lt_and_map_irreducible_and_separable
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_3} {L : Type u_4} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NontriviallyNormedField L] [IsUltrametricDist L] [CompleteSpace L] [inst_4 : Algebra K L], DenseRange ⇑(Algebra.algebraMap K L) → ∀ (f : Polynomial L), f.Monic → Irreducible f → f.Separable → ∀ {ε : ℝ}, 0 < ε → ∃ g, g.Monic ∧ g.natDegree = f.natDegree ∧ Polynomial.l1Norm (NormedField.toAbsoluteValue L) (f - Polynomial.map (Algebra.algebraMap K L) g) < ε ∧ Irreducible (Polynomial.map (Algebra.algebraMap K L) g) ∧ (Polynomial.map (Algebra.algebraMap K L) g).Separable
statement:
theorem exists_monic_and_natDegree_eq_and_l1Norm_sub_lt_and_map_irreducible_and_separable
    {K L : Type*} [Field K] [NontriviallyNormedField L]
    [IsUltrametricDist L] [CompleteSpace L] [Algebra K L]
    (hdense : DenseRange (algebraMap K L))
    (f : L[X]) (hf : f.Monic) (hirr : Irreducible f) (hsep : f.Separable)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ g : K[X], g.Monic ∧ g.natDegree = f.natDegree ∧
      l1Norm (NormedField.toAbsoluteValue L)
        (f - g.map (algebraMap K L)) < ε ∧
      Irreducible (g.map (algebraMap K L)) ∧
      (g.map (algebraMap K L)).Separable

docstring:
Standard monic Hensel factor lifting, generic in the ideal.

If `A` is `I`-adically complete and a monic polynomial `f` reduces modulo `I`
to a product of monic coprime polynomials, the factorization lifts to `A`.
The proof packages the residue factorization via the universal coprime
factorization ring, lifts its structure map through `I`-adic completeness,
and evaluates the universal factors over `A`.
name: Polynomial.exists_monic_coprime_factorization_of_isAdicComplete
signature: ∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A] (f : Polynomial A), f.Monic → ∀ (g_bar h_bar : Polynomial (A ⧸ I)), g_bar.Monic → h_bar.Monic → Polynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) f = g_bar * h_bar → IsCoprime g_bar h_bar → ∃ g h, g.Monic ∧ h.Monic ∧ f = g * h ∧ Polynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) g = g_bar ∧ Polynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) h = h_bar
statement:
theorem exists_monic_coprime_factorization_of_isAdicComplete
    (I : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (f : A[X]) (hf : f.Monic)
    (g_bar h_bar : (A ⧸ I)[X])
    (hg : g_bar.Monic) (hh : h_bar.Monic)
    (hfac : f.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = g_bar * h_bar)
    (hcop : IsCoprime g_bar h_bar) :
    ∃ g h : A[X], g.Monic ∧ h.Monic ∧ f = g * h ∧
      g.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = g_bar ∧
      h.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = h_bar

docstring:
Degree corollary of monic Hensel factor lifting.

The lifted factors have the same degrees as the residue factors. The
`Nontrivial (A ⧸ I)` hypothesis is sharp: over the trivial quotient every
reduction equality is vacuous, so no degree conclusion can hold there.
name: Polynomial.exists_monic_coprime_factorization_of_isAdicComplete_natDegree
signature: ∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A] [Nontrivial (A ⧸ I)] (f : Polynomial A), f.Monic → ∀ (g_bar h_bar : Polynomial (A ⧸ I)), g_bar.Monic → h_bar.Monic → Polynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) f = g_bar * h_bar → IsCoprime g_bar h_bar → ∃ g h, g.Monic ∧ h.Monic ∧ f = g * h ∧ Polynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) g = g_bar ∧ Polynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) h = h_bar ∧ g.natDegree = g_bar.natDegree ∧ h.natDegree = h_bar.natDegree
statement:
theorem exists_monic_coprime_factorization_of_isAdicComplete_natDegree
    (I : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A] [Nontrivial (A ⧸ I)]
    (f : A[X]) (hf : f.Monic)
    (g_bar h_bar : (A ⧸ I)[X])
    (hg : g_bar.Monic) (hh : h_bar.Monic)
    (hfac : f.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = g_bar * h_bar)
    (hcop : IsCoprime g_bar h_bar) :
    ∃ g h : A[X], g.Monic ∧ h.Monic ∧ f = g * h ∧
      g.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = g_bar ∧
      h.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = h_bar ∧
      g.natDegree = g_bar.natDegree ∧ h.natDegree = h_bar.natDegree

name: Polynomial.exists_pos_adjoinRoot_algEquiv_of_l1Norm_sub_lt

docstring: Unfolding characterization of level-`k` completeness.
name: Polynomial.isKComplete_iff
signature: ∀ {F : Type u_1} [inst : Field F] [inst_1 : Finite F] (f : Polynomial F) (k : ℕ), f.IsKComplete k ↔ ∀ i ≤ k, Function.Bijective fun x ↦ Polynomial.eval x (f + Polynomial.C ↑i * Polynomial.X)
statement:
theorem isKComplete_iff {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F] (f : Polynomial F)
    (k : ℕ) :
    IsKComplete f k ↔ ∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ k →
      Function.Bijective fun x =>
        (f + Polynomial.C (i : F) * Polynomial.X).eval x

docstring:
Source-facing positive-level characterization: `(k + 1)`-completeness splits
into `k`-completeness plus the new top translated polynomial.
name: Polynomial.isKComplete_succ_iff
signature: ∀ {F : Type u_1} [inst : Field F] [inst_1 : Finite F] (f : Polynomial F) (k : ℕ), f.IsKComplete (k + 1) ↔ f.IsKComplete k ∧ (f + Polynomial.C ↑(k + 1) * Polynomial.X).IsPermutationPolynomial

theorem isKComplete_succ_iff {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    (f : Polynomial F) (k : ℕ) :
    IsKComplete f (k + 1) ↔ IsKComplete f k ∧
      IsPermutationPolynomial

docstring:
For a state `f` on a unital C⋆-algebra (`f 1 = 1`), the GNS space has a unit cyclic vector
`ξ`: `f a = ⟪ξ, π(a) ξ⟫` for all `a`, and the vectors `π(a) ξ` span a dense subspace.
`cStarAlgebra_gns_cyclic_vector` is the source-shaped form.
name: PositiveLinearMap.exists_gns_cyclic_vector
signature: ∀ {A : Type u} [inst : CStarAlgebra A] [inst_1 : PartialOrder A] [inst_2 : StarOrderedRing A] (f : A →ₚ[ℂ] ℂ), f 1 = 1 → ∃ ξ, ‖ξ‖ = 1 ∧ (∀ (a : A), f a = Inner.inner ℂ ξ ((f.gnsStarAlgHom a) ξ)) ∧ Dense ↑(Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun a ↦ (f.gnsStarAlgHom a) ξ))
statement:
theorem exists_gns_cyclic_vector
    {A : Type u} [CStarAlgebra A] [PartialOrder A] [StarOrderedRing A]
    (f : A →ₚ[ℂ] ℂ) (hf : f (1 : A) = (1 : ℂ)) :
    ∃ (ξ : f.GNS), ‖ξ‖ = 1 ∧
      (∀ a : A, f a = ⟪ξ, (f.gnsStarAlgHom a) ξ⟫_ℂ) ∧
      Dense (↑(Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun a : A => (f.gnsStarAlgHom a) ξ)) : Set f.GNS)

docstring:
Taylor's formula for formal power series: the exponential generating series of the
successive derivatives of `f` is `f(t + u)`.

This is equation (5.32) in Emanuele Munarini, *Combinatorial Identities for the Tricomi
Polynomials*, Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), Article 20.9.4. The variables `t` and `u`
are represented by `MvPowerSeries.X 0` and `MvPowerSeries.X 1`.
name: PowerSeries.taylorFormula
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Algebra ℚ R] (f : PowerSeries R), (fun d ↦ (↑(d 1).factorial)⁻¹ • (PowerSeries.coeff (d 0)) ((⇑PowerSeries.derivative)^[d 1] f)) = MvPowerSeries.subst (fun x ↦ MvPowerSeries.X 0 + MvPowerSeries.X 1) f
statement:
theorem taylorFormula {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [Algebra ℚ R]
    (f : PowerSeries R) :
    (fun d : Fin 2 →₀ ℕ =>
      ((d 1).factorial : ℚ)⁻¹ •
        coeff (d 0) (d⁄dX^[d 1] f)) =
      MvPowerSeries.subst
        (fun _ : Unit =>
          MvPowerSeries.X (0 : Fin 2) + MvPowerSeries.X (1 : Fin 2)) f

docstring:
Hoeffding's inequality for a sum of independent Bernoulli variables
(concept `jis_grounded_4cd778f9d6394cee44270586`,
`hoeffding_bernoulli_sum_abs_tail`): strict two-sided tail
`Prob(|X_n - n * p| > ε * n) ≤ 2 * exp (-2 * ε ^ 2 * n)`.
Source: `https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL28/Jackson/jackson5.tex`
(Proposition, Hoeffding's Inequality, Thm. 2 of Hoe63).
Proves `Wanted` entry `hoeffding_bernoulli_sum_abs_tail`.
name: ProbabilityTheory.hoeffding_bernoulli_sum_abs_tail
signature: ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {n : ℕ} (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ) (p ε : ℝ), ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ → (∀ (i : Fin n), AEMeasurable (X i) μ) → (∀ (i : Fin n), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, X i ω = 0 ∨ X i ω = 1) → (∀ (i : Fin n), ∫ (x : Ω), X i x ∂μ = p) → 0 < ε → μ.real {ω | ε * ↑n < |∑ i, X i ω - ↑n * p|} ≤ 2 * Real.exp (-2 * ε ^ 2 * ↑n)
statement:
theorem hoeffding_bernoulli_sum_abs_tail {n : ℕ} (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ)
    (p ε : ℝ) (h_indep : iIndepFun X μ)
    (hmeas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (hBernoulli : ∀ i, ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, X i ω = 0 ∨ X i ω = 1)
    (hexp : ∀ i, ∫ x, X i x ∂μ = p) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    μ.real {ω | ε * (n : ℝ) < |(∑ i, X i ω) - (n : ℝ) * p|} ≤
      2 * Real.exp (-2 * ε ^ 2 * (n : ℝ))

docstring:
One-sided Hoeffding binomial lower tail for independent Bernoulli variables
with common mean `p` (JIS concept `jis_grounded_4cd778f9d6394cee44270586`,
Griffiths JIS VOL16 Eq. `hoeff`, source lines 167-191,
`https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL16/Griffiths/griffiths22.tex`,
source object `9d2fd3574fc15b79a0e00894b68d9608850dec38628c212a69d57f903588a30c`).
Proves `Wanted` entry `hoeffding_binomial_lower_tail`.
name: ProbabilityTheory.hoeffding_binomial_lower_tail
signature: ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {n : ℕ} (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ) (p ε : ℝ), ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ → (∀ (i : Fin n), AEMeasurable (X i) μ) → (∀ (i : Fin n), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, X i ω = 0 ∨ X i ω = 1) → (∀ (i : Fin n), ∫ (x : Ω), X i x ∂μ = p) → 0 < ε → μ.real {ω | ∑ i, X i ω ≤ ↑n * (p - ε)} ≤ Real.exp (-2 * ε ^ 2 * ↑n)
statement:
theorem hoeffding_binomial_lower_tail {Ω : Type*}
    [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
    [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {n : ℕ}
    (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ) (p ε : ℝ)
    (h_indep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
    (hmeas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (hBernoulli : ∀ i, ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, X i ω = 0 ∨ X i ω = 1)
    (hexp : ∀ i, ∫ x, X i x ∂μ = p)
    (hε : 0 < ε) :
    μ.real {ω | (∑ i, X i ω) ≤ (n : ℝ) * (p - ε)} ≤
      Real.exp (-2 * ε ^ 2 * (n : ℝ))

docstring:
**The Paley-Zygmund Inequality**: If `Z ≥ 0` is a random variable with finite variance, and if
`0 ≤ θ ≤ 1`, then `P(Z > θ * EZ) ≥ (1-θ)^2 (EZ)^2/E(Z^2)`.
name: ProbabilityTheory.paley_zygmund
signature: ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {m0 : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {Z : Ω → ℝ}, 0 ≤ᵐ[μ] Z → MeasureTheory.MemLp Z 2 μ → ∀ {θ : ℝ}, 0 ≤ θ → θ ≤ 1 → (1 - θ) ^ 2 * (∫ (ω : Ω), Z ω ∂μ) ^ 2 ≤ (∫ (ω : Ω), Z ω ^ 2 ∂μ) * μ.real {ω | θ * ∫ (ω : Ω), Z ω ∂μ < Z ω}
statement:
theorem paley_zygmund [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {Z : Ω → ℝ} (hZ_nn : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ] Z) (hZ2 : MemLp Z 2 μ)
    {θ : ℝ} (hθ0 : 0 ≤ θ) (hθ1 : θ ≤ 1) :
    (1 - θ) ^ 2 * (∫ ω, Z ω ∂μ) ^ 2 ≤
      (∫ ω, Z ω ^ 2 ∂μ) * μ.real {ω | θ * ∫ ω, Z ω ∂μ < Z ω}

docstring: The pointwise orthogonal sum of two equally indexed systems of quadratic forms.
name: QuadraticForm.systemOrthogonalSum
signature: {R : Type u_1} → {M : Type u_2} → {N : Type u_3} → {ι : Type u_4} → [inst : CommSemiring R] → [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] → [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid N] → [inst_3 : _root_.Module R M] → [inst_4 : _root_.Module R N] → (ι → QuadraticForm R M) → (ι → QuadraticForm R N) → ι → QuadraticForm R (M × N)
statement:
def systemOrthogonalSum (Q : ι → QuadraticForm R M) (Q' : ι → QuadraticForm R N) :
    ι → QuadraticForm R (M × N)

docstring: Evaluation of a pointwise orthogonal sum.
name: QuadraticForm.systemOrthogonalSum_apply
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid N] [inst_3 : _root_.Module R M] [inst_4 : _root_.Module R N] (Q : ι → QuadraticForm R M) (Q' : ι → QuadraticForm R N) (i : ι) (x : M × N), (QuadraticForm.systemOrthogonalSum Q Q' i) x = (Q i) x.1 + (Q' i) x.2
statement:
theorem systemOrthogonalSum_apply (Q : ι → QuadraticForm R M)
    (Q' : ι → QuadraticForm R N) (i : ι) (x : M × N) :
    systemOrthogonalSum Q Q' i x = Q i x.1 + Q' i x.2

docstring: The left summand restricts to the original left-hand system.
name: QuadraticForm.systemOrthogonalSum_inl
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid N] [inst_3 : _root_.Module R M] [inst_4 : _root_.Module R N] (Q : ι → QuadraticForm R M) (Q' : ι → QuadraticForm R N) (i : ι) (x : M), (QuadraticForm.systemOrthogonalSum Q Q' i) (x, 0) = (Q i) x
statement:
theorem systemOrthogonalSum_inl (Q : ι → QuadraticForm R M)
    (Q' : ι → QuadraticForm R N) (i : ι) (x : M) :
    systemOrthogonalSum Q Q' i (x, 0) = Q i x

docstring: The right summand restricts to the original right-hand system.
name: QuadraticForm.systemOrthogonalSum_inr
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid N] [inst_3 : _root_.Module R M] [inst_4 : _root_.Module R N] (Q : ι → QuadraticForm R M) (Q' : ι → QuadraticForm R N) (i : ι) (y : N), (QuadraticForm.systemOrthogonalSum Q Q' i) (0, y) = (Q' i) y
statement:
theorem systemOrthogonalSum_inr (Q : ι → QuadraticForm R M)
    (Q' : ι → QuadraticForm R N) (i : ι) (y : N) :
    systemOrthogonalSum Q Q' i (0, y) = Q' i y

Canonical isomorphism `A ⧸ B ≃* f.range ⧸ (B.map f).subgroupOf f.range`
for a homomorphism `f : A →* C` of commutative groups and a subgroup
`B : Subgroup A` containing `f.ker`.
name: QuotientGroup.quotientEquivRangeQuotient
signature: {A : Type u_1} → {C : Type u_2} → [inst : CommGroup A] → [inst_1 : CommGroup C] → (f : A →* C) → (B : Subgroup A) → f.ker ≤ B → A ⧸ B ≃* ↥f.range ⧸ (Subgroup.map f B).subgroupOf f.range
statement:
noncomputable def quotientEquivRangeQuotient
    {A C : Type*} [CommGroup A] [CommGroup C]
    (f : A →* C) (B : Subgroup A) (hB : f.ker ≤ B) :
    A ⧸ B ≃* f.range ⧸ (B.map f).subgroupOf f.range

docstring: Evaluation of `QuotientGroup.quotientEquivRangeQuotient` on representatives.
name: QuotientGroup.quotientEquivRangeQuotient_mk
signature: ∀ {A : Type u_1} {C : Type u_2} [inst : CommGroup A] [inst_1 : CommGroup C] (f : A →* C) (B : Subgroup A) (hB : f.ker ≤ B) (a : A), (QuotientGroup.quotientEquivRangeQuotient f B hB) ↑a = ↑(f.rangeRestrict a)

docstring:
Index for `M_ℚ`: inequivalent normalised absolute values on `ℚ`.

* `infinite` is the ordinary archimedean absolute value.
* `finite prime` is the `p`-adic absolute value for `prime = ⟨p, hp⟩`.
name: Rat.Place
signature: Type
statement: inductive Place : Type

docstring:
The completed field `ℚ_v` attached to a place `v`. Coerced from the
selected bundle.
name: Rat.Place.CompletedField
signature: Rat.Place → Type
statement: noncomputable abbrev CompletedField (v : Place) : Type

docstring:
Bundled carrier together with the `NormedField` / `CompleteSpace`
instances needed for the completed field `ℚ_v`.

Using a bundle avoids a direct dependent family `Place → Type` returning
`Padic p`, which loses the local `Fact` dictionary and causes kernel
declaration mismatches in projected instances. Instance-valued fields use
bracket syntax so the bundle itself carries the instances.
name: Rat.Place.CompletedFieldBundle
signature: Type 1
statement: structure CompletedFieldBundle

docstring:
Normalised real-valued absolute value attached to a place.

Reuses `Rat.AbsoluteValue.real` at infinity and `Rat.AbsoluteValue.padic`
at a finite prime. `Rat.AbsoluteValue.padic` takes `[Fact p.Prime]`,
so the proof in `prime` is turned into a local `Fact` dictionary.
name: Rat.Place.absoluteValue
signature: Rat.Place → AbsoluteValue ℚ ℝ
statement: noncomputable def absoluteValue : Place → AbsoluteValue ℚ ℝ

docstring: Evaluation at a finite prime.
name: Rat.Place.absoluteValue_finite_apply
statement:
theorem absoluteValue_finite_apply (prime : Nat.Primes) (q : ℚ) :
    let _ : Fact prime.1.Prime := ⟨prime.2⟩
    absoluteValue (.finite prime) q = Rat.AbsoluteValue.padic prime.1 q

docstring: Evaluation at infinity.

signature: ∀ (q : ℚ), Rat.Place.infinite.absoluteValue q = |↑q|
statement:
theorem absoluteValue_infinite_apply (q : ℚ) :
    absoluteValue .infinite q = |(q : ℝ)|

docstring:
Bundle selection by place. Exactly `ℝ` at infinity and `Padic p` at

docstring:
The image of `ℚ` is dense in each completed field `ℚ_v`.

Uses `Rat.denseRange_cast (𝕜 := ℝ)` at infinity and

docstring:
Canonical ring embedding `ℚ →+* ℚ_v`.

At infinity this is `Rat.castHom ℝ`; at a finite prime it is
`Rat.castHom (Padic p)` under the local `Fact p.Prime` instance.

signature: (v : Rat.Place) → ℚ →+* v.CompletedField
statement: noncomputable def embedding : (v : Place) → ℚ →+* CompletedField v

docstring:
The embedding norm is the selected absolute value:

`‖embedding v q‖ = v.absoluteValue q`.

At infinity this follows by unfolding the selected embedding and absolute
value with `Rat.AbsoluteValue.real_eq_abs` and closing the resulting
`|(q : ℝ)| = ↑|q|` with `Rat.cast_abs` in the reverse direction;
`p`-adically it is `Padic.eq_padicNorm`.
name: Rat.Place.embedding_norm_eq_absoluteValue
signature: ∀ (v : Rat.Place) (q : ℚ), ‖v.embedding q‖ = v.absoluteValue q
statement:
theorem embedding_norm_eq_absoluteValue (v : Place) (q : ℚ) :
    ‖embedding v q‖ = v.absoluteValue q

docstring:
Translation of `Rat.AbsoluteValue.equiv_real_or_padic` into the
uniform place index.

`Rat.AbsoluteValue.equiv_real_or_padic` takes `f.IsNontrivial` and
concludes `f ≈ real ∨ ∃! p, ∃ (_ : Fact p.Prime), f ≈ padic p`;
this is repackaged as `∃ v : Place, f ≈ v.absoluteValue`, matching the
conclusion notation of Ostrowski directly.
name: Rat.Place.exists_place_equiv

statement:
theorem exists_place_equiv (f : AbsoluteValue ℚ ℝ) (hf : f.IsNontrivial) :
    ∃ v : Place, f ≈ v.absoluteValue

docstring:

Preserves the unique-prime payload of `Rat.AbsoluteValue.equiv_real_or_padic`;
the opposite constructor is excluded via `Rat.AbsoluteValue.not_real_isEquiv_padic`
and equivalence symmetry/transitivity.
name: Rat.Place.exists_unique_place_equiv
signature: ∀ (f : AbsoluteValue ℚ ℝ), f.IsNontrivial → ∃! v, f ≈ v.absoluteValue
statement:
theorem exists_unique_place_equiv (f : AbsoluteValue ℚ ℝ) (hf : f.IsNontrivial) :
    ∃! v : Place, f ≈ v.absoluteValue

docstring:
`IsDickmanDeBruijn ρ` says that `ρ` is the Dickman–de Bruijn function, extended by zero to
negative inputs. Continuity is asserted only on the original nonnegative domain, since the total
zero extension is discontinuous at zero.

docstring:
Domain of the normalized logarithmic integral: `0 ≤ x` and `x ≠ 1`.

`1` is excluded because `1 / log t` is singular at `t = 1`; the classical
integral `∫₀ˣ dt / log t` has no finite real value at `x = 1` and is
understood as a Cauchy principal value for `x ≠ 1`.

Source: arXiv:2306.14073v1 and arXiv:2309.16007v1, classical `li(x) := PV ∫₀ˣ dt/log t`
with lower limit `0` and principal value at `t = 1`.
name: Real.LogarithmicIntegralDomain
signature: Type
statement: abbrev LogarithmicIntegralDomain : Type

docstring:
Catalan's constant, defined by its alternating reciprocal odd-square
series `∑ n, (-1)^n / (2n+1)^2`.
name: Real.catalanConstant
signature: ℝ
statement: noncomputable def catalanConstant : ℝ

docstring:
Characteristic equation: Catalan's constant is the sum of its
defining alternating series. Downstream users should rewrite with this
lemma (or `Real.hasSum_catalanConstant`) instead of unfolding the
definition.
name: Real.catalanConstant_eq_tsum
signature: Real.catalanConstant = ∑' (n : ℕ), (-1) ^ n / (2 * ↑n + 1) ^ 2
statement:
theorem catalanConstant_eq_tsum :
    catalanConstant = ∑' n : ℕ, (-1 : ℝ) ^ n / (2 * (n : ℝ) + 1) ^ 2

docstring: Trigamma series on `(1, ∞)`: `(log ∘ Gamma)''(y + 1) = ∑ 1/(y+j+1)²` for `y > 0`.
name: Real.deriv_deriv_log_Gamma_add_one
signature: ∀ (y : ℝ), 0 < y → deriv (deriv fun t ↦ Real.log (Real.Gamma t)) (y + 1) = ∑' (j : ℕ), 1 / (y + ↑j + 1) ^ 2
statement:
theorem deriv_deriv_log_Gamma_add_one (y : ℝ) (hy : 0 < y) :
    deriv (deriv (fun t => Real.log (Real.Gamma t))) (y + 1)
      = ∑' j : ℕ, 1 / (y + (j : ℝ) + 1) ^ 2

docstring: On `(0, ∞)`, the derivative of `log ∘ Gamma` is `Gamma' / Gamma`.
name: Real.deriv_log_Gamma
signature: ∀ (u : ℝ), 0 < u → deriv (fun t ↦ Real.log (Real.Gamma t)) u = deriv Real.Gamma u / Real.Gamma u
statement:
theorem deriv_log_Gamma (u : ℝ) (hu : 0 < u) :
    deriv (fun t => Real.log (Real.Gamma t)) u
      = deriv Real.Gamma u / Real.Gamma u

name: Real.eulerMascheroniConstant_eq_regularized_integrals
signature: ↑Real.eulerMascheroniConstant = (∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..1, ↑((1 - Real.exp (-t)) / t)) - ∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Ioi 1, ↑(Real.exp (-t) / t)
statement:
theorem eulerMascheroniConstant_eq_regularized_integrals :
    (Real.eulerMascheroniConstant : ℂ) =
      (∫ t : ℝ in 0..1, (((1 - Real.exp (-t)) / t : ℝ) : ℂ)) -
        ∫ t : ℝ in Ioi 1, ((Real.exp (-t) / t : ℝ) : ℂ)

docstring:
There exists a unique total real function satisfying the Dickman–de Bruijn characterization.
Source: [O. Gorodetsky, *Rigidity of Averages over the Two Largest Prime
Factors*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05191), which characterizes the unique continuous function on
the nonnegative reals and specifies its zero extension to negative inputs; Lean packages those
clauses in `Real.IsDickmanDeBruijn`.

Proves `Wanted` entry `existsUnique_isDickmanDeBruijn`.
name: Real.existsUnique_isDickmanDeBruijn
signature: ∃! ρ, Real.IsDickmanDeBruijn ρ
statement:
theorem existsUnique_isDickmanDeBruijn :
    ∃! ρ : ℝ → ℝ, IsDickmanDeBruijn ρ

docstring:
Fourier transform of a dilated function: scaling `x ↦ f (a * x)` by
`a ≠ 0` scales the transform by `|a|⁻¹` and dilates frequencies by `a⁻¹`.
No integrability hypothesis is needed because Mathlib's Bochner integral is
totalized, so the identity also uses that convention for nonintegrable

    𝓕 (fun x => f (a * x)) y = (|a|⁻¹ : ℝ) • 𝓕 f (y / a)

docstring:

below `1` the chart agrees with `∫₀ˣ` near `x`, above `1` it agrees with a
paired principal-value constant plus `∫₂ˣ`, whose derivative is `(log x)⁻¹`.

docstring:
Normalized Cauchy-principal-value logarithmic integral `li`.

For `0 ≤ x < 1`, `li x = ∫ t in 0..x, (log t)⁻¹`. For `x > 1`,
`li x = (∫ u in 0..1, ((log (1 - u))⁻¹ + (log (1 + u))⁻¹)) +
        ∫ t in 2..x, (log t)⁻¹`,
where the first integral is the paired symmetric principal value
`PV ∫₀² dt / log t = ∫₀¹ ((log (1-u))⁻¹ + (log (1+u))⁻¹) du` obtained
by `t = 1 ∓ u`. The value at `0` is `0`. The function is not defined at
`1` because the integrand is singular there. Single-point totalizations
`(log 1)⁻¹ = 0` and `(log 0)⁻¹ = 0` do not affect Lebesgue interval
integrals.

Source: arXiv:2306.14073v1 and arXiv:2309.16007v1, normalized lower limit `0`
and Cauchy principal value at `t = 1` via symmetric pairing.
name: Real.logarithmicIntegral
signature: Real.LogarithmicIntegralDomain → ℝ
statement: noncomputable def logarithmicIntegral (x : LogarithmicIntegralDomain) : ℝ

docstring:
Global real-valued extension of `logarithmicIntegral`.

Agrees with `Real.logarithmicIntegral` on `0 ≤ x ∧ x ≠ 1` and is `0`
elsewhere (junk). At `x > 0, x ≠ 1` the value is locally determined by the
integral, so `HasDerivAt` at such `x` does not depend on the junk choice.
name: Real.logarithmicIntegralReal
signature: ℝ → ℝ
statement: noncomputable def logarithmicIntegralReal (x : ℝ) : ℝ

name: Real.logarithmicIntegralReal_of_lt_one

statement:
theorem logarithmicIntegralReal_of_lt_one {x : ℝ} (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx1 : x < 1) :
    Real.logarithmicIntegralReal x = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..x, (Real.log t)⁻¹

name: Real.logarithmicIntegralReal_of_one_lt
signature: ∀ {x : ℝ}, 1 < x → x.logarithmicIntegralReal = (∫ (u : ℝ) in 0..1, (Real.log (1 - u))⁻¹ + (Real.log (1 + u))⁻¹) + ∫ (t : ℝ) in 2..x, (Real.log t)⁻¹
statement:

    Real.logarithmicIntegralReal x =
      (∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..(1 : ℝ), ((Real.log (1 - u))⁻¹ + (Real.log (1 + u))⁻¹)) +
        ∫ t in (2 : ℝ)..x, (Real.log t)⁻¹

docstring:

docstring:
Unfolding for the upper branch `1 < x`.

The paired integral `∫₀¹ ((log (1 - u))⁻¹ + (log (1 + u))⁻¹)` is the
symmetric principal value `PV ∫₀²`.

Source: Direct unfolding of the `x > 1` branch; `¬ x < 1` from `1 < x`.
name: Real.logarithmicIntegral_of_one_lt
signature: ∀ {x : Real.LogarithmicIntegralDomain}, 1 < ↑x → Real.logarithmicIntegral x = (∫ (u : ℝ) in 0..1, (Real.log (1 - u))⁻¹ + (Real.log (1 + u))⁻¹) + ∫ (t : ℝ) in 2..↑x, (Real.log t)⁻¹
statement:
theorem logarithmicIntegral_of_one_lt {x : LogarithmicIntegralDomain} (hx : 1 < x.val) :
    logarithmicIntegral x =
      (∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..(1 : ℝ), ((Real.log (1 - u))⁻¹ + (Real.log (1 + u))⁻¹)) +
        ∫ t in (2 : ℝ)..x.val, (Real.log t)⁻¹

docstring:
An all-orders Bernoulli-polynomial expansion obtained from a logarithmic
first-difference equation. The normalization `u n → 0` fixes the otherwise
undetermined additive constant. Its coefficients use Mathlib's
`Polynomial.bernoulli`, evaluated by `Polynomial.aeval`.
name: Real.tendsto_pow_mul_sub_bernoulli_sum_of_log_diff
signature: ∀ {u : ℕ → ℝ} (α β c : ℝ), Filter.Tendsto u Filter.atTop (nhds 0) → (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, u (n + 1) - u n = Real.log (1 + α / (↑n + c)) - Real.log (1 + β / (↑n + c)) + (β - α) * Real.log (1 + 1 / (↑n + c))) → ∀ (M : ℕ), Filter.Tendsto (fun n ↦ (↑n + c) ^ M * (u n - ∑ j ∈ Finset.range M, (-1) ^ (j + 2) * ((Polynomial.aeval α) (Polynomial.bernoulli (j + 2)) - (Polynomial.aeval β) (Polynomial.bernoulli (j + 2))) / (↑(j + 1) * ↑(j + 2)) * (1 / (↑n + c) ^ (j + 1)))) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
statement:
public theorem _root_.Real.tendsto_pow_mul_sub_bernoulli_sum_of_log_diff
    {u : ℕ → ℝ} (α β c : ℝ)
    (hu : Filter.Tendsto u Filter.atTop (nhds 0))
    (hstep : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
      u (n + 1) - u n =
        Real.log (1 + α / (n + c : ℝ)) - Real.log (1 + β / (n + c : ℝ)) +
          (β - α) * Real.log (1 + 1 / (n + c : ℝ))) :
    ∀ M : ℕ,
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun n : ℕ =>
          (n + c : ℝ) ^ M *
            (u n - ∑ j ∈ Finset.range M,
              (-1 : ℝ) ^ (j + 2) *
                (Polynomial.aeval α (Polynomial.bernoulli (j + 2)) -
                  Polynomial.aeval β (Polynomial.bernoulli (j + 2))) /
                  ((j + 1 : ℕ) * (j + 2 : ℕ)) *
                (1 / (n + c : ℝ) ^ (j + 1))))
        Filter.atTop (nhds 0)

docstring:
Local Galois data for the Artin Euler factor at a rational prime.

For the finite Galois group `G = Gal(L/ℚ)`, `decomposition = G_w` is the
decomposition subgroup at a place `w|p`, `inertia = I_w` is its normal inertia
subgroup, and `frobenius = σ_w ∈ G_w/I_w` is the Frobenius coset.  The
representation is restricted to `G_w` and then `I_w`-invariants are taken,
so `G_w/I_w` acts on `V^{I_w}` and `frobenius` determines the local operator.

docstring:
The totalized inverse of the Artin local denominator at the rational prime `p`.

`ρ` is restricted to the decomposition subgroup and the resulting
`I_w`-invariants carry the quotient action `G_w/I_w`; evaluating that
action at `frobenius` gives the operator whose determinant is inverted.
The hypothesis `[Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]` makes the determinant
available via `LinearMap.det` on the finite-dimensional invariant subspace.
At a zero of the denominator, complex inversion gives the totalized value `0`;
use `ArtinLocalFactorRegular` when a genuine finite Euler factor is required.
name: Representation.artinLocalFactorRaw
signature: {G : Type u} → [inst : Group G] → [inst_1 : Finite G] → {V : Type v} → [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] → [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] → Representation ℂ G V → [Module.Free ℂ V] → [Module.Finite ℂ V] → Nat.Primes → Representation.ArtinLocalDatum G → ℂ → ℂ

    [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V] (p : Nat.Primes)
    (d : ArtinLocalDatum G) (s : ℂ) : ℂ

docstring:
A one-dimensional trivial quotient action has the expected degree-one
Euler factor `(1 - p^{-s})^{-1}`.  This is the unramified trivial-character
contribution that yields the Riemann-zeta local factor.
name: Representation.artinLocalFactorRaw_of_action_eq_id
signature: ∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : Finite G] {V : Type v} [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (ρ : Representation ℂ G V) [inst_4 : Module.Free ℂ V] [inst_5 : Module.Finite ℂ V] (p : Nat.Primes) (d : Representation.ArtinLocalDatum G) (s : ℂ), (Representation.quotientToInvariants (MonoidHom.comp ρ d.decomposition.subtype) d.inertia) d.frobenius = LinearMap.id → Module.finrank ℂ ↥(Representation.invariants ((MonoidHom.comp ρ d.decomposition.subtype).comp d.inertia.subtype)) = 1 → ρ.artinLocalFactorRaw p d s = (1 - ↑↑p ^ (-s))⁻¹
statement:
theorem artinLocalFactorRaw_of_action_eq_id (ρ : Representation ℂ G V)
    [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V] (p : Nat.Primes)
    (d : ArtinLocalDatum G) (s : ℂ)
    (hact : (Representation.quotientToInvariants
      (ρ.comp d.decomposition.subtype : Representation ℂ d.decomposition V)
      d.inertia) d.frobenius = LinearMap.id)
    (hdim : Module.finrank ℂ (invariants
      ((ρ.comp d.decomposition.subtype : Representation ℂ d.decomposition V).comp
        d.inertia.subtype)) = 1) :
    artinLocalFactorRaw ρ p d s = (1 - (p.1 : ℂ) ^ (-s))⁻¹

docstring:
A trivial quotient action gives the scalar Euler factor raised to the
dimension of the inertia-invariant subspace.
name: Representation.artinLocalFactorRaw_of_action_eq_id_general
signature: ∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : Finite G] {V : Type v} [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (ρ : Representation ℂ G V) [inst_4 : Module.Free ℂ V] [inst_5 : Module.Finite ℂ V] (p : Nat.Primes) (d : Representation.ArtinLocalDatum G) (s : ℂ), (Representation.quotientToInvariants (MonoidHom.comp ρ d.decomposition.subtype) d.inertia) d.frobenius = LinearMap.id → ρ.artinLocalFactorRaw p d s = ((1 - ↑↑p ^ (-s)) ^ Module.finrank ℂ ↥(Representation.invariants ((MonoidHom.comp ρ d.decomposition.subtype).comp d.inertia.subtype)))⁻¹
statement:
theorem artinLocalFactorRaw_of_action_eq_id_general (ρ : Representation ℂ G V)
    [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V] (p : Nat.Primes)
    (d : ArtinLocalDatum G) (s : ℂ)
    (hact : (Representation.quotientToInvariants
      (ρ.comp d.decomposition.subtype : Representation ℂ d.decomposition V)
      d.inertia) d.frobenius = LinearMap.id) :
    artinLocalFactorRaw ρ p d s =
      ((1 - (p.1 : ℂ) ^ (-s)) ^ Module.finrank ℂ (invariants
      ((ρ.comp d.decomposition.subtype : Representation ℂ d.decomposition V).comp
        d.inertia.subtype)))⁻¹

name: Representation.artinLocalFactorRaw_zero
signature: ∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : Finite G] {V : Type v} [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (ρ : Representation ℂ G V) [inst_4 : Module.Free ℂ V] [inst_5 : Module.Finite ℂ V] (p : Nat.Primes) (d : Representation.ArtinLocalDatum G), ρ.artinLocalFactorRaw p d 0 = (LinearMap.det (LinearMap.id - (Representation.quotientToInvariants (MonoidHom.comp ρ d.decomposition.subtype) d.inertia) d.frobenius))⁻¹
statement:
theorem artinLocalFactorRaw_zero (ρ : Representation ℂ G V)
    [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V] (p : Nat.Primes)
    (d : ArtinLocalDatum G) :
    artinLocalFactorRaw ρ p d 0 =
      (LinearMap.det (LinearMap.id -
        ((Representation.quotientToInvariants
          (ρ.comp d.decomposition.subtype : Representation ℂ d.decomposition V)
          d.inertia) d.frobenius)))⁻¹

(i.e., relative to all of `ℕ`).

name: Set.lowerDensity
signature: {β : Type u_1} → [inst : Preorder β] → [LocallyFiniteOrderBot β] → Set β → optParam (Set β) Set.univ → ℝ
statement:
noncomputable def lowerDensity {β : Type*} [Preorder β] [LocallyFiniteOrderBot β]
    (S : Set β) (A : Set β := Set.univ) : ℝ

name: Set.lowerDensity_le_one
signature: ∀ {β : Type u_1} [inst : Preorder β] [inst_1 : LocallyFiniteOrderBot β] (S : Set β) (A : optParam (Set β) Set.univ), S.lowerDensity A ≤ 1

theorem lowerDensity_le_one {β : Type*} [Preorder β] [LocallyFiniteOrderBot β]
    (S : Set β) (A : Set β := Set.univ) : S.lowerDensity A ≤ 1

name: Set.lowerDensity_nonneg
signature: ∀ {β : Type u_1} [inst : Preorder β] [inst_1 : LocallyFiniteOrderBot β] (S : Set β) (A : optParam (Set β) Set.univ), 0 ≤ S.lowerDensity A

docstring:
Given a set `S` and an element `b` in an order `β`, where all intervals bounded above are finite,
we define the partial density of `S` (relative to a set `A`) to be the proportion of elements in
`{x ∈ A | x < b}` that lie in `S ∩ A`.

This definition was inspired from https://github.com/b-mehta/unit-fractions
name: Set.partialDensity
signature: {β : Type u_1} → [inst : Preorder β] → [LocallyFiniteOrderBot β] → Set β → optParam (Set β) Set.univ → β → ℝ
statement:
noncomputable abbrev partialDensity {β : Type*} [Preorder β] [LocallyFiniteOrderBot β]
    (S : Set β) (A : Set β := Set.univ) (b : β) : ℝ

name: Set.partialDensity_le_one
signature: ∀ {β : Type u_1} [inst : Preorder β] [inst_1 : LocallyFiniteOrderBot β] (S : Set β) (A : optParam (Set β) Set.univ) (b : β), S.partialDensity A b ≤ 1
statement:
theorem partialDensity_le_one {β : Type*} [Preorder β] [LocallyFiniteOrderBot β]
    (S : Set β) (A : Set β := Set.univ) (b : β) : S.partialDensity A b ≤ 1

name: Set.triplewise_empty
signature: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (r : α → α → α → Prop), ∅.Triplewise r
statement:
theorem triplewise_empty (r : α → α → α → Prop) :
    Set.Triplewise ∅ r

name: Set.triplewise_insert
signature: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {r : α → α → α → Prop} {s : Set α} {x : α}, (Insert.insert x s).Triplewise r ↔ s.Triplewise r ∧ ∀ y ∈ s, ∀ z ∈ s, x ≠ y → x ≠ z → y ≠ z → r x y z ∧ r y x z ∧ r y z x
statement:
theorem triplewise_insert :
    (insert x s).Triplewise r ↔ s.Triplewise r ∧
    ∀ y ∈ s, ∀ z ∈ s, x ≠ y → x ≠ z → y ≠ z → r x y z ∧ r y x z ∧ r y z x

name: Set.triplewise_insert_of_not_mem
signature: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {r : α → α → α → Prop} {s : Set α} {x : α}, x ∉ s → ((Insert.insert x s).Triplewise r ↔ s.Triplewise r ∧ ∀ y ∈ s, ∀ z ∈ s, y ≠ z → r x y z ∧ r y x z ∧ r y z x)
statement:
theorem triplewise_insert_of_not_mem (hx : x ∉ s) :
    (insert x s).Triplewise r ↔ s.Triplewise r ∧
    ∀ y ∈ s, ∀ z ∈ s, y ≠ z → r x y z ∧ r y x z ∧ r y z x

name: Set.triplewise_of_encard_lt
signature: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {s : Set α} (r : α → α → α → Prop), s.encard < 3 → s.Triplewise r
statement:
theorem triplewise_of_encard_lt (r : α → α → α → Prop)
    (h : s.encard < 3) : s.Triplewise r

name: Set.triplewise_pair
signature: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {x y : α} (r : α → α → α → Prop), {x, y}.Triplewise r
statement:
theorem triplewise_pair
    (r : α → α → α → Prop) : Set.Triplewise {x, y} r

name: Set.triplewise_set_pred_iff
signature: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {S : Set α} {P : Set α → Prop}, (S.Triplewise fun x1 x2 x3 ↦ P {x1, x2, x3}) ↔ ∀ T ⊆ S, T.ncard = 3 → P T
statement:
theorem triplewise_set_pred_iff {S : Set α} {P : Set α → Prop} :
    S.Triplewise (P {·, ·, ·}) ↔ ∀ T ⊆ S, T.ncard = 3 → P T

name: Set.triplewise_singleton
signature: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {x : α} (r : α → α → α → Prop), {x}.Triplewise r
statement:
theorem triplewise_singleton (r : α → α → α → Prop) :
    Set.Triplewise {x} r

docstring:

density of `S` (relative to a set `A`) to be the limsup of the partial densities of `S`

docstring: Some `m` vertices contain at least `k` edges of `H`.
name: SetFamily.ContainsSubgraph
signature: {V : Type u_1} → [DecidableEq V] → Finset (Finset V) → ℕ → ℕ → Prop
statement:
public def ContainsSubgraph {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (H : Finset (Finset V)) (m k : ℕ) : Prop

docstring:
A vertex finset `I` is independent in `H` when no edge of `H` is fully
contained in `I`.
name: SetFamily.IsIndependent
signature: {V : Type u_1} → Finset (Finset V) → Finset V → Prop
statement: def IsIndependent (H : Finset (Finset V)) (I : Finset V) : Prop

docstring:
An `n`-vertex triple system modelled as a finset of unordered triples:
every edge has cardinality three, and every pair of distinct vertices lies
in exactly one edge of `H`.
name: SetFamily.IsSteinerTripleSystem
signature: {V : Type u_1} → Finset (Finset V) → Prop
statement: def IsSteinerTripleSystem (H : Finset (Finset V)) : Prop

docstring: A finite hypergraph is `r`-uniform when every edge has cardinality `r`.
name: SetFamily.IsUniform
signature: {V : Type u_1} → Finset (Finset V) → ℕ → Prop
statement: public def IsUniform {V : Type*} (H : Finset (Finset V)) (r : ℕ) : Prop

docstring: Unfolding characterization of finite subhypergraph containment.
name: SetFamily.containsSubgraph_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] (H : Finset (Finset V)) (m k : ℕ), SetFamily.ContainsSubgraph H m k ↔ ∃ S, S.card = m ∧ k ≤ {e ∈ H | e ⊆ S}.card
statement:
public theorem containsSubgraph_iff {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (H : Finset (Finset V)) (m k : ℕ) :
    ContainsSubgraph H m k ↔
      ∃ S : Finset V, S.card = m ∧ k ≤ (H.filter fun e => e ⊆ S).card

docstring:
Unique membership in a singleton family: when the only edge satisfies `P`,
it is the unique edge satisfying `P`.
name: SetFamily.existsUnique_mem_singleton
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {t : Finset V} {P : Finset V → Prop}, P t → ∃! e, e ∈ {t} ∧ P e
statement:
theorem existsUnique_mem_singleton {t : Finset V} {P : Finset V → Prop}
    (hP : P t) : ∃! e : Finset V, e ∈ ({t} : Finset (Finset V)) ∧ P e

docstring: Every vertex set is independent in the empty hypergraph.
name: SetFamily.isIndependent_empty_hypergraph
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} (I : Finset V), SetFamily.IsIndependent ∅ I
statement:
theorem isIndependent_empty_hypergraph (I : Finset V) :
    IsIndependent (∅ : Finset (Finset V)) I

docstring: The empty vertex set is independent iff every edge is nonempty.
name: SetFamily.isIndependent_empty_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} (H : Finset (Finset V)), SetFamily.IsIndependent H ∅ ↔ ∀ e ∈ H, e.Nonempty
statement:
theorem isIndependent_empty_iff (H : Finset (Finset V)) :
    IsIndependent H ∅ ↔ ∀ e ∈ H, e.Nonempty

docstring: Unfolding lemma for `IsIndependent`.
name: SetFamily.isIndependent_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} (H : Finset (Finset V)) (I : Finset V), SetFamily.IsIndependent H I ↔ ∀ e ∈ H, ¬e ⊆ I
statement:
theorem isIndependent_iff (H : Finset (Finset V)) (I : Finset V) :
    IsIndependent H I ↔ ∀ e ∈ H, ¬ e ⊆ I

docstring: Independence persists to subsets of the independent set.
name: SetFamily.isIndependent_of_subset
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {H : Finset (Finset V)} {I J : Finset V}, SetFamily.IsIndependent H I → J ⊆ I → SetFamily.IsIndependent H J

theorem isIndependent_of_subset {H : Finset (Finset V)} {I J : Finset V}
    (h : IsIndependent H I) (hJI : J ⊆ I) : IsIndependent H J

docstring: Unfolding characterization of uniformity.
name: SetFamily.isUniform_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} (H : Finset (Finset V)) (r : ℕ), SetFamily.IsUniform H r ↔ ∀ e ∈ H, e.card = r
statement:
public theorem isUniform_iff {V : Type*} (H : Finset (Finset V)) (r : ℕ) :
    IsUniform H r ↔ ∀ e ∈ H, e.card = r

docstring: Unique pair coverage from a Steiner triple system.

docstring: Uniformity projection from a Steiner triple system.

theorem uniform_of_isSteinerTripleSystem {H : Finset (Finset V)}
    (h : IsSteinerTripleSystem H) : IsUniform H 3

docstring:
A finite graph is CDS-colorable if it has a proper coloring
by natural numbers such that for all `k > 0`, the number of
vertices with color `< k` equals the maximum size of
the union of `k` independent sets.
name: SimpleGraph.CDSColorable
signature: {α : Type u_2} → [Fintype α] → SimpleGraph α → Prop
statement: def CDSColorable [Fintype α] (G : SimpleGraph α) : Prop

docstring:
`G.Cocolorable n` means that the vertices of `G` can be colored with `n` colors so that each
color class induces either an independent set or a complete graph.
name: SimpleGraph.Cocolorable
signature: {V : Type u_1} → SimpleGraph V → ℕ → Prop
statement: def Cocolorable (G : SimpleGraph V) (n : ℕ) : Prop

docstring:
Finite cocolorability description of the cochromatic number, mirroring
`Colorable.chromaticNumber_eq_sInf`.
name: SimpleGraph.Cocolorable.cochromaticNumber_eq_sInf
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} (G : SimpleGraph V) {n : ℕ}, G.Cocolorable n → G.cochromaticNumber = ↑(InfSet.sInf {n' | G.Cocolorable n'})
statement:
theorem Cocolorable.cochromaticNumber_eq_sInf {n : ℕ} (h : G.Cocolorable n) :
    G.cochromaticNumber = sInf {n' : ℕ | G.Cocolorable n'}

docstring:
Every proper coloring is a cocoloring: color classes inducing `⊥` also satisfy the
`⊥ ∨ ⊤` disjunction.
name: SimpleGraph.Colorable.cocolorable
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} (G : SimpleGraph V) {n : ℕ}, G.Colorable n → G.Cocolorable n
statement: theorem Colorable.cocolorable {n : ℕ} (hc : G.Colorable n) : G.Cocolorable n

docstring:
A finite connected simple graph whose vertex degrees are all even has a closed Eulerian
trail.
name: SimpleGraph.Connected.exists_isEulerian
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : SimpleGraph V} [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj], G.Connected → (∀ (v : V), Even (G.degree v)) → ∃ u p, p.IsEulerian
statement:
public theorem Connected.exists_isEulerian {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    {G : SimpleGraph V} [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : G.Connected)
    (heven : ∀ v, Even (G.degree v)) :
    ∃ (u : V) (p : G.Walk u u), p.IsEulerian

docstring: The square of a connected graph is connected.
name: SimpleGraph.Connected.square
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {G : SimpleGraph V}, G.Connected → G.square.Connected
statement:
public theorem Connected.square {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : G.Connected) :
    G.square.Connected

docstring:
A finite simple graph whose non-isolated vertices induce a connected graph and whose
degrees are all even has a closed Eulerian trail. Isolated vertices are irrelevant to an Euler
tour.
name: SimpleGraph.ConnectedSupport.exists_isEulerian
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : SimpleGraph V} [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj], (SimpleGraph.induce G.support G).Connected → (∀ (v : V), Even (G.degree v)) → ∃ u p, p.IsEulerian
statement:
public theorem ConnectedSupport.exists_isEulerian {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] {G : SimpleGraph V} [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hG : (G.induce G.support).Connected)
    (heven : ∀ v, Even (G.degree v)) :
    ∃ (u : V) (p : G.Walk u u), p.IsEulerian

statement: def Cycle.length {G : SimpleGraph V} (c : Cycle G) : ℕ

docstring:
`G` is dichromatically `k`-colourable if every orientation admits a

statement: def DichromaticColorable (k : ℕ) : Prop

theorem DichromaticColorable.of_edgeless (hempty : ∀ u v, ¬ G.Adj u v) :

docstring: A loopless multigraph whose parallel edges are distinguished by an edge type.

signature: Type u_1 → Type u_2 → Type (max u_1 u_2)

name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.Inc
signature: {V : Type u_1} → {E : Type u_2} → SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E → V → E → Prop
statement: public def Inc (v : V) (e : E) : Prop

docstring: A walk that records the identity of every traversed multiedge.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk
signature: {V : Type u_1} → {E : Type u_2} → SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E → V → V → Type (max u_1 u_2)
statement: public inductive IndexedWalk : V → V → Type _

docstring: An indexed trail is Eulerian when it uses every edge identity.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.IsEulerian
signature: {V : Type u_1} → {E : Type u_2} → (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) → {u v : V} → M.IndexedWalk u v → Prop
statement: public def IsEulerian {u v : V} (p : M.IndexedWalk u v) : Prop

docstring: An indexed walk is a trail when it uses no edge identity twice.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.IsTrail
signature: {V : Type u_1} → {E : Type u_2} → (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) → {u v : V} → M.IndexedWalk u v → Prop
statement: public def IsTrail {u v : V} (p : M.IndexedWalk u v) : Prop

docstring: The edge identities traversed by an indexed walk.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.edges
signature: {V : Type u_1} → {E : Type u_2} → (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) → {u v : V} → M.IndexedWalk u v → List E
statement: public def edges {u v : V} : M.IndexedWalk u v → List E

docstring: Prepending an indexed edge prepends its identity to the edge list.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.edges_cons
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) {u v w : V} (e : E) (he : M.ends e = s(u, v)) (p : M.IndexedWalk v w), SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.edges M (SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.cons e he p) = e :: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.edges M p
statement:
public theorem edges_cons {u v w : V} (e : E) (he : M.ends e = s(u, v))

docstring: The empty indexed walk has no edges.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.edges_nil
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) (v : V), SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.edges M (SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.nil v) = []
statement: public theorem edges_nil (v : V) : (IndexedWalk.nil v : M.IndexedWalk v v).edges = []

docstring: Forgetting edge identities maps each edge to its unordered endpoint pair.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.edges_toWalk
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) {u v : V} (p : M.IndexedWalk u v), (SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.toWalk M p).edges = List.map M.ends (SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.edges M p)
statement:
public theorem edges_toWalk {u v : V} (p : M.IndexedWalk u v) :
    p.toWalk.edges = p.edges.map M.ends

docstring: An indexed walk is Eulerian exactly when it is a trail containing every edge identity.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.isEulerian_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) {u v : V} (p : M.IndexedWalk u v), SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.IsEulerian M p ↔ SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.IsTrail M p ∧ ∀ (e : E), e ∈ SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.edges M p
statement:
public theorem isEulerian_iff {u v : V} (p : M.IndexedWalk u v) :
    p.IsEulerian ↔ p.IsTrail ∧ ∀ e, e ∈ p.edges

docstring: An indexed walk is a trail exactly when its edge list has no duplicates.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.isTrail_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) {u v : V} (p : M.IndexedWalk u v), SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.IsTrail M p ↔ (SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.edges M p).Nodup
statement:
public theorem isTrail_iff {u v : V} (p : M.IndexedWalk u v) :
    p.IsTrail ↔ p.edges.Nodup

docstring: Forgetting edge identities preserves the number of traversed edges.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.length_toWalk
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) {u v : V} (p : M.IndexedWalk u v), (SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.toWalk M p).length = (SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.edges M p).length
statement:
public theorem length_toWalk {u v : V} (p : M.IndexedWalk u v) :
    p.toWalk.length = p.edges.length

docstring: The vertices of an indexed walk, including both endpoints.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.support
signature: {V : Type u_1} → {E : Type u_2} → (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) → {u v : V} → M.IndexedWalk u v → List V
statement: public def support {u v : V} : M.IndexedWalk u v → List V

docstring: Prepending an indexed edge prepends its initial vertex to the support.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.support_cons
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) {u v w : V} (e : E) (he : M.ends e = s(u, v)) (p : M.IndexedWalk v w), SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.support M (SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.cons e he p) = u :: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.support M p
statement:
public theorem support_cons {u v w : V} (e : E) (he : M.ends e = s(u, v))
    (p : M.IndexedWalk v w) : (IndexedWalk.cons e he p).support = u :: p.support

docstring: The support of the empty indexed walk is its sole vertex.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.support_nil
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) (v : V), SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.support M (SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.nil v) = [v]
statement: public theorem support_nil (v : V) : (IndexedWalk.nil v : M.IndexedWalk v v).support = [v]

docstring: Forgetting edge identities preserves the vertex support.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.support_toWalk
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) {u v : V} (p : M.IndexedWalk u v), (SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.toWalk M p).support = SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.support M p
statement:
public theorem support_toWalk {u v : V} (p : M.IndexedWalk u v) :
    p.toWalk.support = p.support

docstring: Forget edge identities in an indexed walk.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.IndexedWalk.toWalk
signature: {V : Type u_1} → {E : Type u_2} → (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) → {u v : V} → M.IndexedWalk u v → M.underlying.Walk u v
statement: public def toWalk {u v : V} : M.IndexedWalk u v → M.underlying.Walk u v

docstring: The number of indexed edges incident with a vertex.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.degree
signature: {V : Type u_1} → {E : Type u_2} → SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E → V → ℕ
statement: public noncomputable def degree (v : V) : ℕ

docstring: The multigraph degree is the cardinality of the set of incident edge identities.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.degree_eq_ncard_inc
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) (v : V), M.degree v = {e | M.Inc v e}.ncard

public theorem degree_eq_ncard_inc (v : V) :

docstring: Every vertex degree is bounded by the maximum degree.
name: SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph.degree_le_maxDegree
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} (M : SimpleGraph.EdgeIndexedMultigraph V E) [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : Finite E] (v : V), M.degree v ≤ M.maxDegree
statement:

statement: def IsPhiCenter (φ : G.Coloring C) (s : Set V) (v : V) : Prop

name: SimpleGraph.IsPlanar
signature: {V : Type u_1} → SimpleGraph V → Prop
statement: public def IsPlanar {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop

docstring:
A homomorphism `f : H →g G` is rainbow for an edge labeling `c` of `G` if it maps distinct
edges of `H` to edges of `G` with distinct labels.

signature: {α : Type u_3} → {V : Type u_4} → {K : Type u_5} → {H : SimpleGraph α} → {G : SimpleGraph V} → H →g G → G.EdgeLabeling K → Prop
statement:

    (c : G.EdgeLabeling K) : Prop

docstring:
A graph `G` is Ramsey size linear if `R(G,H)` is bounded linearly by the
number of edges of every finite graph `H` without isolated vertices.
name: SimpleGraph.IsRamseySizeLinear
signature: {α : Type u_1} → [Fintype α] → SimpleGraph α → Prop
statement: def IsRamseySizeLinear {α : Type*} [Fintype α] (G : SimpleGraph α) : Prop

docstring:
In a strongly regular graph with `μ = 0`, the endpoints of a nontrivial
two-edge walk are adjacent.
name: SimpleGraph.IsSRGWith.adj_of_adj_of_adj_of_mu_zero
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {n k ℓ : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph V} [inst_1 : DecidableRel G.Adj], G.IsSRGWith n k ℓ 0 → ∀ {u v w : V}, G.Adj u v → G.Adj v w → u ≠ w → G.Adj u w
statement:
public theorem _root_.SimpleGraph.IsSRGWith.adj_of_adj_of_adj_of_mu_zero
    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] {n k ℓ : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph V} [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (h : G.IsSRGWith n k ℓ 0) {u v w : V} (huv : G.Adj u v) (hvw : G.Adj v w)
    (huw : u ≠ w) : G.Adj u w

docstring:
Every adjacency eigenvalue other than the regular degree of a strongly regular graph
satisfies the standard strongly regular graph quadratic.
name: SimpleGraph.IsSRGWith.nonprincipal_eigenvalue_quadratic
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {n k ℓ μ : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph V} [inst_1 : DecidableRel G.Adj] [inst_2 : DecidableEq V], G.IsSRGWith n k ℓ μ → ∀ {x : ℂ}, x ≠ ↑k → Module.End.HasEigenvalue (Matrix.toLin' (SimpleGraph.adjMatrix ℂ G)) x → x ^ 2 = (↑ℓ - ↑μ) * x + (↑k - ↑μ)

docstring:
`H`-saturation: `G` is `H`-free and maximal with that property in the
graph-inclusion order.

statement: def IsSaturated (G : SimpleGraph W) : Prop

docstring: A non-edge `xy` of `G` is `F`-saturating if adding it creates a copy of `F`.
name: SimpleGraph.IsSaturatingNonedge
signature: {V : Type u_1} → {W : Type u_2} → SimpleGraph V → SimpleGraph W → W → W → Prop
statement: def IsSaturatingNonedge (x y : W) : Prop

name: SimpleGraph.IsSaturatingNonedge.ne
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} (F : SimpleGraph V) (G : SimpleGraph W) {x y : W}, F.IsSaturatingNonedge G x y → x ≠ y
statement: theorem IsSaturatingNonedge.ne {x y : W} (h : IsSaturatingNonedge F G x y) : x ≠ y

docstring:
Under the source's `F`-free hypothesis, a saturating non-edge creates a copy
of `F` where none existed.
name: SimpleGraph.IsSaturatingNonedge.newCopy_of_free
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} (F : SimpleGraph V) (G : SimpleGraph W) {x y : W}, F.IsSaturatingNonedge G x y → F.Free G → F.IsContained (G ⊔ SimpleGraph.edge x y) ∧ ¬F.IsContained G
statement:
theorem IsSaturatingNonedge.newCopy_of_free {x y : W} (h : IsSaturatingNonedge F G x y)
    (hfree : Free F G) :
    IsContained F (G ⊔ edge x y) ∧ ¬IsContained F G

name: SimpleGraph.IsSaturatingNonedge.not_adj
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} (F : SimpleGraph V) (G : SimpleGraph W) {x y : W}, F.IsSaturatingNonedge G x y → ¬G.Adj x y
statement:
theorem IsSaturatingNonedge.not_adj {x y : W} (h : IsSaturatingNonedge F G x y) :
    ¬G.Adj x y

name: SimpleGraph.IsSaturatingNonedge.symm
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} (F : SimpleGraph V) (G : SimpleGraph W) {x y : W}, F.IsSaturatingNonedge G x y → F.IsSaturatingNonedge G y x
statement:
theorem IsSaturatingNonedge.symm {x y : W} (h : IsSaturatingNonedge F G x y) :
    IsSaturatingNonedge F G y x

docstring:
Uniform vertex expansion: every vertex set `S` with `|S| ≤ |V| / 2`
has at least `h * |S|` neighbours outside `S`.
name: SimpleGraph.IsUniformVertexExpander
signature: {V : Type u_1} → SimpleGraph V → [Finite V] → ℝ → Prop
statement: def IsUniformVertexExpander [Finite V] (h : ℝ) : Prop

docstring: A uniform vertex expander satisfies `0 < h`.
name: SimpleGraph.IsUniformVertexExpander.pos
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst : Finite V] {h : ℝ}, G.IsUniformVertexExpander h → 0 < h
statement:
theorem IsUniformVertexExpander.pos [Finite V] {h : ℝ}
    (hh : G.IsUniformVertexExpander h) : 0 < h

docstring: Small-set expansion clause of a uniform vertex expander.
name: SimpleGraph.IsUniformVertexExpander.small_expansion
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst : Finite V] {h : ℝ}, G.IsUniformVertexExpander h → ∀ (S : Set V), ↑S.ncard ≤ ↑(Nat.card V) / 2 → h * ↑S.ncard ≤ ↑(G.externalNeighborSet S).ncard
statement:
theorem IsUniformVertexExpander.small_expansion [Finite V] {h : ℝ}
    (hh : G.IsUniformVertexExpander h)
    (S : Set V) (hS : (S.ncard : ℝ) ≤ (Nat.card V : ℝ) / 2) :
    h * (S.ncard : ℝ) ≤ ((G.externalNeighborSet S).ncard : ℝ)

docstring:
`G` is a **unique subgraph** of `H` if there is exactly one subgraph of `H` isomorphic to
`G`. Subgraphs of `H` are taken in the spanning sense: elements `G' ≤ H` of the lattice
`SimpleGraph V`, i.e. subsets of the edges of `H` (not necessarily induced).
name: SimpleGraph.IsUniqueSubgraph
signature: {V : Type u_1} → SimpleGraph V → SimpleGraph V → Prop
statement: def IsUniqueSubgraph (G H : SimpleGraph V) : Prop

docstring:
`IsVertexConnected k G` means that `G` has more than `k` vertices and
stays connected after removing any set of fewer than `k` vertices.
name: SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected
signature: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → ℕ → SimpleGraph V → Prop
statement: public def IsVertexConnected {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (k : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop

docstring: A `k`-vertex-connected graph has more than `k` vertices.
name: SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.card_gt
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {k : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph V}, SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected k G → k < Fintype.card V
statement:
public theorem IsVertexConnected.card_gt {V : Type*} [Fintype V] {k : ℕ}
    {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : G.IsVertexConnected k) : k < Fintype.card V

docstring: A positively vertex-connected graph is connected.
name: SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.connected
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {k : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph V}, SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected k G → 0 < k → G.Connected
statement:
public theorem IsVertexConnected.connected {V : Type*} [Fintype V] {k : ℕ}
    {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : G.IsVertexConnected k) (hk : 0 < k) : G.Connected

docstring:
Deleting one vertex from a graph of vertex connectivity at least two leaves a connected
induced graph.
name: SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.connected_compl_singleton
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {k : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph V}, SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected k G → 1 < k → ∀ (v : V), (SimpleGraph.induce (↑{v})ᶜ G).Connected

docstring:
Deleting fewer than `k` vertices from a `k`-vertex-connected graph leaves a connected
induced graph.
name: SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.connected_induce_compl
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {k : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph V}, SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected k G → ∀ (S : Finset V), S.card < k → (SimpleGraph.induce (↑S)ᶜ G).Connected

docstring:
Contracting the complement of a connected set with at least two vertices in a
2-vertex-connected graph produces another 2-vertex-connected graph.
name: SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.contractOutside
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V} {D : Set V} [inst_1 : Fintype ↑D], SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected 2 G → 1 < Fintype.card ↑D → (SimpleGraph.induce D G).Connected → Dᶜ.Nonempty → SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected 2 (G.contractOutside D)
statement:
public theorem IsVertexConnected.contractOutside {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    {G : SimpleGraph V} {D : Set V} [Fintype D] (hG : G.IsVertexConnected 2)
    (hDcard : 1 < Fintype.card D) (hDconn : (G.induce D).Connected)
    (hDout : Dᶜ.Nonempty) : (G.contractOutside D).IsVertexConnected 2

docstring:
In a finite 2-vertex-connected graph, every prescribed vertex lies on a cycle with a
different vertex whose neighbors all lie on the cycle.
name: SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.exists_cycle_bound_vertex
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V}, SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected 2 G → ∀ (x : V), ∃ c, c.IsCycle ∧ ∃ y, y ≠ x ∧ c.IsBoundVertex y
statement:
public theorem IsVertexConnected.exists_cycle_bound_vertex
    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : G.IsVertexConnected 2) (x : V) :
    ∃ c : G.Walk x x, c.IsCycle ∧ ∃ y, y ≠ x ∧ c.IsBoundVertex y

docstring: Every vertex of a finite 2-vertex-connected graph lies on a cycle.
name: SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.exists_cycle_through
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V}, SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected 2 G → ∀ (x : V), ∃ c, c.IsCycle
statement:
public theorem IsVertexConnected.exists_cycle_through {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : G.IsVertexConnected 2) (x : V) :
    ∃ c : G.Walk x x, c.IsCycle

docstring:
In a 2-vertex-connected graph on at least five vertices, every vertex has at least four
neighbors in the graph square.
name: SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.four_le_square_degree
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V} [inst_1 : DecidableRel G.square.Adj], SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected 2 G → 5 ≤ Fintype.card V → ∀ (v : V), 4 ≤ G.square.degree v
statement:
public theorem IsVertexConnected.four_le_square_degree
    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V}
    [DecidableRel G.square.Adj] (hG : G.IsVertexConnected 2)
    (hcard : 5 ≤ Fintype.card V) (v : V) : 4 ≤ G.square.degree v

docstring:
Every 2-connected finite graph has a rooted Hamiltonian cycle in its square whose two
root edges belong to the original graph.
name: SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.hasStrongSquareCycle
signature: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : SimpleGraph V}, SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected 2 G → ∀ (x : V), G.HasStrongSquareCycle x

docstring: Every vertex of a finite 2-vertex-connected graph has degree at least two.
name: SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.two_le_degree
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V} [inst_1 : DecidableRel G.Adj], SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected 2 G → ∀ (v : V), 2 ≤ G.degree v
statement:
public theorem IsVertexConnected.two_le_degree {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    {G : SimpleGraph V} [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : G.IsVertexConnected 2) (v : V) :
    2 ≤ G.degree v

docstring:
A graph is vertex-transitive when its automorphism group acts transitively
on vertices.
name: SimpleGraph.IsVertexTransitive
signature: {V : Type u_1} → SimpleGraph V → Prop
statement: def IsVertexTransitive {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop

docstring: Reachability between supported vertices lifts to the graph induced on its support.
name: SimpleGraph.Reachable.induce_support
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {G : SimpleGraph V} {u v : V}, G.Reachable u v → ∀ (hu : u ∈ G.support) (hv : v ∈ G.support), (SimpleGraph.induce G.support G).Reachable ⟨u, hu⟩ ⟨v, hv⟩

docstring:
Equality of chromatic symmetric functions, represented transparently
through the coefficient characterization: agreement of all coloring-profile
counts for every finite palette and multiplicity profile.
name: SimpleGraph.SameChromaticSymmetricFunction
signature: {V : Type u_1} → {W : Type u_2} → [Finite V] → [Finite W] → SimpleGraph V → SimpleGraph W → Prop
statement:
def SameChromaticSymmetricFunction [Finite V] [Finite W]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W) : Prop

docstring:
Isomorphic graphs have equal chromatic symmetric functions: colorings and
their color-class fibers transport along the isomorphism.
name: SimpleGraph.SameChromaticSymmetricFunction.of_iso
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W} [inst : Finite V] [inst_1 : Finite W] (e : G ≃g H), G.SameChromaticSymmetricFunction H
statement:
theorem SameChromaticSymmetricFunction.of_iso [Finite V] [Finite W] (e : G ≃g H) :
    SameChromaticSymmetricFunction G H

docstring: Every graph has the same chromatic symmetric function as itself.
name: SimpleGraph.SameChromaticSymmetricFunction.refl
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.SameChromaticSymmetricFunction G
statement:
theorem SameChromaticSymmetricFunction.refl [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    SameChromaticSymmetricFunction G G

docstring: Symmetry of chromatic-symmetric-function equality.
name: SimpleGraph.SameChromaticSymmetricFunction.symm
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W} [inst : Finite V] [inst_1 : Finite W], G.SameChromaticSymmetricFunction H → H.SameChromaticSymmetricFunction G
statement:
theorem SameChromaticSymmetricFunction.symm
    [Finite V] [Finite W]
    (h : SameChromaticSymmetricFunction G H) : SameChromaticSymmetricFunction H G

docstring: Transitivity of chromatic-symmetric-function equality.
name: SimpleGraph.SameChromaticSymmetricFunction.trans
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W} [inst : Finite V] [inst_1 : Finite W] {U : Type u_3} [inst_2 : Finite U] {K : SimpleGraph U}, G.SameChromaticSymmetricFunction H → H.SameChromaticSymmetricFunction K → G.SameChromaticSymmetricFunction K
statement:
theorem SameChromaticSymmetricFunction.trans [Finite V] [Finite W]
    {U : Type*} [Finite U] {K : SimpleGraph U}
    (hGH : SameChromaticSymmetricFunction G H)
    (hHK : SameChromaticSymmetricFunction H K) : SameChromaticSymmetricFunction G K

statement: def Subgraph.IsCriticalVertex (v : V) (G' : G.Subgraph) : Prop

statement: def Subgraph.IsCriticalVerts (verts : Set V) (G' : G.Subgraph) : Prop

docstring: A vertex on a closed walk is bound to the walk when every neighbor also lies on it.
name: SimpleGraph.Walk.IsBoundVertex
signature: {V : Type u_1} → {G : SimpleGraph V} → {x : V} → G.Walk x x → V → Prop
statement:
public def Walk.IsBoundVertex {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} {x : V}
    (c : G.Walk x x) (y : V) : Prop

docstring: An Eulerian trail uses exactly one incidence for every edge at a vertex.
name: SimpleGraph.Walk.IsEulerian.countP_edges_eq_degree
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : SimpleGraph V} [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj] {u v : V} {p : G.Walk u v}, p.IsEulerian → ∀ (x : V), List.countP (fun x_1 ↦ Decidable.decide (x ∈ x_1)) p.edges = G.degree x
statement:
public theorem Walk.IsEulerian.countP_edges_eq_degree {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] {G : SimpleGraph V} [DecidableRel G.Adj] {u v : V}
    {p : G.Walk u v} (hp : p.IsEulerian) (x : V) :
    p.edges.countP (x ∈ ·) = G.degree x

docstring: A cycle is globally longest if no cycle in the graph has more edges.
name: SimpleGraph.Walk.IsLongestCycle
signature: {V : Type u_1} → {G : SimpleGraph V} → {v : V} → G.Walk v v → Prop
statement:
public def IsLongestCycle {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} {v : V}
    (p : G.Walk v v) : Prop

docstring: A vertex is bound to a closed walk exactly when it and all its neighbors lie on the walk.
name: SimpleGraph.Walk.isBoundVertex_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {G : SimpleGraph V} {x : V} (c : G.Walk x x) (y : V), c.IsBoundVertex y ↔ y ∈ c.support ∧ ∀ ⦃z : V⦄, G.Adj y z → z ∈ c.support

docstring: Adjacency unfolds to symmetric-difference cardinality one.
name: SimpleGraph.adj_iff
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (x y : G.SimplexVertex), G.simplexGraph.Adj x y ↔ (symmDiff ↑x ↑y).card = 1
statement:
public theorem adj_iff (x y : SimplexVertex G) :
    (simplexGraph G).Adj x y ↔ (x.val ∆ y.val).card = 1

docstring:
The anti-Ramsey number $\mathrm{AR}(n, H)$: the maximum number of colors in an edge coloring of
$K_n$ (that is, a labeling of the edges of $K_n$ using every color) that contains no rainbow copy
of $H$, i.e. no injective homomorphism (copy) of $H$ whose edges all receive different colors.
name: SimpleGraph.antiRamseyNum
signature: {α : Type u_3} → [Fintype α] → SimpleGraph α → ℕ → ℕ
statement: noncomputable def antiRamseyNum {α : Type*} [Fintype α] (H : SimpleGraph α) (n : ℕ) : ℕ

docstring: Iterate `G.bfsStep` at most `n` times, stopping as soon as no new vertex shows up.
name: SimpleGraph.bfsIterate
signature: {V : Type u_1} → {G : SimpleGraph V} → [Fintype V] → [DecidableEq V] → [DecidableRel G.Adj] → ℕ → Finset V → Finset V
statement: def bfsIterate : ℕ → Finset V → Finset V

name: SimpleGraph.bfsIterate_eq_iterate_bfsStep
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {G : SimpleGraph V} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj] (n : ℕ) (s : Finset V), SimpleGraph.bfsIterate n s = G.bfsStep^[n] s
statement:
lemma bfsIterate_eq_iterate_bfsStep (n : ℕ) (s : Finset V) :
    G.bfsIterate n s = G.bfsStep^[n] s

docstring:
One round of breadth-first search: `G.bfsStep s` consists of the vertices of `s` together with
their neighbours.
name: SimpleGraph.bfsStep
signature: {V : Type u_1} → (G : SimpleGraph V) → [Fintype V] → [DecidableEq V] → [DecidableRel G.Adj] → Finset V → Finset V
statement: def bfsStep : Finset V

name: SimpleGraph.bfsStep_mono
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {G : SimpleGraph V} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj] {s t : Finset V}, s ⊆ t → G.bfsStep s ⊆ G.bfsStep t
statement: lemma bfsStep_mono (hst : s ⊆ t) : G.bfsStep s ⊆ G.bfsStep t

docstring:
The book number of `G`: the maximum, over adjacent ordered vertex pairs,
of the number of common neighbors (triangles sharing that edge). Nonedges
contribute zero.
name: SimpleGraph.bookNumber
signature: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → (G : SimpleGraph V) → [DecidableRel G.Adj] → ℕ
statement: noncomputable def bookNumber (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℕ

docstring:
A uniform bound on every adjacent pair's common-neighbor count bounds the
book number.
name: SimpleGraph.bookNumber_le
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V} [inst_1 : DecidableRel G.Adj] (b : ℕ), (∀ (u v : V), G.Adj u v → {w | G.Adj u w ∧ G.Adj v w}.card ≤ b) → G.bookNumber ≤ b
statement:
theorem bookNumber_le (b : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ u v : V, G.Adj u v →
      (Finset.univ.filter fun w => G.Adj u w ∧ G.Adj v w).card ≤ b) :
    G.bookNumber ≤ b

docstring: If at least two vertices are contracted, the contraction has strictly fewer vertices.
name: SimpleGraph.card_contractOutside_lt
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (D : Set V) [inst_1 : Fintype ↑D] [inst_2 : Fintype ↑Dᶜ], 2 ≤ Fintype.card ↑Dᶜ → Fintype.card (Option ↑D) < Fintype.card V

name: SimpleGraph.card_div_indepNum_le_chromaticNumber
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {G : SimpleGraph V}, ↑⌈↑(Nat.card V) / ↑G.indepNum⌉₊ ≤ G.chromaticNumber
statement: lemma card_div_indepNum_le_chromaticNumber : ⌈(Nat.card V / α(G) : ℚ≥0)⌉₊ ≤ G.chromaticNumber

docstring: Any acyclic induced vertex set is bounded by the induced forest number.
name: SimpleGraph.card_le_inducedForestNumber
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (s : Finset V), (SimpleGraph.induce (↑s) G).IsAcyclic → s.card ≤ G.inducedForestNumber
statement:
theorem card_le_inducedForestNumber (G : SimpleGraph V) (s : Finset V)
    (h : (G.induce (↑s : Set V)).IsAcyclic) :
    s.card ≤ G.inducedForestNumber

docstring: **Caro–Wei bound** restated via the independence number.
name: SimpleGraph.caroWei_le_indepNum
signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {G : SimpleGraph V} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableRel G.Adj], ∑ v, 1 / (↑(G.degree v) + 1) ≤ ↑G.indepNum
statement:
theorem caroWei_le_indepNum :
    ∑ v, (1 : ℝ) / (G.degree v + 1) ≤ G.indepNum

docstring:
The chromatic cardinal is the minimal number of colors need to color it. In contrast to
`chromaticNumber`, which assigns `⊤ : ℕ∞` to all non-finitely colorable graphs, this definition
returns a `Cardinal` and can therefore distinguish between different infinite chromatic numbers.
name: SimpleGraph.chromaticCardinal
signature: {V : Type u} → SimpleGraph V → Cardinal
statement: noncomputable def chromaticCardinal.{u} {V : Type u} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Cardinal

docstring:
Number of proper colorings of `G` with labeled colors `Fin k` in which
each color occurs with exactly the prescribed multiplicity. These counts are
the coefficients of the chromatic symmetric function.
name: SimpleGraph.chromaticProfileCount
signature: {V : Type u_1} → [Finite V] → SimpleGraph V → (k : ℕ) → (Fin k → ℕ) → ℕ

docstring:
Generalized Turán number `ex(n, T, H)`: the maximum possible number of
copies of pattern `T` in an `H`-free host graph on `n` vertices. `G.copyCount T`
counts copies of pattern `T` in host `G`, and `H.Free G` states that `G` is
`H`-free. The intended domain from the source is patterns `T` and `H` with no
isolated vertices; the definition itself does not require this.

The total definition follows Mathlib's `Finset.sup` convention used by
`SimpleGraph.extremalNumber`: it is the supremum of `G.copyCount T` over the
filtered family `Finset.univ.filter (fun G : SimpleGraph (Fin n) => H.Free G)`.
As with `Finset.sup` over `ℕ`, the value is `0` when the filtered family is
empty.
name: SimpleGraph.generalizedExtremalNumber
signature: ℕ → {α : Type u_1} → {β : Type u_2} → [Fintype α] → SimpleGraph α → SimpleGraph β → ℕ

docstring:
The generalized Turán number unfolds to the exact filtered `Finset.sup`
expression: the supremum of `G.copyCount T` over all `H`-free hosts on
`Fin n`.
name: SimpleGraph.generalizedExtremalNumber_eq_sup
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ) {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype α] (T : SimpleGraph α) (H : SimpleGraph β), SimpleGraph.generalizedExtremalNumber n T H = {G | H.Free G}.sup fun G ↦ G.copyCount T
statement:
public theorem generalizedExtremalNumber_eq_sup (n : ℕ)
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α]
    (T : SimpleGraph α) (H : SimpleGraph β) :
    generalizedExtremalNumber n T H =
      Finset.sup (Finset.univ.filter (fun G : SimpleGraph (Fin n) => H.Free G))
        (fun G => G.copyCount T)

docstring:
Upper-bound characterization: the generalized Turán number is at most `m`
if and only if every `H`-free host has at most `m` copies of `T`.
name: SimpleGraph.generalizedExtremalNumber_le_iff
signature: ∀ (n : ℕ) {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype α] (T : SimpleGraph α) (H : SimpleGraph β) (m : ℕ), SimpleGraph.generalizedExtremalNumber n T H ≤ m ↔ ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), H.Free G → G.copyCount T ≤ m
statement:
public theorem generalizedExtremalNumber_le_iff (n : ℕ)
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α]
    (T : SimpleGraph α) (H : SimpleGraph β)
    (m : ℕ) :
    generalizedExtremalNumber n T H ≤ m ↔
      ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), H.Free G → G.copyCount T ≤ m

signature: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (x : V), G.HasStrongSquareCycle x ↔ ∃ p, p.IsHamiltonianCycle ∧ G.Adj x p.snd ∧ G.Adj p.penultimate x

docstring:
For a finite vertex type, the number of distinct unique subgraphs of `H`: the number of
isomorphism classes of graphs
that occur exactly once as a subgraph of `H`. The set-builder ranges over spanning subgraphs
`G ≤ H` satisfying `IsUniqueSubgraph G H`; mapping each such `G` to its isomorphism class is a
bijection onto the once-occurring classes. In particular, automorphic copies do not inflate the
count: if distinct `G₁ ≤ H` and `G₂ ≤ H` are isomorphic, neither satisfies `IsUniqueSubgraph`
(the other is a second isomorphic copy), so neither is counted.
name: SimpleGraph.uniqueSubgraphCount
signature: {V : Type u_1} → [Finite V] → SimpleGraph V → ℕ
statement: noncomputable def uniqueSubgraphCount [Finite V] (H : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ

Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).

statement: structure StrictCoveringSystem (R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] extends CoveringSystem R
