docstring: Dual of a nonzero submodule as the multiplication dual submodule.
name: Submodule.dualEquivMulDualSubmodule
signature: {A : Type u_1} → {K : Type u_2} → [inst : CommRing A] → [IsDomain A] → [inst_2 : Field K] → [inst_3 : Algebra A K] → [IsFractionRing A K] → (M : Submodule A K) → M ≠ ⊥ → Module.Dual A ↥M ≃ₗ[A] ↥(LinearMap.BilinForm.dualSubmodule (LinearMap.mul K K) M)
statement:
noncomputable def Submodule.dualEquivMulDualSubmodule (M : Submodule A K) (hM : M ≠ ⊥) :
    Module.Dual A M ≃ₗ[A] LinearMap.BilinForm.dualSubmodule
      (LinearMap.mul K K : LinearMap.BilinForm K K) M

docstring: Evaluation of the multiplication dual equivalence.
name: Submodule.dualEquivMulDualSubmodule_spec
signature: ∀ {A : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : IsDomain A] [inst_2 : Field K] [inst_3 : Algebra A K] [inst_4 : IsFractionRing A K] (M : Submodule A K) (hM : M ≠ ⊥) (f : Module.Dual A ↥M) (m : ↥M), (Algebra.algebraMap A K) (f m) = ↑((M.dualEquivMulDualSubmodule hM) f) * ↑m
statement:
theorem Submodule.dualEquivMulDualSubmodule_spec (M : Submodule A K) (hM : M ≠ ⊥)
    (f : Module.Dual A M) (m : M) :
    algebraMap A K (f m) = (Submodule.dualEquivMulDualSubmodule M hM f : K) * (m : K)

docstring: Every dual element is multiplication by a fraction.
name: Submodule.exists_mul_rep
signature: ∀ {A : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [inst_2 : Field K] [inst_3 : Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] (M : Submodule A K), M ≠ ⊥ → ∀ (f : Module.Dual A ↥M), ∃ x, ∀ (m : ↥M), (Algebra.algebraMap A K) (f m) = x * ↑m
statement:
theorem Submodule.exists_mul_rep (M : Submodule A K) (hM : M ≠ ⊥)
    (f : Module.Dual A M) :
    ∃ x : K, ∀ m : M, algebraMap A K (f m) = x * m

docstring:
Any submodule `N` of a finite free module `M` over a PID has a Smith normal form: bases
`bM` of `M` and `bN` of `N` with `bN i = a i • bM i`, nonzero coefficients `a i`, and the
invariant-factor divisibility chain `a i ∣ a (i+1)`. This refines
`Submodule.exists_smith_normal_form_of_le`, which gives no divisibility chain.
`MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.SmithNormalFormWanted.smithNormalForm` is the source-shaped form.
name: Submodule.exists_smith_normal_form_dvd_chain
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsPrincipalIdealRing R] [inst_3 : AddCommGroup M] [inst_4 : _root_.Module R M] [Module.Free R M] [Module.Finite R M] (N : Submodule R M), ∃ n m, ∃ (hnm : n ≤ m), ∃ bM bN a, (∀ (i : Fin n), ↑(bN i) = a i • bM (Fin.castLE hnm i)) ∧ (∀ (i : Fin n), a i ≠ 0) ∧ ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi1 : i < n) (hi2 : i + 1 < n), a ⟨i, hi1⟩ ∣ a ⟨i + 1, hi2⟩
statement:
theorem exists_smith_normal_form_dvd_chain
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsPrincipalIdealRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Free R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (N : Submodule R M) :
    ∃ (n m : ℕ) (hnm : n ≤ m) (bM : Module.Basis (Fin m) R M)
      (bN : Module.Basis (Fin n) R N) (a : Fin n → R),
      (∀ i, (bN i : M) = a i • bM (Fin.castLE hnm i)) ∧
      (∀ i, a i ≠ 0) ∧
      (∀ (i : ℕ) (hi1 : i < n) (hi2 : i + 1 < n), a ⟨i, hi1⟩ ∣ a ⟨i + 1, hi2⟩)

docstring: If `M` spans `V` over the fraction field, its subtype is a localized module map.
name: Submodule.isLocalizedModule_subtype_of_span_eq_top
signature: ∀ {A : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : Field K] [inst_2 : Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] [inst_4 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_5 : _root_.Module A V] [inst_6 : _root_.Module K V] [IsScalarTower A K V] (M : Submodule A V), Submodule.span K ↑M = ⊤ → IsLocalizedModule (nonZeroDivisors A) M.subtype
statement:
theorem Submodule.isLocalizedModule_subtype_of_span_eq_top (M : Submodule A V)
    (hspan : Submodule.span K (M : Set V) = ⊤) :
    IsLocalizedModule (A⁰) M.subtype

docstring:
Localization commutes with submodule division for a finitely generated
denominator.
name: Submodule.localized'_div_of_fg
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} {K : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : CommRing K] [inst_3 : Algebra R S] [inst_4 : Algebra R K] [inst_5 : Algebra S K] [inst_6 : IsScalarTower R S K] {p : Submonoid R} [inst_7 : IsLocalization p S] [inst_8 : IsLocalizedModule p LinearMap.id] (I J : Submodule R K), J.FG → Submodule.localized' S p LinearMap.id (I / J) = Submodule.localized' S p LinearMap.id I / Submodule.localized' S p LinearMap.id J
statement:
lemma localized'_div_of_fg (I J : Submodule R K) (hJ : J.FG) :
    (I / J).localized' S p (.id : K →ₗ[R] K) =
      I.localized' S p (.id : K →ₗ[R] K) /
        J.localized' S p (.id : K →ₗ[R] K)

docstring:
Cassels' embedding theorem: the subring generated by a finite subset of a
characteristic-zero field embeds injectively into `ℤ_[p]` for some prime `p ≥ 3`.

J. W. S. Cassels, "An embedding theorem for fields", Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. 14
(1976), 193–198.
name: Subring.exists_injective_ringHom_closure_padicInt
signature: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (S : Finset K), ∃ p, ∃ (hp : Nat.Prime p), 3 ≤ p ∧ ∃ phi, Function.Injective ⇑phi
statement:
public theorem exists_injective_ringHom_closure_padicInt {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K]
    (S : Finset K) :
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime),
      letI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hp⟩
      3 ≤ p ∧ ∃ phi : Subring.closure (↑S : Set K) →+* ℤ_[p],
        Function.Injective phi

name: SumSquares.mem_solutions

docstring:
The jointly periodic points of `f`: points periodic for `f` and periodic for
the unit shift. No common temporal period is required.

name: SymbolicDynamics.FullShift.mem_jointlyPeriodicPoints
signature: ∀ (N : ℕ) (f : SymbolicDynamics.FullShift.FullShiftSpace N → SymbolicDynamics.FullShift.FullShiftSpace N) (x : SymbolicDynamics.FullShift.FullShiftSpace N), x ∈ SymbolicDynamics.FullShift.jointlyPeriodicPoints N f ↔ x ∈ Function.periodicPts f ∧ x ∈ Function.periodicPts (SymbolicDynamics.FullShift.unitShift N)

theorem mem_jointlyPeriodicPoints (N : ℕ) (f : FullShiftSpace N → FullShiftSpace N)

name: TateCohomology.herbrandQuotient_eq
signature: ∀ {R G : Type u} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Group G] [inst_2 : Fintype G] (M : Rep R G) (h : TateCohomology.HerbrandFinite M), TateCohomology.herbrandQuotient M h = ↑(Nat.card ↑(tateCohomology M 0)) / ↑(Nat.card ↑(tateCohomology M (-1)))

docstring:
A shared finite constant, ratio, and actual function witness sharp equality.
Source: arXiv:1012.2061v1, Theorem Th2.loglog, lines 739-762.
No numerical value or globally unique maximizing ratio is asserted.
name: TorusSobolev.LogarithmicRemainderWanted.exactGlobalExtremal
signature: ∃ L δ u, TorusSobolev.sharpRemainderValue = ↑L ∧ TorusSobolev.UniformRemainderBound L ∧ 1 < δ ∧ TorusSobolev.ConditionalAdmissible u δ ∧ ↑(u 0 ^ 2) = TorusSobolev.theta δ ∧ TorusSobolev.IsExplicitExtremal u ∧ u 0 ^ 2 = 1 / (4 * Real.pi) * (Real.log δ + Real.log (1 + Real.log δ) + L)

  ∃ L δ : ℝ, ∃ u : C(Torus, ℝ), sharpRemainderValue = (L : EReal) ∧

    (((u 0) ^ 2 : ℝ) : EReal) = theta δ ∧ IsExplicitExtremal u ∧

docstring:
Source: Grimmer–Shu–Wang, retained introduction, best-iterate rate 1.0564.
One positive schedule and global rate constants precede every objective and
bounded initial sublevel set. D bounds that whole sublevel set, not merely
the initial distance. The explicit block construction and proof are unproved.
name: WantedExt.Analysis.Convex.GradientDescentExponentBoundsWanted.gsw_best_iterate_primary_bound
signature: ∃ s, (∀ (k : ℕ), 0 < s k) ∧ ∃ C, 0 < C ∧ ∃ K, 0 < K ∧ ∀ (d : ℕ) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ), IsUnitSmoothConvex f → ∀ (xstar : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), (∀ (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), f xstar ≤ f x) → ∀ (x₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (D : ℝ), 0 ≤ D → (∀ (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), f x ≤ f x₀ → ‖x - xstar‖ ≤ D) → ∀ (T : ℕ), K ≤ T → ∃ i ≤ T, f (gradientDescentTrajectory f s x₀ i) - f xstar ≤ C * D ^ 2 / ↑T ^ (2641 / 2500)
statement:
private theorem_wanted gsw_best_iterate_primary_bound :
    ∃ s : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k, 0 < s k) ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ K : ℕ, 0 < K ∧
      ∀ (d : ℕ) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ), IsUnitSmoothConvex f →
        ∀ xstar : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), (∀ x, f xstar ≤ f x) →

docstring:
The codimension-two subconfiguration and one scaled projected point.
This is an unproved claim.
Source: Grinsztajn (2026), Sections 4-6.
name: WantedExt.Geometry.BorsukStructuredConstructionsWanted.grinsztajnProjectedPointConstruction
statement:
private theorem_wanted grinsztajnProjectedPointConstruction : (by
  classical
  exact ∃ (e : BrouwerOrthogonalBasis ≃ Fin 416)
      (x : Fin 416 → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 65)) (B : Fin 3 → Finset (Fin 416))
      (b : Fin 416),
    let G := brouwerG2FourGraph.comap e.symm
    let C := Finset.univ \ (Finset.univ.biUnion B)
    let S : Fin 3 → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 65) := fun i => ∑ v ∈ B i, x v
    let U := Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range S)
    let W := Uᗮ
    let z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 65) := W.orthogonalProjectionOnto (x b)
    let t : ℝ := (Real.sqrt 222 - 1) / 13
    let p := t • z
    let X := (x '' (C : Set (Fin 416))) ∪ {p}
    G.IsSRGWith 416 100 36 20 ∧ Function.Injective x ∧
    (∀ u v, inner ℝ (x u) (x v) =
      if u = v then 90 else if G.Adj u v then 18 else -6) ∧
    (∀ i, (B i).card = 32) ∧
    (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (B i) (B j)) ∧
    C.card = 320 ∧ b ∈ B 0 ∧
    Module.finrank ℝ U = 2 ∧ Module.finrank ℝ W = 63 ∧
    (∀ c ∈ C, x c ∈ W) ∧
    z = x b - (1 / 32 : ℝ) • S 0 ∧ ‖z‖ ^ 2 = 78 ∧
    0 < t ∧ 78 * t ^ 2 + 12 * t = 102 ∧
    (∀ c ∈ C, dist p (x c) ^ 2 = if G.Adj b c then 192 - 48 * t else 192) ∧
    X.ncard = 321 ∧ ediam X = ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt 192) ∧
    (∀ Y ⊆ X, ediam Y < ediam X → Y.ncard ≤ 5) ∧
    ∃ φ : W ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 63),
      let X₆₃ := φ '' {y : W | (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 65)) ∈ X}
      X₆₃.ncard = 321 ∧ ¬HasBorsukCover 64 X₆₃ ∧
        (65 : ℕ∞) ≤ setBorsukNumber X₆₃)

statement:
private theorem_wanted jenrichBrouwerStructuredConstruction : (by
  classical
  exact ∃ (e : BrouwerOrthogonalBasis ≃ Fin 416)
      (x : Fin 416 → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 65)) (B : Fin 3 → Finset (Fin 416)),
    let G := brouwerG2FourGraph.comap e.symm
    let C := Finset.univ \ (Finset.univ.biUnion B)
    let S : Fin 3 → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 65) := fun i => ∑ v ∈ B i, x v
    let W := (Submodule.span ℝ {S 1 - S 2})ᗮ
    let A := C ∪ B 0
    G.IsSRGWith 416 100 36 20 ∧ Function.Injective x ∧
    (∀ u v, inner ℝ (x u) (x v) =
      if u = v then 90 else if G.Adj u v then 18 else -6) ∧
    (∀ i, (B i).card = 32) ∧ (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (B i) (B j)) ∧
    C.card = 320 ∧ A.card = 352 ∧ Module.finrank ℝ W = 64 ∧
    (∀ a ∈ A, x a ∈ W) ∧
    ∃ φ : W ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 64),
      let X := φ '' {y : W | (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 65)) ∈ x '' (A : Set (Fin 416))}
      X.ncard = 352 ∧ IsTwoDistanceSet X ∧

docstring:
An elliptic curve over an algebraic closure of `ZMod p` is supersingular when every geometric
point killed by `p` is zero.

This is the `r = 1` form of the equivalent torsion condition in arXiv:2308.11539v1,
`main.tex`, lines 164–170.
name: WeierstrassCurve.Affine.IsSupersingular
signature: {p : ℕ} → [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] → (W : WeierstrassCurve.Affine (AlgebraicClosure (ZMod p))) → [WeierstrassCurve.IsElliptic W] → Prop
statement:
def IsSupersingular {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    (W : WeierstrassCurve.Affine (AlgebraicClosure (ZMod p))) [W.IsElliptic] : Prop

name: WeierstrassCurve.Affine.IsSupersingular.iff_pow_torsion
signature: ∀ {p : ℕ} [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (W : WeierstrassCurve.Affine (AlgebraicClosure (ZMod p))) [inst_1 : WeierstrassCurve.IsElliptic W], W.IsSupersingular ↔ ∀ (r : ℕ), 0 < r → ∀ (P : W.Point), p ^ r • P = 0 → P = 0
statement:
theorem IsSupersingular.iff_pow_torsion {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    (W : WeierstrassCurve.Affine (AlgebraicClosure (ZMod p))) [W.IsElliptic] :
    W.IsSupersingular ↔
      ∀ r : ℕ, 0 < r → ∀ P : W.Point, (p ^ r) • P = 0 → P = 0

docstring: Trivial `p ^ r`-torsion for every positive `r` implies supersingularity.
name: WeierstrassCurve.Affine.IsSupersingular.of_pow_torsion
signature: ∀ {p : ℕ} [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (W : WeierstrassCurve.Affine (AlgebraicClosure (ZMod p))) [inst_1 : WeierstrassCurve.IsElliptic W], (∀ (r : ℕ), 0 < r → ∀ (P : W.Point), p ^ r • P = 0 → P = 0) → W.IsSupersingular
statement:
theorem IsSupersingular.of_pow_torsion {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    (W : WeierstrassCurve.Affine (AlgebraicClosure (ZMod p))) [W.IsElliptic]
    (h : ∀ r : ℕ, 0 < r → ∀ P : W.Point, (p ^ r) • P = 0 → P = 0) :
    W.IsSupersingular

docstring: A supersingular elliptic curve has trivial `p ^ r`-torsion for every positive `r`.
name: WeierstrassCurve.Affine.IsSupersingular.pow_torsion
signature: ∀ {p : ℕ} [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (W : WeierstrassCurve.Affine (AlgebraicClosure (ZMod p))) [inst_1 : WeierstrassCurve.IsElliptic W], W.IsSupersingular → ∀ {r : ℕ}, 0 < r → ∀ {P : W.Point}, p ^ r • P = 0 → P = 0
statement:
theorem IsSupersingular.pow_torsion {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]

    (h : W.IsSupersingular) {r : ℕ} (hr : 0 < r)
    {P : W.Point} (hP : (p ^ r) • P = 0) : P = 0

docstring:
Block harmonic sum vanishing modulo `p ^ 2` for primes `p ≥ 5`.

Source: Jerry Metzger and Thomas Richards, "A Prisoner Problem Variation",
`https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL18/Metzger/metz1.tex`, lines 657–662
(live file SHA-256
`660bfcb06fb3e08814f30b24659410fba256effd4161ec1cca7ea9fc3d20b0ec`;
exact source-span SHA-256
`0aa191b703844e65e7e2fd1c181532b3409c2720e7317d93f130d66c66f34d0f`;
concept `jis_dep_8bfbdf778d8b84efc2cbaafc`).

Cited original: L. Carlitz, "A note on Wolstenholme's theorem", American
Mathematical Monthly 61 (1954), 174–176.

Here `k : ℕ` follows the source application; the sum runs over `r = 1, …, p - 1`
via `Finset.Ico 1 p`; under the hypotheses all denominators are units modulo
`p ^ 2`.
Proves `Wanted` entry `ZMod.carlitz_sum_inv_block_Ico_eq_zero_of_five_le`.
name: ZMod.carlitz_sum_inv_block_Ico_eq_zero_of_five_le
signature: ∀ (p k : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → 5 ≤ p → ∑ r ∈ Finset.Ico 1 p, (↑(k * p + r))⁻¹ = 0
statement:
theorem ZMod.carlitz_sum_inv_block_Ico_eq_zero_of_five_le
    (p k : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hp5 : 5 ≤ p) :
    (Finset.Ico 1 p).sum
      (fun r => (((k * p + r : ℕ) : ZMod (p ^ 2))⁻¹)) = 0

docstring:
The Abel continuation `F_f(s) = s * ∫ x in Ioi 1, A(⌊x⌋) * x^(-s-1)`,
in the exact conventions of `LSeries_eq_mul_integral`.
name: abelContinuation

statement: def abelContinuation (f : ℕ → ℂ) (s : ℂ) : ℂ

docstring:
Agreement with `LSeries f s` at summable points. The hypothesis `0 ≤ σ`
is required only here, because the public `LSeries_eq_mul_integral` API
requires it; no claim is made about `LSeries f` itself where it is
nonsummable (there it is `0` by definition).
name: abelContinuation_eq_LSeries
signature: ∀ (f : ℕ → ℂ) {σ : ℝ}, 0 ≤ σ → ∀ {s : ℂ}, σ < s.re → LSeriesSummable f s → ((fun n ↦ abelPartialSum f n) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n ↦ ↑n ^ σ) → abelContinuation f s = LSeries f s
statement:
theorem abelContinuation_eq_LSeries (f : ℕ → ℂ) {σ : ℝ} (hσ : 0 ≤ σ) {s : ℂ}
    (hs : σ < s.re) (hS : LSeriesSummable f s)
    (hO : (fun n => abelPartialSum f n) =O[atTop] fun n => ((n : ℝ) ^ σ : ℝ)) :
    abelContinuation f s = LSeries f s

docstring:
The Abel integral equals `s` times the Mellin transform at `-s`.
This is the bridge that transfers Mellin holomorphy to the continuation.
name: abelContinuation_eq_mul_mellin
signature: ∀ (f : ℕ → ℂ) {σ : ℝ} {s : ℂ}, σ < s.re → ((fun n ↦ abelPartialSum f n) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n ↦ ↑n ^ σ) → abelContinuation f s = s * mellin (abelSummatory f) (-s)
statement:
theorem abelContinuation_eq_mul_mellin (f : ℕ → ℂ) {σ : ℝ} {s : ℂ}
    (hs : σ < s.re)
    (hO : (fun n => abelPartialSum f n) =O[atTop] fun n => ((n : ℝ) ^ σ : ℝ)) :
    abelContinuation f s = s * mellin (abelSummatory f) (-s)

docstring:
Tame different-ideal equality: under `map 𝔪A = 𝔪B ^ e` with
`IsUnit (e : B)`, the different ideal equals `𝔪B ^ (e - 1)`. This is the
correct tame equality, not the false wild equality in ATLAS.

signature: ∀ (A : Type u_1) (B : Type u_2) [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : CommRing B] [inst_2 : IsDomain A] [inst_3 : IsDomain B] [inst_4 : IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [inst_5 : IsDiscreteValuationRing B] [inst_6 : Algebra A B] [inst_7 : Module.IsTorsionFree A B] [inst_8 : Module.Finite A B] [Algebra.IsSeparable (FractionRing A) (FractionRing B)] [Algebra.IsSeparable (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)] (e : ℕ), IsUnit ↑e → Ideal.map (Algebra.algebraMap A B) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ e → differentIdeal A B = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ (e - 1)

      maximalIdeal B ^ e) :

docstring:
Holomorphy of the Laplace transform from an eventual exponential Big-O bound.

This completes the source-shaped endpoint as a corrected, strengthened-premise
formalization of the ATLAS N320 intended holomorphy claim: with
`LocallyIntegrableOn f (Set.Ici 0)` explicitly repairing the missing endpoint
condition, an eventual bound `f =O[atTop] exp (a * t)` gives holomorphy on
`{s | a < s.re}`. ATLAS's piecewise continuity on `ℝ_{>0}` does not supply
near-zero integrability (counterexample `f(t) = 1/t`). The `Ici 0` hypothesis is
load-bearing: local integrability on the open ray plus an `atTop` bound would not
suffice. This is not a literal proof of the under-specified source wording.
name: differentiableOn_laplace_of_isBigO_exp
signature: ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℂ E] (f : ℝ → E) (a : ℝ), MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrableOn f (Set.Ici 0) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume → (f =O[Filter.atTop] fun t ↦ Real.exp (a * t)) → ∀ [CompleteSpace E], DifferentiableOn ℂ (laplace f) {s | a < s.re}
statement:
theorem differentiableOn_laplace_of_isBigO_exp
    (f : ℝ → E) (a : ℝ)
    (hf : LocallyIntegrableOn f (Set.Ici 0))
    (hO : f =O[Filter.atTop] (fun t : ℝ => Real.exp (a * t)))
    [CompleteSpace E] :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (laplace f) {s | a < s.re}

docstring:
Lagrange–Bürmann inversion formula, coefficient form: if `A = X * subst A phi`
with `coeff 0 phi ≠ 0`, then for `n ≥ 1`,
`n * [X^n](subst A g) = [X^(n-1)](derivative g * phi ^ n)`.
This is the division-free form over a commutative ring: no division by `n` is
required. The hypothesis `hn : 0 < n` prevents truncated subtraction at zero in
`n - 1`. No reversion or analytic variant is claimed.
Primary source: Alexander M. Haupt, "Enumeration of S-omino Towers and
Row-Convex k-omino Towers," JIS 24 (2021), proposition at lines 400–407,
https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL24/Haupt/haupt4.tex, file SHA-256
`1b412146e9dba7d9302d274268baf3e35239b8369473faf57f086f918e3b66af`, span SHA-256
`ba6bf0dfa1cffa8a22bf10e4f7528c86dbe5ced596286dee93a765f5db3774cf`.
Corroborating power specialization: Dmitry Kruchinin and Vladimir Kruchinin,
"A Method for Obtaining Generating Functions for Central Coefficients of
Triangles," JIS 15 (2012), lines 199–210,
https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL15/Kruchinin/kruchinin5.tex, file SHA-256
`abb875f7d7951467436cf43c9c7d0dd662fdfd05382952f542ad53b2ebfcea8f`, span SHA-256
`805d5ab3e7352b021e119fb2bec5cfd477f4a01469758b601fb7a9ea4c5f0d36`.
Source concept `jis_grounded_b2a0ba5cfa34a62aa3e66f0f`;
variants `formal_implicit_composition` and `formal_power_specialization`.

Proves `Wanted` entry `fps_lagrange_burmann_coeff`.
name: fps_lagrange_burmann_coeff
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (A phi g : PowerSeries R), PowerSeries.HasSubst A → (PowerSeries.coeff 0) phi ≠ 0 → A = PowerSeries.X * PowerSeries.subst A phi → ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ↑n * (PowerSeries.coeff n) (PowerSeries.subst A g) = (PowerSeries.coeff (n - 1)) (PowerSeries.derivative g * phi ^ n)
statement:
theorem fps_lagrange_burmann_coeff {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (A phi g : PowerSeries R)
    (hsubst : PowerSeries.HasSubst A) (hphi : PowerSeries.coeff 0 phi ≠ 0)
    (hfix : A = PowerSeries.X * PowerSeries.subst A phi) (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    (n : R) * PowerSeries.coeff n (PowerSeries.subst A g) =
      PowerSeries.coeff (n - 1) (PowerSeries.derivative g * phi ^ n)

name: fps_lagrange_burmann_coeff'
signature: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (A phi g : PowerSeries R), A = PowerSeries.X * PowerSeries.subst A phi → ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ↑n * (PowerSeries.coeff n) (PowerSeries.subst A g) = (PowerSeries.coeff (n - 1)) (PowerSeries.derivative g * phi ^ n)
statement:

    (n : R) * PowerSeries.coeff n (PowerSeries.subst A g) =

docstring:
Tame integral-trace surjectivity: under `map 𝔪A = 𝔪B ^ e` with
`IsUnit (e : B)`, the integral trace `Algebra.intTrace A B` is surjective.
Separability supplies a residue element of trace one, lifted to `b : B`;
since `e` is a unit, the bridge identity
`residue_intTrace_eq_nsmul_trace_residue_of_map_maximalIdeal_eq_pow` makes
`Algebra.intTrace A B b` a unit, and scaling `b` by an arbitrary `a` against
that unit hits every target. The `IsUnit (e : B)` form is ergonomic for the
eventual tame ramification criterion; localness makes it equivalent to
unitness in `A`. This proves the tame trace-surjectivity input only: it does
not prove the mixed-characteristic wild bound, nor ATLAS's false exact wild
equality.

docstring:
Laplace convergence from a source-shaped eventual exponential Big-O bound.

This is the first half of a corrected, strengthened-premise formalization of the
ATLAS N320 intended convergence claim: a locally integrable function with
`f =O[atTop] exp (a * t)` has a convergent Laplace transform for `a < s.re`.
The `LocallyIntegrableOn f (Set.Ici 0)` premise explicitly repairs the missing
endpoint condition: ATLAS's piecewise continuity on `ℝ_{>0}` does not supply
near-zero integrability (counterexample `f(t) = 1/t`); the tail is handled by the
asymptotic integrability API. This is not a literal proof of the under-specified
source wording.
name: laplaceConvergent_of_isBigO_exp
signature: ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℂ E] (f : ℝ → E) (a : ℝ), MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrableOn f (Set.Ici 0) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume → (f =O[Filter.atTop] fun t ↦ Real.exp (a * t)) → ∀ {s : ℂ}, a < s.re → LaplaceConvergent f s
statement:
theorem laplaceConvergent_of_isBigO_exp
    (f : ℝ → E) (a : ℝ)
    (hloc : LocallyIntegrableOn f (Set.Ici 0))
    (ho : f =O[Filter.atTop] (fun t : ℝ => Real.exp (a * t)))
    {s : ℂ} (hs : a < s.re) :
    LaplaceConvergent f s

docstring: Combined fractionality and nontriviality for sandwiched lattices.

docstring: Upper bound for the lattice discriminant from a containing basis lattice.

docstring:
A linear Legendre-symbol sum over a complete residue system vanishes when
the slope is nonzero modulo the odd prime `p`.

This is the first corollary of Theorem `thm1` in Ram Krishna Pandey and
Anshumaan Parashar, *On Certain Sums with Quadratic Expressions Involving the
Legendre Symbol*, Journal of Integer Sequences 21 (2018), Article 18.4.7,
lines 190–193,
<https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL21/Pandey/pandey14.tex>.
The proof here reindexes Mathlib's `quadraticChar_sum_zero`
through the affine permutation `x ↦ b * x + c` of `ZMod p`.
name: legendreSym.sum_linear_eq_zero
signature: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], Odd p → ∀ (b c : ℤ), ¬↑p ∣ b → ∑ ℓ ∈ Finset.range p, legendreSym p (b * ↑ℓ + c) = 0
statement:
public theorem sum_linear_eq_zero
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hpodd : Odd p) (b c : ℤ) (hb : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b) :
    ∑ ℓ ∈ Finset.range p, legendreSym p (b * (ℓ : ℤ) + c) = 0

statement: def linearAsymptoticDirichletContinuation (a : ℕ → ℂ) (ρ s : ℂ) : ℂ

docstring: Cleared-denominator factorization away from `1`.
name: linearAsymptoticDirichletContinuation_eq_inv_sub_mul
signature: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℂ) (ρ : ℂ) {s : ℂ}, s ≠ 1 → linearAsymptoticDirichletContinuation a ρ s = (s - 1)⁻¹ * (ρ * riemannZeta₁ s + (s - 1) * abelContinuation (fun n ↦ a n - ρ) s)
statement:
theorem linearAsymptoticDirichletContinuation_eq_inv_sub_mul
    (a : ℕ → ℂ) (ρ : ℂ) {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 1) :
    linearAsymptoticDirichletContinuation a ρ s =
      (s - 1)⁻¹ *
        (ρ * riemannZeta₁ s + (s - 1) * abelContinuation (fun n => a n - ρ) s)

docstring:
Under `map 𝔪A ≤ 𝔪B ^ n`, the defining ideal `map 𝔪A ⊔ 𝔪B ^ n` collapses
to `𝔪B ^ n`, by `sup_eq_right`.
name: maximalIdealPowQuotientIdeal_eq
signature: ∀ (A : Type u_1) (B : Type u_2) [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : CommRing B] [inst_2 : IsDomain A] [inst_3 : IsDomain B] [inst_4 : IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [inst_5 : IsDiscreteValuationRing B] [inst_6 : Algebra A B] (n : ℕ), Ideal.map (Algebra.algebraMap A B) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ n → Ideal.map (Algebra.algebraMap A B) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ⊔ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ n = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ n
statement:
theorem maximalIdealPowQuotientIdeal_eq (n : ℕ)
    (h : Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal A) ≤ maximalIdeal B ^ n) :
    (Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal A) ⊔ maximalIdeal B ^ n :
      Ideal B) = maximalIdeal B ^ n

docstring:
The defining ideals shrink with `n`: `map 𝔪A ⊔ 𝔪B ^ (n + 1)` is contained
in `map 𝔪A ⊔ 𝔪B ^ n`, by `Ideal.pow_le_pow_right n.le_succ` and lattice
monotonicity.
name: maximalIdealPowQuotientIdeal_le
signature: ∀ (A : Type u_1) (B : Type u_2) [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : CommRing B] [inst_2 : IsDomain A] [inst_3 : IsDomain B] [inst_4 : IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [inst_5 : IsDiscreteValuationRing B] [inst_6 : Algebra A B] (n : ℕ), Ideal.map (Algebra.algebraMap A B) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ⊔ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ (n + 1) ≤ Ideal.map (Algebra.algebraMap A B) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ⊔ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ n
statement:
theorem maximalIdealPowQuotientIdeal_le (n : ℕ) :
    (Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal A) ⊔ maximalIdeal B ^ (n + 1) :
      Ideal B) ≤
      Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal A) ⊔ maximalIdeal B ^ n

docstring:
Newman's Tauberian theorem: a bounded measurable function on the positive ray
whose Laplace transform extends analytically to the closed right half-plane has
convergent partial integrals tending to the value at zero.
name: newman_tauberian
signature: ∀ (f : ℝ → ℂ) (B : ℝ), MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable f (MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.restrict (Set.Ioi 0)) → 0 ≤ B → (∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → ‖f t‖ ≤ B) → ∀ (G : ℂ → ℂ), AnalyticOnNhd ℂ G {s | 0 ≤ s.re} → (∀ (s : ℂ), 0 < s.re → HasLaplace f s (G s)) → Filter.Tendsto (fun T ↦ ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..T, f t) Filter.atTop (nhds (G 0))
statement:
theorem newman_tauberian (f : ℝ → ℂ) (B : ℝ)
    (hfmeas : AEStronglyMeasurable f (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Ioi 0)))
    (hB : 0 ≤ B) (hbound : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ‖f t‖ ≤ B)
    (G : ℂ → ℂ)
    (hG_analytic : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ G {s | 0 ≤ s.re})
    (hG : ∀ s : ℂ, 0 < s.re → HasLaplace f s (G s)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun T : ℝ => ∫ t : ℝ in (0 : ℝ)..T, f t)
      Filter.atTop (𝓝 (G 0))

docstring:
The `n`-th maximal-ideal graded piece of `B` is `ResidueField A`-linearly
the kernel of the factor map from index `n + 1` to index `n`, when
`map 𝔪A ≤ 𝔪B ^ (n + 1)`. The map sends a graded representative to the
corresponding quotient representative, which lies in the kernel because the
representative lies in `𝔪B ^ n`. Bijectivity goes through the quotient-ring
equivalence `residueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotientEquivPow` (replacing the source
ideal by `𝔪B ^ (n + 1)`), `Ideal.powQuotPowSuccLinearEquivMapMkPowSuccPow`, and
`Ideal.Quotient.factor_ker`. Residue-base scalar compatibility is checked on
representatives via the scalar tower through `ResidueField B` (there is no

docstring:
Integral-trace residue bridge: under `map 𝔪A = 𝔪B ^ e`, the residue of
`Algebra.intTrace A B b` equals `e` times the residue-field trace of
`residue B b`. The proof combines Mathlib's quotient-trace identity
`Algebra.trace_quotient_eq_of_isDedekindDomain` (at `p := maximalIdeal A`,
whose quotient is `ResidueField A`) with the iterated quotient trace formula
`trace_residueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient`: since `he` collapses the defining
ideal `map 𝔪A ⊔ 𝔪B ^ e` to `map 𝔪A`, the custom quotient is
`ResidueField A`-algebra equivalent to `B ⧸ map 𝔪A` via
`Ideal.quotEquivOfEq` (fixing representatives, with scalar compatibility
checked on representatives as in
`factorResidueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient`), and trace conjugacy
(`Algebra.trace_eq_of_algEquiv`) transports the Mathlib identity to the
custom quotient. The DVR hypotheses supply the Dedekind and integrally-closed
instances. This is new bridge infrastructure for the corrected ATLAS N261
quotient-filtration route, not a source theorem: it controls the integral
trace only modulo `maximalIdeal A` and does not prove the wild
mixed-characteristic fractional-dual bound.
name: residue_intTrace_eq_nsmul_trace_residue_of_map_maximalIdeal_eq_pow
signature: ∀ (A : Type u_1) (B : Type u_2) [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : CommRing B] [inst_2 : IsDomain A] [inst_3 : IsDomain B] [inst_4 : IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [inst_5 : IsDiscreteValuationRing B] [inst_6 : Algebra A B] (e : ℕ) [inst_7 : Module.IsTorsionFree A B] [inst_8 : Module.Finite A B], Ideal.map (Algebra.algebraMap A B) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ e → ∀ (b : B), (IsLocalRing.residue A) ((Algebra.intTrace A B) b) = e • (Algebra.trace (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)) ((IsLocalRing.residue B) b)
statement:
theorem residue_intTrace_eq_nsmul_trace_residue_of_map_maximalIdeal_eq_pow
    (e : ℕ)
    [Module.IsTorsionFree A B] [Module.Finite A B]
    (he : Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal A) =
      maximalIdeal B ^ e)
    (b : B) :
    residue A (Algebra.intTrace A B b) =
      e • Algebra.trace (ResidueField A)
        (ResidueField B) (residue B b)

docstring:

docstring:
Schnirelmann's sumset inequality: the density of `A + B` is at least
`σ(A) + σ(B) - σ(A) * σ(B)` when both sets contain zero.
name: schnirelmannDensity_add_lower_bound
signature: ∀ {A B : Set ℕ} [inst : DecidablePred fun x ↦ x ∈ A] [inst_1 : DecidablePred fun x ↦ x ∈ B] [inst_2 : DecidablePred fun x ↦ x ∈ A + B], 0 ∈ A → 0 ∈ B → schnirelmannDensity A + schnirelmannDensity B - schnirelmannDensity A * schnirelmannDensity B ≤ schnirelmannDensity (A + B)
statement:
theorem _root_.schnirelmannDensity_add_lower_bound {A B : Set ℕ}

        schnirelmannDensity A * schnirelmannDensity B ≤
      schnirelmannDensity (A + B)

docstring:

summability is assumed. The proof applies public Abel summation
(`tendsto_sum_mul_atTop_nhds_one_sub_integral₀`) to the zero-padded
coefficients `c n = if n = 0 then 0 else f n`, whose partial sums agree
with `abelPartialSum f`, with weight `x ↦ (x : ℂ) ^ (-s)`.
name: tendsto_abelContinuation_Icc
signature: ∀ (f : ℕ → ℂ) {σ : ℝ} {s : ℂ}, σ < s.re → ((fun n ↦ abelPartialSum f n) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n ↦ ↑n ^ σ) → Filter.Tendsto (fun N ↦ ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, LSeries.term f s n) Filter.atTop (nhds (abelContinuation f s))
statement:

      fun n => ((n : ℝ) ^ σ : ℝ)) :
    Tendsto (fun N => ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, LSeries.term f s n) atTop

docstring:
The all-orders logarithmic asymptotic expansion of the Catalan numbers at an
arbitrary real shift, with coefficients given by differences of Bernoulli polynomials.
name: tendsto_pow_mul_log_catalan_sub_bernoulli_sum
signature: ∀ (c : ℝ) (M : ℕ), Filter.Tendsto (fun n ↦ (↑n + c) ^ M * (Real.log (↑(catalan n) * √(Real.pi * (↑n + c) ^ 3) / 4 ^ n) - ∑ j ∈ Finset.range M, (-1) ^ (j + 2) * ((Polynomial.aeval (1 / 2 - c)) (Polynomial.bernoulli (j + 2)) - (Polynomial.aeval (2 - c)) (Polynomial.bernoulli (j + 2))) / (↑(j + 1) * ↑(j + 2)) * (1 / (↑n + c) ^ (j + 1)))) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
statement:
public theorem _root_.tendsto_pow_mul_log_catalan_sub_bernoulli_sum (c : ℝ) :
    ∀ M : ℕ,
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun n : ℕ =>
          (n + c : ℝ) ^ M *
            (Real.log ((catalan n : ℝ) *
                Real.sqrt (Real.pi * (n + c : ℝ) ^ 3) / (4 : ℝ) ^ n) -
              ∑ j ∈ Finset.range M,
                (-1 : ℝ) ^ (j + 2) *
                  (Polynomial.aeval (1 / 2 - c) (Polynomial.bernoulli (j + 2)) -
                    Polynomial.aeval (2 - c) (Polynomial.bernoulli (j + 2))) /
                    ((j + 1 : ℕ) * (j + 2 : ℕ)) *
                  (1 / (n + c : ℝ) ^ (j + 1))))
        Filter.atTop (nhds 0)

docstring:
Iterated quotient trace formula: the algebra trace of multiplication by
the representative `b` on quotient index `n` equals `n` times the
residue-field trace of `residue B b`. The proof is by induction on `n`: at
index zero the defining ideal is the whole ring so the representative is
zero, and the successor case combines the one-step recurrence
`trace_residueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient_succ` with the induction
hypothesis. The graded-piece module/tower hypotheses of the one-step
recurrence are installed locally from the canonical restriction of scalars
along `algebraMap (ResidueField A) (ResidueField B)`, so they do not appear
in the public signature. This is new prerequisite infrastructure for the
corrected ATLAS N261 quotient-filtration route, not a source theorem.
name: trace_residueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient
signature: ∀ (A : Type u_1) (B : Type u_2) [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : CommRing B] [inst_2 : IsDomain A] [inst_3 : IsDomain B] [inst_4 : IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [inst_5 : IsDiscreteValuationRing B] [inst_6 : Algebra A B] (n : ℕ), Ideal.map (Algebra.algebraMap A B) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ n → ∀ [inst_7 : IsLocalHom (Algebra.algebraMap A B)] [FiniteDimensional (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (ResidueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient A B n)] (b : B), (Algebra.trace (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (ResidueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient A B n)) ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (Algebra.algebraMap A B) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ⊔ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ n)) b) = n • (Algebra.trace (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)) ((IsLocalRing.residue B) b)
statement:
theorem trace_residueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient
    (n : ℕ)
    (h : Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal A) ≤ maximalIdeal B ^ n)
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    [FiniteDimensional (ResidueField A)
      (ResidueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient A B n)]
    (b : B) :
    Algebra.trace (ResidueField A)
        (ResidueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient A B n)
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ b) =
      n • Algebra.trace (ResidueField A) (ResidueField B)
        (IsLocalRing.residue B b)

docstring:
One-step trace recurrence across the maximal-ideal-power quotient tower:
the algebra trace of multiplication by the representative `b` on quotient
index `n + 1` splits as the residue-field trace of `residue B b` plus the
algebra trace of multiplication by the representative `b` on quotient index
`n`. The proof uses the factor map as the surjective intertwiner
(`map_mul` gives multiplication compatibility), identifies its kernel with
the graded piece, transports the kernel-restriction trace by conjugacy, and
applies the graded-piece trace theorem. This is new prerequisite
infrastructure for the corrected ATLAS N261 quotient-filtration route, not a

name: trace_residueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient_succ
signature: ∀ (A : Type u_1) (B : Type u_2) [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : CommRing B] [inst_2 : IsDomain A] [inst_3 : IsDomain B] [inst_4 : IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [inst_5 : IsDiscreteValuationRing B] [inst_6 : Algebra A B] (n : ℕ), Ideal.map (Algebra.algebraMap A B) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ (n + 1) → ∀ [inst_7 : IsLocalHom (Algebra.algebraMap A B)] [inst_8 : _root_.Module (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (IsDiscreteValuationRing.MaximalIdealGradedPiece B n)] [IsScalarTower (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) (IsDiscreteValuationRing.MaximalIdealGradedPiece B n)] [FiniteDimensional (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (ResidueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient A B (n + 1))] (b : B), (Algebra.trace (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (ResidueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient A B (n + 1))) ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (Algebra.algebraMap A B) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ⊔ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ (n + 1))) b) = (Algebra.trace (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)) ((IsLocalRing.residue B) b) + (Algebra.trace (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (ResidueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient A B n)) ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (Algebra.algebraMap A B) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ⊔ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ n)) b)
statement:
theorem trace_residueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient_succ
    (n : ℕ)
    (hSucc : Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal A) ≤
      maximalIdeal B ^ (n + 1))
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    [Module (ResidueField A)
      (IsDiscreteValuationRing.MaximalIdealGradedPiece B n)]
    [IsScalarTower (ResidueField A) (ResidueField B)
      (IsDiscreteValuationRing.MaximalIdealGradedPiece B n)]
    [FiniteDimensional (ResidueField A)
      (ResidueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient A B (n + 1))]
    (b : B) :
    Algebra.trace (ResidueField A)
        (ResidueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient A B (n + 1))
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ b) =
      Algebra.trace (ResidueField A) (ResidueField B)
        (IsLocalRing.residue B b) +
        Algebra.trace (ResidueField A)
          (ResidueFieldMaximalIdealPowQuotient A B n)
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ b)

docstring:
The number of unit-distance pairs of a finite set of `n` points is at most $\binom{n}{2}$,
the total number of unordered pairs of distinct points.
name: unitDistNum_le_choose_two
signature: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] (s : Finset X), unitDistNum s ≤ s.card.choose 2
statement: theorem unitDistNum_le_choose_two (s : Finset X) : unitDistNum s ≤ (#s).choose 2
